Causes enemies to forget that you are there. If they were attacking you, they might stop. Also gives a powerful shield for a short time.
When you are back in Avadon, visit your four companions often. They will frequently have more to say.
You start out being able to equip one scarab. As you gain levels, you will be able to use more of them.
Most scarabs are obtained by helping people in Avadon. Talk to the officials there and see if they have work for you.
When you are in Avadon, you can train all four of your assistants and supply them with equipment and scarabs.
When you leave Avadon to go on a mission, you may choose two companions to take with you. You can leave Avadon by yourself, but it is very dangerous.
When you leave companions behind in Avadon, they will practice and learn on their own. As you gain levels, all of your companions will too.
Locations appear on the world map when people in towns tell you about them.
Hold down the Shift key to see the names of all visible creatures.
Hold down the Tab key to see a full map of the area you are in.
You have a Junk Bag on your inventory screen. Put items into it that you just want to sell back in town. Then, when you are selling, you can unload everything in it with one click.
You can Control-Click items in your pack or on the ground to move them into your junk bag. They can all then be sold very quickly when you are selling in a store.
When in Avadon, all of your characters can shop, equip items, and sell unwanted gear. When on the inventory screen, click a character's portrait to see its equipment.
Are you unhappy with how you trained a character? Find Trainer Leala in the Beraza Woods. She can enable you to retrain all of your skills.
Don't actually like Redbeard much? Perhaps, with great care and skill, you might find a way to replace him.
If the game is too difficult, you can make it easier using the Preferences window. To bring it up, load your saved game, press the Disk button and select Preferences.
You can use the 'f' key on the keyboard as a shortcut to start and stop fights. Hit the space bar to end a character's turn early.
You can use the 'g' key on the keyboard as a shortcut to get items.
Using abilities causes fatigue. You need to return to Avadon occasionally to rest. Otherwise, you will be too tired to fight well.
To end your turn in combat, press the space bar.
To quickly switch between melee and missile weapons in combat, type 'w'.
In combat, each character can be set to use your main weapon or missile weapon. To switch, use the buttons at the bottom of the screen (or type 'w').
Your health goes up as you gain levels. You can also train your Endurance when you gain levels to gain health.
Press the Journal button (it looks like a book) to see lists of all of your special items and current quests.
Press the F3 key to quickly save the game. Press F4 to load your Quicksave slot.
As you travel, Avadon will occasionally automatically save your game. This saved game will be called _Autosave._
If you kill a monster who is much weaker than you, you receive less experience. If you kill a monster much tougher than you, you get more experience.
There are four Quick Spell buttons at the bottom of the screen. Press one to assign a spell to it. You can then select that spell very easily.
You can cast the spells in the four Quick Spell slots by pressing F5, F6, F7, or F8.
To change a spell attached to a Quick Spell button, right-click the button.
When you leave an area, you will see a map of the world. Select your new destination. As you talk to people and receive quests, more locations will appear on the map.
Remember that you can see a list of quests you have received by pressing the Journal button (to the left of the Start/End Combat button).
When getting items, some of them will be marked 'NY'. This means Not Yours. You can't steal them when someone is looking.
During a difficult fight against a powerful enemy, watch the top of the screen for notes. These messages can give valuable hints about what to do to defeat the enemy.
For people who are new to fantasy role-playing games or just want to easily experience the storyline. Your foes are far less threatening.
The game starts out quite easy but becomes a challenge as you get close to the end. A nice, moderate difficulty level.
A harder difficulty setting for the more experienced gamer. Your foes will do more damage and be a lot harder to kill.
The ultimate challenge for the warriors of Avadon. You will need to use every trick and fully utilize every ability to defeat the nasty enemies arrayed against you.
Unconsciousness and Death
One of your characters has just been knocked unconscious. This happens when your Health level reaches zero.
Once combat is over, your unconscious characters can be revived. A Resurrection scroll can bring back a knocked-out ally before battle is done.
Poison and Acid
One of your characters has been afflicted with Poison or Acid. This will damage the character every turn until it fades away or is cured.
Some characters have abilities that can cure poison and other such harmful conditions. Curing Brew can also help.
Stopping Movement
When you are next to a foe and then move away, your enemy will stop your movement. You will only be able to move one space for the rest of the turn.
If you need to end your turn early, you can do this by pressing the Space Bar or clicking on your active character.
Fatigue and Vitality
Your character is low on Vitality. Using your more powerful abilities fatigues you, draining Vitality. When you are out, you can't use your strong abilities anymore.
To cure fatigue, return to Avadon or an Arrival Pylon. You can also drink a Potion of Vitality.
You are now hasted. Each of your abilities and attacks has a chance of using fewer action points, enabling you to act again during your turn.
You are a warrior of the Midlands Pact.

The Pact is an alliance of five nations, banded together for safety. The Farlands, enemies of the Pact, surround it on all sides. These are nations of barbarians, raiders, titans. Faded, jealous Empires, all waiting for a sign of weakness.
The Pact has one purpose: To crush the Farlands and keep them weak and divided. Otherwise, they will invade your homeland, take what they want, and massacre whoever stands in their way.

You have spent your life training and preparing to defend the Pact, and you have done well. Your skill and potential has earned you the greatest of honors. You have been sent to serve at a new fortress ...
Avadon.
Avadon. The Black Fortress.

The warriors of Avadon watch over the five nations of the Pact. When anyone acts to harm the peace and tranquility of the Pact, Avadon has the authority to destroy them. Its authority and independence are almost without limit.

And Avadon's power is not only over the outsiders of the Farlands. Anyone who tries to weaken the Pact from within is subject to punishment. Brigands, spies, politicians, all have reason to fear the eye of Avadon, and the attention of its master: Keeper Redbeard.

Avadon has watched over the Pact for three centuries. Its warriors wield the finest weapons. Its wizards can learn the most powerful spells. And the keeper of the Black Fortress, Redbeard, directs them all.

Few outsiders know anything about Redbeard. There are plenty of rumors. Some say that he has three wives, each a deadly warrior. You've heard that assassins try to kill him every week. They all fail and, in turn, receive the most gruesome punishments imaginable. Some believe that Redbeard can see into your dreams.
Outsiders, if they are lucky, never get close enough to Avadon to learn the truth. But you ... Today you will meet Redbeard yourself. You are standing outside the gates of the Black Fortress.

You stand on the bridge, over a deep, misty chasm. The iron gates of Avadon are before you. Beyond is your new life, full of adventure, danger, power, wealth, and service to the Pact. The Black Fortress looms over you, perched on an enormous, granite peak. The gates open a crack, granting you entrance.
You step through, and your service to Avadon begins ...
Service to Avadon is a true honor, and the rewards are great. Wealth. Power. Sometimes, even fame. But there is a down side as well: the risk of ending up in the crypts deep below the Black Fortress.
Alas, your journey in Avadon's service has come to an end. Redbeard and his servants will have to fight the conspiracy against the Pact without your help.
But don't give up! Perhaps, knowing what you know now, you can prevail against your foes. Rise and fight again, in the service of Avadon!
When you fall under Redbeard's onslaught and lose consciousness, you think that it is the end for you.

Then they wake you up. You are in a dark, stone hall, standing in a magic circle. Magical bonds hold you in place. As you realize where you are, you begin to despair. You are in the dungeons of Avadon.

Redbeard sometimes makes an example of those who are disloyal to him. You serve as an educational display for the servants of Avadon for many, many years. As war rages outside, dark, horrible decades stretch ahead of you ...
The sun rose the next morning over a blasted and burned Avadon. The assassins who snuck in through the low tunnels had all either been killed or managed to escape.
The survivors, stunned by the brazen attack upon the heart of Avadon's power, wandered the halls, taking note of the damage.

The destruction was considerable. The libraries were burned. Eye Leira, librarian of Avadon, was found murdered in the stacks. Centuries of records and accumulated knowledge, not to mention invaluable reports on the current state of Lynaeus, were now ashes.
Many of the Hands who survived the attacks and ambushes of the last few months were dead. Workshops were destroyed. The mind-reading crystals of the dungeons were smashed.
The stunned, surviving Hands and Eyes followed their first instinct, which was to look for Heart Miranda, Redbeard's most trusted administrator.
They did not find her. They did not yet know of her treachery. Of course, they will have many chances to curse it in the months to come.
So then they went to Redbeard's Tower, looking for their leader. When they found that the gates to the Hall of Resolution were sealed, panic began to spread.
Then, just as the newly terrified and broken warriors of Avadon were about to shed their training and determination, loot the citadel, and flee, the gates opened. They ran through.
In the hall, they found Redbeard. You stood by his side. You had been sorely tested, a number of times, and yet you remained loyal to the Pact.
All of your companions were absent, each tempted away from their duties by their own goals. You remained, and your constancy will be rewarded.

One of your companions still stood by your side, inspired by you to remain loyal to the Pact. The others were absent, each tempted away from their duties by their own goals. You remained, and your constancy will be rewarded.

Your companions still stood by your side, inspired by you to remain loyal to the Pact. Once full of doubt, they finally were helped to see that their true enemies were not in Avadon, but the Farlands.

They found a hall that had seen fierce battle. The ground was scorched, and blood splattered the walls. And yet, you lived. You stood by Redbeard's side, bruised and battered. He had beaten you into submission, a treatment he had been forced to give many wavering servants before now.
Both you and Redbeard have a hard time standing, both beaten as you were by the ferocity of your battle. The Hands before you look slightly awed.
Redbeard says, _I am relieved that you did not drag any of your companions to doom with you. They were all weak, in their way, and yet they were strong in the end._
Redbeard says, _Your survival comes at a price. There is a debt that needs to be paid for your defiance of me._

Sevilin, your once-loyal companion, is taken away to be executed. He looks at you one final time and says, _My people learn from birth of the sacredness of the law. I will submit to it now, and with dignity._ He is taken away.

Shima Threespear, brave warrior of Holklanda, is taken away to be executed. Before he is dragged off, he says, _It was an honor to fight by your side. In the end, my sacred duties compelled me. I have no regrets._ He is taken away.

Jenell, shaman of the Wyldrylm, is taken away to be executed. Before she leaves, she bows her head. _I have no apologies for anything. I fought for what is best for my people. I have but one request. I want to die in the garden, near nature._ Her wish is granted.

Nathalie, young and ambitious sorceress of the Kellem, is taken away to be executed. In her final hour, she looks terribly young. She tries to speak, but can only choke back a sob. When she faints, the guards carry her away and carry out the sentence with merciful speed.
Since none of your companions joined you in your final, futile battle, none of them are subjected to a final, gruesome punishment. You can at least feel pleased about that.

Redbeard turns to you and places a hand on your shoulder. _I know that you have followed a difficult path lately. The work you have had to do was hard, you have been given many chances to doubt the work we do, and, perhaps, my leadership has not been as strong as it should be._
_Yet, you have prevailed. You have withstood both danger and confusion, and you have stayed loyal. I will remember this, and you will be rewarded._
In the hall, they find Redbeard's body. It is something they did not think they would see in their lifetime: Avadon's most cunning Keeper, finally defeated.
You stand there, bruised, battered, and triumphant. And alone. None of your companions came with you to seize power. None of them will be rewarded.
You stand there, bruised, battered, and triumphant. One of your companions stands by your side, ready to be rewarded for great loyalty.
You stand there, bruised, battered, and triumphant. Your companions stand by your side, ready to be rewarded for their great loyalty.
Once they have taken in the scene, the Hands, one by one, kneel to you. Perhaps an assassin will slay you or Hanvar's Council will unseat you. Until then, you are the Keeper of Avadon.
Sevilin turns to you. _The law is clear. You are Keeper now. I know my duty. I will fight by your side. I swear my loyalty to you._
Shima Threespear bows deeply to you. _I knew that I saw greatness in you. My old family lies dead. My new family is here in Avadon. I swear loyalty to you._
Jenell looks disturbed, but, after some thought, turns and kneels to you. _I hope you will maintain the humility Redbeard lost. I owe you my life, and that chance, so I swear loyalty to you._

Nathalie looks around the room, barely able to comprehend all that has happened. Then she turns to you. _You saw the greatness in me when none else did. My power can do great things for you. I swear I will do all I can._
It is a long, somber, lonely moment. You wish that you had companions by your side, people you could trust and rely on. And yet, in the end, the Keeper of Avadon is truly alone.

Then, as more and more survivors of the assault enter the hall, Redbeard starts questioning the Hands. He learns of the damage that was suffered and the loyal servants that were lost. His feelings are clearly visible on his face. First, surprise and shock. Then limitless rage.
He stands and steps forward, ready to give a speech to his demoralized followers.
_I ... I owe you an apology. I am old. For the first time, I think I might be too old. And yet, this crisis has happened while I am in charge. It is my responsibility, and I will face it._

_I have been complacent. I have not watched the day-to-day operation of this fortress enough. I have trusted my servants, and some of them have rewarded us with betrayal. From now until I fall, I will not let my attention wander again._
_We don't know who is responsible for the attacks we have suffered, both on our Hands in the field and Avadon itself. I promise you this. We will find out, and we will be avenged._

_We know who is responsible for the attacks we have suffered. His name is Dheless. He is in the Tawon Empire. He has spread his conspiracy against us to all corners of Lynaeus. That is all we know so far, but we will learn more soon._
_The Pact is under attack, my friends! Hanvar's Council is divided and confused, and it relies upon Avadon to save it. We will not shrink from this task!_

The Hands in attendance cheer at this. They have been reminded who they are: Servants of the Pact, and of Avadon. They practically run from the room, ready to rebuild this fortress and begin the hunt.

You join them. It is the beginning of months of hard work. As investigations begin and many difficult conversations happen with Hanvar's Council, you learn something of what has been happening elsewhere in Lynaeus.

Since you are now a Heart, you help to direct them. It is the beginning of months of hard work. As investigations begin and many difficult conversations happen with Hanvar's Council, you learn something of what has been happening elsewhere in Lynaeus.

Since you are now their Keeper, you direct them. It is the beginning of months of hard work. As investigations begin and many difficult conversations happen with Hanvar's Council, you learn something of what has been happening elsewhere in Lynaeus.

Then, as more and more survivors of the assault enter the hall, you start to question the Hands. You learn of the damage that was suffered and the loyal servants that were lost. Despite your ambivalent feelings about Avadon and the power of the Pact, it is hard not to be angered by the wanton destruction.

Then, as more and more survivors of the assault enter the hall, you start to question the Hands. You learn of the damage that was suffered and the loyal servants that were lost. To hear what was done to Avadon, your fortress, fills you with fury.
The Hands watch you, waiting for leadership. You are forced to give your first speech as Keeper of Avadon.

_Redbeard was a skilled Keeper, but he was old, and he had gone astray. Avadon had power, but not the justice that needed to accompany it. Now this crisis has happened while I am in charge. It is our responsibility, and we will face it._

_Redbeard was a skilled Keeper, but he was old, and he had become weak. Avadon must not ever be distracted. The Pact relies upon our power and our willingness to use it. Now this crisis has happened while I am in charge. It is our responsibility, and we will face it._
_I will not be complacent. I will have servants, but I will never put too much trust in them. From now until I fall, Avadon's Keeper's attention will not wander again._
Eventually, Avadon is rebuilt. The damage is repaired. More Hands are quickly recruited. And yet, it has lost many of its most experienced servants and almost all of its records.

Worse, it has lost its aura of invulnerability. For the first time in many years, many stop fearing Avadon. While on missions, Hands are frequently attacked and sometimes killed. There is little fear of reprisal.
Walls are easily repaired. Wounds to reputation are far harder to cure.
Hanvar's Council, long jealous and fearful of Avadon's influence, tries to weaken its power. Avadon is then forced to use some of its limited power to defend itself from attacks from within the Pact.

They are hard days. Redbeard works to the limits of human endurance and beyond. When one problem is solved, two spring up to replace it. Unrest in Lynaeus, both in the Pact and the Farlands, increases dramatically.

It is a hard time. You work to the limits of human endurance and beyond. When one problem is solved, two spring up to replace it. Unrest in Lynaeus, both in the Pact and the Farlands, increases dramatically.

Sometimes, you aren't sure whether you should just let Avadon collapse now. You decide against it, instead letting it crumble slowly. As long as you are in charge of Avadon, you will make sure that it decays. To prevent instant assassination, however, you create the impression of hard, loyal work.
But, when times are hardest, your fellow warriors develop a habit. They look each other in the eye and say, _We are Avadon._ Then they work and learn and fight twice as hard.
But, when times are hardest, the people under your command develop a habit. They look each other in the eye and say, _We are Avadon._ Then they work and learn and fight twice as hard.
They do not know who is working to undermine the Pact, but they are determined to find out. As attacks increase, they struggle to learn the identity of their assailant. He or she can't hide forever.

Though they know that one called Dheless is working to undermine the Pact, they are unable to find him. As attacks increase, they struggle to learn the location of their assailant. And yet, he can't hide forever.
Day and night, they leave the Black Fortress, risking attacks as they roam the free roads, trying to find the hidden enemy before Lynaeus crumbles into war.
The first volleys have been launched.
The true battle still lies ahead.
You will be ready for it.

Things are not well in the Pact. Holklanda and Kellemderiel edge closer and closer to war. Instead of concentrating on defending themselves from the enemies at the gates, the Pact states jockey for advantage and plan for civil war.
From time to time, you hear tales of Duke Gryfyn. He travels through Kellemderiel in secret, urging his people to leave the Pact and ally with the Tawon Empire. Many are listening to him.
The allies of Duke Gryfyn travel through Kellemderiel in secret, urging his people to leave the Pact and ally with the Tawon Empire. Many are listening to them.
For the first time in many years, the Pact seems to be in danger of falling apart. Avadon hunts for those who would tear the alliance apart, but it soon finds itself attacked from another direction.

The unrest in the Wretch Lands does not end. It only grows worse. The people of The Kva have to fight off constant incursions of wretches, ogres, and even the occasional titan. Zhethron continues to aid the Pact, but only because of his grievous wounds. When he recovers, he might well depart.

The dragon Zephyrine soon shows herself to be no ally to the Pact. She only grows more firmly entrenched in the Wretch Lands, building her defenses and gathering allies. It will be some time before anyone has the strength to dislodge her.
One small bright spot is that you were able to defeat the dragon Zephyrine. With her gone, the Pact will have a much easier time subduing this wild land.

Fortunately, you were able to return the secret papers you found in the lair of the titans to Avadon. Once these messages are decoded, the hidden lairs of many hostile Farlanders are revealed. Using this information, The Kva is able to do much to destroy their enemies.
Alas, in the dry wastes of southeast Lynaeus, many hard battles lie ahead.
In Khemeria, much as predicted, the many enemies of Dhorl Stead soon gather. They rush in, ready to destroy Dhorl Stead and claim Oghrym'Tor for themselves.

However, they soon find that, while the leaders of Dhorl Stead are gone, many of its best hunters and warriors survived. They take up residence inside the fortress and, with great courage and resolve, defeat the invaders.
Thus, though Laurella's journey to Avadon resulted in much carnage in her home, Dhorl Stead was able to survive and remain free.
They find a Stead greatly depleted. Most of its best warriors were lost during your assault. The invaders charge through Dhorl Stead's meager defenses and seize Carsta'Arl's mighty fortress.
Within weeks of your final departure, Dhorl Stead is no more.
The news from the Beraza Woods is grim. You know now that Duke Gryfyn had Monitor Shigaz and his fellow warriors murdered.
However, Avadon is unable to convince Holklanda that this assault was the act of a traitor. The Holklandans only see the murder of their countrymen by their hated rivals.

Hanvar's Council does all it can to calm the two rivals, to little avail. For the first time in almost a century, the Pact seems threatened by civil war. If it is not prevented, it will be a disaster beyond reckoning. It is here that the hidden foes of the Pact have scored their true victory.
It will only be revealed in the months and years to come whether this wound to the Pact is a mortal one.

Happily, you were able to banish the demon lord Beloch back to the infernal realms from which he came. In these chaotic times, it is unlikely that Avadon would have found the time and resources to deal with this powerful threat.

Unfortunately, the demon lord Beloch remains in Khemeria, precariously balanced between our world and the infernal realms. In these chaotic times, Avadon is unable to find the time and resources to deal with this powerful threat.
So far, nobody has found a way to master Beloch and help the beast to enter our world. All you can do is hope that this powerful threat stays trapped where it is ...
Report to Avadon.
You have just arrived at Avadon. Find someone in authority you can report to, like the old man on the east side of the entry courtyard.
Find Heart Miranda.
Walk through the gate and speak with Heart Miranda. She is currently in charge and will hopefully help you to get settled in with a minimum of violence.
Go To Dungeons.
The recent disruption has enabled many prisoners in the Avadon Dungeons to escape. Go south and speak with Sevilin and Nathalie, the Hands who can help you to regain control.
Then go downstairs, find Eye Mamora, and do whatever he tells you to do.
Meet Redbeard
At last, you can meet Keeper Redbeard, master of Avadon. The stairs to his tower are in the center of the main floor. Go upstairs and introduce yourself.
Return to Miranda.
Go back downstairs and find Heart Miranda's office. Speak with her and she will hopefully give you some time to settle in.
Get Supplies.
For your upcoming mission, you will get some supplies and equipment. This includes a scarab, whatever that is.
Speak with Smith Duman and Craftmaster Nicodemus. You can find them in the southeastern quadrant of Avadon.
Aiding Zhethron.
First, go to the northwest corner of Avadon and meet Shima and Jenell, two more Hands who can help you on your missions. Then go to the portal in the southern edge of Avadon.
Travel through it and find your way to the dragon Zhethron. Speak with the creature and do whatever is required to pacify it.
The Beast of Khemeria.

You need to go to Khemeria, one of the Farlands. A monster in the woods is hunting the townsfolk. Normally, Avadon would not care, but the presence of the creature might mean illegal magic is being performed.
Use the portal in the northern chamber. Go there, find the creature, and act as you see fit. And, if possible, don't let the rulers there know your purpose until absolutely necessary.
Ogre Raiders.

Once again, the dragon Zhethron is angry and requires assistance. Take the southern portal back to Goldcrag, visit the creature, and do what is required to keep it happy. Apparently, ogre attacks are involved.
See Redbeard.
Return to Redbeard's tower and speak with the Keeper. He has decided that some task requires his personal attention.
Hunting the Wizard
Research has revealed that the creature you hunted down in Khemeria was, indeed, the product of illegal magic. This insolence cannot be tolerated.
Use the northern portal to return to the Farlands, find the wizard or witch responsible, and destroy the offender.
The Titan Peaks.
There is new word from The Kva. Titans have been sighted in the area around Goldcrag, and the dragon Zhethron was wounded while hunting them.

Return there and speak with Zhethron. Action must be taken to drive back these huge and dangerous creatures. Also, find any evidence you can to show who is urging these creatures to rise up against the Pact.
Hunting the Lord.
It has been revealed that Carsta'Arl, the lord you met in Khemeria, was responsible for the rogue wizard's research. He has been acting directly against the Pact, and he must be brought to justice.
Heart Miranda gave you orders to use the northern portal to return to Khemeria. Go to Carsta'Arl's keep, arrest him, and bring him back. If he refuses, kill him.
Castle Vebeaux.
For decades, the lands of Holklanda and Kellemderiel have been on the brink of war. There is a rare chance to bring peace between the two, and Redbeard is sending you there to help.
Use the eastern portal to travel to Castle Vebeaux in Kellemderiel and meet with Duke Gryfyn there. Observe and do whatever you can to aid in the negotiations.
Back to Vebeaux.

Use the eastern portal to return to Castle Vebeaux in Kellemderiel. Find Duke Gryfyn. Something has happened to interfere with their combined raids in the Beraza woods, and you need to do whatever you can to calm the angry Kellem and Holklandans.
Bringing the Peace.

There is good news from Castle Vebeaux. After months of successful cooperation, the Kellem and Holklandans are on the brink of negotiating a new peace. Duke Gryfyn has requested that you help with security.
Use the eastern portal to return to Kellemderiel and aid Duke Gryfyn during this delicate process.
Return to Avadon.
Something terrible has happened. You have been betrayed and driven from Castle Vebeaux.
You need to find a way to return to Avadon and report to Redbeard what has happened.
Search Brasula's Quarters.
Hand Callan of Avadon asked a small favor of you. Go downstairs and search the quarters of Brasula, an envoy from the Tawon Empire. She is looking for evidence that Brasula is a spy.
The Lower Cells.
During the recent troubles in the Avadon dungeons, a dangerous prisoner, Shadow Tarkus, escaped. Hand Callan asked you to search the lower tunnels and see if he is hiding down there.
The stairway down to the lower caves is in the southeast corner of the dungeon.
Deal With Tartam.
You met a man named Abi in Avadon. He is from The Kva. He told you that there is a suspicious man named Tartam living west of Goldcrag.
Abi believes that Tartam is selling quality weapons to the wretch tribes, which is a serious crime. He asked you to investigate.
The Bandits of Beraza.
Envoy Brasula of the Tawon Empire (one of the Farlands) has come to Avadon to hire a Hand. There is a Dharamite bandit named Eudor in the Beraza woods, who has been leading raids into Tawon lands.
This sort of thing disrupts the peace, which is bad. Brasula will pay a bounty if you can bring Eudor to justice.
Recover Herenus

Envoy Brasula of the Tawon Empire (one of the Farlands) has come to Avadon to hire a Hand. There is a wizard named Herenus living deep within the Beraza Woods. Brasula wants him to return to the Empire.
Your mission is simple. Find him and deliver the message, 'Your clan has a golden throne.' That's it.
Find Quennel.
Fabron is an envoy from Kellemderiel, currently in Avadon. He asked for your help. He believes that there is a man named Quennel in the dungeons. Find him and see if he can be released.
Angevine In Exile.
Fabron is an envoy from Kellemderiel, currently in Avadon. He asked for your help. There is a mage named Angevine who is believed to be living somewhere near Goldcrag.
Angevine has made someone in Kellemderiel extremely angry and Fabron offers a generous reward if you find and kill her.
History Scrolls.
Eye Leira is the librarian of Avadon. She is constantly trying to acquire arcane scrolls for her collection. If you find any, she will pay well for them.
Clear the Stacks.

Eye Leira is the librarian of Avadon. During the recent troubles, the upper towers became infested with undead and nobody has come to clear them out. She will pay a bounty if you can go upstairs and rid her of the unholy entities.
The Krysanth.

Eye Leira is the librarian of Avadon. She has learned that a copy of a rare and valuable magical tome, The Krysanth, is in the tower of the wizard Moritz'Kri. She asked you to return to that dark place and look for the book.
Leira offered you an enchanted athame, a small, sharp dagger, which might be of use in breaking through any wards in the tower.
Wretch's Message.
There is a wretch named Svarl loitering just outside Redbeard's hall. He will give you a reward if you deliver a letter to Redbeard. Of course, your master might be annoyed if you waste his time.
The Rival Tribe.

Svarl, the wretch who loiters outside Redbeard's hall, has offered a reward for your help. There is a tribe of wretches called the Hegra clan, in the Jhereth Deeps. They have been bothering Svarl's clan.
You will be paid if you can wipe out the Hegra Clan. A gruesome bit of assassination, of course, but it's just wretches, so nobody will be concerned.
Sevilin's Directions.
Sevelin has left Avadon. He went alone to deal with some urgent business in The Kva. He has not returned.
If you want to hunt him down and get him to return, he left information for you in his quarters in Avadon.
Jenell's Message.
You received a message from Jenell when you returned to Avadon. She left for Khemeria on some urgent, dangerous business. She left word that, if you want to help, you can follow her.
If you want to find her and bring her back, she left word of where she left for in her quarters.
Nathalie's Expedition.

The mage Nathalie has left Avadon and returned to the Beraza Woods. She is going on some sort of hunting expedition. If you want to help her (or keep her from getting herself killed), she left information about her destination in her quarters.
Sevilin's Hunt.

Sevelin has left Avadon to return to The Kva. He is hunting down the brigands who attacked him and killed his fellows. If you want to help him with his quest, so that he will return, you have a map to the area of The Kva where he can be found.
Shima's Vengeance.
You found a hint in Shima's quarters of where he left for. The map directed you to a camp in Holklanda just west of the Beraza Woods.
If you want to bring Shima back to Avadon, going back to the Beraza Woods might be a good way to start.
Jenell's Ideals.

Some warriors of the Wyldrylm have fled into Khemeria. Jenell has gone back to Khemeria to try to find and help them. You found a note in her quarters. It said that she will leave word of her destination with Runner Faiga, a warrior in Dhorl Stead.
Nathalie's Ambition.
Nathalie has gone back to the Beraza Woods. She is going to try to hunt down the powerful drake that escaped you earlier. It is a terribly foolhardy thing to try to do alone.
She left a letter for you. If you want to find her, she said that she will leave a message for you in the cavern in the Beraza Pits where you met the drake before.
Shima's Directions.
Shima Threespear confronted you when you returned to Avadon. He is going to hunt those who dishonored his family.
If you want to help him (and to bring him back to Avadon), he said that he left a map to his destination in his quarters. His quarters are downstairs from the main kitchen.
Secure the Dungeons.

You found Eye Mamora in the Avadon dungeons. He told you to enter the dungeons and secure them. Hunt for four prisoners: Ghroz, Hansi, Quiria, and Shadow Tarkus. If any of them refuse to come peacefully, you should kill them.
Find Ghroz.
Ghroz is an escaped wretch in the Avadon dungeons. Find him and, if he refuses to submit, kill him.
Find Hansi.
Hansi is an escaped Khemerian barbarian in the Avadon dungeons. Find him and, if he refuses to submit, kill him.
Find Quiria.
Quiria is an escaped mage in the Avadon dungeons. Find her and, if she refuses to submit, kill her.
Find Shadow Tarkus.
Shadow Tarkus is an escaped spy and assassin in the Avadon dungeons. He is an extremely cunning and dangerous agent. Explore the upper dungeons and find out if he is hiding there.
The Red Wolves.
Monitor Sibel is the superior to the soldiers of Goldcrag. The remote town has been hounded by increasing numbers of wild and dangerous wolves.
There are packs of wolves with red-tinged fur on the road between Goldcrag and Zhethron's lair. Kill eight of these fierce creatures, and Sibel will pay you a bounty.
The Dire Wolf Pack.
There is a pack of vicious, twisted dire wolves in the cactus thickets outside of Zhethron's Aerie. Hunt them down to earn a bounty.
Hunt Nightshade.

There is a vicious and enchanted wolf called Nightshade hunting the roads outside of Zhethron's Aerie. Sibel will pay a generous bounty if you hunt the creature down. It has been sighted south to the dragon's gates.
The Ogre's Theft.
You met a smith named Berak in Goldcrag. He recently lost a caravan of valuable goods. They were stolen south of the gate to Zhethron's Aerie.
Investigate the area around the lost caravan and see if you can find the lost goods. Berak will pay if you can find them.
Blue Ore.

You met a smith named Berak in Goldcrag. He will pay well if you can bring enough samples of a certain sort of blue ore. It can be found in the wilds to the south, especially around the Jhereth Deeps.
Titan's War Club.

You met a smith named Berak in Goldcrag. When he learned that there were titans in the hills to the south, he decided to obtain one of their iron ceremonial clubs. These items are said to have remarkable craftsmanship.
If you can find one of them, bring it to him for a reward.
The Rat Cave.
Elder Okan is an informal watcher of the farmers in Goldcrag. The soldiers have not been helping them, so they have saved money to hire warriors to rid them of pests.
A series of caves to the southeast has been infested with enormous rats. Go there and wipe out the nest to earn a bounty.
Okan's Spiders.
His cellars are full of huge, vicious spiders, in desperate need of crushing. The entrance to the cellar is behind his home to the west.
Goldcrag Reptiles.
The cactus thickets to the south have grown infested with vicious lizards. Enter the thickets to hunt them down and destroy them.
The Sixth Ritual.
Seeker Azarni is a mage from Holklanda. You met her in the inn of Goldcrag. She came to the dragon Zhethron to try to find a special tome. The dragon turned her away.
Enter Zhethron's library and see if it contains the secret Azarni desires: the Sixth Ritual of Inner Vision. Whatever that is.
A Dragon's Tooth.
A man named Alfans came from the Wyldrylm to Goldcrag to try to obtain a fresh dragon's tooth, to make a cure for a plague devastating his village. The dragon refused.
Fresh dragon's teeth are rare and difficult to get, and dragons tend to use them to chew things. However, if you can find one, Alfans will greatly appreciate it.
Halrik's Farm.

You met a farmer named Halrik in his farm west of Goldcrag. His farm has been raided by a band of wretches living to the west. Halrik will pay a bounty if you can keep those creatures from attacking him again.
Neray the Smuggler.
Tartam is an agent of Avadon, pretending to be a tanner in the lands outside Zhethron's Aerie. He is trying to find a smuggler named Neray, who is selling fine weapons to the wretches nearby.
This is a serious crime. Find Neray, see if she is guilty, and, if so, bring her to justice.
Ahmed's Libram.
You met a powerful mage named Angevine, who lives in a tower west of Goldcrag. She asked you to steal a book from the dragon Zhethron, a potentially dangerous task.
The book is a journal of magical research called Ahmed's Libram. It is in the dragon's library.
The Wayfarer.

A mysterious man, dressed like a shadowwalker, approached you just outside Zhethron's Aerie. He called himself the Wayfarer. He offered a reward if you can enter the dragon's lair and find out what someone named Ryozo was trying to hire the dragon to do.
If you are willing to do this and learn this information, leave it under a barrel behind the stone spire where you met the Wayfarer.
The Wretch Invasion.

You met Watcher Harissa just inside the entrance to Zhethron's Aerie. The outer chambers have been overrun by wretches, and the dragon hasn't been helping them. Kill the creatures and report back to Harissa.
Lost Soldiers.
Watcher Harissa is the woefully overtaxed commander of the soldiers in Zhethron's Aerie. She is using some of her resources to hire Hands to help her troops.
A patrol of four soldiers has gone missing near the large wretch lair to the south. Harissa wants you to find out what happened to them and, if necessary, rescue them.
The Missing Scouts.
She sent a group of scouts to investigate the ogres in the Jhereth Deeps. Once again, they have not returned. Find them and help them to return to safety.
Hunt Splinterbone.
There is a lone, wild, old titan named Splinterbone living near the invading titans to the south. Should you encounter that creature, kill him for a generous bounty.
Bounty: Fire Lizards.
Keeper Ilhan is one of the workers in Zhethron's Aerie, tasked to keep the outer chambers clean, safe, and a source of fresh fodder for the dragon.
There are several fire lizards loose in the northeast tunnels, and they are starting to stalk and injure Ilhan's workers. The keeper will pay you if you can hunt them all down.
Evict Fyrassa.
There is an obnoxious drake named Fyrassa in the tunnels under the dragon's lair. It has long outstayed its welcome, and Ilhan asked you, with great pleasure, to find and evict it.
The Assassin Spiridon.

There is an envoy from the Wyldrylm in Zhethron's Aerie. Her name is Teria. She told you of an assassin named Spiridon who is held in Avadon. He killed several members of her tribe, and she will pay you if you can help with their revenge.
Thara's Papers.
Keeper Thara is the dragon's personal assistant and advisor. When the wretches attacked, they stole three folders containing records of recent envoy visits to the dragon.
That information is supposed to be secret. If, while raiding the wretches, you find those papers, Thara will pay to get them back.
Zephyrine's Intentions.
Keeper Thara is the dragon's personal assistant and advisor. She has learned of Zephyrine, the new dragon in the area.
She has offered a reward if you can go to Zephyrine and ask simply ask what her intentions are. Seems simple enough.
The Wretch Lair.

The dragon Zhethron told you what has been irritating him: wretches. There is a large warren of them to the south, sending pests to sneak into his lair and steal his stuff. To pacify the dragon, you must go there and drive them out.
The Jhereth Deeps.

Zhethron's lair is still being raided, this time by ogres. Fortunately, the dragon was able to find out that their tribe is hiding in the Jhereth Deeps. He gave you directions. Go there and drive them out.
War With the Titans.

Now a horde of titans have moved into the lands south of The Kva. Their presence this close to Pact lands can't be tolerated. Zhethron discovered where their camp is, becoming seriously wounded in the process.
A Blade of Kva soldiers has been sent to the titan lair ahead of you. They will be under your command and can assist you in an assault on the fortress.
Ryozo's Papers.
The Wayfarer contacted you in the Jhereth Deeps. He told you that Commander Ryozo, back in Zhethron's Aerie, is a traitor. You can find papers proving this somewhere back there.
If you can find the papers and turn them in to an official there, a reward will be waiting for you in a crate back in the Deeps.
Destroy the Papers.

The Wayfarer contacted you not far from the lair of the titans. There might be papers hidden in there, indicating who has been directing and supporting the titans. If you can destroy them, the Wayfarer will pay you well the next time you meet.
The Ghostly Crown.
You encountered a strange shade near the lair of the titans, under where the Pact soldiers were camped. It couldn't speak, but it seemed to want a crown or other piece of headgear.
The Widow of Bones.

Runner Kellen is a hunter in the village of Dhorl Stead. He offered a bounty if you could find and slay a huge, twisted, arachnid creature. He called it the Widow of Bones and told you that it could be found in the Dhorla Woods, near Moritz'Kri's tower.
Stara Stead Raiders.

Runner Kellen is a hunter in the village of Dhorl Stead. He offered a bounty if you could drive out some raiders that came from nearby Stara Stead. They have been chased to the deep woods where you hunted the Shadow Beast.
Bounty: Snapfang.

In Dhorl Stead, you met a clanless Khemerian warrior named Runner Faiga. She offers trophies to brave warriors who can hunt down deadly foes. For example, a huge bat with a broken fang in the tunnels under Dhorl Stead.
Find and kill the creature and you will receive a bounty.
Aid Shavon.

In Dhorl Stead, you met a clanless Khemerian warrior named Runner Faiga. She offers trophies to brave warriors who can hunt down deadly foes. One such hunter, a man named Shavon, went to the Dhorla Woods. He hasn't been heard from for a while.
Go north, find Shavon, and help him to complete his mission.
Moritz'Kri's Prisoners.

In Dhorl Stead, you met a clanless Khemerian warrior named Runner Faiga. She offers trophies to brave warriors who can complete difficult tasks. For example, Faiga has heard rumors that Moritz'Kri has Khemerians held prisoner in his tower.
See if this is true. If so, free the prisoners.
Corrupted Circle.

Unni is an aging shaman in the village of Dhorl Stead. She wants to reclaim some of the old holy places that have been neglected in recent years. There is a stone circle in the Dhorla Woods that has been infested by dark forces.
Enter the circle and dare them to challenge you. Then drive them out.
Unni's Totem.

Unni is an aging shaman in the village of Dhorl Stead. She wants to reclaim some of the old holy places that have been neglected in recent years. She needs a certain wooden totem to reclaim the circle in the Dhorla Woods.
Unfortunately, Moritz'Kri claimed that totem and took it into his tower. Unni asked you to reclaim it.
Moritz'Kri's Recipes.

Arilda is a shaman and alchemist in the Dhorla Woods. She has no love for the wizard Moritz'Kri. That mage claims to have a book of powerful potion recipes, and Arilda wants it. She says that she will reward you if you bring it to her.
Ogre Skulltaker.

While hunting the Shadow Beast in the deep woods, you met a hunter named Runner Kasch. He warned you that there is a huge ogre roaming the forest. It can be identified by the Khemerian skull it wears around its neck.
It is a huge and dangerous creature, and Kasch will pay a bounty if you can find and slay it.
The Stolen Totem.
You met Lady Antje in Oghrym'Tor. Now that you are going to Moritz'Kri's Tower, she asked you to look for something for her. A small wooden totem, of the sort often used to adorn stone circles.
If you can bring it to her, you will be rewarded.
The Draining Bats.
Hunter Klement, a warrior in Oghrym'Tor, learned of your journey to Moritz'Kri's Tower. He told you how he has been hunting a colony of warped bats. Their nest is within the wizard's tower.
If you can find and slay them, he will pay you a bounty.
Shaman Theresia
Jenell insists on searching the Jarlswood and finding Shaman Theresia. The rogue shaman is stirring up trouble in Khemeria and went so far as to try to kill a Hand. She must be stopped.
Your companion also wants to kill as few Wyldrylm warriors as possible, though you can defend yourself if necessary.
Monitor Shigaz's Hunt.
Duke Gryfyn of Castle Vebeaux called you to his castle to aid him in his quest to bring peace to the Pact. You are to speak with Monitor Shigaz and go with him deep into the Beraza Woods.
There, you will aid him to clear out a nest of monsters, proving that it is possible to work together to rid the forest of its pests. Shigaz can tell you more.
Beraza Bandit Pits.
Duke Gryfyn of Castle Vebeaux called you to his castle to aid him in his quest to bring peace to the Pact. You are to go and speak with Monitor Shigaz once again.
Then you will return to the Beraza Woods and work with him to hunt down and destroy a group of bandits that have been raiding Holklanda.
Aid Monitor Shigaz.

Duke Gryfyn of Castle Vebeaux called you to his castle to aid him in his quest to bring peace to the Pact. You are to help Monitor Shigaz to secure the castle, so that assassins cannot reach the Holklandan envoys.
Monitor Shigaz is currently in an excavation under the castle. The stairway down to where you can meet him is by the barracks, just south of the Great Hall.
Escape Castle Vebeaux.
Something has gone horribly wrong. Monitor Shigaz and his warriors have been murdered, and Duke Gryfyn is sending packs of wolves and basilisks to hunt you down.
A speedy escape from the castle might be wise.
Vengeance Upon Gryfyn.
You have escaped from Castle Vebeaux, but now you are a wanted criminal. You have fled deep into the Beraza Woods, and you have no doubt that Duke Gryfyn has sent hunters to track you.
Unless you can find a way to enter Castle Vebeaux and use the pylon to return to Avadon, you will be trapped out here, alone and hunted.
Hand Gavin.
You learned in Castle Vebeaux of Hand Gavin. He is a servant of Avadon who was accused of treason and fled into the Beraza Woods.
Catching an escaped traitor seems like a sure path to status and commendation.
Bounty: Basilisks.
Tender Melisande is a skilled and ambitious animal trainer in Castle Vebeaux. She told you how several escaped basilisks are menacing the road west of the castle.
If you can kill five of the creatures, she will give you a bounty.
Basilisk Eggs.
Tender Melisande is a skilled and ambitious animal trainer in Castle Vebeaux. She is always looking for young creatures that she can mold to her will, wisely or not.
She told you that, when you are hunting the Beraza Woods, if you can find some basilisk eggs, she will pay very well for them.
A Drake Egg.
She told you that, when you are hunting the Beraza Woods, if you can find a drake egg, she will pay very well for it.
Vebeaux Tunnel.
You met Commander Peveral in Castle Vebeaux. He sometimes hires Hands with free time to perform missions for him.
He believes that smugglers in the small settlement west of Castle Vebeaux are trying to dig a tunnel. Investigate and see if you can find it and deal with the miscreants.
Hidden Ogres.
He has had reports that ogres are trying to settle in the Beraza Woods. Their colony is hidden, but they might have left bones and trash near its entrance.
Forbidden Magic Samples.
Incantatrix Questa is the head sorceress for Castle Vebeaux. She learned that you were hunting magically warped creatures in the woods, and she was very interested.
If you can bring her a sample of whatever was used to affect the creatures, she will reward you. However, the legality of passing on forbidden magic to her is questionable.
Incantor Manon.
Incantatrix Questa is the head sorceress for Castle Vebeaux. She told you about a mage named Incantor Manon. He was accused of a crime and fled into the Beraza Woods.
Should you find him, she would like for you to tell him that it is safe for him to return to the castle.
Follow Orian.
Eye Acacia is Avadon's observer in Castle Vebeaux. She is always watching for spies in the Beraza Woods, but she has lost the youthful vigor necessary to hunt them down herself.
There is a suspicious woodsman named Orian in the woods. She asked you to follow him and see what he is doing out there. If you have trouble finding him, look for abandoned camps.
Hunt Down Orian.
Now that you have discovered that Orian is a spy, Eye Acacia wants him dealt with. She will pay a bounty if you can return him to Avadon, or, failing that, kill him.
Vinvella's Hunt
You met a hunter named Vinvella on the outskirts of the Beraza Woods. She is tasked to hunt down some nasty spiders, but she can't kill them all by herself. She will pay you a bounty if you help her.
The Ruined Hall.

Huntsman Gable lives at the east edge of the Beraza Woods. He told you how there is a ruined house to the southwest. It is infested with rats and, he believes, something worse. He asked you to go there and clean the place out.
Aiding Calantha.
You met the Wayfarer on the Beraza Woods road. Unsurprisingly, you have been offered another bribe to use the powers of Avadon.
He asked you to find the gatemaster of Castle Vebeaux. You are to convince him to give a merchant named Calantha permission to pass through the castle.
Drake Skins.
Belda is a leatherworker deep in the Beraza Woods. In return for a cash payment and two drake skins, she can make leather armor of considerable quality.
Hunting Down Cahil.
Sevilin tracked down Cahil to a remote region called the White Plains. If you want to win his loyalty, you will have to help him get revenge on this cruel brigand.
Zhossa Mindtaker.

Nathalie is determined to hunt down the drake Zhossa Mindtaker. If you don't help her in this, she is unlikely to forgive you. She has hunted the drake down to a crumbling tower in the mountains north of the Beraza Woods.
Calantha's Competition.
The Wayfarer brought you an offer of work. Calantha, a merchant outside the west gate of Castle Vebeaux, wants to be rid of Charon, a competitor.
If you want to help Calantha (for a generous payment), you can tell the authorities in the Castle that Charon is guilty of, oh, something or other.
Hunting the Huntress.

Hand Gavin told you that his warriors have long been hunted by beasts trained by a particular huntress from Castle Vebeaux. She has recently emerged from the Castle to help hunt for you. Gavin will only help you if you can rid him of her.
Her encampment is to the south, across the river. She is somewhere to the east of the bridge you crossed to reach Gavin's camp.
Back To Vebeaux.
Hand Gavin will help you to slip back in to Castle Vebeaux. First, however, you must clear a path back to that fortress.
From Gavin's home, fight your way to the east, avoiding the main road. At one point, you will find a hidden pathway, marked by a rusty shield on a rock outcropping.

A blademaster is a true warrior. He is most comfortable in a massive suit of plate armor, wielding a sword and shield or a huge halberd, striding boldly into a crowd of foes and sending them flying with mighty blows. Blademasters are not subtle.
Blademasters are natural leaders. Their war cries can strengthen their allies and weaken their foes. They can also challenge enemies, keeping them away from fragile members of your group.
The most important statistic for a blademaster is Strength, though you should invest in some Dexterity as well.

The shadowwalkers are warriors of the shadows. They count on cunning and evasion, slipping through the guards of their enemies and delivering lethal blows. They can attack with blades, thrown razor disks, and pots of noxious and deadly alchemical substances. And then vanish into thin air.
Shadowwalkers have many tricks to evade, stun, poison, and heavily damage foes. Also, shadowwalkers can pick locks and disarm traps.
The most important statistic for a shadowwalker is Dexterity, though you should invest in some Strength as well.

The shaman has dedicated her life to nature, and nature, in return, has rewarded her with great power. She can use her connection to the wilds to heal and bless her allies. And, when angered, she can call wind, lightning, and fire to devastate those who challenge her.
A shaman is rarely alone. She can call wolves or, eventually, drakes to serve and protect her. Also, she has the unique ability to heal wounded allies.
Shamans, when training, should try to invest in Intelligence and Dexterity.

The sorceress has dedicated her life to the mastery of the arcane arts. Fragile in battle, she makes up for it with the ability to summon forth clouds of fire, lightning, or ice, obliterating her foes.

But that is not all. A sorceress can cloud the minds of foes, even potentially causing them to fight for her. She can bless allies and curse enemies. She can even use spells to pick locks and disarm traps.
The most important statistic for a Sorceress is Intelligence, though you should invest in some Dexterity as well.

This is a faintly glowing pearl on a gold chain. When wearing it, almost all gates in Avadon will open for you.
This is a tiny knife, razor-sharp and inscribed with runes. It has been enchanted with the ability to cut through magical wards.
This is a book of magical rituals and spells, written in an obscure runic language and bound in black leather. Holding the book makes your hair stand on end and your skin numb.
This gruesome trophy is a sample of flesh from the beast that was stalking townsfolk in Khemeria. The mages of Avadon wanted to examine it.
You obtained these records in the tower of Moritz'Kri. Hopefully, Avadon can use them to figure out who, if anyone, was supplying and commanding that rogue wizard.
You found these ratty scrolls in the lair of the titans. Maybe they can help Avadon to determine who has been causing these creatures to invade The Kva.
This is a parchment envelope, wrinkled and stained with bits of food. A wretch named Svarl gave it to you to deliver to Redbeard.
These fragments of rock look like iron ore, but with an odd, bluish tinge. You are collecting them in a burlap sack to take back to Goldcrag.

This is a titan's ceremonial club. The handle is polished oak and the head is wrought iron. The iron has a strange texture. The craftsmanship is very unusual. The thing is five feet long and very heavy. You wear it strapped to your back.
This is a fresh tooth of the dragon Zephyrine. A valuable and rare magical ingredient, in the right hands.
This is the magical journal of a wizard named Ahmed. You try to understand the cramped writing within, but you don't understand it. It's not a sort of magic you have ever studied.
This is a message for the Wayfarer, describing why Ryozo was trying to hire the dragon Zhethron. You are supposed to place it under a barrel outside the entrance to the dragon's lair.

You found these papers inside Commander Ryozo's quarters. They are letters to the Tawon Empire, offering to try to turn the dragon against the Pact. If genuine, they are evidence of, at the very least, light treason.
This is a set of records in a thick leather binding. The pages detail the boons requested from the dragon Zhethron over the last several months. The wretches have left the thing very grimy.
This is a very old and tarnished metal circlet. You found it in the lair of the titans.
This is an old, polished wooden totem, covered with intricate carvings and set with semi-precious stones. When you touch it with your bare hands, you feel cold and full of fear.

This is a book of potions recipes, taken from the tower of the wizard Moritz'Kri. You flipped through it, but you don't know enough about alchemy to make use of it. If you tried to use it, you'd probably end up poisoned and exploded at the same time.
This is a clutch of four basilisk eggs. Small, tough, leathery things, that carry a singularly dangerous payload.
This is the egg of a drake, an extremely rare and valuable item among particularly ambitious or amoral wizards and animal trainers.
This is a clay flask full of green goo. The stuff is mobile, highly enchanted, and ready to be either studied or used in reckless magical experiments.
Unni, a shaman in Dhorl Stead, blessed you. Her ward provides a small amount of protection from magical attacks (fire, cold, energy). (1% higher resistance)
Unni, a shaman in Dhorl Stead, blessed you. Her ward provides protection from magical attacks (fire, cold, energy). (2% higher resistance)
You received special training from a hunter in the deep woods near Dhorl Stead. Your missile attacks will do more damage (2 levels higher).
You received special training from a hunter in the deep woods near Dhorl Stead. Your melee attacks will do more damage (2 levels higher).
You received special training while in Holklanda. Melee attacks will now do slightly less damage to you. (2% higher melee damage resistance)
You received special training from a Kellem in Holklanda. You have a better chance of resisting enemy mental attacks. (8% higher chance of resisting mental attacks)
This heavy iron key will get you into the inner cells and lower tunnels of the Avadon dungeons.
You found this key on the body of Quiria, an escaped prisoner. It will open several gates in the Avadon dungeons.
You found this copper key, green with tarnish, in the caves of wretches south of Zhethron's Aerie.
You found this iron key, slightly bent and tinged with rust, in the caves of wretches south of Zhethron's Aerie.
This is a heavy steel key. You obtained it in the mines in the Jhereth deeps. Three deep scratches have been placed halfway up its length, though it's not immediately apparent what they signify.
You found this polished steel key in the fortress of Oghrym'Tor.
This strange key is made of metal, but translucent. It seems to exist halfway between this world and another. You found it in Moritz'Kri's tower.
This key was given to you by a shadowwalker named Harua. You met him in a bandit lair in the Beraza Woods.
You found this key on the body of the leader of a group of bandits in the Beraza Woods. It is made of crystal and is almost invisible. It must bear some sort of enchantment.

You start to cross Avadon's entry garden. Considering how terrified most of Lynaeus is of this fortress, it seems rather pleasant. Ponds. Nicely tended lawn.
To the east is another pair of gates, leading farther into the fortress. A pair of guards, wearing plate armor and wielding massive swords, stand to either side.
There is also an elderly man in long flowing robes. He has a pair of what looks like wolves in front of him. He is shouting commands at them. They don't seem concerned.
(Keep crossing the courtyard to the east.)
You step into the entry courtyard of Avadon. Fresh supplies are stacked everywhere, waiting to be distributed to the warriors and craftspeople. When Avadon wants something, it gets it.

However, the atmosphere of the fort is not what you expected. It is chaos. Guards and workers are running everywhere. You hear shouting in the distance. The smell of smoke (and, you think, blood) hangs in the air.
After a lifetime of hearing how deadly and invulnerable Avadon is, this chaos is somehow even more worrying.

A woman stands in the middle of the courtyard, an island in the chaos, and directs the workers. This must be the Miranda you are supposed to present your letter of introduction to. (Click her to talk to her.)
You enter Avadon's main storeroom, where most of the food, wood, and so on brought to the Black Fortress are kept.
There has recently been a fight here. The stone floor is scorched, and splatters of blood dot the walls. The wounded (and dead) have been hauled away.
Only one person is visible from here. A young sorceress stands by the scorched area, looking down at it. She is smiling.

There are several locked storerooms back here. They probably contain valuable equipment, reserved for someone important. Though, considering the chaos, you doubt anyone would mind if you borrowed something.
However, to get the locks open, you will need to find some lockpicks.
Fortunately, you have a lockpick. That might be enough to get one of the locks open.
(You use lockpicks to pick locks. Alas, the picks break when used. Shadowwalkers and Sorceresses have skills that reduce the number of picks you need to open a lock.)

You are at the entrance to the Avadon dungeons, final resting place of many foolish enough to fight the Pact. You notice that a heavy cloak has been left on a table nearby. It might be wise to put it on before descending into the low tunnels.
These quarters have been set aside for you. By the standards of Avadon, they are fairly plain. Compared to what you are used to, however, they are amazingly opulent.

This round hall is in the center of this floor of Avadon. A spiral staircase dominates the room, rising thirty feet straight up and through a hole in the ceiling. Huge, emotionless, unblinking guards watch the chamber, ready to instantly impale anyone who seems the slightest bit untrustworthy.
You concentrate on looking trustworthy.
These stairs lead up to the chambers of Redbeard, Keeper of Avadon, the merciless guardian of the Pact. Whom you now need to face. You shudder.
This is the main dining hall of Avadon. It is a whirlwind of activity every hour of the day, as Hands, envoys, supplicants, and diplomats grab hasty meals before returning to their business.
Most of the people here ignore you. One man stares at you openly. He is a shadowwalker, sitting by himself at a long table. He sips some wine and nods at you.

This is a second garden, larger and more beautiful than the first. Planters ring the hall, full of rare and fragile plants from all over Lynaeus. Visitors to Avadon frequently come here to breathe fresh air and try to relax. It is not easy to stay calm under the constant gaze of Keeper Redbeard.
There is a young woman walking among the trees. She is barefoot and wears a loose leather tunic and dress. You suspect that she is from the Wyldrylm. When she sees you, she nods solemnly.
Avadon has many guards, all of them outfitted in fine armor and the highest-quality weapons. They are warriors in the service of the Black Fortress, but they are not sent out into the field.
They all regard you with a mix of contempt for your inexperience and envy at your potential. And, of course, should you turn out to be an assassin sent to kill Redbeard, they are ready to kill you.
Now that you have gained some experience, the guards are starting to look at you with a little bit of respect. They stand quietly at attention when you pass.
They stand quietly at attention as you pass. Your success out in the field has earned you a lot of respect, tinged with envy because you get to actually leave Avadon.
The old man watches you and his wolves quietly. He seems disinclined to get involved in your disagreement.

Craftmaster Nicodemus is distracted by the dead wolves. He examines them closely, trying to figure out what he can do to not create something so hideous and useless next time. He mutters, _I'm busy. Go see Heart Miranda._
The disgusting wolf-creature snarls at you when you get close.

Of course, Avadon requires a host of servants, cooks, craftspeople, and so on to keep it functioning. They are well-paid, well-fed, and at constant risk of falling victim to escaped prisoners, deranged assassins, or malfunctioning magical experiments.
All of them recognize your rank and relatively high importance. They give you satisfyingly humble nods before they continue about their work.
Even among their ranks, rumors of your many remarkable achievements have started to spread. They give you brief, satisfying looks of awe before they continue about their work.
This wheel controls the gate to the dungeons. You start to turn it, but then you realize that you might want to actually report to someone in Avadon first and find out what you should be doing.
This wheel controls the gate to the dungeons. You start to turn it, but then you realize that you should speak with Sevilin and Nathalie first. They can, after all, help you in the dungeons.
This wheel controls the gate to the dungeons. You start to turn it, but then you realize that you should probably equip some protective gear first. Like the cloak you saw.
This wheel controls the gate to the dungeons. With great effort, you turn it. The gate opens, clearing your path to the dangerous depths below.
The gate is open. You don't need to do anything else with this wheel. For now.

This is one of the catalogs for the Avadon library. They have thousands of rare tomes here, some centuries old. Taking them out of the library for any reason subjects all but the most influential to gruesome penalties.
Craftmaster Nicodemus has several young assistants. They do simple crafts, help him to test his inventions, and try to avoid being accidentally incinerated.
You notice that his helpers spend most of their time in this half of the workshop. When the Craftmaster needs to test something, he tends to grab the first person he sees. As you know all too well.
You meet one of the Eyes of Avadon, skilled sages who gather and organize massive amounts of information. Then, when Hands go into danger, they can do so equipped with as much knowledge as possible.
For all their value, they are a quiet and standoffish crew. You try to speak with them, but, apart from a warning about removing tomes or scrolls from the library, you learn little.

This cabinet contains some of the possessions of Envoy Brasula, one of the many diplomats who constantly haunt the halls of Avadon. You poke through them quickly, looking for anything of interest. You find nothing.
Then, since Hand Callan asked you to look through her goods, you do a much more thorough search. There are dresses. Bottles of perfume. A few scrolls of poetry. Nothing odd or incriminating.
If Brasula is a spy, you lack the skills to find her out.

This cabinet contains some of the possessions of Envoy Valna, one of the many diplomats that come to Avadon from the Pact and the Farlands. There are clothes, daggers, bits of armor, and some sheets of paper. The papers contain diagrams and scribbles in a foreign tongue. Nothing you can understand.
Then, remembering that you saw Valna acting oddly in the Hall of Statues, you look more closely. There is nothing odd in the box, but, beneath it, you find a crumpled note. It reads:
_I feel we are always being watched. If I am to tell you of Avadon, we must find a better place to meet, and I must be paid more. - Admes._

You get closer to the old man and his two wolves. Though, from this distance, you can see that something is not right about these animals. Like their lack of hair, and their purple flesh, and the veins throbbing all along their backs and legs.
The man in robes is holding up a scrap of meat and giving suggestions like, _Stand! Sit! Roll over!_ The wolf-creatures don't respond.
Then you get close, which gets an instant reaction out of them. They turn and look at you. Then they bare their teeth and begin to snarl.
(Select one of the reactions below.)
(Watch them quietly.)
The twisted wolf-things are no longer distracted by the pitiful scraps of meat the old man dangles before them. You seem much softer and fresher.
However, the old man and the guards don't seem to react to this. They just watch, silently and with interest.
(Back away.)
The twisted wolf-things immediately scent your fear. They turn away from the pitiful scraps of meat the old man dangles before them. You seem much softer and fresher.
Ummm ... Could you control those ... things?

_No. As you can see, I can't. I thought I might, but ..._ The old man sighs. The twisted wolf-things turn away from the pitiful scraps of meat the old man offered them. You seem much softer and fresher.
What are you doing? Help me!
One of the guards smirks. The old man looks surprised. _But you are a Hand. You are supposed to aid in my work. This is your job! I will explain more when you are done._
The creatures lurch clumsily toward you, one to your right, one to the left. Then they start to run, teeth bared.
Is this meant to be some sort of test?

The guards smile, perhaps thinking back to trials of their own, but the old man shakes his head. _A test? No. You are a Hand. You are supposed to aid in my work. This is your job! I will explain more when you are done._
Call back your pets, old man, before I have to destroy them.
The old man shakes his head sadly. _That is all right. I think it is necessary. You are a Hand. You are supposed to aid in my work. This is your job! I will explain more when you are done._
(Prepare to defend yourself.)
You have little equipment, but you were not foolish enough to travel through the wilderness without a weapon. You prepare to rid the garden of the old man's pets.
(When the wolves attack, you will enter combat mode. You will then learn how to defend yourself.)
The hideous wolf-creatures lie at your feet, dead. The guards, realizing that they have a mess to clean up, look annoyed. The old man just looks sad.

_Another month of work, gone. I suppose I must work on my other trinkets for a while. I ... Oh. I am sorry. I am Craftmaster Nicodemus, one of the mages of Avadon. I think I will be helping you in the future._
You will be helping me?

_Oh, yes. You are one of Redbeard's new Hands, yes? When you are given tasks, I will be giving you the benefit of my magic. Some of it even works better than these constructions._ He waves at the wolves.
You called me a Hand?
_Oh, yes. Redbeard has Hands, Eyes, and Hearts. I am an Eye, and ... Oh, I am sure this will be explained inside._
How dare you send your creatures to attack me?
_What? You are annoyed? But Hands help me to deal with failed experiments all the time. It is the price they pay for the aid I give them. But you are young and new. You will understand in time._
_I suppose you should see Heart Miranda. I think she is waiting for you, and she will explain what you need to know._
I was glad to help. Who do I report to?
Nicodemus nods. _That is the spirit. But you do not report to me. I was only trying to train the creatures here to get away from the chaos inside._
Where is Heart Miranda?

Craftmaster Nicodemus makes a signal. The gates begin to slowly open. _Miranda is inside, directing things. There has been a serious ... disturbance. And she will be happy for your help. Now, please excuse me._
Then he turns to his wolves, going down on one knee to examine them.
(Go east through the gate to find Heart Miranda. Her position is now marked on the map window.)

This is the legendary library of Avadon. Books on history, magic, and the many languages and cultures of Lynaeus surround you. The library is cared for by a number of Eyes, who watch you with mistrust when you get close to their precious tomes.
Dust and flakes of parchment are heavy in the air back here. You sneeze. This passage must lead to back storage for less useful tomes.
It is cold and still. Unnaturally so. You hear an unnerving clicking, scraping sound coming from the top of the stairs.

The moment you enter this dome, your hair stands on end. There is a portal in the magic circle to the south. It is a doorway made of raw magical energy, maintained in a delicate balance of power by the wizards of Avadon.
Through the doorway, you can see an arid landscape. There are thickets of cacti in the distance. It is miraculous. With one step, you can take a month's journey.
You enter one of Avadon's many towers. This short, squat spire was used as a zoo of sorts. Beasts were brought here from all over Lynaeus for study, held in place by a web of magical bonds.

And this is where the problems that have afflicted the fortress began. Something happened to the delicate magical spells, throwing them out of balance. The floors are scorched. The stone is cracked. The gooey remnants of the former exhibits have sprayed everywhere.

Looking around, you have no idea what might have caused this disaster. It did, however, have one survivor. A hellhound is still held within the magic circle to the west. It has been driven mad by neglect and hunger. (Not that these creatures are ever calm to begin with.)

This is the second floor of the holding tower. The magical disaster was not confined to the floor below. This chamber is similarly ravaged. A body still lies on the floor by a cracked pillar. You are the first person to come up here since the wards exploded.
But you are not alone. You can hear deep, wet breathing in the shadows. Something is up here with you.
These are the deep stacks of the Avadon library, where thousands of musty tomes on every conceivable topic are stored in a seemingly endless array of bookshelves.

The librarians have not come up here recently, and you soon realize why. It is very dark and deathly cold. And you can hear something in the shadows. Something softly scraping along the stone corridors.
You find yourself checking to make sure that your weapon is handy.
When you enter Sevilin's quarters, you see that he has left a note pinned to one of the spears on his weapon rack. You take it down and read it. It says:
_[N] - I apologize for shirking my duty and leaving you. And yet, we of Avadon have another duty, equally as great. We must avenge the loss of our brothers._

_I have gone to The Kva to continue my hunt for the brigands. I have learned that they might be in a remote region called the White Plains. Since none have offered to help find them, I go alone. And yet, I would not turn down company._
_Should I not return, I wish you well. Beware the treachery that surrounds you. - Sevilin._
You enter Shima's room, looking for any sign of where he might have gone. You search the room thoroughly, but you only find one sign.

There is a map on his bed. It depicts the Beraza Woods and the neighboring parts of Holklanda. On it, an area west of the woods, in Holklandan territory, has been circled. He has also written, _Watch the roads. Roaming ogres._
This is the only sign you can find of where he went. It will have to do. (A new location has been revealed on the Beraza Woods map.)
When you enter Jenell's chambers, your eyes are instantly drawn to the folded sheet of papyrus. You open it and, with some effort, read her sloppy handwriting.

_To [N]. I do not expect you to share my obsession with preserving the ways of my people. But I do hope you understand that I care for the beliefs of all the people of the Pact. I think they must be respected._
_I return to Khemeria to find those of the Wyldrylm that are lost there. It is dangerous for one of my people to go there alone. I will rely on the aura of Avadon to protect me._
_Should you follow and should I learn anything, I will leave word with Runner Faiga of Dhorl Stead before I depart. She is worthy, for a Khemerian. - Jenell_

You enter Nathalie's chambers, trying to find some sign of where she went. Surprisingly, she left no sign. No letter, no map. With a small amount of guilt, you search through her private papers for some clue. In her notes, you find one thing of interest:

_I will show them what I can do, and I will take whatever steps I can. This cunning drake, with the power to warp minds, must be hunted. I trust [N] to not try to steal my glory, but others may take the credit away from me nonetheless._

_I am resolved. I will go to the Beraza Pits, and I will find this drake. If I am lost, this letter may be found. I may leave some signs of my passage, so that a rescue mission might find me if needed. Look for messages first where we fought the drake._
_Or, if necessary, so what is left of my remains can be collected._

You get close enough to the infernal to take a nice, long look. It is very rare to get so close to these huge, unpredictable creatures. Fortunately, the collar it wears shocks it painfully whenever it tries to lunge at you.
Eventually, you leave them to return to work. If the magic of their collars ever fails, this chamber will become very dangerous.

Avadon has an enormous workshop, where weapons, armor, and magical trinkets are produced and maintained by a skilled cadre of crafters. The smoke is thick, and the raw power in the air makes your hair stand on end.
To the south, you can see Craftmaster Nicodemus. Happily, there are no wolves with him this time. He holds a delicate ring on an anvil with a pair of tongs and taps it carefully with a large hammer.

You enter Craftmaster Nicodemus's private forge, where much of his most creative (if not necessarily useful) work takes place. Avadon is built over a natural steam vent, and much of that heat is directed into this chamber.

Two of Nicodemus's assistants are moving things around to the north. Not humans, but humanoid. Tall, scaly, with horns and fangs. Somehow, Nicodemus has bound two infernals to his service. Fortunately, collars around their necks hold them in bondage.
