You start to enter the portal to The Kva. Peering through the magical doorway, the stark deserts of southern Lynaeus beckon to you.
Then you realize that using these portals without permission or instruction would not be wise, and could be dangerous. You decide to not pass through just yet.
Then you realize that you have not yet spoken to both Shima and Jenell, the other Hands available to you. Perhaps it would be a good idea to meet all of the resources available to you.
(Their locations are marked with stars on the area map. Hold the Tab key to see the entire map.)
You return to the main floor of Avadon, eager to report to Heart Miranda of the successful completion of your first mission.
Your potential companions have returned to their quarters, waiting to be called back to duty.

(When in Avadon, you can visit your companions and speak with them. You can also access their inventories and change what items they have equipped. When you leave Avadon once again, you can choose who will come with you.)
The obelisk says:
IN MEMORY OF HEROM OF THE KVA |  FIRST KEEPER OF AVADON |  [N], he died for you.
You read it again. There it is ... Your name appears to be carved into the stone. What a unique bit of magic.

You start to enter the portal to Khemeria. Then you remember that you have not yet spoken with Laurella, the girl whose information led to you taking this journey in the first place. Apparently, she can always be found lurking just outside of Redbeard's hall.

You walk up to the woman in the middle of the room. Like Craftmaster Nicodemus, she is wearing long, flowing robes. The traditional garb of the mage. She is in her early fifties. She has served here for a long time.

She stops shouting orders and turns to you. _Well. Pity you didn't show up just a few hours ago. We could have used you. Do you have a letter of introduction?_ Fortunately, you were given one before you came here. She holds out her hand for it.
Heart Miranda is still directing the workers and guards. She barks out a constant string of orders, which are all instantly obeyed. It is fair to say that everyone is terrified of her.
Who are you?
She blinks twice. Then she extends her hand. _I told you to give me your papers. Ignoring the orders of a Heart is unwise._
What is going on here?
_Avadon only gives information to one of our own. Until I have read your letter of introduction, you are nothing to us._
(Give the letter.)
She takes the letter, reads it, and nods. _Then I formally welcome you, [N], and I declare you a Hand of Avadon, with all privileges and responsibilities attached. Congratulations._
She wads up the letter and tosses it onto the floor. A servant instantly collects it and carries it off.
_Normally, there would be a period of settling in, testing, and so on, but we have had some problems. All of our Hands are out in the field, and there is something I need you to do. Now._
Can you tell me about yourself?
_I ... What? Security is broken, dozens are dead, and you want to know ... Who am I? I am a Heart of Avadon. You will do everything I say, or you will suffer. I think that is clear enough._
I am a Hand? What does that mean?

_So much to learn, so little time to teach it. Avadon has Hands, Eyes, and Hearts. And the Keeper. I am a Heart, an honored advisor to the Keeper. You are a Hand. Your job is to go out and do what needs doing._
_There will be time to learn more when things are under control._
What has happened here?
_You will soon learn that, in Avadon, you are told only what you need to know. This is for your protection and ours._
What do you need me to do?

She nods. _Yes. Enthusiasm. That is what I like to hear. We are trying to get things in the main fortress under control, but we have had to send most of our Hands away. That means we need you to enter the dungeons and restore order. Round up some stray prisoners._

_You do not need to go alone. There are two Hands who can help you. They are ... Sevilin and Nathalie, I believe._ She points to the south. _On the way down to the dungeons, you can choose one of them to help you._
_Once you have met the other Hands, go downstairs and speak with Eye Mamora. He will tell you what fires to put out._
(The stairs down to the dungeons are now marked on the automap.)
I have met Nathalie and Sevilin.
_Good. They are not the assistants I would have chosen for you, but our resources are limited. You may take one of them with you into the dungeon. The other can help to keep watch._
(When you go downstairs, you will be able to choose who will travel with you.)
The dungeons have been secured.
You tell Heart Miranda what happened in the dungeons. She is furious, though happily not at you. _The holding pens empty? Tarkus gone? Someone has had a successful day's work._
_Still, you have done well, and under difficult circumstances. I think you have earned a long rest. Settle in, find your feet, get supplied._

She gives you an amulet on a copper chain. A yellow stone dangles from the end. _This will give you passage into the areas of Avadon you are allowed to explore. Your quarters are southeast of here, near my office._
_One more brief task awaits you, and then you can go settle in._
Where can I learn more?
_I think there is a book on the topic near the quarters assigned to you. You can read it at your leisure. Later._
Who is the Keeper?
_Surely you have heard of Redbeard, mighty master of Avadon. Do well, and you will stand before him. Displease him, and ..._ She gives you an evil smile.
Who decides what I get to learn?
_The Keeper and the Hearts. Like me._
And what do I have to know?
_That we are having a very long day, and you need to help us to keep it from getting longer._
Who are Sevilin and Nathalie?
_Young Hands like you, eager to distinguish themselves. In one case, extremely, painfully eager. I can spare one of them for your clean-up task._
What do I need to do in the dungeons?
_That is up to Eye Mamora. Do what he says. You may use any equipment you may find, and, if you survive, it will reflect very well upon you._
That is vague. I don't want to die without knowing exactly why.
_Trust me. At the moment of your death, you will not care in the slightest about why it happened. Now you are here, and it is time for you to serve. Go._
I will go right away.
She nods. _Good. With luck, you will be more suitable to service than the other available Hands. Go._
What do I need to do?

_Redbeard always meets all of his new servants. Even on this difficult day, I do not think he would wish his orders ignored. Ascend into the central tower and speak with him._ She points to the east. _The stairs are in the central chamber._
_Would you like some advice?_
I think I can manage on my own.
_Oh? Really? I look forward to seeing the results. If you need me later, I will be in my office, near your quarters._ She returns to shouting orders.
I would appreciate it.
_Redbeard has been bringing about the deaths of foes of the Pact since long before you were born. Your life is meaningless to him. Only the Pact matters._
_I would remember that before engaging in any youthful impudence or mischief. That is all. If you need me later, I will be in my office, near your quarters._ She returns to shouting orders.

Heart Miranda is sitting at her desk, sorting through a worryingly high stack of incident reports. She looks up at you. _You haven't seen Redbeard, have you? You don't have the proper look of awe. Go upstairs and talk to him._
You track down Heart Miranda in her office. Even though the smell of blood and smoke is still in the air, she sits at her desk as if nothing unusual has happened.
She looks up at you and brushes her graying hair out of her eyes. _So you have been to see Redbeard? And how did it go?_
Miranda looks up at you from her desk. _What else do you need to know? There is much to do, and little time to do it._
I managed to survive.
She nods. _That is the proper attitude. Respect, care, and the lack of complacency. Redbeard is the most dangerous man in Lynaeus._
_Now, I know that I told you that you would be allowed some time to settle in. I'm afraid that will have to wait._
He didn't seem so impressive.
She nods and chuckles. _Of course. That is how he lures his opponents into moments of weakness and carelessness. And then they end up ..._ She points downward, toward the dungeons.
He said that I could have a rest.
She laughs. _Of course. Always wanting to curry favor with the new Hands. Redbeard can be charming, in his way. But I am afraid that this will have to wait._
What do you mean?

_The problems we have had mean that we are desperately short on Hands. There is a task that has been waiting to be completed for some time. We do not like to seem tardy or inattentive, so I am going to send you._
_Of course, you will be supplied first._
What has been happening here?
She sniffs the air. _Ah. That smoke will clear soon. I can see why it is still on your mind._
_We had an incident. Within the fortress. A rare event that will not be repeated. There has been, at the same time, some turmoil in parts of Lynaeus._
I'd like to know more about Redbeard.
_Ah, yes. So many rumors, so little knowledge. All new Eyes and Hands must be told what is true and what is not. Do you have any questions?_
_First, you need supplies. As a servant of Avadon, you have fantastic resources at your disposal. Before I send you into the field, you can tap into them._
_Go speak with Smith Duman and get your first scarab. Find Craftmaster Nicodemus and see what he has made for you. Then return to me._
(Their locations are marked on your map with stars. Hold down the Tab key to see a map of the entire area.)
What happened inside the fortress?
_We are still investigating. We suspect that a spell went out of control in the holding cells. The pulse of energy disrupted the other spells that held prisoners and imprisoned specimens in place._
_It is all under control._
Problems elsewhere?
_There have been a variety of incidents in the Farlands. Riots in the Tawon Empire. Raiders from Svorgald. More freaks coming out of the Corruption._
_These things happen. However, it has required us to send out most of our Hands. They will soon return._
This all happened at once?
_Yes. That is part of life in Avadon. Months of inactivity, followed by several messes landing in our laps at once. Don't be concerned._
Does he have three wives?
She laughs bitterly. _Yes, and I am one of them. Callan and Leira are the others. We are not actually married, of course. It is simply our nickname._
_We have served him for so long, so loyally, that this is the name we have been given. Not kindly, I think. No matter._
Can he read my mind?
_No. I don't think so. But he understands the weaknesses of humanity so well that he might as well be able to._
Are there many attempts on his life?

For a moment, you see a flicker of ... something in her eyes, but it passes instantly. _Yes. That is true. Whoever destroys Redbeard takes his place, with the unlimited wealth and power that accompany it._
_But they always fail. You saw in the dungeons what happens then._
I have received my supplies.

_Then you are ready for your first journey into the outside world as a representative of Avadon. Sooner than I might have wanted to send you, perhaps, but you will only be dealing with wretches, so it should be fine._
Where do I need to go?
Miranda pulls a wrinkled sheet of papyrus from deep in one of the stacks on her desk and inspects it. _Ah, yes. The dragon Zhethron. How interesting. Meeting a dragon on your first trip out._

_The dragon is troubled by wretches. We want to keep the creature happy. He hasn't received personal attention from Avadon in some time, so we are sending you. Go clear out his pests, then return to me._

_And, I am happy to say, two more Hands have returned from the field. They are available to help you. Be sure to speak with them before you depart. I can spare two of the four available to help you with this task. I doubt that you will need more._
I am helping a dragon?
_Dragons are some of the most valuable allies for the Pact. Of course, not all dragons are allied with us, but those creatures are wise enough to hide far away._
_Beasts such as Zhethron provide knowledge and military aid. In return, we must, at times, help ease their egos by sending Hands to do their bidding._
How can I reach the dragon?

She points toward the southern tower. _The portal there has been charged to take you to the town of Goldcrag, in The Kva. Once there, it will not be difficult to find your way to Zhethron's Aerie. Many travel there to buy various sorts of assistance from the greedy old reptile._
Tell me about the two other Hands.
She consults another paper on her desk. _One is Shima Threespear, a young shadowwalker of some skill. Quite promising, I think. He is often found in the dining hall._
_The other is Jenell. She is a shaman, recently arrived from the Wyldrylm and eager to prove herself. She spends much of her time in the garden in the northwest corner of the fortress._
Who should I take with me?
_That will be your decision. See which one you mesh best with and which one has skills to complement your own._
Why are these Hands still here instead of out in the field?
_Ahhhh ... They are young. Perhaps less tested than others, and thus less likely to be selected. But I assure you that you will be able to ... to work well with them._
I have aided Zhethron.
Miranda asks you a few questions about the wretches. Then she pulls a familiar scroll from her papers and makes a few decisive 'X' marks on it. _Then this can go into the records._
_Though I do wonder. Did anything unusual occur when you were in The Kva?_
I met a shadowwalker on the road. He wanted me to get information for him.
_Oh, really? Describe this person._ You do. _I am not sure who this person is, or whether he is a servant of Avadon. It is good that you told me everything you know._
_Remember, many people will try to turn your service of Redbeard to their own ends. You must be very careful in deciding who you help and who you don't._
The wretches were being led by an ogre. I think he was stirring them up.
_Hmmmm. Such things are known to happen._ She makes some notes on the paper. _This merits more investigation. It is good that you told me._
The people around Goldcrag feel that the Pact is ignoring them. They are angry.

She holds out her hands. _What can we do? You have seen the chaos that afflicts us, inside and outside of Avadon. Should we tell them that strange incidents are happening all over Lynaeus and we haven't the forces to deal with them? Tell them that we are weak?_
_No, we will appear strong and do what we can. Goldcrag will get our attention. It must simply wait its turn._
I don't have anything else to add.

She nods and folds up the paper. _This will be kept in the records. And, with that, you are a true servant of Avadon._ Before you have time to ask if you can rest and settle in, she continues. _But we are still ... Our supply of Hands is limited._
_Another task requires doing. Another minor hunting expedition. Nothing of importance, I am sure, but I am sending you._
Miranda looks up at you from her desk. _I am always available to help Hands who are about to go out in harm's way. What do you need?_
She smiles faintly. She seems an oasis of calm in this unsettled place.
She sits on the edge of her chair and stares at you, her earlier relaxed demeanor around you completely gone.
I would like to know more about you.
She reclines back in her chair. _Hands always ask about that. I don't understand why. I am not sure that I am that interesting._
_Since we will be working together, however, I think I have a minute to spare. I came here from Dharam when I was young. I was an Eye, but I drew Redbeard's notice._
Tell me about Dharam.
_A nation of the Pact, on the eastern coast of Lynaeus. A land of sailors and merchants, and of great learning. Many libraries. Most of the best Eyes come from there._
You were an Eye?

She gestures at the mad profusion of paperwork on her desk. _I am most comfortable when I am gathering, sorting, and distilling piles of information. That is what Eyes do. I spent many years in Avadon's library._
_Then, out of all of us, I caught Redbeard's eye._
Why did Redbeard promote you?

_Why did ... Why indeed?_ She is silent for a time. _I ... We Eyes had to prepare reports for him. He noticed that mine were more useful than most, I think. More helpful. More information, I suppose._
_So he made me a Heart. An advisor. One who gives not just facts, but opinions. He consults with me about everything. Enough that some call me one of his 'wives.' When I am out of earshot._
He trusts you that much?
_Child, Redbeard trusts no one. But he mistrusts some less. He reads my reports and advice. But who knows how many agents, how many Hearts, that man has?_
You are not the only one called his 'wife'?
_I am one of three. None of us are flattered by the term. We are loyal servants. That is all._
Does Redbeard have an actual wife?
_He is married to his power. And his awesome duty._
Heart Miranda frowns. _You have done your best to dig up facts about me. I fail to see why I need to contribute any little tidbits of my own._
I learned something about you in the dungeons. I would like to ask about it.
Heart Miranda frowns. The air in her chambers suddenly becomes very chilly. _Oh, really? You have been digging up information on people in Avadon? Including your superiors?_
_Tell me. What have you learned?_
Actually, nothing. Never mind.

_So I thought. It is possible to misinterpret stray bits of information. In fact, it is easy to do so. I suggest you leave and spend some time collecting your thoughts. I am very busy._ She waves you away.
You were engaged to someone who tried to kill Redbeard.

Her face flushes red. She would not look more startled if you slapped her. _You ... you ... You dare? You answer my decades of loyal service by throwing this in my face? After all I have done? And sacrificed!_
I apologize. I should not have asked.
_But you did. Avadon rarely forgives errors. I never do. You are fortunate that I have such dire need of Hands. Now leave, and hope that I forgive you._ She waves you away.
But it is true.

She speaks as if she is choking. _It is true. And how do you think that Redbeard learned of my love's ... of what that man would do? Who do you think told him? Which woman do you think sacrificed her own heart to serve him?_
_You are fortunate that I have such dire need of Hands. I must still use you. But, for now, get out of my sight._ She waves you away.
What are you doing now?
She waves at the piles of papers on her desk. There is a wild profusion of scrolls, letters, and even a stone tablet or two. Some are new. Some are yellowed and dusty.
_Everyone comes here to get the help of Avadon. Their petitions come to me. I keep track and decide what deserves the attention of Avadon and what can be safely ignored._
_Of course, the shortage of Hands makes things more difficult._
Most petitions are ignored?
_Of course. No matter what we like to pretend, Avadon's resources are limited. We only act when we think that the stability and safety of the Pact are threatened._
Can I choose to help people myself?
_Of course, you can help petitioners you meet in the tower if you choose, as long as it does not interfere with your duties._
And you give information to Redbeard?
_Yes. The Keeper is spared the endless litany of begging. I scrape the scum of true information off the top of this ocean of pleading, and then I ... I describe the scum to him, I suppose._
You are still short of Hands?
_We are, but this will not last long, I think._
You are short of Hands even now?

_Some of them have been ... detained in the Farlands longer than we had hoped. It happens from time to time. Redbeard has been informed, and we are confident that the problem will soon be solved. Do not concern yourself._
What is my next mission?

Heart Miranda takes a sheet of papyrus from a pile on her desk. The writing on it is crude and full of misspellings. _An unusual petition, from a girl named Laurella. Normally, it would be ignored, but ..._ Her voice trails off for a moment.

_You are going to Khemeria. That is the part of the Wyldrylm that split off and opposed the Pact. Apparently, there is some horrible monster there hunting the populace. You need to investigate. See if there is anything there that merits our attention. And if there is a beast, bring back a sample of its flesh to be examined by our mages._
_To get there, there is something I must give you._
Tell me about Laurella.
_She tends to linger outside of Redbeard's chambers until they throw her out. You can go and speak with her yourself. In fact, I suggest that you do before you depart. She is ... spirited._
_In fact, to present her petition, she walked all the way here from Khemeria. Through the lands of hostile tribes. Alone. Her dedication has attracted our attention._
Why does this merit our attention?
_Because Laurella described the beast to me, and the affair has the stink of uncontrolled magery. Redbeard agrees._
_Someone in the Farlands may be concealing something from us. If so, they must be dealt with. And, if necessary, punished._
Should I discuss this with Redbeard?
_No. You will only rarely speak with Redbeard directly. Your orders come from me._
What do I need to get from you?

She collects the yellow crystal she gave you earlier. In return, she gives you a gold chain with a blue gemstone. _The portal you need to use is on the far side of the library. It will take you to Khemeria. The Farlands. Hostile territory._
_You should also see the craftmaster. I'm sure he will have something else to give you for your journey._
How should I proceed?

_Once you have spoken with Laurella, you should go there and find ..._ She checks a scroll. _Oghrym'Tor. It is a fortress there. Ask questions. Learn the truth of this monster. Destroy it, if you choose. And watch for signs of magic that could threaten the Pact._
_And remember, these are the Farlands, and you are from Avadon. Accept no insolence. Demand obedience. All of them, from the loftiest lord to the most pathetic peasant, answer to you._
_And one more thing. Do not let the local lords or soldiers know why you are there until absolutely necessary. My instincts tell me that quiet and secrecy would serve you well here._
I have investigated the beast in Khemeria. (Tell the tale.)
As Heart Miranda listens to the tale, she grows angrier and angrier. _Laurella seems to have unwittingly revealed some very questionable behavior on the part of her people._
_This has the stink of powerful magic about it. I will pass knowledge of your investigation to Redbeard. He will want to know. Is there anything else you wish to share?_
I was not allowed into their fortress.
_What? Not even let through the door? Oh, they have been too long out of the gaze of Avadon if they think this behavior will be tolerated._
Their wizard killed the beast before I could speak with it.

_And I do not need to tell you how suspicious that behavior is. Perhaps they have heard rumors that Avadon is overstretched, and they think that they can taunt us in such a way. We will continue to watch these Khemerians very closely._
I was again contacted by a shadowwalker. He spoke against Avadon.

You tell the story to Miranda. She seems strangely unmoved. _Perhaps you are being stalked. Someone might want to cultivate you as a spy. Or kill you. It's actually not mysterious or unusual. It's routine, in fact._
_Speak with this creature or kill it. Whichever you choose. He is not important to our great work._
I don't have anything else to report.
_All right. You have told us enough to make more work._ She collects the sample you took from the beast.
_And, I am sad to say, what you uncovered in your trip to The Kva has only increased your labors. No rest yet. You must head back there immediately._
What do I need to do in The Kva?

_You rid the dragon of one problem and another appears. The wretches are gone, but ogres are now attacking Goldcrag. Some of them are even raiding Zhethron's lair. The dragon is furious. I am not pleased either._

_Happily, the southern portal will still take you where you need to go. Return to the dragon and learn what you can of this towering ogre menace. And make sure that I do not need to send you there again._
_Oh, and there is one more thing._
Where are the ogres coming from?

_Goldcrag is near the Titan Peaks, one of the Farlands. Horribly inhospitable mountains, full of titans. Of no interest to the Pact, as long as they stay out of our lands. The ogres seem to be coming from the border of that region._
_Zhethron will tell you more._
Why is this a matter for Avadon?
_Why am I asking you to kill pests? To expend your valuable time hunting down mere ogres? A good question._
_Ogres are extremely disorganized creatures. Wretches, even more so. And yet, all at once, the humanoids in that region have started acting in an oddly coordinated way._
_This bothers me. I want to be convinced that I should not be worried._
Should I consult with Redbeard?
_He might want to ask you how you are settling in. You would not be in danger if you tried to speak with him. However, I doubt very much that he cares about these ogres._
What should I do?
_I don't think that subtlety is necessary. Kill anything that is causing Zhethron to be irritated and thus causing that reptile to bother me._
What else did you want to tell me?
_Hand Callan tells me that she has never met you. You should make sure to speak with her. She is a source of much valuable information. She is in the entry courtyard._
I have hunted down the ogres to Zhethron's satisfaction.
You describe the battle against the ogres. _So the reptile is content? For now? I hope its ego has been satisfied by our efforts on its behalf. Not that a dragon is ever content._
_Is there anything else you wish to tell me about events in The Kva?_
A dragon named Zephyrine was protecting the ogres.

_Zephyrine ... Zephyrine ... Sounds familiar._ She consults a list of dragons. _Ah, yes. A pest. Has shown signs of great disloyalty in the past. To be honest, I would not be unhappy if that creature were ... dispatched._
_Not that I would send a Hand to do the deed. I don't need any dead Hands on my conscience._
The ogres were led by a titan.

_But of course. That must be why they were so organized. Hopefully, that titan was working alone. But, honestly, I would not be surprised if I had to send a group of more experienced Hands to The Kva sometime soon._
I have nothing else to report.
_Then you will be pleased to know that you are about to receive a true honor. Redbeard wishes to see you. Yes, I have told the Keeper of your successes, and he may have a task for you._
_The absence of the other Hands is a stroke of luck for you. You may be rising very quickly in the hierarchy of Avadon._
The other Hands haven't returned?
_Many of them have been out on many missions. There is an unusual amount of tumult. There have been ... losses. Not your concern. They will be replaced very soon._
_But enough talk. Redbeard is waiting for you._ She waves you off.
I will go see him.
_That is wise. I would not delay. It is a true opportunity._ She waves you off.
Do you have any orders for me?
_I would not dream of giving you orders, not when Redbeard has need of you._
Redbeard sent me back here. What are my orders?

Heart Miranda grimaces and pulls a fresh message from the top of a stack of papers. _It is a report from one of our mages. It is based on the beastflesh you brought back to us from Khemeria. And, as expected, it shows that the creature was made by dark magic, hidden from Avadon._
_This, combined with their earlier insolence, is completely unacceptable. You must return to the Farlands, to ..._ She checks the paper. _Dhorl Stead._
_Find the wizard responsible for this act and kill him or her, and bring what you can of the criminal's research back to me._
The mage must be killed?
_Yes. Whoever is responsible must die. In less trying times, we might have been in a more forgiving mood. But I have had a terrible few weeks, and I am in the mood to make someone an example._
Why is such a mage so dangerous?
_Such magical experiments can create diseases, plagues of pests, deadly monsters that can attack the Pact and do enormous harm. Of all the work wizards do, such creations are the most forbidden._
Is Laurella still here?

_She is. She has been encouraged to leave, but she remains. Perhaps she has some futile desire to speak for her people. You can speak with her if you wish. You might learn something useful, though I doubt it._
_Return to Khemeria. Enter the fortress of Oghrym'Tor and confront the local lord. Perhaps he will be honest and forthright with you, and thus spare his own insignificant skin._
_If he does not help you, start breaking things until someone does. It is very important that the work that created that monstrosity ends. Now._
The beast was created by a wizard named Moritz'Kri. He is dead. (Give the papers.)
You describe your mission and present a satchel of charred scrolls. Heart Miranda nods approvingly. _And now, I have a little test for you. I would like to see how your judgment is evolving._
_Do you think your work in Dhorl Stead is complete?_
I think so. The lord aided me, and the mage is dead.

Miranda smirks. _You may be correct. I hope you are. But I doubt it. We should not end our examination. Once a place has attracted the gaze of Avadon, the gaze must remain until all foes of the Pact are burned away._
_But that is a fight for another day._
I doubt the wizard was acting alone.

Miranda thinks. _You may be right. I hope you are not, but you probably are. We should not end our examination. Once a place has attracted the gaze of Avadon, the gaze must remain until all foes of the Pact are burned away._
It doesn't matter. They have not been properly punished for their earlier insolence.

For a moment, you can't read Miranda's expression. Then she nods. _It is more work, but you are probably right. Once a place has attracted the gaze of Avadon, the gaze must remain until all foes of the Pact are burned away._
And for now?
_For now, you must continue to fight. Not just for the Pact, but to protect us from the Keeper's displeasure. Redbeard is angry. You must return to The Kva._
_Redbeard is angry. Problems with humanoids continue near Goldcrag, and now the dragon Zhethron has been injured. The problem now is titans, as we should have suspected all along._

_I think we are close to the source of this problem. You must return to Zhethron. Evaluate the lizard's condition and learn what he knows. Then destroy the titans before he kills himself attacking them again._
Wait. Titans?
_Yes. Far stronger than wretches or ogres, and far more organized. Though they are normally wise enough to refrain from attacking the Pact and its allies._
_But Zhethron seems to have found that they were instigating the attacks against him. He was angry, and he did what enraged dragons do._
Zhethron fought the titans?

_He seems to feel that Avadon was not doing our part in our bargain. And he is probably right. He hunted the titans and attacked them. I understand that he felled a number of them, until their flung boulders knocked him from the sky._
_He returned to safety, but he is seriously wounded._
Why is Redbeard angry?

_Because he feels that we should have seen this coming and prevented it. And it does not matter whether the charge is just or not. We serve at his pleasure. If he wants to make an example of us by sending us to the dungeons, he can._
_Take the southern portal and return to see Zhethron. He can tell you where the titans are. They have acted against the Pact, and their lives are forfeit._
_Also, find any evidence you can to show who is urging these creatures to rise up against us, and bring the villain back to me. Not the dragon, me._
The titans have been wiped out, though the dragon is still angry.

Heart Miranda nods. She seems very interested. _Then, at last, we have gotten to the source of one of the conspiracies plaguing us. Did you find any evidence of whether they were acting alone or at the instigation of others?_
I found these letters. Here. (Give them.)

She takes the scrolls and examines them. _In code. Of course. But a code, I am sure, that titans could decipher. Which means it is simple, which means that the Eyes will translate these messages in no time at all._
_As a reward for your industry, I will consult with the quartermaster and see if there are any locked vaults in the storerooms that can be opened for you._
_You have done very well. Your efforts will, I think, even turn aside Redbeard's rage. And that is good, because he wishes to see you._
I found no evidence of any sort.
_Really?_ She raises her eyebrows. _So the titans acted alone? No help from anyone?_
We can't know for sure. I found no evidence one way or the other.
_I see. Well, Zhethron is happy, so Redbeard will not be angry. Or as angry._
_And that is good, because he wishes to see you. Go upstairs and see him. I wish you luck. Hopefully, he is not in the mood to punish you._
I suspect that that is the case.
_I see. Well, Zhethron is content, so Redbeard will not be angry. Or as angry._
Redbeard sent me back to you. What are my orders?
_We have analyzed the papers you brought from the tower of the Khemerian wizard. We found that he had recently received some rare powders, gems, and other alchemical materials._

She consults some papers. _And here is the interesting part. Weeks before that, their lord, Carsta'Arl, had imported exactly those materials from Holklanda. In other words, their lord was supplying the rogue wizard._
_We have no choice. Carsta'Arl must be brought to Avadon to answer our charges. If he refuses, he is to be killed. Only then will the gaze of Avadon be satisfied._
But did Carsta'Arl know what his wizard was doing?
_That is what he must be brought here to find out. But it hardly matters. Being clumsy enough to give unlimited supplies to a mad wizard is still a crime, if it threatens the Pact._
What if I have to attack Carsta'Arl's fortress?
_Then do so. Do not fear. You will have allies. Strike decisively and without fear. I have already put plans in motion._
_The important thing is that their lord is subjected to the will of Avadon. Prisoner. Or dead. Those are the only choices._
What should I do about the people of Dhorl Stead?
_Whatever you wish. The whole land is subject to the wrath of Avadon. Punish. Be merciful. Your decision. We trust your judgment completely._

_Who?_ Miranda digs up records of your previous expeditions. _Oh. Her. She left some weeks ago. Hopefully, your work will be done before she gets home. I'm not sure she will want to see what is about to happen._
Carsta'Arl, the lord of Dhorl Stead, is dead.

You describe the carnage to Heart Miranda. She seems strangely unmoved by your tale of destruction. _I'm sure, by now, the tale has spread throughout Khemeria and beyond. That is what comes from attracting the gaze of Avadon._
_It is done. There is no more need to think on it._
Did we do the right thing?
Her face is cold. _Right? What is right? What an odd concept. We are Avadon. Our actions become right because it is us that do them. Have you not yet learned that?_
What will happen to Dhorl Stead?
_They have been weakened. And, considering the fate of weakened lands in Khemeria, well, I would not plan to live there any time soon. The next few years will not be pleasant for them._
I am proud of what we did. The Pact is safer for it.
_How could anything else be true? Anyway, you were only following our orders, so you can be comforted. If you ever develop moral qualms, what happens is not your fault. In a sense, anyway._
_It does not matter, either way. As long as Redbeard lives, you will do what he and his servants command. And that leads you to your next mission._
I do not think what happened was justified.
_Well, you were only following our orders, so you can be comforted. Whatever your moral qualms, what happened was not your fault. In a sense, anyway._
_It does not matter either way. As long as Redbeard lives, you will do what he and his servants command. And that leads you to your next mission._
Another mission? When can I rest?
_When you are dead. You serve Avadon now. Even when you are not active, you will not be resting. You will always wait for the will of Redbeard._
_Return to Redbeard. He ..._ She suddenly looks very tired. _I need to write a report on your mission and file it away. You ... Just go._ She waves you away.
Miranda is writing a brief account of your battle against Carsta'Arl. _We are still short of Hands. Go to Redbeard. He will instruct you._
Still short of Hands? After all this? Where are they?

_Some are still on their missions. Some are lost. Many are dead. Avadon has been ... surprised by the intensity of the opposition its agents have been receiving in the Farlands. Far more have been lost than expected._
I will report to Redbeard.
_That is wise. He can, after all, have you killed with a wave of his hand. We are all completely at his mercy. Never forget that._ She waves you off.
You are always here. We are always working. Is there always this much chaos?
She starts to give you a quick, sharp dismissal, but something stops her. She sighs, sets down her pen, and sits back in her chair.
For a moment, she seems to forget how irritated she is with you.
_It is not normal. These troubles ... I have had this post for a long time. I do not often get tired, but ..._ She shakes her head.
How long have you served here?
_Thirty years. Thirty years. Long enough that I am called his wife. Me ... his wife. It ..._ She rests her chin on her chest for a long moment. At first, you think she might have fallen asleep.
Then her head snaps up. She laughs. _It has been a long time. I don't know why I do it. Except, of course, for the wealth and power._
You are wealthy?

_You have roamed Lynaeus. You have seen how poor most of our lands are. We are still trying to recover from many decades of war. Compared to them, we live in constant luxury. When we're not out fighting._
How much power do you have?

_This desk looks humble, does it not? And yet, from here, I send warriors and assassins to all the known lands. Redbeard makes a few big decisions. I make many little ones. And the little ones matter greatly. Yes, they do._
Will you ever retire?
_And if I did? If I set foot outside this fortress? To face the grudges of the families of all that we have acted against? How long do you think I would last?_
_And you? Do you think you will ever leave Avadon's service?_
When I have enough wealth and influence, I plan to retire in comfort.
_Many do. And, as you follow our orders, remember how many will want revenge on you. I had such dreams once, but ..._ She shakes her head and picks up her pen.
_We must return to business._
_Enough talk. You have orders to follow._ Her brief moment of tolerance for you has ended.
I wish to die in the service of Avadon.
_A noble wish. And one that is always granted, in the end._ She shakes her head and picks up her pen.
That is all I need to know.
She dips her pen in ink and grabs a handful of scrolls. _Then go forth and fight for Avadon._
You stagger away from the platform, barely able to remain standing. Something about this journey makes it far worse than previous times you used the pylons.

Finally, your senses start to return to you. You look around, only to find that you are alone. Your companions have gone missing. You look back at the portal. The nimbus of power that surrounds it is faded and flickering. That might explain the difficulty of the journey.

Then you hear something to the west. An explosion. Then screaming. Then the sounds of fighting. The smell of smoke is heavy in the air, and the guards are gone. The floor under your feet vibrates from distant impacts.
Something has gone very wrong here. Avadon is under attack.

As you walk around the corner, the gate to the south, which leads to the barracks, is open. Three Avadon guards run through it. Their weapons are drawn and their armor is scratched and scorched. They are fleeing for their lives.

Moments later, several more warriors pass under the open gate, chasing them. They wear the garb of shadowwalkers, black masks obscuring their faces. And yet, they don't move like shadowwalkers, and the weapons are wrong.
The blades of their pursuers are drawn and stained with blood. They pursue the guards of Avadon with silent, deadly purpose.
You approach the portal, only to find that it is flickering unpredictably and occasionally fading entirely. Trying to use it to travel seems dangerous, if not suicidal. You back away.

There is a young warrior standing guard by the passage to the south, keeping close watch in case anything else nasty comes out of it. He turns to look at you. You see that he is about your age. His face bears a nasty scar, running diagonally down his face.
He says, _Greetings. I am Sevilin. You are here to stand guard with me? No. I suppose not. We need to go fight now, don't we? I knew the time would come. I'll follow my orders. I always do._
Sevilin stares morbidly at the southern corridor. _Nothing has come out of there since the wretches. Someone will need to go down and investigate soon._ He sounds very grim.
What are you doing here?
_Just trying to be of aid. When things went wrong this morning, all of the Hands were sent out on this mission or that. Only I was left._ He points to the north. _And Nathalie._
_When wretches came out of the dungeons, I thought I would stand guard until someone found a use for me. The gate is closed, but wretches can slip through the bars._
You have been wounded. Do you need help?
At first, Sevilin isn't sure what you mean. He looks down at his armor, looking for signs of an injury. Then he realizes that you are referring to his scar and laughs bitterly.
_You mean this? This is an old mark. Easy to forget it is there. I only remember it when I look in the mirror. Or when a stranger sees me._
I am going to clean out the dungeons.
He nods. _I am not surprised. Miranda needs to send a Hand down there to clean it up. And you show up, in need of testing. I am not offended that I was passed over._
Do you know what went wrong?

_I don't know. The Hearts and Eyes won't share any information with someone as lowly as me. As far as I can tell, something exploded, and everything escaped from the dungeons below. The Hands can't help, because they have all been sent out of the fortress on missions._
He absent-mindedly touches his scar. _Being a servant of Avadon doesn't keep us safe. Just the opposite._
Do you know what is happening in the dungeon?
_No, but it must have been ugly. Few of the guards on duty down there made it out._
How did it happen?
He looks exasperated. _Even if I enjoyed discussing it, this is not the best time._
And you can still fight?
_Of course, if I am ever chosen for a mission again._
You think you were passed over? Why?
_I do not question the wisdom of Redbeard or the Hearts. They choose who to send into danger for their own reasons. I have learned to simply, quietly accept._
I can select one Hand to enter the dungeon with me.
For a moment, his eyes show a glint of interest. Maybe even hope. _I came to Avadon to serve. I have spent ... too long not serving. I was born to fight. I am ready._
What can you do for me?
_I am a blademaster of Avadon. I can stand toe to toe with our foes and defeat them with blade and armor. And, if needed, I can stand in their way to keep them from reaching you._
You are prepared to fight? Right now?
He raps his armor with his knuckle. Then he rests one hand on the pommel of his blade. _I will give everything to prove I can still be a warrior of Avadon._
I need to consider Nathalie.
He deflates slightly. _Yes. Yes. Of course you do. If you take her ... I suppose Avadon needs guards in the corridors as much as anything else._
(When you enter the dungeons, you will be able to choose who travels with you.)
I think I will choose you.
He pats his blade with a gauntleted hand. _Then I am ready._
There is a young warrior patrolling the storeroom, carefully watching the passage to the south. You soon realize that he is not Heart Miranda.
Sevilin is sitting in his quarters, working on maintaining his weapons. There are a variety of blades on the desk in front of him. He takes great care to sharpen and polish each one.
He looks up at you. _What do you wish of me, [N]?_
As you look into his eyes, you can see that they have become haunted. The confrontation with the bandits has troubled him greatly.
I'd like to know more about where you are from.

He nods. _I am a warrior of The Kva, upholder of the Stone Code._ He smiles wryly. _I learned early on that others do not appreciate me holding forth on the virtues of my land. I only do so when asked._
Others don't admire your land?
_There are five lands in the Pact, each with their own traditions and practices. While interest in survival holds us together, there is a ... lack of respect for each other's ways._
_After all, it was less than a century ago that we were all embroiled in a vicious civil war. And there are still many grudges._
Why did you come to Avadon?
_Because I believe in the justice of the Stone Code, and I believe in the wisdom of the Pact. I came here to be a living example, to show to all that the Stone Code has much to teach us._
And have you had success?
_First, I learned that people from other lands have no interest in fairly evaluating our ways._
He self-consciously touches the scar on his cheek. _Then a mission went horribly wrong, and I lost any value as a good example._
Tell me more about the Stone Code.
_It is a set of laws, harsh and fair. And, unlike in other states, they apply to all. From the peasants to the lords and the monarch, all must obey them or be exposed as a sham to all._
_It is not like Avadon, where one man is the law and all fear him. Not, I hasten to add, that I would ever criticize Avadon._
He sounds especially bitter as he says this.
Can you give me an example of one of your laws?

_Of course. Consider theft. If a thief steals more than ten coins worth of goods, the miscreant is brought before a judge to hear the facts of the case. If the judge finds guilt, other factors, such as starvation or desperation, are considered._

_Then three penalties can be given. Removal of the hand, branding of a 'T' on the criminal's wrist, or banishment can be applied. Branding is most common. It is far from rare to see people, even nobles and the young, with that telltale mark._
Is that not harsh?
_It is harsh. Life is harsh in The Kva. Stealing a bag of meal worth ten coins can doom a family to starvation. The weight of the punishment matches the crime._
And how do regular folk know the laws?

_They are carved on stones in the middle of each village. Thus, the Stone Code. All are able to approach and see what they may and may not do. Another point in its favor, one that I have described to any who would listen._
That's a nice collection of blades.
He nods. _My master in The Kva told me that a true craftsman is never satisfied by less than the finest tools. If my blades were dirty or not properly sharp, he would ... show his displeasure._
Can you tell me more about your scar?
Hand Sevilin frowns. _Yes. Yes, if you are to trust me with your life, you should know of me. This is nothing that should be kept secret._
_I showed some promise when I arrived, so I was soon sent with a band of other Hands back to my beloved Kva. We were to hunt a pack of bandits._
Why was Avadon interested in mere bandits?
_Because they were hiding in The Kva and raiding over the border in Kellemderiel. This sort of thing raises tension between the Pact states and thus involves Avadon._
What happened?
_There is actually little to tell. We followed their trail. We camped. They attacked in the night, but the Hand on watch was not properly attentive._
_We fought them off, but at the end, only two of us were still standing. The other died of his wounds not long after. And I received this._ He touches the scar on his cheek.
_I returned to Avadon. I was not disgraced, but a cloud hung over me. None wished to take me on their missions. You are my last chance, I think._
And what happened to the bandits?

_Nothing yet. Redbeard has sent others to hunt them, I think. I am not told the details. I can't imagine such an outrage against warriors of Avadon going unanswered._ You can see on his face that he has some doubts.
_Nothing yet. Now that I know where their leader is, however, I will make sure that they answer for their crimes soon enough._
Are you more content now that the bandits have been slain?
_What can I say to that? Vengeance is ours. This is good. But what I saw of Avadon, its cravenness, Redbeard's lack of action, it ..._
He shakes his head. _Excuse me, [N], I am rambling. I am content, though I have much to think on. As, perhaps, do you._
As you emerge from the portal, you are surprised to find Sevilin waiting for you. He seems quite distressed.
_Excuse me. I need a moment of your time. I spoke with the other Hands as soon as they appeared. I can't help you if I don't know what you have been doing._
Can this wait?
He shakes his head. _It can't. It is of great importance to me._
Go on.
_One Hand mentioned a bandit you saw briefly. One who had a scar close to mine. He fled. Is this true?_
It is not. (Lie.)
Sevilin nods, but you can see that he doesn't believe you. _I understand. You do not wish to be involved. Thank you for your ... help. Excuse me._ Face flushed, he turns and walks off.
That is the case.
He nods. _I did not dare to hope. That is the bandit who attacked my band. Who killed all of us but me. Who gave me this._ He points at his scar.
_They insulted the Pact, and they defied Avadon. I don't know why Redbeard allows them to live, but the honor of this keep and the Stone Code demand that they do not go unpunished._
We have greater matters to deal with. Forget it. For now.
_Yes. Greater matters. Hunting stray beasts and the scut work of dragons. Far more important than the honor of Avadon._
_I have heard what you said. You will learn of my decision later._ Face flushed, he turns smartly on one heel and stalks off.
Being a Hand leaves you free to act. Do what you must.
He nods. _I appreciate that, [N]. And, I hope, should the time come, you will fight alongside me. If you need me, I will be in my quarters._ He turns and walks off.
And I would be happy to aid you.
He nods, pleased. _Should I learn more, I may need to leave quickly. When I go, however, I will be sure to leave word of my destination. I thank you for your support._
_If you need me, I will be in my quarters._ He turns and walks off.
Sevilin is sitting at his desk, polishing and preparing his weapons. However, he is not looking well. His eyes are bloodshot, and his hands tremble gently. He has not been sleeping well. Or at all.
_Excuse me, [N]._ he says. _I was not expecting you. I was just preparing to rest._
I will leave you, then. Get some sleep.
He nods. _Of course. You are right. I should not be seen so ... unready. I will sleep immediately. I will do what it takes to rest._ He removes a bottle from his desk and staggers off toward his bed.
What is bothering you?
_I ... I cannot stop thinking about that bandit. The one with the scar. The one who scarred me. He did it, you know. He marked me to match him. To make me like him. He ..._ He trails off.
The bandit will be dealt with. Pull yourself together.
He nods. _Yes. We know where the bandit is. We can wait, and ... No. The bandit will flee soon. Someone must act. I ... I must rest. Prepare. Think clearly. You are right._
_I will rest. Do what I can to prepare myself. Whatever it takes to sleep. Excuse me._ He removes a bottle from his desk and staggers off toward his bed.
Forget about it and do what you must to ready yourself.
_Forget it? How can I? The insult, against Avadon, against the Pact. How I can forget him, with his blade, coming ..._ He shakes his head.
_You are correct. I must rest. Do what I can to prepare myself. Whatever it takes to sleep. Excuse me._ He removes a bottle from his desk and staggers off toward his bed.
Just go to bed. Now.
Sevilin is still sitting at his desk. His weapons, all immaculate, go untouched. Instead, he stares at the torch on the wall, lost in thought.
He looks up at you. _Greetings, [N]. I was hoping that you would come and see me._
_I never had the chance to properly thank you._
I was glad for the chance to help you.
_Your loyalty was appreciated. I owe you my life._
_You brought justice. It is something I did not expect to see._
_You did, of course, let a vicious thug and murderer go free. But I ... I must try to accept that Avadon is the way it is. It is futile for me to try to change it._
_In any case, I have much to think on._
You distracted me from my duty. Don't let it happen again.
He nods. _I see. Avadon had a shortage of Hands. You did not want to see one go to waste. It was a pragmatic act. And yet, I do owe you my life._
_And you brought justice. It is something I did not expect to see._
What are you thinking about?

_The brigand's final words. I knew that Avadon was a place where justice could be bought. When a Hand decides who to help and who to ignore, a heavy purse swings the balance one way or the other. But to spare one who killed Hands, even for information, it bothers me._
_That such a factor determined whether that murderer would live or die ... It is ... perplexing._
He seems to have decided to, for the moment, forget about your releasing the brigand.
I try not to think about it.
_Yes. I have seen that. None of the Hands think about it. They come here and they accept the power they see as their due. But me, I ..._
_I must rest and think. And I hope, some time soon, you will return to discuss this further. Anything else?_
I will have to consider that.
_I am glad to hear of it. Such reflection is a rare thing here. The Hands arrive and they accept the power they see as their due. But me, I ..._
It is not up to us to question Avadon.
Sevilin suddenly seems suspicious. _I see. I admire your unencumbered way of looking at Avadon. And yet, perhaps we might discuss this later. Maybe you will decide to ..._ He sighs. _Anything else?_

Sevilin is still sitting at his desk. Something has changed about him. Something is different. He is not tending to his weapons for the moment. He simply looks at the torch on the wall and smiles. He is ... You know now. He is content.
He looks up at you. _Ahhh ... Greetings, [N]. I am pleased to see you. I have had much time to think._
And what have you been thinking about?
_I have simply been considering Avadon and my place in it. And what might be done to make this fortress a more just, efficient place._

You ask what he means, but he suddenly becomes evasive. _Oh, I would not concern you with this right now. You have so much to do. So many missions to complete, rewards to earn. Tell me, what did you wish to discuss?_
_I think that I can trust you. I would share some of my thoughts with you. I owe you my life, after all._

_Now, I would never be so foolish as to criticize Redbeard. That would be madness. I will simply say that Avadon has become ... undisciplined. There is nothing like the Stone Code, no predictability, no honor, no justice._
_It is simply people acting for their own interests, letting their blades be purchased, elevating gold above the good of the Pact._
He speaks quietly, and you know why. If Redbeard knew what he was saying, the results for him would be unpleasant.
You are sure that you are not just resentful of what happened to you?
_It is true that we were sent into enemy territory without enough warriors, equipment, or support. Because of the inattention of our masters, good people died._
_But that is only a symptom of the true problem. Power and gold matter in Avadon, not the proper carrying out of our duties._
And what do you think should happen?

He laughs, a strangely carefree sound in these dim stone halls. _I don't know! It was so much work just to discover and wrestle with this truth. Now that I have accepted it, I do not know how to proceed._
_What do you think I should do?_ He looks at you very intently. You suspect that, for him, much depends on your response.
I feel that the problem begins and ends with the leader. With Redbeard.

He nods somberly. _I did not have the courage to say the words aloud, but, now that they are out, they have the feeling of truth. I believe it. And, as I am sane, I am terrified. Let us talk of other things. We both have much to think about._
I do not know what to do either. All I know is that things must change.
He nods somberly. _Yes. Things must change. And, in Avadon, things change in only one place. In ..._ It takes some time to build up the courage to speak the words. _In the center tower._
_Now, let us talk of other things. We both have much to think about._
I am a loyal servant of Redbeard. I will not act against him.

He nods sadly. _I thought you might say as much. And you are correct. Please dismiss this conversation as the ramblings of a tired soul. We still have much to do together, and I still swear that I will fight loyally by your side._
_Now, let of talk of other things. We both have much to think about._

When you get close to the young sorceress, she looks up at you. She is breathing hard, still charged with adrenaline from her recent battle. _I did it! I killed them. By myself. Not that I will get any notice for it, of course._
She takes a moment to calm down. _Oh. I am sorry. I am Nathalie. A Hand of Avadon. I have spent long enough waiting for action that I need to take a moment to luxuriate in it._
Nathalie has calmed down a little from when you first met her. _Still here? Surely there is more to do. I only hope I can take part in it._
What happened here?
_Three wretches came out of the dungeon. I was in the main courtyard when I heard them. I surprised and dispatched them, but not before ..._
Wretches?
_Vile little humanoids. Dumb and hungry. The scourge of the known lands. I don't know why Redbeard would bother to keep them around._
Did they do any harm?
_They killed the quartermaster. Not a warrior, but a good man. I spent many hours speaking with him while waiting for something to do. A minute earlier and I might have saved him._
I am a Hand as well.
She nods. _You have the look. And a weapon. I hope you have more luck getting sent out than I do._
She looks startled. _What? You? No offense, but you have been here what? Ten minutes? When some of us have been waiting ..._
Once again, she calms down. _But you will probably need help. Isn't that the case? Taking one of the other Hands with you, to share in the glory. Yes?_
You have been wanting to go fight?

_Of course! I have spent my life working, training, and sharpening my talents, to fight for Avadon. All those years, sun-up to sun-down, and my reward? Sitting in the Black Fortress waiting to be allowed to risk my life._
_Yes, I want to fight. I ask and ask, but here I stay._
I can take one Hand into the dungeons with me.

It doesn't take her long to do the math. _One Hand, out of two. Me and Sevilin. The warrior. Well, speak to Sevilin and compare._ She looks at the scorched marks. _I am eager and competent. He is, well, you can see for yourself._
_When you go downstairs, if you wish, I will come and join you. But you will select me? Yes?_

_I am a trained sorceress. I can summon bolts of fire and ice and direct them at our foes. I do not rely on crude armor or mundane weapons, however, so you might wish to help me keep a safe distance from our foes._
We will see.
You see the gleam of enthusiasm in her eyes. _All right. I will be standing ready._
She nods. You see the gleam of enthusiasm in her eyes. _All right. You will not regret the decision._
A warrior would be useful.
Her eyes darken in an instant. _Useful, yes. But ideal? I will be waiting here, standing ready, in case you change your mind._
There is a young sorceress standing here, looking down at scorch marks on the ground. You soon realize that she is not Heart Miranda.

The mage Nathalie is sitting at her desk, surrounded by papers and scrolls. It appears that her every free moment is lost in study, reading obscure tracts and learning new magical techniques. Such dedication is unusual even at the rarified level of Avadon.
She sits with you, reluctantly accepting a brief rest. _What do you wish of me, fellow Hand?_
Now that you see her in good lighting, you realize how young she is. She is seventeen at most, amazingly young for a warrior of Avadon.
Though she is still very young for a warrior of Avadon, her labors and wounds make her seem far older. There is something driven in her gaze that makes you want to look away.
Where are you from?
_I am from Kellemderiel, jewel of Lynaeus. A place of beauty and wonders, and home to the greatest of colleges and academies._ She blushes slightly. _But I will cease there._
_Others tire quickly of hearing descriptions of my homeland, even accurate ones._ She adds ruefully, _And I must make an effort to make friends where I can._
Tell me more about Kellemderiel.
_Ah, but you attempt to tempt me, yes? To draw me into a new speech so you can mock me behind my back? Know that I am used to it. I will believe what I believe._
_I will simply say that we are a place of culture, good breeding, long tradition, and great order. Even a Holklandan must admit that, whatever else he convinces himself of._
There are fine colleges there?

_Indeed. Only Dharam matches us in our libraries and our respect for learning. The finest workers of magic come from Kellemderiel, without question. Not the crude shamanic arts of the west, but true magery._
Others don't like hearing about your land?
_The Pact has five lands, and the history among them has not been untroubled. Though the civil wars of the Black Age are a century past, many grudges remain._
_For example, I have learned to say little about the Beraza Woods, though it is a topic dear to the heart of all true Kellem._
And who of the Pact do you hate?
_Understand, I claim to hate none of my mates in the Pact. Not even the Holklandans. Open Arms Within, the Stone Wall Beyond. I believe this, even when every drop of my Kellem blood fights it._
Tell me more about the Beraza Woods.
_I have learned well not to discuss it, not if I ever wish to be used in a mission again._
_Instead, I will let Redbeard tell you of it, since that region has had his attention of late. I only hope that he remembers who the true owners of that contested land are._
Where did you get those papers?
She looks at the scrolls on her desk. _The librarian. Eye Leira. Even though she is Holklandan, she is very kind about letting me see the papers. She collects magical writings from all over Lynaeus._
_I am not supposed to have anything from the library in my room, but she helps me._
How?
_She lets me borrow papers that are of interest, but not unique enough to become a part of the permanent collection._
_I look at them and then return them for destruction. Then none of my rival Hands get to see them._ She smiles sweetly.
What are you preparing for?
She looks ruefully at the stacks of papers. _I came to Avadon because I knew I was destined for greatness. This place was to be the fulcrum from which I could move the world._
_But things have not worked out as well as I had hoped. So I prepare._
You are destined for greatness?

_I am! I am tired of concealing it! It was clear from the time I could walk. My mastery of magic is deep within me. I was the youngest student in the history of the Academy. At times, I even taught my teacher._

_I was the youngest graduate in centuries. Only two mages in the history of Kellemderiel earned their robes before me. Only three received a true staff sooner. My innate talent is clear! Everyone recognizes it but Avadon!_
That seems impressive.
She seems slightly embarrassed by her outburst. _I apologize. Such words only get me in trouble. And yet, I must say it from time to time, so I do not forget it._
So you came to Avadon.

_Of course. Avadon is the true power in Lynaeus. When I looked at myself honestly, looked at the potential I had been given, I knew that it was the one place where I could truly live up to what I should do._
And she talks, she flexes the hand on her injured arm. The bitterness that has crept into her voice is unmistakable.
What happened once you were here?
_I was accepted, of course, as I knew I would be. And then I was not used! I was treated as a mere apprentice, given lessons in skills I had mastered years before! They even tried to make me an Eye!_
_I pushed for more to do whenever I could. And so I made enemies of those I most relied upon to use me. But I am patient, and I will show my true worth._
Why didn't they use you?
_They said it was because I was too young. As if that makes me untrustworthy! As if my skills, which they themselves admitted were superior, could not help make up for such shortcomings!_
_And, perhaps, there was envy there as well. And fear. I would not guess what was happening in their minds._
You have enemies now?
_Well, that might be a strong word. Perhaps I at times pushed too persistently to be allowed to serve. Perhaps I irritated Heart Miranda more than was wise._
_So they mock me. It is no matter. They will learn._ She looks at the scrolls. _I will study, and I will show them._
How do you feel about Avadon now?

She rests her injured hand on one of her scrolls. You suspect that it is taking some effort to keep her from tearing it apart. _I do everything I can to show them my value. Before, they mocked me. Now they pity and avoid me. When I was fighting for them!_
What will you do?
_I will show them. No matter what it takes, I will show them. Now excuse me. I must return to my studies._ She turns away.

When you approach Nathalie, she sets a scroll aside and rises from her chair. There is an intensity in her eyes that is unsettling in one so small and so young. _I have been meaning to talk to you. There is something we must discuss._
I am quite busy.
_Well, it cannot wait. I have tried and tried to show patience, but in this time of crisis, I can wait no more._
What is it?
She seems surprised. _I ... I am glad that you will listen. I tried to be patient, but in this time of crisis I can wait no more._
_I want to know why you have not called upon me more! There are so few Hands available, and my raw talent is, frankly, greater than that of those you have called upon._
_I want to know why we are not doing more! This is a time of chaos. We should not be so idle. You should be taking me through the portals and hunting down those who have dared to challenge Avadon._
_When will you be taking me out to fight?_
It is my decision. I will bring you when I will it, and not a moment before.
Nathalie takes a step back. Her temper narrowly stays under control. _I ... Yes. Of course. This is a familiar situation. I have heard those words before._
_I ... I will be patient. Yes. Excuse my outburst._
She attempts to smile. _Do you wish anything else?_
Be patient. All Hands wish the chance to fight for Avadon.

She nods. Then she dismisses your words with a wave of her hand. _Be patient. How I hate the word! Every day, a bit more of my youthful strength and potential sloughs away, but I am told to be docile and drown in my patience._
_But I will withstand it. I will stay patient. I have learned my lesson._
You are right. We should hunt together more often.
She nods, surprised. _I am grateful that you said so. I have had to wait for too long to hear those words. You need not worry. I will risk everything to show you what I am capable of._
She smiles. _Do you wish anything else?_
No. Return to your studies.
_I will. When the call comes, I will be prepared._ She returns to her desk.
There is something else I want to discuss.
She sits at her desk and sips some tea. _Of course._

You are surprised to find that Nathalie is standing in the hall, waiting for you. She is shaking with agitation. _Excuse me. I see that you are returning from the field. Without me. That is not surprising._
_However, I have heard something from the other Hands. I wish to ask about it._
Excuse me. I am busy.

Nathalie stands still for a moment, trying to, at last, be patient. She fails. She stands in your way. _This is a time of crisis. This may be my last chance to act, to show my potential. I will speak._
What do you want to know?
She nods, pleased that you will listen. _I heard that there was something in Beraza. Something that is worth hunting. For the good of Avadon, of course._
_I heard that there was a drake in the Beraza Woods. A powerful specimen, with considerable and unusual magical capabilities. The impudent lizard attacked agents of Avadon. Then it escaped._
_I will set aside my feelings about Avadon's meddling in the Beraza Woods. The head of such a creature would be a worthy trophy to bear back to Avadon._
Meddling in the Beraza Woods?
_The Beraza Woods belong to Kellemderiel. All but the stubborn, hidebound warriors of Holklanda admit it. But this is an argument I have no interest in starting now._
A trophy?
_The head of such a drake, killed both for vengeance and for study._ Her eyes gleam. _Yes, that would make them notice us. Recognize our worth. And it is just one drake. A pest!_
What do you want from me?
_Come with me. I will find where it is, and we will hunt it!_
That is not part of our mission. Let the creature go.
She opens her mouth. Then, after some thought, she closes it again. _I ... see. Your advice seems wise. I will ... consider it._
_I will be in my chambers if you have any more need of me._ She turns and leaves.
If you find out where it is, I will consider helping you. Maybe.
She nods. _You are wise to consider it. It would be a great deal of glory for us to share. ... Share._ She looks you over. _Yes. I will let you know._
It sounds like a worthy prize. I will help you to hunt it down.

She nods. At first, she is enthusiastic. _You are wise to consider it. It would be a great deal of glory for us to share. ... Share._ She rolls the word around in her mouth. It is distasteful. _Yes. I will let you know._

Nathalie sits at her desk and looks down at her arm. The healers of Avadon are skilled. The bandages are already off. The scars are still there, of course, but she has even regained much of the range of motion in her hand.
She looks up at you. There are wrinkles around her eyes, odd in one so young. She has not been sleeping well. _Kind of you to come and see me. I ... I owe you much. What do you wish of me?_
How is your arm?
She holds the injured arm up and looks at it, as if it is an alien thing. _They think that this will quiet me down. Teach me some humility. Remove my ambition. Make me content with joining ... them._
_But they are wrong. Some of its dexterity returns with every day. I will soon regain my full power._
Are you recovering well?
She laughs bitterly. _Oh, yes. I am fine. As strong as ever. Not that I ever get any credit for it! Not that my worth will ever be properly valued!_
_Yes, I am recovering well, because I have learned the true lesson. One that I'm sure you have learned as well._
What do they say about you?
_I am a young stripling, a child, outmatched, annoying, useless, to be pitied and ignored. They probably want to make me a scullery maid! Oh, yes, they will allow me to clean their bedpans. Me!_
_I have said that they will see my true power and skill. I still mean it._
What lesson have you learned?

_That Avadon is for the asleep. That Redbeard brings us here to be his servants. That we will never be allowed to change anything, to have any power, to live up to our true potential. We will collect our bribes and sleep in our silk sheets and die fat and docile._
_No. If we are to make any difference in this world, if we are to be noticed, we must act._
She ends with that oddly vague statement. Then she looks at you, waiting for a response. You are once again amazed at how young she looks, and how much raw ambition is visible upon her face.
I am comfortable with how Avadon is run. I have no intention of changing it.
She nods. _I see. Excuse me. Ignore what I have been saying. I am tired, and my wound ... pains me. Please leave me. I am in need of much preparation._ She returns to work.
There is some wisdom in what you say.
She nods. _A proper, diplomatic answer. I understand. But there will come a time when mere diplomacy will not suffice._
_Excuse me. Ignore what I have been saying. I am tired, and my wound ... pains me. Please leave me. I am in need of much preparation._ She returns to work.
You are right. Power won't be given. It must be taken.
She nods. She says nothing in response. At last, Nathalie has seemed to learn that there can be much value in silence.
Then she says, _But excuse me. Ignore what I have been saying. I am tired, and my wound ... pains me. Please leave me. I am in need of much preparation._ She returns to work.
Once again, you approach Craftmaster Nicodemus. You feel a bit safer this time, as he doesn't have any mad, twisted wolves with him. He sets his hammer aside and nods to you.
_I see that you have settled in. And now you are here to receive supplies, yes? That is my purpose in life._ He smiles. _I am here to protect the Hands. How can I help you?_
Craftmaster Nicodemus sets his work aside whenever any Hand comes to him for help. He does a very good job of concealing his irritation at being kept from his labors.
I can get supplies from you?
_Of course, as soon as Heart Miranda lets me know that you are entitled. You might wish to speak with her. Now, excuse me._ He returns to working on his ring.
Heart Miranda sent me to get supplies.
He nods. _I have received word from her. You are very fortunate. I am skilled in the crafting of magical goods, and Avadon puts the finest resources at my disposal._
_When you are given a mission, come to me. I will give you the most useful, freshly crafted magical tool I still have available._
Items you still have available?
He coughs slightly. _Ah ... As you may know, most of our Hands have had to go out on missions, and many of my more ... pyrotechnic items have been taken._
_Don't worry. I will make sure that anything I give you will do ... something._
Are your items as reliable as your wolves?
He is unfazed. _Oh, dear. You have a grudge about that little incident? Then I apologize. And I will continue to apologize any time something similar happens._
What do you have for me now?

He has an assistant fetch a long baton of polished oak for you. _This is a rod of attraction. I am quite pleased with it. Watch._ The assistant starts to walk away. Nicodemus waves the wand, and an invisible hand seizes the young man and yanks him back to you.
_See? Quite marvelous. You are dismissed._ The assistant, now somewhat bruised and sprained, staggers away. Nicodemus hands you the wand.
What is it good for?

_For bringing things that are farther away closer to you! Like, say, irritating enemy mages. I admit, it lacks fire, lightning, or the more flashy magical manifestations, but it is a wand of great utility._
_Now, how else can I help you?_
_Really? How novel. There is little to tell, though. Not much to say about me beyond my work._
_I come from Dharam, where from a young age I showed great talents. Both with magic and with mundane crafts. Word of my existence reached Redbeard, who brought me here._
Can you tell me more about Dharam?

_Ah ... My beautiful coastal home. I have not been there for so long. I have a book about it here somewhere, if you wish to learn more. The next time the portals are set to take Hands there, I must return for a visit._
Redbeard found you when you were young? How old does that make Redbeard?
_Redbeard became Keeper in the year 6257. It is now 6312. And yet, he looks so young. Remarkable, yes? The Keeper of Avadon has resources beyond even what is available to me. I am envious._
And you are loyal to the cause of Avadon?
_The ... cause? The ... Oh. Fighting for the Pact. Yes. I'm afraid that I don't give those political issues much thought._
Then why did you come here?
He looks at you as if you are mad. _Why, the resources!_ He waves a hand at his massive workshop. _All this! All mine, for my beautiful work! My magical inventions will grant me immortality!_

_For centuries, they will speak of the incomparable genius of Craftmaster Nicodemus, while greater minds die forgotten in the mud because they never had such tools with which to express their genius._
Tell me more about your work.

He nods eagerly. _Yes. My work. Tools for the Hands. Weapons and trickery to help them escape danger and do the work of Avadon. I receive only the best of supplies. And I also have a wide variety of loyal and talented assistants, culled from all over Lynaeus._
Can you make weapons for me?
_I do little else. Of course, steel and fire are not the only weapons. The best weapons are those that help you to fully utilize your own cunning._
Or, reading between the lines, he makes whatever he wants and you try to find a way to make it help you.
And your equipment always works?

_Of course! Well, it always does something, anyway. Perhaps the results can be a bit unpredictable. But that is a small price to pay to have magical artifacts that have never existed before. Your enemies will always be surprised!_ And so, you suspect, will you.
Tell me about your assistants.

_Loyal and intelligent. Carefully screened to remove those likely to assassinate me. Always ready to help me to test new inventions._ You note that all of his assistants try to spend their time in the far end of the workshop, out of his sight.
_And, in my private workshop, I have other, more magically skilled and durable helpers._
_Ahhh ... It is not something I like to boast about. However, if you enter my private workshop, please do not remove their control collars. The results would be troublesome._
Can you teach me about enchantments?
_I would be happy to! Let me see the enchantment you have obtained._ He soon finds that you lack one. _Ahhhh ... Well, when you have one, please bring it to me and I will explain how to use it._

_I would be happy to! There exist crystals that are infused with raw magical energy. On the right sort of anvil, like this one ..._ He nods at his anvil. _You can transfer that energy into a weapon or piece of armor, infusing it with power._
He points to the east. _I will have an assistant unlock one of my storerooms. There is such a crystal in there. You may use it._
How do I use the enchantment?
_Place the piece of armor or weapon on this anvil. Place the crystal on the item. Smash the crystal. The magic of the anvil will bind the loose power into the equipment._
(To enchant an item, use the anvil. Detailed instructions will appear.)
Are there any limitations I should know about?

_Well, the crystal power is inherently raw and unstable. You can only place the power of one crystal in any item. And, once the item has been infused with power, that power is there to stay. It cannot be removed or replaced._
Do you have something for me for my next mission?

_I am so happy that you asked!_ He claps his hands and a wincing assistant brings you a pouch. You feel something moving inside. You open it and find a bunch of rat tails. They are still moving, writhing and twitching. Some of them still have bits of gore attached.
