_Oh, don't make that face. Those tails are infused with the life energy of entire rats. In battle, take a handful out and throw it onto the floor, and you will have an army at your disposal!_
_And that reminds me. Some time, you may wish to ask me about enchanting your equipment._
Do you have something for me for my next mission? I am returning to The Kva.

_Ah, The Kva. Never been. Sounds horrible._ He claps his hands. With a soft poofing sound, a terrified assistant suddenly appears next to him. She wears a pair of thick wool pants under her dress. She removes them, brushes them off, and hands them to you.
_A marvelous invention. They allow you to reposition yourself on the other side of a battlefield in an instant._
And can I control this movement?
_Of course you can! And, by that, I mean that you will. Soon. I am working hard on making that control possible._

_Indeed! I would like for you to be prepared, should you ever need to defend instead of attack._ He claps his hands. An assistant runs up, carrying a mundane-looking clay brick. He hands it to you as if he is happy to be rid of it, and then he runs off.
_That brick, if put in the proper position, will eventually become a wall. It grows! Granted, it may take some time. The speed of the enchantment is the next thing I am working on._

_Yes, a bit of alchemy for a change._ He claps his hands, and an assistant staggers up to you bearing a wine bottle. The young woman's eyes don't seem to be focusing properly. Nicodemus nods and she staggers off.

_The gremlins were fairy creatures, or so we are told. We haven't seen any sign of them for centuries. Legends say they made wine that could have amazing effects. I think I have been able to reproduce their lost recipe._
_When you drink this brew, it will fill you with great strength! And, perhaps, make you wobbly._

Nicodemus claps his hands. A servant approaches, holding a pouch at the far end of a long pair of tongs. He deposits the pouch directly into your hands. It is icy cold. You can't let it contact bare skin, for fear of frostbite.
You look inside. There are three short lengths of bone. _Break one of those,_ Nicodemus says, _And the power within will emerge to aid you. You can also use them to chill drinks._
Do you have something for me for my next mission? I am off to Kellemderiel.

_Of course._ He claps his hands. A small, warty wretch emerges from the shadows and hands you a wand. The moment the wand leaves his hands, he resumes the appearance of a young man. _Unique, yes? Perfect for infiltration._
_Of course, I don't know if you are planning to infiltrate anything. But, if you do, you have a way to infiltrate very well._
Ummm ... Can't you just make something to heal me or shoot fireballs or something?

_What? How mundane! And, of course, while I can make such crude tools, the other Hands grab them up right away when I do. You are simply receiving what is left. And this, I think, makes you the lucky one._

_Just one moment._ He claps his hands. There is a flash of light to the east. A bitter, burnt smell fills the workshop. An assistant bearing a scroll runs up to you, pausing only to extinguish her hair.

You take the scroll. _I suspect you want something that can summon a rain of lightning, yes? That is the sort of thing you Hands always want. And that spell will call limitless lightning from the sky. You are welcome._

Nicodemus looks grim. _I wish to help, but things have been ... difficult. I am told little, but there seem to be far fewer Hands available than there were a few weeks ago. This has meant that I have received fewer supplies._

An assistant, swathed in bandages, brings you a large flask. _This is all I have left to give you. It is a powerful strength potion. However, it has been known to cause ... cramping in those who imbibe it. I would not drink too much._
That is all I need.
_Then I will return to my work. So many Hands who need my help. So many assistants who need to help me test things. Excuse me ..._
This chamber is a small, crowded smithy. The air is hot and full of ash. Multiple chimneys suck the smoke out of the fortress to keep it from wafting down the halls.
There is a lone smith manning the forge. He is a short, stocky man with a deeply tanned complexion. You suspect that he is from The Kva. He grimaces as you enter.

_Another Hand come for supplies? Well, I'll do what I can, but I make no promises. I am Smith Duman._ He reaches out to shake your hand. As he does, his glove pulls away from his hand, revealing that it has been branded with a 'T'.
Smith Duman continues to work in the smithy. He divides his time between repairing blades and plate armor and organizing the goods left behind by the quartermaster.
He has been getting little sleep. He stumbles clumsily back and forth across the room as he works, grimacing and muttering obscenities.
Can I get some supplies?
_Of course. I'm the acting quartermaster now. Why not ask me? But first, I need to hear from Heart Miranda that you can be supplied. You should go and talk to her._
Heart Miranda sent me to see you.
_Of course she did. I am the quartermaster for now. As if I didn't have enough to do. She probably wants me to give you a scarab too. I only have one left, but you can have it._
You aren't normally the quartermaster?

_Me? One of the finest smiths in Lynaeus? Of course not! But then wretches killed the old quartermaster, and everyone has been too distracted to replace him. So Miranda gave me the touch. You'll be trading with me for what you need._
A scarab?

_Yes, a scarab._ He removes a piece of jewelry from a pouch. It is, indeed, a small metal scarab, on a thin chain. Its six legs end in needle points. _This is Avadon magic. Powerful. Only we can use it._
Its legs look ... sharp.
_Of course. You wear it under your armor. The legs dig in, and the magic goes deep within your being. Don't wince. Many in the Farlands would kill for the power they bring._
What sort of power do they give?
_They can make you stronger. Or faster. They can give you magical powers. Scarabs will sustain you no matter how far you get from Avadon or how many foes attack you._
_I should know. I've made many of them._
I'll take the scarab.

He hands it to you reverently. _There it is. When you wear it, it grabs on. Nobody can steal it. However, you can only take it off or put it on in the safety of Avadon. Anywhere else, it won't let itself be stolen._
_And a warning. Don't wear too many. You need to be strong to withstand their power. They give, but they also take._
(You can currently equip one scarab. You can equip one more for each seven levels you gain. You can only equip or remove them when on the main floor of Avadon.)
Can I trade with you?
He nods. _That is what I am forced to do, until they bother to find a new quartermaster. Which won't happen until things are under control again. Which could take weeks._
_You can sell things to me that you find in the field. In return, I will sell you new, quality equipment. Even scarabs, when I can get them._
What exactly has been going on?
_I'll tell you exactly what they told me._ And then he stands there silently. You get the point.
Wait. You will buy and sell me things? I am a Hand! Why don't you just give equipment to me?

_Oh, how many times Hands have given that little speech. To answer your question, it is Redbeard's orders. Avadon has great resources, but great responsibilities as well. We don't have near as much as we should._
_So Redbeard will make you earn your keep._
Earn my keep how?

_When you are on a mission, you may keep what treasure you find. If someone hires you to do something, as long as it does not hurt the Pact or keep you from your duties, you can keep what you earn. And you can trade what you find back to me._
_Would you rather hand everything you find to me and then settle for what I give you back? I thought not._
Let me see what you have for sale.
_All right. I think I have sorted through everything enough to trade properly. I have arms and weapons, supplies, and scarabs._
_Also, I have managed to locate a few valuable items. Most of them have been brought back by the other Hands. The ones that survived, anyway._
I want to buy arms and armor.
You conclude your business.
Avadon has access to the finest weaponry and supplies. However, it doesn't just hand them out. All Hands have to earn quality equipment.
I want to buy supplies.
I want to buy scarabs.
I want to buy quality goods.
I don't need anything else.
_All right. Since you don't need anything else, can I get back to work?_
I have something I want to sell.
You conclude your business. (To buy back items you have sold, tell Smith Duman that you would like to buy supplies.)
I'd like to know more about you.
_You would? I suppose that is friendly of you, though I am too busy for such talk._ He absent-mindedly scratches the back of his right hand, where you saw the 'T' brand earlier.
_I am from The Kva. I came here to use my skills to serve the Pact. It is a great honor that Redbeard took me in. There is little else I can say._
I am constantly being sent out. Can I get more supplies?
He sighs. _I have heard that you are sent out a lot. But you keep coming back, which leaves you better off than the other Hands. From what I hear._
_I will have one of the side chambers in the main supply room unlocked for you. You can take what you find inside. The Hands those items were being held for ... They won't need them now._
Tell me about The Kva.

_It is a harsh land, but it is beautiful. But then, I hear you will be spending time there. Do not let its roughness distract you. There is such ... such beauty there. My family is there, and I am glad for them._
Tell me about them.
_I would rather not. Suffice it to say that they are well. Growing. Moving on._
I would like to learn more about it.
_I believe there is a book on The Kva by the southern portal. It was left there to inform Hands and Eyes who were assigned to travel there. Proper preparation, and all that._
How did you get that 'T' brand?
His back stiffens. _I do not discuss it. And, were I you, I would learn to be a little more polite when dealing with those in Avadon. You can't afford to make enemies._
Can you tell me about that 'T' brand?
His back stiffens slightly. Then he sighs. _Perhaps you should learn more of my land. You spend enough time there. However, I would not discuss it right now. I have much work to do._
You have a mark on your hand.

His shoulders slump. You can see how exhausted he is, working alone in this workshop until he is on the edge of collapse. He pulls back the leather of his glove, revealing the ugly, red brand. The 'T' standing out angrily against his dark flesh.
_I was branded in The Kva. Branded and banished. I am a criminal there. I can never return._
_I was a very talented smith. I earned many fine commissions, though I lacked the acumen to turn them into wealth. I have a fine family, two sons and two daughters._
_And then my youngest son fell ill. Gravely ill. Mundane medicine would not help. He required magical assistance. A potion._
And you could not afford it?

_No. So I stole it, and I treated my son. In the middle of the night, I watched the color return to his cheeks. But I was as poor a thief as I was a man of business. The guard came and hauled me away before the sun came up._
_I was sent before a judge, there to answer to the Stone Code._

_I was threatened with death, or the loss of a hand. But, as the Code is harsh, it is also just. The judge was allowed to hear my full tale. He chose to be merciful. I was only branded a thief before my family and banished. For life._
That is horribly unjust.
_No. the Stone Code is harsh, yes, but just. Even, from time to time, merciful. The Code sustains The Kva, that land that I love, and every day I work to protect it._
The Stone Code sounds very just.

_Yes. Harsh, but just. Even, from time to time, merciful. Some nights, I remember my wife and think that I should have lost my life. But no. The Code sustains The Kva, that land that I love, and every day I work to protect it._
And you came to Avadon?
_It seemed the best way to use my services to protect the Pact, and thus my homeland. It was a long walk, but Redbeard was kind enough to take me in at the end of it._
And have you seen your family since?
_No. I fear I will never see them again. Happily, my position here gives me some influence. I have made sure that they are looked after and protected. And they will be._
_But only as long as they follow the Stone Code. If they turn from it, I turn from them._
_And now, I thank you for easing my solitude. But I must return to work. And so, I think, must you._
I need nothing else.
_Then we must return to work. The Pact requires for all of us to do all we can to keep the savages of the Farlands at bay._
A middle-aged woman crosses the courtyard back and forth, shouting orders to the soldiers and workers. As Hands enter and leave, she grabs them and gives them extra jobs to do.
She wears a well-worn bow over her shoulder, and the insignia on her shoulder shows her to have considerable authority.

She looks you over. _A new Hand. Always good to see, especially in times like these. I am Hand Callan. Heart Miranda will want most of your time, I think, but when she doesn't have her claws in you, you answer to me._

Hand Callan continues to tirelessly roam the halls of Avadon, looking for anyone who seems the least bit idle and putting them to work. She occasionally looks at you wistfully. _There's much I could have you do, but Miranda has reserved you. What do you need of me?_

She laughs. _Cleaning up messes. Why don't you come back and talk to me later? Miranda has made it clear that she reserves your labor for herself, and I don't need an argument right now. Go talk to her._
Callan returns to work.
Can I talk to you?
_Hmmm?_ She looks over at you. _I suppose so. I think you've had time to settle in._ She shakes your hand. _[N], is it? Good to meet you._
_I am the head Hand here. Redbeard says so. When you aren't following the orders of him or the Hearts, you will answer to me. Though, the way things are looking, you will be busy for some time._
_I know everything about the Hands, including the ones that have been assigned to help you. What do you want to know?_
_I was raised in the wide fields of the Wyldrylm, to the west. Wild, free lands. I was part of a proud tribe, that has long fought the Corruption for the good of the Pact._
_But that was not enough for me. I was the finest archer in our tribe. I decided to put my skills to use here._
What is the Corruption?
_A blasted land of crags, peaks, and monstrosities. A lesson to all why it is important for Avadon to bring mad wizards to heel as quickly as possible._
_Fortunately, it's not much of a bother. The occasional horror slithers out, and we fill it with arrows. Nothing we cannot defeat._
Why did you leave your homeland?
She shrugs. _I miss the fields and woods, I suppose, but the simple truth is this. Unlike most of my people, I have developed a taste for cities. Love them, in fact._
What are your duties here?
_I look after the Hands. When Redbeard needs some of them for one of his jobs, he talks to me directly. When he suspects disloyalty, he asks me to find it._
_I spend a lot of time dealing with him directly. More than most. Enough to earn a nickname._
What is your nickname?
_They say that I am one of his three wives, along with Heart Miranda and Eye Leira. They hate the name. It just makes me laugh._
You look for disloyalty?
Her smile fades. _Any Hand can turn out to be an assassin. Any Hand can grow weak and sell out the Pact for a big enough bribe. And, when they do, Redbeard counts on me to uncover the crime._
_And I do. If you ever suspect treachery, I am the one you must tell._
Tell me more about Redbeard.
_Everyone fears him. It is terribly unjust, since none do more or fight more fiercely to help the people of the Pact sleep securely in our beds._
_I have nothing to fear from him. You know why? Because I am loyal, and I fight for right. Follow my example, and you need not fear either._
I want to talk about what has been happening lately.
She looks unsettled. _Understandable. It is a difficult time, with one disaster following another. It does happen._
_Though I admit I am becoming very suspicious._

_There was an accident in one of the towers. A pulse of magic disrupted much of Avadon. At the same time, there was an unusual amount of trouble in the Farlands. Most of our Hands had to be sent away._
Tell me about the accident.
_One of the towers was used to imprison creatures of interest. Usually the results of magical experimentation, or monsters that wandered out of the Corruption._
_They were held in place with runes of power._
Tell me about this tower.
_The stairs up to it are near your quarters and Miranda's office._
She notes the amulet around your neck. _You do not yet have authority to enter it._

_Nobody knows for sure. There was a pulse of power. The runes burned themselves out. The keepers died. The wave of energy disrupted spells all over Avadon. Beasts escaped. The dungeons were disrupted._
What caused the problem?
_It is a mystery._ She looks quite unsettled. _It is worrying._
She notes the amulet around your neck. _Should you be given the authority to enter the tower, I would be interested in your opinion._
I have been up there.
_I see. And what did you think?_
I don't know anything about that sort of magic.
She nods. _An honest response. No matter. I have spoken with the Eyes. They will soon approach the truth of the matter._
_What else did you wish to discuss?_
I'm not sure, but I suspect it was a simple accident.
_A sensible response. Sane people do not see conspiracies in every corner. But then, Avadon is not a place for the sane._
I'm not an expert, but I don't see how such a thing just happens.

_You and I have much in common, I think. Sane people do not see conspiracies in every corner. But then, Avadon is not a place for the sane. No matter. I have spoken with the Eyes. They will soon approach the truth of the matter._
What sort of disruptions have been happening?
_The normal things. Riots. Conspiracies against the Pact. People of the Pact not being treated with due respect in the Farlands. Monster infestations._
You aren't concerned about this extra activity from the enemy?
_Not really. Busy times are not unusual. Sometimes, more things go wrong._
_Though it is always alarming when it happens._
Things are still not under control?
_No. I confess we are having more difficulties with the forces we are meeting than I expected. But ... I think we will be victorious soon._
And all of the Hands are still away?
_No. The distractions continue. As soon as they come back, they must be sent off again._
She seems unsettled. _That is, when we have Hands to send._

_The activity by itself does not concern me. However, we are suffering casualties. Monster ambushes. Intense riots. Even the isolated poisoning. Loyal Hands, ones that have served for years, are not returning._
_But this is a matter for me and Redbeard. All I can say is that you should be very cautious._
Can we discuss my companions?
She nods. _Of course. You often will not be able to choose who you work with. However, I am here to make it easier to fight alongside these unexpected allies._
_I would like to know anything unusual that happens in your dealings with them. After all, they may not necessarily be those I would choose to work with you._
Why wouldn't you choose them?
She seems nervous. _Some Hands don't settle into life at Avadon as well as others. Some of them may have ... qualities or opinions that give them a difficult time here._
What does that have to do with the Hands available to me?

_The trials we have faced may have left behind a greater concentration of ..._ She shakes her head. _Actually, never mind. They have the full backing of Avadon. They will serve the cause of the Pact well._ She obviously has nothing else to say on this topic.
You want me to report on my fellow warriors?

_Of course I do. You think I'm ashamed to say it? The Pact is ever threatened. Assassins and traitors are everywhere. These are facts. If you have reason to suspect one of your allies threatens Avadon, it is your duty to say so._
Sevilin left to hunt the bandits who attacked his patrol.
She nods. _This is in his rights as a Hand of Avadon. They attacked our warriors. Retribution is right and just. Is there anything else we should know about it?_
We managed to track down Cahil. The matter is settled.
You tell her what happened. _I hope that you have made peace with what you learned. We would be unhappy if any of our Hands ... found reason to resent us. Thank you for this report._
Sevilin is annoyed with Redbeard for pardoning Cahil.

_I see. All Hands know that their work here has risks, and we all sometimes need to make sacrifices for the greater good. Thank you for letting us know about this. We will do what we can to relieve his concerns._
Shima left Avadon to hunt down those who betrayed his family.
She nods. _We had suspected this. He was absent. Certain battles occurred. We are not unobservant._
She looks at you intently. _And tell me. Did Shima learn anything unusual during his exertions?_
Not that I know of. He is now content.
She seems relieved. _If he is content, then we are as well. Holklandan politics can be a bloody business. As long as it does not threaten the Pact, we do not interfere._
He learned that Redbeard favors his enemies, the Honored Forge. He is upset about it.

_I ... see. That is untrue, of course. I don't see why Redbeard would care to favor one Holklandan clan over another. I will take steps to make sure Shima's doubts about us are put to rest. Thank you for letting us know about this._
He learned that Redbeard aided in the attack on his family. He is quite angry about it.

_I ... see. That isn't true, of course. I don't see why Redbeard would worry himself over such a minor Holklandan conflict. I will take steps to make sure Shima's doubts about us are put to rest. Thank you for letting us know about this._
Jenell slipped away from Avadon to help some warriors of the Wyldrylm.
_Ah, yes. We had wondered where she went to. Our information about happenings in the Wyldrylm can be faulty._
_And, when you were there, did you learn anything about the tribesfolk she aided?_
They were poor and isolated in enemy territory. She helped to rescue them. That is all I know.
_Really? And you know nothing of the reason they were hiding out there, far from the safety of the Pact and Avadon? I am surprised that you learned nothing else._
_But I will be content with your tale, and I will hope that Jenell is content as well._
She was protecting them from the justice of Avadon.

_Well, that would explain why they were hiding. Sometimes, the tribesfolk attack Pact soldiers. When I get the chance, I will speak with Jenell and try to make her see the sense inherent in our laws._
_Thank you for bringing this problem to me. It should be corrected._
Nathalie left Avadon to hunt down a drake. I had to rescue her.
_Of course. Nathalie. Always eager to fight. Sometimes overeager. Occasionally even maddening in her persistence and impatience._
_But the drake was a foe, and she did well to remove it. Is there anything else I should know?_
Only that she is content to serve Avadon as best she can.
Callan seems unconvinced. _Really? That means that she has gained great wisdom. And shed an enormous amount of ambition. Thank you for letting us know._
She seems even angrier and more ambitious than before.
_Yes. Ambitious. A word everyone uses to describe her. And a dangerous quality to have in Avadon. But I will speak with her. Perhaps, as she ages and her wound heals, calm will return. We will see._
_Thank you for letting us know._
I have nothing to say about them.
She nods. _Understandable. But I hope, when you learn more, you will confide in me._
Is there anything I can do for you?
_I am always happy when enterprising Hands offer themselves for extra work. I know Miranda keeps you busy, but there is a small task that I would like done. It will take very little time._

_We have an envoy from the Tawon Empire. Name is Brasula. She has been here for some time. More than usual. Since the Tawon Empire is an old foe of the Pact, this requires attention. I would like for you to search her quarters and see if you can find any evidence of spying or other such behavior._
Where are her quarters?
_She is staying in the lower guest quarters, under the main dining hall._
Will she mind if I search her quarters?
_She is of the Farlands, not the Pact. She has no choice but to accept it. Remember our principles. The Stone Wall Beyond._
_However, it might be wise to do the search when she is not actually present._
I searched Brasula's room. There was nothing suspicious.
_Really? Interesting. This means that she must be very good at hiding evidence of her guilt._
Perhaps she is innocent.
She laughs. _Nobody is innocent. Especially diplomats from the Farlands. But do not worry. You have been useful. And you should be rewarded._
She removes a scarab from her pouch and hands it to you. _Thank you for your help. I may need more assistance in the future._
I'm sure you are right. I can continue to investigate.
She laughs. _I appreciate your eagerness, but this is now work for the Eyes. You did well. You should be rewarded._
Do you need more help?
_Not yet. I am still continuing my own investigation. Return and speak with me later._

_I am sad to say that I do. I am continuing the investigation of the troubles in the dungeons. A valuable prisoner, Shadow Tarkus, was lost. I want to give you access to the lower cells. I think that he may be there._
Where are the lower cells?
_Descend to the dungeons once again, and go east._
How can I enter the lower cells?
She removes a key from her pouch and hands it to you. _This is quite a privilege. Most Hands never get such access._
Tell me about Shadow Tarkus.

_A truly valuable prisoner. A skilled infiltrator and spy, who will do anything for a price. But he only works for the Farlands and against Avadon. Quite an eccentric. We were learning valuable things from his mind._
_But now he is gone, and we want him back. We have been unable to find any signs of where he fled to, which makes me suspect that he is hiding right under our feet._
Tell me about the lower cells.

_They were destroyed by an earthquake about forty years ago and allowed to become a haven for mold and pests. And, I suspect, escapees from the dungeon. Search them and see if Tarkus is there. Then report to me what you have learned._
I thoroughly searched the lower cells. Shadow Tarkus is not there.
_Ah. Disappointing. Though at least you managed to reduce the pest population down there. The hunt will continue elsewhere. Thank you for your help._
She gives you another scarab. _That is one of the first scarabs I earned when I was but a new Hand. You have great promise. Wear it well._
Is there anything else I can do for you?
_The way things are going? I don't doubt it. Return to me later. For now, I must investigate. Something is amiss in the Pact, and I am determined to uncover it._
I saw something suspicious in the quarters of Valna.
You instantly have Callan's full attention. _Really? What did you discover?_
Uhhh ... Nothing I can be sure of. I will continue to investigate.
_That seems wise. It is not a good thing to prematurely punish the envoys of other states. Be sure to keep me informed when you learn something definite._
Valna has been buying information from Admes.
_Admes ... Admes ... Ah. I remember. One of the stewards. Shifty fellow. I will make sure that he is swiftly punished for this treason._
_And, as for Valna, she will be watched closely. However, she was only doing what envoys from the Farlands do. Such treachery is in their nature._
She gives you a pouch of coins and a pat on the shoulder. _Very well done. The spy will be made an example of. Excuse me._ She walks off.
_Back to the hunt, then. This is a dark time, but, with courage, we will defeat the enemies of the Pact._
There is an aging man here in the garden, walking around and enjoying the flora. This is a courtyard, so you are surrounded by cool, fresh mountain air. He inhales it deeply.

Then he turns to you and frowns. _Ah, a Hand. I am only enjoying what I do not usually get. I am Abi, representative of The Kva._ The Kva is a harsh desert land, so you can see why all of this greenery has an appeal.

Abi of The Kva continues to wander the garden, closely inspecting all of the different plants and insects. Even the weeds hold a fascination for him. He is aware of your presence, though he does little to acknowledge it.
This is a lovely garden.
_Yes._ He pauses to sniff a flower.
You are from The Kva?
_I am. I am spending six months here. Then I will return._
Can you tell me more about The Kva?
_I am a poor teacher._
Why six months?
He admires a praying mantis as it consumes its prey. _Then I will be replaced by another._
Why are you here?
_As a representative._
For?
_The Kva._
How do you represent them?

He sighs, realizing that his efforts to avoid conversation are coming to naught. _The Kva, from time to time, needs help dealing with outsiders. Needs help Avadon can provide. So they send requests to me. I pass them on to your Hearts and Hands._
Is this a prestigious post?
_Yes. Quite luxurious and well-paid. If I am not assassinated, I will be pleased to have served this term._
How does Avadon respond to your inquiries?
_Generally with great indifference._
What sort of things do you ask for?
_Usually help managing the wretches and the titans. And, of course, protecting us against the swindles and offenses of our so-called allies in the Pact._
And can I help you?
He seems surprised. _A warrior of Avadon, offering to help? This is a surprise._
_Yes, you can help. Finding out who is selling weaponry to the wretches will directly help the Pact._

_If you ever happen to find yourself in Goldcrag, there is a man living outside of it. His name is Tartam. I believe he is acting against the Pact. You should deal with him the way ... the way Avadon does._
What is Tartam doing?
_Wretches are the eternal plague of The Kva, and we believe that this Tartam person is selling weapons to them. Avadon acts delightfully decisively toward those who would arm the Farlands._
And what do you want me to do?
_Train the gaze of Avadon upon him. Death to foes of the Pact. And so on._
Why don't you deal with him?

_We of The Kva follow the Stone Code, which limits what the leaders of smaller towns may do without proof. If the head of a province was available and willing, Tartam could be crushed in a moment. No proof needed. However, they lack the influence._
I have spoken with Tartam. Someone is selling arms to the wretches, but it is not him.
_I see. And I suppose you will provide no more information than this? I thought not._
_We of The Kva reward those who aid us. If you can uncover these traitors, you will be rewarded._
I found out who was selling arms to the wretches. It is no longer a problem.
_I see. Nobody can escape the gaze of Avadon, once it has been drawn. I give you the thanks of The Kva. Oh, and payment. The Hands must be paid._
He gives you a large pouch of coins and a delicate, gold signet ring.
_I have been told that, in your current difficulties, I should not take up any more of your time. It is unwise to ignore the will of Avadon._
There is a tall, elegant woman sitting at this table. She wears a long, flowing dress that must have been fantastically expensive. She sips wine and reads a scroll.

When you approach, she stands and bows. _Always best to be polite to the warriors of our masters. We have learned, if nothing else, to be humble. I am Envoy Brasula, of the Tawon Empire._ She sits down and reclaims her goblet of wine.
Envoy Brasula sits and sips her wine. The diplomat from the Tawon Empire makes everything around her, even the splendor of Avadon, seem a bit shabby by her mere presence.
She gives a tiny, enigmatic half-smile. _What else do you need, warrior of the Pact?_
I need to search your quarters.
She arches an eyebrow. _Really? I appreciate the honesty. Though I confess, I am surprised you Hands haven't pawed through all of my possessions already._
_I will make sure that the door is unlocked for you. Please feel free to do what you will, although I would appreciate it if you do not overly handle my garments. It has been a problem._
I would like to speak with you.
_And I with you. We of the Tawon Empire always want to deal with Avadon. However, at this point, I only have work for you if you travel to the Beraza Woods._
I don't.
She sighs. _Not unusual. Well, I wish you the best of travels, but there is no profit in further conversation for either of us._ She returns to her scroll.
I am able to go there.
She sets down her scroll, her interest piqued. _Indeed? Well, I may have work for you. The Tawon Empire may be old and weak, but some wealth remains in our dusty vaults._
Tell me more about the Tawon Empire.
_Well, if you would like to learn more, there is a book on it in my quarters. I'm sure some of Avadon's agents have already been in there._ She winks.
_But what to add? We are an old power, dusty and tired, held down under the boot of those we once ruled. Your Pact, young and energetic._
You don't seem so bitter about it.
_Why should I be? Empires rise and fall. Avadon was built. And, one day, it will crumble. The Pact is young, and our Empire is old. That age has given us a certain perspective._
The Empire used to rule over us?
_The Tawon Empire used to rule most of Lynaeus. Thus the word 'Empire.' We grew old and complacent, and we lost those lands. But we have memories. And ambitions._
What do you think of the Pact?

_A young, energetic power. Very successful, and very full of itself. But you are only a century from a gruesome civil war, and your five nations are constantly at each other's throats. The Tawon Empire will outlast you._
You may have a point.
She nods. _Of course. If more gain your wisdom and vision, you may have hope. But I do not think this will happen. Did you wish to discuss something else?_
You have no right to judge us, Farlander.
_Ahhh ... Open Arms Within, Stone Wall Beyond, yes? We will see how far that takes you in the cauldron that is our world. Did you wish to discuss something else?_
You come here to hire Hands? But you aren't part of the Pact.
_Of course. That makes it more important to hire your kind, not less. We do all we can to avoid the anger of Avadon._
What do you hire our kind to do?

_Anything that keeps your armies from attacking us. Assassinating malcontents. Aiding us with the bureaucracies of the Pact. A variety of small sorts of assistance. Many great old fortunes have been used to bribe the Pact._
What would the Pact do to the Tawon Empire?

_You have incredible power. Invasion and assassination, but more than that. Tariffs. Shutting off our trade. Seizing our ships. Claiming pieces of land. The Pact has devised many ways to torment us over the centuries._
_But I am not bitter. The wheel turns. Powers rise. And fall._
What sort of work do you have for me?
_It is a perfect job for a Hand of Avadon. Paying you handsomely to do what you should already do._
_There is a pack of bandits in the Beraza Woods, led by a Dharamite named Eudor. They have been raiding our lands. We want them to stop. We will pay very well if you get them to._
Why can't you kill them?
_Because if we sent any soldiers over the border in the Pact, we would be savagely punished. And thus, we have to pay you._
Tell me more about the bandits.
_They hide in the Beraza Woods, land that the Pact is unable to properly control. Thus, they cross our borders, raid, and return with impunity._
_They think having those woods to hide in protects them. We will prove them wrong._
Why should Avadon get involved?
_Apart from the payment I will give you for success? Eudor is acting to disrupt the peace and aggravate the Empire. Stopping him is very much in the interest of Avadon._ She does have a point.
Eudor will bother you no longer.
You tell the tale to Brasula. She is pleased.
_I had not realized how satisfying news of his death would be. It is money well spent. Especially since it is not my money._
_I had wished fervently for his death, but his terror will have to do._
She gives you a hefty pouch of gold and coins. _We are grateful, and we may have even more lucrative work for you._
Is there anything else you will pay me to do?
_Hrmmm._ She looks you over. _Perhaps when you are more experienced. No offense._

_In fact, there is. There is a mage named Herenus hiding deep in the Beraza Woods. He is an exile of the Tawon Empire. He needs to return. Find him and tell him that, 'Your clan has a golden throne.' Very simple message, and you will be paid well._
Where is he?
_Somewhere in the Beraza Woods. No idea where. If he is still alive. Nobody has seen him for twenty years. Perhaps he has a different name. Or face._
Why is he wanted? And what does that message mean?
_I do not know. Some noble in the Tawon Empire wanted this done. They sent me the task and the fee and asked me to find a Hand. My part of the job has ended._
I found Herenus.
You tell her what happened. _How interesting._
_He says he won't go. Don't believe him. None resist the chance to return from exile._
_And he will even return. The nobles will be so pleased that I'm sure they will pay me more for my aid._
_And your reward._ She gives you another pouch of gold coins and a beautiful ring. _A gift from the Tawon Empire._
Anything else that needs to be done?
_Perhaps. Maybe soon. When your fortress has solved all of the little problems that are aggravating it. Which I am sure will happen soon._
Good day to you.
She happily returns to her scroll. _And to you. What civilization there is in Avadon, I will enjoy it._

There is an old woman wandering among the library shelves. She inspects everything intently, swooping in instantly to correct anything that is out of place. She may seem unsteady on her feet, but when she sees a scroll in the wrong position on a shelf she is all action.

Then she sees you. First, she inspects your hands to make sure that you aren't about to get grime on her precious tomes. Then she says, in a whispery voice, _Ah, a Hand. Haven't seen many of you in here over the last few weeks._
_I am Eye Leira, head librarian. I hope you are here to assist me._
Eye Leira speaks with you, her voice never rising above a whisper. As you talk, something about her seems strangely disconnected. It is as if she has to concentrate carefully to interact with people.
Tell me about the library.
She looks at the impeccably ordered lines of books with pride. _The library of Avadon is the envy of Lynaeus, the finest accumulation of information in the known lands._
Is this really all of the books you have?
There is a long pause. She stares at a shelf. Then she remembers that you are there. _What? This paltry collection? No, this is just the works I felt had immediate interest._
_The tower above us has the deep stacks, a collection of works ten times the size of what you see here._
There are no better libraries anywhere?
She smiles faintly. _There were, especially in the Tawon Empire. Then my Eyes got to them._
Why does Avadon need such a library?
Her voice is flat, as if reciting a speech memorized long ago. _The job of Avadon is to protect the Pact. It does so by watching all lands for threats._
_We cannot see a threat without understanding the people. We cannot understand the many people of Lynaeus without the knowledge here._
What sort of books do you keep?

_We keep what we need to understand the cultures. Not just histories, but legends and tales. Works of etiquette. Language studies. If you need to understand Svorgald, or The Kva, or the sources of the Corruption, you come here._
And I can take out any book I want?
Eye Leira finally shows an emotion: horror. _Of course not. The Hands would only destroy my valuable tomes. Only Hearts and the Keeper himself may take works from the library._
Do Hands ever recover works for you?

Eye Leira smiles. _They try, but they tend to be damaged and dirty and useless. However, if you find any papers of magical interest in your travels, we would accept them for inspection. And reimburse you for the effort._
_I do realize how Hands hate to do anything for free._
I have found some papers with notes on magic. (Give them.)
Eye Leira takes the papers and inspects them. _Excellent. If there is new magical research, we want it to be under our control._ She has an assistant fetch a pouch of coins for you.
_Also, since you have actually contributed something to the knowledge of the library, I have a personal repayment for you._ She gives you a scarab.
How long have you served in Avadon?
There is a long pause, long enough to make you wonder if she heard the question. Then she says, _I have been in Avadon for almost fifty years, almost as long as Redbeard._
_I have served him for ... for ... a long time. Long enough to earn my title._ She smiles wryly. _He likes having me around. He likes that I tell my story._

_I am from Holklanda, though I have been here for so long that I barely remember it. It is a proud place, and some there resent the power Avadon has over it._ She stops speaking for a moment. _But I am telling my tale unbidden now._
What is your title?
_They call me one of Redbeard's wives. A joke that I never found funny in the slightest._
Will you tell me your story?
_Of course. I came here from Holklanda with two others, both Hands. Our goal was to assassinate Redbeard. We settled in as best we could, learned the workings of the fortress, and waited._
Why are you telling me this?
Her eyes betray no emotion. _Because it is part of my purpose here. As a librarian, I educate. This story teaches the futility of opposing Redbeard._
Why did you want to kill Redbeard?
_Because some in Holklanda hated the power an outsider had over them. They are all long gone now. It has been so long that I can remember few of the details._
_He found out. He always finds out. I imagine he suspected us from the beginning. So we were taken to the dungeons._
What did they do to you?

_They read all contained within our minds, and used it. They did not touch our bodies. They did not need to. Then Redbeard came to me personally. He knew that I was broken. He offered me this post, as a servant and living example. I accepted._
And your two companions?
_They would never submit. They were true believers. They were executed. The bodies were burned, and their ashes returned to Holklanda._
And you have served here ever since?
_Yes. Unharmed, except that the reading of my mind left me ... disconnected. Or maybe it was not the reading. Maybe I have been broken by the knowledge of my failure, my surrender._
_It does not matter. I became a new person, a servant of Avadon. Comfortable and loyal. There is no point in ever opposing Redbeard. That is the lesson, and my tale is done._
_How else can I help you?_
I have learned something about you. You are the one who betrayed your companions.

Eye Leira looks away. _Yes. It is true. Redbeard allows me to keep that part out of my stories. I hated Redbeard and the power of Avadon. Sometimes I still do. But my fear was greater. So I confessed the plan to the Hearts, though I am sure they would have found out anyway._
_But I am still broken, still obedient, and nobody doubts otherwise. Now excuse me. I must return to work._ She turns and walks away from you.
You said that you need assistance?
_Yes, and the Hands have been unable to help me so far. I understand, in fact, that you are one of the few Hands left actually in Avadon._

_The recent disturbances in the fortress released several beasts that were under study. Some of them have taken up residence in our stacks, keeping us from obtaining needed tomes. Would you kindly destroy them?_
What do you know about the creatures?
_They are skeletons. We are Eyes, not warriors. Simply go upstairs and strike them until they no longer move. We would be happy to clean up the mess when you are finished._
I am too busy to help you.
_Then I am too busy to speak with you. Until we receive aid, however, we will be unable to provide Avadon with the knowledge it needs. This may have consequences. Excuse me._ She turns and walks off.
I will help you.
She nods. _Then I will have the door to the tower unlocked for you. Let me know when it is safe for my scribes to ascend._
I have destroyed the unliving creatures in the stacks.
_Then, at last, our library can function properly. I thank you for your help. I will reward you with the magic of Avadon._ She removes a scarab from a pouch and hands it to you.
_You seem to have promise, and there is always much that must be done. Perhaps the Eyes will have profitable work for you later._
She thinks. _Nothing that would justify the effort and the price. Perhaps later._
Is there anything I can do for you now?
For once, Eye Leira seems interested and engaged. _For some time now, we have been trying to obtain a copy of a very rare tome of magic called the Krysanth. We have had no luck. This angers me._
_I understand that you have been in the tower of a wizard in Khemeria. He had a magical library of some quality. Perhaps he has a copy of this book._
_I wish you to return to his tower and search for it. I can give you something that will help you to pierce any magical defenses._
What is the Krysanth?
_That is what is so maddening. I am not sure. All I know is that it is very rare and greatly in demand, and those who obtain it gain power rapidly. Often in a way threatening to the Pact._
Where in the tower should I look?

_Anywhere where there are books. Especially any chambers you were unable to explore earlier due to the wizard's defenses. From what I have learned of his capabilities, I suspect he has a number of tomes of note._
What can you give me?

She sends a scribe into the stacks. He soon returns, reverently bearing something wrapped in velvet. He hands the item to you. You unwrap it and find a small dagger, razor-sharp and etched with runes.
_It is a runed athame, an enchanted dagger that can cut through tendrils of magic in the air. If a door is held closed with runic magic, that blade will sever it._
Here is the Krysanth. (Give it to her.)

The moment she sees the tome, her hands fly out and grab it. Her arms are surprisingly strong. _Yes. After so many years. So much knowledge. So much potential. I can feel it._ She runs her fingers lovingly over the black leather.

She sends a scribe to get your reward, delivered in a leather pouch. It is a jeweled scarab and a small collection of precious stones. _I will record your service. For centuries, the archivists of Avadon will remember your valiant efforts._
_Now ... Now I must study. So many questions, about to be answered ..._ She wanders off.
What have you learned about the Krysanth?
_What have I learned? I ... I ... It is still so early to say. It is a complicated tome. Each page will take ... weeks to decipher. Yes. But we are prepared to make a presentation in time._
_Is there? Perhaps. I have not thought on it. I have been ... occupied. Return later. Perhaps there will be more to do._
_Is it? Yes. Well. I will return to work._ She wanders off.

You meet a tall, swarthy woman, well over six feet tall and heavily muscled. Politeness is not important to her. She quickly brushes past you, as if she did not see you. Or as if she wants to avoid you.

There is a tall, swarthy woman sitting at this table, writing a letter and drinking ale. She is well over six feet tall and heavily muscled. She would look very comfortable with an axe in her hand, if Farlanders were allowed to carry blades in Avadon.
She looks at you with irritation. _I am Valna of Svorgald. And you are a Hand. Sorry. Not buying aid today. Leave me be._
Valna is sitting at her table, drinking and writing. She does her best to ignore you.
If she has any concern about your knowledge of her spying, she does a masterful job of concealing it.
Tell me about Svorgald.

She leans back in her chair and frowns. _I suppose it is my duty to tell people of our land. We are warriors of the sea, off the east coast of Lynaeus. Feared and envied by the weak and sensitive souls of Dharam._
And you are part of the Farlands.
_If you say so. I understand that is your term for those too brave and independent to bow and scrape before the Pact._
Warriors of the sea?
_We are. Our ships and our mariners are unmatched. We can go where we will, take what we will._
So 'Warrior of the Sea' is another term for 'pirate.'
_Call us what you will. We were the sea's masters. And we will be again, when your Pact returns to civil war._
And you are an envoy here?
_I am. But I do not bribe your warriors to murder in the night. When lies are told about us, I am here to answer them. No more._
I saw papers in your room. You are spying on us.

If you expected any shock at your accusation, you are disappointed. She is unsurprised and unrepentant. _That may be the case. Svorgald is isolated now in the face of the Pact. We learn what we can to survive._
Spies will be punished.
_I fear nothing Avadon can do to me._ You can see in her eyes that she speaks the truth.
For a fee, this can be forgotten.
Valna does not move. _I will not bribe a Hand, especially one who has been snuffling around in my private things. Report me or not. It does not matter. Now leave me._
I should turn you in.
_Yes. You should. Go and do what you choose. I will not beg or grovel, and I fear nothing Avadon can do. I only acted to help my people. Now leave me._
I want to discuss something else.
_When I need to speak for my people, I will speak with you. Until then, I will be left alone._ She returns to her scroll, ignoring you.
You meet one of Avadon's stewards in the hallway. He runs past you, making a show of being in a great hurry. Odd.

There is a young steward at this table, polishing a pair of large leather boots. Your presence seems to make him incredibly nervous, though that is the response most people would have to a warrior of Avadon.
He looks up at you. _I ... I ... Greetings. I am Admes. Did you need something? Mending? Polishing?_
Admes sets aside his work to speak with you. He is still very nervous. He keeps from shaking only with great effort.
What do you do here?
_I ... I am just a steward. I tend to the guests. Help them. Keep things clean. I am not a warrior, or an Eye. We just keep Avadon running._
Tell me about the guests.
_Avadon gets many visitors. From the Pact and the Farlands. They all want help, or to sell information, or to influence Avadon. And they stay down here, and I help them._
What do you do for the guests?
_Get them food. Tend to their needs. Answer their questions, tell them about etiquette, and help them to not make any embarrassing mistakes._
_I am from Dharam. I was a servant there, in a merchant's villa. I met a Hand when he was staying with us. The Hand liked me and brought me here._
You didn't mind leaving the villa?
_Well, my master was buying shiploads of stolen goods from Svorgald. Avadon was angry. By the time they were done, there was not much villa left to serve._
You have been giving information to Valna.
Admes drops the boot. He starts to shake uncontrollably. You give him a minute to control himself. _I ... I ... I am sorry. She ... She threatened me. And ... Oh, they can tell if I lie, can't they?_
_I was weak! I am sorry! Please don't turn me in! They will kill me! I beg you!_
I will spare you, but only if you pay me.
_Pay you? But I don't have anything to pay ... Oh. I suppose you won't believe that. Yes, I get tips from time to time. Find lost things. And so on. Spare me, and I will give you everything I find!_
He leaves and soon returns with a heavy pouch. _This is everything Valna gave me. I give it to you, for the good of Avadon. And thank you for sparing me._
I won't turn you in, but don't let this happen again.

He falls to his knees. _Oh, thank you. Thank you, thank you. I will never again act against Avadon._ Your act of mercy has earned Redbeard his most loyal of followers. He starts to cry uncontrollably. Eventually, you just wander off.
You will have to answer for your crimes.

He looks down at the boots in his hands. _I suppose I knew that this would happen. Please ... Don't keep me waiting long. I will not flee. I will go to the dungeon. Unless, of course, you change your mind and decide to be merciful._
I have not yet turned you in.
_Oh, thank you, thank you. I am grateful for every moment of life I get to atone for my mistakes._
What do you have to give me?
_Oh, yes. I have something. It is amazing what people forget in their rooms when they leave. I have been setting aside the best such items for you._
He gives you a scroll tube. _I found this only last week. No idea what the scroll does. I don't tinker with magic. But it might help you._
_I just found this yesterday._ He gives you a small ceramic flask filled with viscous green liquid. _Something so disgusting must have magic in it, yes?_

_You are in luck. I found something just this morning._ He gives you a long willow wand. It glows very faintly in the dim light of the basement. _Seems dangerous and powerful. Just the thing for you._
_I ... I'm sorry. I have nothing right now. Give me a little more time. I will find something. I promise!_ You leave the pitiful creature behind.

There is a man in black garb, a mask, and leather armor sitting at this table. His appearance is rather incongruous in this crowded, busy dining hall. He sits alone, and he constantly scratches at his mask, as if it is bothering him.

Then he sees you. He jumps to his feet and bows deeply. _Heart Miranda told me of you. You are [N], yes? I am Shima Threespear, proud Shadowwalker of Holklanda. I place my blade and razordisks at your service, should you have need of me._
Is your mask bothering you?

His face is covered, so you can't see his expression. He shrugs slightly. _It itches from time to time, especially when I am inside and it is warm. But the mask is the mark of my caste, so I wear it proudly in Avadon._
You are from Holklanda.
_I ... That is true._ He suspects that you are about to ask more about it. _But I would discuss it at another time. I have just arrived from the field, and I am eager to return._
You are a Shadowwalker?
_I am. Normally, I would not wear this garb where others could see me. In Avadon, however, among my allies, I let you see it so that you know my purpose._
So it is unusual to be dressed like this?
_Of course. We say that when one not of our clan sees the mask, it is the last thing they see. But I am a warrior of Avadon now, so all of Avadon are my clanmates._
Why are you sitting here?
_I must eat. And I, whenever I can, talk to those who travel through. We Shadowwalkers learn all we can of every land, so that we can be prepared when we are sent there._
I can choose you to come with me on my next mission, in The Kva.
_Then I would be honored to serve Redbeard by your side. My armor is light, but my arm is fast. I can duck in, strike a lethal blow, and disappear in the shadows, all in a single moment._
_We are assassins, warriors of the darkness. If we find ourselves fighting toe to toe, we have somehow failed. We bring rapid death, and then we disappear._
_I do all I do for the honor of the Threespear Clan. I will wait to see if you have use for me._
I will consider bringing you.
He nods. _I would welcome it. I do not wish to spend more time on guard duty or menial work, and I feel that I have much to prove._
Before you can ask him to elaborate, he sits back down at the table. _I will wait here for your command. Excuse me while I prepare._ He returns to his meal.
I will definitely choose you to accompany me.
He nods. His mask cannot entirely conceal his enthusiasm. _I welcome that news. I do not wish to spend more time on guard duty or menial work, and I feel that I have much to prove._
I don't think I will need your services.

No response emerges from behind that mask of his. _I see. That is your decision. I do not wish to spend more time on guard duty or menial work, and I have much to prove, and I will do it however I can._
Shima is still resting and eating, determined to be ready for any missions that await him. _Excuse me, [N]. I will prepare. I must await your call._
Shima Threespear is sitting at his customary seat in the dining hall, watching with interest those who come and go. He talks with all who are not frightened by his odd regalia.
You sit with him for a time. He is silent, though you sense that he is eager to speak with you.
You are from Holklanda?
He nods slowly. _I am. I have only been a warrior of Avadon for three years._
Tell me about Holklanda.

_It is not like Avadon. Not like any land in Lynaeus. It is very ..._ He looks out at the boisterous activity of the dining hall. _Very ordered. Quiet and calm on the surface. It is as violent and torn as every other land on Lynaeus, but in a much more dignified way._
Is Holklanda content as part of the Pact?
_Of course. As proud as we are, we know that we are safest from the warriors of Khemeria and the Tawon Empire when we band with others._
_We have our rivalries. And we and Kellemderiel have spilled much of each other's blood, but we still are wise enough to know that the Pact means survival. Thus, I am here fighting for it._
Why did you come here?
He is silent for some time. Then he says, _I ask your pardon, [N]. That is a tale from my own life. I am a warrior of Avadon now, fighting for the honor of my clan. I would not discuss it._
If we are to fight side by side, I must know more about you.
_You may know all, every single fact, about my life since I walked through the Avadon gates. The old life? It is dead and gone. You must accept this._
I understand.
He nods silently.
Do you learn much from the people passing through?
_Of course. Most choose not to speak with me. But from those who do, I absorb every bit of knowledge I can about the lands of Lynaeus. About the Pact, and the Farlands._
Why don't they speak with you?

_Shadowwalkers are feared, and it is wise to do so. As with Avadon, the attention of a shadowwalker can be fatal. And yet some, once they sense that I am not currently tasked to kill them, are interested to actually meet one of my kind._
What sorts of bits of knowledge do you look for?
_Scraps of language, of etiquette, of knowing when to nod and speak and be silent. The sort of details that can mean the difference between discovery and concealment when spying in the Farlands._
And most fear you.
_Yes. Shadowwalkers are spies and assassins. That holds a natural terror for most. Understandably, perhaps._
You are not ashamed to be a spy and assassin?
_No. Are you? We are both warriors of Avadon. Spying and killing are our most frequent work. I wish to discuss something else._
Let us discuss something else.
Shima Threespear nods.
I'd like to know more about the Threespear Clan.
He is silent, judging how much he should say. Then he says, _Holklanda has many clans. Some are mighty, some are weak. They rise and fall over the centuries. Some high, some low, then it reverses._

He nods slowly and checks to make sure nobody nearby is eavesdropping. Then he speaks. _I will tell you the tale, though it causes me great pain. I had hoped to leave this part of my story at the Avadon gates, but if we spend time in Holklanda, this will be impossible._
_I will try to make it brief. Five years ago, the leader of our clan put himself in position to be a Juror of Holklanda. We believed that he would succeed, and it would have won us great honor._
A Juror?
_In Holklanda, a Juror is like a ... a lord, or a duke, or a councilor. But also with his own army. It is a position of great authority and honor._
And what happened then?
_I don't think you will be surprised to learn that our plans went awry. The head of a rival clan, the Honored Forge, put himself into competition for the position._
Is that unusual?

_Not at all. It is honorable to compete. It is expensive and time-consuming to perform the rituals needed to become a Juror, and it shows the wish for a stronger Holklanda. Normally, they would have competed. A winner would be chosen. Both would have gained in stature. But not this time._
What went wrong?

_The leader of the Honored Forge was ... determined to prevail. He spread rumors about our clan leader. About minor crimes he had committed. About certain private practices. The papers he spread stained our reputation._
What rumors were spread?
_Do not ask me to repeat them. They would be hot bile in my mouth, sickening me._
What happened to your clan leader?
_He killed himself, of course. It was the only way to begin purging the stain._
Were the claims true?
_Perhaps. I do not think on it. Even if they were true, they were no worse than what all others do in private. It was revealing these secrets to harm us that was the crime._
And so you came here.
He nods. _All clans exist on a wheel, one time high, one time low. By fighting here, I begin to restore our reputation. I am beginning a work that may take centuries._
_But you must know this. In Holklanda, I may encounter members of the Honored Forge. There is a debt of honor, and I may be compelled to pay it in blood._
Do what you need to, as long as it does not interfere with our work here.
He nods. _I would not harm my clan farther by failing in my sworn duty here. I appreciate your understanding. That is all I have to say on the topic._
And I would fight by your side.
He shakes his head. _This is between the Threespear Clan and the Honored Forge. I would not distract Avadon's warriors with this private matter._
_But ... I thank you for your kind words. That is all I have to say on the topic._
Your work is here now. Set your old grudges aside.
He is silent for a long time. There is little he can say in response to that.
Finally, he says, _That is all I have to say on the topic._
_At this point, after what I have learned, there is nothing I can say about my clan with certainty. I must think. I must ... make a decision._ He says nothing more on the topic.
And the Threespear Clan?
_It is low. Thus I am here, fighting for its reputation. But that is from my life before the Avadon gates. I would discuss it no more._
I need to go.
He nods. _I will await your call._ He returns to his meal.

Shima Threespear is sitting at his customary table. And, as usual, he is alone. He slowly sips some ale. You have not seen him drink before. Then he looks up at you. You can see in his eyes that he is agitated.
_Welcome, [N]. Please join me. I welcome the company, and I ... I need to speak with you._
How is the ale?
_It is ... unfamiliar. Any sort of spirit leaves me with a splitting headache. Any such revelry is repaid with a greater rate of pain. And yet ... At times, I feel the need._
What is wrong?
_That is what I need to speak with you about._
What do you need to tell me?
_I have heard a rumor. It had the ring of truth about it. We may soon be sent to Holklanda, my Homeland. It means that I must speak with you, so that we are both prepared._
_Our work is taking us to Holklanda. To my land. It means that I must speak with you, so that we are both prepared._
Is this something I need to know?
_It is, if we are to fight together without your being confused by my actions._

_I am of the Threespear Clan. Once proud. Then, very recently, brought low by the treachery of another clan, the Honored Forge. You do not need to ask me about my clan and its history, but you may wish to. It is good to understand._

You return to speak with Shima Threespear. If anything, he looks more distressed than before. He is still sipping ale, though you suspect that, from the way he holds his head, he has a massive headache.
_Greetings, [N]. Please join me. I could use the company, and the diners today are more afraid of speaking with me than usual. I wish to discuss Holklanda with you._
I do not want to discuss your peoples' politics unless it directly affects our missions.
_I ..._ He pauses. _I see. I have troubled you overmuch with my private struggles already. What else do you wish to discuss?_
What do you wish to say?
_I told you before that I thought we were going to Holklanda. Now I know that this is the case. I suspect that we will be returning, as well._

_Holklanda is a large land. The chance of our meeting the Honored Forge is small. And yet, I can't keep from thinking on it. The struggles of my clan continue to torment me. I must ask a boon of you._
You wish to kill them.
_That, yes. They owe us blood. Not all of their lives, but some of them. But there is ... more._
Why does it bother you so?
_There are so many mysteries about what happened. Why was the Honored Forge so determined to fight us? Were the tales they spread about my clan true? And, if so, how did they learn what they did?_
_Until these questions are answered, until I can be sure my clan knows its true enemy, I cannot rest._
What boon do you wish?
_Simple awareness. When in the Beraza Woods, if you see any signs that the Honored Forge is there, let me know. That is all I ask._
What will you do with that knowledge?
_What I must, to be able to live with honor intact._
I must say no. This is not the business of Avadon.
_I ... I do understand. I do not hold this against you. I promise that I will do what I can to attend to my duty here without distraction. I will try. Did you want to discuss something else?_
I will be watchful.
_I thank you, and I can ask no more. And, in return, I promise that I will do what I can to attend to my duty here without distraction. Did you want to discuss something else?_
You walk away from the portal, still slightly dazed from your instantaneous journey of hundreds of miles. As your vision clears, you see that Shima Threespear is waiting for you. He is clearly upset.
_I need to speak with you, [N]. It is about the matter of my clan._
Your clan? What do you mean?

_I am of the Threespear Clan, recently dishonored in a political struggle by the Honored Forge. I am here to regain my clan's honor, but I cannot back away from a chance at vengeance. I could have told you about this in leisure before, but now there is no time._
Can this wait until later?
Shima looks longingly at the portal. _It can't. I am sorry._
What do we need to discuss?
_I need to know if you saw any signs of the Honored Forge clan during your journey through the Beraza Woods. Did you learn anything of their presence?_
You notice that Shima has a folded sheet of paper in his hand. It is falling apart, as if it has been opened and read many times.
I know nothing of it. (Lie.)
Shima takes a step back, surprised. _I will assume, [N], that you are simply unaware and not truly trying to deceive one who would risk his life for you._
He holds up the letter. _From what is left of my clan. They have been vigilant, ever-watching their new mortal foes. It took them little time to read Shigaz's report of your recent adventures._
_The Honored Forge is in the Beraza Woods. I do not know why, or if it is related to our purpose there. It does not matter._
Yes. They have warriors there.

He nods and holds up the letter. _From what is left of my clan. They have been vigilant, ever-watching their new mortal foes. It took them little time to read Shigaz's report of your recent adventures._
_The Honored Forge is in Beraza. I do not know why, or if it is related to our purpose there. It does not matter._
_They are there. In our reach._

_I will go to Beraza. We Hands are given wide latitude to act in the way we think most benefits Avadon. Now I hunt the treacherous killers of the Honored Forge. I am simply doing you the honor of letting you know, so that you do not waste time looking for me._
He takes a step toward the portal.
Why does this obsess you so?

_The Honored Forge ... I do not know why they did what they did. Or how. Until I understand, my clan will not be safe. It will not be able to defend itself. I apologize. I do not wish to abandon you, but I must. I have no choice._
I order you to remain.
Shima shakes his head. _I am sure you think you are acting to my benefit, so I will not hold this against you. However, I am a Hand of Avadon. I do not answer to you. I act as I must._
_If anyone needs to learn what happened to me, I left papers of interest in my quarters. Farewell._ And then he turns and steps into the portal. A moment later, he is gone.
Go. Do what you must do.
He nods. _I thank you, [N]. I hope to return safely to aid you. But I ... I am alone. I will try to survive, but I am not full of hope._
Let me come with you.
_I cannot allow it. I am already shirking my duty. I will not tempt others to abandon Avadon in its time of need. I must go alone, whatever the cost._

Shima Threespear is sitting at his customary table. He eats bread and sips water. He seems unharmed and unchanged by his recent expedition. Your superiors have not punished him. The only change is the anger in his eyes, recognized only by you.
_Welcome, [N]. It is good to see you. I would ... I would talk to you._

_You came after me and saved my life. You helped me learn much. I am wiser for your help. And I will forgive you for turning aside my blade. Harua Honored Forge should be dead, but I will not hold a grudge against you._
_I will fight by your side in days to come. I owe you that much, but no more._
_Please excuse me. I have much to think about. Much to decide._ He returns to his meal.
I have risked enough for you. I will know nothing more of your clan's troubles.
Shima nods. The mask does a marvelous job of masking his reaction. _I understand. I owe you my life. I will be content with that and expect no more help from you._
_Please excuse me, then. I have much to think about._ He returns to his meal.
He lowers his voice to a whisper. _I have learned much recently. Things I would have been happier not to know. About what happened to my clan, about Redbeard, about Avadon's part in what happened._
_Redbeard destroyed my clan's reputation, a reputation that took centuries to build. He may have had his reasons, but it was not just._
This is dangerous talk.
_It is the facts. What remains is to decide how I will act. I do not need to include Redbeard in the list of those whose blood must be spilt._
And what do you wish of me?
_Your counsel. How can I live with this burden of knowledge that has been placed upon me?_
Put aside any thought of fighting Redbeard. He did what was best for the Pact.

_I ... I understand. You speak truth. Redbeard did what he thought best before, and he does so now. My hatred for him burns, but I will still serve. I will fight well, and I will build my clan's reputation. Like a true Holklandan._
_Thank you, [N]. Now please leave me. I have much to think about._
You must find your own path. I can't say what you should do.
He nods. _I value your honesty, and you are correct. The true Holklandan finds answers within himself. I must face my own duty, my own honor, and decide how to act._
Those who commit such crimes must pay. Even Redbeard.
_You speak words of death, but they are full of truth. Redbeard is not a warrior of honor, he is an arbitrary and capricious puppet-master._

There is a woman wandering the Avadon gardens. She wears a long, loose leather dress, and several beads and symbols hang from around her neck. She is older than you. You guess that she has served in Avadon for at least a few years.
As you approach her, you feel as if you are being watched. Something slinks through the trees, watching you. When you turn to see what it is, it fades back into the shadows.
She smiles. _Greetings. Heart Miranda described you to me. You are [N], the newest Hand in Avadon. I am Jenell, shaman of the Wyldrylm. I will be working at your side, if you choose._
Is there something stalking me?

She nods and laughs. Despite the recent troubles, she is in high spirits. _The beasts of the woods tend to keep an eye on me. As do the beasts of this garden. Do not worry. As long as you don't move too suddenly, you will be fine._
She might be joking.
You are from the Wyldrylm?
_This is true. I am of one of the southern tribes, though I have not been home for some years. I am polite enough to not describe my land unless asked._
And if I ask?
_Then I would be happy to tell. Later. For now, I have heard that there is work to do._
I can choose to bring you with me on missions.
_So Heart Miranda has explained to me. This was not unwelcome news. You seem competent enough, and I am eager for any excuse to escape this tomb of stone._
This tomb of stone?
_I serve Avadon, but I am not fully at my ease within its walls. I prefer to be out in the open air._
If you do not like Avadon, why did you come?
_It is a long tale, and not one I tell to those I have just met._
How can you aid me?
_I am a shaman, one who has shown great skill in my chosen path. I can call creatures to aid us in battle._
_I can summon venom and clawed spirits to strike down our foes from afar. And I am no stranger to the healing arts. I can revive you when you have become wounded._
_There is much I can do for you, and all I ask is for you to take me out of this stone fortress._
You are a skilled worker of magic, like Nathalie?
_In skill, I have much in common with Nathalie. I do, however, lack much of her arrogance and limitless ambition. And, unlike her, there are some in Avadon who claim to like me._
Perhaps I will leave you here for now.
_That is disappointing, but the choice was, after all, left with you. Should you ever desire healing more effective than bandages, I will be here._ She walks off into the trees.
I may bring you with me.

She looks pleased. _I hope you continue to consider it. My service to Avadon has been above reproach. Now I must go. My companion has run off, and I fear that he will be causing mischief._ She walks off into the trees.
I will definitely choose you.

She looks pleased. _It is not a decision you will regret. My service to Avadon has been above reproach. Now I must go. My companion has run off, and I fear that he will be causing mischief._ She walks off into the trees.

Jenell is currently searching the undergrowth for someone or something. _Excuse me. I must be rescuing my companion before he angers someone. Do not worry. Should you choose me to accompany you, I will be ready._
Jenell is, as usual, in the garden. It seems to be one of the few places in Avadon where she is comfortable. You notice that birds tends to cluster in nearby branches when she is around.
She says, _Is there anything else you wish of me?_
Tell me about the Wyldrylm.

She stares sadly at the small stands of trees nearby. _I will not bore you with descriptions of how lovely it is. Everyone thinks that their home is beautiful, even those who live in that waste they call The Kva._
_The Wyldrylm is a land of tribes, fierce and independent. They fight each other and work together in equal measure, but we are all one family when we face the dangers of Lynaeus._
How many tribes are there?
_It is hard to say. There are a dozen large ones and many smaller ones. However, the webs of alliances are so complicated that it can be difficult to tell where one tribe ends and another begins._
Do they ever fight each other?

_There are skirmishes, but rarely is anyone killed. This is very different from how things were even a hundred years ago. Of late, however, we have been so focused on our enemies in Lynaeus that our elders are loath to spend our energies fighting our own kind._
What dangers threaten you?

_Like all in the Pact, we fear the Farlands. The Khemerians to the north always watch us from their stone towers. They have abandoned our ways to live like outsiders, and it has made them weak and jealous._
_And to the south is the madness of the Corruption. The less said of that dark and infested place, the better._
You miss your homeland.
_I do. However, I rarely return. I am not of them anymore. They see me as an outsider, no matter how much I try to prove that I argue for them inside Avadon._
They have rejected you?
_Those of the Wyldrylm are not used to the laws of outsiders. Especially those who live in a crude stone block like this fortress._
_They should love me more than they do, since I argue for their ways tirelessly. But, though I love them, they are not always wise._
How do you argue for them?
_I am always arguing for restraint in Avadon's ways. It can be an aggravation to them. Few enjoy the truth._
_Though, lately, I have come to realize that, perhaps, words may not be enough when facing the power-mad._
Why are you always in this garden?
_Because, as artificial and carefully tended as it is, I long to feel fresh, clean air on my face and grass under my feet._
_If I am too far from the creatures of the wild for too long, I become irritable and hard to deal with._
And the animals come to you?
_There is something about me that draws them. It is part of my power. Of course, when they come, they may then try to eat me. They may be wild and noble, but they can always be hungry and dumb._
_Fortunately, I can both call and dismiss them when needed._
Do you talk to animals?

_No. They don't talk. They are not intelligent in the way we are. Remember, I respect them, but I also command them. They are not my friends. They are my servants. I care for them, but they also serve my purposes._
_You want to hear my story? I am happy to tell it, but it leads to discussions of politics and philosophy. It is not something the Hands face with enthusiasm. You have been warned._
Oh. Let's discuss something else.
She laughs. _Oh, dear. I scared you off. All right. What would you talk about?_
I'm not afraid.

_I am pleased. As you know, I am from one of the southern tribes of the Wyldrylm. I showed great promise as a youth. The beasts of the wild would come as I called, and they would obey. Before I was even of marrying age, I could match the elders in this regard._
_There was envy. I was told that I was not welcome. Then I saw a way to help my people. Some Hands from Avadon passed through our settlement. I met them, showed them my power, and left with them._
The elders drove you out? Why?
_Because they were doddering old fools, jealous and insecure. It does happen, after all. I love the Wyldrylm, but it is not without flaw. Sometimes the wrong people rise to power._
You did not stay and fight?
_I do not stay where I am not welcome. Instead, I fight here. I am more welcome, and I can make more of a difference._
How do you help your own people here?

_I help my people, and all people of the Pact, by arguing for restraint. When Hands are allowed to decide a course of action, I argue that Avadon should be humble. No law binds us. That means that we should show great caution._
But you still support the cause of Avadon?
_I do, when it acts against the aggression of the Farlands. When Avadon crushes the freedom of the states of the Pact, then I argue._
What do the Hearts and Redbeard think of this?
_I am fortunate in that they welcome debate. They tolerate my arguments, within reason. I must always recognize when I have lost an argument._
Do you think Avadon can use its power with wisdom?
_I ... Once I thought so. Now I wonder if any can hold the power of Avadon and not be warped by it. I ... It is a worrying thought. I would discuss something else for now._
_I will respond honestly. I do not know. I had noble intentions, but ... I don't know why I came, and I don't know why I stay._
_But I am considering the question, and I will soon have an answer._
