You emerge from the portal slowly. If you move too quickly after being magically wrenched across Lynaeus, the headache is murderous. As your vision clears, you are surprised to see Jenell waiting for you. It is odd seeing her outside of the garden.
_Welcome back to Avadon,_ she says. _I have been speaking with the other Hands. Now I must talk to you._
I don't have time to talk right now.
She stands in your way. _I am sorry, but it is important. We must speak._
What do you want?

entries.text: _I was told that you met several tribesmen from the Wyldrylm. They were hiding in Khemeria, scared of the power of Avadon. Is that true?_
It is, but I do not see it as important.
_It is vitally important. It touches the purpose of Avadon, and how it might have gone wrong. And how it can be repaired._ This seems to be a conversation she is determined to have.
They were there. What do you want to know about them?
_I don't need to know about them. Their story is an old one. I need to talk to you about us, about what we will do._
_Those hiding tribesmen, they were only trying to enforce the Right of the Roads, one of the oldest traditions of my people. All tribes are allowed to take tolls from those who cross their lands._
_Avadon has decided, over the last few years, to steal it from us. I have argued against this. And I still will._
Why is it so important?

_Because, for many tribes on the poorer stretches of land, the tolls of those who pass is a major source of food and coin. Families will starve because of this, for a right we have had for centuries._
Why did Avadon take this right away?

_Because they have declared that certain roads, many roads, will be free for travel, purely unencumbered, for all. This sounds perfectly fair, of course, until it is your land that is being taken and controlled._
So what will you do about it?

_I have not decided. Never before has Avadon acted against the customs of the Wyldrylm in such a ... blatant manner. I need to argue more, of course. But meanwhile, those folk of the tribes are lost in Khemeria, starving and alone._
You should forget them. You have duties here.
_Yes. I have heard such things from the other Hands a thousand times. However, nobody can expect me to abandon my people, especially not to those vile Khemerians._
She turns and walks off, heading back to her garden.
I can't tell you what you should do.
She nods. _That is fair. I can't expect you to understand the ways of my tribe, and I can't force you to care about this as much as I do. I have much to think about. Quickly._
You should go and help them.

She nods. _I think you must be right. And yet, it is a long distance from thought to action. I must think. I must plan. I must ... It is so tight in here. The ceiling is so low. I can't think. I must have air ..._
Jenell continues to pace around the garden. Her earlier carefree attitude is completely gone. Her struggles in Khemeria are still very much with her.
_Oh, [N]. It is you. I am thinking about Avadon. Something I wish ... I wish I could stop doing it._
I don't need to hear more. You have caused enough trouble.

She turns and looks at you, startled. _I am sorry. I did not realize that you ... Of course, I will keep my worries to myself. Excuse me._ She walks off. Shadowy figures in the undergrowth follow her.
What are you thinking?
_I left my homeland because the elders and shamans were jealous of me. That is what I say, and it is true. But that is not all. I left because I was angry._
Why?

_Because I wanted to change things. I saw the foolish things that they did, strange practices that went back centuries, and I ... I had to leave. I knew I had to change things, so I went to a place where I was sure that they needed changing._
Should you have stayed to change your tribe's ways?
_I don't think so. I don't know. When I see something I don't like, how do I tell whether it is wrong or I just haven't seen the reason for it yet?_
_But Avadon ... Avadon could improve. I am sure of it._
So you will change Avadon.
_I must try. The power they hold ... Can it ever be used justly? Or will they take away my peoples' ways, one by one, until there is nothing left that makes us ... us?_
_Redbeard does not care about our ways. Or anyone's ways. Can we live with him?_
That is a dangerous thing to say.
_Yes. It ... is. So I ... Please forget I said it. I must think more. Much more._ She walks off. Shadowy figures in the undergrowth follow her.
You should keep arguing.

_I will. I will keep using my voice. But words ... they seem so weak. So inadequate. Sometimes, people need to ... I must think. Much more._ She walks off. Shadowy figures in the undergrowth follow her.
Sometimes, you need to act.

_I am surprised to finally hear someone say it, but I think ... Words ... they seem so weak. So inadequate. Sometimes, people need to act. I must think. Much more._ She walks off. Shadowy figures in the undergrowth follow her.

Jenell is still pacing back and forth in the garden. She has regained her carefree, smiling attitude. However, as you talk to her, you feel like there are lots of pairs of eyes watching you from the undergrowth. You start to feel nervous.
_Ah, [N],_ she says. _It is good that you stopped by. I wish to speak with you._
As long as you have set aside any foolish thoughts of challenging Avadon.

She smiles bitterly. _Of course. I will not trouble you with any such thoughts. I have made my peace with it. The unquestioned rule of Avadon is all we have. And all we deserve. It was good to see you. Please excuse me._
She turns and leaves. As she goes, you realize she didn't tell you what she was thinking about.
What did you want to talk about?

_About what has been happening in Lynaeus. About Avadon erasing the ancient customs of the Wyldrylm. Settling to its own liking the ownership of the Beraza Woods. Taking more control of the Pact with every passing year._
_I have been thinking of it, and so have the other Hands._
You talk with the other Hands?
_From time to time. At meals. It can't be helped._
What do the other Hands think?
_You should talk to them. All of them. You might be surprised at the wisdom you hear. Perhaps even from Nathalie, as unlikely as that seems._
And have you come to a conclusion?
_Not yet. I wanted to talk to you first. I wanted to ask you a question. A simple bit of philosophy, nothing that the Hearts would have any trouble with._
_Do you think that it is possible for Avadon to exert too much power over Lynaeus? Do you think that it might reach the point where someone needs to restrain it?_ She watches you intently.
I think that it has already reached that point.
She nods. _A sentiment I have heard more and more of late. Whispered, of course. Thank you for your honesty._
It is possible.
She nods. _A careful, diplomatic answer. All I was wondering was if you would admit the possibility. You did. That makes you, in some eyes, a foe of Avadon. Of course, I do not feel that way._
No. Avadon needs all of its power to protect the Pact.
_I see. Many would agree with you. Many would give Avadon all of the power it could possibly wish in return for its protection. They would give Avadon the entire world. I thank you for your honesty._
And what do you feel?
_Me? I feel what I have said all along. What good does it do for Avadon to protect the Pact if it takes away all that makes our lands valuable?_
_Now I must go. We will talk again soon, I am sure. All of us._ She walks off into the garden.
Are you planning to do something?
_I am planning to do what I have done. Serve, work with you as needed, and think. And enjoy this lovely garden._
There is a steward wandering among the office and quarters of the Hands and Hearts. He is an aging man, crisply dressed, the very picture of dignity.
He gives you a little bow. _I welcome you, Hand of Avadon. I am Polus. I will serve you when you desire. Tend to your needs. Deliver messages. Whatever it takes to ease your mind._
Polus stands unobtrusively off to the side. He seems calm and non-threatening, and yet he is ready to spring into action the moment you need something.
Then he says, quietly, _[N], I was given a message of some importance. When you have the time._
_I am from the Tawon Empire. I have been honored with this posting, and I have been here for twenty years._
The Tawon Empire? Isn't that one of the Farlands?
_The Tawon Empire is the enemy of the Pact, but I do not concern myself with politics. I exist to provide quality service._
Do you know anything about the troubles Avadon has been facing?
His mouth develops a slight tic. _I know nothing of that. I do not pay attention to politics. I only serve._
_I take care of the distracting needs of the Hands, Eyes, and Hearts, so that they can focus on their work._
How can you help me?
_I can provide food. Clean linens. Light. Whatever your day-to-day needs require._
I am hungry.
Polus leaves for a minute. He soon returns with a mug of ale and some fresh bread. _Will you need anything else?_
I need some linens.
Polus leaves for a minute. He soon returns with an immaculately clean blanket, pillow, and towel. _Will you need anything else?_
I need light for my chambers.
Polus leaves for a minute. He soon returns with a candle. _Will you need anything else?_
_All right. I will be here if you need me._
What message do you have for me?
_It is from Sevilin. He asked me to tell you that he had to depart to The Kva. He had some urgent business there, and he did not know when he would return._
_He added that if you needed to know where he went, he left some information in his quarters._
Where are his quarters?
_Just across the hallway from Miranda's office._
Where did he leave for?
_All I know is that he used the portal to The Kva. I know nothing more. Do you need anything else?_
_Jenell came to see me. She told me that she had to depart. She went to ... To Khemeria, I believe. She was in a hurry, but if you wanted to help her, you were welcome._
Where did she go?
_I am sorry. I do not know. But she said that she left some notes in her quarters._
_They are in the chambers below the dining hall._
Do you know why she went to Khemeria?
_She did not say. She only said that you should look in her quarters. Do you need anything else?_
_Nathalie, the young, excitable sorceress, came to see me. She seemed unusually pleased. She said that she was departing for Holklanda._
_She did not tell me. She tends to treat me with disdain. However, she said that she left some notes in her quarters. It's across the hall from your rooms._
What was she doing?
_I am not sure. I did note that she seemed prepared for a hunting expedition. In the woods. That is all I know. My apologies. Do you need anything else?_

You try to talk to the surviving Avadon guards. They are not full Hands, but they are as competent and loyal warriors as the Pact has to offer. Whatever has happened here, however, has reduced them to quivering wrecks.

The best you can tell from their breathless, panicked answers to your questions, the attack happened in the middle of the night. They woke up to find most of the gates closed and locked and assassins everywhere. They have been running and fighting ever since, and they don't know where Redbeard is or if he is well. That is all you learn.
You manage to land a solid blow on Miranda. She seems slightly dazed, and blood starts to flow. She looks down at it with disbelief.
Miranda starts to walk away from the portal to pursue you. Then she stops, shaking her head in disbelief.
_What am I doing? My days of battle are long past, and you are truly dangerous. No, I will deal with you later._

She allows herself to fall backwards. Through the portal. Moments after she vanishes, the field of energy begins to warp and flicker. The city within fades away. Following her through the portal is impossible. Miranda is gone. You suddenly feel a great need to find Redbeard. He is most likely to be in his tower.

There are several Avadon guards cowering here. One is seriously wounded. The others are shocked insensate by the fury of the surprise assault. You try to goad them into action, but they refuse to move. At this point, all they are hoping for is survival.
At last, you find a familiar face. Very familiar. Heart Miranda is here, standing next to a portal. Through the portal, you can see a faint cityscape of old buildings and tall, elegant spires.

And yet, like everything else you have seen, something is not right here. Miranda is wearing traveling clothes and a thick, leather cloak. She holds a bulging satchel in one hand and a wand in the other. There are two dead servants in the room, a Hand and an Eye.
As you approach her, she watches you warily. _Ah, [N]. You have returned to Avadon. Perhaps not too late, either. You have arrived in interesting times. Times when things can change very quickly._
(Look through the portal.)
You look through the portal and try to identify the city you are seeing. You have never been there, but something about it seems very familiar.
Miranda, what has happened here?
_An attack. The assassins came in the middle of the night. Some Avadon warriors were traitors, and they allowed the assassins entry. At least, that is my guess._
Then, oddly, she smiles. _I have been avoiding the invaders. I had much to do._
Who killed these two people?
_Oh, assassins, no doubt,_ she says airily. _That is the sort of thing that has been happening in your absence._
I need to report what has happened.
_What? Report? I ... Oh, yes. I would like to know what has happened in Castle Vebeaux. That information has not reached me yet._
_We did get word from Duke Gryfyn about the accusations against you and your flight into the woods. Now you have returned. Tell me, what happened to Duke Gryfyn?_
Are you going somewhere?
Heart Miranda watches you warily. When she speaks again, it is in her sharpest, most commanding voice. _Do not interrogate me, Hand. It is I who needs answers from you._
I need to report to Redbeard. Where is he?
_He is trapped in his tower. We've heard nothing from him. He may be wounded, or dead. You will report to me._
I don't know. I slipped past him to return to Avadon. (Lie.)
Heart Miranda is distracted enough that the lie seems to slip by her. _So Duke Gryfyn survives your no doubt dramatic rampage. Very interesting. Very useful._
_And tell me this: Did you find any evidence indicating who is responsible for the attacks against Avadon?_
Duke Gryfyn fled his castle. I let him go.

Strangely, Heart Miranda isn't nearly as bothered by this news as you thought she would be. In fact, she seems pleased. _You did? Really? How fascinating. Very useful information. I will be sure to act upon it._
Duke Gryfyn was a traitor. He is dead at my hand.
Heart Miranda nods somberly. _If you try to kill the king, it is a very good idea not to miss. He let you escape, and he paid the price._
I need some answers before I tell you anything else.
_Oh, I will tell you all you want to know. Very soon. Have no worries. However, you must first finish your report._
I haven't learned anything. Yet.
Heart Miranda nods. _I am sure that the assassins have done a very good job of hiding all evidence. This is ... significant._
_I have but one more question, and then I will know what I need to._
I haven't learned anything. (Lie.)
Heart Miranda nods. She seems to believe the lie. _I am sure that the assassins have done a very good job of hiding all evidence. This is ... significant._
I found evidence that someone named Dheless is responsible.
Heart Miranda nods somberly. _So the traitors were not as careful about destroying evidence as they could have been. Should have been? We will see. We will see._
_The Wayfarer was going to track you down in the Beraza Woods. It was chaotic. His success was far from assured. Did he find you, and what happened?_
Wait. How do you know of the Wayfarer?
_Simple child. You think a mysterious stranger could track one of my Hands for months without me knowing? Without my permission? Answer my question._
The Wayfarer found me, but I listened to nothing he had to say. (Lie.)
Miranda looks doubtful. _That is not likely. You have never seemed to be one to stay silent. Still, your report is noted. That is all I need to know from you._
I met the Wayfarer, and he spoke treason to me. So I killed him.

Miranda seems shocked. _Shadow Tarkus is dead? That is ... dramatic news. He took a great risk contacting you. Truly, he has paid for it._ Apparently, The Wayfarer was Shadow Tarkus, one of the prisoners who escaped from Avadon about the time you first arrived. But how did Miranda know that? _Valuable information. That is all I need to know from you._
I met the Wayfarer, and he spoke treason to me. I drove him off.

Miranda nods. _The Wayfarer thought that you might be turned away from Avadon. He took a great risk tracking you down, and it clearly did not pay off. For him, I mean._ Though she seems lost in thought, you note that she is edging closer and closer to the portal. _Valuable information. That is all I need to know from you._
The Wayfarer suggested I try to take power in Avadon. I said that I would.

Heart Miranda seems surprised. _He suggested treason, and you accepted? And then you told me? Very bold, [N]. It makes me wonder what you have learned, and what you are here to do. Very interesting. That is all I need to know from you._
There are now things that I need to know.
You start to ask Miranda a question, when you look at the portal again. You recognize the buildings on the other side.

You have never been in the Tawon Empire, the largest and most powerful of the Farlands, but you have seen drawings of the cities there. Proud, crumbling, large, built from stone. The portal now leads to one of them, with its distinctive marble halls and elegant spires. You look from the spires to Miranda. The wand in her hand now points at you. There is no trace of a smile on her face.
Turn aside your wand, Miranda.

_I think not. You are too dangerous and unpredictable, whatever your plans. My work in Avadon is done. I am taking my records, and I am leaving. The Black Fortress can crumble into dust, for all I care!_
Why are you going to the Tawon Empire?
_Yes, my new home. The center of power in the new order. My work in Avadon is done. I am taking my records, and I am leaving. The Black Fortress can crumble into dust, for all I care!_
Um, what's going on?
_Is it not clear? It is not a good time to grow confused, [N]. My work in Avadon is done. I am taking my records, and I am leaving. The Black Fortress can crumble into dust, for all I care!_
Why are you betraying Avadon?

_Avadon!_ She spits out the word. _A thousand curses on its name! When I came here with my husband, we thought to be loyal servants. Then we saw the corruption. We saw how distant and arbitrary Redbeard had become._
_I was still content to serve. Loyal, but with regret. My poor, foolish husband was more idealistic._
But you were Redbeard's most loyal servant!

_His most loyal slave! Redbeard long ago became distant and arbitrary, and his Hands were fully corrupt. When my husband and I came here, we thought we could improve things. I soon gave up on that foolish dream. He was more idealistic._
And what happened?

_He tried to kill Redbeard. He failed. I was forced to renounce my darling before his eyes. Then Redbeard had him killed. To save my own life, I swore total loyalty to Redbeard. I groveled. I abased myself. And I dreamed of revenge._
So you are behind everything that has happened. The dead Hands. The chaos across Lynaeus.
_Don't be foolish. I have been very valuable, but I am not the source of the attacks against the Pact. I've been a useful tool to Avadon's enemies, and no more._
Do you know who attacked Avadon?
_The Farlands. The enemies of the Pact. The oppressed, who are going to crush Avadon into dust and win their freedom from the Pact's rule._
Miranda's eyes get a mad glint. _Those who tolerated all of the corruption, the cruelty, the deaths of those who would make things better, they will all pay._
Why are you telling me all this?
_Not because I like to talk. I tell you because you are my special creation. You were groomed by me to see all of the weaknesses of Avadon. In you, I saw the potential. At last, the true potential._
I've heard enough about your treachery. (Attack.)
You try to take Heart Miranda by surprise. It doesn't work. She raises her wand and edges ever closer to the portal that can carry her to safety.
_I thought we might turn you, that you might replace Redbeard. Keeper [N]! Instead, you are as servile as all the others!_ With a word of command, power flies out of the wand.
Potential for what?

_Potential to strike down Redbeard at last! Potential to become Keeper! Keeper [N]! You could do it, I thought, if you were properly pushed. Surrounded by potential traitors. Tempted and taught by the Wayfarer._
Surrounded by traitors?

_I gathered all of the Hands of the most dubious loyalty, the ones with the greatest grudges against Avadon, I partnered them with you. Your friends are not powerful enough to change anything. Too arrogant, or inept, or confused._
_Their purpose was to shake your loyalty, or, if nothing else, to show you the true nature of Redbeard's power._
You sent the Wayfarer?

_He is one of the most loyal and effective servants of the enemies of Avadon. At my suggestion, he was sent to instruct you in just how corrupt Avadon was. He tried to teach you how much The Black Fortress misuses its power._
Enough talking. What do you want, Miranda?
_I've seen how well you fight. How much cunning you have, how much skill. I want you to take the power you deserve, that you were destined to have._
_Redbeard is up there now. Up in his tower. He may be dead, but, knowing how hardy that old serpent is, probably not. You must go up there and strike him down. Become the Keeper!_
You truly think that I can succeed?
_I think you have as good a chance as is possible. Redbeard has been thrown off-balance. You can take him by surprise._
Isn't this just a trick to weaken Avadon further?
_Perhaps. It will weaken Avadon in the short term, while you consolidate your power. And yet, in the long run, it might be the thing that saves Avadon._
Why do you want to see Avadon with a new Keeper?
_The Pact, as it exists now, is doomed. However, Avadon might be useful to a newer, reduced Pact. I hate Redbeard, but I still care about the people he failed to look after._
I am loyal to Redbeard and Avadon, whatever its flaws.
Miranda nods somberly. _Then my noble effort to turn you has failed. Oh, well. We have plenty of other ways to destroy the old tyrant. We will manage._
I will unseat Redbeard and become Keeper.
Miranda is relieved. _Some thought that my efforts were a waste of time. I will be pleased to report that they were not._

_Redbeard is in his tower, if he still lives. Find your allies. They arrived ahead of you and have already gone to the tower. Sway them to your cause, find the old serpent, and strike him down. As for me, I must leave. It would mean my death to stay._
What happens now?
_Now you die. You have revealed to me that you know too much. We can't let you live._ She points her wand at you and mutters a word of power. Energy flows from the tip ...
What will you do now?
_I will leave for my new home in the Farlands. We will work to destroy Avadon and slay Redbeard, if he lives. My vengeance has only just begun._
No. A traitor like you can't be allowed to live. (Attack.)
Then go.
Miranda salutes you with her wand. _Safe travels, [N], and a final warning. This ship is sinking. I suggest that you find a new home. Otherwise, we will have no choice but to destroy you._

Then she turns and steps through the portal. Moments after she vanishes, the field of energy begins to warp and flicker. The city within fades away. Following her through the portal is impossible. Miranda is gone. You suddenly feel a great need to find Redbeard. He is most likely to be in his tower.
No. You are too dangerous. You need to die. (Attack.)

_Tying up loose ends, eh? You show great potential. You seem like a Keeper of Avadon already. And yet, if you don't mind, I choose not to die today._ With a word of command, power flies out of the wand.
Goodbye, Miranda.
_Farewell, [N]. Safe travels to you, and good luck. You hunt the most dangerous of prey. I hope, for all our sakes, that you succeed._
So much to ponder.
I have my sworn duty.
It is good to see you.
Curse these walls.
Come, my servant.
This room is secure.
I am ready to serve.
I want to fight.
I am bored.
My talents are wasted.
We should go hunting.
Talking: Nicodemus watches the fight with interest. He makes no move to help you.
I will keep watch.
You are a new Hand?
I wait to be called.
I will regain my honor.
I can still fight.
When will I be called?
Is all well?
Do we have a new mission?
I am eager to hunt.
You are [N]?
I have been waiting.
There are two people talking back here. When you get close, they leave very quickly. Odd.
Lady Antje
Lady Antje calls to the wood spirits. You feel a powerful presence nearby, shielding her.
Corrupted Beast
Khemerian Warrior
Talking: Lord Carsta'Arl watches your battle with his wizard without saying a word. Or lifting a finger to help.
Dagobert of the Forge
Khemerian Cultist
Dagobert lets out a roar of rage! He starts to attack you with renewed vigor.
Your attacks are starting to wear Dagobert down. He lets out a roar and attacks you with berserk fury.
Hunter Klement
Fuzzy
Leggy
Merchant
Oghrym'Tor Guard
Charmed Guard
Defender Familiar
Khemerian Master
Shaman Romy
Escaped Titan
High Torturer
Assistant Torturer
You hear the sound of steel grinding over stone. It comes from somewhere nearby.
Clang!
Clang! Clang!
Hmmph.
Avadon. Bah.
Come, seeker.
This is my center of power.
You come for my lord?
Do not fear.
Fascinating.
Quality gear.
Seems trained.
A dangerous foe.
A word, if you please.
The dread lord awaits.
I will not trouble you.
You'll get what you deserve.
Step forward.
I will grant an audience.
You cost me my wizard.
It was a great loss.
I did what Avadon asked.
The three images of Carsta'Arl shimmer and switch places.
Warped Ratling
The sign says - NORTHWEST RING. Lady Antje's Grove.
The sign says - SOUTH RING. Moritz'Kri's Workshop.
The sign says - WEST RING. Courtyard. Audience Hall.
The sign says - NORTHEAST RING. Barracks. Training.
The sign says - SOUTHEAST RING. Lord's Hall.

You enter Oghrym'Tor, the stone fortress from which Dhorl Stead is ruled. Khemerian architecture lacks all subtlety. Most of the walls are short and thick, made of rough-hewn blocks of granite crudely mortared together.

Signs of the viciousness of the Khemerians are everywhere. This is no sophisticated castle of Kellemderiel. Gruesome trophies line the paths, and stocks wait ready for anyone who angers Lord Carsta'Arl.
Nathalie looks around and smirks. _Back in Kellemderiel, even our privies are better made. And better smelling, as well._
Past the entry courtyard, you can see a large hall to the east. That must be where the rulers of this place await you. In fact, as soon as you enter, the wizard Moritz'Kri emerges to meet you.

You enter the throne room of Lord Carsta'Arl. There is a wide carpet in the center of the room. Supplicants stand there as they plead for aid. The blood spatters on the fabric provide a hint of how that usually goes.

Lord Carsta'Arl himself sits in his throne and watches you. He is well into middle-age, but he maintains much of his muscle. He wears an old suit of fine plate armor, imported long ago and at great expense from the Tawon Empire.
You meet the gaze of this old warrior and despot. This is his throne room, so he does not rise. However, his arrogant demeanor fades quickly as the Hands of Avadon approach.
Shima leans close to you and whispers, _He hides it well, but he is afraid. And he is not used to being afraid. Be wary. He is unpredictable._
Oghrym'Tor is five rings of stone, arranged in a circle. You instantly sense that this ring is occupied by the wizard Moritz'Kri. Raw magic is heavy in the air.
It is quiet. The rogue mage has left no guards or other defenders. You smell smoke. And, you think, blood.
Nathalie is instantly alert. The chance to duel a wizard has filled her with worrying enthusiasm.

Moritz'Kri maintains a small magical workshop here. The walls are scorched, and several dead youths are lying on the floor. His apprentices, freshly killed. For some reason, he destroyed them as he passed through.
The wizard is cornered in his lair. Trapped, afraid, and ready to kill indiscriminately.

Oghrym'Tor is five rings of stone, arranged in a circle. This ring is full of thick vegetation. The plants are carefully tended, green, and amazingly thick and lush. Wildlife watches you from the undergrowth.
Jenell looks around and sniffs the air. _There is one of my kind here. A servant of nature, serving a place of darkness._
You hear a soft, musical voice, coming from deeper in the grove. _Visitors? I am pleased. Come. I would meet you._

This ring of Oghrym'Tor is for the warriors. Their barracks are here. And their training fields. And the smithy and dining hall. It is a self-contained world, where they prepare to unleash wild savagery on the nearby Steads.
If there is anyplace you would expect to meet fierce resistance, it would be here. And yet it is empty and quiet.
_Too quiet,_ Sevilin whispers.
You emerge from the tunnels under the fortress into the fresh air. You have managed to slip into another ring.
This ring of Oghrym'Tor is reserved for Lord Carsta'Arl. The ancestral wooden hall of his clan is here before you. Oghrym'Tor was built around it, and it is still here. Old, sagging, but intact.

The five rings of Oghrym'Tor surround a central clearing. It is full of lush vegetation, tended to by the late Lady Antje. None of the violence and destruction that have creeped through Oghrym'Tor have come here. Yet.
To the northwest, on the other side of a small lake, you hear a horn. A long, harsh note. A call of challenge. At last, cornered and bereft of servants, Lord Carsta'Arl is calling you to battle.

The passage ahead is natural, a long curving stone passage under the Khemerian fortress. The walls, floor, and ceiling are covered with globules of green slime. The air reeks of vinegar and sulfur. Bones crunch underfoot.
On the wall, you recognize the symbol of Moritz'Kri. The passage ahead must contain the last of his vile experiments. You can finally rid the world of the last of that monster's creations.
You return to the fortress Oghrym'Tor. You expected a vigorous defense. Warriors and shamans, led by Carsta'Arl.

Instead, there is nobody here. Everything is quiet. The forge is cold. The merchants and guards are gone. The keep seems abandoned, but you know better. The only way Lord Carsta'Arl will leave his ancestral fortress is feet first.
He is here somewhere, waiting for you.
This huge, natural chamber is dominated by a black, clear pool of water. It is both an emergency reservoir and a quiet retreat for residents of the fort.

As you get close to the wall here, you think you hear something. You lean closer. It sounds like scratching. You realize what you are hearing but, before you can back away, rocks fall away from the wall, revealing a low tunnel.
Then a cloud of foul gas billows out. You start to gasp and choke.
As you walk down this passage, mist begins to rise from the pools to either side. The ground grows very slippery. It becomes impossible to move quickly without falling.

You immediately suspect an ambush. You are not disappointed. Suddenly, archers step out from behind the huge stone pillars to the east and west. As you look around for a place to take shelter, you are sprayed with projectiles.
Khemerian Sharpshooter
Khemerian Hunter
There is a wheel here. A chain emerged from a hole in the ground and wraps around the wheel. With great effort, you are able to turn the wheel enough to pull up about four feet of chain, but no more.
Then you hear a grinding sound. The wheel is stuck.
You try to turn this wheel, but it is still stuck.
Lord Carsta'Arl reaches the gate separating you from the grove in the center of the fortress. His misty body floats through the iron bars and grows solid again.
He looks back at you. _If you would fight a lord of the Dhorla, you will earn the privilege!_ Then he walks off.
You have delivered a solid blow to Moritz'Kri. He stumbles back and then ... starts to crumble. He screams. His body bursts into flame. Smoke billows out. He crumbles into a pile of black dust.

This impressive pyrotechnic illusion would be enough to fool anyone else, but not someone of your training. You notice a faint wisp of smoke break off from the bitter cloud and float away to the west.
Lord Carsta'Arl smiles wryly and starts to applaud.
As you approach Moritz'Kri, he shakes his head. _I was already impolite to speak before my lord. Now you must talk to him. I'm sure he will give you all that you deserve._
There are several merchants here, come to deliver goods to Oghrym'Tor. They all get very silent when you approach.
Some of them are Farlanders. Others are from the Pact, selling goods to these dangerous outsiders. Either way, they have no reason to seek out the attention of Avadon.

The guards of Oghrym'Tor are powerful and vicious warriors, skilled enough to present a challenge even to the envoys of Avadon. These proud Khemerians have no desire to talk to you. They do snarl a bit, though.
Antje collapses. Her wood spirits fade away. The light in the grove grows a little fainter. The plants seem to shrink back a little. As she dies, her magic rapidly fades.
She rolls over onto her back and looks toward the grove in the center of the fortress. _Carsta ..._ she gasps. _I ... I failed you ... I am sorry._ And then her eyes close for the last time.

Lady Antje throws her arms wide, looks up at the sky, and lets out a keening howl. A cold wind blows through the grove. You feel that a new, powerful presence has entered the grove, but you aren't sure where.

Antje looks at you, and you realize that her form has grown indistinct. There is a strange, shimmering barrier around her. Something has started to protect her. She lets out a mocking laugh. _Now you see what happens when you fight a shaman in her place of power!_
With one final blow, the Khemerians now have one less master smith. He crumples to the ground. A spiked gauntlet falls from one of his fists and rolls a few feet away.
Another defender of Lord Carsta'Arl has fallen, but you are still far from where he is making his final stand.
There is a massive titan standing on this stone platform. Damaged chains hang from his wrists. They didn't break, though. Acid has eaten them away.

The beast lumbers into the light, and you get a good look at it. You have seen a lot of Moritz'Kri's horrors, but this beast is exceptionally hideous. Its skeleton is twisted, its skin is pallid and green, and its whole body is covered with green pustules. Sometimes they pop, letting out clouds of acrid gas.
It is disgusting.
Then the corrupted titan lumbers toward you. Conversation would do no good. The beast is entirely mindless. All it knows is that it sees potential food.
The titan stops moving. At first, it only seems vaguely ill, discomforted. ÊThen its entire body spasms and a few of its many pustules start to inflate and pop, releasing a cloud of vile acid.
Now that it is not moving, you could get away from it without it stopping you. Might be wise.
The titan's pustules stop popping. It seems to return to its senses. Then it lumbers toward you again, letting out an angry gurgling noise.

The titan is mortally wounded. It falls to the ground. The acid infusing its body is no longer safely contained. Its sickly green flesh starts to bubble and dissolve. In minutes, there is nothing left of the creature (and Moritz'Kri's mad work) but a pool of hissing goo. You keep a safe distance, as it smells kind of bad.

Hunter Klement is the next defender to fall before your attacks. As he falls, he looks terribly embarrassed. _How did I go wrong?_ he moans. _A better bow? A more direct attack? Less banter? More spiders? What did I do wrong? I ... Aaaarrrghhhhh._ And he dies.
You search through his pockets and find a crude iron key. You keep it.

Lord Carsta'Arl falls to the ground. His doppelgangers fade away. From the ground, he looks in the direction of where Lady Antje fell. He coughs and gasps. Then he apologizes. Not to her, but to his ancestors.

_Father ... grandfather ..._ he gasps. _It is all lost. All fallen. The other Steads ... they will ... will ... I am sorry._ And then, overwhelmed with the magnitude of all his people have lost, he dies. Merciful, really.
The justice of Avadon has been done. All miscreants have been dispatched. You are free to return home.
You realize that, as solid as the three Khemerians look, only one of them is real. The others are illusions.

As you watch them carefully, trying to figure out where to strike, they shimmer. Then they trade places, moving faster than your eye can track. Even when you are sure which one is real, a moment later it has moved.
Name
Once again, you meet Moritz'Kri, the head wizard of Dhorl Stead. You last saw him when he attacked the Shadow Beast. Now he is waiting at the end of Lord Carsta'Arl's hall. He isn't happy to see you.

He gives you a perfunctory bow. _So the Hand of Avadon has returned to us. [N], was it? I suppose you have stopped by our fortress for a reason. Perhaps I can help you, so that you don't need to stay here longer than necessary?_
Have you learned anything about where the Shadow Beast came from?
_Not yet, but I assure you that I am sparing no effort in tracking down the source of the creature. If you leave and return later, there may be more I can tell you._
Stand aside. I will speak to your Lord and nobody else.
Moritz'Kri starts to speak, but then he thinks better of it. _I can see that you are determined. I'm sure that Lord Carsta'Arl would be happy to aid you._ He turns and walks back into the hall.
Perhaps you can help me.
He smiles. _Of course. Why have you returned to Dhorl Stead?_
The Shadow Beast was created by a wizard. I have been sent to find out who.

Moritz'Kri seems interested. _Really? It is definitely a possibility, but we can't be sure how the Shadow Beast was created. Maybe it was not made by a wizard at all. I will continue to investigate and let you know what I learn._
I believe the Shadow Beast was created by you. We need to speak of it.
Moritz'Kri nods, unconcerned. _An understandable suspicion. And yet, we don't even know if the beast was created. Maybe it arrived from elsewhere and just took up residence in those caves._
_If you have proof I was involved, I would like to see it. Otherwise, I will attend to my lord._ He turns and walks back into the hall.
Actually, I will speak with your Lord instead.
_I ... see. Of course, I will not stand in the way of Avadon. I doubt that our Lord can tell you anything I couldn't, but ..._ He steps back. Then he turns and walks back into the hall.
I don't need anything else here.
_We are most relieved. Feel free to stop by the smithy to get any repairs you need before you leave._ He turns and walks back into the hall.

You step forward to face Lord Carsta'Arl, the warlord that commands Dhorl Stead and all of the lands around it. He nods to you somberly. You can't tell whether he is being ceremonial or just very cautious.

_It has been some time since I have had the honor of a visit from the envoys of Avadon. I am Carsta'Arl, as I am sure you know. Master of these lands. And you are [N], yes? We welcome you with all honors you are due._
He pauses. Everyone in attendance leans forward expectantly. _How can I help you?_
Why was I not allowed into this fortress before?

_Ahhh ... That was most unfortunate. I was not informed that a Hand of Avadon was here. Had I known, the gates would have been thrown open instantly. Rest assured that those responsible have been savagely punished._
I am here to locate a certain wizard, who has broken the laws of Avadon.

There is a long silence. Carsta'Arl looks nervous. Moritz'Kri takes a slight step closer. _I understand. And I suppose that this regards the strange creature you and Moritz'Kri, working together, hunted down in our woods._
_But what do you need from me?_
I am here to find out where the Shadow Beast came from.
_Ah ... yes. This regards the strange creature you hunted down in our woods. A mysterious beast, and I am happy that you and Moritz'Kri, working together, rid us of it._
I need to find the Farlander wizard who created the beast. This violated the laws of the Pact.

_But I am told that the beast just appeared in our woods! You found it in an abandoned cave, yes? There was old magical equipment there, or so I am told, but that is not proof that the creature was made there._
_There is no evidence that a Farlander made the creature, is there?
The flesh samples we took from the creature prove a wizard's involvement.

Lord Carsta'Arl nods somberly, as if considering this. Of course, he knows as little as you about the samples or the tests performed on them. All he knows is that Avadon is here, and it must be satisfied.
_So it was made by a wizard. And you need the wizard._
My superiors have told me that they are sure. The evidence was enough for them, so it is enough for me.
Lord Carsta'Arl nods somberly. _Then there is nothing to debate. A decision has been made, and the Farlanders must submit. Avadon is here and must be satisfied._
_The thing was made by a wizard. And you need the wizard._
I am from Avadon. I don't need evidence. There is a criminal mage here somewhere, and I will not stop until justice is done.

Lord Carsta'Arl nods somberly. _I have lived my life under the watch of Avadon. I know that appealing to justice never works, but I must still try it from time to time. Avadon is here and must be satisfied._
That is so.

Lord Carsta'Arl is silent. The hall grows very quiet and tense. The guards don't know what is going on. Moritz'Kri's hands tighten into fists. The lord ponders his options, determined to appease Avadon while giving away as little as possible.

Finally, he makes a decision. He looks up at you. _I had heard the warnings. I had been told that I must act. Now I am forced. I regret greatly what I must do._ Moritz'Kri, hearing this, grins viciously.
What are you saying?

The aging lord sighs. When he speaks again, his voice is loud, so that there can be no confusion about his words. _Moritz'Kri, I had been warned that you were up to strange experiments in that tower of yours._
_I knew nothing of what you were doing. Nothing! I should have been more alert. Now I know that you were creating abominations. For that crime, you will have to pay._
Moritz'Kri's vicious grin fades instantly. _What? You abandon me? After all ... After ... You are giving in to them? Coward! Lickspittle!_
Carsta'Arl stares straight ahead, ignoring this tirade.
Moritz'Kri, you are under arrest. Come with me.
Moritz'Kri looks to Carsta'Arl and the guards for support. They look away. He snarls. _You come into this hall and challenge me? You are far from home, Avadon, and you will die for your arrogance!_
He stretches out his fingers, and flames fly from them. The guards watch with great interest, but they do not intervene.
Carsta'Arl, have your guards subdue the criminal.
Carsta'Arl shakes his head. _He is your prisoner. You will take him yourself. If he will be taken._
At that, the wizard stretches out his fingers, and flames fly from them. Moritz'Kri says, _Avadon, you will die for your arrogance!_ The guards watch with great interest, but they do not intervene.
Moritz'Kri, you will die for what you have done. (Attack him.)
As you draw your weapon, Moritz'Kri snarls. _You come into this hall and challenge me? You are far from home, Avadon, and you will die for your arrogance!_
Lord Carsta'Arl looks at the sooty smear on the ground where Moritz'Kri was. _A fascinating trick. The wizard has many, you will find. I withdraw my protection from him. He is your prey now._
_I will make sure that the gates to his part of Oghrym'Tor are open._
Where did he go?

_I have seen him use such magic before. When he has used such spells, it has been to retire to his ring of the fortress. It is just to the south. I will make sure that you have entry. He may be there now._
You expect me to believe you didn't know what he was doing?

The lord instantly grows angry. _You can enter my hall. You can take away my prized wizard. You will not call me liar in front of my warriors! If you anger me enough, I will slay you, whatever the consequences._
He waves you away. _Go. Find your prey._
You will find the wizard and bring him to me.

Lord Carsta'Arl shakes his head, clearly annoyed. _You can enter my hall. You can take away my prized wizard. I have lost him. Now he is your problem, and I will not sacrifice my warriors hunting him for you._
I will go and hunt him now.
_Then I would start your hunt in the ring of the fortress to the south. Go quickly. Otherwise, the wizard may flee. And, if he has fled already, you might find out where he has gone._
He waves you away. _I have done all I can for you. Go. Find your prey._
Jenell looks at all of the books with disgust. _Records? Laws? Paperwork? Forms? What is this? The Kva? They have abandoned everything that makes our people great!_
Nathalie sighs. _Yes. Yes. The Khemerians are bad. Very bad. Let's go._
Sevilin says, _I don't see what's bad with a little codification. I ..._ Jenell glares at him. _Never mind._
Nathalie is moving slowly. Her wounded arm is bothering her. She keeps prodding at it with her finger and then wincing in pain.
She mutters quietly, _They're laughing at me back at Avadon. I'm sure of it. Waiting to see me slow down. To fail. Never. Never._
Shima looks at her with concern, then at you. Then he shrugs.
Sevilin looks at her with concern. Then he edges away from her slightly.
Maybe you should go back to Avadon.
_I would rather die,_ she says, and you believe her. She walks on in grim silence.
Do you need anything?
_Only to advance and fight. This is all I wanted. I will not slow down._ She walks on in grim silence.

Jenell looks around in fascination. _I never thought I would see this much of a Khemerian fortress. And to be able to do so while destroying it ... It seemed like too much to hope for. Being with Avadon does have its advantages._
You enter Lord Carsta'Arl's torture chambers. Unimaginable suffering has taken place in here. Sevilin shakes his head. _Such madness. All the lives lost here, because of Carsta'Arl's whims._
Shima looks over at him. _Are you saying that The Kva doesn't have a thousand rooms like this one in its fortresses?_
Nathalie looks over at him. _Are you saying that The Kva doesn't have a thousand rooms like this one in its fortresses?_
Jenell looks over at him. _Are you saying that The Kva doesn't have a thousand rooms like this one in its fortresses?_

Sevilin nods. _Of course we do have such chambers in The Kva, but we are far more organized about it. People are only ever tortured due to strict legal principles. I think that makes all the difference._
Lord Carsta'Arl sits in his throne. Warriors and scribes still walk around, trying their best to keep the fortress running normally despite the recent ugliness.
He says, _What else do you need? I have proved my willingness to aid Avadon._
There is something I need to discuss with you.
He shakes his head. _As long as there may be a dangerous fugitive in my fortress, I cannot concentrate properly. You should go south and search Moritz'Kri's ring._
_And be careful. It would be unfortunate if a trap kept you from leaving his halls alive._
I have driven Moritz'Kri out.

_That is good. I thank you for sparing my people from his retribution. Moritz'Kri is not welcome in my lands. He will find no succor here. That is all the aid I will give you in this matter. I am done with it._
How did you become lord of Dhorl Stead?
_My great grandfather was a chieftain of Dhorl Stead. He was the first to adopt the glorious new ways. He laid the first stone of this mighty fortress with his own hands._
_Since then, my clan has passed down the rulership from father to son, and each of us has done all we can to bring safety to our Stead._
Jenell says, _That is not the way of our people. True leaders earn their power. It is not just given._
Who decided that you would follow your father as lord?
_My father did. Some objected. He buried their heads in our gardens. They still feed my lady's plants. This is the way of Khemeria._
How does the Stead feel about you having power?
_Why should I concern myself about that? Does Avadon worry about the carping of every powerless nothing who objects to its rules?_
_These are the ways of Khemeria, and you don't need to concern yourself with them. If those who oppose me were strong enough to unseat me, they would do so. If not, they do not deserve this throne._
Did Avadon approve of you taking power?
_Avadon did not notice or care. As long as its rules are obeyed, it doesn't care who is in charge or what we do or who we punish or how we punish them._
I care.
_Everyone is allowed their hobbies. Their eccentricities. You might care, but Redbeard does not._
_What else do you need?_
As it should be. All we need is obedience.
_And you have it. You have taken my prized wizard. However, I will not be judged by you. You have obedience. That is all._
I want to know more about Dhorl Stead.
_We are one of many Steads in Khemeria, all butting up against each other. All building stone keeps and fighting and shedding blood for the same land._
_I do all I can to keep Dhorl Stead safe and strong. It is my sworn duty to my people. That is why I kept Moritz'Kri with me and ignored his ... shortcomings._
Do the other Steads threaten you?
_Of course. It is the way of Khemeria. If I ever show weakness, if I ever fell, their raiders will pour into our woods. They will slaughter the men and then ... It will be ugly._
_My rule is harsh, I admit, but I do all I can to avoid that fate._
How did Moritz'Kri help you?
_Khemeria has shamans, and they are useful. They have their little tricks, learned in the hedges._
With great effort, Jenell manages to hold her tongue.
_But mages, that call fire and lightning from the skies, they are true power. Moritz'Kri was a great aid to us. It is sad that he must be taken._
How do you defend yourself from the other Steads?

_By attacking them! If they are weak, if they are losing their lands, if their warriors have been slain, they cannot attack us! When I lead our raiders and take their land, they are less able to threaten us._
And are you at war now?
_Of course. In Khemeria, the war never ends. It keeps us strong. And, should the Pact ever weaken and fall, we will be ready to take our place as a true power._
_I hope I live to see the day._
I still need to hunt down Moritz'Kri.
_I have released him to you. He is no longer welcome here. What happens now is between him and Avadon. I am not involved._
Why was Moritz'Kri creating those monstrosities?
_I don't understand the ways of wizards. The practice of the art can leave them ... unhinged._
He looks at Nathalie. _No offense intended._ She smiles.
And you really knew nothing of what Moritz'Kri was doing?
He grows flushed, but he holds his temper. _You accuse me of what, in the eyes of Avadon, is a serious crime. I knew nothing of what he was doing in his tower._
Shima whispers to you, _That is a lie, of course. He knew something. But how much?_
Sevilin whispers to you, _That is a lie, of course. He knew something. But how much?_
Where might I find the wizard?
_If he has fled our lands, you may never find him._

_However, if he is still near, you will find him in his tower, in the Dhorla Woods. He might be foolish enough to take a stand there, or he might be delayed there while he gathers his treasures and tomes._
I will require your assistance.
_I will send none of my warriors into the tower of an angry wizard. Complain to Avadon if you wish. This decision is final._
Moritz'Kri is dead.
_I knew it would be thus. He angered Avadon. He paid their price. I only hope that Dhorl Stead will not suffer for it._
Will you be able to defend yourself?
_Of course. We will train harder. We will be more vicious. We will resume night raids, slitting the throats of the enemy as they sleep. We can no longer afford to be weak or hesitant._
_This is what the gaze of Avadon brings._
Why don't you get a new mage?
_You think it is simple? Mages of skill are very rare anywhere in Lynaeus. Moritz'Kri was a unique prize. He cannot be replaced._
Then he looks at Nathalie and smiles. _Unless you are available for hire?_
Nathalie laughs at the warlord's suggestion. _I am sure you would make proper use of me, but I am happy with my current position, thank you._
That is all I need here.
_Then I hope that you will speak with our merchants before you leave. Tell Avadon. We are not its foes. You do not need to punish Dhorl Stead._

At last, you find someone in Oghrym'Tor. It is Lord Carsta'Arl himself, sitting on his throne. His drawn blade lies across his lap, and he holds a small, glass globe in his left hand. It is full of swirling gray mist.
He looks across at you, and this time the fear in his eyes is clear. He knows that, after a lifetime spent behind thick walls, his destruction has come. He is struggling to face it with dignity.
_So,_ he says, _Avadon has returned. It is no surprise. Some of us still live, after all. Tell me, [N]. Why have you come. Say the words._
There does not need to be violence.
_Oh, but there does. I assure you of that. You are young, but you still must see there is no other way. I have duties, and they are sacred._
I know that you were giving Moritz'Kri the supplies for his experiments.
He laughs. _Of course I was. I will lie no longer. I had no choice. I will break every law Avadon has if that is what it takes for my clan to not fall!_
Lord Carsta'Arl of Khemeria, I have been sent to bring you to Avadon.
_Of course you have. You know that I was supplying Moritz'Kri, yes? I knew I was taking a risk, and now I lose all. It was necessary for my Stead to survive. It was my duty._
Why did you help Moritz'Kri?

_The neighboring Steads grew stronger every year. They plot against us. We were in true danger. And Moritz'Kri came to me. He promised power. An army of undead horrors. Packs of lethal warbeasts. All I needed to beat back our attackers and make them pay!_
Did you realize what horrors your wizard unleashed on Dhorl Stead?
_Of course I did. Unfortunate, all of it. But Moritz'Kri made good on his promise. I did gain power. Soon, you will face it yourself._
The wizard experimented on your people.
_I send people to die every day, to keep us all safe. It is their duty. This is no different._
You broke the Pact's laws. Now you must submit or die.
_And if I choose to die? If I say I will never return to the Black Fortress? What then?_
You can say all of this back at Avadon.
_So that my mind can be stripped clean in your dungeons? All secrets lost and my people abandoned? Well, I will never return to the Black Fortress. What do you say to that?_
I will have to think about that. (Leave.)
Lord Carsta'Arl says, _I appreciate the reprieve. All the more time to prepare the defenses of my people, should I fall. I will await your return and the final reckoning._
I will force you to come with me. Orders are orders.

Lord Carsta'Arl lets out a deep sigh. He picks up a goblet and takes a final swig of wine. _So be it. Let the chase begin._ Then he raises the glass globe over his head. You lunge forward, and he crushes it in his mailed fist.

Mist emerges from the glass and wraps around Carsta'Arl. In a moment, he has taken the form of mist. He says, in a spectral voice, _One of my wizard's gifts. It will last just long enough ..._ And he drifts down the hall to the east.
Actually, I've been waiting for my chance to kill you. (Attack.)
As you charge, Carsta'Arl raises the glass globe over his head. You lunge forward, and he crushes it in his mailed fist.

A blacksmith has been allowed to set up this forge just inside of the gates of the fortress, right next to the main audience hall. The sound of hammers ringing against blades must be constantly audible within.

The smith is a massive Khemerian, over six feet tall and mighty of thew. When you greet him, he gives you a grim little salute with his hammer. He wears a pair of massive steel gauntlets, with little spikes protruding from the fingers.
_I am Dagobert of the Forge,_ he says in a deep voice. _Honored to be the personal smith of Lord Carsta'Arl. I have been told to trade with you, so that Avadon can see our skill in weaponcraft._
Dagobert of the Forge hammers at a steel blade as he talks to you. He never removes his steel, spiked gauntlets. You are sure that their metal points have little bits of flesh stuck to them.
Why is the forge inside the fortress?
_Because, when Lord Carsta'Arl deals with the lords of the other steads, he wants them to hear me make blades. The blades that will be butchering their soldiers._
_It is an honor and a reminder._
An honor for you?
_Of course. All know that my steelwork is the finest in Khemeria._
A reminder of what?
_The sound of my forge tells everyone we are not weaklings like the Tawon or the Kellem. We are not backward followers of the old ways, like the Wyldrylm. We are Khemeria. We are born to kill._
Tell me about your crafts.

_I work steel. My blades keep their edge better than any in our land. They last longer, they bend farther without breaking. Because I am commanded, I can sell them to you, so you can see how mighty they are and can be afraid._
What makes you think they are so good?

_I wield them myself. I am no coward smith that never leaves the forge. I test my weapons myself. Carsta'Arl hates it, but he knows I insist. I only call a blade from my hand great when I have taken a life with it._
Who do you kill?
_Wretches. Ogres. Other Khemer. Wyldrylm raiders, once they have entered my land and are fair game._ He gives you an ugly grin. _Nothing that would break your laws, Avadon._
And your spiked gauntlets?
He flexes his fingers. _My own invention, for me alone. Sometimes, I kill with these alone, for my own amusement._
Dagobert's steelwork is like the man himself. Ugly, powerfully made, and very dangerous.
He nods, and, without another word, returns to his work.
There is a beautiful young woman walking through the grove that fills this ring of the fortress. She is a shaman, something you don't see frequently in Khemeria.

She turns to you and gives you a smile and a little bow. She is trying to seem harmless, but you can see the glint of steel in her eyes and sense the beasts concealed in the thickets that surround you.
She says, _Welcome, Hand, to my grove. I am Antje, Lady of Oghrym'Tor. We have so few visitors that I wanted to make sure to see you in person._

Lady Antje reclines on a marble bench and looks up at you. The air is cool and pleasant, and the sun shines down upon your skin. This ring should be tranquil, but you sense beasts constantly closing in on you from all sides.
_What else do you wish to speak of, Hand?_
You are Lord Carsta'Arl's wife?
_I have that honor. Of many possible partners, he chose me. He recognized my power, and he knows that the old ways still have their uses._
Isn't he a bit older than you?
Her eyes glint with a flicker of annoyance. _My lord is more ... energetic than any four men half his age. You don't need to worry about the details of our partnership._
And he uses your powers?
_Of course. Mages are useful, but Moritz'Kri is too arrogant to understand that there are things only shamans can do and only shamans can see._
What do you think of Moritz'Kri?
_That he is about to suffer the punishment he has earned for making such abominations against nature._
_He created abominations against nature. I regret the loss of his power, but not his much deserved death._
Why did he choose you?
_Because all rivals for his attention faded before my beauty and skill. Or disappeared while walking in the woods._
Disappeared?
She smiles demurely. _If one wishes to engage in power politics in Khemeria, one should know to take proper precautions. If one does not ..._ She smiles.
I have met few shamans here.
_There are very few. In fact, the only other nearby is that useless old fool Unni. Tired and preachy, she is. Happily, we will not have to tolerate her for long._
Why do you dislike her so?

_Because she doesn't understand that the only way the old ways can be allowed to exist is in the service of the new ways. It is the only way we can grow stronger. We keep what works and discard the rest._
She looks at Jenell, who has flushed red. _If it weren't for the Pact,_ Antje adds, _the Wyldrylm would have submitted to our might long ago._
Why won't she be around for long?
_Because she is old. Time always does us the kindness of erasing those with outdated ideas._
Tell me about this grove.
She looks around and smiles. _It is lovely, is it not? But it is not wasted, not merely a useless lovely thing like in Kellemderiel or the Wyldrylm._
She looks you in the eye. _It is a center of power, to defend us against those who would harm us._
Then she smiles and lets out a sigh that is almost girlish. _But it could be better. There is something that would make it perfect._
What is this grove for?
_What is its purpose? It provides a link between me and the earth. I can see far. I can hear much. I can call servants and send them to do my bidding._
Did you ever see the Shadow Beast from here?
_I could sense it. It was an abomination. When it was near, nature was closed to me. I only knew of its presence by a blackness in my vision. I am glad that you and Moritz'Kri destroyed it._
_A powerful wood totem. It was once in one of the neglected stone circles. Then Moritz'Kri took it into his tower._
_If you happened to find yourself in his tower, found the totem, and returned it to me, I would give you a reward worthy of my position._
Why would Moritz'Kri take it?
_His power is not our power. I think he thought that he could possess some of the might that is mine. He is foolish._
_Of course, now he is dead. A fit punishment._
I found the wooden totem. (Give it to her.)

You set the totem on the floor in front of her. She closes her eyes and rests her hand upon it. Soon, her features contort in grief and anger. She pulls her hand back. _That fool. He tried to warp its power to his will._
_It is damaged, and it will takes weeks of work to return it to a state I can use._
_Still, you deserve a reward for your aid to me. I would not cheat a Hand of Avadon._ She takes a pendant and a crystal from her pouch and hands them to you.
I gave that totem to Unni.

Lady Antje is enraged. You hear deep growls coming from the woods around you. _What? The totem was wasted on that old fool? She will probably just put it in some circle, out in the woods. I knew I should not has asked a Hand for help. Leave me!_
I will be going now.
_Then I will not keep you. I hope you find what you are seeking in our lands. And, of course, leave us._
There is a hunter casually leaning against this carved wooden pillar. He chews on a length of straw and watches you with an expression that could only be called 'insolent'.
But he is not a Khemerian. His armor is too ornate and his skin is too pale. In fact, you think he is from the Tawon Empire, another of the Farlands.
He smirks at you as you pass. _[N], yes? From Avadon? I wanted to get a chance to see you. I am Hunter Klement._
Hunter Klement is still watching you intently. Sizing you up, most likely. _Yes, it is interesting to see you. Very interesting._
_The Tawon Empire. Not ashamed to say it. The once great empire, that will be great again. The Pact won't endure._
You don't care for the Pact?
_You mean, do I like the Pact? I don't hate it. I don't like it. It is like a storm. Hard, but it ends._
Why don't you think the Pact will last?
He smiles as if amused by a private thought. _Nothing lasts. Everything dies. And the Tawon will rise again._
That sounds a lot like insolence, Farlander.
His smile fades. _I would not insult Avadon. We know how you respond. Let's talk about something else._
Let's talk about something else.
_A touchy topic. I see. What do you want to know?_

He leans back against the pillar and brushes some hair out of his eyes. _I am a fine hunter, one of the best in northern Lynaeus. But Tawon, despite its glories, is too civilized a land to truly test my skills._
And Lord Carsta'Arl allowed you to come?
_The lord is wise. He welcomes all who will help Dhorl Stead defend itself against its neighbors. Hunters. Wizards. Assassins._
You came here to hunt?
_Of course. Khemeria has the finest game in the northern Farlands. Spiders. Wolves. Khemerians. Of course, if I get bored here, I will have to go to the Corruption._
The Corruption?
_Far to the southwest. A place of wild, untamed magic. Some wizards went mad and tried to see how much damage they could do. Turns out, it was a lot._
_The creatures there ..._ He smiles. _Their heads would look very worthy on my wall back home._
Why did you want to see me?
_Wanted to see what sorts of warrior Avadon is sending out._ He inspects your gear. _Interesting._
And?
_It is interesting._
_I have been impressed. The only way I could learn more were if you and I were to test our skills against each other. I'm sure that will never happen._ He smiles.
Why are you evaluating me?
_Simple interest. Of course, I would love to have the chance to test your skills._
You don't have the right to test me, Farlander.
He nods. _Understood, and agreed. But I am allowed to be curious, and the test I had in mind would be interesting._
_I thank you for your time. Good day._
A test? I am interested.
_Well, I will let you settle your business here first. When you are ready to leave, see me again._
_Well, Lord Cartsa'Arl asked a favor of me. There is a flock of bats roaming the woods to the north. Strange creatures, that drain the life from those they attack. He asked for me to slay them._
_I tracked them, and I found where they are. It is a place I am forbidden to go. If you can slay them, I will give you a token of my respect._
Where are they?
_They nest in the hills just beyond Moritz'Kri's tower. I have been forbidden to go there by Carsta'Arl. I asked and was refused. You, however, can go there whether he allows it or not._
Are they dangerous?
_Oh, very dangerous. Maybe even lethal. I feel terrible about sending a Hand of Avadon into such danger._
I destroyed the bats by Moritz'Kri's tower.

You tell Klement the tale. He is fascinated. _Interesting. You have showed both drive and technique. I thought that Hands of Avadon would be slow and weak, bureaucrats and children of wealth. I was wrong._
He removes a bundle of javelins from his back and hands them to you. _These are very well-made, but they are too loud for my taste. I give them to you as tribute to your skill._
And you have no more tests?
_The only other test of value would be if you and I faced each other. I hope that never happens._ But, judging from the look in his eye, he would not mind at all.
It turns out, Moritz'Kri did not flee this fortress. He hid in his lair, gathering his notes and valuable supplies. He now stands in the middle of a ring of runes, several heavy satchels at his feet.
When he sees you, he sneers. _Too slow, Avadon. My cowardly lord forces me to retreat. I thought he must kill you._
_Instead, I return to my tower. You want to face me? You will do so in my place of power!_
What happened to your apprentices?
_I killed them. They knew about my great work. I didn't want to risk them telling you about it. No, you must visit me and see it first-hand._
I command you to return with me to Avadon. Right now! Don't make me count to ten!
Moritz'Kri snickers. _I am no errant child. I am a wizard, as fine as any of the Pact. When you see what I have done, you will tremble and submit to me!_
You are going to wait in your tower for me to kill you?
_No. I am going to wait in my tower for you to come and be devoured. What I have done will ... Well, why spoil the surprise?_
He laughs and mutters a word of power. Before you can stop him, he has vanished in a cloud of greasy black smoke, which wafts through the gates to the north.
There is no question this time. Moritz'Kri has left this fortress. Now the chase begins.
I will be at your tower soon enough.
_I am counting on it! The gates will be left open, ready for you to enter. And, when you see ... Well, why spoil the surprise?_
A lone shaman waits for you in this grove. She is a young, delicate, beautiful woman. She says, _I am Lady Antje of Oghrym'Tor. You have come to my grove, and to your death._
You return to the grove of Lady Antje and are surprised to find that she is still here, waiting for you.

She looks at you with loathing. Though there are no guards here, she seems unconcerned. She watches you approach silently, and, as you get closer, the plants seem to grow thicker and the shadows deeper.
_I knew it. The moment I heard that Avadon had come to Dhorl Stead, I knew this battle would come. Now your flesh will serve to feed my plants, and my pets._
How did you know that?
_Because that is what always happens. Avadon has power, and it loves to use it. It always finds a way to destroy us. It was that foolish girl Laurella who sent you, wasn't it?_
Jenell says, _Why must we talk to her? She defiles everything good. She must die._
How did you know of Laurella?

_Before she went to you, she came to us. Camped outside our keep night and day. How could we not notice her? It was only when we made clear that we were ready to kill her to end her pestering that she left._
_She thought she was so wise, when all she did was bring destruction._
None of this is necessary. I only came for Lord Carsta'Arl.

_My lord? You think my husband will submit to you? He is ten times the warrior you are! The moment I saw him, I knew he would rise to greatness! Avadon will never stop him! I will make sure he is not even troubled by you!_
Step aside, shaman. I have no quarrel with you.
_No quarrel? Now you will see just what an enemy you have made, by threatening my lord!_
She lets out a long, low snarl. It isn't a human sound, but the growl of a wolf. The sound is echoed from the undergrowth all around you. Antje, Lady of Dhorl Stead, calls for her allies to aid her.
You would stop me? You face the wrath of Avadon! (Attack.)
She nods. _Good. Yes. I protect my lord, or I die a true Khemerian!_

A lone man, massively muscular and wearing thick, hide armor, is waiting for you in the middle of the clearing. He has no weapon. Instead, he wears a pair of steel gauntlets, covered with spikes. He says, _I am Dagobert of the Forge, and I am ready to test my work._
Dagobert of the Forge is waiting for you in the middle of this clearing. He wears thick hide armor and his steel gauntlets, festooned with spikes. He smirks as you approach.
_My Lord is not yet ready to face you. He is taking a moment to mourn the loss of his lady. I have promised him that I will avenge her, or die trying._
Is nobody in this doomed fortress going to simply let me by?
_Surrender? Submit? We are not like the craven forest creatures of the Wyldrylm! Khemerians are born with only one question in their heads. 'Will I die well?'_
You really think you can face me alone?
_Alone? Who said anything about alone? No, to live, you will have to dull your blade on waves of our finest warriors! Khemerians, to arms!_
Dagobert blows his horn. Sure enough, moments later, you hear crazed war cries coming from all around you.
All right. It's your turn. Come on. (Attack.)
_My turn? Well, not just mine! Many wish for the right to avenge wise Lady Antje! I will not steal all the glory!_
As you charge, Dagobert blows his horn. Sure enough, moments later, you hear crazed war cries coming from all around you.

Unsurprisingly, a warrior is waiting for you in Lord Carsta'Arl's hall. However, it's not a Khemerian. His clothes and accent mark him as being from another of the Farlands, the Tawon Empire. He smirks at you. _I am Klement. I'm sorry I didn't get a chance to meet you before. Better late than never, eh?_

Unsurprisingly, a warrior is waiting for you in Lord Carsta'Arl's hall. It is Hunter Klement, the traveling warrior from the Tawon Empire. The circumstances are very different, but his smirk and swaggering attitude have not changed at all.

Like many hunters, he keeps animals at his side to aid him. They are not dogs or falcons, though, but spiders. Huge, drooling, tame spiders, each on a length of chain. _You noticed my pets, eh? I am not foolish. I will not set aside any fair advantage when dueling a warrior of Avadon._
You have pet spiders?
_Moritz'Kri offered his fascinating creations to protect Khemerians. For a price, I received a truly unique pair of pets. Terrifying, impressive, and able to catch small prey when it hides up trees._
You are here to defend Lord Carsta'Arl?

He laughs and spits on the lord's polished floor. _Lord Carsta'Arl? Like any true son of Tawon would care about any of these savages! I am not here to avenge anyone. I am here to try my skills against a true foe. At last I meet a warrior deserving of my attention!_
You intend to duel me?

_Of course. I have hunted all other game, animal, titan, and human, and never failed to show my skill. I will claim to be the finest hunter of the Tawon! All I have to do is risk myself in one final gamble. I will slay a Hand of Avadon. In success, I will be a legend!_
If you kill a Hand, Avadon will never let you live.

_Really?_ he smirks. _Very soon, Avadon will be unable to protect itself, let alone avenge its lost. Do you know how many Hands have been murdered in the last few months? Have they been avenged?_ He laughs.
_I think that was enough banter._ He drops the chains holding the spiders. _Fuzzy! Leggy! Attack!_
Is that glory really worth the risk?
_Bah! The people of the Pact have been safe and rich for too long. Now they are fat and lazy, unable to comprehend risk and danger! That is why they will fall!_
This is interesting. I gain glory from killing loud-mouthed Farlanders.

_Ah! A retort! I am loud, it is true, but I match my words with skill with blade and bow. I have killed a drake single-handed. I have bested titan chieftains. Soon, I will hunt the Corruption itself. But first, I ..._
_I'm afraid I am rambling. It is a flaw of mine. That was enough banter._ He drops the chains holding the spiders. _Fuzzy! Leggy! Attack!_
At last, you face Lord Carsta'Arl. Surprisingly, he is alone in the grove. You would have thought that this fortress has enough warriors to defend him, but he has been abandoned.

This mighty warlord, who has brought about the deaths of many thousands, is kneeling in the dirt. His blade is at his side, and he looks exhausted and bereft of hope. If Khemerians ever cried, he would be now, mourning all that he has lost, but he would rather die than seem weak before a Hand of Avadon.
As you approach, he rises slowly to his feet. _You are here. The time has come. I knew, the moment I heard that Avadon's gaze was upon us, that this moment would come._
Where are your guards?

_I sent them away while you were dallying with Hunter Klement. I had to wound one of them before they would go. They will be needed to protect Dhorl Stead from invaders after we are gone. I doubt they will succeed, but they must be here to try._
I slew Lady Antje.
_You think I did not know? I know she faced you and fought well. It was a good partnership we had. Enough so to make me feel feelings of weakness unworthy of a Khemerian lord._
_I bear no grudge. You did what you must do. Of course, I will still try to avenge her._
Lord Carsta'Arl, I have been sent from Avadon. You must return there with me or die.
_To enter the dungeons of the Black Fortress and have my spirit destroyed would be worse than death. No, I choose to die. I only need a moment for my regrets._
I am very, very tired of talking. (Attack.)
He nods. _Of course. There is too much talk. Instead, I will show. A final trinket Moritz'Kri gave me, a marvelous example of his skills._

There is a necklace around his neck. Three pearls hang from it. He rips it from his neck, throws it to the ground, and dashes it underfoot. Moments later, there is not one warrior standing before you, but three. All of them equally solid, all lethal. They charge.
Regrets?

_I was too greedy. The gaze of Avadon always casts over the Farlands, looking for targets. It finds examples and unleashes its power upon them. And yet, I thought that, if I was cunning, I could gain enough power to destroy all the nearby Steads when the chaos comes. I was so close. If I could only have evaded you for a few more weeks, I would be a great lord._
That is why you supplied Moritz'Kri?
_Of course. He provided much power in return for very little wealth. And yet, he lacked restraint. He let the Shadow Beast roam instead of hunting it down as he should have. He undid us all._
The chaos comes? What do you mean?
Lord Carsta'Arl smiles for perhaps the last time. _But why should I spoil the surprise? You will soon see it for yourself._
You think a few weeks would have saved you?
_I do. I truly do. But I am growing weak and talkative and delaying the inevitable. All who live must die. It is my time._
And there is no way to settle this peacefully?

He lets out a long, harsh laugh. _Settle? Peacefully? Fool, what did you expect when you came here? This is Khemeria! Now let me show you a final trinket Moritz'Kri gave me, a marvelous example of his skills._
Then let us settle this. (Attack.)
He nods. _Of course. Enough talk. Instead, I will show. A final trinket Moritz'Kri gave me, a marvelous example of his skills._
Vile Titan
The titan stops moving. Vile gas starts to seep out of its body.
The titan starts to move again.
Spirit of the Woods
You hear Lady Antje cry out in anger. Her protective aura fades.
Muck Lizard
Young Basilisk
Arilda
Wyldrylm Hunters
Vid
Deep Woods Hunter
Young Widowspawn
Widowspawn
Dark Widowspawn
Runner Lore
Khemerian Shaman
Ruby Defender
Emerald Defender
Basilisk
Bladeward Skeleton
Crumbling Bones
I am sworn to help.
Stay in this chamber.
You are a thief.
Tick. Tick.
Grind.
Rumble. Rumble.
Greetings, warrior.
You are from the Pact.
I wish no fight with you.
The icy presence grows stronger.
The icy presence grows weaker.

You are deep within the Dhorla Woods now, far from the protection of Avadon. Out here in the Farlands, it is important to always be careful. For some, the temptation to slay a servant of the Pact can be overwhelming.
You have been following the directions you received. Supposedly, if you follow the paths through this region to the northwest, you will be in the area where the shadowy beast was most often seen.

Although you are far from any large settlement, this area is not mere wilderness. You can sense an energy in the air, making your hair stand slightly on end. There is powerful magic concentrated nearby.

When you emerge from the woods, you get a clear view of the mountains to the northeast. A massive stone tower rises from a granite crag far above you. Lights flicker in its windows, and, even in the sun, mist hangs heavily around it.
This must be the source of the magic you sensed earlier. A wizard's tower, watching over these woods. A road winds up through the mountains to the northeast, defended by several stone gateways.
Nathalie looks up at the structure with naked envy. _I'll have to get myself one of those someday._
