You reach the bottom of an old, crumbling spiral staircase. When your eyes adjust to the darkness, you look around.
This looks like a grave burrow, and it's old. Centuries, at least. Far older than the memories of the Khemerian tribes, anyway. The entrance looks like it was only recently uncovered.
Jenell sniffs the air. _This is very old. Not the work of the tribes. They burn their dead. Have done so for a very, very long time._
A few pairs of footprints disappear off into the shadows. Several people entered here. But, as far as you can tell, none returned.

There is a stone stairway here. It is recent construction, descending steeply into the damp earth. Several totems surround it, and a heavy, medicinal reek wafts up from the pit. Several small gifts have been left here.
Jenell sniffs the air and smiles. _Ah. Potions. A nice, safe place for it. Easily buried when something goes wrong._
Nathalie sniffs the air and smiles. _Ah. Potions. Only Khemerian magic, but effective enough. A nice, safe place to do it. Easily buried when something goes wrong._

There is a camp of young Khemerian hunters here. They sit around the fire, eating a thick game stew and telling stories. And then they see you. You stare at each other awkwardly, each side unsure if a fight is about to happen.
And then some spiders decide to do you a favor and break the tension. They scuttle out of the undergrowth where they were hiding, trying to ensnare a delicious Farlander or two.

You emerge in a rocky clearing at the base of the mountains. There is a stone circle here. It has been a place of worship and ceremony for Khemerian tribes for hundreds of years. The massive stones are covered with moss and still stand tall despite centuries of weather and wear.
And yet, the place has clearly been neglected. Nobody has tended to it for years. Weeds grow up through cracks in the stones, and bones and droppings are everywhere.
Jenell says, _Predictable. And shameful. When a circle is allowed to crumble like this, it becomes very difficult to reclaim it._
As you explore, you start to feel a chill. Something strange is in the air here.
As you enter this dark section of the woods, you notice thick clumps of web hanging from the trees. The sound of wildlife becomes notably absent. These groves have been infested by large spiders.

The wizard Moritz'Kri has left the gate to his tower guarded, but open. As you step through, you feel tiny wisps constantly brushing against your cheeks and arms. Invisible presences surround you. You have little doubt that Moritz'Kri is aware of your every move.

And yet, he is allowing you into his tower. Instead of hiding from a confrontation with Avadon, he welcomes it. Everything screams that this is one enormous trap. And yet, Redbeard's orders were clear.
The wizard must come with you to Avadon, or die.

One of the hunters turns to you, stunned by the ease with which the spiders snuck up on the camp and attacked. The young Khemerian stammers, _Thank you for your help. I ... I would not have expected ... Thank you._
Then the survivors pack up their goods and their wounded and flee south to the safety of Dhorl Stead.
When you enter the shaman's private chambers, the rune on the floor flashes. There is a bright burst of light and a small poof of smoke. You are no longer alone in the room.
A giant arachnid is lurking in the shadows. Motes of dark, shimmering energy hover around her. Long strands of thick, green goo hang from her jaws and spinnerets.

This terrifying creature has been infesting this region with her ravenous young. She sees you as a fresh and healthy source of food for her children. Before you have a chance to prepare, she is on you ...
The giant cave widow collapses, hissing and bubbling, in a pool of her own ichor and goo. The horror has been destroyed.

And yet ... It is odd. This is, obviously, no ordinary spider. It seems to have been warped by magic. Perhaps stray magic from the tower to the north. Or, perhaps someone created it? It might bear further investigation.

Spiders aren't normally noisy creatures. Thus, you are surprised when this huge widow lets out a long, furious screech. It lurches toward you, maddened by pain and determined to drive you from her lair.
The cry has attracted her young. Several spiders drop from the tops of the stone pillars.
You stand in the stone circle. For a moment, you feel a powerful chill. Something invisible brushes against you. It startles you, and you jump back.
Then it is gone. The sun is warm, the breeze is cool, and there is nothing else in the circle with you.
You stand in the stone circle. For a moment, you feel a powerful chill. Something invisible brushes against you. This must be what Unni told you about in Dhorl Stead, the corruption of the circle.
You were warned about this, so you stand fast. The icy presence fades for a moment. Then it returns, hanging back, just at the edge of your perception. It's out there, watching.
You continue to stand in the circle. The presence is still there, somewhere on the periphery. Its curiosity is starting to turn into aggravation.
The spirit seems to feel that you have taunted it enough. It becomes visible for a moment, a swirling cloud of dark mist. Then it coalesces into a shape, a lumpy, lopsided parody of the human form.
It stands at the outskirts of the circle, staring in. Then, as it steps forward, all of the dry bones surrounding the circle start to rattle together.
The dark presence fades away with a long, soft sigh. Much work remains before this circle can be restored, but this was a necessary first step.

Two huge, stone sentinels have been placed at the gate to Moritz'Kri's tower. One has two huge emeralds for eyes. The other has two rubies. You suspect that trying to steal these gems would invite retribution.

When you get close, the statues turn to you. You hear a voice, though their mouths don't move. It says, _You are at the tower of the mighty wizard Moritz'Kri, master mage of Dhorl Stead. He is not in attendance. You will leave._
Then the statues return to their upright positions.
You squint and look carefully. There is something in the back corner of this crypt. A translucent figure, so faint that you can barely see it.
You try to focus on it, but then it is gone. When you get close to it, it flits away.
You track down the insubstantial shade again. It is easier this time ... Somehow, it has grown more solid. It looks like the spirit of a human, but you can't tell more.
You approach it, but then it is gone. It flits away again, drifting down the corridor.
The shade is standing in front of a closed gate. It is more substantial. It looks like an old man, wearing clothes in an unfamiliar and archaic style.

The ghost turns to look at you, though it is still too faint to see the expression on its face. Then it turns back to the closed gate. There is a rumbling sound. Dust falls from the ceiling, and the gate slowly begins to open.
Sevilin says, _This is a merry chase, though I usually prefer not to seek out audiences with the undead._

The shade is waiting for you in this large, opulent crypt. It turns to greet you. It is solid enough to see clearly. It is still the spirit of an old man, dead and buried centuries ago. But you also see his face. He is enraged. You have invaded his tomb, and he is furious.
The bones around you begin to rattle and reassemble themselves into skeletons. The ghost opens his mouth, and an ear-splitting howl fills the chamber.
Shima turns and looks at you. _Why were we chasing a ghost through a crypt again?_

There is a skeleton standing by this crypt. It has indeed been magically animated, though it was then left to stand guard for many years. Too many. When you get close to it and it turns, the effort of movement makes it crumble to bits before your eyes.

You meet a young Khemerian hunter. He is sitting by a small, smokeless fire sharpening his blade. He is understandably nervous about being out alone in the wilds. When you enter the grove, he instantly leaps to his feet.

But then he remembers the custom of civility in the wild. He sits down and invites you to join him. _If you aren't going to attack me, you might as well sit and rest for a minute. I am Shavon, a hunter of Khemeria._
Shavon watches you from the other side of the fire. _I've never sat with a warrior of the Pact. I don't want to fight. Rest your feet and move on._
Isn't it dangerous to be out in these woods alone?
_Of course, but I am hunting. It is dangerous. I hunt creatures, and they hunt me. But none of them will surprise me. Khemerians sleep light._
Anything dangerous I should know about?
_Near here? Spiders, I guess. Most of them are to the east. They move through the woods very quietly, but I can hear them._
Are there other settlements out here?
_There is a shaman to the northwest. She lives underground. And the tower of the wizard Moritz'Kri is to the northeast._ He shudders. _But I would never go there._
I'm hunting for a strange beast. It's always wreathed in shadow.
He nods. _Heard of it. Seen strange tracks. Never encountered the creature. If I did, I would just run. Not that it would do any good._
Is it ever seen around here?
_No. It's probably scared of the wizard. I know I am._
What are you hunting?
He looks around and thinks. _It is private. It is between me and Runner Faiga, and I won't let you steal my bounty._
Runner Faiga sent me to find you.
Shavon immediately looks distressed. _What? You are trying to steal my bounty! I have stalked my prey for days like a real warrior, as good as any clanless ever has! You won't steal my trophy._
All right. Never mind.
Shavon waves you away. _These woods are full of prey. Find your own._
Calm down. I just want to help you. I won't steal anything.
You explain to Shavon that you don't care about his trophy. _Ahhh,_ he says. _Well, I don't want help. But my prey is dangerous and needs to be killed, so I will take it. To keep people safe._
_I am hunting basilisks. They have been seen in this area, and they're very dangerous. I've tracked them to the pit to the south._
Jenell mutters, _I must admit, this Shavon is no coward. I would not hunt a basilisk alone._
I want to talk about the basilisks.
_They are deadly. Their gaze can leave you stunned, unable to flee or defend yourself. Then they eat you alive. They are horrors._
_Let me know when you can help me._
How can they be defeated?
_Their gaze has limits. When they stun one foe, others can rush in to slay the beast. That is why I need help with them. The only reason._
I am not ready to help you yet.
_Well, don't think I will wait forever. Go prepare. I will be here. Ready._
Let's go kill basilisks.
Shavon nods and rises. _Finally, I can kill the beasts and go back to a warm bed. They are in the pit to the south. Just follow. Kill anything with scales and four legs._
_We will need to call them. It takes a great deal of noise. And remember,_ he says, _I am lead hunter. The honors are mine. Understood? Follow._
He moves quickly and silently to the south.
I'll be going now.
Shavon nods silently, making no effort to stop you.

Shavon raises the trapdoor, looks down into the dank pit, and grimaces. _Fighting in caves. That is the part I hate. Give me a pitched battle in the woods any day. Ah, well. Nothing to it but ..._ He slips down into the darkness.
Someone has placed a gong here, near the foul, murky pool of water. It has been here for a long time. The metal is tarnished and the wood supports are starting to rot.
Shavon nods and smiles. _That is fortunate. I think it'll take lots of noise to anger the big basilisk enough to come out._ He stands ready near the water. _Lay into it, and be ready._
Strike the gong.
A loud crashing noise echoes through the tunnels. Nothing else happens.
Shavon shakes his head. _That all you got? That's not enough to anger a basilisk._
Hit the gong a lot.

As Shavon waits, you begin to smash the gong repeatedly. _More!_ he shouts. _Louder!_ You double your efforts. Mold crumbles off of the metal and the wood supports begin to crack. The din is deafening.

Though Shavon is dead, you remember what he said about basilisks being drawn by loud noises. You begin to smash the gong repeatedly. Mold crumbles off of the metal and the wood supports begin to crack. The din is deafening.

The crashing noise of the gong soon has an effect. The water starts to bubble. Large, reptilian shapes are visible under the scum on the surface. And then the aggravated creatures burst forth, eager to eliminate the annoyance.
Pit Lizard
Mother Basilisk
Leave the gong alone.
You let the cave continue to be peaceful and silent.

Shavon gives the dead basilisk a nasty kick and nods approvingly. _Nasty creature. Larger than I thought. If you weren't here ... Not good for me. So I am grateful. Now I will return to collect my trophy. Safe travels, Pact warrior._
He takes a knife and collects a small, gruesome trophy from the huge basilisk. Then he turns and leaves.
There is an old, withered woman working in this dank chamber. At least, you assume she is old. The foul substances bubbling all around her might have resulted in premature old age.

She looks at you. Then she raises a piece of glass to her eye and looks at you through that. Then she lets out a long, hissing laugh. _I am not fooled. You are not of my tribe. You are a Pact warrior. A foe._
_But, in this chamber, all are welcome. I am Arilda. While you are in this place and cause no harm, I will aid you._

Arilda tends to her many bubbling pots and hissing mixtures while she speaks with you. _Still wish to see the customs of the barbarian Farlanders, yes? Well, I will help you while you are in my warren. All are aided here._
Why do you live out here?
She smiles and stirs a pot of simmering green goop. _I like the solitude. I like being close to the wilds, despite the tower. But mainly because the settlements do not like the smell._
_And it keeps me far from the devastation of Dhorl Stead. I will still aid you, as I have sworn, but know that the things you have done make me hate you all the same._
Is it not dangerous to be out here?
_Oh, the woods have their pests, it is true. But even the most mindless are not foolish enough to enter my home to do me harm._
_That reminds me. You should stay in this chamber. If you explore my tunnels, you might encounter a trap._
You can't live near the settlements?
_The smell of boiling spider eyes and roasted newt makes them ill. And, from time to time, a mixture goes wrong and puts out a cloud of smoke that ... You would be happier not to breathe it._
_So I work my magic far from where people live. And I work in warrens, so, if there is a disaster, the traces of it may be easily buried._
Tell me about the tower.
_The tower, to the northeast. Home of Moritz'Kri. A wizard, student of the arts of outsiders. An enemy to the old ways, infecting the woods with ..._ She shakes her head. _I am rambling._
_Perhaps I only speak from envy. I know that he has knowledge, and he hoards it._
I am hunting Mortiz-Kri.
_And about time. Anyone walking in these woods can feel the curse of his warped works. And yet, I am not foolish enough to think that the attention of Avadon can bring anyone any good._
The wizard is dead by my hand.

She nods. _I know. It is impossible to miss the changes. And yet, the foulness of his magic will infect these woods for many years to come. As long as the taint remains, Moritz'Kri is not truly dead._
What can you tell me of Moritz'Kri?
_I have met him but once, the last time I delivered my potions to Oghrym'Tor. Before Lord Carsta'Arl told me my services were no longer needed._
_It was Moritz'Kri who turned me away. He bragged that his book of potion recipes so far outpaced my knowledge that ..._ She shakes her head. _Condescending worm._
You envy something of the wizard's?
She starts to say something, but then she stops. _No. You are not going to the wizard's tower. Your goal is ... elsewhere._
_Until you are entering the wizard's lair, I will not share my wishes with you. It would be unsafe._
_Yes, I do. I never forget an insult, and you ... You are going to his tower, yes? He once bragged about his mighty book of potion recipes._
_I want it. If you bring it to me, I will trade with you my special charms. The ones reserved only for my clan. The clan that abandoned me to throw in their lot with that wizard._
I found this in Moritz'Kri's tower. (Give her the book of recipes.)
Arilda greedily seizes the tome and begins to flip through it. Then she laughs. _Hah! I was a fool, to be taken in by that charlatan. His store of secrets was only as large as mine._
_And yet, a bargain is a bargain. I will still trade with you. A fair punishment for me for being so gullible. My store of charms and quality potions is available to you._
I want to see what potions you have for sale.
_After you have been rooting around in my private chambers? Now that you have invaded my privacy, I am no longer obligated to aid you._
She sighs. _Except for my special charms. I did swear I would sell you those, after all._
I would like to trade for your potions.
_That is my purpose and my training, and I am obligated by oath to aid all peaceful travelers who come this way. It is what I have sacrificed to master the healing arts._
_But nothing is free. You will have to pay for my art._
That will be fine.
She nods. _Then, as long as you are respectful and stay out of my private chambers, you can see my wares._
I am from Avadon. You will not charge me, or you will suffer for it.
Arilda frowns and flushes red. Suddenly, the air in here seems choked with smoke. The ceiling seems lower. The walls close in. And Arilda seems to have grown much larger.

And then, moments later, everything is back to normal, but you feel very light-headed. Arilda says, _Already accept that I am being generous, Pact warrior. Do not try your luck farther. As long as you are respectful and stay out of my private chambers, you can see my wares._
Shima smiles, fascinated. _A cunning illusion. I was completely taken in. That time._
Let me see your potions.
Arilda's Potions
Arilda sells a variety of fresh potions made of all-natural ingredients. She is bound by oath to help all peaceful travelers.
Let me see your charms.
Arilda's Charms
Arilda will let you see her special charms, normally only available to members of her clan.
_Then I send you back out to the road, and I hope that you leave here after doing as little harm to my people as possible._
The path ahead leads into a thick, dark forest. The trees crowd in onto the pathway from either side. Sevilin stops walking and takes a deep breath.
_Pardon me, [N]. I am just collecting myself. I just remembered ... the ambush._
Well, ready yourself and hurry up.

Sevilin nods, but he doesn't move. _There has been some doubt about me since it all happened. I've heard the whispers about me, the rumors. I think I should tell you what happened, so there is no doubt about me._
I'd like to hear more about the ambush.
Sevilin nods. _I have been waiting for a good time. I've heard the whispers about me, the rumors. I think I should tell you what happened, so there is no doubt about me._
_It was in The Kva. The northern parts, not the dry wastes you have seen. A huge forest. Much like this one._
_There were six of us, all Hands, sent to hunt down a brigand. Only a few months ago. Hard to believe. But they were waiting for us. They knew we were coming, and they hit us at night._
Why was this brigand being hunted?
_I don't know. Redbeard never bothered to tell us. He said that we were to watch for any signs of ogres near them, but that is the only thing he said._
Six Hands? That seems like a lot.
_We were young. Only just arrived, eager to prove ourselves. We ... We did not succeed._
Who attacked you?
_The leader of the bandits himself. His name is Cahil. He's hard to miss. His left hand was burned in an ambush. It's nothing but a twisted mass of scars._
_His right hand works fine, however. First, he used a wand. Then his blade. He and his thugs rushed us late at night, and we were not ready._
They took you by surprise?
_I will be ashamed of it until my dying day, but yes. They moved soundlessly and with amazing speed, but we still should not have been surprised._
How many of them were there?
_Only ten. Few enough that six Hands should have destroyed them with no effort. But they ... They took us entirely by surprise._
What happened then?

_We fought the best we could. We grabbed our weapons and ..._ Sevilin shakes his head. _They overpowered us, one at a time. One of them used magic to stun us. I saw Cahil deliver the death blow three times. His men made sure the Hands looked him in the eye._
_And then it was only me and one other. She stayed and died. I fled and lived._
Shima looks away, embarrassed to hear Sevilin admit to such cowardice.
Jenell nods sadly. _I can understand. It is impossible to know what we will do in such a case._
Nathalie says, _I spend all these months hoping to be picked for a fight, and you run from one. It's not fair._
How did Avadon react to your running away?

_As you would expect. They were sympathetic, to my face. They called me coward behind my back. I was not selected for any missions until you arrived. Were it not for you, my time at Avadon would have ended soon._
Why didn't you stay and fight?
_Because the battle was lost. The woman who stayed? She should have fled too and returned with me later. Her pride killed her. Not a popular view, but I still believe it._
Is that all you want to say?
_Yes. I will not have you rely on me to protect your life without your knowing my story. I wouldn't have you hear only the rumors. I am ashamed of what happened, but I have learned._
You deserve a second chance.
Sevilin nods. _I thank you, [N]. All I have wanted was a chance to prove myself again. I thank you for that._ He walks toward the woods.
I am only taking a coward with me because I have no better choice.

Sevilin nods grimly. _Well, I will do all I can to prove myself. I am no coward. I am ready to die now to keep from shaming Avadon again, and I hope that you will be too. Enough talking. Let's go._ He walks toward the woods.
I would have done the same thing.

Sevilin frowns. _Don't say that. What I did was wrong. I would have died, but I would not have shamed Avadon. I am ready to die now, and I hope that you will be too. I am ready now. Let's go._ He walks toward the woods.

Shima reaches up and pulls a wisp of web from a tree branch. He smiles. _This ... It reminds me ... When my father lived, we made the spider web the symbol of the Threespear clan. I think that symbol would only have lasted one generation, but ..._
Why were you called the Threespear clan?

_A long story, involving much involved Holklandan history. The origin of my clan involved a civil war, an alliance of three clans, a different civil war, another alliance ... It is all quite complicated._
Why did he change the symbol?

_My father admired spiders greatly. Their industry. The way they help us. The way that, despite their virtue, they are hated and feared. It ... It appealed to him. He was very wise. Though, in the end, he lacked in cunning._
What is your clan's symbol now?
_We have none. My clan is dissolved and dishonored. If someone did select a symbol for us, it would probably be something that smells bad._ He smiles wearily. _Let's move on._
Now that you are away from Dhorl Stead, Jenell relaxes slightly. She grows nervous again, however, whenever the tower comes into view.
_That tower, it is like a wound. A stain. It corrupts the woods. Such a thing would never be allowed in the Wyldrylm._
The Wyldrylm doesn't have wizards?
_No. Our shamans provide power and wisdom enough to protect our lands._
It corrupts the woods?
_It is ... It is hard to explain. There is a ... It's a sense of wrongness. It takes many years of training to be able to feel it. Moritz'Kri is doing something that ... Avadon should intervene._
_Enough of this. Let us move on._
Are you sure you just aren't scared of wizards?
_Scared? You think I fear their kind? Hah! I draw on the power of the world itself! I don't fear mages, and I don't fear Khemerians. Enough. Let's move on._
Nathalie takes in the view ahead with awe. The tower. The sentinels. And even a dramatic backdrop. She sighs happily. _Someday, I will have this for myself. It is glorious._
Sevilin smiles. _Maybe you can have this one. You can evict Moritz'Kri._
Shima smiles. _Yes, it would be a lovely target. Infiltrating such supposedly invulnerable fortresses is a shadowwalker's bread and butter._
Jenell laughs. _Yes. It is a gaudy and boastful spire, designed to laugh in the face of the wilds. It would suit you well._
Nathalie continues. _Mock all you like. A secluded place to learn and experiment, what more could any wizard want? Yes, I might claim it for myself. We will see._

There are several tribal warriors standing around the wreckage of a small caravan. They have just robbed it and are picking through the remains for any items of value. There are no bodies. It looks like all the defenders fled into the woods.

Then they see you. They grab their weapons and move to defend themselves. You look at the markings on their faces and realize that these are not Khemerians. They are from the Wyldrylm, people of the Pact.

Then they see you. They grab their weapons and move to defend themselves. Jenell looks at the markings on their faces and gasps. _These are not Khemerians. They are from the Wyldrylm, people of the Pact!_
Their leader brandishes his weapon, but he looks terrified. _Pact warriors? You came all the way here to find us? Well, I am Vid, these are my people, and we will not submit!_
Submit? I have no idea who you are.

The warriors confer with each other briefly. Vid turns to you. _Really? That is a relief to us. We have been driven out of the Wyldrylm by a great injustice, and we are glad that Avadon's assassins have not yet found us._
Actually, I am hunting the strange beast that stalks these woods.
The warriors confer with each other briefly. Vid turns to you. _In that case, we would help you if we could. But, while we have heard of this creature, we have never seen it._
_We have been driven out of the Wyldrylm by a great injustice, and we are glad that Avadon's assassins have not yet found us._
Ummmm ... yes! Avadon has hunted you down at last! You ... criminal?
Vid detects the uncertainty in your voice. _And you are hunting us for the crime of ..._
I forget for the moment, but I'm sure it will come to me.
_I see. Well, it is impossible to forget the injustice that is being visited upon us. Since you don't know what it is, I will tell you._
What injustice is that?

Vid steps forward. You see that he is very young, but he bears the trophies of a warrior far older. _We are from the Wyldrylm, warriors of courage and honor. But a rival clan was sneaking into our hunting grounds and stealing our game._
_Of course, our honor demanded that we punish them for this, but they were using the Pact's free roads to travel into and out of our lands._
Jenell nods. _Ahhh. I see. I understand completely._
Jenell, what do you see?
_That their enemies were using the Pact's laws to rob Vid's tribe. It was a cowardly act, deserving of severe punishment. But the Pact would not see it that way._
Vid nods. _Yes. The sister sees it perfectly._ Jenell blushes slightly.
The free roads?

_Your Pact has roads that run all over Lynaeus. All can travel on them safely and without tolls. But, in the Wyldrylm, the land of clans has always been held as sacred, and the tolls are a major source of wealth for us._
_The free roads are an insult to the Wyldrylm. For other tribes to use them to enter our most private lands ... it was too much._
Why is this clan your enemy?
The question clearly makes no sense to Vid. _Some clans are allies, some are foes. It was always thus. I don't see what is hard to understand._
And what did you do exactly?
_Well, they thought the free roads protected them. The raiders were returning home, heavy with game, careless, and noisy._ _And drunk,_ one of the other warriors mutters.
_Our punishment for them was swift and merciful. Two, we killed. Two, we cut. The rest were allowed to leave with only a beating._
Jenell nods. _You indeed showed restraint._
Vid nods at the memory. _And yet, that was enough to anger the Pact, once the kin of the lost warriors betrayed us to them._
They should not have betrayed you?
Vid spits. _What true tribe of the Wyldrylm needs outsiders to settle these grudges?_
And so you fled?

_The Pact warriors came for us within the week. When our clan told us of their coming, we fled north. Now we live here, robbing the foul Khemerians to live. But for bad luck, you never would have found that we are here. Now Avadon will be angry with us._
This is bad news for them. People of the Pact are not allowed to hunt and raid Farlanders without permission. It angers the Farlanders and disrupts the peace of the Pact, which really annoys Avadon.
Jenell says, _Yes. Bad fortune indeed. It would be better if Avadon never knows you are here._ She turns to look at you.
Sevilin whispers, _It is unfortunate, but Avadon should still know of this, and I think Jenell would want to know too._
Shima whispers, _They seem kind enough, but they are breaking the law. Avadon should know of this, and I think Jenell would want to know too._
Nathalie whispers, _I admire their spirit, but they are breaking the law. Avadon should know of this, and I think Jenell would want to know too._
I will keep your secret, for now.

Vid nods. _I am grateful. I know that, in the end, our secret will be found out. At least we will have more time to flee. I only hope that our leader sees that leaving is the wise course. I don't think that he will. We will see._
Vid and his warriors gather their weapons and stolen goods and prepare to leave.
I am a servant of Avadon. I can't just let this pass.

Vid nods. _I see. You have your oaths and I have mine. I would happily submit and flee deeper into the woods, but our leader ... He has more anger than I do. I will try to convince him to submit, but ... We will see._
The laws of the Pact are harsh, but just. You are breaking them.

Vid nods. _That is true. I see that. I can be convinced to change, to find a different way to survive. I would happily submit and flee deeper into the woods, but our leader ... He has more anger than I do. I will try to convince him to submit, but ... We will see._
Wait. I need to know something else.
Vid turns back. _I am sorry. We need to return to our fellow warriors and decide what to do next. I don't think our leader will be wise, but ... there is no time to spare._
Vid looks Jenell in the eyes. They exchange a long glance.
Then the Wyldrylm warriors, moving with great speed and grace disappear into the trees.
(Watch them go.)
A shadowwalker walks out of the woods ahead of you. He hasn't drawn his blade, so you keep yours sheathed. You start looking around for signs of an ambush, but everything seems safe.
Then, as the man gets closer, you realize that he is strangely similar to the shadowwalker who contacted you outside Zhethron's lair, the one who asked you to call him the Wayfarer.
Then he reaches you, bows, and says, _Greetings. It is good to see you again._ And you realize that the Wayfarer has somehow followed you here, all the way to the other side of Lynaeus.
How did you get here?

He gives a little shrug. _Avadon is not the only faction that is wealthy and powerful. Others have remarkable resources as well, including the ability to help their honored servants to move very quickly._
Why have you followed me here?
_Followed you? I did not know I was following you. I only heard that Hands were coming here. I followed them, and it turned out to be you._

_You should grow used to it. Now that you are a Hand, you will be constantly sought out by those who would give you wealth and other rewards for your aid. For example, the way I asked you for help in The Kva._
Greetings. It is good to see you again.
_Agreed. I am pleased to see you again. You seem to be a young Hand with great potential, and it will be very profitable for us both for me to build a relationship with you early._

_You should grow used to being sought out. Now that you are a Hand, you will be constantly sought out by those who would give you wealth and other rewards for your aid. For example, the way I asked you for help in The Kva._
I haven't retrieved the information you asked for.
_I am aware of that. You still have time, though, if you return to Zhethron's Aerie soon. The offer I gave you will not last forever, however._
I retrieved the information you asked for.
_I am aware of that. I am grateful, and I hope that you returned to our contact point to collect your reward. I am happy that my trust in your skills was not misplaced._

He laughs. _Oh, you will have other opportunities for employment, to be sure. Do not worry. However, I am not trolling for aid at the moment. I have just come north to learn what will happen to poor Dhorl Stead._
_Now that Avadon has been called, we want to know how far the destruction will spread. So, if you can tell me, why are you here?_
And who has sent you?
_We all have secrets. That is mine. My employer wishes to remain private, for now._
Will you pay me if I tell you?
He thinks about it and shakes his head. _Not for that bit of information. I am mainly here to watch, not to spy._
I can't tell you why I am here.

The Wayfarer nods. _No? But you are here in the wilds. On a hunt, perhaps? No matter. I don't care about the purpose, only the effects. I mainly want to see how much of Dhorl Stead ends up destroyed._
I have come to hunt a deadly beast wreathed in shadow. Seen it?
_No, fortunately. You hunt just one beast? How interesting. But, shadows? A magical creation? A sign of illegal experimentation? It will be interesting to see._
_But no matter. I don't care about the purpose, only the effects. I mainly want to see how much of Dhorl Stead ends up destroyed._
I will destroy as much of this place as is necessary to uphold the law.
_Of course. And that is how it works out. There are always ways in which the law is broken. Once Avadon's gaze is on a place, destruction follows. Its power demands to be used._
_I am only here to watch the process. It is rare to see it from beginning to end._
I doubt any of it will be destroyed. I am only hunting one beast.

_You are ... touching in your optimism. Sadly, that is rarely how these things work out. You think that there is only one small problem here? Once Avadon's gaze is on a place, destruction follows. Its power demands to be used._
It's not up to me. It's up to Redbeard.

_That is true. Sadly, there are none on Lynaeus more eager to use their power, and few more apt at rooting out treason to be destroyed. Once Avadon's gaze is on a place, destruction follows. Its power demands to be used._
It will be different this time.
The Wayfarer nods. _But of course. Now I must go and find a place to conceal myself. The roads are unsafe, and I have much to learn. Excuse me._
He gives you a polite bow and leaves to the south. You try to ask him another question, but he only responds with a wave.
I will destroy as much of Khemeria as I need to.
The Wayfarer nods. _Of course. The Khemerians are the enemy, after all. Now I must go and find a place to conceal myself. The roads are unsafe, and I have much to learn. Excuse me._
Goodbye.
_Farewell, and safe travels._ He gives you a polite bow and leaves to the south.
Wait. I want to know something else.

A boulder to your right starts to shift slightly. You draw your weapons, prepared to fight a rock beast or something, only to see the Wayfarer stand up. He was concealed under a blanket with a cunningly accurate stone pattern.
Shima clucks his tongue. _Hmmm. Nice technique._
The Wayfarer quickly folds up the sheet and walks toward you. _Well met. I knew you would be along this path soon. Took slightly longer than I expected, to tell the truth._
Greetings to you.
The Wayfarer nods. _Always a pleasure. I would love to exchange news of what is happening in Lynaeus. Sadly, I can't stay and talk._
Not you again.
He holds out his hands. _As I said before, you will have to grow used to such attention now that you are a Hand. My interruption will be brief. Sadly, I can't stay and talk._
How have you tracked me here?

_But I did not track you at all. I learned Hands were returning here. I came and waited, and here you are. I would love to exchange news of what is happening in Lynaeus. Sadly, I can't stay and talk._
Where are you going?
_To take a few more notes about the current, imperiled state of Dhorl Stead. Then I must flit off to faraway lands to continue my work. You are not the only Hand who works with me._
Why can't you stay?
_Because this area is about to become very dangerous. Fire. Battle. Uncontrolled magic. Moritz'Kri is an unpredictable and dangerous creature, and I don't want to be ensnared._
_Sadly, my predictions are coming true. The destruction will ensnare more and more of Dhorl Stead._
What do you know of Moritz'Kri?
_Very little. He is powerful and unpredictable. I suppose it is surprising it has taken so long for Avadon to come for him._
_There is something very powerful in his tower. I would be very careful in there._
I will destroy as much as is necessary to destroy foes of the Pact.

_That is your oath. You started hunting a beast in the wilds. Now you have come here. Soon, the destruction will move closer to Dhorl Stead. I only wait to see how much of these lands will be destroyed and what the final justification is._
I am only hunting Moritz'Kri, not all of Dhorl Stead.
_Trust one who has seen this many times. That is how this proceeds. Hunt a beast. Hunt a wizard. Move closer and closer to the city in the center._
_I only wait to see how much of these lands will be destroyed and what the final justification is._
Are you criticizing Avadon?

_I would not dream of it. Not when we both know how Avadon deals with those who speak against it. However, all of this is the result of Redbeard's orders. When you see what happens, I only ask that you remember the source._
Perhaps it will be different this time.

_I hope so, but things I have seen make me doubt that. If things go wrong, I ask you to remember one thing. All of this is the result of Redbeard's orders. When you see what happens, I only ask that you remember the source._
Well, I have work to do. I'll be going.
_Of course. The mission must be completed. Redbeard is not safe to displease._
_I ask you to remember one thing. All of this is the result of Redbeard's orders. When you see what happens, I only ask that you remember the source._
And you?
_But I need to go. I can feel the battle coming. If I am only to observe, I need to move on._ He nods to you and moves stealthily to the south.
(Leave.)
The Wayfarer gives you a slight bow. Then he walks off stealthily to the south.

There is a rough, muddy road here, that curves up to the north and toward Moritz'Kri's tower. A patrol of Khemerian warriors guards it. They aren't happy about it. They have also been told of warriors of Avadon in the area. They really aren't happy about that either.
They are trying to seem as unthreatening as possible. They don't want a fight with Avadon. Their leader walks up to you and nods. _I am Lore. We are watching this road. We ... We guard the tower._
She shudders. _We have never been in it. That is the wizard's domain. We don't ... Don't want to enter it. Ever._ You ask her to elaborate, but she declines.
Who told you of me?
_I ... Uhhh ... I forget. It is not a surprise, though. The arrival of Avadon is important news._
Have you seen any strange beasts around here?
_We've heard stories of strange things in the Dhorla Woods, but we've seen no sign of them. Perhaps they fear the wizard. They should._
_We ... We have to question everyone on this road. Why you are here. You should tell us that. If ... If you want._
I am [N], Hand of Avadon, and I will not be questioned by you.
Lore takes a step back. _No ... No ... Of course. We ... We understand how things are. And we won't get between a wizard and Avadon._
_I will not question Avadon. Please move on. We will not slow you._ They step out of your way. Then they spare no time getting away from you.
I want to see the wizard.
_Oh. I am afraid that I must disappoint you. Moritz'Kri is currently in the fortress. Oghrym'Tor._ She doesn't seem unhappy about it.
_And that is all we need. We won't trouble you further._ They step out of your way. Then they spare no time getting away from you.
I am hunting for a shadowy creature that stalks Dhorl Stead.
She seems relieved. _What? You have heard of that thing? That shadowy creature they tell tales about. We have seen nothing of it. I don't think it's real._
_Then again, I will not question Avadon. Please move on. We will not slow you._ They step out of your way. Then they spare no time getting away from you.
I am merely exploring. It is no concern of yours.
Lore seems slightly relieved. _Of course. Khemeria is a lovely country with many beautiful sights. I hope that you enjoy them. And hunt the deer. They are delicious!_
You stop the warriors guarding the road and speak with them. They are still terrified of you. You learn nothing of value before they move on.
There are several warriors guarding the road south of Moritz'Kri's tower. When they see you, they are terrified. They don't run, though. Instead they draw their blades and stand in your way.

Their leader nocks an arrow to the string of her bow. _I am Lore, invader of Avadon, and I have my orders. You will not reach the wizard's tower. You die first._ Her hands shake, and the arrow wobbles uncertainly on the bowstring.
It is suicide to oppose Avadon. You must flee.
She shakes her head. _Moritz'Kri came to us and said what would happen if we let you by. What ... What horrors ... We have no choice. Curse the fates for putting us between you and him!_
And, before you can respond, Lore takes aim. You have to defend yourself.
Tell me about the wizard. Maybe we can come to a peaceful arrangement.

She shakes her head. _Moritz'Kri came to us. He said you would make all sorts of offers. Said, if we accepted, horrible things would ... to us ... We have no choice. Curse the fates for putting us between you and him!_
You would block me, Farlander? You will die! (Attack.)
When you charge the warriors, their lifetimes of training kick in. All uncertainty leaves them. They prepare to fight to the death.
Foul Presence
Whirling Bones
Young Hunter
Flee!
We didn't hear a thing!
We need to go home.
Talking: This hunter is currently distracted by spiders.
Talking: The hunters are too busy to talk. They are returning to Dhorl Stead as quickly as they can.
Faded Shade
Vengeful Shade
The ghost calls forth bones to destroy you.
Talking: The shade floats away before you can get close to it.
Shavon
Ring the gong.
Home at last!
Talking: Shavon shushes you. He is on the hunt now, constantly alert for anything that might attack.
The Wayfarer
Talking: The Wayfarer ignores you.
Widow of Bones
Talking: They don't stop to talk to you. They are heading back into the deep woods.
The Shadow Beast
Your attacks knock some shadows loose from the beast.
Vicious Wisp
The shadowy beast fades into the woods.
You no longer sense the shadowy beast near you.
Shadow Defender
Talking: The beast ignores you.
Runner Kasch
Corrupted Rat
Vapor Rat
Warped Widow
Leaping Spider
Liese
Khemerian Raider
Sage Derasa
Radiant Reptile
Goo Lizard
Bone Spider
I see few people now.
This is our land.
The beast is out there.
You don't belong here.
I train the worthy.
Beware the shadows.
The woods are safer now.
Khemerian Assassin

These must be the woods you were directed to in Dhorl Stead, the dark thickets where the shadowy beast has been seen most often. The thick trees and undergrowth stretch off to the west. You are sure that someone is watching you from those shadows.
And yet, these woods are not untouched by humans. You can see the wooden walls of a settlement to the southwest. A thin line of smoke from a single cookfire stretches up into the sky.

You enter the settlement, or what is left of it. There are only two intact halls. The rest of the log buildings were still being built when this encampment was abandoned. The forest is already starting to reclaim this painstakingly cleared land.
The smoke is rising from a hole in the roof of the eastern hall. The west hall is ominously silent.
You enter the ruins of a second abandoned settlement. It was smaller than the first. It was abandoned more recently and in a much more violent fashion.
Only one of the halls in this settlement was completed. The half-finished walls of several other structures are already crumbling and rotting.

Bloodstains are visible nearby, probably a few weeks old. Only the shelter of branches and leaves kept them from being washed away in the rain. The last humans in this place might have intended to flee, but they were too late.
The moist soil under the woods above are criss-crossed by several long tunnels. Some are natural, and others were excavated by Khemerians. Thick roots have already burrowed down through the ceiling.
The smell of rotting vegetation (and meat?) is heavy in the humid air. You can hear beasts down here with you, hissing and hunting in the darkness.
This pathway is lined with totems, gruesome trophies taken recently, stuck onto sharpened pieces of wood, and jammed into the mud. Two of the trophies are from Khemerians.
You hear drunken singing to the west. Also, wet chewing noises.

You find something fascinating and strangely unsurprising. In this remote chamber, dug out of the dirt and surrounded by a moat, you find a mage's workshop. It is fully equipped. Alchemical equipment. Magic circles. Paper and pens.
It hasn't been used for several weeks. Moss and mold are steadily advancing over the precious equipment. And yet, you suspect that this workshop isn't needed anymore. It has achieved its purpose.
A huge, shadowy creature paces through the crumbling workshop. Then it sees you and flees to the south. At last, you have tracked the beast to its lair.
The woods ahead are so dark that you can barely see. The mossy trunks seem to squeeze in on you from all sides. You are sure that someone is watching you.
There are several small lizards hanging from the walls and ceiling of this tunnel. Their skins have strange, glistening rainbow hues, and their eyes glow.
These creatures are another sign that some strange, powerful magic is at work in these woods. When these reptiles get larger, you suspect that each will be dangerous in its own special way.
A vicious fight took place in this crude log hall. The blood stains seem fairly fresh, but the remains have been reduced to skeletons. At first, it seems odd.
Then the bones begin to move under their own power, and the hall becomes deathly cold. Someone placed a trap here, and you stumbled into it.
As you explore the ruins of this village, several Khemerians step out of the forest. Some of them have bows. All are aimed at you.

You start to ask them what happened, but then you see their eyes. You have had enough training to instantly recognize that they aren't in their right minds. Have they been charmed? Did they forage the wrong mushrooms? You can't be sure, and they certainly can't tell you.
You duck for cover just as the first few arrows fly.
Khemerian Archer
Khemerian Runner
Charmed Sage
A Khemerian warrior steps out onto the path in front of you. His blade is drawn, and his face and arms bear many scars. His cold expression instantly puts you on your guard.

As he smirks at you, you hear rustling in the brush behind you. _You're a long way from home, Avadon, and you have a loose tongue. The beast of the woods is our business. And, when you never go home, they will think it's because the creature devoured you._
Then the assassins close in, ready to kill.
A stiff breeze blows through the woods. You feel slightly dizzy. It seems like the trees are closing in on you.
A moment later, the feeling passes, but the forest feels different somehow.
You pull on the trapdoor, but it won't budge. Something is holding it locked from below. These woods seem determined to play tricks on you.
The woods grow deathly quiet. All animal sounds fade away. Then you hear strange scraping and moaning sounds. They are faint at first, but getting closer.
As you look around for whatever is hunting you, you see a familiar form has appeared down the path.
Once again, the Shadow Beast lunges toward you. This time, it doesn't make any sounds. It is still angry from your last encounter. It leaps for your throat.
You reach the top of the steps and push on the trapdoor, but it won't budge. Something has barred it from above.
A man suddenly darts out of the shadows at you, blade in hand, murder in his eyes. As you prepare to defend yourself, he skids to a stop. _Wait! I thought you were ..._ He sheathes his blade.
_I am Runner Kasch. I apologize. I thought you were an invader._ Then he looks at you more closely. _You are not a Khemerian. Who are you? What are you doing here?_
Runner Kasch sits at the table and sharpens his sword. He keeps a large assortment of blades, spears and bows nearby and properly maintained. If anyone tries to rob this settlement, he is ready.
I am [N], a Hand of Avadon, and you will assist me.
_Avadon? Here? I was not aware. I ... I have done nothing wrong, committed no crime. I am only defending this settlement._
I am hunting for the shadowy beast that lurks in these woods.
Kasch looks surprised. _I had thought that we were being abandoned to the creature. It is out there. I try to keep it at bay, but ... If I step out past my fires, I think it will come for me._
I was hunting for the shadowy beast that lurks in these woods. Now I am exploring.
_It has been some time since I saw the beast. So it was you who rid us of it? I am grateful._
My identity and purpose are my own business.
Runner Kasch nods, but he seems suspicious. _I will not pry. You are clearly an outsider. As long as you do not attempt to steal our land, I will not hinder you._
Tell me about this settlement.
_It was one of two in this area. We were trying to expand our clans into these dark woods. It was not wise. They are too thick, too unfriendly. There is ... dark magic here._
_I have not been to the northern settlement in months. I have heard nothing from them. As for us, most of us fled after the shadowy beast took a third victim._
_Now that the beast is gone, however, I know that many will return soon._
Where did the villagers flee to?
_To other settlements near here, other lands claimed by our clan. Some might return one day. Most won't._
Why did you try to settle in such a place?
_Land is growing scarce in Khemeria, and the punishments for taking the land of another clan are harsh. It leads to true war. Much blood. Flayings._
_We saw that these woods were unsettled, and we tried to claim them. It has not ... been a success._
No contact with it? I would like to visit the northern settlement.
_It is not easy. It is to the north, over the river, but there is no bridge._
_There was a tunnel under the river, dug out by raiders and smugglers. It might not have collapsed yet. You might look for it. I would like to know if that settlement is well._
I have been to the northern settlement. It has been destroyed.
_I am not surprised. Even though they are not of my clan, that is sad news._
Why are you still here?
_Because not all of us wanted to surrender this land. Land is rare and valuable. If we can keep the beasts away and build a village here, it will be good for our clan._
_I am staying here to keep our claim alive and to keep beasts from destroying what buildings we have made._
_I am also trying to find a way to keep the shadowy monster at bay._
How do you spend your days?
_I hunt and gather wood for the fires, though I never walk too far from this village. I also keep my weapons ready. I will fight to the death to keep intruders from our land._
_It is difficult, though. I see other creatures moving closer, beasts that would take what we have worked so hard to make. And yet, I can't leave to hunt them._
Such as?
_I have seen an ogre. It walks up and down the river, hunting for prey. It doesn't fear the beast. It certainly doesn't fear me. I watched it once. It wore the skull of a Khemerian around its neck._
_The vile thing should be destroyed, before it attracts more of its kind. I can't do it, though. It is too large, and I must stay here._
How do you stay safe at night?
_I pile the fires very high. I bar the door. I sleep with my blades handy._
_I have not slept well for weeks. Sometimes I think I will never sleep well again._
How have you kept the creature back?
_It seems to only come to this village at night. I keep fires lit, and the light seems to annoy it._
_And yet, I don't think this will keep the creature back forever. I can feel it out there. It ... It watches me. I think it just toys with me._
I am interested in the shadowy beast that lurks in these woods.
Runner Kasch leans forward, immediately attentive. _You hunt the creature? Of late, it is hard to find anyone outside these walls who believes it exists. For those who live here, there is no doubt._
Has it attacked you?
_Me, no. So far, it has only watched me. Several of my clanmates fell to it. It savaged them when they walked too far down the paths to the west._
Does it always attack those it sees?
_No. At least half the time, it only watches and flees. Perhaps it only hunts when it hungers._
How many times have you seen it?
_At least five times, I have seen a cloud of shadow tracking me. Sometimes, on the other side of the river. Sometimes, much closer._
_And yet, it never attacks. It only watches. And, sometimes, it makes sounds._
Why doesn't it attack you?
_I can't see inside its mind. I don't know. I do know that, if it did attack, I would likely not survive._
It makes sounds?
_It does. It sounds like ... I do not want to seem mad. It makes coughs and gurgles and hisses. All sorts of different sounds. Then it becomes more angry as it makes the noises. Then it flees._
_I don't understand it._
Where might I find it?
He thinks carefully. _Its lair isn't near my village. I haven't tried to track it, so there is little I can tell you._
_I do know that all of the attacks took place to the west. If you hunt there, you might pick up its trail._
I slew the shadowy beast that lurked in these woods.

You tell the tale of your victory over the Shadow Beast. Kasch nods approvingly. _I know that you are a Pact warrior, a foe of Khemeria, but I am still grateful. Now my clan can return and properly claim this land._
He gives you a leather tube. It contains a sheepskin scroll. _That is a token of our gratitude._
Do you have any supplies to spare?
_No. I barely have food and weapons for my own survival._
_What little I have to spare, I could only give to one who helped hunt down our foes._
I hunted down that ogre that was worrying you.
You tell the tale to Kasch. _I am grateful for your aid. That thing was hunting closer and closer to this settlement, and mere fires would not keep it away. Honor demands I pay you a bounty._
He unlocks one of the northern doors.
I will be moving on.
_Then I wish you safe travels, stranger. Though you are not of Khemeria, I do enjoy seeing another human face._ He returns to sharpening his blade.
This small hall is mostly full of target dummies and weapons, both real and for practice. There is an armed woman here, well into middle-age. She watches you as you approach, examining you intently.
_I know what you are,_ she says. _The armor. The complexion. The arrogance. You are Pact. No, not just Pact. Avadon._ Her voice is tinged with distaste.
_I am Liese. Once a Runner, now a teacher. I am not sure why you are here, but I have my guess. I knew the beast would draw hunters._

Liese picks up wooden weapons and brushes the dust off of the practice dummies. _Until recently, many warriors trekked out here to be trained by me. Now I must be content with you. It will not always be thus, I hope._
What are you doing out here?
_I am a teacher. I have spent my life hunting these woods, and I pass my knowledge on to worthy young warriors._
Why do you live so far from town?
_Because my training involves great pain and deprivation. It is easier to command submission when the comforts of home are far away._
Isn't it dangerous out here?
_Very much. When I grow too slow, something will take me. I hope it will be quick. I doubt it will be._
_But that would be preferable to knowing I let a mere beast drive me from my home._
What do you teach the warriors?

_The life of a Khemerian requires constant vigilance and strength. Any day, a rival Stead may attack us, or we may be called by our lord to raze another Stead. Either way, we must always be ready to spill blood._
_A life of waste and savagery,_ Jenell says.
Liese smiles. _But it makes us strong. That is why you must cower under the protection of the Pact. You fear us._
It is very different in the Pact.
_Yes. That is because you let yourselves grow weak. One day, you will be punished for that weakness._
And when will that day come?
_I don't know. Probably long after I am dead, and the punishment will be delivered by someone else entirely. I want to live to see it, but I doubt that I will._
I would like for you to train me.

Liese smirks. _Me? Train a Hand of Avadon? I might. I swore to aid all worthy warriors who submit to me. However, you must prove yourself to me first. What have you slain that earns you the right to be trained by a Khemerian?_
I slew a mighty ogre in the caves below us.
_Mighty? That mangy thing? I laugh. That thing wasn't even worth dulling my blade with its skull._
I have slain the Shadow Beast.
Liese slowly nods. _I cannot deny that accomplishment. You slew something even I hesitated to hunt. Yes, I will teach you a small amount of what I know. For a price._
I am from Avadon. You will help me, or else.
Her face burns red. _I am a true Runner of Khemeria, and I will not be commanded by your kind. Or spoken to thus in my own home. Leave me. Return when you have learned manners._ She turns away.
I have slain many mighty creatures.
_Not here. You have killed something, I am sure, but not a beast of Khemeria. Leave me. Return when you can claim worthiness._ She turns away.
She nods. _I will live up to my oath. However, I will not let you see all of my secrets. There are too many, and it would take too long._
_If you give me proper tribute, however, I will teach you. I can make you more effective with missiles or with melee weapons. Each lesson will cost only three thousand coins. I do not negotiate._
Improve the aim of my missiles. (Pay 3000 coins.)
You don't have enough money. Liese shakes her head. _I train nobody without tribute._
Liese takes your money and works you over for several hours, placing several sorts of missiles in your hands, having you aim, and smacking your hands with a stick when your form is imperfect.
When your session has concluded, you are exhausted and your hands are in agony. And yet, your skill has improved.
Improve my skill with weapons. (Pay 3000 coins.)

Liese takes your money and works you over for several hours, placing different weapons in your hands, having you strike the practice dummies, and smacking your hands with a stick when your form is imperfect.
I don't require training.
_Then what else do you have to say before you leave my home?_
_I have taught you everything I am willing to teach you._
I am hunting the shadowy beast that lurks in these woods.
Liese nods. _I am not surprised. Enemy or not, I can see you are a true warrior. What else would draw you out here?_
Have you seen the beast?
_I have. It comes to me almost every week. Of course, I can sense it well before it can get within striking distance of me. It makes its squawking noises, grows angry, and leaves._
Why have you not hunted it?
_It is too fast. To kill it, I would have to corner it in its lair. I am skilled, but I am not foolhardy enough to fight such a beast in its own territory._
It squawks at you?
_And hisses and barks and makes all manner of strange noises. Then, when I fail to respond, it grows angry. Then it flees._
_I would almost find the creature charming, were it not for all those that it has murdered._
_I don't know. But I do have a guess._
_Some foolhardy souls from Dhorl Stead were building a small settlement across the river to the east. Not long ago, I saw much smoke rising in that direction. Since then, it has been silent._
_If you can find your way over the river to the east, perhaps you might be able to pick up the beast's trail. I suspect you will find fresh devastation._
Has the forest been more peaceful lately?
_It has. And, based on your noticeable sense of pride and smugness, I would guess that you are responsible. In that case, I am grateful. And yet, I have not forgotten that we are enemies._
_I teach its warriors, and the warriors from other Steads that travel to me. As for Lord Carsta'Arl and Moritz'Kri and their following or not following of the old ways, I have nothing to say._
You have no opinions?
_I have many opinions. I keep them to myself._
Do you follow the old ways?
_I do, when they serve Khemeria. And only then._
She looks at Jenell as if defying your companion to argue. For once, the young shaman stays silent.
I was sent to hunt Moritz'Kri.
_I will not say anything against the wizard, but I also won't stop you from hunting him. He has not been a friend to me._
I was sent for Lord Carsta'Arl.
_He dared Avadon to attack us. We did not stop it. We will all pay the price, and we deserve it._
_Hopefully, others will learn from our mistakes. They will not defy Avadon until they are able to defend themselves. Or not attack until they can deliver a mortal blow._
Liese nods. _I will not lie and say I am sad to see you go, Avadon. But watch yourself. These woods are full of beasts, and I cannot hunt them all._
Your prey has been destroyed. You can finally begin your long journey back to the safety of Avadon. As you walk through the woods, Sevilin looks over at you.
_That wizard ... Moritz'Kri ... Did you think that there was anything suspicious about how he acted?_
I think everything he said made sense.
Sevilin nods. _I'll trust your judgment. It would be nice for there to be one person on the whole continent of Lynaeus we don't have to hunt down._
Very suspicious. Very, very suspicious.
Sevilin smiles. _It is nice to know that I am not going mad. Happily, the next step is for Heart Miranda to decide. I know that her judgment is good._
That is not for me to decide.
Sevilin smiles. _Yes, we are Hands, not Hearts. Happily, the next step is for Heart Miranda to hear all that has happened and to decide. I know that her judgment is good._
Shima bends down and picks up a long tube of glass. _Look at this._
Nathalie looks at it. She nods, fascinated. _Yes, that is odd._
Sevilin looks confused. _Yes? Glass? What of it?_
The shadowwalker sniffs the glass and says, _This is alchemical equipment. Recently used. A strange thing to find in an isolated barbarian village. Unless more is happening here._

Jenell taps you on the arm. _Pardon me, [N]. I need to talk to you. I am disturbed. I did not expect to meet Wyldrylm warriors up here. I certainly did not expect to see them on the run from the Pact. Like criminals!_
Do we really have to discuss this now?
Jenell frowns. _No, not now. But it will be discussed. I will not let ..._ She shakes her head. _Later._ And she walks on.
They are criminals, aren't they?
_Only for defending their land. For trying to use rights that the Wyldrylm has held dear since centuries before the Pact came along._
_I am wondering ..._ She looks over at you. _Do you think something should be done?_
I don't think that they should be here, either.
She nods. _I thought you might see it that way. Avadon does not always care about justice. I thought that you might be different._
_Since you have such an opinion ... Do you think something should be done?_
It is too small a matter to concern us.
Jenell says, in a voice full of bitterness, _Of course. Wyldrylm matters are always too small for Avadon. We're just little barbarian people. Tiny. Unimportant. I am never allowed to forget._
She walks on in grim silence.
They are lawbreakers. The only thing I would do is hunt them down.
Jenell says, in a voice full of bitterness, _Of course. That is the way of Avadon. The Wyldrylm only exists to be controlled and punished. Like a dog._
I would help them, but only for your sake.
_Well, I appreciate the sentiment, and I will remember that you said so._
And that is all she says. She walks on in silence.
Yes, we should aid them.
_I will remember that you said so._
Nathalie takes a deep breath and smiles. _Oh, it is good to be out of Avadon. Out in the sunlight and fresh air, on the hunt._
_I have to thank you, [N]. Until you came along, my time in Avadon was not ... happy. I was going to waste._
How did you come to be at Avadon?
_Even when I was young, I showed an aptitude for magic. By the time I was coming into womanhood, I had learned all the local sages had to teach. I could have grown to greatness in Kellemderiel._
_Instead, when I was fifteen, I traveled the free roads to Avadon. There, I rotted for two years._
You are enjoying this?
_Of course. I thought I would feel fear, but I don't. Only joy at the chance to put my power to true use._
How were you going to waste?

_I was accepted into Avadon, but, it turned out, only for training. Even though I was already fifteen, they would not send me on missions. And they said I was too ambitious. Too enthusiastic. Too eager to destroy the foes of the Pact._
_As if those traits could ever be flaws!_
Shima says, quietly, _Some of us have spent time being the targets of such ... energy. It does not always lead to wisdom._
They wanted to train you?
_They did say that I showed real potential. They wanted the sages of Avadon to teach me. To sit in dark rooms with old people and dusty scrolls. This, here now, is the only true training._
Are you ambitious?
She smiles demurely. _I only exist to serve mighty Redbeard, Keeper of Avadon. Don't worry. I will follow orders. Just don't send me back into the dark._
And what do you want?
She stops and looks you in the eye. _I am seventeen. I am done with waiting! I want to fulfill the great destiny that is set before me._ She speaks with the peculiar certainty of the young.
Jenell looks down at this small, delicate mage with a strange expression on her face. She acts as if she is looking at some new, strange, alien creature.
Nathalie continues, _I want to perfect my powers. I want to be a credit to Kellemderiel. And I want to find those who would return the Pact to the days of darkness and burn them to the ground._
Too much bravado is dangerous.
_Pfaugh! I am tired of such warnings. The Pact was built on bravado! Call me foolish. Call me eccentric. Just let me hunt! It is what I was born to do!_
She turns sharply and walks down the path.
I wish you luck in that noble goal.
She gives you a little curtsy and laughs. _I knew it the moment I saw you, [N]. I knew you would help me. I think we will have a very productive partnership. If Avadon lets us._
She turns and walks down the path.
You are a very, very, very odd girl.
Nathalie blushes slightly. _That is far from the worst thing I have been called since I came to Avadon. Come on. My eccentricities call for me to hunt!_ She giggles and walks down the path.
There are several hunters of the deep woods sitting around this firepit. They are roasting a freshly killed deer, unconcerned about anyone who might be drawn by the delicious smells.
When you get close, they jump to their feet and draw their blades. Then they realize that you clearly aren't Khemerians.
One of them says, _Move on, Pact warrior. We are here to deal with Dhorl Stead. We have no argument with you._
The Khemerian raiders are still sitting around their small cookfire. One of them says, _You have come back? Move on. We have nothing to do with you._
One of them takes a swig of ale and says, _We are here to watch Dhorl Stead. They are weaklings and upstarts, and we ... Wait. It is none of your business. Move on._
It's not wise to talk like that to a warrior of Avadon.
A warrior smirks. _Avadon? Everyone from your lands says they are friends of Avadon. We aren't scared. What would Avadon be doing out here?_
You'd better move on, or I'll make you.
The warriors look at each other, smiling. Then they rise to their feet, drawing their weapons. _Nobody will miss a few warriors from the Pact. And, if you are missed, Dhorl Stead will be blamed._
Then they attack.
(Just leave.)
They smirk at you as they go. Then they go back to consuming their venison.

The woods seem to grow darker. An icy wind blows down the path. You look around and see that something has joined you. It is a four-legged beast, shoulder high. It's hard to make out any details of its body. It is wreathed in swirling, black shadows.
You brace yourself, ready for a battle. It watches you silently, neither approaching nor retreating.
And then it starts to make noise. Strange, gurgling barking sounds.
(Listen.)
The sounds keep coming out. At first, they sound like gibberish. Then, you start to pick out things that almost sound like fragments of speech. Sounds like, _Ease_ and _Essss._
But none of it makes sense.
(Attack!)
You charge the creature, half-expecting for it to shy away. It doesn't. Instead, it snarls and bares its teeth. The white and red of its fangs are one detail that is very clear in the shadows.
Then it charges you.
(Keep listening.)
The creature keeps making the sounds. At first, you think that they are becoming clearer. Then they become cruder again.
The beast is starting to become frustrated.
(Mimic the sounds back to it.)
You copy the sounds the creature makes as closely as you can. It doesn't calm the beast. Instead, it seems to make it even angrier. Its barks become louder and more indistinct.
I can't understand you.

The creature is silent for a moment, listening to your words. Then it lets out a long, pained howl of frustration, snarls and bares its teeth. The white and red of its fangs are one detail that is very clear in the shadows.

The creature keeps making its sounds, the few clear syllables devolving into a mess of angry gibberish. Then it lets out a long, pained howl of frustration, snarls and bares its teeth. The white and red of its fangs are one detail that is very clear in the shadows.
Your attacks connect with the creature. It is surrounded with shadows, but its flesh is satisfyingly solid.

Then one blow not only wounds the beast but tears loose a fragment of the shadows surrounding it. The shadow pools on the ground. Then it starts to grow, taking the form of another wolf. Smaller and less distinct, but very, very fast.
The Shadow Beast howls in anger and pain. Then it turns and runs. Its body becomes less distinct and the shadows grow stronger. You try to block it, but it flows around you, running to safety.

The Shadow Beast reaches the shore of the river, but it doesn't stop. It runs across the surface of the flowing water. In moments, it's on the other side of the river. Then it disappears into the trees, leaving behind only a few splatters of black blood.

There is a small island in the middle of this underground lake. On it, you find an ogre dozing in a crude nest of sticks. He is surrounded by piles of trash and pools of unpleasant greenish liquid. You aren't sure how something surrounded by so much water can smell so bad.
Then your foot lands in some slime with a loud squish. In moments, the ogre is on his feet. He has a lot of bones hanging from leather thongs around his neck, including one human skull.
He snarls at you. _Hhrrrrahhh! What you do in my lair? Why you here?_
I am hunting for a shadowy beast. Seen it?
_Hhrrr? That thing? I see it. It hunts. It want you. But I get you! I get you, not beast._
Before you can respond, he snarls and lunges at you. The smell makes you want to gag.
I want to ask you about these woods.
_Rrrruhhh? Woods? You talk? I not talk! I ogre! I take! I hunt! Eat! I get you._
Speak with respect, creature. I am from Avadon!
He looks confused. _Avadon? What Avadon? That thing to eat? Tasty thing? You Avadon? I eat Avadon!_
I am hunting monsters. Like, say, you. (Attack.)
The ogre lets out a loud roar and charges you. He doesn't have quite enough intelligence to feel fear. The smell makes you want to gag.
At last, you enter the lair of the Shadow Beast. The remains of many of its victims are scattered on the floor. Many of them are from the small settlement above. The smell is horrible.

The creature itself lurks in the back of the cave. It lies curled on the floor, making pitiful mewling noises and licking its wounds. Its previous encounters with you have left it seriously hurt. The shadows around it are starting to fade.
When you get close to it, it rises, turns toward you, and opens its mouth. No sound comes out.
(Wait.)
When it sees that you aren't going to attack, the creature starts to let out some more of its strange, hacking sounds. And then it lets out an actual, clear word: _I ..._
The beast takes a step back. It seems as surprised by this as you are.
Nathalie says, _How fascinating. A savage killer, but made with a mind._
Jenell looks disgusted. _The horror hunts for sport, and now it wants to talk? What has been created here?_
The creature starts to let out some more of its strange, hacking sounds. As you rush toward it, weapon out, it lets out an actual, clear sound: _I ..._
But then it moves to defend itself. Trapped, it is ready to fight to the death.
You what?
It says, _I ... I ... I ..._ Then it pauses. Then it says, _No ... No ..._ It is searching for another word, but it can't seem to grasp it. Once again, it is growing more agitated.
Are you trying to talk?

It looks at you, its head tilted to one side. It seems to understand what you said. Then it says, _No ... No ..._ It is searching for another word, but it can't seem to grasp it. Once again, it is growing more agitated.
(Keep waiting.)

It watches you for a moment, making sure that you aren't about to attack. Then it says, _No ... No ..._ It is searching for another word, but it can't seem to grasp it. Once again, it is growing more agitated.
Keep calm. Speak slowly.
The creature ignores your words. It rocks from side to side. Some of its wounds reopen, and blood trickles down its side. It keeps saying, _No ... No ... NO! ... NO!_
Then it looks up at you. Its eyes seem sad. It is ready to give up. It starts to walk forward, stepping over its victims. And then it pounces ...
The creature keeps repeating its one word. _No ... No ... NO! ... NO!_ It rocks from side to side. Some of its wounds reopen, and blood trickles down its side. It is in great pain.
(Attack it first.)
The creature keeps repeating its one word. _No ... No ... NO! ... NO!_ It rocks from side to side. It seems like it has forgotten that you are there. You try to take advantage of its distraction.
Unfortunately, the moment you begin to shift forward, it looks up at you. It stops talking. It seems to give up. It pads forward over the bones of its victims. Then it pounces ...

The Shadow Beast slumps to the ground. It has almost no energy left. Though it has been wounded enough times to kill any natural beast ten times over, the dark magic within it sustains it. Lacking the power it provides, its shade servants fade away.
It looks up at you and says, with surprising clarity, _No. No hurt. No hurt._
So you can talk now?
_Hrrrr ... No hurt. No ... I ... I no hurt. No hurt you._
The beast looks up at you. It seems confused and surprised by the words it has finally managed to form.
I'll stop hurting you if you surrender.
_Hrrrr ... No hurt. No ... I ... I no hurt. I ... Ender._
Your words won't save you, monster. (Attack.)
The creature bows its head, ready for the death blow to come. Then something happens. It raises its head. It has smelled something. It lets out a long, low, horrible growl.
It doesn't move to attack, though. It is looking around, waiting for something. Or someone.
Why can I trust you after the horrible things you have done?
The beast is confused. It isn't quite smart enough to understand everything you say.
Why did you kill all of these people?
_Hrrr ... Hurt. Hurt. Hurt!_ You can't be sure exactly what it means, but, with some time, it might be able to explain more clearly.
It takes a step forward and bows its head. _Hurt. No hurt. You no hurt._ Then it takes another step forward. It seems to be submitting to you.
Sevilin is fascinated. _A full surrender? Not what I expected. Quite a trophy, though._
Shima watches the creature closely. _This sort of behavior can be a trick, but I don't think that is the case here. The beast seems well and truly beaten._
I will take you back to Avadon.
The beast understands what you say. It lowers its head and takes a few steps forward. For a brief moment, you think that one of these missions is going to end well.
Then something happens. It raises its head. It has smelled something. It lets out a long, low, horrible growl.
I will deliver you to Dhorl Stead.

The beast shudders in horror. It understands what you said, and this fate fills it with horror. Still, it lowers its heads and takes a few steps forward. For a brief moment, you think that one of these missions is going to end well.
You need to be destroyed.
The beast understands what you say. It lowers its heads and takes a few steps forward. It waits for the death blow with quiet dignity.
A man walks into the cave and joins you. It is Moritz'Kri, the wizard of Dhorl Stead, the mage who turned you away from the gates of the fortress.
He points his wand at the beast. _Excellent work. I didn't think it was real, but you proved me wrong. Now we can destroy the horror together._
He speaks without turning his gaze from the beast. _Nothing happens in these woods without my notice. My servants are everywhere._
Yes. Destroy it.
The shadow beast lets out a long, horrible roar. It looks at the wizard with total fear and loathing. _Ahrrrr! No! No!_
It has almost no strength left, but it will use all that it has to defy you to the end.
Wait! Don't kill it!
The beast looks from you to the wizard, confused. Moritz'Kri sneers. _Look at the bones. The beast has been murdering us. We will be avenged._
Fire flares from his wand. The beast snarls and uses what little remains of its strength to pounce.
At last, the Shadow Beast is dead. The shadows finally fade, revealing a large, twisted, wolflike creature. You can return to Avadon, but, first, you must obtain a sample of its flesh.
As you bend down by the creature, Moritz'Kri walks up beside you. _What are you doing?_
Stay back, Farlander. This does not concern you.
Moritz'Kri starts to respond, but then he thinks better of it. _All right. If you must._ You collect a tooth and some bits of flesh and fur.
As you rise, the wizard stares at you. He is trying to make a decision.
I need to take something back to Avadon.
Moritz'Kri says, _That beast is our prize. Before you can take anything, we need to ..._ You ignore the Farlander. You collect a tooth and some bits of flesh and fur.
Why did you kill the creature?
Mortiz'Kri looks at the bones. _The thing was a horror. These bodies cry for vengeance. I gave it to them, so that they may rest at peace. Their ashes will be sent to the sky._
_The people here are under my protection. I owe them no less._
