The beast seemed very scared of you.
_Of course. Most creatures, human and not, can sense my power. You are from Avadon, so you are not affected. As soon as it saw me, it knew I was its doom. Of course it was scared._
Do you know anything about this hidden workshop?

Moritz'Kri's lip curls slightly. He looks at the dusty circles and equipment with disdain. _I have my own tower, the finest place of magical learning in Khemeria. I don't know what rival would burrow out this squalid little place, but I will find out._
_My guess is that whoever made this place ended up being devoured by the beast._
I will be returning to Avadon.
The wizard starts to say something. Then he stops. He examines you closely. He is still trying to make a decision.
Yes? Anything else?

The mage sighs. Whatever he has decided, he doesn't seem happy about it. _I ... No. We ... We thank you for your help. Now that your business in Dhorl Stead is done, we wish you a safe journey back home._
_I will report this victory over our foe to Lord Carsta'Arl. Excuse me._ He turns and walks toward the exit.
The mage watches you silently as you go. Whatever he was trying to decide, you have more important work to do. You leave, ready to return home. Moritz'Kri follows soon after.
You try to get the Shadow Beast's attention, but it is fixated on the intruder that is approaching.
Two large clumps of shadow break off from the beast. They immediately solidify into two huge, insubstantial wolves. They aren't animals, only mindless constructs. But still very dangerous.
Moritz'Kri says, _I don't have time to talk. I must report what has happened to Oghrym'Tor._
Moritz'Kri says, _There is no time to talk. We must complete the hunt._
Skulltaker
Stara Stead Raider
Skulltaker is furious! He goes into a berserk frenzy!
Initiate Vala
Initiate Tria
Initiate Extari
An Initiate blinks back to a runic circle. The crystals by the circle begin to glow.
Beloch the Scourge
When no foe is near Beloch, he takes this chance to calm down and heal himself.
Ghost of Moritz'Kri
Beloch pushes at the energy membrane holding him in. It is thinner now.
Beloch creates two horrible, giant creatures. They are covered with green, goopy, acidic slime.
Titan Abomination
Beloch unleashes two more servants. They are large imps with thick, scaly hides. They move very quickly.
Gnarled Imp
Beloch releases the energy membrane holding him in. It is thicker now.
Beloch starts to look for a nearby target to curse.
Beloch casts a mighty curse on a nearby foe.
Beloch sees no foes nearby. His curse goes uncast.
Fresh defenders arrive via the stairs to the east and west.
Tower Defender
Growing Demon
A demon grows to full size!
Beloch's Servant
High Initiate Helma
High Initiate Helma realizes that she is losing the battle. She reaches up and crushes a crystal hanging from her neck. An aura of power surrounds her.
Steelward Imp
Runeward Imp
Fireward Imp
Iceward Imp
Curseward Imp
Ivo
Ivo manages, with difficulty, to climb the stairs.
Talking: Ivo stumbles past you. He is determined to do whatever it is he is doing.
Sharpshooter Kerem
Apprentice Tela
Draining Bat
Warped Tribesman
Tower Apprentice
Sticky Imp
Bedchamber Sentinel
Beastkeeper Harmon
Harmon's Watchbeast
Watchbat
Watchwolf
It's too late.
Curse the wizard.
Urrrghhhh.
Cough. Cough.
Squeak.
Squeak! Squeak!
Watch out for witches!

You finally reach the entrance to Moritz'Kri's Tower. Or one of the entrances. This is another of several huge fortifications guarding the road. They get higher as you go to the north, until you finally reach the gigantic, granite spire that is the wizard's tower.

The gates ahead are guarded. Not by magical constructs, but by Khemerian soldiers, who train their bows on you as you get closer. As you come close to being in range, you can see that the warriors are standing very still. They don't say a word, and their eyes are glazed over.
Moritz'Kri has decided to keep his defenders' morale high by the simple step of magically controlling their minds. To reach your target, you will have to defend yourself from these unfortunates.
You reach the far side of this fortification and enter a large clearing, where visiting merchants can drop off supplies and have them carried into the fort.
Then you see Moritz'Kri. The wizard is standing in the middle of the road. Instantly, you reach for your weapon.
But then you realize that he is standing absolutely still, staring off into nothingness. If you look hard, you can see through him. He is a shade, placed here to wait for you.

You enter a gigantic hall. A throne and several marble benches are arranged surrounding a central platform. A magic circle is in the center. Carsta'Arl and the other lords could come here for a demonstration of whatever magical goodies the wizard developed for them.
Right now, a bored demon stands in the middle of the circle. Nobody else is here. The infernal beast yawns as you enter. Then it sits down and starts gnawing on a bone.
At last, you are before Moritz'Kri's actual tower. It looms above you. The entrance is just to the northeast, and the gate is open. The raw magical power in the air is giving you a headache.

But that is not all you see in this huge clearing. To the east, you can see another tower, much smaller than the main complex. To the west, you see the ruins of a small tower. Its walls crumbled from the force of a massive explosion. Bats circle over it.
And to the northwest, a line of black, greasy smoke rises from behind the rocky spires. You can hear rumbles and howls, and the grass and other plants grow more sickly in that direction.

Powerful, experimental magic is a difficult endeavor, and mishaps can have horrible effects. Like the Shadow Beast preying on the townsfolk. Or the tower to the southwest, which appears to have completely exploded.
Nathalie looks at the rubble and smirks. _I bet Moritz'Kri didn't try that experiment again._

The ground around the ruins is scorched and strewn with rubble. The guards and apprentices stay away from here. You do notice that a lot of bats are circling the shattered tower, and some of them are very large.
You get closer to the walled off compound to the north. Black, greasy smoke still rises from beyond the gate, and the air carries a powerful reek of sulfur.
Nathalie looks at the barrier, eyes gleaming. _The wizard must be doing something remarkable here. Something amazing._ She winks at you. _It will be fun to destroy it._

As you get closer, the feeling of dark magic in the air gets heavier. Only your prolonged training enables you to not turn back. Or flee in terror. The gates are sealed and protected with runes. Whatever Moritz'Kri is doing back there, you can't get in this way.
Shima looks at the sealed gate and shakes his head. _I think I have a guess where the wizard is hiding. It will be hard to find a way in, but we have no choice._
You enter the small, eastern tower. You immediately realize why Moritz'Kri set the work here far from his main tower.
The reek of prisoners and wild beasts is heavy in the air. The sound of shouts and roars echoes through the halls. This is the place where he creates many of his horrors.

This huge hall looks like yet another amphitheater. However, you realize that it's not for showing off Moritz'Kri's creations. It's for pitting them against each other, evaluating their skill in battle. Mops are everywhere, but they haven't been able to entirely clear away the stains.

Jenell shudders in horror. _How ... How is this ... We and the Khemerians are from the same stock. The same origins, the same ideals. How did they let themselves sink so far? I mourn for them. They are lost._
As you enter this part of the ruin, a colony of bats settles down in the rocks to the south. They are enormous creatures with huge, almost comically large fangs. More of Moritz'Kri's work, no doubt.

The bats don't seem very aggressive. They watch you and hiss a lot as you approach, but they haven't attacked yet. You notice one odd thing, though. The closer you get, the slower and more sluggish you feel. Odd.
As you cross the arena, you realize that several cages to the north have been left open. Three of Moritz'Kri's monstrosities have been left inside, mistreated, hungry, and increasingly vicious.
These massive wolves step out of their cages and pad south, stalking you.
Singefur Beast
Shockfur Beast
Rimefur Beast

This is yet another of Moritz'Kri's workshops. However, after the wizard fled the tower, something went wrong. Several apprentices were gruesomely killed here, but not until after they scorched the walls and floor with their attempts to defend themselves.
You look around, trying to figure out what killed them. Then you hear squeaking from behind you. The concealed beasts that ambushed the apprentices emerge from the shadows behind you.
Warped Bat

There is a locked door here. Not an ordinary one, either. There is a large, glowing rune of protection etched into the floor in front of it. Wisps of light float up from the rune and waft toward the door, promising a bad day for anyone who wants to pick the lock.
Happily, the athame you received in Redbeard's Tower should have the power necessary to break the ward.
This was a huge, lovely cavern, featuring a peaceful lake and a forest of delicate stalagmites, formed by countless centuries of dripping water.

Someone has been smashing down the stone formations and replacing them with rows of cages. The cages are currently clean and empty. When the work was completed, Moritz'Kri would have had the space to massively expand the scope of his twisted experiments.
Happily, you have interrupted the process.

You turn this wheel. Looking down through the grate to the south, you can see that you are opening a gate below you. You finish opening the gate and then smash the wheel, keeping anyone from closing it behind you.
You look at the wheel. It is still broken.

You try to open this strong box. When you touch it, however, a powerful shock sears your fingers and forces you to jump back. Until you can find a way past the spell (or destroy the source of its power), you won't be able to get inside.
You open the strongbox. As you do, your fingers receive a slight shock. A spell was holding it shut, but the magic is quickly fading way.

There are two things of interest. First, there is a sheaf of sheets of papyrus, covered with dense writing. All of it is in an odd magical dialect. You can't understand it, but you are sure Avadon would be interested.

Second, under the sheaf of papers, you find a key. It was hard to see. It is made of metal, but translucent. It seems to exist halfway between this world and another. You take everything. This is all very helpful, but Moritz'Kri still needs to be found.
The box is still empty.

This case is filled with a remarkable variety of trophies, totems, and other minor artifacts. Moritz'Kri must have obtained them, examined them, found them of insufficient interest, and stored them away.
You search through them, but you find nothing you can use. You close the case.
Remembering an earlier request, you look through the case for a wooden totem, the sort that might add power to a stone circle. You find something of interest in the back.

It is definitely a totem, weather-beaten and covered with moss. When you touch it, you feel a brief surge of hostile magic. Then the sensation fades. You put it in a bag, careful not to touch it with bare skin.

As you cross this oddly empty workshop, the gate slams shut behind you. A cloud of sulfurous smoke appears in the center of the room, blocking your vision. When it fades, the ring of torches has vanished. In their place, you see a ... creature.

It looks like a demon. Sort of. Actually, it looks like a human that has been painfully altered by Moritz'Kri to be more demonish. The thing is red, twisted, and covered with scales. It barely seems to recognize that you are there. It stares at the ground and breathes heavily.

Then it lets out a long, tortured gurgle. Its muscles tense. It starts to concentrate. Two things happen. The air around the beast starts to grow very hot. And an invisible hand starts dragging you slowly across the stone toward the creature.

The demon-thing concentrates harder, exerting the power infused into its body by Moritz'Kri's spells. The invisible hands grabbing at you grow stronger. You slide slowly, inexorably across the floor toward the creature.

The demon-thing continues to moan and mumble. Its eyes glow red. The muscles in its face and neck grow taut. Then, with a final burst of effort, the air around the beast briefly catches fire. Everything near the creature is bathed in searing heat.
With a final blow, the demon-thing falls to the ground. The invisible hands release you. The air grows cooler. For a moment, the beast's mind returns to it.
It looks up at you and rasps, _Thank ... you ..._ and then it expires.
The magic holding you prisoner fades away. The gates slowly open.
Once again, the gate closes behind you. Another of Moritz'Kri's experiments appears before you, ready for one final battle-test. Actually, there are two identical experiments, one in each circle.

They are humans. Or were, before the wizard infused them with who knows what bizarre magic. Their skin is blue. Their mouths are full of fangs. And, most interestingly, the two creatures are tethered by a long, thin thread of magical light.
The beasts step out of their circles and lurch toward you. Moritz'Kri has kept them hungry, so that they attack intruders with great enthusiasm.
One of the twins stumbles, weakened by your attacks. The other looks at it with a strange, almost touching look of concern. The creatures maintain some human emotions.
Then the stronger sends a pulse of energy along the thread of light to the weaker. The more-damaged beast is revived. It gives its twin a fanged grin of gratitude.

Slaying the first of the twin monsters caused horrible pain to the survivor. After the loss of its partner, death seems to come as a blessing. Mortally wounded, it crawls across the floor to its twin. It reaches the other, grabs its hand, and expires.
The gates slowly open.
There are three people waiting in these alcoves, each standing in a magic circle. Each circle is flanked by a pair of tall, glowing crystal spires. As you enter, they look at you with loathing.
_Moritz'Kri did not lie,_ says the first.
_The invader of Avadon has come. [N] is here,_ says the second.
_Let us show the might of the apprentices of Moritz'Kri! Let us prove ourselves,_ shouts the third. And then they attack.

The final apprentice of Moritz'Kri falls before your attack. You had predicted that the Khemerian wizard would be a harsh master, but it is horrifying how casually he is throwing away those sworn to his service.
The gate in the northwest corner opens. You must be close to the top of the tower.
One of the apprentices disappears in a cloud of shimmering blue sparks. A moment later, he reappears in his stone circle. Then the crystals flanking the circle begin to pulse and hum.
As you watch in horror, power flows into the circle. The energy quickly revives the apprentice.
High Initiate Helma suffers a mortal blow. She is dead before she hits the ground. Moritz'Kri is now out of apprentices.
And yet, you have searched all of his tower, and you have found no sign of the cruel, Khemerian wizard. Perhaps there is something in this workshop to show where he has gone.
_Squeak!_

When you get close to the image of Moritz'Kri, it suddenly comes to life. You jump back, prepared to dodge bolts of fire or lightning or whatever. Happily, the shade seems to only be capable of looking and talking, not fighting.

The shade looks around for a bit, as if confused. Then it sees you. When it speaks, Moritz'Kri's voice comes out. _Where ... Where ... Ah. Yes. Only the empty gate. I see you now, [N]. I will be watching you as you destroy my tower. Or fall to it._
Is that really you, wizard?

_It is I. Through these delicate constructs I can watch all that happens in my tower. And, sometimes, in the lands beyond. When that Laurella girl returns to these lands, I will see it. I have a delightful vengeance planned for her._
You can see me?
_Oh, yes. I see you, standing there, puffed up with arrogance, thinking you have a hope of containing the powers I have unleashed._
_You don't._
Where are you hiding?
The shade's face is expressionless, but you can hear the amusement in the wizard's voice. _I won't tell you, of course. You will have to seek me out._
_I opened the gates for you. You will be tested. And, if you are worthy, you will be used and consumed._
I demand, in the name of Avadon, that you come out.
The shade's face is expressionless, but you can hear the irritation in the wizard's voice. _Ever the arrogance, even in the jaws of your doom. Once, it amused me. Now I only wish to see it crushed._
Why did you let me in?
_Because keeping the gates closed would have solved nothing. You would have returned with more force. Better instead to invite you in when you are few and let your arrogance lead you to your doom._
What are you doing?
The shade's face doesn't move, but you hear laughter. _You will find out soon._
I am coming for you.
_Of course. If you survive the tests, you will have the chance to face me. I hope you succeed. I want to see the look in your eyes as you are devoured._
There is no deal we can work out?
_Of course not. We are long past dealing. You will face my tests. If you succeed, I will see the look in your eyes as you are devoured._
So be it. (Walk past the shade.)
As you walk by, the shade becomes motionless. Moritz'Kri is no longer looking at you through it.
Well, I won't let you watch me anymore. (Destroy the shade.)
Moritz'Kri says, _Well, I ... Wait! ..._ And, with one blow, the shade pops like a bubble.
You get closer to the demon in the circle. You can see that it is a huge, gnarled specimen, bearing centuries of battle scars and an iron collar of obedience around its neck.

It looks over at you and snorts. _So you are the mortal the wizard told me to stop. Your name is ..._ It concentrates on you. _... [N]. Yes, [N]. Well, [N], I don't see the wizard here. I think I will just let you by to spite him._
Moritz'Kri is summoning demons too?
_Bah! He does not! We were too much work to control, so he changed to making his servants with magic instead. But he keeps me around as a plaything. He shows me off to his guests to impress them!_
_I hope you kill him._
Die, infernal beast! (Attack.)
The demon looks startled. _What? You would challenge a lord of the infernal realms? When I would let you pass? I suppose I have to kill you after all. Serves you right!_
The creature stands up straight and, with no trouble, walks out of the binding circle. As it approaches, you hear soldiers shouting to the east and west.
I will simply pass by. (Walk past.)

The demon mockingly waves you by. Then the iron collar does something. It reaches up with clawed hands and grabs the metal, which is starting to glow red. _Curse you, wizard! I must obey orders after all!_

There are several grimy books on this pedestal. They mostly contain lists of the creatures imprisoned here, the magical treatments they received in this room, and the horrible ends. It's unsettling reading.
Interestingly, you do find the entry for the Shadow Beast. It was tested in battle a number of times, always prevailed, and was finally marked as, _Escaped. Apprentice responsible dealt with._

Under the ledgers, you find a stained and burnt notebook. Flipping through it, you find that it is a collection of alchemical recipes, written in Moritz'Kri's own hand. Might be valuable. You take it.
You have found Moritz'Kri at last. Not in time, though. The ritual he fled to his tower to perform is complete. He is no longer alone.

He stands fearlessly in front of a dark portal. It is a tear in reality. Beyond the veil, you can faintly see a blackened landscape of lava and bones. It is the creature standing in the portal, however, that draws much of your attention.
It is a demon, enormous, muscular, and full of raw power. It stands in the portal almost as if it is stuck. Moritz'Kri, the mad wizard who called it from beyond, is standing there talking to it.

Several shelves of books have been secured in this cavern, a bleak chamber of bare stone. The chill in this cave is not natural. Much of it comes from the tomes, bound in black leather, that surround you.
The demons who assaulted you on the way in might not have been summoned by Moritz'Kri. They might simply have been attracted by the dark power bound into these pages.
You approach the pedestal cautiously. The books stacked upon it, decorated with skulls and other grim motifs, give you pause. Avadon only hunts down dark magic like this to destroy it, not use it.
You look a little closer, and then you back away. Anything you learn here could only come to hurt you later.

And yet, there is one book here of definite interest to Avadon. It's at the bottom of the pile, but you can see its name on the spine: _The Krysanth._ You slide it out of the pile, taking care not to touch any of the other books.
You try to open this sarcophagus. It takes a massive amount of effort and straining, but you manage to dislodge the stone lid.
As it clatters to the floor, something rises from within. Something very angry to have been imprisoned for so long.
You examine the sarcophagus. All it contains are scraps of cloth and a handful of bone chips.
Vengeful Bones
As the lid clatters to the floor, a cloud of choking snow and dust flies out of the sealed crypt. Several creatures rise from within, all very angry to have been imprisoned for so long.
You try to open the sarcophagus. However, the moment you touch it, a powerful chill starts to spread up your arms. With difficulty, you pry your frozen hands loose.
Hateful Bones
The portal is a terrifying rip in the fabric of reality, opening a path to the infernal realms, from which there is no return.
You decide that it's wise to keep your distance. As long as Beloch is here, there is no way to close the portal.
Now that Beloch is gone, the portal is closing on its own. Soon, it will disappear entirely.
Once again, you are smacking Moritz'Kri around. However, instead of in Carsta'Arl's throne room, you are in his home ground, standing before a demon he summoned.
Moritz'Kri calls out, _Beloch, I command you. Give me shielding from beyond!_

Beloch looks at you and shrugs, as if to say, _What can you do?_ Then he pokes at the membrane that holds him out of your world. Imps start to appear in a circle around you. As each appears, a faint shield of energy appears around the wizard.
Moritz'Kri looks around. _Clever. You have lured me away from my protector. A problem easily solved ..._
He fades away. A moment later, you see him standing in front of Beloch.
Moritz'Kri looks to Beloch. _You want to be trapped there? If not, I require stronger aid!_
Beloch nods. _I suppose that is part of a bargain. I have no shortage of irritable souls stored away._ Once again, the demon pokes at the membrane of energy that holds him in.
Infernals begin to come through. When they arrive, they are small and delicate. However, they immediately begin to grow.
Moritz'Kri stumbles back, beaten and bloodied. He looks over at Beloch, who watches impassively. _Demon, do you want into our world or not? Save me!_
Beloch smiles. _And if I save you, will you give me what I ask?_
_Everything,_ Moritz'Kri cries! _Everything!_

Beloch laughs. _Everything? How can I refuse such an offer?_ He pokes at the membrane, and a pack of the hounds of hell are unleashed. They are much reduced in strength from passing through the barrier, but they are still deadly.
Moritz'Kri falls to his knees. His protector has failed him. His strength has faded. He falls backward and crawls toward Beloch, hoping for aid. _Please, Beloch, help me._

_No, wizard,_ Beloch intones. _You promised me everything! And everything is what I shall have!_ He reaches out, using all his strength, and his clawed hand stretches the membrane holding him until a small hole appears in it.
He grabs Moritz'Kri around the wrist. As the wizard screams in agony and pure terror, Beloch pulls him through the barrier and into the infernal realms.
Then the battle is done. The wizard has gone. Beloch's imps disappear. You are left in the arena, staring at the demon. He shows no signs of going anywhere.
Your mission is completed, and the demon lord is held in place. You are free to return to Avadon now, or to come back and deal with the demon when you have gained strength.
Beloch watches you with interest. However, as long as Moritz'Kri commands him, he can't talk to you.
Beloch pushes at the energy membrane that holds him in. It grows thinner, temporarily reducing the protection it gives him.
With the barrier thinner, he concentrates and sends some of his power through. It coalesces into two gibbering monstrosities, which gurgle and shamble toward you.
Beloch releases the membrane, which snaps back to full strength. It holds him back and keeps him from fully entering your world. However, it also provides him with a good deal of protection.
Beloch raises a hand and starts pointing his claw. Your hair stands on end. He is looking for a nearby target to deliver a powerful curse to.
One of your blows knocks Beloch off-balance. He takes an involuntarily step backwards before he catches himself.
Then he snarls, his calm demeanor gone. _You would truly challenge me? The mighty Beloch? Well, I have another servant who can aid me. Come out, worm!_
A shade appears before you. It is the translucent form of Moritz'Kri. His body appears unharmed, but his eyes betray a tale of infernal imprisonment and unending torment.
Beloch says, _This is your chance for revenge, scum. Help me drive these pitiful creatures away._
You knock Beloch off balance. He takes a step backwards, and then another. This was the opening you were waiting for.
You leap forward, jump, and fling yourself against the membrane of energy. Your shoulder strikes Beloch the Scourge in the middle of the shoulder before he can regain his balance.
As the barrier flings you back to safety, the mighty demon falls. Screaming in rage, he falls through the hole of reality. He howls, _[N], you will pay!_, and then he is gone.
Though he suffered enough wounds to kill twenty lesser beings, you are sure that the creature will live. And he will have a grudge against you. An eternal one.
But you aren't afraid. You are a warrior of Avadon.

There is a Khemerian tribesman curled up in the corner here. Somehow, he avoided being killed by the warped creatures surrounding him. He is obviously unwell. His skin has a sickly green tinge, and he is shaking and covered with sweat.
Jenell kneels down and mops his brow. As much as she hates Khemerians, even she feels sympathy for this pathetic soul.
He looks up at you. _Help? Help at last? I ... I am Ivo. Still. I ... Free the others? I can! I can help before it's too late?_
What has Moritz'Kri done to you?
_The ... wizard?_ Ivo uses some of his meager remaining energy to spit on the stone floor. _He does this to us. Making ... warriors. Warriors to kill ... I don't know. It was him. He does this._
Sevilin chooses an inappropriate moment to wax philosophical. _The Kva would never tolerate this sort of thing. This defies any sense of order, of justice. The Farlands are a savage place._
Shima shrugs. _This happens everywhere. The only thing that changes is whether we notice it or not._
Can I help you?
_I am ... I will be fine. Must help ... Must free others. I am lost._
How did you come to be here?
_Moritz'Kri takes ... clanless. Those in deep woods. Not missed. Wife taken. Wife lost. Now ... me. Can ... help others. All I want._
Nathalie winces. _I admire enthusiasm in one's magical work, but this is definitely excessive._
Just stay here. I'll be back soon.
Your words have the opposite of the intended effect. Ivo grips the wall and pulls himself to his feet. _Not much time. I stole the key! I can save them!_
He lurches off to the northeast.
Ivo nods weakly. _Yes! Yes! Must ... be strong!_ He grips the wall and pulls himself to his feet. _Not much time. I stole the key! I can save them!_

Ivo reaches the gate and pulls a key from his pocket. He must have stolen it in the confusion after Moritz'Kri abandoned this tower. He puts it in the keyhole of the gate and turns it. He uses the last of his strength to lift the gate, though it only rises a few feet before it becomes stuck.
Strange. That gate is very heavy. You wonder where he got the strength, in his pitiful state, to lift it.

Then he turns, and you see that Moritz'Kri's magic has finally succeeded in consuming Ivo. All comprehension has gone from his eyes. He debates whether to attack you or the prisoners in the cell beyond. He chooses you ...
Corrupted Khemerian
There are four pitiful, hungry Khemerians in the back of this cell. They are all trembling, not from sickness but from abject terror.
But Khemerians, whatever one might think of them, are made of strong stuff. Once they realize that the gate is open, they grab weapons and scraps of food and run for the stairs.
Before they leave, you ask them if they know where Moritz'Kri is. They have no idea. However, they provide several sincere suggestions for things you can do to the mad wizard before he expires.
Sevilin looks up the stairs, no doubt imagining the traps and horrors Moritz'Kri left behind in his tower.
_Walking into an ambush is still difficult for me, harder than it should be for a Hand of Avadon. And yet, knowing that we brought the scum who attacked me to justice helps. Let's go. I'm ready._

He shudders in horror. _Walking into an ambush is still difficult for me, harder than it should be for a Hand of Avadon. I can't help but think about the scum who attacked me. And,_ he adds bitterly, _who got away._
_Let's go. We have no choice._
This long hall is Moritz'Kri's art gallery. Shima looks at the pieces on the walls. _For a barbarian among barbarians, the wizard has excellent taste. Lovely pieces, brought from all over Lynaeus. _
Jenell shakes her head. _Pieces from everywhere but here. The wizard has nothing but shame for his own people._
Nathalie nods. _Even tapestries from Kellemderial. Good taste, indeed. And expensive._
Shima looks more closely at a painting. _Interesting._
In what way?
_That one so twisted and cruel can still appreciate the lovely and refined. For example, our rivals in Holklanda, the Honored Forge, were renowned for their love of fine pottery and sculpture._
_Yes, they must have loved admiring their pots and vases after a long, exhausting day of destroying my family and murdering my father._
Let's go.
Shima looks at you. _I ... I am sorry. I am so embarrassed. I ... The magic here. It is starting to ... distract me. Let us go._
Are you all right?
_Am I ... I ..._ He stands up, clearly embarrassed. _I am sorry. That was a shameful display. It ... The magic here. It is starting to ... distract me. Let us go._

When she sees the stairs ahead, Jenell seems very tired. _Another floor, another series of the wizard's disgusting workshops. I did not think Khemeria could disgust me more. And to think that some of my fellows of the Wyldrylm felt they needed to hide here._
_I am relieved we were able to help them. I hope they can find a safe place to live. Though, of course, they should have been allowed to stay where they were._
_But we abandoned them,_ she adds bitterly. _Left them to be hunted by the Khemerians. Avadon's justice._
_I am sorry. This place ... It affects me. Let us go._

Nathalie looks into yet another workshop, with scorched floors and magic circles, and shakes her head. _Oh, for the ... Has Moritz'Kri ever, even once, exercised even a tiniest bit of restraint? Ever?_
Sevilin says, _I thought you envied this tower._
Shima says, _Was I mistaken? It seemed that you admired this tower._
Jenell says, _You have never been one for restraint yourself. You really don't want a tower like this?_
Nathalie says, _I want a tower like this, someday. Yet, I think three or four workshops are enough. More than that shows a dangerous lack of focus and discipline._

You enter Moritz'Kri's Tower. It is truly spectacular. Even though the stones that make up the walls are crude and uneven, the spire stretches far above you, even higher than Redbeard's tower. The wizard was determined that his home awe any who entered it.
And, to greet visitors, another shade of Moritz'Kri stands before you. It is motionless at first. It takes a moment to alert Moritz'Kri that you are here.

Then, at last, it comes to life. You hear Moritz'Kri's voice, irritated and distracted. _Yes? What? Who? Ah! It is [N], come into my home. I don't have time to talk. My preparations are at a critical stage._
_Also, please do not destroy this shade. They require some concentration to replace._
Stop spying on me, wizard. (Destroy the shade.)
_What? Won't you ... No! These are so difficult to make ..._ With one blow, the shade pops and fades.
I don't have time to banter with you. (Walk past.)
_All right. I think we will meet soon ... Wait. This part is critical. I must ..._ Suddenly, you hear a rumbling to the northwest. The tower begins to shudder around you. Then it is still.
_Perfect. Another stage complete. See you soon ..._ And then the shade is motionless again.
I am going to enter your tower.
_Of course. I am counting on it. You will blunder through, smashing and stabbing, in the honored Avadon tradition. I was actually counting on it. Saves me some time._

_Preparing. I still need two hours or so to complete my work. Exactly the amount of time it should take to smash your way through my tower. Assuming, of course, that my defenders don't kill you. Honestly, I'm not sure whether I want them to or not._
You don't mind me smashing up your tower?
_The tower is only stone. Soon, I will be able to have a hundred such homes, if I want. As for my defenders, I ... Wait. Yes. It is time. I ..._ The shade is suddenly motionless.
The shade starts to talk again. _Wait. This part is critical. I must ..._ Suddenly, you hear a rumbling to the northwest. The tower begins to shudder around you. Then it is still.

Once again, you find one of Moritz'Kri's shades placed here to greet (or spy upon) those who visit the caves under his tower. It takes some time, but the wizard finally looks through the eyes of this shade, sees you, and begins to speak.
_You passed through the tower. That means that all of my apprentices are dead. Unfortunate, but necessary. I will expect to see you soon._
_And please do not destroy this shade. In addition to being a waste of a cunningly made magical construct, it causes its controller some pain._
I prefer silence. (Destroy the shade.)
Moritz'Kri, expecting this, abandons the shade. It becomes motionless a moment before your blow shatters it.

Shortly after, there is another earthquake, strong enough to make you think that the tower is about to collapse above you. You hear the stone of the spire groaning and cracking. And then the tremor ceases. Something has happened, something powerful.
You wanted me to destroy your apprentices?

_Callous, I know, but they knew too many of my secrets. They could not be allowed to compete with me or to reveal what they knew to the Pact. It was a risk they accepted when they came here. Though, I confess, their grim fate was far more likely than they realized._
I have seen more of the horrors you have been creating.

_Horrors? You are close enough to touch the finest, most cunning magical creations in all of Lynaeus, and you call them horrors?_ He sighs. _There is no appreciation for fine craftsmanship these days._
_However, what you have seen is of little importance compared to my final work!_
I call them horrors, and I destroyed them.
_No matter. Now that I know the secrets, I can always make more. Though, once my final work is completed, it will not be necessary._
Why did you make them?

_Because I thought that I could craft an army of mighty beasts strong enough to destroy the Pact. I was wrong. To bring down game that large, I need a ... a ... No. I will not spoil the surprise. It will consume you soon enough._
Did Carsta'Arl tell you to make them?
_Heh. I am a Khemerian at heart. Though my lord turned craven and abandoned me, I will not betray him in return. So, no. Carsta'Arl knew nothing of my forbidden crafts._
And what are you making now? What is your final work?
_It is ... is ... Already? Yes! It is ready! The runes worked faster than I expected. It is time to break through ..._ The shade emits a long, nonsensical chant. It grows louder and deeper.
The stone starts to shake under his feet. Above you, you can hear the walls of the tower cracking and groaning. Dust showers from the ceiling ...
Stop!
The chanting reaches a crescendo. The earthquake becomes strong enough to make you fear that the spire above will collapse. And then, in an instant, it ceases.
You hear Moritz'Kri again. He sounds out of breath but very pleased with himself. _It is done. Yes. Come. It is time._
What has happened?
_The end. Of the Pact. Of you. Of this Age. Come see. Please. It is ... glorious. Hurry. Don't hurry. It doesn't matter. The end. Is the same._
The shade becomes motionless. The next time the wizard speaks with you, he intends for it to be in person.

You step out into the highest chamber of Moritz'Kri's tower. It is a beautiful workshop, featuring the finest magical tomes and alchemical equipment. Many of the wizard's most delicate and powerful spells must have been cast here.

However, you are disappointed to find that the wizard himself is not here. Instead, you find a robed woman in her twenties. She wields a beautiful, carved wooden staff. She looks so furious that she can barely contain herself.
She says, _I am High Initiate Helma, first of Moritz'Kri's students! I will slay you for what you have done here today!_
Die, mage! (Attack.)
Helma smiles. She raises her staff over her head. Lightning crackles along its length. _Die, scum of Avadon!_
Helma stops short. _Wait. Why? Why avenge my fellow students? Why prove myself to my master? It is an honor to be allowed to do battle with you!_
Seems reasonable. (Attack.)
Helma grins, far more confident than she should be. She raises her staff over her head. Lightning crackles along its length. _Die, scum of Avadon!_
Moritz'Kri abandoned you to die. He already killed his apprentices in Oghrym'Tor.
Helma stops and lowers her staff. _He ... I ... I knew they died. But I thought ... I should not believe you. But ... He did not take me. He left me here. Alone._
She looks up at you. _This is not a good time and place to fight. If I leave, I will be avenged upon you, only not today. Do you understand?_
Where is the wizard?
_I would not mind letting him kill you instead of me. The last I saw him, he was entering the caves below the tower. You will need a key. Once I am gone, it will not be difficult to find._
Actually, that doesn't sound so great. (Attack.)
Helma nods. She is ready to fight, though her confidence is gone. She raises her staff over her head. Lightning crackles along its length. _Die, scum of Avadon!_
Understood. Go.
Helma nods and lowers her staff. _I hope the wizard kills you. Also, I wouldn't mind if you beat him up a bit as well._
Then she runs down the stairs and is gone.

You walk up behind Moritz'Kri, close enough to get a better look at what he has done. He has opened a rift to the infernal realms, and something is trying to come through. An enormous beast, a lord of the demonic realms. It struggles to push through, eager to spread terror and destruction.

But something is holding it back. It is most of the way through the dark fissure, but a gossamer sheet of energy holds it back. It tries to claw its way loose, but the field resists its mighty attacks.

Your attempt to sneak up on the wizard, unsurprisingly, doesn't work. He turns to face you, exhausted and sweaty, but triumphant. _Behold! Behold Beloch the Scourge! Soon it will be in our world, under my command, ready to ravage the Pact!_
Moritz'Kri, you are guilty of illegal magic. You must return with me to Avadon.
Moritz'Kri laughs. _I admire you, [N]. Even here, at the gateway to the infernal realms, you trust in the power of Avadon._
_But I have summoned Beloch to make your power meaningless! Today marks the beginning of the end for Avadon!_
Beloch the Scourge listens to this exchange and smiles. Once it is loose, you suspect that it will find a way of doing to your world whatever it wants.
What have you done? Are you mad?
_Mad? Yes, they called me mad. But I will show them! I will show them all!_ He thinks on this. _Actually, I do sound a bit mad, don't I? No, I am not mad. I have never been more rational._
_I have summoned Beloch to make your power meaningless! Today marks the beginning of the end for Avadon!_
Why have you done this?

_Because, for my entire life, I have wanted only one thing. I have wanted to remove the boot on Khemeria's neck. I longed for the destruction of the Pact. But, for all my power, I am only one man. This is the only way to achieve my life's goal._
Wasn't making monstrous creatures enough for you?
_No! That is the whole point! The ghouls, the Shadow Beast, those are curiosities. They should be toured through the provinces as a show, not relied upon to destroy Avadon._
_Once, I consorted with infernals. Then I returned to that work, once I found that there was one I could summon mighty enough for the great task!_ Beloch smiles and nods modestly.
Your demon appears to be stuck.

_You are correct. He is trapped now, between one world and the other. To bring him the rest of the way, there must be a sacrifice. Souls of courage, bearing true power and strength. Brought before him, their blood spilled on the gossamer bonds that hold Beloch back._
_Then he will be free, and at my command!_ Beloch, fifteen feet tall and infused with the raw power of the infernal realms, shrugs.
You should have saved some apprentices to be sacrificed.
_Those worms? Those servants? They were only fit to slow you down. And they barely achieved that!_
Why don't you sacrifice yourself?
_I considered it. I am no coward. If I thought it would end the Pact, I would give my life in an instant._
_However, without me to control it, Beloch would go mad. All would serve to feed him, not just those of the Pact._
_It is true,_ Beloch adds in a deep voice. _I cannot deny it._
You think that you can sacrifice me?

_I will. I will subdue you with my power. I will draw you to the portal. In your last moments of life, as you bleed from many wounds, I will feed you into the maw of Beloch. He will eat your very life essence, and he will break free from these bonds._
_So now you will try to resist. It is your way. And then the end will come._
You must reverse this experiment!
_It is not possible. Beloch is here. To force him to return is beyond even my power. Enough talk._

_Beloch,_ Moritz'Kri shouts, _serve me!_ The demon can only send a sliver of his power through the barrier to the wizard, but what he can give, he gives. _Yessss ..._ the mad Khemerian says. _At lassssst! It issss time!_
You must return to Avadon or die. There is no other option. (Attack.)
_I have tired at last of your bravado. Do you not see that you have stumbled into your final ..._ He shakes his head. Beads of sweat fly from his brow. _Enough talk. It is time!_
Now that Moritz'Kri is dead, Beloch the Scourge stands before you. The magical bonds hold it in place. It seems like it could step back through the portal if it wanted to, but it doesn't.
The demon looks down at you and smiles. Being near it makes you feel the same existential terror you felt when you faced the dragons in The Kva.
You realize that you don't need to fight this creature yourself. You can always leave it for Avadon's mages.
_So,_ it rumbles, _We are at an impasse._
Tell me about yourself.
_I am Beloch the Scourge, Commander of the Fifth Circle in the Black Realms. I have killed and been slain times beyond counting in our constant warfare, in my realm, this realm, and beyond._
How did you come to be so high a rank?
_Through my raw power and utter mercilessness. If you don't believe me, you may try my strength at any time, mortal._
How old are you?
_I do not know. All memory of my brief, mortal life faded long ago. Perhaps it is a mercy. It is sad, though, that you could not be properly sacrificed to me._
And why is that?
_I wish to take your memories, feed upon them, live them, enjoy them, feel all of your secrets. It is the closest to wonderful mortal life my kind can have._
_And then, when I am done, I still have your mindless husk to enjoy as a snack._
We aren't at an impasse at all. You see, I can do this. (Walk away.)
As you walk away, Beloch laughs. _But I am still here, in your realm, ready to break free. I am patient! I will not be left here forever!_
Then you are out of earshot, but you can take no solace in it. You know that he is right.
What did you mean, an impasse?
_Moritz'Kri invited me into your realm. True, I have not been able to fully enter._ He distastefully pokes at the magical barrier with a long claw.
_But you can't drive me out either. I will stay here until I find a way into your world._
Didn't Moritz'Kri force you to come here?

_He invited me. True, it was an invitation I would have found very difficult to resist. The truth is that I wanted to come. Once I tricked and destroyed the mad wizard, I would have had a wonderful time._
Why do you want into our world?
_Because your kind is such soft and easy prey. I wish to roam your lands. I can take much and eat much before you find a way to banish me._
Why don't you just go back where you came from?
_I could. I choose not to. I see a rare and wonderful opportunity in your world._
I can drive you back.

Beloch was waiting for those words. _Really?_ He seems to grow before you. No, wait. He is growing. The air grows hot and foul. You struggle to keep from gagging. It is all you can do to keep from fleeing in terror.
_You can challenge me. Try to drive me back. Risk my taking you in and feeding on you. Is that what you want?_ You see that you are facing a truly worthy and extremely dangerous foe.
I will not fight you. In the name of Avadon, I command you to leave our lands.
_Avadon? What is ... Oh! The little wizard was going on about you. He wanted me to attack you, I think. Avadon means nothing to me. I have no fear of it._

You step out of the pylon grotto and into the grand garden of Castle Vebeaux. Since this is a major fortress of the Pact, its portal to Avadon has a prominent placement in a particularly lovely area of the fortress.
The castle itself is many centuries old, placed atop a tall, natural spire of rock. It has seen many battles, especially during the Black Age, but it has never been taken by a foe.

And yet, it has all of the elegance prized by the Kellem. This garden, placed where it can catch as much sunlight as possible, is a lovely place to walk, get fresh air, and plot and scheme ways to meet Duke Gryfyn and gain political advantage.

You enter the famed Grand Hall of Castle Vebeaux. For almost a thousand years, most of the great decrees and negotiations of western Kellemderiel took place in this chamber. Though the tile work wasn't always quite so nice.

To the north, sitting on his throne, you see what could only be Duke Gryfyn. He is a young man, stylishly dressed and extremely handsome. His assistant stands next to him, consulting with him and shouting out the next courtier or envoy who will receive a precious minute of his time.

The rest of the hall is full of said courtiers and envoys, orbiting around Gryfyn like planets around the sun, muttering witty asides to each other and looking for any chance to get a valuable bit of information or scrap of political advantage.
It doesn't take long to make you wish you were back in a nice mine somewhere, hacking at wretches.
There is a second beautiful garden to the west of the Great Hall. The pathway is lined with lovely fountains, and the grass is tended to with great attentiveness.

At the west end of the path is a vantage point, where visitors can look out over the vast Beraza Woods to the west. It is a dark, thick forest, nearly untouched by human settlement. Neither Holklanda nor Kellemderiel will allow foreign settlers in the woods they consider to be theirs.
There is a warrior in Holklandan garb standing there and staring out at the woods. He is the only Holklandan you have seen in the fortress. He may be the warrior you were sent to help.
This is the main kitchen of Castle Vebeaux. Meals are prepared here for everyone of import in the fortress, from the duke on down.

Kellemderiel is very proud of its cuisine. Every land in the Pact is able to make good food, but the Kellem have developed a style of cooking of great delicacy and complexity. No other race in Lynaeus takes the Finer Things so seriously.
There is an enormous undercroft under Castle Vebeaux, running the entire length of the fortress. It is held up by many pillars, both natural and man-made.

The main entrances to the fortress are at the east and west ends of the gallery. These entryways have huge steel gates and multiple guardhouses. And, of course, they can be collapsed in the event of a siege.

Of course, most merchants and other common folk aren't allowed into the main floor of the castle. Caravans making deliveries do so down here. There is a noisy and boisterous bazaar in the center of the undercroft.
This side chamber is full of the reek of animals and fresh meat. You detect wolves and ... something else. It takes a moment to place it. Then you see one. It's a basilisk.
The beasts of Castle Vebeaux are raised and trained here. They are used for the hunts of the nobles, not to defend the castle itself.

The presence of basilisks is quite unusual. You would not have thought that such magical and dangerous creatures could be domesticated. Surely the head trainer will have something interesting to say on the topic.

You step out of Castle Vebeaux into the crisp air of the Beraza Woods. Few travelers dare to travel through this dark and dangerous forest, which is one of the reasons you have been sent here. It must be tamed.
A rough and uneven road stretches to the west. If you travel to the west, you will reach several farmhouses, and then the forest itself. It is time to follow the road and meet up with Monitor Shigaz.

This chamber is full of tools, carts, lamps, and other digging gear. A trapdoor leads down into the depths. This must be where you can access the new excavation under Castle Vebeaux. Monitor Shigaz is waiting for you below.
There are no workers here. And no guards. It is oddly silent. Perhaps Shigaz sent everyone away before he went downstairs.

(You are near the start of a very long and eventful encounter. If there is anything you have been wanting to do, like change scarabs or hunt down absent team members, you might wish to do it before you go downstairs.)

You emerge into a clearing. The stone spire Castle Vebeaux rests upon looms behind you. You can clearly see, over fifty feet above you, the ramparts Monitor Shigaz used to look out over the Beraza Woods.

There are four people there. Three of them wear the garb of Holklandans. The fourth is easily recognizable by the gold circlet he wears. It is Duke Gryfyn. You realize that your bloodied weapons and scratched armor are clearly visible from where you stand.
The Holklandans must be the envoys, come to discuss diplomatic matters. However, when the duke points at you and shouts an alarm, you realize that something is going very wrong.

Moments later, the Holklandans are pointing at you and shouting. You hear horns. One of the Holklandans has to be physically restrained from attacking the duke. And, as the four of them step back from the rampart, you can hear the castle enter a state of alarm.

You wander through the castle storerooms. All of the supplies here are meant to sustain the fortress should it ever be under siege. You realize that most of the provisions are fresh, recently purchased by Duke Gryfyn. He is preparing for war. But with whom?

As you move forward, the quiet of the dark hall is broken by the distant cry of a horn. And then shouting. Your intrusion has been discovered. If you have any hope of reaching the portal back to Avadon alive, you will have to move quickly.
You return to the spectacular Great Hall of Castle Vebeaux. The expanse of polished marble floors is now free of courtiers. When the alarm was raised, they had the good sense to flee immediately.
Disappointingly, Lord Gryfyn is not here to greet or confront you. In fact, although the gate behind his throne is now open, there are no guards to be seen.
Instead, there is a lone mage, waiting to meet you. She stands in front of the throne, flexing her fingers nervously.
Nathalie looks thrilled. Her eyes glow a little with excitement. _A duel with one of my kind, a sorceress of Kellemderiel. Yes. Perfect. Yes._

You enter the private royal chambers of Duke Gryfyn. You wish you were able to relax and enjoy some of the limitless luxury that surrounds you. Sadly, the constant stream of people who want to kill you hampers your enjoyment.
You can hear, in the corridors ahead, quiet muttering and the soft metallic sounds of chainmail. If the duke is still here, he has plenty of guards.
You return to the lovely gardens of Castle Vebeaux. The gateway to the portal back to Avadon is just ahead.
But what you see makes your heart sink. The massive gate to the portal has been closed. A large band of guards stands in front of it. Warriors in plate. Archers. Mages.

Even if you were able to defeat them, you would not be able to open the gate from this side. If you want to reach the pylon, you will have to find another route. You do remember that there was a narrow access tunnel in the back of the pylon grove. But how can you reach it?
You enter a large, natural cavern. It must have been under Castle Vebeaux all along, until the workers dug a shaft that opened up into it.

There are several armed figures at the far end of the cave. They wear heavy cloaks and hoods that obscure their faces. They are watching the western passage and arguing. You hear one of them say, _I'm not going to fight him!_
Then one of the warriors turns and notices you. _The Hand,_ he shouts. _Get him!_ And they charge, weapons drawn. Shigaz is not among them.

You find Duke Gryfyn's private desk. It is empty. You suspect that all of its former contents wound up in the fire.
This trapdoor won't open. It feels like it has been barred from the other side. You find that you are unable to get it open.
Duke Gryfyn must take his hunting very seriously. You have never seen a trained wolf this large and fierce, of course. Most people aren't crazy enough to try to train wolves like this at all.
When you get close, it lets out a long, low, chilling growl. You decide to keep a safe distance.
In all your travels, you have never heard of anyone determined and foolhardy enough to try to train basilisks. And yet, three of the creatures lurk in the back of this cell.

They watch you hungrily with their beady eyes. Their lizard brains wonder, in their simple way, if it is worth the risk to freeze you with a glance and slowly eat you alive. Happily, they decide not to.

This box once contained private correspondence. Someone recently and hurriedly pulled all of the papers out of it. Only scraps remain.
Looking closer, you notice one small rectangle of parchment, caught between the boards at the base of the chest. You take it and read it. It says, simply:
_Gryfyn - I told you. The Holklandans would only take your openness as weakness. No matter. Together, we will do great things. - Dheless._
You take note of this. It might be significant.
You open the box. It is empty.

You lie there, stunned, completely unable to move. And yet, you are horribly conscious. You try to gain control of yourself and rise to your feet, so that you can defend yourself from the onslaught of Duke Gryfyn's warriors.

But, alas, by the time you regain a little control of your limbs, the duke's soldiers have surrounded you. You wait for them to arrest you. Their orders are very different. A few efficient blows from a halberd, and your service to Avadon comes to a speedy end.
You try to speak to these courtiers. When you get close, however, they immediately find that they need to be somewhere else. You fail to engage any of them in conversation.
Castle Vebeaux has quite a few apprentices, each here to learn the difficult and useful crafts practiced here. In return for knowledge, they are worked nearly to death.
They are polite to you, but they make it clear that they don't have time to talk. You let them go.

There are several merchants here, negotiating with great enthusiasm. None of them have the time or interest to talk to you. They point at a merchant at the west end of the bazaar. _Talk to Varell. He will have what you need._
The courtiers of the Great Hall do their best to avoid you. The attention of Avadon can be, after all, quite unsafe. Before they wander off, you catch this snippet of conversation:
_I believe that Duke Gryfyn actually wants to change things. That makes him a dangerous man._
_Did you see what Calorel was wearing? A bold choice. Or maybe his vision is going._
_It becomes more expensive to get a caravan through this castle every year. Prose has grown greedy. He will pay for it._
_They're excavating new tunnels in the Undercroft. I've heard some odd rumors about what has been happening down there._
_Who cares about the Beraza Woods? Really? Monsters, spies, and brigands. That's all there is. Let the wretches have it!_
_Peace with Holklanda? It won't happen. Hanvar's Council forces us to be civil to them, but that is all they deserve._
_Have you heard how little sleep the duke is getting? Perhaps he is close to seeing the impossibility of his goal._

Only the most disciplined of Kellemderiel soldiers are recruited to defend Castle Vebeaux. Disciplined, and quiet. Though they will exchange pleasantries and give directions, you are unable to draw any of them into deeper conversation.

As you dodge the hot pans and pots of boiling liquid, you try to engage some of the workers in the kitchen in conversation. They, in turn, threaten you with a dousing of hot grease if you don't get out of their way and let them cook.
Believing the sincerity of the threat, you depart.

Let the courtiers lurk in the corners and wait for their turn with the duke. You are from Avadon. You will speak to whomever you want to whenever you want to. You ignore their envious gazes as you approach Duke Gryfyn.

As his assistant sighs in irritation and starts to rearrange his schedule with sharp motions of her pen, the Duke of Castle Gryfyn rises to greet you. He has a blazing smile and youthful enthusiasm, and he seems genuinely happy to see you.
_[N], Hand of Avadon! I am honored to welcome you to Kellemderiel, and I am glad that Redbeard sees the rare opportunity that lies before us. My other business can wait. This is too important._
Duke Gryfyn grins at you, eager to speak. _My time is yours, Hand of Avadon. What do you wish to speak of?_
His assistant continues to rearrange his schedule, making little annoyed noises as she writes on her scroll. Duke Gryfyn ignores her with a mischievous smile.
I have come here from Avadon at Redbeard's command. What do you need of me?

Duke Gryfyn rises from his chair and walks to the south, enabling him to look to the west and see the Beraza Woods spread out below the castle. The courtiers suddenly become very quiet, eager to see what will happen.
_You wish to hear my request again? That is worth my time. I want to make sure that I am very clear. Helps to avoid troublesome misunderstandings._

_I am a young Duke, but I ..._ He is silent for a time, choosing his words very carefully. Soon, he steels himself for what he needs to say. _I have decided that I will be a great leader of the Kellem. I will do whatever is needed to keep them strong, for far into the future._
_For that reason, this eternal argument with Holklanda over the Beraza Woods needs to be settled. We cannot continue as we have done, with this grudge tormenting both sides._
You want peace with Holklanda?
_Yes. An honorable peace. That is why I have invited an envoy of Holklanda here. His name is Monitor Shigaz. He is highly esteemed by his people._

_The Beraza Woods are not patrolled by soldiers from either nation, which has enabled them to become a nest of brigands and other pests. I want to work with the Holklandans to pacify the region. That is why I need you._
What good will hunting brigands and monsters do?

_Understand, the enmity between our two peoples is over a century old. Peace will be difficult to obtain. The first step is to start talking again, to work together, to show good faith. It will require years and patience, but I am young._
So what must I do?
_Monitor Shigaz waits for you just outside my hall to the west. I ask that you go with him and several Kellem soldiers to a region of the Beraza Woods and pacify it._
_Speak with Shigaz. Find out what he wishes. Go with him to complete the mission. Report to me when you are successful._
He turns to Shima. _Holklandan, I am not your enemy. I have made it known that any who trouble you must answer to me directly._ Shima nods, greatly relieved.
Why does Avadon need to be involved?

_Because Monitor Shigaz insisted on it. He is willing to hear me out, but he is ... mistrustful of the Kellem. He will only go out with Kellem soldiers if he has Hands of Avadon to ... keep watch, I suppose._
Is Monitor Shigaz interested in peace?

Duke Gryfyn lets out a wicked laugh. _Not at all! Not in the least! I invited him here on the pretense of discussing trade issues. He was furious when he learned that I wanted to talk peace. It took many fast words to even get him to consider my ideas._
_But he is open to the possibility of peace, so the time to act is now._
What threat is in the part of the woods we're going to?
_Oh, I'm not sure. Something magical. Not brigands, I think. Odd monsters. I'm sure Shigaz will describe them._
I think this is a fool's errand, but I will try to help.
Duke Gryfyn shrugs. _Your honesty is ... refreshing. All I ask is that you help, as Redbeard intended you to. Shigaz is waiting for you._
Gryfyn's assistant nudges his arm, but he waves her away. _I can spare a bit more time if you need any other information._
It is a noble goal. I will do what I can.
Duke Gryfyn smiles. _It is strangely refreshing to meet someone who doesn't think that I am mad. All I ask is that you help, as Redbeard intended you to. Shigaz is waiting for you._
He turns to Nathalie and smiles. _Also, young sorceress of the Kellem, I have heard of you. I am very eager to hear if your skills are as sharp as I have been told._ Nathalie almost swoons.
I would like to discuss my mission.

_I am a young Duke._ He speaks with much more confidence than he did the first time he described the mission to you. _I have decided that I will be a great leader of the Kellem. I will do whatever is needed to keep them strong, for far into the future._
_For that reason, this eternal argument with Holklanda over the Beraza Woods needs to be settled._
I have completed my investigation of the pits.

You describe, in detail, what happened in the Beraza Pits. He reacts to the news of the death of his soldiers with great calm. _Their families will be honored to know that they sacrificed their lives for a worthy cause._
_Monitor Shigaz has already returned, and his version of the tale matches yours exactly. And, I am pleased to say, the deaths of the Kellem warriors touched him greatly._
_Please return to Redbeard and thank him on my behalf for your help. This is a very promising beginning to a long task._
So Shigaz will work with you?
_There has been no result so dramatic. Shigaz is surprised and intrigued, but he still hates and fears Kellemderiel. Many long conversations lie ahead before the next step._
I will return to Avadon.
_I wish you a safe journey, and I am sure that my scribe will thank you for not taking up my time._ He winks at her.
Do you need anything else from Avadon at the moment?
_No. This is a slow process. Shigaz, in the Holklandan way, carefully considers every single step, and then he must contact home for instructions._
_Don't fear. If I have need of you, I will send word to Redbeard using the pylon._
Why have you asked for Avadon's help once again?
_Because I have continued to negotiate with Monitor Shigaz. He is starting to see reason in my words, and he is taking a risk to do so. I am going to take a similar risk._
_Deep in the Beraza Woods, there is a band of Kellem bandits. They are well-established, and their presence and their constant raids into our rivals' lands anger the Holklandans greatly._

_I have acknowledged that these bandits exist. I have given Shigaz permission to hunt them down, but he will only do so if you can travel with him once again. It is a real risk for me, but, if you succeed, it will do much to help the Holklandans to trust me._
You acknowledged the bandits exist? You have denied that they exist before?
_No, of course not. I have simply never made a comment one way or the other. I saw no benefit in doing so until now._
How well-established are the bandits?
_Oh, evidence suggests that they have been there for some time, foolishly secure in the knowledge that I would never allow them to be hunted down._
_It pleases me greatly to be able to punish their arrogance._
Why is this a risk for you?
_Because I am allowing a Holklandan to kill Kellem. Scum Kellem, to be sure, but still Kellem. There will be a lot of angry nobles when news of this gets out. Still, it is necessary._
_I have a plan, a plan to keep Kellemderiel great, and this peace effort is a necessary part of it._
Why does Shigaz want me with him?
_You will have to ask him. Perhaps he thinks that you are competent. Perhaps he doesn't trust us. And maybe he just likes you._
Is there anything else I need to know?
Duke Gryfyn thinks about this. _Perhaps. There is one more thing you should know about the Beraza Woods. There is a rogue Hand out there. A disgraced Hand of Avadon. His name is Gavin._
_You are unlikely to find any sign of him, but it might be helpful to be warned about him._
Shigaz and I have defeated the Kellem bandits.

You tell Duke Gryfyn the tale of your adventure. He listens with rapt attention and laughs with delight. _My sending a Holklandan to kill Kellem. Oh, the nobles will have fits! Never mind that they were thugs and killers and deserved every bit of their reward._
_Please return to Redbeard and convey my gratitude. Soon, I think we will be able to make a decisive step._
How is Monitor Shigaz?
_It took some effort, but we managed to convince him to let our sages and healers tend to him. He is now quite well._
What will the next step be?
_I will not say yet. It will only serve to give my rivals a chance to undercut me. I have taken them by surprise on every step of this journey, and I will continue to do so._
I saw no sign of Hand Gavin.
_I am not surprised. The Beraza Woods are a large place, after all. Thank you for looking._
You have called me back here. What is happening?

Duke Gryfyn says, _As you might have been told back in Avadon, my efforts to end our arguments with Holklanda are having some success. Envoys from our rival nation will soon be arriving here at Castle Vebeaux._
_Before negotiations can begin, your friend Monitor Shigaz has been exploring our castle. Security reasons. He is worried about assassins reaching the Holklandan envoys. He asked for your help._
What will you be negotiating?
_Probably nothing of any significance. The importance is that our representatives will be talking. This has not happened in years._
_The Holklandans have their own, strong ideas of honor, and Kellem soldiers sacrificing their lives carries some weight with them._
When will the envoys be here?
_They could arrive at any hour. When they are here, I will greet them here in this hall._
What does Shigaz need?
_Word has spread through Kellemderiel that envoys from Holklanda are coming here. That might draw assassins, sent by nobles who have their own reasons to force our struggle to continue._
_For that reason, Monitor Shigaz is searching our fort for assassins. A bit paranoid, perhaps, but I do want to keep him calm._
Do you believe that there will be any assassins?
_I think that it is possible, but unlikely. I am powerful. The other nobles know that it would be foolish to embarrass me._
Where is Shigaz?

_There are new excavations underneath our fortress. We are digging out a new series of halls. Shigaz suspected that infiltrators might find their way in through the new tunnels. He is down there now._
_The stairs down to those tunnels are just to the south of this hall. I will make sure that you can gain access._
And if I do find assassins?

_You have the power of Avadon. Do whatever you need to do to help the stability of the Pact. Just remember, if someone were to slay a Holklandan envoy in a Kellemderiel fort, it would be ... very unfortunate._
I will go downstairs and see him.
_I am grateful. Much can be achieved now. All we need is to keep the Holklandans calm. If they are angered, years of peace inside the Pact are at risk._
_Do you need anything else before you go?_
Tell me more about your Castle.
_It is one of the oldest, most glorious fortresses in Kellemderiel. Our people have defended themselves on this spire of rock for almost a thousand years._
_It has been laid siege to many times, but it has never fallen._
When was it besieged last?
_A century ago, in the Black Age. Holklandan warriors surrounded us for two years, but we stood._
_We have enormous mounds of supplies in the Undercroft. Even in times of peace, we are always ready to defend ourselves._
Has it been attacked many times?
_I am afraid so. For all of our love of the finer things, the lords of Kellemderiel have never been shy about waging war on each other._
_Of course, Avadon has done much to prevent such strife. They have exercised their power to protect the Kellem from themselves._
How long has your family ruled here?
_For about three centuries. One of my ancestors survived a particularly spirited spate of assassinations. He and his clan took hold here._
_From this post, we saw the rise of the Pact and Avadon, with all that has meant for us. They have completely changed the way of the Kellem, but in a beneficial way._
How has Kellemderiel changed?
_Once, we acted as we wished, sometimes wisely, sometimes not. Now we must answer to Avadon's Council in all things. And yet, we are safer now, so it was a fair trade._
I would like to know more about the Beraza Woods.
_It is a forest. Only that. No more or less valuable than any other forest in Lynaeus. And yet, it is special because both Holkland and Kellemderiel lay claim to it._
_It is a matter of great pride for both lands, and I think either side would rather go to war than submit. I think that this is madness, and I am not ashamed to say it._
How did this come to be?

_In the Black Age, the brutal civil war that tore apart the Pact a century ago. Then Avadon rose and helped to bring peace. Many arguments were settled, but, when we had mostly settled our differences, the fate of the Beraza Woods had not been decided._
_I think they thought that, with time, both sides would calm down and find a peaceful solution to the problem. This has not happened._
What can be done with the woods to make both sides happy?

_I don't know. Probably nothing, not yet. Perhaps they can be divided. Or one side can purchase claim from the other. All I know is that a solution must be found, before this simmering dispute turns into violence._
Why doesn't Kellemderiel just give up the Beraza Woods?
_Because we are a proud people, and many of us would rather die than simply abandon the claim. Quite literally rather die. Or die fighting._
Why are you trying so hard to make peace with Holklanda?
Duke Gryfyn looks around at the courtiers and envoys of other dukes of Kellemderiel. They don't seem like they are listening and yet, you are sure, they don't miss a single word.
_I am trying to make peace with nobody. I only wish conversation. A calming, if you will. I don't want to say more at this point._

_It is not politic to speak, and yet I feel I should. This is a time of great tumult. Of great indecision. The Pact flirts with weakness, and its future is in the balance. I must do what I can to create a strong Kellemderiel._
Great indecision? What are you trying to decide?
_I need to decide what is best for Kellemderiel. That means that, at this point, I am trying to bring greater peace and stability to the Pact, even if it costs our pride._
Why is there such chaos right now?
He thinks about this, shakes his head slightly, and says, _It will happen eventually. Peace never happens forever. There is no reason this time is more uncertain than any other._
And yet you sense there is something else he is not saying.
You think the Pact flirts with weakness?
_The Pact is a great power, but it is aging. It is suffering the weakness of Empire, or complacency brought on by too much strength for too long._
_What is happening to Avadon? Its Hands are being attacked, yes? Even in Avadon itself? This is a symptom._
I agree. We must do our best to defend the Pact.
_Of course. That is what I have been doing. Only remember, the tail does not wag the dog. I serve the Pact so that Kellemderiel is strong. My great love is for my people. There can be no other way._
_So, please, do what you can to help me._
_I have much to do. What else do you need to know?_
It is dangerous for you to speak so openly of the Pact's weakness.
_Really? I am a Duke of the Kellem. What is the Pact, if not me? I am a great part of this mighty union, and I will not be lectured about my duties._
I'd like to know more about Hand Gavin.
Duke Gryfyn nods somberly. _Yes. The rogue Hand. A very ugly business. He was using my castle as a base for his operations. Exploring Beraza. Looking for spies. That sort of thing._
_Then I learned that he was actually disloyal. He was spying on us and sending information to the Tawon Empire. Before he could be caught, however, he fled._
_I am surprised that you are still interested in him. I think your time traveling in the woods is done._
How long ago was this?
_Only a few months. It shames me that we have not yet brought him to justice._
How did you learn of his treachery?
_A lucky chance. It was a misdelivered letter. It was meant for Hand Gavin, but given to my assistant, Jenaya, by mistake. She read it, found that it was from the Tawon, and led to an investigation._
_In Gavin's quarters, we found all of the evidence of his treachery we needed. However, by the time we could inform Redbeard and get permission to seize the traitor, he had fled._
Where is Gavin now?
_He fled west into the wilds of the Beraza Woods. An untamed territory, and one, alas, that he had spent some time exploring. He is probably still out there now._
What should I do if I find him?
_It would be best if he was abducted and brought to the Avadon dungeons. However, in the wilds of Beraza, that might not be possible. Killing him may be your only option._
_Of course, I hope that you do not spend time out in the woods. Your pressing business is here in the Castle._
_Then I bid you good hunting, [N] of Avadon._ His scribe leaps forward, ready to move him along to the next item in his schedule.
Once again, you approach Duke Gryfyn in his Great Hall. He seems even more energetic than before. The young lord practically bounces in his seat with excitement.
_You have come. I am most pleased. My efforts to bring peace between Kellemderiel and Holklanda have had progress. My talks with Monitor Shigaz have gone well._
_Now that you have returned, our efforts to bring a more secure peace to the Pact can continue._

Once again, you approach Duke Gryfyn in his Great Hall. His energy and optimism have faded, and he has been suffering a number of sleepless nights. And yet, when he sees you, the mischievous glint returns to his eyes.
_I welcome you back, [N]. I am sorry for my reduced state. The closer victory gets, the more I worry. I will bring Kellemderiel to a better place, and yet I can't sleep._
_I have called you here for an errand. Perhaps beneath you, but your presence will increase chances of my success, so I have asked for it._

There is a scribe standing at Duke Gryfyn's side. She bears a heavy armload of scrolls, requests for aid, and other business the duke needs to attend to. She is the one who determines how every minute of his time is spent, so, of course, she sees you as a natural enemy.
_Greetings,_ she says, with a shallow curtsy. _I am Scribe Jenaya, the duke's assistant. I thank you for coming, and I hope that you will not take too much of his time._
Scribe Jenaya watches you balefully, the huge pile of undone work balanced in her arms. _Do you need anything else? I need to initiate my lord's next meeting._
What is your job here?
_I am the gateway to Duke Gryfyn's time. I arrange meetings for him. Parcel out his time into increments, minute by minute. Make sure he sees who he needs to see, when he needs to._
Is the duke's schedule busy?

_Busy?_ She laughs. _He is one of the four Dukes of Kellemderiel. His power and responsibilities are truly great. Once, the duke would even meet envoys while dressing and bathing in the morning and sign decrees as his head struck the pillow at night._
_Duke Gryfyn ended those practices. I still mourn the governing time it costs him._
I can't take his time?
_You are a Hand of Avadon. You can gobble up as much of it as you want. I only ask that you don't. There is much rulership that needs to take place._
_Then good day to you. I must ... Oh, it never ends._ She looks down at the scrolls, lets out an exasperated sigh, and walks away.

There is a path winding through the woods, going to the north and to the west. From the north, you hear shouting and howling. Already, the defenders of Castle Vebeaux are sending hunting parties in the woods. It is as if they were already prepared to do so.
The western path leads away from the castle. It seems very tempting.
From this vantage point, Jenell looks out over the Beraza Woods. She says, _They are lovely. One of the wildest, most unspoiled stretches of forest outside the Wyldrylm._
_'Tis a pity we are trying to help Kellemderiel and Holklanda settle it. Raze and pacify it. Still, I suppose that it is my duty._

Sevilin suddenly lets out an angry roar and strikes the wall with his mailed fist. _I am so tired of this. My men and I were betrayed by Avadon. Then we were betrayed by Gryfyn. We risk so much, suffer so much, to serve, and we never get gratitude. Not for a moment!_
Nathalie silently looks down at her twisted arm. She is quiet, but you are sure that she agrees.
Jenell looks away. She is silent, but you suspect that she agrees.
Shima looks away. He is silent, but you suspect that he agrees.
Be patient. Perhaps soon we will have a chance to stand up for ourselves.
_I hope so, [N]. I do. I am angry, and I am ready to act._ He calms down and moves on.
Calm yourself. Remember your duty.
Sevilin starts to say an angry retort. Then he calms himself. _I ... Yes, [N]. I am sorry. Let us go._
