Nathalie is practically skipping as she moves down the hall. _Look at all of this! What beauty! What glory! When I'm in Avadon, this is what I miss most of all. Actual beauty! And I'm here! I'm actually here!_
She looks around at all of the art and finery, barely able to restrain herself.

As you approach the Great Hall, Shima is, even by his standards, somber. _This is ... not a mission I would have chosen. I am an exiled Holklandan. To be here, in a Kellem fortress, to aid a Holklandan ..._
_It is perhaps the worst place I could possibly be._
Why is it dangerous for you to be in this fortress?
_Because, for all the Pact's talk of cooperation, Kellemderiel and Holklanda are enemies. This fortress saw much bloodshed during the Black Age. Many of my people died outside its gates._
_Suffice it to say that I do not intend to go for walks by myself._
You are worried about meeting a Holklandan?
_I am an exile. My family is disgraced. I will count myself lucky if I am not attacked._
_And if I meet a member of the Honored Forge Clan? My family's destroyers? I ... I am not sure what I will do._
Don't worry. I am at your side.
He nods. _Thank you, [N]. That is a comfort._
I count on you to stay strong and remember your duty.
_Of course, [N]. I will do my duty. It is all I have left._
Shima looks out at the gate toward the Beraza Woods. _They ... They are out there. Somehow ... I suspect it._
Who is out there?
_The Honored Forge Clan. The liars. The treacherous worms. My enemy._
It doesn't matter. We have a job to do.
Shima is silent. You aren't even sure if he heard you.
And, if possible, we can deal with them.
Shima nods. He doesn't say anything, but there is a tiny smile on his face.

There is a lone Holklandan standing at these ramparts, staring out over the Beraza Woods. Considering the long-standing grudges between Holklanda and Kellemderiel, you can see why everyone nearby is staying a healthy distance from him.
He wears the insignia of a Monitor in the armies of the Pact. This means that, while he might have hundreds of soldiers under his command, he is out of place here in the halls of high power.

When you approach, he turns and faces you. He looks grim. _Ah ... You are [N], yes? I am Monitor Shigaz. Duke Gryfyn sent word you were here, in his enthusiastic way. I hope you have spoken to him about this fool's errand we are all on._
Monitor Shigaz stares silently out over the Beraza woods, lost in thought. He does not mind his solitude here in the fortress of his rivals. In fact, he seems to relish it.
Duke Gryfyn has not told me why I am here.

_Then, before I speak with you, I would prefer that you hear the Duke's plan from his own mouth. It is a marvelous expression of youthful optimism._ Based on the wrinkles on his face, you would guess that Shigaz is close to forty years old.
_When you have spoken to him, I will be here._
Duke Gryfyn has told me why I am here.
_Then you have heard his plan for a new, glowing peace. It is a marvelous expression of youthful optimism._ Based on the wrinkles on his face, you would guess that Shigaz is close to forty years old.
_And yet, his energy is infectious. As long as a Hand is present to witness the affair, I might give Gryfyn's idea a chance._

Then he looks at Shima. _I ... know you. You are Shima, yes? Of the Threespear clan? I have heard of you. Family disgraced. Fled to Avadon. Since you are under their protection, I will tolerate your presence._ Shima nods.
You don't believe that Duke Gryfyn's plan is wise?
_Wise? Perhaps. I can't judge wisdom. All I know is that wisdom is rarely enough to stir people to act in this world. And yet, my superiors surprised me by allowing me to work with him._
Despite your doubts, you are helping him?

_Duke Gryfyn has a persistence and enthusiasm that can be ... hard to resist. I believe his attempts to help Kellemderiel are genuine. If he believes that this can be achieved by settling affairs with Holklanda, that is all to the good._
Why are the Holklandans letting you work with him?
_It is not my place to judge my betters. However, it does occur to me that, for all of their warlike talk, they may truly and secretly wish for this petty argument between nations to end._
_Anything is possible in time, even wisdom._
What are we going to do?
_We are going to do something that nobody could argue with. We are going to rid the Beraza Woods of one of its infestations of vile creatures._
_There is a region of the Beraza Woods called the Pits. One particular pit seems to be infested with vile creatures. We will be cleaning it out._

He removes a scroll from his pouch and hands it to you. _That is a map. Leave this castle to the west and follow the road through the Beraza Woods. The map will lead you to where I and several Kellem soldiers will meet you._
(The Beraza Woods are now available as a destination on the World Map. You can travel through there to reach the region where Shigaz will meet you.)
What sort of monsters?
_The sorts of creatures made by aberrant magic, if you have seen such a thing._ You tell him that you are intimately familiar with such aberrations.
_It is shameful that the dispute over ownership of the woods enables such horrors to escape destruction. That ends now._
Who will be hunting the beasts?

_You, me, and three stout warriors of the Kellem. That the soldiers of Holklanda and Kellemderiel will be fighting side by side is a remarkable thing. That alone is an accomplishment for the young Duke._
Where should I go from here?
_Descend to the Undercroft, pass through the west gate, and travel west through the Beraza Woods. Follow the main road to the west. You will come to our camp in a day's journey._
You have heard of Shima?

_I am a lowly soldier, but all Holklandans know the wisdom of knowing who among our people wields influence in Avadon. Especially an exile from a disgraced house._ He turns to Shima. _I am not of the Honored Forge that destroyed your family. I am not your enemy._
Shima nods. _I appreciate that. And, if I may ask, will we meet any warriors of the Honored Forge among your retinue?_
Shigaz is emotionless. _I will not be questioned by you about my warriors. You must be content with my good wishes._
How did you come to be here in Castle Vebeaux?
_Duke Gryfyn requested that Holklanda send an envoy, on the pretense of discussing trade. It was not a desirable job, so I was given it._
_And now he has adopted me as a diplomat. It is ... strange._
Why didn't anyone want to accept the task?

_It is dangerous for one of my people to come to Kellemderiel, for many reasons. The job was passed around from soldier to diplomat to courtier and back again, until it landed on my desk. Me, a lowly monitor._
Why did you accept the task?

_Partly because I did not think it would be honorable to refuse. And partly because my career has been ... lackluster. Without distinction. Before I retired, I wanted to do something different, notable, even if it was a tedious trade negotiation._
_Of course, I then found that much more was happening._
How will Holklanda react to your work here?
_I honestly have no idea. They seem receptive, but ... I don't know. I am trapped, a tiny grit of sand between two great powers. I will do what I can._
How are the Holklandans reacting to your work here?
_With ... enthusiasm. I am surprised. I am finding that I am gaining influence and importance, despite a life spent trying hard to avoid such burdens._
What is our new task?
_We are going to hunt bandits. Bandits of the Kellem. They live in the western half of the Beraza Woods and grow fat raiding Holklandan settlements._
_We are going to destroy them. It is surprising and gratifying that Duke Gryfyn is supporting this, if long overdue._
He looks at Shima. _I have made sure that no warriors of the Honored Forge will fight at our side. I would not force you to stand shoulder to shoulder with a sworn enemy._
Why is it surprising that Gryfyn would do this?
_The lords of Kellemderiel won't let Holklandans kill any of their people, even if those people are vile, dirty bandits and thugs. Until now, they would not even admit that those bandits exist._
_Now Duke Gryfyn will actually act to stop them. This is ... just. There is no other word._
Shima, what do you have to say about the Honored Forge?
_Only that their warriors should stay out of my way. They destroyed my family. No true Holklandan could forget such a thing._
Monitor Shigaz shakes his head. _Young one, Holklandans forget such crimes all the time. Never forgive, but often forget, so that we all can survive. I hope you can make peace with your anger._
One look at Shima's face tells you that such peace is quite unlikely.
Where should I go?
_To a meeting point of several disused roads._ He pulls a map from a tube on his belt and shows it to you. _This is the place. Go there and meet me. We will fight together to destroy the bandits._
(The location of the Bandit Roads is now on your map. You will be able to travel there.)
You will fight with me this time?
_I will. Now that my superiors in Holklanda seem to actually support this scheme, I will not appear a coward in their eyes. Also, I long to kill the Kellem who have been raiding my people._
You have been at Castle Vebeaux for some time now.
_Yes. Far longer than I expected. It is difficult. I miss my people, my family, and good, simple food._
_And yet, Duke Gryfyn. He keeps ... talking to me. Infecting me with his enthusiasm._
Why does he pay you so much attention?
_I don't know. He asks me so many questions. About Holklanda. Our ways. Our stubbornness and hopes for peace._
_I try to convince him that his hopes are foolish. I think, sometimes, that he is starting to tire and believe my dark words. And yet, he pushes on. I admire him for that._
Is he convincing you that there is hope for peace?
_A little, I confess it. I am infecting him with pessimism in return. And yet, I think I do him no favors with that._
I will be going, then.
_All right. I hope to meet you soon in the Beraza Woods. If nothing else, we have the chance to rid the Pact of a few pests._

When the master trainer of the Vebeaux kennels sees you, she is eager to talk to you. She is a short, stocky woman who clearly spends a lot of time out in the sun. Her work has left her hands and arms covered with as many scars and claw marks as you would expect.
_Welcome, Hand of Avadon. I am Tender Melisande, and I am honored to welcome you to my kennel. We have been doing much hard work here, and the advances in training techniques we ... Excuse me._

You look to the side and see that one of Melisande's assistants has been paralyzed by a basilisk. She pulls out a whip, runs over, saves his life, and returns to you. _Excuse me. Anyway. I really wanted to talk to you._

Trainer Melisande happily speaks with you, though she never looks away from the work of her assistants. She is ever ready to rush somewhere to deliver reassuring words or the lash of her whip. Whatever is needed.
_It is hard work,_ she pants. _The dukes of Kellemderiel always insist on a kennel of the highest quality._
You are the head trainer here?
She gives you a friendly smile. _I am. It is a great honor, to tend to the kennel of a duke of Kellemderiel. All of our royalty take pleasure in their animals, especially when hunting._
_But only our duke has basilisks in his care. Don't think he never boasts about it._
How long have you worked in this kennel?

_For most of my thirty years. I first worked in the kennel when I was ten, bringing food and cleaning the ... leavings. I had a knack with calming the animals. The old Tender noticed it, and he trained me._
_It is very, very rare for a mere peasant to rise so far._
These animals are used for hunting?
_Mainly. They hunt the wild game of the Beraza Woods, some of which can be very dangerous. The animals are also for show and companionship, and for ... other things._
What other things?
_My charges have been called upon to track down criminals. It is very rare, but it happens. It turns out that my basilisks are excellent trackers, and no brigand has ever escaped their gaze._
What do you train there?

_I train dogs and war wolves. All creatures of spotless pedigree and skill. However, I'm sure you have noticed my basilisks. That is what gets everyone's attention. I am the only trainer in Lynaeus that has tamed these beasts._
Why bother to train basilisks?
_They are amazing creatures! Raw muscle, containing powerful magic. Why, a dog can fetch felled game, but a basilisk's gaze can freeze an elk solid at fifty paces._
_Also, to the Kellem, there is value in doing something nobody has ever done. The more useless and dangerous, the better._
Why are they so hard to train?
_Well, they are lizards. Mindless meat eaters. Also, the power of their gaze makes them absolutely lethal._
_And yet, they respond to my commands. Sadly, I am the only one they obey, but I hope I can change that._
What happens if nobody else can learn to train them?
She grins wickedly. _Then, when I die, Duke Gryfyn will have a lot of deadly, unmanageable pests in his Undercroft._
Why were you so eager to meet me?

_Heh! It was pure self-interest! I hear a lot of things. For example, I have learned that you might be traveling into the woods. Also, you are a Hand of Avadon, so I know that your aid might be for sale._
_If so, I would trade some of my resources for some of your aid._
I am far too busy.
_Ah, well. Not surprising. I thank you for stopping by, and I had best return to work. Don't let the basilisks look at you for too long._ She winks and walks off, whip in hand.
_I need to control the local basilisk population. It has increased much lately, and I'm afraid I am to blame._
_There are a number of basilisks loose in the Beraza Woods near Castle Vebeaux. Kill five of them, and I will pay you a bounty._
Why are you to blame?
_I pay generous bounties to anyone who can bring live basilisks to me. Not all of them can be trained, but a few can. The rest are destroyed._
_Sadly, not all of the hunters can control the basilisks. They end up being paralyzed or devoured, and the basilisks get loose in the woods near the castle. Unfortunate._
Why haven't the soldiers already done this?
_Because the idea of being frozen by a basilisk's gaze and then slowly eaten alive, frozen in place, unable to move, and feeling every moment of it, causes them some concern._
I have killed five basilisks.

_That is good news for us. As a reward, I will give you some items that will aid greatly in basilisk hunting. Now that I think on it, perhaps I should have given them to you before the hunt, not after._
She gives you a wand and two crystals. _Ever pleased to help a Hand of Avadon. And, if you wish another bounty, there are other things I need._
What else can I do for you?

_Well, there were lots of basilisk in the woods near the Castle. I am hoping that they might have laid some eggs. I have found the eggs of those creatures to be oddly difficult to obtain. Very fragile, you see. Don't survive long journeys._
_Return to the woods and see if you can find some of their eggs. You will be rewarded, I assure you._
I found some basilisk eggs. (Give them to her very carefully.)

She takes the eggs, holds them up to the light, sniffs them, and nods her approval. _I think that two or three of these are viable. We will see if the creatures are easier to tame if I tend them from birth._
She has an assistant fetch a helmet for you. It is beautiful Kellem craftsmanship. _I thank you for your assistance. The skill of Avadon is great._
Anything else I can do for you?
_Perhaps ... perhaps. But not yet. Return to me later._
Anything else I can hunt for?

_There is one thing I would like you to watch for, but I do not think you will find it. You recently encountered a drake in our woods. I sent soldiers to search its lair for an egg, but they found nothing. It had already been looted._
_To tame a drake would be a great achievement. If you ever find a drake egg, bring it to me. I will pay you very well. It will also please the duke._
Any idea where I should look?
_I suggest looking under drakes. With all of the traveling you do, you are sure to find one of those creatures eventually._
You really think that you can train a drake?
_Probably not, but it will be very interesting, yes?_
Why will the duke be so pleased?

_I am not sure. The last time he came to the kennels, he seemed very worried. He told me to do all I could to help the keep defend itself. I think that he is expecting trouble, and I will do all I can to aid him._
I found a drake egg. (Give it to her very carefully.)

She reverently takes the leathery object in both hands. For a moment, you think that she is going to weep with happiness. _A drake. To raise a drake. What a marvelous thing ... The duke will be so pleased._
She has an assistant bring you a thick leather belt, studded with pieces of precious titansteel. _This is too bulky for me, but I think it will suit you well. I am very grateful for your aid._
Do you require more help?
_Not yet. First, the drake egg will have to hatch. Then we will see if there is anything I require to raise the creature. Oh, this is an exciting time. I can barely sleep at night!_
There is an aging, obese bureaucrat of the Pact sitting at this table. He shuffles papers around and frequently drinks from the goblet of wine on his desk.

When he turns and sees you, his attitude of arrogant confidence instantly fades. He rises to his feet, sweat beading out on his forehead. _Ahhh ... The Hand. I did not hear you enter. I ... I am Gatemaster Prose._
His clothes are stylish and clearly very expensive. Being the gatemaster for a castle like this one is a lucrative post.

Gatemaster Prose continues to stand at attention and answer your every question. He constantly casts longing glances at his chair. He wishes for nothing more than to recline comfortably in the absence of anyone from Avadon.
What exactly do you do?
_I am the gatemaster here. Every merchant who wishes to travel through Castle Vebeaux requires my permission. Then they must pay the toll, and I collect it._
_Duke Gryfyn places great trust in me. I do my best to justify it._
When do you deny a merchant permission to pass through?
_What? Why, that hardly ever happens, and only when I suspect the merchant of being dishonest or disloyal to the Pact._ You suspect that bribes also work their way in there somewhere.
Merchants must pay to pass through here?
_Of course. The ability to charge a toll for safe passage through our lands is one of the oldest and most valued privileges of the Kellemderiel lords._
Jenell says, _Of course, my people of the Wyldrylm receive no such allowance._ She is irked.
Isn't Castle Vebeaux on a free road?
_Ahhh ..._ he coughs. _Yes. Well, the free road actually ends just before our Castle and resumes on the other side. Special dispensation from Hanvar's Council, you see._
You seem to be doing very well for yourself.
He looks down at his rich clothes and gold jewelry. _I work very hard for my duke. He gives me compensation in return._ His hands tremble slightly.
And the occasional bit of bribery has nothing to do with it?
_I ... I ... I am sorry, Hand of Avadon. I have much work to do. Honest work. I must return to it. If you have any suspicions about me, please take your proof to my superiors. Excuse me._
He plops back down into his chair and makes a big act of shuffling through his papers.
I'm sure you earned every coin.
_I ... I ... Thank you. I am very fortunate. However, I have much work to do. Hard work. Please excuse me._
I have a request for you.
_Really? You do?_ A trickle of sweat runs down his cheek. He shifts nervously from one foot to the other. _Of course. I ... I would aid Avadon however I can._
It is about Calantha. She is a Dharam merchant, camped outside the west gate.

_I ... I am familiar with the name. I ... I decided to not let her pass. She seemed ... suspicious. And unhelpful. And I ... That was my decision. I did not know that it would attract any attention. What ... What do you want from me?_
You were bribed to not let her through.
Prose looks terrified. _Please ... I did not mean to anger Avadon. It was a minor business affair, and there were interests of Kellem merchants to watch out for._
Calantha is to be allowed through. Immediately.

_Of course! I will ... I will adjust the paperwork immediately. Trader Charon will want his ... But that is not important. I hope you will not be angry at me for the confusion. Excuse me. I will make sure your request is completed._
He returns to his chair, chastened, and begins to fill out the appropriate paperwork.
Actually, it's not important to me.
_I ... I thank you. You are most kind. I will ... Will return to work now. With your permission? Good day._
I believe that the merchant Charon might need to be jailed.

Gatemaster Prose is shocked. _Really? But ... But ..._ He sighs. _You are of Avadon. Your word is law. If it must be done ... But I am the wrong person to ask. Commander Peveral, upstairs, is the one who has the power you need._
_Now, please excuse me. I ... I must work._ He plops back down into his chair and makes a big act of shuffling through his papers.

The man sitting at this desk wears the insignia of a Commander in the Pact army. This makes him very important, with a huge force under his control. Not surprising, considering the stature of Castle Vebeaux.

When you enter, he sets aside his pen and rises to greet you. _Welcome, Hand of Avadon. I am Commander Peveral of Castle Vebeaux. I have been informed that Duke Gryfyn requested your presence, and I will do all I can to aid you._

Commander Peveral sits at his desk, which is covered with thick piles of maps, messages, orders, and the other debris that comes from command. He says, _What else do you need? I have been told to cooperate._

_I ..._ He checks the papers on his desk. _You have not spoken with Duke Gryfyn yet, have you? I would not speak with you before our leader does. You will find him in the Great Hall._ He points to the west.
I have spoken with Duke Gryfyn.
_I am glad. I would not speak with you before our leader has. You know, then, why you have come and what the duke is attempting._
_It is a ... a bold effort. I am sworn to help, no matter what the risks._

_I command the soldiers that defend Castle Vebeaux. I make sure they are equipped and trained and that we have enough supplies to withstand a siege. This castle needs to always be able to defend itself with no notice._
_Also, when I have more things that need doing than soldiers to do them, I can hire skilled warriors to aid me._ He gives you a significant look.
You are always expecting a battle?

_Of course. We are not one of the calm, sedate, pretty fortresses sitting snug in the center of Kellemderiel. We are on the border of contested territory. We are also a two day's hike from Holklanda, a country we were at war with a century ago._
_Castle Vebeaux's history is one of sieges and battle, and we have never been taken._
You gather lots of supplies?
_We are always ready for a siege. We always have water and food reserves in the Undercroft sufficient to last us for years. It is expensive, but we are always happy to have them when we need them._
_It has been a challenge recently, though. Duke Gryfyn has ordered me to stock in extra supplies, and quickly._
Why is that?

_I don't know. The duke doesn't explain his decision for me. However, he is acting very boldly to give Kellemderiel and the Pact a secure future. He might suspect that someone intends to lash out at him to keep him from succeeding._
My services are occasionally available for hire.
The commander nods. _I am pleased to hear it. Castle Vebeaux has constant problems with smugglers, trying to slip goods past us without permission or tariffs._
_I have been informed that smugglers are digging a tunnel under the river to the west. I would like for you to find it and close it._
Why do they smuggle goods?

_Because otherwise, to pass the castle, they must pay a few coins for each wagon of goods going through. It is one of the most ancient and valued privileges of the dukes of Kellemderiel, and they get angry and violent when they are denied._
Who was your informer?
_I would rather not say. This person is risking his or her life by telling me what he or she did._
Where should I look?
_Somewhere at the entrance to the Beraza Woods. There are a few farms and other buildings there. That is where the tunnel is. Probably._
What do you think of the duke's peace efforts?
The commander smiles. _Excuse me. I can't help but contain my relief. Many nobles of Kellemderiel are born to the rank and ... not skilled or engaged. It is risky to say much more than that._
_However, Duke Gryfyn is different. He made it clear, from the moment his father died and he ascended, that he wished to use his position to make a better future for our people._
You are Kellem?
_Of course. In theory, I am of the Pact army, and any position in the forces of the Pact can be held by a citizen of any of the five nations._
_In practice, only someone Kellemderiel born will be given a position of such importance in a duke's castle._
Do you think that trying to make peace with Holklanda is wise?
_I would never dare express my own opinion. I do know that some of our nobles are angered by his efforts. And, if they decide to act, it is my job to defend the duke._
How have the peace efforts been going?
_I have heard that Duke Gryfyn has been negotiating day and night, both with the Holklandan envoy and his allied nobles. All have noticed that he has not been sleeping. His temper is short._
But he is still trying?
_Everyone tries to convince him that peace is impossible. I hope that he doesn't listen to them. The end of this conflict would be very good for the Pact._
Do you have many dealings with Avadon?
He seems nervous. _I ... Many Hands come through here. They often come see me for information and assistance._
_I always help them as well as I can, until it turns out that they ... are not what they appear._
_Recently, I had to try to arrest a Hand. It was ... quite disturbing. I want to aid Avadon, not fight it._
What do you mean, not what they appear?
_There was difficulty recently with one of the Hands in Avadon. He was ... not loyal. We tried to arrest him, but he escaped._
_I would rather not discuss it now. I assure you that I am entirely loyal to the Pact._
Tell me more about what happened.

_His name was Hand Gavin. I am not sure about the exact details. Somehow, it was discovered that he was spying for the Tawon Empire. Duke Gryfyn commanded that he be arrested and taken back to Avadon._

_He fled into the Beraza Woods. We have sent Tender Melisande and her basilisks to hunt for him, but we have had no luck bringing the traitor to justice. Beware him when you are in the woods. He is very dangerous._
What was the evidence against him?
_I ... You are asking me to accuse a servant of Avadon. That can be ... dangerous. I don't want to offend you. I'm sure Duke Gryfyn could tell you all you need to know._
I want to talk to you about a merchant named Charon.
Peveral suddenly becomes wary. _I ... I am aware of him. He trades with merchants at the border of the Beraza Woods. He has come to your attention? Why?_
It might be possible that he is a traitor.

Peveral says, in a flat, emotionless voice, _The word of a servant of Avadon is enough to condemn him. As I am sure that you know. I would not question your judgment with a man who has always seemed completely loyal to the Pact._
_What do you wish me to do?_
He is an enemy of the Pact. Arrest him.
Peveral looks down at his desk. His shoulders slump. _Avadon has commanded. I will obey. It will be done. Please excuse me._ He grabs a piece of paper and slowly begins to write out the order.
Actually, never mind. Leave him be.
Peveral nods, relieved. _I am glad to hear it. He has always seemed, at least to my eyes, entirely loyal._
_What else do you wish to know?_
I found the smuggler tunnel and cleared it out.
You tell the tale. Peveral is pleased. _I thank you on behalf of my duke and the royal treasury._
He pays you a generous satchel of coins. _I hope that you find this reward adequate for your troubles._
He looks through the papers on his desk. _Not at this point. Give me some time to find a task equal to your skills. Come and ask me later._
He looks through the papers on his desk. _In fact, there is. I understand that your travels will take you near the western roads, the ones plagued with bandits._

_As if that was not enough trouble, ogres have been sighted by our patrols in that area. They have a lair hidden somewhere near there. We can't tolerate ogres in those woods. They need to be driven out._
Why are ogres such a problem?

_They are large, violent, prone to brigandry, and hate humans. They are supposed to confine themselves to the Titan Peaks and other remote parts of the Farlands. They know that they are forbidden to enter Pact lands, and they defy us at their peril._
Their lair is hidden?
_It is. We have, as yet, been unable to find it. I do have some advice should you try to find them._
Yes?
_They are sloppy creatures. Watch for bones and other leavings. That might mark their presence. Also, they might have found a way to conceal the entrance to their lair._
_Watch cliff walls for concealed doors or switches. Look for buttons, dark areas, or other such discolorations. Such marks might betray the entrance to their lair._
I found the tribe of ogres you told me about. They are gone.
You tell Peveral the tale. He is pleased. Your reward, however, is strangely plain. A copper ring, heavily tarnished.
_Do not be deceived by the plainness of that bit of jewelry. It is too ugly to be openly worn by a servant of this fortress, but it contains powerful magic._

Castle Vebeaux is, of course, outfitted with a large and well-equipped magical workshop and apothecary. This woman is in charge. Like most mages of a certain age, she seems perpetually distracted, but she is willing to give you at least a quarter of her attention.
She brushes her long, uncombed hair out of her eyes and inspects you. _Ahhh ... Avadon, yes? Heard you were coming. I am Incantatrix Questa. I run the workshop. Answer to Duke Gryfyn directly._
_He would want me to help you. I will. Can sell you scrolls. Products of our workshop. Would ask for help from you in return, if possible._

Incantatrix Questa is happy to speak with you, in her clipped, distracted way. However, much of her mind is always off contemplating magic and alchemy. She always thinks about both projects taking place by now and those that will happen in the future.
She looks at you. _What?_
Tell me about your workshop.
_What?_ She seems slightly irritated by the question. _Avadon has a magical workshop, yes? You know what it is. What it does. What we make and watch._
_Hands always ask obvious questions._
What do you make?
_Potions. Wands. Scrolls. Things to help defend Castle Vebeaux from attack. We have stockpiled such weapons for a century._
_And now Duke Gryfyn. Wants more. More, more, more. I am a loyal servant._
Who do you watch?
_Anyone in the Beraza Woods. We always watch for invaders. Any signs of the enemy. Or any enemy._
You deal with many Hands?
_Hands often come to us for help of all sorts. We help all of them. And they often don't turn out to be traitors._
You try to get her to elaborate on that, but she becomes distracted.
Can you trade with me?
_Or course. We have some potions, scrolls, and wands available. For loyal servants of the Pact._

_Also, I can provide blessings. I have long studied. The magical arts. Of both Kellemderiel and Holklanda. The enemy. They are difficult, but I can provide them. Only three thousand coins each. For expenses._
_One blessing will protect you from the blades of your enemies. The other will shield you from their attacks on your mind._
Can I see your potions?
Questa's Potions
Questa's workshop constantly produces potions with varied and powerful effects.
Can I see your scrolls and other enchanted devices?
Questa's Workshop
Questa's workshop constantly produces scrolls and other enchanted items with varied and powerful effects.
Please protect me from melee attacks. (Pay 3000 coins.)
You try to pay, but you lack the money. Questa is irked. _We need you to pay. Supplies are expensive!_

Incantor Questa collects your payment, takes you to an enchanted circle, and engages in several hours of preparation. The blessing itself makes your skin burn horribly, but the casting of it is very quick.
Incantatrix Questa wipes off her hands with a towel and nods approvingly. _Now you are protected from blades._
Please protect me from mental attacks. (Pay 3000 coins.)
Incantatrix Questa wipes off her hands with a towel and nods approvingly. _Now you are protected from attacks on your mind._
That is all that I need.
_Good. Anything else?_
I would like to know more about Duke Gryfyn.
_He is the duke. That means that I have to obey him. So I do. I know he is doing lots of things. I don't concern myself with them._
You want help from me?
_I do. I speak with people. I hear rumors. I have heard that you are going to the Beraza Pits. Magically altered creatures there. Very promising._
_If you find the workshop where they were changed, I want to know about it. Have a sample of what was used to change them, if it exists._
What makes you think such a workshop exists?
_Just a guess. You go and find nothing? Then I have nothing to ask for. However, such creatures don't just appear. They must be made. In a place._
So you want to be given samples of forbidden magic?
_I ..._ For a moment, you have her full attention. _I want nothing that would anger Avadon or break the laws of the Pact. I will only study the magic, not replicate it. To fight, we must understand._
I have a sample of goo from the breeding pit. (Show it to her.)
You open the jar and show her the green goo, still shifting around under its own power. Her eyes light up. _Powerful stuff. Forbidden, but ... intriguing._
_Can I ... Can I have it? I will reward you._
All right. (Give it to her.)
She takes it reverently and seals the jar. _Yes. We will be ... careful. Study this magic. Marvelous._
_In return, I will give you ..._ She gives you one of her old magical rods. It is dinged up a bit, but still powerful.
_Also, when you trade with me, I can bless you. The materials for the spell are expensive, but you will find it to be worth it._
It is too dangerous. You must destroy it.

For a moment, Incantatrix is furious. Then she calms down. _Of course. Destroy knowledge. Will of Avadon. All right._ Without ceremony, she takes the goo and pours it into the forge. A puff of foul smoke, and it is gone.
_Wish this had gone better. Still. Thank you for effort._ No reward is forthcoming.
Does anything else need to be done?
She thinks. _Yes._ There is a long pause. _What? Oh, you meant now? No. Not yet. Return later. I may have more work for enterprising Hands who want powerful magical rewards._

_Yes. I will take your question as an offer of aid. There is a wizard hiding in the western Beraza Woods. Name is Incantor Manon. Fled recently. The duke sends word. He wants the wizard to come back. All crimes pardoned. I will pay you if you deliver the message._
Why do you think that I will encounter this mage?
_Is thought that he fled to region full of bandits. Safe for him, I suppose. Am told you are going there. Might just be rumor, but still thought it wise to ask you for help._
Why did Incantor Manon flee?

_He said impolitic things while drunk. About youth and inexperience of duke. About madness of going for peace with Holklanda. Angering dukes of Kellemderiel is unwise, especially when they feel that they have things to prove._
Why does Duke Gryfyn want him back?

_Do I look like a duke? Or a duchess? Am neither. I only follow orders. Duke promises me that Manon is safe to return. Thinks I can send message with magic. Can only do this if Manon is not hiding location with his own magic._
_But he is, so I ask you._
I convinced Incantor Manon to return.

_He is already here. I thank you._ There is a long, awkward pause. _Oh. You want a reward. Yes. Here._ A beautiful steel breastplate is brought for you. _Nice, yes? Perhaps overpayment, but Gryfyn very much desired more wizards in residence._
The Undercroft of Castle Vebeaux contains an enormous smithy, capable of tending to the needs of both a small army and countless passing merchant caravans.

The head blacksmith is not happy to see you. That isn't an unusual reaction to the presence of a Hand of Avadon. However, seeing you seems to make him genuinely angry. He tosses a massive hammer from one hand to another and glowers at you.
_I am Smith Bevice,_ he grumbles. _Hands of Avadon are always welcome here. You can buy the very best of my equipment.  Always happy to help._
Smith Bevice stands by his huge anvil and glowers at you. Every passing moment seems to make him like you less.
Tell me about your forge.
_It supplies blades and armor to all the soldiers of Castle Vebeaux. And, thanks to you, we're sure to need plenty of blades soon._
Do you have some sort of problem with me?
Bevice realizes that he might be close to crossing a line. _No. No. No problem. What do you need?_
Why do you think that?
_Because our duke is trying to give away the Beraza Woods to the Holklandans. That's right. I said it. I'm not shy about it. That's what he's doing, and you are here to help him._
What do you have against the Holklandans?
_My family still remembers the loved ones we lost in the Black Age. It was a century ago, but know this, Hand. Some of us have long memories._
What do you think that the duke should do?
_Use the blades I make and take those woods back! They are ours! We shouldn't be expected to pretend otherwise._
The apprentices, used to these rants, quietly find other rooms to work in.
You see that there is a Holklandan standing before you?
Smith Bevice says, _Sorry._ He doesn't sound quite sincere. _Sometimes a loyal Kellem needs to speak his mind. Let me make it up to you. We can always trade._
I want to trade with you.
_Of course. I have weapons and armor. Finest Kellem workmanship, and therefore unmatched in all of Lynaeus._
_I don't get to sell to many Hands. It's an honor, no matter what harm you're trying to do here._
And, since I am a Hand, you will be happy to give me a discount.
With effort, Bevice managed to choke back down his enraged response. His face grows flushed, but he remembers who he is dealing with. _Of ... course._
The honor is mine. I'd like to see what you have.
Smith Bevice softens slightly at this diplomatic response. _Then come and look!_
Let me see the weapons you have for sale.
Smith Bevice, true to his word, sells a variety of high-quality weapons. He even does a good job of concealing his anger while he shows them to you.
Let me see the armor you have for sale.
Smith Bevice, true to his word, sells a variety of high-quality armor. He even does a good job of concealing his anger while he shows them to you.
_Then I'll get back to my work. If we are going to need more good blades, it's up to me to make them._ He turns back to his forge.

One area of Castle Vebeaux's eternal bazaar has been claimed by a young trader. He is a Kellem with sharp eyes, rough clothes, and a willingness to drop everything the moment someone from Avadon appears.

_Wait! Wait! Come over here,_ he says, waving you closer. _I am Varell. Tinker, trader; the merchant who can get you anything you need before you go out into the wild. It's dangerous out there. You need to be prepared!_

Varell gives you an obsequious little bow. _I am honored whenever a Hand speaks with me before heading out into danger. I only hope that something I sell can provide the edge you need to keep from succumbing to peril._

_I do. When they come to Kellemderiel, they often pass through this keep. Don't worry. I won't make you ask for a discount. Hands already get one. It is only fair, considering how dangerous the roads have been for them lately._
Dangerous roads? What do you mean?

Varell is stopped short by this. _I ... Haven't you ... I'm sorry. I shouldn't pass on rumors. I've only heard that many Hands have been ... I apologize. I will talk about trading. That is what I do._
Can you tell me what has been happening in the castle?

_Oh ... oh ... It sounds like you are trying to discuss politics with me. I don't do that. I have no opinions. None at all. It is difficult enough obtaining the right to trade in the Castle without making those in power angry._
How did you get the right to trade here?

_You speak with Gatemaster Prose. And, with enough consideration, he might consider granting you a very temporary license._ When he says _consideration,_ you note that he lightly taps his cashbox with his foot.
_It is difficult, at times, but it is the Kellem way._
And you have no comments about what Duke Gryfyn has been doing?
_I know nothing about it. I've tried very hard to know nothing about it._
Let's trade.
_Of course. I am buying and selling at the moment._
What do you have for sale?
Varell the Trader
Varell shows you the supplies piled in heaps in his little area of the bazaar. It's a mixed bunch of stuff, but some of it is, as promised, useful.
_But you will. I'm sure you will. And, when you do, I hope you remember that Varell's prices will not be beaten._ He turns and begins to scan the bazaar for his next customer.

There is an old woman sitting at this desk. Based on the symbol on her robe and on the wall outside her office, she is here from Avadon. Her office is full of clutter, the debris of many years of service.

She stands and briefly shakes your hand. _[N], yes? Redbeard made sure that I knew you were coming to aid Duke Gryfyn. I am Eye Acacia. There is little I can do for you, but I did want to give you a kind word before you left._

Eye Acacia sits at her desk and sips from a mug of strong, herbal tea. _It is good to be visited by others from Avadon. It's a lonely post. Everyone is always so afraid of us. Sometimes with good reason, I'm afraid._
What is your role here?

_I am one of Avadon's watchers. In major castles like this one, Redbeard often places an Eye to watch things. This way, he does not have to rely entirely on rumors, and, if Duke Gryfyn needs Avadon's opinion on something, he can get it instantly._
_It is a position of great responsibility. I have duties both inside and outside the castle._
Are you from Kellemderiel?
_Of course not. Redbeard would never place a Kellem to watch over Kellemderiel. He wants his watchers to be as neutral as possible. I am a Dharamite, though I have not been home in many years._
How long have you been here?

_I have been honored to serve here almost thirty years. I have no regrets. It is a long posting, and there is much work. However, the food is excellent, and Agate, across the hall, gives me a discount on the stylish robes she makes._
What are your duties inside the castle?
_Whenever someone wants to give Avadon information or ask for a boon, they can come to me. Mainly, however, I watch and listen. I am Redbeard's eyes and ears. It is my primary purpose._
What are your duties outside the castle?
_Well, I was to occasionally travel the Beraza Woods. Watch things there, too. But then I ... Well, I aged._
_It is a shame. There are things happening out there we should be attending to, but I lack the resources._
Anything I can help you with?
She smiles. _I hoped you would ask. The Beraza Woods is sparsely settled, but it attracts those who appreciate the lack of authority. Smugglers, spies, and the like._
_I have heard patrols discussing a man named Orian. They often see him wandering out there. He claims to be a woodsman. He seems mad. They find him amusing. I find him suspicious._
_If you see him, follow him around for a bit. I would like to know if he ever shows signs of not being who he seems._
Where should I look for him?
_Along the main east-west road running through the woods. It might take some searching to find him. If you find an abandoned campsite, it might be one of his._
And you think he is a spy?
_Probably not. However, my job is to watch the things I feel need watching. He qualifies. If he is innocent, the gaze of Avadon will pass him by._
I'm sorry to hear that.
_It is difficult, but I'm sure I can find someone to help me. Eventually._
What do you think of Duke Gryfyn?
She smiles and sips some tea. _I wish the Pact had many more like him. He was born to wealth and power, and he is determined to do great things._
_He wants peace with Holklanda. A risky path, to be sure, but I hope that he succeeds._
Do you think there is hope of peace between Kellemderiel and Holklanda?
_Yes, but not in my lifetime. Still, if it happens, it will be because of the energy and courage of people like Duke Gryfyn._
_Such a peace would be a great thing for Avadon. Assassinating everyone in Kellemderiel and Holklanda who tries to foment a war over the Beraza Woods takes up a good deal of our time._
Anything else I should know about the duke?
_Not at this point. He seems energetic, competent, and sincere._
She thinks on this. _Only that the stress of his self-imposed quest to do great things for Kellemderiel is wearing him down. Happily, his efforts seem to be having some success._
Avadon has had many problems lately.
Her face darkens. _I have heard. I know that there was even combat in the halls of the Black Fortress, yes? Deaths. Escaped Prisoners. Shadow Tarkus slipped from the cells of the fortress._
_Many things have gone wrong lately. Suspiciously many things._
Do you know why everything is going wrong?
_No, and it is part of my job to say nothing until I am sure of it. Rest assured, every Eye is investigating._
Do you know anything about Hand Gavin?
_The Hand who was accused of spying for the Tawon Empire? What little I know I am not free to say._
Any advice for me?
_Only to be prepared and watch your back. It is very dangerous on the roads for a Hand these days. Especially in a wild place like the Beraza Woods._
I followed Orian. He was leaving messages for the Tawon Empire.
You tell the tale, including the news of Orian's escape. _A Tawon spy? Another one? The Tawon Empire has been oddly busy of late. Redbeard will learn of this._

She takes a scarab out of her desk, looks at it, shakes her head, and replaces it. Instead, she removes three gemstones and hands them to you. _Thank you for your information. I will make sure that news of Orian's crime is spread._
She also unlocks her storeroom for you. _Help yourself to everything but what is in the box._

_Of course, and you won't find it to be a surprise. If you see Orian, capture him. Or, since that will probably be inconvenient, kill him. In troubled times, we must make it clear that spies will not be tolerated._
The charming old woman sips her tea, seemingly unconcerned by the death she has just ordered. _You will be rewarded._
Orian is dead.
_One less spy for the Farlands, then. I hope someone learns from this example._

She removes a scarab from her desk and hands it to you. _I no longer use these things. I find that they pain me greatly as I age. You will make good use of it, I am sure. Don't worry. I have cleaned it._
She walks into her storeroom for a moment. _I have also unlocked the supply box. Take what you need._
_No. Duke Gryfyn's work is important. I would not distract you from it further._
You approach the runed pylon. It senses the amulet around your neck that marks you as a servant of Avadon. The glowing stone sends out a wave of restoring energy, erasing your fatigue in an instant.
(Return to this pylon to rest. You can also touch it to be instantly returned to Avadon.)
Stay here.
You turn and walk away from the pylon.
You touch the pylon. In an instant, you are surrounded by a cloud of energy that wrenches you back to Avadon ...

The land of Kellemderiel is famed for its love of fine food, fine clothes, and general beauty of their surroundings. Thus, it isn't surprising that the one shop allowed in the upper halls of Castle Vebeaux sells clothes.

The tailor walks up to you, looks at what you are wearing, and allows herself only a tiny lip curl of distaste. _I am Agate,_ she says, _Tailor of Castle Vebeaux, licensed by Duke Gryfyn himself. It is great, great fortune that brought you to me._

Agate the tailor attends to you carefully, discussing fashion and the affairs of the day in a lovely, lilting voice. She does a good job on concealing her view that everything you are wearing should just be hauled off and burned.
Castle Vebeaux has its own tailor?
_Of course. We should have more than one. Every noble and courtier who visits these halls must dress in the most fashionable garb. It tends to be necessary to get one's wishes to be taken seriously._
Fashion is important here?
_Extremely so. We are the Kellem, after all. Whatever we do must be done perfectly. Not like the sloppy ... other people of the Pact. I do not wish to be insulting._
Are stylish clothes expensive?

_Oh, of course. If they were cheap, how could they be stylish? The clothes are expensive, and styles change constantly. Being able to stay current is how one shows that he or she is a person of means and importance._
And what do you think of fashion in Avadon?
She coughs slightly. _The dress there is very ... functional. I'm sure ... that you can tolerate it. But there is always room for improvement, yes?_
You have a special license to trade here?
_Of course. Otherwise, there is no way that the duke would allow a mere shop in these hallowed halls._
How did you receive such a privilege?
_Pure skill. No bribes were employed. My family has simply made the finest garb for the royal family of Castle Vebeaux for over a hundred years._
I would like to trade with you.

_That is a great relief. I hope that you find my work to your liking. Some of the clothes are even made from materials that can hold an enchantment. You need not sacrifice protection for fashion, not in my shop._
Agate the Tailor
Agate's skill with a needle and thread are all that she promised. Her handiwork is truly exceptional, and, in some cases, enchanted.
Can I sell things to you?
Her lower lip curls. She looks at what you are wearing. _I am very ... selective about what I sell in my shop. If you wish to sell items, I suggest that you go to the bazaar in the Undercroft._
_Then I wish you safe travels, and the courage to maintain a proper appearance under even the most challenging of circumstances._

There is a man in glorious and ornate plate armor wandering this garden. Everything about him communicates great wealth and influence. The broadsword hanging from his belt also lets you know that he would be dangerous in a duel.
He looks at you with distaste. _A Hand? What does Avadon wish of Viscount Varoche?_
Viscount Varoche looks no more pleased to see you than he did before. _Avadon has returned. And yet, I still have nothing to say to it._
_But I have nothing to say to you. If you have a problem with this, complain of me to Redbeard. I will stay with my private thoughts._ He turns and walks off.
Are you one of Duke Gryfyn's men?
_I do, in fact, answer to the duke, whatever path he chooses. Wise or unwise. This is the business of the Kellem, not Avadon. I will now take my leave._ He turns and walks off.
There are four people in this room. All Holklandan, from the look of their garb. Three of them are dead. Freshly murdered, probably by the thugs to the east.

The fourth man sits against a pillar of stone, blade lying against his lap. He is grievously wounded, stabbed several times in the stomach and chest. As he pulls himself, agonizingly slowly, to his feet, you can see that it is Monitor Shigaz.
He does not greet you the way you expected. When he recognizes you in the dim light, he spits out, _You! You will pay for this treachery!_ He starts to stagger toward you.
Where did these other Holklandans come from?
Shigaz stops advancing. He looks furious. _As if you do not know! You waited until my warriors could get here to help me, so you could murder us all!_
Lower your blade, Shigaz.
Shigaz lets out a loud, _Hah!_ Then he winces in agony. _We did that once before. Then we were attacked. I drove the assassins off myself, but it was too late for us._
What happened here, Shigaz? I am not your foe.
Shigaz lets out a loud, _Hah!_ Then he winces in agony. _You come to finish the job yourself, and you try to trick me. That ... That must be it. I drove off your assassins. Now you come._
It is not wise to threaten a Hand of Avadon.
_You think so? Hands have been murdered by the dozens in the last few ... You ... This is the only way you can kill your prey? Murder? Like cowards? Sending those assassins to slay me?_
Those assassins? I have already fought them.
Shagiz shakes his head, clearly delirious. _No ... Tricks ... Tricks ... All dead. All dead. I will stop you ..._

You try to respond, but Shigaz won't listen. With his last reserves of strength, he raises his blade over his head and charges at you. He will have to be subdued if there is any hope of saving his life.
Lower your blade, Shigaz, or I will have to subdue you.
_I did ... That ... Did it once. They killed us. At your orders. Your orders! I am weak, but I ... I will stop you!_
I've heard enough threats. (Attack.)
_The traitor shows his true face, eh? I will die in this foul cave, but you will ... will ..._ He starts to pass out, realizes what is happening, rallies, and charges you.
Shigaz falls to the ground. His wounds were mortal, but he still had some strength left. All of that is gone. His blade falls to the floor with a clatter. He looks up at you.
_I don't understand it,_ he rasps through blood-spattered lips. _The peace ... Betrayed me ... Why?_
(Try to heal him.)
He weakly pushes your hand away. _No ... Pain ends. Is good. Just want to know ... Why?_
I really don't know what you are talking about.
_You ... [N], is it true? I ... I fought by you. I ... Why did you come down here?_
Betray you? You attacked me!
_But you ... You don't know? The assassins ... You really didn't know them? Why did you come down here?_
Why did I kill you? Because you attacked a Hand of Avadon. You deserve this. (Kill him.)
_But I ... I don't understand. I ..._ And then you end his suffering.
This is all very strange. Perhaps you can find a clue in the tunnel to the west that will make things clearer.
Duke Gryfyn told me that you wanted my help down here.
_The duke? But ... He told me to bring my warriors down ... Said something was heard. He sent me. Said nothing about ..._
_Don't ... understand._
I was looking for you, and then assassins attacked me.
_Didn't expect ... To see you. Duke told me to come ... down here. Said things were heard. Said Avadon wanted ... Wanted me to secure tunnels._
There is no time to talk. Wait here. I'll look ahead. (Leave.)
You start to secure the area. A minute later, you look back and see that Monitor Shigaz has expired.
The cave seems to be safe. Perhaps you can find a clue in the tunnel to the west that will make things clearer.
The duke sent you down here?
_So ... strange. Peace so close? And he ... sends me? Assassins. Attacks. I ..._
And then he closes his eyes. At the end, clarity evades him. He is gone, and leaving you alone in the cavern.
Why would someone want to kill you?
_Don't know. Someone hunting us. Waiting here. And duke ... duke sent me ... No. I ..._
I will try to save you. You can tell your story back in the castle.
Shigaz smiles slightly. _Struggle over. Fighting over. Think of ... home. Of family. One ... last time. I ... understand ..._

You catch up with Hand Gavin, who is standing by the lake and looking up at Castle Vebeaux. Most people would be terrified to the point of collapse by the prospect of infiltrating a fort like this one. Not a Hand of Avadon. Gavin is as excited and carefree as a small child.
He looks over at you. _So, [N], I see you have arrived. It will be an honor to have you at my side for the assault._
Gavin is still waiting to begin the assault. He is starting to seem somewhat impatient. _[N], are you ready to begin? Time is short, and we might be discovered at any moment._
Where are your warriors?
_Back at camp. They are not Hands. They are mere brigands of the hills. Trusting them during such an escapade as this would be unwise._
How will we get in?
He chuckles. _Avadon has many resources. There is not a single fortress anywhere in the Pact that we don't have a concealed entrance into. Entry will not be difficult._
But what if Duke Gryfyn knows about it?
_He won't. These tunnels are some of Avadon's most closely guarded secrets. Redbeard let me labor out here for a decade before he told me about it._
Where is it?
_You can follow me to it. You will be privy to a great and valuable secret. I hope that you appreciate it._
Where will we be in the fortress?
_In the supply chambers, where Castle Vebeaux keeps supplies in case of a siege. Hardly any guards. We should not have to struggle until we reach the upper floor._
What is our plan?
_Once we slip into the castle, we will be in the supply chambers. We will climb the stairway at the far end. Then we will be just west of the Great Hall._
_When we are up there, we must rush to the final goal. We need to tolerate as few distractions as possible._
Is that stairway the best route up?
_I think so. Even though we will have to work our way around the Great Hall, we should escape the Undercroft before they send too many soldiers down to hunt us._
What about Duke Gryfyn?
_Ignore him. He will be well-guarded. Redbeard will deal with him. We need to concentrate on our real goal._
What is our goal?

_Avadon. We must reach the portal, go through, and tell Redbeard what has been happening here. Duke Gryfyn has decided to act in a public way. That means that whatever Avadon's enemies have been planning has begun._
_We must return to Avadon. I shudder to think how much may depend on it._
Is there nothing else we should try to do?
_It is tempting to try to enter the duke's quarters and learn who he is working with and what his true goal is. However, returning to Avadon is far more important._
Are you ready to begin the attack?
_Painfully, desperately so. I only wish we could see the look on the duke's face after we slip by him and use the portal._
_And you? Are you prepared?_
I'm ready. Let's go.
Hand Gavin nods and claps you on the shoulder. _It is an honor to fight by your side. This will be difficult, and we'll probably die. At least we're sure to take a few of them with us._
_Follow. Stay close._ He turns and walks through the woods.
I'm not ready yet.
You have succeeded in denting Hand Gavin's enthusiasm. _Then do what you need to do, and hurry!_

Gavin reaches an old section of stone wall, set in the base of the cliff. The blocks are massive and very, very old. Gavin kneels and brushes aside a bit of moss, revealing a patch of mortar. There is a small, smooth stone in the center of the patch. Gavin lightly rests a fingertip on it.
_Three presses. The stone slides aside. We slip in. We need to keep from being seen as long as possible._
I'll follow you.
Gavin nods. _Agreed._
You should follow me.
Gavin frowns. _Perhaps I will take the lead. I have spent far more time in the fortress than you._
You are sure Duke Gryfyn doesn't know about this door?
Gavin smiles. _If he did, we would already be surrounded by basilisks._
Go ahead.
Gavin presses the stone twice. It sinks into the mortar each time with a satisfying click. He pauses for a moment. Then he presses the switch a third time.
The sound of stone grinding on stone is surprisingly quiet. A narrow doorway opens before you. Gavin starts to rise. And then you hear it. A soft, high-pitched noise.
It sounds so familiar, but it takes a moment for you to place it. It was in the bandit lair. When Shigaz opened the locked door. And then ...
Get back!
As you shout the warning, your companion, thinking quickly, pulls you back. This is what saves your life.
As you shout the warning, you leap away. This quick reaction is what saves your life.
The arcs of lightning that fly out only graze you. That slight contact flings you twenty feet away. It takes you a full minute to realize that you are still alive.
(Try to get up.)
You stagger to your feet and walk back to Gavin's body. A bolt struck him square in the chest. It left a tiny hole, passing straight through his heart and emerging on the other side.
And now your guide and defender is gone. But the castle is open before you, and the need to return to Avadon is no less pressing.

You step forward and face the master sorceress of Castle Vebeaux. She stands in your path, ready to stop you from passing the throne. She says, _I am Incantatrix Questa. You are [N]. I wish I had met you in calmer times, before your betrayal._

You step forward and face Incantatrix Questa, the master sorceress of Castle Vebeaux. She stands in your path, ready to stop you from passing the throne. She says, _So, [N], we meet now. I liked you better before you betrayed us._
_Duke Gryfyn told me that you are a traitor. Said I must stop you. They are the orders of my duke. I must follow them._
What did the Duke tell you?
_You are a traitor. You and your ally Hands, like Gavin. Come to cause war between Kellemderiel and Holklanda. To sell us all to the Tawon Empire._
_I simply repeat what I was told._
Another guard trying to stop me? You will have no more success. (Attack.)

Questa holds her hands wide, stares at you, and begins to chant. She projects her power, filling the air of the Great Hall. Her eyes begin to glow. _Step forward then. To pass, you must face my power._
And you believe it?
She looks away for a moment. _It does not match ... what I have seen. What you have done. The preparations the duke has made. There is much I don't understand._
If you have doubts, why are you stopping me?
_Because I am sworn. My duke has ordered. I must obey._
I am innocent. It is the duke that is betraying you.
_Then you may sympathize. I am trapped between great powers, between Avadon and my master. But I am sworn. I follow my master._
You don't need to die here. I can spare you.
_No. You are the one who must ask to be spared. My power is great. I apologize in advance if I kill you unjustly._
You defy Avadon. You will now pay the price. (Attack.)
_Perhaps. My power is great. I apologize in advance if I kill you unjustly._

Incantatrix Questa makes a quick, elaborate set of motions with her hands. For a moment, you have to admire the skill and confidence with which she works her enchantments. She makes it seem effortless.
And then, a moment later, you feel yourself ripped away. You are elsewhere, and servants from the nether regions have come to defend her.
You knock Incantor Questa back with a sharp blow. The powerful magical barriers she has wrapped around herself begin to flicker and fade.
_No ..._ she gasps. _We forgot here. Were arrogant. The power ... of Avadon. The training. Avadon always gets the best of all of us._
She looks up at you. _You ... The duke? Is it true? Does he lie to us? Are you a traitor?_
The duke lies. He is the traitor.
She nods slowly. _All these months, all the odd requests, I knew he was slipping away. And then he broke. He did not always hate the Pact. The change came ..._
_It does not matter. I do not wish to die. Not for him. I wish to leave._
I do hate the Pact, actually, but so does the duke.
She shakes her head, beaten. _But, if I abandon the duke, I must fight for the Pact. And you are an enemy to that as well? Then it is hopeless for me._
_This is the end. I did not think it would be ... this way._ She raises her hands, ready to fight to the death.
I am as loyal as you are.
She nods slowly. _I can see that now. I should have trusted my instincts. I knew that the duke was ... slipping. I leave him to you._
_I do not wish to die. Not for him. I wish to leave._
Nathalie can barely restrain her power. _It's a trick. Burn her down!_
Why should I believe that you are loyal? It might be a trick.
_I don't know. All I have to argue for me is a lifetime of service. I am ... tired._
I will spare you.
_I thank you. Avadon and the Pact will not regret your action. I will spread word of what has happened here._
She turns and walks toward the west gate. As she walks, she starts to glow. Then she becomes insubstantial. And then she is gone.
As she vanishes, the wards she placed on the gates she was guarding fade away. As she departs, she gives you one final gift. You hear a gate slowly open.
You still aided him and attacked me. You must pay.
_You reject my offer? You turn away my service? Then your hands will deal an injustice. And yet, when I fall, I will still give you a boon. The one who betrayed my trust must pay._
She looks around. _This is the end. I did not think it would be ... this way._ She raises her hands, ready to fight to the death.
With a final blow, you shatter Questa's magical shield and blast her body backwards. She falls onto the throne, mortally wounded.
As her eyes lose focus, she gasps, _Gryfyn, you took my trust. You ... misused it. You will ... face justice._ She closes her eyes.
As she dies, the wards she placed on the gates she was guarding fade away. She gives you one final gift. You hear a gate slowly open.
This is a private dining hall for Duke Gryfyn and his most valued guests. Several huge warriors are waiting for you. Sadly, the duke is not among them.
Their leader steps forward. He is in his thirties, burly and scarred, and barely able to restrain his enthusiasm for battle. _I am Monitor Rance, head of the Kellemderiel royal guard._
_Duke Gryfyn told me that, if I saw you, we were to kill you. I will take the honor for myself. I will tear you apart with my bare hands._
Duke Gryfyn is a traitor. He is not worthy of your loyalty.
_A traitor? Hah! He does everything he does to bring strength to Kellemderiel. Avadon can call him whatever it wants. To us, to the true people, he is a savior!_
You think that you can defeat me?
_I think that Avadon is fat and lazy, unable to protect its own. Not its Hands. Not Eye Acacia, dead at my hand. In your dying moments, you will see how weak you have become._
This is your last chance to survive. Step aside.
Monitor Rance snarls at you. _Your offer of mercy marks you as a weakling. Watch this, fellows. Watch how a true warrior of the Kellem faces Avadon!_
Your threats against a Hand of Avadon will cost you your life.
_Spoken like a warrior. Enjoy your last moments of hope. Watch this, fellows. Watch how a true warrior of the Kellem faces Avadon!_
Monitor Rance has been slain. The last of Gryfyn's defenders have fallen.

You look around, wondering where to go next. As you look, the gate in the east wall of the banquet hall slowly opens. You hear a weak voice from within. _I see I have no choice but to face you. I am ready._
You enter the sitting room of the royal house of Castle Vebeaux. A roaring fire burns in the fireplace, making the room warm and comfortable. At last, you have found Duke Gryfyn.

He stands at the far end of the hall, facing you. He is unarmed and unarmored. Though he is young, he faces his likely death with great poise. Only a slight, barely perceptible trembling of his hand betrays his terror.
_So you have come,_ he says. _I suppose I should have expected it. I was barely able to destroy all the papers I needed to._ You look into the fire and realize that it is full of ledgers and scrolls.
_You have come for me. I can see the murder in your eyes. And yet, I demand the right to explain myself. I have given all for my people, and I am owed that much._
The right to explain how you became a traitor?
_Traitor? Avadon casts that word around so easily. Do you realize that not everyone who disagrees with you is a traitor?_
_I am no traitor. I never have been. I have always been true to my most sacred oaths._
I have had my fill of talking. (Attack.)
The duke raises his hand. You stop moving. A force holds you back. He is unarmed, but he is not without power. _I will say my piece. You have your accusations against me, and I will defend myself._
You claim that you are not a traitor?
_I am not. Not to the Kellem. Everything I have done, everything, I have done to keep Kellemderiel safe, secure, and powerful in the chaotic, violent times to come._
You really expect me to believe that?
_I only ask you to acknowledge what is completely obvious._
And what of the Pact?
_The Pact only has value to the extent that it protects and aids the nations within it. Hanvar's Council is confused. Avadon is corrupt. Its states hate and fear each other. Its time is ending._
If you were loyal, why did you try to kill Hand Gavin?
_Because he stumbled upon some correspondence between me and the Tawon Empire, and he misunderstood it. The Tawon were sending me offers, and I was declining them._
_Gavin misunderstood the messages. He thought I was trying to leave the Pact. In fact, I was not there yet. Hand or not, he deserved to die for the clumsy and foolish way he used his power._
Why did you have the Holklandans killed?
For the first time, you see Gryfyn truly angry. _After I tried so hard to make peace with them? It was because they were fools._

_By striving for peace with our rivals, I was truly trying to save the Pact. I risked so much for them. And then their envoys arrived, after all I did, and they presented me with a new list of demands. And nothing else._

_Do you understand that? I gambled all to bring us closer to peace. Instead of working with me, they demanded that we humiliate and abase ourselves. It was then that I realized that there would be no peace within the Pact._
So you gave up.
He sighs. _I am young. I have talent. I have energy. But ... there are limits. I can't do all I ask of myself. I look in the mirror, and I hate what I see for its pitiful weakness._
_But my oath remains. I must serve Kellemderiel. If the Pact is corrupt and cannot make peace with itself, I must look for my own allies._
_Fortunately, there is one within the Tawon Empire, one with great influence, who has been contacting me. Who is offering a new alliance._
Exactly who contacted you?
_He does not wish for his name to be known, as Avadon would find it to be very useful. Perhaps, if you can reconsider your path, you may learn it one day._
You notice that, just for a moment, Gryfyn's eyes flick toward the northwest corner of the room. Odd.
What does the Tawon Empire want?

_Power. Security. What we all want. It is time for the alliances of Lynaeus to shift. The Pact will end. Avadon will crumble, made to pay for its arrogance. Wars will happen. New political structures will form._
_When that happens, I want to make sure that Kellemderiel is on top._
You really think that Kellemderiel will leave the Pact?

_You think there will be a Pact for them to belong to? Do you not see how ineffectual and weak Avadon has become? How corrupt? Have you not seen it yourself with your own eyes? Think of what you have seen!_
_The people of Kellemderiel are confused and frightened. They know that the old way is not working for them. The first leader who steps forward and gives them hope will be given control._
Why are you telling me all of this?

_Because I know, deep down, you see that I am right! You have seen the weakness and corruption firsthand. You can join us. Redbeard is due to be overthrown. If he were replaced with one who understands the need for a new order, much bloodshed could be avoided._
_And, if you see the sanity of my words, you must free me. I am still a powerful ally, with great wealth and influence._
The Wayfarer tried to convince me to do that same thing.
The Wayfarer? Ahhhh ... I think I know of whom you speak. I have heard many rumors of that one. He is not one of mine. He serves the Tawon._
What exactly would you have me do?

_Let me go. Use the pylon to return to Avadon. A passage through my quarters will allow you to reach it. Return to Avadon and seize it! Depose Redbeard! You have the strength! Don't allow yourself to be passively dragged along by the doomed!_
I am loyal to the Pact. You must die, traitor. (Attack.)

The duke nods. _Then I have failed to save you. I will mourn you. However, you must know that I am not weak. My servants have given me the finest in magical protection. I will not be easy to assassinate. But feel free to try._
He mutters a word of command. In an instant, all of his jewelry begins to glow. He raises a hand. _Like Gavin, like all of the other Hands, you must die to make way for a better world._
I sympathize, but you can't be trusted. Also, you tried to kill me. You must die. (Attack.)
And what will happen if I release you?

_I will not be a quiet, passive exile, if that is what you are wondering. I will travel Kellemderiel, building allies, spreading wisdom, and raising an army. As long as I live, I will do what I can to sustain my people, no matter what Avadon says._
_So tell me. Do you understand me? Do you see the justice in what I wish? Will you let me go?_
Nathalie looks down at her burned, twisted arm. _Has Avadon done enough for me to convince me to strike down my own duke?_
Sevilin looks at him somberly. _One risking all for his own people. Avadon should use him as an example._
Shima says, _I have lost my home. It has taught me how much my land means to me. But I would never spare a Kellem who has murdered my own kind._
Jenell nods. _I see the justice. I wish the Wyldrylm had some like you._
Gryfyn smiles in response. _They do. They have you._
No, after all you have done, I can't let you live. (Attack.)
You may go. I set you free.

Duke Gryfyn bows to you. _Then I thank you, and I wish you luck in the deadly path that lies ahead of you. War is coming. I hope that I can be a proper ally to you one day. First, of course, you must have the strength and cunning to forge a faction of your own._
As he talks, you can see that he is fading away. The enchantment he is using is a slow, fragile one, and, had you attacked him, he would not have had time to use it.
When he is almost gone, he says, _The way is clear. Were I you, I would return to Avadon very quickly. I wish you good fortune, [N]. If Avadon had more like you, it ..._ And then the duke is gone.
You deal the duke a grievous wound. He falls to his knees and grabs a pendant hanging from around his neck. _I must ... flee. I ..._ As he squeezes the pendant, he slowly begins to fade away.
With one blow, you knock his hand off of the pendant. He collapses to the floor. He is on his side, facing the fireplace.
He chuckles quietly. _I remember ... Played here, and as a ... a boy. How funny. How ..._
And he dies. You close his eyes. The way ahead is clear. You can return to Avadon.
Vinvella
Huntsman Gable
Calantha
Trader Charon
Padget
Beraza Hunter
Kellem Patrol
Kellem Farmer
Wretch Infiltrator
Wretch Taskmaster
Angry Farmer
Vicious Rat
Lightning Rat
Wandering Spirit
Trainer Leala
Welcome.
Watch out for the art.
Scratch. Scratch.
Scrape. Scrape.
Say if you need anything.
Always willing to help Avadon.
For you, low prices.
Help me to help you.
Squish!
Curse you, slugs!
Mind where you step.
Do you need training?
Focus!
Keep your eye on the target.
Be sure to block.
And if you see a basilisk?
I earn my bounties.
Greetings, hunter.
Always be alert.
Strange. The tunnel ends here, but you think you can hear something nearby. It sounds like metal hitting stone, but very faint.
You have reached the eastern edge of the Beraza Woods. To the east, Castle Vebeaux looms above you. To the west, uncontrolled wilderness.

Uncontrolled, but not untraveled. A road cuts through the woods to the west. It is an uneven thing, mainly marked by wagon ruts. Sometimes, it's hard to tell that there is a road there at all. Still, it is the most-traveled route through the forest.

There is a small settlement here. There are farms, a trading post to the north, and what looks like an outpost of hunters to the south. People who make their living off the woods and who aren't scared of the dangerous creatures (and people) that lurk within.

You take your first step into the Beraza Woods. The thick trees almost seem to close in on you. Few hunters and settlers are brave enough to walk deep within this forest. Kellem intruders are often killed by Holklandans, and vice versa.
You can hear lots of wildlife. Birdsong is heavy in the air, and squirrels and other small creatures are common up in the branches.
However, at ground level, the dirt bears the tracks of many larger predators. You were told that hostile creatures thrive in this neglected forest. The evidence of this is everywhere.
The road through the Beraza Woods cuts through several abandoned, rotting buildings. They were built a bit far from safety, and something forced their builders to abandon them.
The woods are growing over the crumbling structures. Soon, they will be gone.
The road through the Beraza Woods continues, in its winding, inconsistent way, to the west. If you keep going in this direction, you will soon reach the area where you were to meet Monitor Shigaz.
(The Beraza Pits are now marked on your World Map.)

You find an abandoned, crumbling house out here deep in the woods. It's been out here for years, untended. But not empty. Something has kept the plants from surging forward and reclaiming this clearing.
As you look around, you feel a strange chill in the air. You feel distinctly unwelcome here.
At first, you think that you have found a particularly narrow and hastily dug root cellar. Then, as your eyes adjust to the dim light, you can see that it is actually a tunnel.
The ceiling is held up with crude timbers. It's not the safest excavation you've ever seen. The tunnel stretches off to the east.

Ever since you entered this remote farmhouse, you have felt a sense of cold and foreboding. The sensation suddenly becomes much more acute. Your breath starts to mist up. You feel a dark presence in the room with you.
And then the feeling fades. You are alone on the pathway, for a moment. Then you hear the telltale rattling of bones in front of and behind you ...
These dank corridors are full of rotten barrels and crates. This old house was once occupied by brigands. They were probably digging out several layers of cellars to hide their stolen goods.
It's doubtful that there is a tunnel under Castle Vebeaux anywhere down here. You are too far from the castle to make the idea practical.
As you look around, you realize that you have seen no signs of any people being here recently. You wonder what happened to the smugglers.

You turn the corner and find that this is where the digging of this tunnel came to an end. A frozen body lies on the floor ahead of you. The smugglers had the singular bad luck to break into an old crypt, and the dark magic here was still active.
Thanks to thousands of years of active magic use by the people of Lynaeus, it's amazing that anyone anywhere has the courage to dig holes at all.
As you reach the end of this tunnel, several people step out of hiding. They all have picks and shovels, which they were using to industriously burrow out a tunnel under the river to the east.
When they see you, they shout an alarm. In moments, they have dropped their tools and drawn their weapons.
Smuggler Elspeth
Kellem Smuggler
The sign says:
HALL OF THE BERAZA HUNTERS
Beraza Trading Post
Underneath, someone has recently added,
Calantha - Proprietor
BERAZA WOODS ROADS
Do not proceed without armed guards!
There are several merchants and hunters browsing this trading post. They make a concerted effort to avoid you. Some of them look a bit ... shifty.
