There is a patrol of Kellem soldiers watching the eastern end of the road through the Beraza Woods. They warn you to, if you go west, watch out for brigands. And spiders. And basilisks.

There are several Kellem farmers tending to these fields. You speak with them for a short time. You learn several interesting facts about cabbage and the raising of cabbage. Also, you find out that the Beraza Woods are terrifying.
This hall belongs to the hunters of the Beraza Woods, warriors tasked by Castle Vebeaux to keep the brigands and monsters in the woods away from the castle gates.
They are a cheery, boisterous bunch, and warriors of Avadon don't scare them. You don't escape their hall without a long, leisurely lunch and an hour of trading stories of hunting and adventure.
You meet a Kellem hunter, preparing to go out on a patrol through the woods. The warrior is too nervous and distracted to talk.
This looks like an old, snug Kellemderiel farmhouse. Several people are inside, cooking the midday meal and tending to their tools and weapons.
They are a dirty, muscular lot. They wear thick leather jerkins, backed with chainmail, and they keep weapons close at hand, probably to defend themselves from the creatures of the woods.
They are also angered by your intrusion and unintimidated by your being from Avadon. They tell you clearly and curtly that you aren't welcome here and that you should leave.

Vinvella looks suspiciously at the thicket to the east. She motions for you to stop and sniffs the air. It doesn't looks any different from any other bunch of shrubbery, but the huntress takes a long, rusty, brush-clearing blade from her belt and hacks it away.
On the other side, you see a small clearing. There are refuse and bones, but no spiders. Vinvella nods silently and moves on.
Vinvella stops at a another thicket, raises her blade, and hacks away at some shrubbery. Once again, she reveals a small clearing.
This time, however, the opening in the trees is full of huge spiders. With one smooth motion, Vinvella sheathes her blade, grabs her bow, and nocks an arrow to the string.
Vinvella stops. She whispers, _You smell that? The rot? The terror? Those creatures have been feeding. Maybe we ..._

Then, with no delay, she hacks away the thick clump of bushes in front of her. On the other side, you see what Vinvella was smelling. Her instincts were miserably accurate. These spiders have recently dined on a wretch.
Vinvella looks at the ground. She is clearly getting frustrated. _Pests. Only pests. No sign of the ... the ... All right. Here. Be ready._

She whips out her blade and slashes through a huge clump of ivy, stretched between two trees. The vines fall away, revealing a large clearing. It is full of spiders. One of them is much larger than the others, and its eyes glow with an unnerving green light.
_Hah!_ Vinvella shouts, delighted. _This is what we were hunting for!_

Vinvella retrieves her blade and puts her bow back onto her shoulder. _Thank you for your help. You can take whatever you find here. I don't use the tools of the dead, but I know that some are far less picky._

She also takes a scrap of leather from her pocket and hands it to you. You inspect the gruesome bit of cured flesh and find that it is a leather armband, inscribed with several lines of tiny runes. _I hope that is fair payment._
_I will return to my camp now. It's time for a few days of rest, I think._ She waves farewell and leaves to the east.

You reach the lowest chamber in these winding tunnels. Here, you find the dark presence the smugglers uncovered. It is the ghost of a sorceress, barely visible. It stands on a rune, etched many years ago, left here for the shade to use should its eternal vigil be disturbed.
The shade points at you and lets out a long, ghastly moan. The air fills with raw magical power. Your hair stands on end. The creature prepares to repel the intruders.
The ghostly spirit moves its hands in a complicated pattern. A web of light appears between them. Then it extends and engulfs the creature's target. Who instantly vanishes.
A moment later, the victim reappears elsewhere. Alone and surrounded.
With a final hideous wail, the shade of the sorceress splits apart and fades away. The dark presence looming over this abandoned house is gone. It is free to rot away and be overgrown in peace.
There is a young warrior of Kellemderiel sitting by this fire. A bow of polished yew is close to hand. She sips from a mug of strong tea and watches the path to the west intently.
When you approach, she motions for you to sit. You join her in silently sipping tea and watching the path.
Finally, she says, _I am Vinvella. You are a hunter. I can tell. No stranger to the woods. Good to have company. I have a lonely hunt ahead._

Vinvella sits by the fire and watches the path. She occasionally leaps up, grabs her bows, and aims an arrow toward the shadowy undergrowth. Then, when she determines that no foe is present, she sits down again.
Can you tell me about these woods?
_The Beraza Woods? Contested land. Not ours. Not the Holklandans. Argued over for year after year._
She looks at Shima. _Not interested in starting an argument. Just stating facts._ He nods.
_Now they're full of pests. Can't hunt them down. That's why commander of the castle put me here._
Why don't you hunt the pests down?
_Because if Kellem soldiers go into the woods, the Holklandans get angry. Make noise in Hanvar's Council. Send assassins to kill them. They send soldiers in, we do the same._
_This makes it a big, lawless zone. Gotten bad out there._
I am hunting in the Beraza Woods.
_I heard rumors. You are Avadon, yes? Not sorry to hear you're here._
_My job. Watch for pests dumb enough to get too close to the castle. Shoot them down. Earn a bounty. Easy work, until the spiders came._
_There are basilisks out there too, but they're smart enough to not come too close._
What do you think should happen to these woods?
_If I had my way? Split them right down the middle. Of course, if I said that in a pub, I'd be in a fight in a second._
Nathalie nods. _And rightfully so. This is Kellem land. No nation of the pact should be expected to give up an inch of its birthright._
Vinvella shrugs.
Nice bow.
She nods. _Thank you. My great, great, great, grandmother made it._
_Spiders. Dumb, big, nasty. Mindless enough to come close to the castle. I'll get a healthy bounty if I can hunt them down and destroy their nests. Too many of them to do it by myself, though._
_Of course, if someone were to help me, I have a valuable reward to give them. Found it in the woods. Not something I can use, but you might be able to._
What sort of reward?
_A bracelet. Looks crude, but it's enchanted._
I can't help you.
_Too bad. Sorry to hear it. Need to get back to my vigil._ She doesn't say anything else. She just watches the woods silently. Eventually, you rise and depart.
Vinvella nods. _Then prepare yourself. Soon, we will hunt._
What are you going to hunt now?
_Don't know. Taking a rest before I go back to the castle. Then I get the bounty. Rest. Drink. Come back out when they have prey for me._
I am ready to begin the hunt.
Vinvella rises, picks up her bow, and checks her quiver. _Follow. Stay close. Be ready. I know the signs the creatures leave. Can drive them out. Don't abandon me. Don't want to die today._
Then she walks off into the woods.
Good day to you. (Get up and leave.)
Vinvella nods silently to you as you rise to depart.

This is a lovely office, decorated in the luxurious Kellem style. The man sitting at the table is a gnarled old hunter, wearing armor of skins and carving a bit of antler on the antique desk. He seems a bit out of place.
When you enter, he looks up at you and squints. _Hrmmm. You're a hunter, eh? Come by to pay your respects? I'm Huntsman Gable. What are you doing here?_
And then he notices Shima. _What? What is a stinking Holklandan doing here? You'll be moving on, if you want to stay safe._

Huntsman Gable sits at his desk, concentrating on carving his bit of antler. It looks like he is making an elaborate gamepiece. This must be how he keeps busy between his many journeys out into the woods.
I have been summoned to do some hunting in the Beraza Woods.
_Really? Well, anyone who came here to brave the forest is all right by me. There is even a bounty available, if you have a mind to work for it._
You have a problem with my companion?

Gable looks at Shima with loathing. _Holklandans want to steal our forest from us. They kill us when we try to hunt for what is ours. They are the enemy._ Shima stares back at him silently, unsurprised by this outburst.
_If you want anything from me, you will get him out of here._
All right. I'll be back later.
You turn away. Shima comes with, though he seems slightly disappointed.
We are Hands of Avadon, and you will find your manners.
This brings Gable up short. _You ... Avadon?_ He looks at Shima again. His loathing is no less, but he nods. _I know better than to anger your kind._
_You want to brave the woods? You're welcome to it. There is even a bounty available, if you have a mind to work for it._
Tell me about this hall.
He looks at his desk with a wry smile. _Built by the castle. About fifty years ago, I think. Gives the hunters a place to stay. And anything made by the Castle is going to have their ... style._
Their style?
He looks at the dusty and smudged painting on the wall. _They only know one way in the castle. Frilly. Fancy. Not all of the Kellem care for that. Some of us live out in the world._
This is a nice office.
_Yes. An office. That is what they made for us, them up in the Castle. Sometimes I wonder if they even know where their venison comes from._
What are you carving?
He holds up the bit of antler and inspects it. _It will be part of a game soon. Just my own little bit of art. Something to decorate this hall. Something that fits._
Can I be trained here?
_Perhaps. Trainer Leala is in the practice hall. She might be able to help you._
You hunt in the forest?
He nods solemnly. _That is what we do, me and my merry band. Castle keeps us here to keep the road clear. Keep the pests back. Hunt them down if they get too close._
And you still hunt?
_I know I have some grey in my hair, but the day I can't put an arrow in a spider's eye at fifty paces is the day you can just bury me._
Where does the road go?
_Straight through to Holklanda. Merchants travel up and down it. And envoys from the enemy._
He gives Shima a nasty look. _And spies._ Shima is typically impassive.
_It has its uses, we keep it clear._
What sorts of pests are out there?
_Lately, lots of giant spiders. And rats. And the usual brigands._
_Worse, there are also basilisks. They make me angry!_
Angry? Why?
_Because they're deadly, and because they were brought here. The animal trainer in the Castle? She pays for people to bring basilisks to her. But the things get loose, right on our doorstep._
_I swear to you, there is something in that castle. Something that drives everyone in there mad._
You mentioned something about a bounty?
He nods. _So I did. We are charged to keep threats a safe distance from the castle. We do well, for all that. But there is one nest of pests that is too dug in, and we can't be rid of them._
_It's a ruined house, not far from here. Full of rats, and I don't know what else. Clear it out and a healthy bounty is yours._
Where is this house?
He points to the southwest. _South of the main road. Down some winding paths. Look for bones. They'll lead you there._
So how did this house get infested?
_Some fool farmers built it. A big clan of them. Found that life in the woods didn't suit them. They left, leaving a nice big lair behind them for whoever chose to move in. The fools._
And then rats moved in?
_At first. Then more of them. I took some hunters out there to get them, but, when we got close ... There's something in there. Something unnatural. You can feel it the moment you get close._
_So that's why I'm hiring mercenaries for the job. It's not the sort of thing we're trained to hunt._
Are there any other bounties available?
He thinks. _Not yet. Nothing we can't handle. Maybe ask me later._
There are undead under that old house.
_Ah. Doesn't surprise me. You can sense them, yes? Well, if you want the bounty, you'll rid us of them. Sort of thing your kind does, right?_
That old farm has been cleared out.
You tell Huntsman Gable the tale. _Interesting. Glad I sent you. Not the sort of prey I would send my warriors to fight. The walking dead? That's wizard business._

He takes a suit of chainmail from a stand and hands it to you, along with a pouch of coins. _For your help. Now we'll get out there and burn that place down and collapse the tunnels. Only way to keep it safe._
Sevelin looks toward the shadowy forest and shudders. _Another dark forest. Natural ambush territory. Full of killers like those that butchered my friends. Killers who are still loose._
_If other nations followed the Stone Code, these lands would no longer be contested._
Shima doesn't say anything about this, but he doesn't seem convinced.
Nathalie lets out a snort. She doesn't seem convinced.
I'm sure the brigands who attacked you will be caught one day.
_Oh, they will. I will make sure of it._
What would the Stone Code say?
_That any solution to the problem is better than a festering wound. Most likely, the lands would be split down the middle. Both sides would be furious, but it would allow the wound to heal._
He smiles. _After what I have seen? If I were any more alert, my eyes would pop out of my head and roam on their own._
Shima looks at the humble collection of buildings at the edge of the forest. _It is a relief to leave Kellemderiel and enter Holklandan land. I was getting tired of the angry stares._
You say that this is Holklandan land?
_Of course. We took this land during the Black Age. It was a time of war, and seizing the territory was our right. It was a blood debt we were owed for all of our people slaughtered by the Kellem._
Nathalie bites her lip. On the brink of such a dangerous journey, she wisely decides not to start an argument.
What do you think should happen to the woods?

He walks in silence for a while, thinking about it. _I am not going to say. I have been exposed to politics too much. I lost my family and my homeland to politics. I came to Avadon to avoid ever thinking about such things again._ He walks on in silence.
This isn't the right time to discuss it.
_Of course. And, now that I think about it, I don't want to talk about it either._ He walks on in silence.

Jenell stops at the edge of the forest. She sniffs the air. _It is sad. It is a beautiful place, but dangerous. Warped. The absence of human control has let dark things into here. Nature has been corrupted._
Absence of humans corrupts nature?

_Our world has dark, powerful forces, always eager to corrupt nature. These assaults often don't come from humans. Nature can be delicate and defenseless, and it requires the presence of a strong hand to keep it from being corrupted._
_Come on._ She strides confidently toward the Beraza Woods. _Let us be the strong hand._
That seems to happen a lot.
_Nature can be a delicate thing, defenseless from the powerful, dark forces that roam the world. The task of the shaman is not to warp nature, but to get others to leave it alone.
_I am glad to be here. I am ready to do my work._ She strides confidently toward the Beraza Woods.
Nathalie looks deeper into the woods. She takes a deep breath and smiles. _Yes. This is a good place. Beautiful, in places. Raw. Even a tinge of natural magic in the air._
_The Kellem have long been willing to shed blood to save this land, and it is right that they do so._ She looks back toward the ruined homes to the east. _Pity it's such a dump._
What is Kellemderiel's claim to this land?
_These woods have been here for centuries. The Holklandans took them from us in the Black Age. When the peace to that civil war was negotiated, our wise ancestors left ownership of it unclear._
_The Holklandans claim that they deserve the land, in payment for all of their people we killed. Hah! As if they did not kill many thousands of my people?_
During all of this, Shima remains painfully, diplomatically quiet.
What do you think of Duke Gryfyn's efforts?
_Admirable, but doomed. We Kellem, for all of our arts and such, never shrink from a fight. For me, the problem is not having enough to fight._
She looks into the forest. _I only hope that there is prey here worthy of me._
Let's go and admire more of these woods.
Nathalie looks over at you and smiles. In the leaf-tinted sunlight, she looks very young. She pats you on the arm. _It would be a pleasure._
Tombs of the Woods Runners
In memory of those who gave all
to keep the woods under control.
Though the woods are full of monsters and bandits, you see a lone figure walking down the road toward you. He is a wrapped in a heavy, black cloak, and he seems entirely unconcerned by the danger.

Then he reaches you and gives a little bow. His face is masked, but you recognize his build and voice. _Well met, [N]. I am surprised to see you here. What a merry coincidence._ It is the Wayfarer, once again.
I am not surprised to see you.

He raises his hand to his chest in mock outrage. _Really? It is not as if I have nothing better to do than to hunt you down. I have business all over Lynaeus. It is only natural that we will frequently meet._
_Would you believe that I am enjoying a relaxing stroll through a lovely forest in autumn? No, you probably would not._
_My affairs drag me all over Lynaeus. Some of my business has brought me here._
Yes. A coincidence. Of course.

He nods. Then he takes a step back in mock surprise. _Wait, are you employing sarcasm on me? Because, perhaps, you think that I am stalking you? Do not have such a high opinion of your own importance._
_No, my affairs drag me all over Lynaeus. Some of my business has brought me here._
What exactly is it you do that takes you so many places?
_I am a ... broker? Is that a good word to use? I find people who need things done. I find people to do them._
_Thus, of course, I am naturally drawn to Hands of Avadon. They have the power and will to do whatever they want. Just, or not. It makes them useful people to know._
Well, do your business with someone else. (Push past him.)
The Wayfarer doesn't step aside. Instead, he blocks your path. _I only ask a moment more of your time. Only for you to hear a few of my words. You will find them to be useful, I promise you._
Step aside, or you will learn the punishment for hindering a Hand of Avadon.
He looks you in the eye. For a moment, his affable exterior drops. His gaze is cold and hostile. Then, slowly, theatrically, he steps aside and waves you past.
_I wish you a safe journey. Have a care, though. The woods are full of ... pitfalls._ Then he turns and continues down the road to the east.
All right. Speak quickly.
_I will be brief. I am at Castle Vebeaux for many reasons. One of them is that there is a merchant who is being treated unjustly. She wishes for someone of influence to speak on her behalf._
And what business brings you here?

_I am gratified by your interest. I am at Castle Vebeaux for many reasons. One of them is that there is a merchant who is being treated unjustly. She wishes for someone of influence to speak on her behalf._

_Her name is Calantha. She wishes only a pass to travel through Castle Vebeaux. She has been unable to marshal sufficient bribes, so she is trapped outside the gates, not far to the east from where we stand._
_She wishes for someone to enter the castle and convince the gatemaster to let her by. Perfect work for a Hand of Avadon._
Why is this perfect work for a Hand?
_Surely, you are joking? Cutting through such bureaucratic tangles is one of the great abilities of your kind. It is also how Hands enrich themselves. Quite efficiently, I assure you._
_Don't feel guilty about it. Sometimes it seems like it is only the ability of the Hands to override foolish laws at will that enables the Pact to function at all._
And I will be rewarded?
_You will be paid, I am assured, generously. And for only a few minutes of risk-free effort! When you have Calantha's pass, collect the reward from her directly._
What exactly do I need to do?
_Simply enter the castle. Find the Gatemaster, fat, bloated, craven tick of a man that he is. Use your influence. It will be easy. And, I think, fun._
Why are you involved in this, anyway?
He smiles. _I only want to help people._
I'll consider it.
_I hope that you do. Work like this is your reward for being a Hand. Take your reward._
He nods to you, steps around you, and walks down the road toward the castle.
It will be done.
_I am pleased to hear it. You are wise. Work like this is your reward for being a Hand. Take your reward._

A merchant has set up a shop, of sorts, on the side of the road. She has laid out straw mats and placed her goods on them in as attractive a manner as possible. Then she sat out in the cold and the wind and the rain, hoping for customers.

When she sees you, she waves for you to approach, though her time outside has sapped most of her enthusiasm. _Welcome, welcome. This is my humble ... shop. I am Calantha, proud merchant of Kellemderiel._
Calantha is still sitting out in the cold. She shivers and looks down at her wares bitterly. _I am still open for business, as you can see. Please let me know if anything I have seems worth having._
This merchant has only just moved into this shop. She is busily arranging her wares, sweeping up the floor, and making everything be to her liking.
When she sees you, she bows. _Ah, the Hand. I understand I owe you much. I am Calantha._
Calantha bustles around her new shop. She has only recently taken ownership of it, and she is positioning everything to her liking. _Welcome, Hand. You are always welcome here. I owe it all to you._
She looks at her wares miserably. Then she looks at her shoes. Once stylish, now caked with mud.
_I need permission to pass through Castle Vebeaux. From Gatemaster Prose, that toad. I can't get it._
Tell me more about the Gatemaster.
She suddenly looks nervous. _I have plenty to say on that subject, but I don't want to make things worse by ... I will be diplomatic. Please do not ask more of it._
I have been asked to speak with the gatemaster on your behalf.

She sits up in her chair, suddenly engaged. _You have? Who met you and ... Never mind. I don't want to know. Yes. You ... You are a Hand, correct? That was what I was hoping for, for what I'm willing to pay._

_Yes, Gatemaster Prose won't give me passage through the castle, that toad. I am trapped here, when I should be selling my wares all through Kellemderiel. I have orders! I have demand! And I can do nothing about it, because I am trapped here!_
I would like to know more about the man who gave me the mission on your behalf.
You describe the Wayfarer to her. She shakes her head. _No, that sounds nothing like the woman I spoke with when I let word out about my wishes. Word of such tasks gets passed from broker to broker._
_I know nothing about the man you spoke to._
How much has the Gatemaster asked you for?
She snorts. _He started at ten thousand coins. Then he raises the amount by a thousand every time I come to him. He so loves to toy with me._
Why does he hinder you?

_I have my suspicions. I suspect that Trader Charon is trying to force me to trade in a different region, or to put me out of business altogether. He wants to be the only merchant trading in this settlement._
Tell me about Charon.

She spits in the direction of the wooden hall to the northeast. _He is in there. Warm. Dry. Gloating over my misfortune. Sometimes, he comes out to taunt me, pretending to be supportive. I loathe him._
I spoke with the gatemaster on your behalf.

She smiles wickedly. _Yes, I know. He sent me word that I can pass through Vebeaux without restriction. Sent the message the moment you left his office, I suspect. I've beaten Trader Charon, but I'm not done with him yet._
_And yes, I know I must pay you, and generously._ She gives you a large pouch of coins. _I am grateful for your aid._
She thinks about this. _I am not sure. Now that I have reliable contacts, I may ... I need to think about the opportunities open to me. I am not ready to act yet._
I have been asked to betray Charon to the authorities.
She nods happily. _Well, fancy that. I always suspected that the cretin was involved in ... unsavory activities. And you will make him pay for it, yes?_
_And, when it's done, I will have a ... A reward for your noble service._
What has Charon done to deserve this?
_Oh, I'm sure he's done something. Everyone has broken some law or other. Avadon can punish anyone at any time, yes? So we all must always be guilty._
I am not sure whether I should do this.

She looks confused. _A Hand of Avadon, refusing to punish someone? That is unusual. Even refreshing. Don't worry yourself about it, though. They're all corrupt, the lot of them. No real harm will be done, and you will be rewarded well._
I will do what has been asked.
She nods. _I am glad. They're all corrupt, the lot of them. No real harm will be done, and you will be rewarded well._
Charon has been arrested.
_Oh, I am aware of that._ She looks around at her new shop with satisfaction. Opportunity piled upon opportunity. That is my life of late._

She brings you a pouch of gold coins and, oddly enough, a rusty horseshoe. _Rewards for your efforts. A generous payment, as promised. I know that the payment seems humble, but trust me. It is a valuable trinket I give you._
I decided not to betray Charon.
_Hmmmph. A fine time for a Hand of Avadon to discover ethics. Since I can't deal with my rival, I must move on. I need to find a place to sell my wares before I starve._
_I bid you farewell. I will not be here for long._
This is now your shop?

She looks around with pride. _Mine now. Sadly, poor old Trader Charon was arrested. I went to see him in the castle. To obtain money for his defense, he sold this shop to me, and for a delightfully low price._
_Yes, opportunity after opportunity. That is my life._
What will happen to Charon?
_I'm sure that I don't care. He has friends. He has money. He will survive somehow. I think._
Where have you come from?

_I am Kellem, born and bred! My home lies to the east. I only go west to Holklanda to obtain goods to sell. I would not admit this too loudly, but many Holklandan crafts are of the highest quality, and there is much profit to be had bringing them here._
What sorts of goods do you carry?
_Holklandan art. Steelwork. Even tools for shadowwalkers, like weaponry and poisons. There is demand for such things in Kellemderiel, though few would admit it._
What do you think of Holklanda?
_I don't, really. Just more people to trade with. I do not care about politics. If everyone in the Pact would just get along, things would be much better._
She brightens up. _Of course! I will do what I can for what few customers pass this way._
_Also, in return for your aid to me, I have certain special items I would be willing to sell._
Let me see your wares.
Calantha's Wares
Calantha has a variety of valuable Holklandan equipment, brought from there with great difficulty and expense.
Let me see your 'special' items.
Calantha has several particularly rare and valuable works of Holklandan craftsmanship, brought from there with great difficulty and expense.
_Then is there anything else you want to discuss before you move on?_
I will be going now. (Leave.)
Calantha nods to you. _I appreciate your company. Safe travels to you._
This middle-aged merchant is surprisingly elegantly dressed for these rustic surroundings. His hair is immaculate, and you think that he is wearing a scent. Subtly and carefully applied, of course.
And yet, he greets you in a friendly, borderline servile way. _Welcome ... You are [N], yes? I learned of your arrival. A trickle of palace gossip does reach me out here._
_I am Trader Charon, and I deal with all who brave the dangers of the Beraza Woods._
Trader Charon is an experienced shopkeeper, staying close enough to you to be available but not close enough to be creepy. When you are present, he pointedly ignores all of his other customers.
Why is there a trading post here?
_Because, as strange as it may seem, there are many who brave the dangerous road through the Beraza Woods. People who carry out a wide variety of activities, though I do not judge._
_These people have needs. I meet them. It is simple enough._
What sorts of 'activities' take place along the road?
He gives you a thin smile. _There are smugglers and brigands, though I never deal with their kind. I deal with hunters, who prowl the woods looking for wild game and brigands._
_And I deal with merchants, who carry on the trade between Holklanda and Kellemderiel._
The road to the west is dangerous?
He nods. _Oh, yes. Thugs and monsters. Monsters and thugs. Happily, the might of Castle Vebeaux keeps them from my door._
Do you know Trader Calantha?
He smirks. Then he walks to the window and looks out of it. _Ah, the poor young lass, stuck out there. For weeks. Unable to proceed through the castle._
_And yet ..._ He seems slightly disturbed. _She can move on, but she doesn't. Why? What is she planning? Ah, well. I'm sure I can deal with it. She is young and simple._
Why was she trapped there?

_Oh, castle politics are such a mystery? Apparently, Gatemaster Prose somehow decided that it was to his benefit to not give her permission to pass the gate. Almost as if someone paid him to discourage merchants to do business in this settlement._
_But those are castle dealings, and I would not pretend to understand them._
_And yet, he gave her permission to pass. Hmmm. She must have allies of her own._
He smirks. _I did. Now she is gone. Passed through the castle to sell her shoddy wares in the east. I knew she would give up eventually._
Can you tell me about the Beraza Woods?
_Wide. Dark. Contested. Dangerous. But a great opportunity for one with the right connections and a head for business._
_Of course you would! I have much that will aid one in your line of work. And please do not worry. Hands of Avadon always receive a discount here. What do you need?_
Charon sells equipment for the sophisticated adventurer, and he makes sure that you receive a discount for all of his wares.
_Then I bid you good day. Must move on. Very busy. Farewell._ He rushes off.
There is a young farmer out tending his crops. You note that he is constantly looking toward the woods to the west, and there is an old broadsword hanging from his belt.
When you approach him, he nods. _Welcome, traveler. I am Padget. Please try not to step on the cabbage._
Padget walks among his crops, picking weeds and mercilessly destroying every slug brave enough to climb up onto an edible leaf.
He seems comfortable with the broadsword hanging from his belt. You suspect that this weapon has been passed down from father to son for several generations.
What are you growing?
_Cabbage. I'll harvest soon, and then I will plant winter wheat._
How is the soil?
_Decent. Better than some._
Who do you sell your produce to?
_The castle. My cabbage has been eaten by some of the most important lords and ladies of Lynaeus. Those of them wise enough to know a good cabbage when they see one, anyway._
Isn't this a dangerous place to have a farm?
He looks west to the woods. _The hunters do a good job of keeping pests away. Most of the creatures that get through, I can kill. Those of them too big to kill, I can outrun._
So you have a sword.
_Yes, and I've had to use it._
Why don't you start a farm in a safer place?
_Because all of the best land in Kellemderiel is held by the lords, and they will never give it up. Not an inch._
_The Beraza Woods have unclaimed land. That is why foolhardy souls like me come here._
I've heard rumors that someone around here is digging a tunnel. Heard anything?

_I ..._ He thinks carefully. _I've heard nothing, though I don't know everything happening in every farmhouse around there. I don't want to make anyone angry, but some of the farmers? They're downright unsocial._
_Now, please excuse me. I need to be returning to work._ He walks off quickly, suddenly not wanting to be seen talking to you.

One of the hunters in this hall is an aging woman in rough, traveling clothes. Her salt and pepper hair stretches down to her waist, and the bow slung over her shoulder looks like it has been used for many years.

She is training the young hunters in this chamber, advising them as they fling missiles at the targets and practice their blade techniques. Her voice is soft and quiet, but they listen attentively to her every word.
When she sees you, she turns away from her charges to greet you. _Welcome, warrior. I am Trainer Leala. Have you come to me for a reason? Many hunters come to me to be trained. Or retrained._
Trainer Leala continues to supervise and admonish her students. Sometimes, she turns to you. _You can join them whenever you want. If you need training or retraining, please let me know._
You train the hunters here?
She nods. _I do. They come here experienced warriors, but they don't know the ways of the Beraza. The thick undergrowth. The pitfalls. The brigands and warped creatures._
_I prepare them so that they don't end up in the graveyard out back._
The woods are dangerous?
_Intensely so. It would be different if soldiers could go into them. A strong force of warriors from Kellemderiel, or Holklanda, or both._
_But neither nation allows soldiers of the other to enter, so a wild place it remains._
Have you hunted out there yourself?
She smiles sadly. _Of course. I would never send someone into a peril I have not faced myself, many times. Of course, those years are past me now._
Anything out there I should watch out for?
_I am the wrong one to ask. I hear so many tales and rumors about the dark woods that I have no idea which ones are correct._
_I have even been told that a drake wanders the dark paths. It has the ability to control the minds of those it sees, or so they say. Perhaps true. Probably not._
Can you train me?
She inspects you with a practiced eye. _No. Your skill is already greater than mine. I can't increase your power, though, with time, I could help you to refocus the strength you already have._
What is retraining?
_Sometimes, as you gain in experience, you may find that you have been trained in ways that no longer work for you. I can help you to refocus that skill in different ways._

(Leala can enable you to respend all of your skill points, putting them into different skills and abilities. You won't lose any levels or experience. Be warned ... if you take her offer, you will need to completely retrain that character.)
I don't need that.
_You are content with the path you have traveled? I am pleased._
There is one in my group I would like you to retrain.
_Of course. I hope you are ready to choose a new path._
Please retrain my first character.
Trainer Leala takes you through a vigorous period of retraining. It takes time and effort, but you soon feel able to, with work, change your abilities.
(You are now able to respend all of this character's skill points.)
Please retrain my second character.
Please retrain my third character.
I've changed my mind. I don't need your help.
She smiles. _I am pleased to hear it. I will return to my charges, who need every bit of help I can provide._ She returns to directing her students.
I don't need any training.
Sorceress Shade
The shade of the sorceress banishes a foe!
The shade of the sorceress calls the dead to life!
Deep Woods Widow
Leaping Widow
Accursed Widow
Talking: Vinvella shushes you. She is concentrating on the hunt.
Talking: Vinvella brushes past you. Now that the hunt is done, she is eager to get out of these woods.
Shhhh.
Let's get there.
Should be easy.
Talking: Monitor Shigaz says that you should descend into the pit and help the Kellem. He is standing guard outside and wants to stay alert.
Talking: The warrior shushes you. Now that they are moving, they are being very quiet and alert.
Blade Lundy
Dabert
Serlait

A good set.
Into the quiver with you.

Welcome, traveler.
The Hand is here.
At last.
We are eager to be done.
