You have spent a long day's march traveling the free road that cuts through the Beraza Woods. The less friendly denizens of these woods know enough to not draw attention to themselves by interfering with travel on a free road, so your journey is uneventful.

And then you round a corner and find a campsite of Pact warriors. Sure enough, Monitor Shigaz is waiting where he said he would be. He is camped with eight soldiers of Kellemderiel. Nobody looks happy to be here.
In fact, Shigaz is sitting by himself on the other side of the camp from the Kellem. Everyone looks furious. It's a tense scene. It's probably a good thing that you arrived when you did.
There is a stone circle dominating this clearing, in the Khemerian style. It looks like recent construction. Smooth stones, free of moss. Probably erected using magic.

There is an old stone staircase in the middle of the circle, descending into the earth. You look around for traps or signs of an ambush. As you do, you realize that you are having a hard time concentrating.

The stones seem to move. Every time you turn your head, one of them seems to have shifted an inch. You try to concentrate on the moldy pine trapdoor. Then you hear something giggling. You aren't sure where the sound came from. Then you look back at the mossy birch trapdoor, and ...

Something is wrong here. There is a force that is making it hard to ... concentrate. You can understand why Duke Gryfyn sent you here first. This sort of dangerous, uncontrolled magic needs to be dealt with.

This was once a large lumber yard. Trees would be cut down, dragged here, turned into boards, and sent east and west. The Beraza Woods are largely uncontrolled, and brave woodsmen can make a good living here.
However, the lumberjacks who lived in this building abandoned it to the elements, and then the bandits moved in. Or maybe the bandits drove them out. Either way, it's now a dangerous place to be.
You smelled this tannery well before you reached it. The few brave souls who hunt the Beraza Woods can bring their skins here to be treated. It's a gruesome, dirty process.
Smoke rises from the chimney of the building to the north. Whoever lives here, they are at home.
You find that the shining steel gate has closed again. It's far too strong for you to break it down. You will need to find a new way out.
You think that you remember something about this gate being open and rusty. Must be a different gate. It's easy to get confused down here.

You step out into a huge cavern and see a lovely sight. At least, if it exists, it's lovely. It is a large subterranean lake, dotted with islands. Most of the islands have candelabras on them, filling the cave with a dim, spectral light.

At first, you think that you have reached a dead end. It looks like there is no way to cross to the islands. Happily, continued exposure and your mental training are slowly enabling you to shake off the confusing effects of this place.

There seems to be something in the mist on the water. You look at it out of the corner of your eye. You think about something else. You just wait. And then, slowly, you start to make them out. Wooden bridges. Rotten and crumbling, but still stable enough to carry you over the icy water.
The magical aura in the air is much stronger here. There is an energy that makes you feel sluggish. It gets harder and harder to put one foot in front of the other.
This spell is familiar, however. So is the reptilian reek in the air. There are basilisks ahead. Several of them.

This cavern also contains a subterranean lake, much smaller than the other one. Natural bridges of stone rise out of the dark water. Someone built walkways running along them. At least it won't be difficult to pass.

You are more worried by the demon watching you from the island in the middle of the lake. Like the earlier infernal you had to fight, this one is hungry, deranged, and trapped in a magic circle. However, this one seems much more inclined to do its duty and repel you.

It lets out a long, loud cackle and throws a pair of fireballs. Not at you. At the walkway to the south. They hit the ground with a loud crack and two puffs of sulfurous smoke. There are now two imps standing there, looking for prey.
You enter a large cavern. Once a large workshop for the wizard who lived here, it is now a ... a ...

What you see at first is a wonderland of mushrooms and tall, elegant fungi. Sparkling, fairylike creatures watch you shyly from the shadows and beckon for you to come play with them. It's strange, lovely, and all a lie.

You close your eyes, take a deep breath, and look again. You peer past the illusion to see what is really there. The three Kellem warriors, Lundy, Dabert, and Serlait, are standing there, swaying from side to side. They don't look at you. Or at anything. Their minds are gone.
They move back and forth in time to the motions of a drake's claw. A huge, withered reptile is watching them, directing them like puppets. Then it sees you. And it sees that you see it.
It lets out a long, raspy sigh. It lowers its claw, and the three soldiers are still. Then it motions for you to approach.
To the west, you see the ruins of another magic workshop. A third huge demon is imprisoned in a magic circle in an alcove in the west wall.
The infernal beast is either unaware of your presence or simply pretends to be. It leans against the wall, eyes closed, stiff like a statue. As you get closer, it doesn't move.

You return to the chamber where you first faced Zhossa the Mindtaker. Sure enough, you find a message from Nathalie. She burnt it into the stone with a narrow lance of fire. She is not a subtle person.
The message says, simply, _The beast's trail is clear. It will not escape the gaze of Avadon._

Below the message is a crude map, also drawn in a thin line of blackened stone. It indicates a region in the mountains to the north, a forest high up between two peaks. If you want to track Nathalie, it seems the next likely place to go.
THESE LANDS CLAIMED FOR EUDOR AND HIS WARRIORS!
KEEP OUT OR DIE!
Acelin and Belda's Leatherwork
No brigands, pests, or solicitors.
No politics.
The wandering woodsman stops in this campsite. He looks around for something. Soon, he sees it. It's a paving stone at the base of a tree.
He kneels down, lifts up the stone, and slips something under it. Then he stands up and, struck by a burst of paranoia, looks around. That's when he sees you.

He sighs. _Seen at last. Didn't think I'd last this long. Still, it will take better than you to catch Orian ..._ He reaches up, grabs one of the charms around his neck, and mutters a word of command. The charm crumbles into dust, and Orian disappears.
Whoever sent him here, he was no ordinary woodsman.
You lift up the stone and find the object Orian deposited there. It's a tiny scroll tube. You open it and read the message within:
_My masters of the Tawon - No news. No sign of Avadon. The Hands already killed have been burned. No movement in Vebeaux. I think the emissary will soon emerge._
And that is all it says.
You approach this wheel, one of two on these eastern islands. The other is to the south. You try to turn the wheel, but it is stuck.
With great effort, you manage to turn this wheel. It turns for three rotations, pulling its chain out of the ground, before it gets stuck.
Nothing else happens.
You approach this wheel, one of two on these eastern islands. The other is to the north. You try to turn the wheel, but it is stuck.
The ground under your feet vibrates slightly. You hear the sound of steel scraping over stone. Something clatters and clanks to the northwest. Then the activity ceases.
The sign is worn and barely legible. It says:
BASILISK HOLDING. STAY BACK!
You look in the basilisk nest, hoping to find valuable treasure among the bones and the trash.
Alas, there is nothing of value.

Instead, you find something much more unusual and interesting. There is a clutch of four basilisk eggs. Small, round, leathery, hardy little things. They might be valuable. Or, at least, incredibly dangerous. You carefully wrap them up and take them.
A third demon was being held in a magic circle. It is an enormous, muscular beast. Its flesh seems to be made of rock. The stone cracks under its massive hooves.
Unlike the other two demons, it dealt with its long imprisonment by retreating within itself. One day, it closed its eyes and simply shut down.

But then you came close. It smelled and heard you. At last, a chance to be freed has presented itself. It opens its eyes and lumbers out of the circle toward you. When it steps past the wards, its skin begins to crack and hiss.
The demon is getting irritated. Constant agony. The efforts of battle. Its skin burning and peeling off in sheets. And yet, it is still not dead.

There is something about the wards that bind it that keep it from just giving up its life. To be free, it must be defeated in battle. It roars in fury and begins to stamp its hooves, its determination to fight you doubled.
There is a somber hunter of the Beraza Woods sitting at this table, sharpening some arrows. He is from Kellemderiel, based on his accent and complexion.
He looks up at you and nods. _Welcome, visitor. I am Acelin. But you don't want to talk to me. Talk to Belda. She does all our trading._
Acelin sits silently at this table, sharpening a set of arrows.
_We work together, Belda and I. I hunt. I gather the skins. She treats and sews them. She has great skill, as you will see if you trade with her._
You hunt in these woods?
_I do. It's dangerous, but I've been out here my whole life. It's where I met Belda, out here in the wilds._
Any advice?
_Learn to be where brigands and monsters aren't. Don't chase trouble. That's the rule I live by, though you don't seem the type to avoid trouble._
Tell me about Belda.
_We ..._ He grows very uncomfortable. _We don't discuss our lives with outsiders until we know them. We are hunters and traders. That is all._
I'd like to know more about all of these skins.
He shakes his head. _Go talk to Belda. They're hers, and I'll be in trouble if I don't let her talk about them._ He waves at her. Then he goes back to silently preparing his arrows.

There is a young Holklandan woman sitting at this table. Scissors and cured sheets of leather are arrayed in front of her. When you approach, she is cutting out the pieces that will soon form a new leather jerkin. Her skill is considerable.

Your presence makes her very nervous, but she manages to meet your gaze and smile shyly. _Welcome, traveler. I am Belda. I hope that you come to trade peacefully. I will sell my work to any who don't mean us harm._
Belda smiles at you. _What else do you need? I have little to offer besides the garments I make, I'm afraid._ She is slowly calming down and becoming comfortable with your presence.
_Acelin and I? We live out here because ... It was not safe to stay where we were. We stay halfway between two lands. That is the only place we can be. It seems appropriate._
Why isn't it safe for you to be elsewhere?
She looks over at Acelin and sighs. _We are from different lands. It makes things ... hard for others to accept. I would rather not talk about it._
Don't brigands ever bother you?
_Not lately. They know that, if they attack us, at least a few of them will die before they can subdue us. We don't have enough of value to make it worth the risk._
Tell me about the woods.
_They are dangerous, lovely, and wild. Acelin and I walk them together sometimes. I am not as skilled with a bow as he is, but I am not useless either._
Seen anything interesting out there lately?
_Interesting to a warrior like yourself? No. We make very sure to avoid that sort of thing._
Tell me about your leatherwork.
_It is simple. Acelin obtains the skins. I work them. I have some small skill at the craft. You can see my wares, if you wish._
_It is a pity you cannot see my shop as it was, back in Holklanda. With the right materials, I can make some superb armor._
Belda's Leather
Belda has remarkable skill working with leather. It's truly a pity she's stuck out here so far from civilization.
What sort of materials do you lack?
_A wider variety of skins. I miss drake skin, mainly. Powerful, versatile stuff, but I would never suggest Acelin take the risk of obtaining it._
_I would love to work with it again, though. With two sheets of it and, say, five hundred coins for my labor and skill, I could make a truly worthy piece of armor for you._
_Then I will return to my work. I wish you a safe journey, wherever you are going._
I would like for you to make a fine suit of armor for me. (Give 500 coins and 2 drake skins.)
Belda shakes her head. _You don't have enough money. To live out here, we must trade with passing merchants, and their wares are expensive._
Belda inspects the skins. _Very nice. Must have been dangerous to obtain them. I can make a fine tunic or a lovely pair of greaves. What would you prefer?_
I'd like a tunic.
Belda collects the materials, money, and tools. Then, determined to keep her techniques secret, she retires to her bedroom. Acelin makes tea for you while you wait.
Eventually, she returns, bearing a beautiful piece of drake skin armor. _It was an honor to make this. A worthy use of my skills. That doesn't happen often these days. I thank you._
I would like greaves.
At last, the exit from this dark pit is within view. Sunlight shines down from above, and you can smell the forest.
As you approach, Nathalie slows down. You turn to look at her. Something has made her very upset.
(Ignore her.)
She is in no mood to be ignored. She looks you in the eye. _It escaped. That beast ... It killed Pact soldiers, it attacked us, and we let it go._
What is wrong, Nathalie?
She looks you in the eye. _It escaped. That beast ... It killed Pact soldiers, it attacked us, and we let it go._
We didn't really have a choice about letting the creature go.
She thinks about this. _Perhaps. Or maybe we were too slow. Too weak. But after what it did ... that insult ... Something will have to be done._
The drake is not important. We have more important work to do.
_Of course it is important. Avadon has grown weak. And why is that? Because we tolerate insults like the one we have just received._
_No. If Avadon is to be preserved, something will have to be done._
You are right. The creature must be hunted down.
_Yes. I knew you would see the truth. If we let insults like this go unanswered, Avadon looks weak. We look weak._
What do you have in mind?

_I don't know, but mark my words. We will discuss this later. I did not spend my whole life dreaming of joining Avadon in order to let prey like that escape. I will not let Redbeard see me as one who ..._
She stops. _Never mind. We can discuss this later. For now, we should make sure Shigaz is still alive._
Shima looks at the Kellem soldiers. He says to you, quietly, _I admire Monitor Shigaz. I don't know if I could so easily bear such insults._
Why is it harder for you than for him?

_When my family was defeated by the Honored Forge and banished, to save myself, I was forced to ... abase myself. I swore I would never be so humiliated again. For anything. That is one reason I went to Avadon._
You may have no choice.
Shima looks at you. You see a naked rage in his eyes that you have never seen before. He says, in a cold voice, _One always has a choice._
Then he calms down and moves on.
A Hand of Avadon will not be treated thus.

Shima looks at you. You see a naked rage in his eyes that you have never seen before. He says, in voice full of emotion, _Thank you, [N]. After what I have been through, a kind word means more to me than you know._
Sevilin walks over to a stalagmite. He rests his hand on it. Then he punches it, hard. As he shakes his sore hand, he smiles.
_Sorry, [N]. I just needed to convince myself that something here is real._
And that stalagmite?
He looks down at his throbbing hand and smiles. _Oh, real. Quite real._

Jenell leans close to one of the trees and examines it. _Yes. Looks normal, until you get close. Leaves too thin. Bark peeling. And ..._ She leans forward, bruises a leaf, and smells it. _Wrong. Just a tiny bit wrong._
What does it mean?
_Magic. Raw magic. Probably uncontrolled. Maybe not. Most likely forbidden. Definitely something these woods would be better rid of._
She walks on with renewed purpose. _Come on. Let's keep the soldiers from killing each other._

You stumble upon a band of filthy, armed denizens of the woods. The moment they see you, they unsteadily leap to their feet and draw their weapons. They have been drinking wine. A lot of it, probably looted from a passing caravan.
One of them stumbles forward and slurs, _What you lookin' at? You know who we are? Eudor's men. Terrors, we are. Raiders. Know what you'll do? Give us everything you got. Everything. Or else._
The other brigands, upon inspecting you, seem to regret that their companion decided to threaten you.
Who is Eudor?

The loudmouth grins at you. His few remaining teeth are stained red with the cheap wine he's been drinking. _Eudor? A fierce ... fierce bandit. War leader. That's right. You've stumbled into his warriors. Bet you're sorry now!_
Is this the same Eudor who has been raiding the Tawon Empire?
_We ... You know about us? Yeah, that's us. We rob those Farlanders. For the Pact! But they were trying to hunt us down, so we're taking a rest down here._
Do you realize that you're threatening a Hand of Avadon?
The loudmouth laughs at you. _Expect me to believe that? Do you? Everyone says they're from Avadon. Lies!_
The increasingly nervous brigands standing behind him seem to be having no trouble at all believing you're from Avadon.
Look, I'll give you a few coins if you'll just save me the trouble of killing you.
The drunken brigand spits on the ground at your feet. _We spit on your offer._ He points at the spit. _See! Spit! You should have just given up!_
He charges you, wildly swinging his blade. The others, probably fearing Eudor's wrath if they don't help the idiot, reluctantly follow.
I really dislike brigands. (Attack.)
The drunken brigand laughs. _Then you have doomed yourself! To being killed! By us!_ The wine has clearly impaired his ability to evaluate risk versus reward.

You meet a Kellem woodsman wandering down this path. He has a hatchet over his shoulder and a nasty, long dagger at his belt. If anything in the woods gives him trouble, he's ready to give it right back. Several charms hang around his neck.

He is dirty, ragged, and unhappy to see you. He gives you a brusque little nod. _I'm Orian. Don't see many strangers out here. Better watch yourself. It can be dangerous. I'll be moving on now._ He starts to walk past you.
You run into Orian the woodsman again. He recognizes you immediately, and he is increasingly unhappy about the disruptions of his solitude. He nervously fingers the charms hanging around his neck.
_I'm scouting. Looking for a good place to get lumber. Near a road. No monsters. I find something, I go back and gather the others._
Isn't this a dangerous place to look for wood?
He nods. _Dangerous. But everywhere is dangerous. What forests are left back in Kellemderiel are all claimed by one duke or another. Trying to fell trees back there is far more dangerous._
Tell me about those charms.
_They're for luck. You can't live in these woods without getting a little superstitious._
Mind if I travel with you for a bit?
He grimaces. _I took up the axe to be able to spend time alone. That's how I work. Alone. I'll be moving along now. Safe travels to you. Far away from me._
He spits, lifts his axe up onto his shoulder, and moves on.
I'll be going, then.
_Me too. Watch yourself. Lots of danger out here if you're careless. Have to keep your eyes and ears open._
You reach the end of what was going to be the bandits' escape tunnel. Sadly for them, they never got around to creating the actual exit. Their leader stands before you, furious.
_What are you doing here?_ he shouts. _We don't raid the Pact. We attack the Tawon Empire only. I am Eudor, and I am no fool. I only bother Farlanders._
Eudor looks and sounds like a Dharamite. He is talking very quickly. _And yet, you break into our fort? Kill all of my warriors? Why?_
Some of your bandits attacked me outside.
_They did? They were drunk, yes? Out of their minds on that swill the Tawon drink, no doubt. Then I apologize. They got what they deserved. But why hunt me down?_
I don't like brigands.
_I don't want you to like me. I just want for you to not break into my home, killing everyone you see. Nobody forced you to come here!_
You only attack the Tawon Empire?
_That's right. I am a good citizen of the Pact. The Kellem? The Holklanders? I don't want to anger them. We go up to the Tawon Empire. Raid until they get wise to us. Flee._
_It's all in good fun, and they're Farlanders. Who cares?_
Well, you have the attention of a Hand of Avadon.
_Avadon? You're from Avadon? Then maybe you'll see reason. You defend the Pact. We would never hurt the Pact, only its enemies. I'm not your enemy!_
Stirring up the Farlands is against the laws of the Pact.

_What? We've only engaged in a bit of robbery. Never killed anyone except to defend ourselves. And they're Farlanders! The whole existence of the Pact is based on extracting what we want from the outsiders!_
I think I'll have to kill you.
He leaps forward, hands out. _Wait! That's not ... You don't have to kill me. I'll go. Never come back. And I'll pay you. Gold! Just let us go!_
Now I have to decide what to do with you.
_Well, we're not the enemy. You can just let us go. I'll even pay you. A big bag of gold, if you spare us._
We met an envoy from the Tawon Empire. She offered a bounty for your head.
_And you would consider it? You would kill a warrior of the Pact for a Farlander? What sort of a Hand are you?_
Nathalie nods. _He has a point._
Sevilin shakes his head. _The law is the law. And I don't like brigands._
_Anyway,_ Eudor continues, _you can just tell her that you killed me. She's from the Farlands. She won't be able to question you!_
Where would you go?
He thinks. _Probably south, to hunt wretches. Can you really care if I hunt wretches?_
It would probably be safest to just kill you. (Attack.)
Eudor lets out a terrified squeal. It appears that he thought he could talk his way out of this. Then he draws his blade, ready to defend himself.
All right. You can go.
Eudor drops to his knees, gasping, overcome with relief. _Thank you. You will never hear from me again._ Then he rises and he and his surviving warriors leave. Running.
Happily, before he leaves, Eudor does not neglect giving you the gold he promised.
The basin is now mercifully empty.

This chamber must have been the main workshop of the wizard who built this complex, and this stone basin was the focus of his work. It is still full of thick, vile green goo. It shifts back and forth in the basin, moving under its own power.
This stinks of magic used to make or warp living things. In other words, forbidden magic. Still, it is sometimes useful to take samples of such stuff back to Avadon for study.
(Look closer.)
You bend close. A long ropy mass of green goo lashes out toward your face. You jump back. The goo slips back into the basin.
Nathalie looks at the stuff with undisguised greed. _Fascinating. I could do fascinating things with that stuff. Ummmm ... If it wasn't illegal, of course._
(Leave the goo alone.)
Unknown, semi-living magic? Better to just keep a safe distance. You back away.
(Take a sample of the goo.)
You pick up a clay jar and a spoon, lift up a thick glob of the goo, and seal it safely away in the container. At first, it seems like everything will be all right.

But then the remaining goo begins to bubble and hiss. You have disturbed some sort of delicate balance. It begins to flow out of the basin, splitting in two and then splitting again. The runes by the walls draw the stuff to it, keeping it from escaping.
When it gets there, however, the vile stuff begins to take on a new form ...
Gooey Bones
Walking Goo
Stalking Goo
You approach Monitor Shigaz nervously. Even from a distance, you can tell how angry he is. He stands at the far side of the camp from the soldiers he is supposed to be fighting with.
When he sees you, he is relieved. Somewhat. _Ah, [N], you have arrived. That means my time in this miserable place is coming to an end._
_When Duke Gryfyn asked for me to fight alongside his soldiers, he promised me ... something better than this. I will stay to help destroy the monsters here, but I ... I have not been treated well._
Monitor Shigaz stares down the dark woods to the northwest. He looks no less angry. _Is it time, [N]? Can we finally leave this place?_
The Holklandan shoots an angry gaze at the Kellem soldiers. _I met with these warriors at the west gate of the castle. We traveled out here. We stopped at this camp._
_Then, trying to talk to them, I saw that I had not received what I was promised. Instead, I got contempt and insults. I am a calm man, but I have been pushed too far._
Insults?
_Kellemderiel and Holklanda hate each other. That is the truth I told Duke Gryfyn again and again. He said some Kellem want peace. Well, wherever they are, they are not here!_

_These warriors have done nothing but belittle me and whisper insults behind my back from the moment we met. From the castle gates all the way to here. They are very fortunate that I am a patient man._
What pushed you too far?
_The first night, they offered me a meal at their camp. I was surprised. 'Why are they telling me to join them?' I thought._
_I am nothing if not observant. As I approached their circle, I saw one of them spit into my stew. Happily, I was wise enough to bring my own food. I have not sat with them since._
Shima nods in sympathy.
Can these soldiers do the job?
He looks over at them and nods begrudgingly. _They can. They are skilled. They are also rude, crude, and ... I am not sure that I can trust them._
And if you can't trust them in battle?
_We will see when the time comes._
Tell me about the forest near here.
_It is mostly calm. There are bandits to the west. Some friendly tanners to the north. Pests off the main road. Nothing important._
_The real threat is our target, to the northwest. I have scouted it. The duke is right to want to clear the place out. It is dangerous._
Tell me about the bandits.
_They avoid us. They don't send out patrols. They only drink and wait. For what, I do not know. As long as we avoid them, they will not be a threat._
Dangerous how?
_It is a simple pit in the ground, but I can sense a power in there. Something that warps minds. Creates illusions._
_The Kellem mock me for my concern, but I and the duke are right and they are wrong. It is the sort of uncontrolled magic the Pact should not tolerate._
_We are all prepared. We wait only for you. Give the word and we will all advance upon the pit._
And when we get there?
_We descend into it and cut out the rot. I hope._ He looks at the Kellem nervously. They look back at him with open dislike.
I am going to scout out the area first.
Shigaz nods. _Seems wise. We will remain here. I hope that you return soon._ He returns to the campfire.
It is time. Let's go.
Shigaz nods and turns to the Kellem warriors. _It is time. Prepare yourself. Let's burn out the infestation._

You soon realize that Monitor Shigaz was not exaggerating about the insolence of the Kellem soldiers. Whenever he speaks, they snicker, make faces, and whisper to each other. And this is in your presence. It must be worse when you aren't here.

However, in time, they manage to get their packs and blades and begin walking down the road to the northwest. Once on the road, the soldiers are quiet and alert. They may be rude, but they are competent.

The Blade in command of the Kellem soldiers is sitting by the fire. He looks like the veteran of a number of campaigns. He isn't vain enough to wear his medals out here in the woods, but the scars tell the tale.

He looks up at you, sips some tea, and nods. _So Shigaz didn't lie. A Hand of Avadon is with us._ He stands and nods. _I am Blade Lundy. There are three of us, ready to fight with you. Clear out a pit, yes? Not a problem._
Blade Lundy is starting to seem impatient. _I will not lie. We are eager to return to the comforts of the forest. Are we ready to begin?_

_Nothing that will surprise you. We are proud Kellem soldiers, and we were placed under the command of a Holklandan. There have been some ... angry words traded. Nothing more than should be expected._
He looks at Shima and seems to be about to say something. Then, wisely, he thinks better of it.
You have insulted the Holklandan?
_We have. The Holklandans are our enemy, and we have been placed under one's command? It is not right._
_We have followed our orders. Shigaz is safe with us. However, you will have to be happy with obedience. We will not pretend to like his kind._
Why were you picked for this mission?
_Because we are good, loyal soldiers! Every other warrior in our barracks threatened that they would leave before they fought alongside a Holklandan._
What do you think of the effort to make peace?
_Peace? Nobody wants peace more than a soldier, but ..._ He spits into the fire. _It is not time yet. Not when the Holklandans won't let us have this forest. It is ours._
What do you think of the mission?

He shrugs. _Shigaz is right about one thing. There is something nasty in that pit. That is why we three were selected. We all have experience fighting in mines and tunnels._ He points at a large stack of ropes nearby.
What is down there?
_I don't know. Some sort of magic gone horribly wrong, I expect. We aren't afraid. We've been trained to handle that sort of thing._
But there are only three of you?
_We're going underground, Hand? What do you want? A big force? An army? Marching in, bugles blaring?_
_No, for this, you want a small force. Fast and merciless. Whatever is down there, it won't last long._
Are you ready to go?
He nods. _Ready and eager. However, I'm not in charge. Shigaz is. Talk to him. When he gives the word, we can go._
You talk to this soldier of Kellemderiel. You find that he is part of a small patrol left here to watch the road. This warrior has nothing to do with your mission and is very happy about it.
The main thing you learn from the conversation is that, if you want to avoid a fight, stay on the road.

You meet Dabert, one of the warriors of Kellemderiel who will be accompanying you into the pit. He is currently examining the group's ropes and climbing tools, making sure that they are in good condition.
He looks up at you. _Talk to Blade Lundy. That's who I answer to._

There is a young archer here, one of the warriors of Kellemderiel who will be accompanying you into the pit. She is an amazingly small woman, well-suited for exploring tunnels and mineshafts. She is sharpening her arrowheads.
She looks up at you. _Talk to Blade Lundy. He gives the orders. The orders I listen to, anyway._
You reach the bottom of the stairs and find yourself in a wide, low cavern. There is a stone walkway, but it is cracked and crumbled. Someone built it years ago, but it has not been maintained.
Whatever has been clouding your mind, it is stronger down here. There are three stone spires surrounding the stairway. However, you aren't sure if the soft red glow that comes from them is real.

The three Kellem soldiers are facing a closed gate to the south. Unlike the walkway, it looks new. The metal doesn't show a touch of rust. Blade Lundy raps the metal with a mailed finger. Then he laughs and steps forward through the bars.
You look again and realize that the gate was open all along. And, even if it wasn't, the bars are so rusty that you could have knocked them down easily. The Kellem warriors smile and step through.
You try to talk to the soldier, but you get a brusque response. _Shush. It's hard enough concentrating down here. Just stay close to us. We've done this before._

You try to scout out this long cavern. It seems to be mostly natural, except for the walkway threading its way through it. Then it seems to change. What was once a stalagmite becomes a statue, or vise versa.
There is a passage leading to the south and a broken bridge that once spanned the underground stream to the east. It is this that has Blade Lundy's attention.
He takes a loop of rope off his shoulder and turns to you. Before he can speak, however, the silence is broken by howling.
Wolves run into the cave to the south. They are mangy, starving creatures, no doubt maddened a bit by the magic in the air. They launch themselves at you, eager for meat.
Mad Wolf

The four soldiers have reached the pit. All of you stand at the edge and look in. The strange magic in the air has not escaped them. They are shuddering as if the air is very cold, but the day is warm.
Blade Lundy, the Kellem commander, looks into the dark stairs. _All right. Get the ropes ready. And the picks. These steps look all right, but that can change._
Then he looks over at Monitor Shigaz. It's an ugly look. _And one more thing._
_We are not going into battle with a Holklandan at our backs. Shigaz goes in front, where we can see him._
Shigaz stands up straight and lets out a long, slow hissing noise. He seems exactly as insulted as he should be.
All right. Whatever it takes to get moving.
Monitor Shigaz looks at you, visibly hurt. _What? [N], you would agree to this? To treat me like a traitor, or a criminal?_
_No, I have developed a plan. One that will put nobody at risk of being near me._
That is not going to happen.
Monitor Shigaz nods. _Thank you, [N], for not treating me like a traitor or criminal. However, I still face entering a dangerous place with three that do._
_This area is infused with magic. It clouds the mind. Creates shades. Illusions. It is not wise for all of us to enter the trap. I will stay here. Guard the exit. Get help if needed._
_Duke Gryfyn asked much of me. But to enter this place with ... them? It is too much. I will not go._

What follows next is sadly predictable. Serlait makes a comment about his courage. Dabert follows up with an unfortunate opinion about his ancestry. And then they are arguing. Hands move dangerously close to blades.
Stop this! Right now!

None of them are so angry that they would dare ignore an order from a Hand of Avadon. They stop arguing. Blade Lundy is furious. _Remember, we are warriors of the Pact! The Pact! I see no Farlanders here. Everyone shut their mouths._
He continues. _Shigaz is right. He can stay here. No more insults. There is wisdom in us not all going in at once._ He turns to you. _[N], are you ready?_
(Wait for them to calm down.)

You wait. And wait. The soldiers grow angrier, the words more heated. Then, finally, Blade Lundy steps in. He is furious. _Shut it! All of you! Remember, we are warriors of the Pact! The Pact! I see no Farlanders here. Everyone shut their mouths._

All of them grow silent, even the Holklandan. He continues. _Shigaz is right. He can stay here. No more insults. There is wisdom in us not all going in at once._ He turns to you. _[N], are you ready?_
Monitor Shigaz, his face burning red, stands off to the side. His weapon is drawn. He is ready to fight. The Kellem warriors walk down the steps into the darkness.
Shigaz looks after them. _I never, never stepped back from a fight in my life. I loathe those three, but I must admit. They are brave to go down there._ He nods to you. _I wish you good fortune._

You emerge from the pit at last, battered and exhausted. After how badly everything has gone so far, you are surprised to find that Monitor Shigaz is still alive. He steps out from behind a stone pillar.
When he sees that it is you, he runs over and helps you out of the darkness. _You are back. I was concerned. I felt a change in the magic that afflicts this place._
And you are still well?
_I have been trained to avoid notice when I do not wish to be seen. What happened to me is not important. What happened in the pit?_
(Tell about the drake.)

Shigaz nods somberly. _That is far more dangerous a foe than any of us expected. Duke Gryfyn was right about one thing. In the absence of direct control, the Beraza Woods are attracting some dangerous residents._
Then he looks confused. He looks at the stairs, waiting for someone else to emerge. When nobody does, he looks at you again. _The Kellem? Where are they?_
Is it really important to you?
_I have had time to calm myself and reflect. I do not like them. They insulted me. Yet, I do not wish them dead. Where are they?_
The drake destroyed them.
Shigaz looks genuinely disturbed by this news. _They died? Died to ... To calm the woods? To bring peace to Holklandan land? I mean ... disputed land?_
_This is ... This has become rather a strange tale. But ... What now?_
They attacked me. They had to die.

Shigaz looks genuinely disturbed by this news. _Attacked you? It must have been the influence of the drake, yes? Of course. And they died to ... To calm the woods? To bring peace to Holklandan land? I mean ... disputed land?_
I need to return to Duke Gryfyn.
_Of course. The duke will be very eager to learn what happened. And, despite the deaths of his soldiers, I think he will be pleased._

_I will think on this. I must also send word back to my people what has happened. Had the Kellem lived, I would have had much less to say. But they gave their lives, and we Holklandans greatly revere such sacrifices._
_Yes, though I was skeptical, there may be an opportunity in Duke Gryfyn's work. I must go now. Go and think._
Will you tell them that you stayed outside and avoided danger?
_Yes. I will say everything, including how the enemy soldiers shamed me with their courage. And yet, I promise you this. I will never back away from such a fight again._
Goodbye, then.
_Yes. I ... There is much to think about. Much to discuss. I wish you a safe journey back._ He walks off on his own, taking great care to conceal himself. Soon, he is lost in the brush.
You return to the three warriors, only to find that they are making preparations to cross the ruined bridge. They have already used a length of rope to lasso a stalagmite on the far side.
Blade Lundy turns to you. He still seems confident, but his eyes keep flickering nervously toward empty corners. He says, _This is a good opportunity. Whoever is here, we can take them by surprise._
_You ... You will go south. We will go east. We will find the prey and flush them into you. We will surround it. We will kill it. All done. I've used this maneuver before. Works well on pests._
Pests? You think that is what we are dealing with?
_Pests. Minor enchantments. Hedge magic. We are decorated warriors of the Kellem, battle-hardened and trained to fight in caves. To us, it will be a pest._
What do you think is back there?
_Probably more wolves. Maybe a ... We will be fine. We are battle-trained and hardened to fight in caves. We are ready._
This is a bad plan. You will stay here with me.

You say this, but they don't really hear you, because they are on the other side of the river. What happened? How did they get over there so quickly? They have already pulled down the ropes they used to cross.
Blade Lundy, Dabert, and Serlait turn in unison, give you a jaunty salute, and then turn and head down the dark tunnel.
Good plan. I'll head south.
Blade Lundy nods. You watch silently as they string a second rope across the river and use them to cross the river. Once across, the three of them turn in unison and give you a jaunty salute.
Then they turn and head down the dark tunnel.

There is an infernal standing in this circle, trapped. Even by the shaky standards of its kind, it is a mad creature. When it sees you, it lunges at you, steps out of the circle, writhes in agony, and jumps back.
_Ahrrrghsssss ..._ it hisses. _Curse you, Adranos,_ he howls. _Leave me here to hunger? Guardian of nothing?_
What are you?
_Me? Plaything of Adranos, useless dust and bones, rotting and held, warped creature, longing and full of hunger!_
Who is Adranos?
The demon screams in impotent rage. _Lost mage, arrogant mage, foolish mage, meat in the end._
Are you the one creating the illusions?
_Me? Hrrrahhh! No! I do not care! To do such magic, must care. No, the usurper, the eater, he takes mind. Taking yours, soon._
Where is Adranos?

_Gone. Taken. Fought the mind taker. Turned to meat. And me ... me ... Brought by Adranos, held to guard, me and the others. Brought. Toys. Kept. Held. Mindtaker laughs at us. Will eat us all! I wish! I wish!_
Others? What others?
_Adranos got several playthings. A set. Three. I am the first. Left us. Adranos, I never thought I would wish you life! You forsook ussss!_
I will end your torment, foul creature. (Attack.)
The infernal leaps out of his circle again. The bonds twist him and fill him with agony, but he no longer cares. _Yessss! Free me! Or feed me! I must have something! Some relief!_
And he lunges at you, his skin cracking and smoking. Even as he fights, the wards are destroying him.
What can I do to free you?
The infernal gives you a vicious smile. _Kill me. But only kill me fair. Is the rules of the game! Of the bonds!_
And then the beast leaps out of his circle again. The bonds twist him and fill him with agony, but he no longer cares. _Yessss! Free me! Or feed me! I must have something! Some relief!_
You walk up to one of the three Kellem warriors. Their plan was to sneak up on the enemy. They didn't get far.
They stand like puppets being held on strings. Their heads loll to the side at an unnatural angle. Their eyes are completely dead.
Whatever the drake did to them, their minds are empty now. Sucked dry. They only exist as the vicious reptile's playthings. You find yourself growing very angry.

You approach the drake. He is a large specimen of his kind, old and withered. Not as awe-inspiring as a dragon, but with the same cruel, avaricious intelligence. He watches you, trying to determine how much of your surroundings you can see. The answer is, of course, all of them.
He sighs again. _Ahsssss. I am Zhossa Mindtaker. It isss rare that any seesss me at all. Let alone facesss me. Who are you, little creature, that I have not yet crushed your spirit._
Nathalie rocks back and forth, barely able to keep from lashing out at the creature instantly. She whispers, _This ... This is true prey. What I dreamed of. I will have this thing dead._
Were you using magic on me? I didn't notice.
The drake smirks slightly. Then he gazes at you intently. You feel slightly dizzy for a moment. _Yes ... [N]. I was using my powersss on ... Avadon? You are of Avadon?_
_That isss difficult. Avadon isss not a foe I would wish. It wasss to avoid such attention that I came here._
Your parlor tricks won't work on a Hand of Avadon.
The drake suddenly looks worried. He gazes at you intently. You feel slightly dizzy for a moment. _You are ... [N]. Of Avadon. Yesss. Avadon. Unfortunate._
_Avadon isss not a foe I would wish. It wasss to avoid such attention that I came here._
I am too well-trained to be controlled by you.
The drake smirks slightly. _Controlled? No. But can I see you?_ He gazes at you intently. You feel slightly dizzy for a moment. _You are ... [N]. Of Avadon. Yesss. Avadon. Unfortunate._
_I wish what all of my kind do. A place to live in solitude. Gather a hoard. Hunt my prey. Raise a clutch of eggsss._
_That isss why I took thisss lair for my own. Ate who I would. Took what wealth came close. Would have kept to myself, until you and your pestsss invaded._
The drake waves his hand, and the three mindless husks of the Kellem soldiers dance like puppets. You grow increasingly angry.
Who lived here before you?

_A mage. Name wasss ..._ He thinks. _Adranos. Yesss. Strong, in hisss way. Thought he would deal with me. Take advantage. Saw in hisss mind, saw hisss plans. I waited for an unguarded moment. I took hisss mind. Devoured him. Claimed hisss home._
The drake seems interested. _Yesss. A way out of this impasse. A way for the Hand of Avadon to move along and leave me be. I will challenge you._
Nathalie looks at the three mindless soldiers with alarm. Then she turns to you and whispers, _There are no deals to be made with a monster like this one. It is our prey. Finish the hunt!_
Enough talking. You attacked a Hand of Avadon. You will die.

Zhossa Mindtaker nods, unconcerned. _Thisss is why I sought solitude. I knew, when Avadon saw me, that thisss would happen. Still, if you are all devoured, none will know of me, and I can flee deeper in the woodsss._
The drake doesn't move to attack, though. He says, simply, _Yesss. We will find a way out of this impasse. I will challenge you._
You will restore the minds of those three soldiers.

Zhossa Mindtaker smiles. _Cannot be done. Their minds are gone. Devoured. I read their thoughts. Did you know they were terrified of you? That isss why they split apart from you when you invaded my lair._
_I could not tell why they were terrified. Now I know they feared Avadon. No matter. They are gone. Only the shell remains._
I will take your trove.
Zhossa thinks on this. _No. You are alone here, and my power is greater than yoursss. Maybe we will declare a peace, but I will not give you all. My trove leavesss with me._
How will you challenge me?

Zhossa thinks on this. _You have come to me. We will play a game of my choosing, you versus my petsss._ The drake nods, and the three mindless soldiers stand alert. Their arms limply raise their weapons.
_Score but a single point against me, and I will leave thisss place to you._
Games? Points? Nonsense! Avadon exists to destroy monsters like you.

The drake inspects you appraisingly. _But you come to my place of power. Perhapsss I cannot destroy you, but you certainly can't destroy me. Thusss, we settle this impasse with a game. It amusesss me, and you have no choice._
And how will you earn points?
_First, my puppets will slay you. Then I will devour you. When that happens, I will also earn a point._
Do what you must, drake. I will fight you however I can.

Zhossa nods. _Understood. Come and face my puppet. If you can damage it enough that I must save it, you will receive a point. One point, and I will withdraw. Fail, and you will be devoured._ The drake smiles.
_Now defend youself!_ Zhossa starts to mumble a spell. You instantly start to feel dizzy. You prepare to defend yourself ...
All right. I will play your game.

Zhossa nods. _I am thrilled. Come and face my puppet. If you can damage it enough that I must save it, you will receive a point. One point, and I will withdraw. Fail, and you will be devoured._ The drake smiles.

You return to face Zhossa Mindtaker. The drake smirks at you. _Your only path of escape from here lies through me. We duel again. Force me to save my pets or feed me. These are your only choices._ The creature begins to cast a spell.
A member of your group flees the drake's chamber. Behind you, you hear it roar an arrogant challenge. _You are a coward? A coward of Avadon? No matter, [N]! You will return to me soon enough!_
And then you find that, while you thought you were running from the drake, you were actually running back toward it ...
The drake completes its spell. A powerful shield surrounds it. _My spellsss of protection are too strong for you. You will fight my puppetsss! Come, empty shellsss. Come and play!_
It makes a gesture, and the mindless body of Dabert lurches toward you. His movements are clumsy, but sure enough to make his blade a danger to you.
He is slow and awkward enough that he won't be able to hinder your movements, but his blade makes fast, wild arcs through the air.
Meanwhile, the drake settles back to watch the battle. It doesn't seem interested in fighting you itself, only in watching you battle for his amusement.

Zhossa mutters a word of command. The two crystal pylons in the east side of the room begin to glow faintly red. The air in the east half of the room begins to shimmer and sparkle. It's a lovely sight, enough so to tempt you into drawing closer.
Shima says, perhaps unnecessarily, _A trap. Strong defensive magic. We should stay out of there._
Nathalie looks at the sparkles with fascination. _Lovely. Also dangerous. We should stay away, lest the drake takes our minds as well._

Zhossa Mindtaker looks amused. _My first puppet is not doing well. Perhaps I should restore it._ The drake mutters a brief spell, and the damage you have done to Dabert's body is crudely repaired. _Point to you!_

_But no. That wasss no challenge for you. I think you must earn another two points to prove yourself. Perhapsss we should add another piece to the game ..._ Serlait's mindless body turns and lurches toward you, her bow in her hand.
Zhossa Mindtaker surveys the battlefield. The drake tries to appear confident, but the energy you are forcing him to expend is weakening him.
He casts the spell of restoration again. The bodies of Serlait and Dabert are made whole, though their wounds bear ugly scars and their bones knit at unnatural angles.
_No! I will not withdraw. I will not submit to Avadon. Third piece, please enter our little game. Three pieces, three more points. You can try to earn them, but you will fail!_
Blade Lundy turns and moves to attack. You look him in the eye, hoping to see some sign of the brave soldier he was. You see no humanity left there.

Your wounds have barely pierced Zhossa Mindtaker's protective spells. The drake looks at the scratch on his foreleg with annoyance. _You attack me as well? Are your other foesss not enough for you? Well, if you want me to join the fray, I will grant your wish for a time ..._

Zhossa Mindtaker notes that one of the warriors is highly damaged. _Ahssss ... Soon, my plaything's body will be too damaged to function. I cannot have thisss. A point to you ..._ The drake expends some of its energy on a powerful healing spell. The soldier's damaged flesh crudely knits together.
The drake seems to breathe more heavily after this effort. Its magical protections might be strong, but there are other ways to wear a foe down ...

Zhossa utters a word of command, releasing the power stored within the pylons in the east side of the room. They pulse with a final burst of energy, filling the east side of the room with bright, hypnotic sparkles of light. Everyone touched by them feels confused.
Zhossa Mindtaker has started to look truly annoyed. It waves a claw. The three soldiers drop to the ground like puppets with the strings cut. Their minds gone, they are all finally allowed to die.
The drake says, _I see we are evenly matched. Too close in strength for my comfort. If I fight you myself, it will be with better oddsss than these._
Then the creature, seemingly unconcerned by your presence, turns and walks toward the gate to the north.
Nathalie watches the creature leave with alarm. _What are you doing? Stop that beast before it escapes!_

The drake reaches the closed steel gate. He walks up to it and then through it, passing through the bars as if they aren't real. And they might not be real, though they look and feel real enough to you.
Zhossa Mindtaker turns and looks at you through the gate. _You were a worthy foe. Quite amusing. Now I will flee to the deep woodsss. Hunt me if you will. I hope we will never meet again._
Then, as Nathalie cries out in impotent rage, the drake turns and disappears into the shadows. Your mind starts to clear. This pit has been cleared of enemies, though at a great cost.
Then the drake turns and disappears into the shadows. Your mind starts to clear. This pit has been cleared of enemies, though at a great cost.
Maddened Infernal
You hear a familiar howling to the east.
Stalking Wolf
You hear more howling to the east. The sound of the battle is drawing hunters.
Infernal Ghlass
The demon steps out of its magic circle. As it howls in agony, it begins to hunt you down.
The demon flings another imp at you.
The demon summons another imp.

Earthshaker Demon

Imp Stalker

The wandering woodsman sees you nearby. He looks nervous.
The wandering woodsman stops at this camp. When he sees you standing nearby, he sits down and gnaws on some dried meat.
The wandering woodsman stops at this camp. He doesn't notice you standing nearby. He looks around the camp for something. Not seeing it, he prepares to move on.
Zhossa Mindtaker
A member of your group somehow wanders back to where the drake is lurking.
Zhossa mutters a word of command. The pylons in the east half of the room start to glow red.
Zhossa mutters a word of command. The pylons in the west half of the room start to glow red.
Zhossa mutters a word of command. The pylons release their energy, which fills the east half of the room.
Zhossa mutters a word of command. The pylons release their energy, which fills the west half of the room.
Zhossa Mindtaker expends some of his limited energy to heal one of his puppets. The drake is visibly weakened. He gasps, 'That's a point for you.'
Cultist Audric
Kellem Raider
Audric summons a shade. It immediately starts moaning.

Welcome, Hand.
What can I do for you?
Stay out of my chambers.
Excuse this humble dwelling.
I broke no laws.
I live a quiet life.
I want to be left alone.
Sorry for all the spiders.
Avoid the north passage.
The west way in is best.
Stay with us.
We have done well.
We must be off.
One of the demonic defenders is surrounded with a reflective shield.
One of the demonic defenders sprouts a shield of thorns.
One of the demonic defenders creates a powerful magical shield.
The brigands decide that you must have gotten away. They turn back and return to their vigil.
The brigands who haven't found you yet decide that you must have gotten away. They turn back and return to their vigil.
Following Monitor Shigaz's directions, you finally reach a remote region of the western Beraza Woods. It's a wild, shadowy tangle, not far from the border of Holklanda.
The road here is more of a path, left by hunters, woodsmen, lost merchants, and the occasional bandit. At this end of the road, as promised, you see Monitor Shigaz.
He sits by a small fire, cooking a pair of squirrels. When he sees you, he waves you forward. For this mission, he is completely alone in the woods.
You enter a large clearing. There is a tower in the center. It is short, squat, and made from huge, rough logs. Construction materials and beds full of fresh herbs surround the structure.
It is eerily cool and quiet in this clearing. And still. Nobody is visible. There are large, sticky clumps of webs stuck to the walls of the tower, but no other clues to whom you might find inside.
In this secluded clearing, you find a tower in the process of construction. Trees are being cut down, shaped into huge, crude logs, and built into a rough but stable structure.
What gets your attention, however, is the nature of the workers. They are not woodsmen, but stone constructs. Living statues that efficiently and tirelessly shape the logs and build the tower.
There is nobody visible out here who is actually alive. If the controller of the living statues is around, he or she must be inside.

The Beraza Woods is constantly patrolled by brave woodsmen, who look for safe areas to set up camp, cut down trees, and carry out wood for Holklanda and Kellemderiel. Several such workers had a large encampment here.
However, they were forced to abandon it, at least a year ago. Several of the buildings have collapsed, and refuse and signs of animal infestation are everywhere.
When you step through the concealed passage, you are immediately surrounded by a thick miasma of foul odors. Sweat. Rotting garbage. Burning meat.
You can't be sure who lives ahead, but this smells an awful lot like the ogre warrens of the Jhereth Deeps. Ogres have a smell all their own, the reek of filth and neglect.
You emerge into a large cavern, full of mist. To the north, you see a lake. And, beyond that, you see the bandits.

They have built a small fortification at the north end of this huge cave. Most of the brigands are camped directly in front of it. A lot of them, armed and drunk. You can hear their singing and carousing from here. Alas, they are not too drunk to overwhelm you should they detect your presence.

As you watch, they send scouts to the south, circling around the lake and watching for intruders. Happily, the sentries stop before they reach you here. Most of the enemy stays at the front gates of their lair. Entering through the front promises to be very dangerous.
The cavern you are in stretches out of sight to the northeast. There appear to be fewer guards in that direction.
You circle around the east side of the large cavern. To the north, a cramped tunnel leads into the darkness away from the brigands.
As you scout out the tunnel, for a moment you think you can see movement in the shadows. Someone watching you. Then there is a flash of movement, and whoever was there is gone.

At last, you slip into the lair of the brigands. It is far nicer than most such lairs. They have been here for some time, settling in and getting comfortable. The delicious smell of stew hangs in the corridors.
A rune has been etched into the floor here. Right now, it is only a symbol. It hasn't been enchanted with defensive magic yet, but you walk around it carefully all the same.
This is a dangerous and well-prepared band of miscreants. If you can't break them now, they will only grow stronger.
There are no human tracks in this corridor. The air grows warmer as you head north. The reek of sulfur is in the air.
As you listen carefully, you hear deep breathing to the north, alternating with the occasional growl. Something big and nasty is lurking not far ahead.
You start to feel very alone. You wonder if the creature ahead might be unrelated to your mission and best left alone.
You try to talk to the construct. It doesn't respond. You stand in its way. It walks around you. It is a mindless creation, made only to cut down trees, shape logs, and place them.
Incantor Manon
Supplicants welcome.
Thieves are burned.
This old sign once had one word on it, but most of the paint has flaked away. Only the first three letters of the word remains: _Her_

There is a crude altar in the cave to the south. Actually, it wasn't crude once. It was lovely and marble. Then the ogres broke it loose from wherever it was before and dragged it here. Now it is crumbling, tilted to one side, and covered with gruesome stains.
A huge ogre shaman stands behind the altar. He wields a bloody dagger in one hand and a horn in the other. Several of his thugs stand behind him.
When you enter, he points at you and roars, _Hrrrah! The intruder! Seize the little creature and bring it to my altar!_
That's odd. Your keen senses are sure that someone is standing near you. You can hear breath, very faintly, and you're almost sure you can detect a presence in the corner.
Then you hear the soft sound of footprints, running off to the east, and the presence is gone.
Once again, you feel the presence, lurking behind the desk. It seems like a human or humanoid, not too large, clearly frightened. It runs away again, though you aren't sure in what direction.

You would never have detected it if you didn't know that there was something to watch for. Someone is hidden by the north wall. You can hear its frightened breath, and there are footprint-shaped disturbances on the floor where it is standing.
You leap forward, cornering it. Two things happen simultaneously. The man becomes visible. And he screams.
Now you can see him clearly. He is a thin, pale man, sickly and unwashed. He wears the robes of a mage, but they are torn and filthy. He is as rough and run down as the tower he lives in.
He stares at you, panting, not saying a word. His hands are out, though, ready to work a spell if necessary to defend himself.
Orian falls to the ground dead. The moment he hits the ground, a pouch hanging from his belt bursts into flames. A clever bit of magic to keep secrets from warriors of the Pact.
At any rate, there is one less spy in your lands. A good day's work.

This nest is particularly large and comfortable, as such things go. It has been padded with bits of fur and branches brought with great difficulty from the surface. There are also many gobbets of meat, waiting to be consumed.
And then, at the bottom of the nest, you see why the drake put so much effort into it. There is a lone egg there, a hardy, leathery thing, waiting to hatch and add another drake to the world.
You recognize that this reddish ovoid has considerable value. You wrap it in fur and put it into your pack. Its warmth radiates out through the padding.
You inspect the small, wooden doorway at the top of the stairs. It is held shut by a glowing padlock, covered with runes. You are sure there was no such thing there when you entered.
The lock is slightly translucent. You realize that it might not, in fact, be real. More of a magical trap, holding form for a period of time. You have no idea how long that might be.
You take the crystal key from your pouch and touch it to the padlock. There is a tinkling sound and a puff of smoke. The lock disappears.
One of the wandering brigands wobbles unsteadily around a clump of stalagmites and sees you. He has a blade in one hand and a horn in the other.
When he realizes that you are an intruder and not a hallucination, he starts to raise the horn to his lips.
The brigand lets out a single, long note with the horn. You instantly hear shouting from the entrance to the bandit camp. The thugs have been roused from their drunken vigil.
They leave their camp, prepared to hunt down the intruders. Finding a place to hide far from their camp seems very tempting.
In the distance, you can hear all hunters who haven't found you yet decide that you must have escaped. Chastened, they return to guarding the front gates.
Harua is tending to Shigaz's wounds. _I am glad you are well, and I am grateful that you have destroyed the leader of the bandits. For now, however, I must tend to my brother here._
The passage north ends in this low, warm cavern, littered with bones, refuse, and the remaining bits of a treasure hoard.
There is a drake here. An old, withered specimen, half blind. However, the fires within it still burn hot, and it has no fear of any tasty morsel that wanders into its lair ...
The drake looks at its nest and lets out a furious wail. Then it turns and attacks you, the intensity of its attacks doubled.
Your blows make the drake wince in pain. It adopts a defensive stance and mutters a spell. A reflective shield appears in front of it, and long, sharp spines grow out of its skin.

As you carefully thread your way down one of the Beraza Wood's winding paths, you realize that someone is following you. It's not hard. He is running, breathing hard, and making no effort to conceal himself.

Then he starts to catch up with you, and you see that he wears the garb of a shadowwalker, which is odd, considering how stealthy he isn't being. It is the Wayfarer, and he pants heavily as he runs up to you.
You notice that Monitor Shigaz moves quietly to one side. He doesn't want to overhear any secret Avadon business.
The Wayfarer says, _I missed you before. I arrived at Castle Vebeaux too late to find you. Happily, your tracks were easy to follow._
How did you know where I went?
_Your fame and influence grows, whether you know it or not. Many are watching you now, from a distance. Waiting to see just how much potential you have, and how it can be used._
I wish that you had missed me.
Your insult is barely noticed. _And yet, here I am. Though you might not wish it to be so, we have business, you and I._
_The papers in the titan fortress. Were you able to find and destroy them, as I asked?_
I'm glad you found me.
He nods. _It is good to continue a profitable relationship, yes? And we have a bit of business to conclude._
Why, again, did you wish them to be destroyed?
The Wayfarer smiles enigmatically, his poise slowly returning. _Because someone offered a payment for it to be done. That is all._
I did not destroy them.

The Wayfarer lets out an irritated sigh. _You will never gain wealth and influence like that. You think Redbeard's missions will provide you power and security? No. It is how you use the power that Avadon gives you that matters._
_But no matter. I have another opportunity for you. A chance to make a fair sum for a moment's work._
I found and destroyed them.

The Wayfarer nods, most pleased. _Then I have a proper reward for you._ He takes a bow from his shoulder and hands it to you. _Not my chosen weapon, of course, but beautifully made. It will serve you well._
_And your good fortune does not end there. I have another opportunity for you. A chance to make a fair sum for a moment's work._
I don't want any more offers of work from you. Leave me.
He opens his mouth and starts to speak. Then he gives you an ugly grin. _Well ... I was not raised to go where I wasn't wanted. You are clearly a loyal servant of Avadon. Propriety, and all that._
_I will offer you no more work. At least, not the minor trifles I have troubled you with up to now._
Don't contact me again.
_Oh, don't say that. There will come a time, very soon, when you will want to hear everything I have to say. Until then, I go where I will, Hand of Avadon._
Before you can ask him to elaborate, he is gone. He turns and walks quickly into the trees.
You have something of value to offer me?
_Oh, yes. There will come a time, very soon, when ... when ..._ He chuckles. _But why spoil the surprise? You will see. Until then, I have much to prepare._
I am listening.
_There is a merchant doing her business near Castle Vebeaux. Our old friend Calantha. An enterprising soul, loyal to the Pact, respectful of Avadon. And annoyed by competition._

_However, another merchant, Charon, has caused her some trouble. She wants to be rid of him for good. A simple word to the authorities, from a Hand of Avadon, will achieve this with little effort and no risk._
_Do this, and Calantha will pay you very well._
What is Charon guilty of?
_Guilty? Are we not all guilty of something? Just tell the commander in the Castle that Charon has committed some crime. You are a Hand of Avadon. He will believe you. He has no choice._
Is that ethical?
_Ethical? What a strange concept. Avadon does not care for ethics. It is above it. You think this will be the first time a Hand condemned an 'innocent' for profit?_
And Calantha will pay me?
_Of course. She knows what you are capable of if she does not._
I will do it.
The Wayfarer nods. _I thought you might. Such power as yours exists only to be used, yes? When the work is done, talk to Calantha for your reward. Now I must be off. Much to do. Much to prepare._
And then he is gone. He turns and walks quickly into the trees.
I can't do that.

The Wayfarer nods. _What a strange ... You have a conscience. How interesting. Avadon has not torn that from you. Yet. But such power as yours exists only to be used, yes? Should you change your mind, the task is still available to you. Now I must be off. Much to do. Much to prepare._
You cautiously approach the mage, who is cowering by the wall behind the table. You have to be careful ... Even a dirty, tired, unwashed wizard can be very dangerous.
Happily, he doesn't seem hostile. He says, in a wavering voice, _You ... You have found me. I ... I am Herenus. I keep to myself. I want to be alone._
His name and accent mark him as being from the Tawon Empire, the strongest and wealthiest of the Farlands. It is strange that someone from outside the Pact would settle here.
Herenus stays in his position by the north wall, watching you closely and shifting from one foot to the other. He occasionally looks self-consciously at the disrepair of his tower.
You are from the Tawon Empire?
He runs his fingers through his greasy hair. _How did ... I ... Yes, I suppose it is obvious enough. I am not of the Pact, but I mean no harm. I am no spy. I don't even ... even go outside._
_I just have a small tower. Just want to hide here._
Did you build this tower?
_I did. Well, my constructs did. One of the many resources of a skilled mage. I have stolen no land, broken no Pact laws. I am humble._
Your tower is a mess.
_I ... Yes. It is. It was once a disguise. To make it look unused. To hide me. But, as time went on, the corruption went from being a ruse to being ... all too real._
Why are you hiding?
_It is a private matter. I have broken no Pact laws. You don't need to trouble yourself with punishing me._
_Tawon politics. As you have been told by others, no doubt._
Why have you come here?
_Why? Why come to the Beraza Woods? It ... It's been a long time. Been here for years. Alone. Mostly alone._
_I ... I fled the Tawon Empire. I am in exile here. I have broken no Pact laws. I only want to be left alone._
Why did you flee?
_Because I would have been killed if I did not. And you know something funny? I am not sure I remember what I did. I angered someone in a different house, I suppose. Yes, it's funny._
He looks down at the filthy, unswept floor. _Funny._
Do you ever think you will return?
_Oh, of course. If I ever tire of life, someone there will be happy to end mine for me._
Are you ever troubled out here?
_Oh no. Even the most foolish bandit knows to stay out of a mage's tower, occupied or not._
Are your services available for hire?
_You mean ... For magic? Magic services?_ He lets out a pained cackle. _You would have to be very foolhardy to rely on a spell of mine. I am very out of practice._
Your clan has a golden throne.

At first, you don't think he heard you. Then, slowly, he looks up at you, his eyes showing a clarity that was absent before. _What? I am recalled? My house? It calls me back? It ... So long. So very long._
_I did not think it would ever happen. But ... Look at me! I am filthy! Shamed! Out of practice! Can I ... Can I ever show my face there again?_
Anything is better than staying here.
He nods. _I ... agree. It will take work to restore myself. I have ... decayed during my time in the woods._.
_Tell my house that I will return to them in time. Thank you, Pact warrior. You have done me a great service._
Actually, I am evicting you. Get out of Pact lands, Farlander.

Herenus looks somewhat stunned. _But I have broken no laws of the Pact. I ... But there are no laws for Farlanders, are there? I must do what you say. I only ask some time to restore myself, and I will leave._
_Tell my house that I will return to them in time. Thank you for bringing me this news._
You're right. You're a mess. Stay here.

He nods. _I am ashamed to admit it, but it is true. I will remain in exile here. Now, however, I will sleep better knowing that murderers are not always at my door. Thank you, Pact warrior. You have done me a service._
You still won't return to the Tawon Empire?
_I have fallen too far. Been shamed too much. Too dirty, too unwashed. I can't face my house like this. Maybe ... someday. But not now._
You are still here?
_It is taking time to restore myself. Remember what I must know. Learn the situation in the Tawon. Bathe. I will be gone soon, I promise you._
As you leave Shigaz's camp, Shima starts looking around cautiously. He seems unusually nervous.
(Ignore him.)
You walk along silently, waiting for Shima to calm down. He doesn't.
_We are going farther west. Closer to Holklanda. I am an exile. It makes me worried._
What will happen to you if you return to Holklanda?
_Nothing. I am a Hand of Avadon. None would dare raise a hand against me. But, then again, that is where my enemy is._
But what are you looking for?
_The Honored Forge. That clan is the enemy of my family, and of me. If they learn I am close, they might be tempted to ... to finish the job they started. So I will be watchful._
Well, we shall stay alert.
_Of course. I am never anything else. I have lost too many people close to me to be otherwise._ And then he shakes his head and is silent.
Shima watches the woods as you pass. He seems dissatisfied. He whispers to you, _This assault ... It is not properly done._
He speaks very quietly. _Shigaz is a strong warrior. He is patient and diplomatic. But his skill as a shadowwalker, it ... I would stay very alert._
What is he doing wrong?

_Moving too far out in the open. Not enough reconnaissance. Not quiet enough. I ... I will show some restraint in my criticism. We shall see what happens. Perhaps there is no need to worry._ He walks on silently.
I will be cautious.
Shima nods. _As will I. That is all I ask._ He walks on silently.
Nathalie walks through the woods, strangely pleased with herself. It is odd, considering that the bandits she is hunting are from Kellemderiel.
She looks over at you. _A good day for hunting, yes?_
It is.
She nods. _A good day to hunt thugs and scum, and, if they think being Kellem will protect them, I will show them how foolish they are._
She walks on, humming very quietly to herself.
And you aren't bothered by our target?

_Of course not. There are some loyal patriots in my homeland who refuse to hunt Kellem, no matter how coarse and criminal they are. But me? They are brigands and scum, and I see them as my rightful prey._

The inside of this wooden tower is actually quite warm and cozy. There is only one resident, sitting on a throne and staring into a magic circle. There is a wisp of blue light floating over the runes.

When you approach, he waves his hand. The light disappears. Then he turns to you and smiles. _Greetings, visitor. I am Incantor Manon. It is rare that I receive visitors in my humble abode. And who are you?_
Incantor Manon lounges in his throne. He idly waves his hand back and forth, as tiny flames dance on and between his fingers. Most wizards don't show off their powers quite so blatantly.
I am [N], Hand of Avadon.
_So I thought. I know of you. Even out here in my remote exile, I do my best to learn what is happening back in dear old Castle Vebeaux._
_But I'm sure you are here for a reason. Perhaps some of my services might be of value to you. I need to keep busy, out here on my lonesome._
I am a soldier of the Pact, hunting in the woods.
_Really? I thought you might be [N], Hand of Avadon. You see, even out here in my remote exile, I do my best to learn what is happening back in dear old Castle Vebeaux._
It is none of your business why I am here.

He frowns. _Oh, but it is, intruder in my home. I see politeness is wasted on you. You are [N], Hand of Avadon. You see, even out here in my remote exile, I do my best to learn what is happening back in dear old Castle Vebeaux._
_But I'm sure, despite your rudeness, that you are here for a reason. Perhaps some of my services might be of value to you. I need to keep busy, out here on my lonesome._
Why are you living out here?
_Oh, Kellemderiel politics. Steeped in tradition. The fortresses. The dukes. The rivalry. The assassins._
_Suffice it to say that sometimes, under certain circumstances, people can say things that are unsafe, and thus they need to retire from the field for a time._
Under certain circumstances?
_Yes, circumstances such as being terribly, terribly drunk at a castle banquet._
Say things that are unsafe?
_Yes, such as that one's beloved duke's efforts to make peace with the Holklandans are doomed to failure._
You really think that?

_Me? Doubt the duke? Of course not. I've learned that lesson. Others may think that the Holklandans will only take Gryfyn's overtures as a sign of weakness and demand more and more concessions in return for nothing._
_But no. Not me._
Retire from the field?
_Yes, in the sense that I have fled Castle Vebeaux, showing my shame and contrition to Duke Gryfyn and keeping him from needing to have me killed._
Tell me about your tower.
_It is humble, but it will grow in time. My constructs will soon make it appropriate for a wizard of the Kellem, even an exiled one._
_You are welcome here, Hand. I only ask one thing._
_Stay out of the upper level. Those are my private chambers._
What services do you offer?
_Nothing, not to someone who thinks nothing of invading my private quarters. Rudeness is offensive to the Kellem._
_Little, as yet. I am still establishing myself here. However, I do have some crafts available that might prove handy to a Hand of Avadon._
Incantor Manon is able to craft a variety of useful magical items. Happily, he still has a few of them in stock.
I don't need anything.
_Then I bid you farewell. I must return to work on my humble tower. Please return when you need my aid._
I am looking for an exiled mage named Herenus.
_Really? You are looking for that crazed old coot? I am surprised. But yes, he is near here. In fact, his tower is a short journey to the northwest. You might find it difficult to find him, though._
What do you know of him?
_As little as possible. When people in our line of work grow unstable, they are dangerous. Best just to keep a distance._
Why will it be hard to find him?
_He covers himself with illusions to hide himself from assassins. Whether the killers are real or only exist in his mind, well, I wouldn't say._
_Still, if you search the tower thoroughly, you might find him. To see past the illusion, you will have to walk close to wherever he is hiding._
I bring word from Castle Vebeaux. You can return.
He jumps up from the throne. _Really? I can leave this miserable hardwood hole and return to civilization? Thank you for this message. I am most pleased._
Why do you think you are being called back?

_I don't know. Maybe Duke Gryfyn has forgiven me. Or he has seen the error of his ways and no longer will strive for peace with Holklanda. Or maybe he wants me close so that he can have me jailed. Or killed._
_It doesn't matter. Anything is worth not having to be in this dank shack any longer. Excuse me. I must prepare to depart._

_Oh, yes. One's return to society must be planned. The proper clothes. The proper hair. The right level of court gossip. Oh, I will return soon. But I will enter the gates of Castle Vebeaux as a true wizard of Kellemderiel, not some bumpkin with pinecones in his hair!_
There are several woodsmen sitting around this fire. Dirty, scowling, heavily-armed woodsmen. Along with hatchets and saws, they also have a variety of blades and bows, all of them close at hand.
When you get close, they inspect you. One of them grumbles, _We are comfortable here, soldier, and breaking no laws. You can move on now._

The man who spoke for the group continues to do so. He points to the south. _Our yard is there. We spend our days cutting down trees. Sawing them into boards. Carting them west and east. We work the woods. Nothing else._
Why are you all armed?
The woodsman snorts. _Have you seen all of the brigands out here? And lizards, and giant spiders? We want to earn our bread, and we don't want to get killed doing it._
I'd like to know something about these woods.
_It has trees. We want to cut them down. That's all we know._
I am a Hand of Avadon. You will show me respect.

The woodsman is painfully unimpressed. _Avadon? What does Avadon care for trees, or for the people who cut them down? We are doing nothing wrong. Just sitting and cooking our daily meal. Leave us, Hand._
Then he turns away. Doesn't seem to be anything else to do here.
I will leave you then.
The woodsman nods. _Much appreciated. We meant no offense. We only want to keep to ourselves._

There is a grimy woodsman sitting by this fire, cooking a pot of thin soup. A pair of implausibly huge wolves sit to either side, obediently waiting to be fed some scraps. This man must be very skilled with animals, to have such massive beasts sit quietly at his beck and call.
Then one of the beasts snarls at you. The man looks over his shoulder at you. You recognize each other instantly.
