It is Orian, the spy for the Tawon Empire you discovered in the woods to the east. His flight into the Beraza Woods has been hard on him. He is thinner and paler than he was when you saw him last. Of course, he has also picked up a pair of formidable pets.
So, Orian, I have found you.
He spits into the fire. His wolves, alert to his distress, let out a pair of deep and alarming snarls. _So you did. The charms my employers gave me hid me and carried me far, but not far enough._
Your employers?
_Don't go being coy, Hand of Avadon. I am tired, but not foolish. You will never learn from my lips who sent me here._
Nice wolves.
He bends down to scratch one of them behind the ear. _Death and Destruction, they are called. Sent to protect me if it is needed._
You are a spy for the Farlands.
_And you will punish me, is that it? You will haul me back to Avadon? Have all my thoughts sucked away in your dungeons? That is what you wish? It will never happen, Hand._
I will let you go.

Orian shakes his head. _You know I am here. That is too much. I have instructions. All Hands I and my fellows meet must be killed. Many of your kind have already fallen. I will happily add to the tally._
_Slay the Hand, my pets! Attack!_ As the wolves lunge forward, Orian mutters a word of command. A ring on his finger begins to glow.
Come back to Avadon with me. It is the only way you will survive.

_You have it backwards. It is the Hands who need to worry about survival. I and my fellows have orders to kill any of your kind we encounter. Many of your kind have already fallen. I will happily add to the tally._
No, you will pay for your treason here and now. (Attack.)
Orian starts to taunt you farther, only to realize that defending himself from the incoming attack might be the wiser course of action.
He shouts, _Slay the Hand, my pets! Attack!_ As the wolves lunge forward, Orian mutters a word of command. A ring on his finger begins to glow.
You approach Shigaz, who is sitting calmly by the fire. You look around for other guards or shadowwalkers, perhaps hiding in the shadows, only to realize that Shigaz is here alone.

He nods to you. _Hello again, [N]. I am glad to see that you have arrived safely. I have already scouted this area. I have narrowed down the number of locations where the Kellem bandits might be hiding._
_Tell me when you are ready, and the hunt can commence._
Shigaz sits by his fire. He is trying to seem calm, but you can sense how agitated he is. He is eager to begin the hunt. _Well, [N]? Are you ready?_
You are here alone?
Shigaz nods. _After the difficulties last time, I did not wish to fight alongside soldiers from Kellemderiel. They did not trust me before. I didn't think they would trust me now._
_But, understand, I still value their sacrifice._
Do you think you are strong enough?
_I am a shadowwalker. We prefer the way of the small force. Stealth. Planning. A fast, lethal assault. It is dangerous, true, but I am comfortable._
Why would they still not trust you?
_Because we are hunting citizens of Kellemderiel. Thugs and brigands, true, but still their kinsmen. I do not want them at my back when the killing starts._
How did your superiors react to the deaths of the Kellem soldiers?

_They were ... surprised. They did not want to give our rivals credit for courage, but, after what happened, they had no choice. It might have even convinced them to take Duke Gryfyn's desire for peace more seriously._
Tell me about these woods.
_They are not so different from what you have seen before. Dark, shadowy, and full of pests._
_You are welcome to take some time to explore before we begin our hunt._
Anything of interest?
_Yes, two wooden towers, one south of here and one to the northwest. The one to the south is newly built. The other seems abandoned._
_I only investigated long enough to verify that the bandits we hunt are not there._

_There is a clan of bandits from Kellemderiel hiding somewhere in this area. They are dangerous and accomplished raiders. We Holklandans have long wished for them to be destroyed. We even went to Hanvar's Council._
_At last, today, we have the chance to be rid of them._
Why has it been so difficult to hunt them?

_Because the brigands are from Kellemderiel, but they only raid Holklanda. We Holklandans have long wanted to send a force to hunt them down, but the Kellem said such an incursion would be seen as an act of war._
_So we have suffered their attacks, until now._
Who went to Hanvar's Council?
_My superiors, Holklandans of great repute, went to the leaders of the Pact to ask for help. The council was as weak and feckless as always. No relief was received._
Why can they finally be hunted?
_Because Duke Gryfyn gave me permission. That is all it took, one word from a person of great influence. Now I will act, before he changes his mind._
Wait here. I wish to investigate on my own.
Monitor Shigaz nods. _Understood. I approve. Scouting ahead and understanding the lay of the land is the way of the shadowwalker. However, I ask that you make haste. I am eager to begin the hunt._
_Are you sure? Once the shadowwalker acts, it is with speed and lethal intent. Things will move very quickly._
_And, this time, I am hoping that you don't abandon me in the middle of the hunt._
Come to think of it, I'd like to scout a bit more.
Shigaz rises and kicks dirt over his small fire. He has few weapons and supplies to gather. _Then we are off. Stay close. Be ready. It is time at last._
He strides off to the north.

Shigaz bends down and closely inspects this totem. _Only recently placed. A fresh trophy. However, these are ogre markings. They must be hiding near here. Not our targets. Let us move on._ He leaves, continuing to the north.
You try to talk to Shigaz, but he shakes his head. _Just remain quiet and stay close,_ he whispers. _The hunt has begun. It ends with death or victory._

Monitor Shigaz fearlessly approaches the group of woodsmen sitting around this fire. Dirty, scowling, heavily-armed woodsmen. Along with hatchets and saws, they also have a variety of blades and bows, all of them close at hand.
Something about them makes Shigaz suspicious. He immediately starts to question them. Who they are. What they are doing here. And, most importantly, why they are so armed.
The woodsmen, all from Kellemderiel, bristle at this questioning. The conversation rapidly becomes heated.
Shigaz, let's go.
Shigaz ignores you. He seems to notice something. He points at a glove on one of their hands. _Blood._
(Wait and watch.)
Shigaz and the woodsmen stare at each other grimly across the fire. Then Shigaz seems to notice something. He points at a glove on the hand of one of the burly men. _Blood._
Everyone turns and looks at the woodsman's leather glove. It has a long slash on the back and is heavily stained with dried blood. However, the man's hand is unharmed.
He snorts, suddenly nervous. _What? Cut myself with an axe. Happens out here. We work hard. Not that a Holklandan would understand._
Their leader steps forward. _We have to work to feed our families. We need to go. We can't waste any more time._

Shigaz pulls out a pouch. He shakes it, and you can hear the coins jingle inside. _Simply return with me to Castle Vebeaux. Only a day's journey, and, once you have answered the questions of the Kellem there, I will pay you far more than you would have earned._
_It is a fair offer, and I ..._

But then the armed men draw their weapons and jump to their feet. They are not innocent woodsmen after all. You have little time before they attack to wonder what happened to the owners of this camp. You doubt that it was pleasant ...
Monitor Shigaz looks at the ruined camp. _Thugs and killers. That is all they are. And yet, this was only a small group. We still need to find their hideout._ He leaves to the south.
Monitor Shigaz returns to the ruined camp. _Still nobody here. Onward._
Monitor Shigaz inspects the abandoned logging camp. He sniffs the air. He kneels and looks at the tracks on the ground. He opens the door of the sole intact building and peeks inside.
Finally, closing the door behind him, he turns to you. _Truly abandoned. Only rats live here now. Come on. We are fast running out of places to search._

Monitor Shigaz looks around this remote valley. There don't seem to be any tracks, but a ruined cart catches his attention. _Interesting,_ he says. _Weathered by the sun and rain, true, but not like I would expect._
He walks to the south.

Monitor Shigaz looks around this nondescript glade. Then he checks to make sure that you are still behind him. _Keep close. I have already searched this area well, but I was waiting to explore the next area until I had your support._
He continues to the south.
Shigaz stops at the cliff wall. He raps it with a mailed knuckle, listens carefully, smiles, and begins to search the stone.
It doesn't take long for him to find what he is after. He pushes in a stone outcropping, and a section of the wall slides away.
He turns to you, unable to conceal a grin. _Well, [N], we are here. No guards. We are unexpected. You and I can strike quickly, with the advantage of surprise._
_But, [N], only you and I. No others._
What?
_I want a very small force for this. You and me. All of your companions must stay behind._
Sevilin does not care for this. _I finally redeem myself, and I am expected to play the coward again? I do not wish to return to Avadon while the battle continues._
Shima nods. _I do not like turning away from a fight, but I will respect a fellow shadowwalker's wishes._
Jenell looks worried. _This is not our way. Wyldrylm warriors do not leave a friend unprotected._
Nathalie is disgusted. _What? You don't trust me, Shigaz? Well, I would rather die than spend yet more time rotting in Avadon while others get to fight._
Shigaz looks embarrassed. _I would not say. At least, not at this point. However, I will not be dissuaded._
I am a Hand of Avadon. I choose who fights at my side.
_But I believe your orders are clear. I am in command of this assault, and I decide how it proceeds. I am sure Redbeard told you something similar._
I will respect your wishes.
_I thank you, Hand of Avadon. I meant no offense to any of your companions._
This is a foolish decision.
_Perhaps. And yet, it is my foolish decision to make. Come, quickly, before the bandits discover that they have been found._
Proceed. I will follow.
Monitor Shigaz nods, gives you a brief salute, turns, and walks through the gap. A moment later, he has slipped down the stairs, not making a sound.
I will not continue, then.
_But you must. It is Redbeard's command, and, if you let me die, he will not be pleased. Enough chat. Hurry._
Then he turns and walks through the gap. A moment later, he has slipped down the stairs, not making a sound.
Monitor Shigaz is waiting for you in the shadows of this crude storeroom. Piles of stolen food and supplies are everywhere.
He turns to you. _I must apologize. I did not wish to send your companions away, but I feel that I had no choice._
It's all right. They talk too much.
_It is not the noise that worries me. It is their ... reliability. Their loyalty. That is what I question._
They can be unreliable.
_Yes. After hunting down the drake, I learned all I could of you and your friends. Their loyalty and reliability have all been ... questionable. At times._
_And yet they were all gathered in one place. Very odd. But no matter. It can be pondered later._
He looks at the closed gate to the east. _Let us go north. That seems to be our only choice._ He walks quickly, staying in the shadows. When he is still, he is almost invisible.
It was an unwise decision.
_This may be true. They are skilled and experienced, after all. However, as strong as they are, their ... their loyalty might be questioned._
Why did you do that?
_Do not think I meant any offense to them. I'm sure that they are skilled and experienced. However, as strong as they are, their ... their loyalty might be questioned._
_I am not a fool. After hunting down the drake, I learned all I could of you and your friends. Their loyalty and reliability have all been ... questionable. At times._
I will not hear the loyalty of my companions questioned!

_You will not? You refuse to hear truth? Well, then judge them by their actions. Their words. Their occasional abandonment of you. Then perhaps you will see why I did not want them to watch my back. But no matter._
Sevilin turns to you. _Know that I am only being driven away against my will. I wish you good hunting, [N], and I hope to see you safely returned to Avadon._ He goes upstairs.
Shima says, _It is Shigaz's right to choose how large his force should be, but I feel that his decision is unwise, shadowwalker or no. Good luck to you._
_And please, if you see anyone from the accursed Honored Forge clan, I need to know._ He nods, turns, and climbs the stairs.
Jenell turns back to the stairway. _I hate anyone and anything that stinks of cowardice, but I am relieved to not have to explore yet another dank pit. Safe hunting, [N]._ She goes back upstairs.
Being sent home before the fighting starts leaves Nathalie so angry that she can barely talk. She nods to you and climbs back up the stairs. She doesn't even honor Shigaz with a glance.
Monitor Shigaz stops at the entry to the room to the north and holds up a hand. _Heh,_ he says. _Clumsy._
For a moment, you aren't sure what he is referring to. Then the bandits step out of their hiding places. It is an ambush, but Shigaz doesn't seem at all frightened.

Shigaz looks at the closed gate to the east. _Unfortunate. It blocks our path, but at least it means that none of the thugs were able to run and alert their fellows. We will need to double back and look for a different route in._
He leaves to the south.

You check on Monitor Shigaz. He is still alive, but his burns and broken ribs have left him in a good deal of pain. He whispers, _Find a way to get out of here. We have to open the door out before they find us._
Then he closes his eyes and silently meditates, trying to maintain consciousness with pure force of will.
Monitor Shigaz looks to the east. The gate that was closed before is now open. Then he looks at the door at the top of the stairs.
It is closed and held shut with a padlock. The lock glows slightly and is covered with runes. Shigaz says several words of an adult nature meant to clearly convey his annoyance.
_A trap. Certainly not the sort I suspected._
What sort of trap?
_That padlock isn't real. It's a work of pure magic. I don't know what caused it to appear. It will fade in time, but that will take longer than we have._
How can we get that lock open?
_Assuming we don't want to stare at it for several hours while the bandits hunt us down? We need to find its maker. He or she will probably have some sort of key or way to dispel it._
Do the bandits know we are here?
_Doubtful. I think this was just a trap. If they knew of our presence, we would have been cornered and charged by now._
What should we do?
Monitor Shigaz looks at the open gate to the east and sighs. _We walk into the obvious ambush._
Doesn't that worry you?
_No. I am now looking forward to it. Come on, [N]. Let's show them that they have locked themselves in with a nightmare._ He walks to the east.
The path soon ends in another portcullis, this one closed. It's an old, rusty thing. It looks like you could easily bend or dislodge one of the bars, making a hole big enough to climb through.

Monitor Shigaz walks up to it and lightly raps a few of the bars with his knuckle. When he strikes the third one, the passage suddenly grows very warm. Three angry-looking red runes suddenly appear on the crossbars of the gate.
Run!
Even before the word passes your lips, Shigaz is turning to run. Several searing balls of fire flow out of the gate. Twisting, he avoids most of them, but one of them strikes the side of his chest.
(Jump back.)
As you leap away, Shigaz turns and starts to run. Several searing balls of fire flow out of the gate. Twisting, he avoids most of them, but one of them strikes the side of his chest.
Shigaz, are you all right?
He doesn't respond. He starts to stagger away from the gate, stumbling toward a corner of the passage.
(Help Shigaz.)
When you get close to Shigaz, he waves you away. He starts to stagger away from the gate, stumbling toward a corner of the passage.

Shigaz gently lowers himself to the floor, partly concealed by a large barrel, and inspects the wound. There's a nasty burn and at least a few broken ribs. He can move, slowly and with great pain, but fighting is out of the question.

He engages in a low, gasping bout of swearing, cursing the traps, whatever mage is in the brigands' hire, and his own carelessness. _Overconfident. I thought ... with a Hand here ... I was clumsy. A disgrace to shadowwalkers._
Perhaps I can heal you.
_You could ... ease my pain. Help a little. But I can't fight. Not for a while. I need ... We need to escape._
_Trap. Another trap. A mage helped the brigands. Probably still here, with our luck._
Was there a way around that trap?
_No ... Had to be set off. But ... could have done it a safer way. I admit I am not as skilled as some._
What now?

Shigaz looks over at the gate. The explosion knocked several bars loose, making it possible to slip through. _You are a Hand. You are strong enough. They are only brigands. I will hide here. Go ... Finish our task._
_Think like a shadowwalker. Hide. Stay in the shadows. They're sure to have patrols. Avoid them. Look for a way to slip farther in unseen._
I don't think I can do it.
_You are ... Hand of Avadon. If you can't save us ... we are doomed. If Hands can't save us, Lynaeus is doomed._ He waves you off. _I will hide here. Hurry. Find a way out._
With great discomfort, he slides under one of the barrels. It's not a very good hiding place, but it might keep him concealed for long enough to buy you some time.
Wait here. I will be back soon.
He nods. _You are a Hand of Avadon. I know ... know you can save us. I will hide here. Hurry. Find a way out._

This cramped cavern is full of shadows. When you get close to one of the shadows, it begins to move on its own. A Holklandan, swathed in black robes and wielding a long, curved blade, slides out of a crack in the wall.
He nods to you. _You are no brigand. I have been watching you, and I can tell. I mean you no harm. In fact, I think we are allied. I am Harua of the Honored Forge, a shadowwalker of the Holklandans._
Harua talks to you very quietly. He never steps out of the narrow crack that conceals him. If bandits discover you, he can become virtually invisible in moments.
I am [N], a Hand of Avadon.
That raises Harua's eyebrows. _I heard rumors that Hands were coming to these woods, it is true, but I did not expect to meet you. I have admiration for your kind._
I am [N], come to hunt bandits.
_Well met, then. We come with a common goal: the hunting of vermin._
Did you say you are of the Honored Forge?

Harua goes from relieved to concerned in the space of an instant. He steps out of the shadows slightly, and you can see that he is no neophyte. He is over thirty, the veteran of many missions, and his blade and razordisks show the signs of years of lethal use.
_Yes. My clan is the Honored Forge. One of the most honored and honorable of the Holklandan clans. Why do you ask?_
I have a companion named Shima. Shima Threespear.
Harua Honored Forge nods slowly _I ... I am familiar with the name. I will not deny it. I am sure he has a grudge against me, and we can address it in due time._
_For now, however, I suggest that we set aside any differences and deal with the brigands that surround us._
A shadowwalker who travels with me has a vendetta against your clan.
Harua Honored Forge nods slowly _One does not ascend in this life without attracting enemies, deserved or not. I am sorry that your friend has a grudge against me, and we can address it in due time._
Nothing. Never mind. Forget that I mentioned it.
Harua Honored Forge nods. _It is already forgotten._ But, of course, he has forgotten nothing. He is still quietly alert.
_In that case, I suggest we discuss the brigands that surround us._
I came here with a shadowwalker named Shigaz. He is wounded.
You tell Harua the tale of your arrival. _I sympathize. Shigaz sounds like he has behaved with honor, but one should have been sent who can recognize and bypass magical traps._
_He is correct that you need to find a way to escape, and quickly. However, to escape, you will need the key to the trap on the entryway. Alas, only the leader of the bandits is likely to have it._
Can you go help Shigaz?
_I regret to say that I have orders, and I must follow them. I would love nothing more than to help my brother, but, first, I must kill the mad cultist who commands these bandits._
Tell me about their leader.
_I have caught but one glimpse of him, when he emerged to bark orders at his servant. He came out swathed in robes. Not a mage, however, but one of the Pact's many secretive cultists._
_Still skilled in magic, of course, and dangerous. Though, I am sure, not a threat to a Hand of Avadon._

With palpable regret, Harua removes a key from his pouch and hands it to you. _Believe me when I say that this was very difficult for me to obtain, and the thug I stole it from spent long, painful hours in the stocks._
_Go west from here, and that key will help you to slip into the bandits' lair unnoticed. Once inside, I suggest you not go south. That is where most of the guards are._
Will you accompany me?
_I work alone. I only ever work alone. However, if you die, I promise to take full advantage of the chaos your final battle causes to avenge you._
_I have been instructed to say little about my purpose, as the politics are dangerous. However, as you are a Hand of Avadon, I think there are a few things I can say._
What can you say?
_The Holklandans have borne the insults of these bandits of Kellemderiel for too long. Perhaps, if their leader woke up dead one morning, the others might consider moving on to new targets._
_Avadon agrees with this estimation. They approved of finding a skilled shadowwalker to infiltrate their lair and remove the ... source of conflict._
And so you were selected?
_The Honored Forge, whether you are aware of it or not, is very close to Redbeard and to the Black Fortress._
Tell me about the bandit lair.
_You have already seen most of it, and, in my time here, I have seen little that you have not spied already._
_I know that their main base is to the west, and that you might wish not to go north._
_I have been inside this complex, using this crack as my base, for four days. I was planning to wait and watch four more days before acting. Such caution and patience are the keys to success._
Tell me about their main base.
_The only entrance to it I have found that is not well guarded is down the corridor to the west. Once inside, an infiltrator would have to work his way north, and quickly._
What is to the north?
_An old drake. The brigands give it meat, and it leaves them alone. There is no concealed entrance back there. Unless you are particularly foolhardy and bloodthirsty, you might avoid that area._
What should we do now?
_We? I work alone. I only work alone._
_I can aid you, however, but only if you tell me more about your situation._
You won't fight with a Hand of Avadon?
_I already do the work of Avadon, though I am no Hand. I will do that work in my own way and my own time._
I will continue my assault.
_Before you go, you should tell me more about your situation. I might be able to help._
Harua Honored Forge nods. _I wish you the best of luck, and I hope that your need for haste does not doom your efforts._
_Should the leader of the bandits fall, I will do my best to aid your friend._

There is an old Kellem man standing in this workshop, his back to you. He wears a set of old, threadbare mage's robes, but he has modified them extensively. Strange designs and random arrangements of runes have been laboriously sewn into them.
Then he turns, giving you a good look at his pale, worn face and his mad eyes. _Ahhhh ..._ he says. _What a pleasure. A visitor. Come to see Audric, yes? A supplicant? One who wishes to join us?_
Yes. Sure. I want to join you.

He giggles, a shrill, unhinged sound. _Yes. Of course. A whimsical intruder. I can see the blood in your eyes, and ..._ He sniffs. _Yes, I smell it in the air. Blood liberated from my servants, I suppose._
_And now you are before me, in the heart of the Circle of the Deepest Earth._
I am a Hand of Avadon, and I have come for you.

_Avadon? What? Avadon has come for us? I supposed I saw that it would come. We have aroused some anger, it is true, and the infidels of the Black Fortress cannot see the truth of the Circle of the Deepest Earth._
I am [N], and I have not come to help you.
_Yes. [N]. You are no ally of ours. I can see the blood in your eyes, and ..._ He sniffs. _Yes, I smell it in the air. Blood liberated from my servants, I suppose._
Um, the Circle of the Deepest Earth?

_What? You have not heard of us? I do so wish I had time to tell you the Truth. The existence of the Deep Spirits that bear all knowledge.  The need for depth. The closeness that gives us enlightenment. The transcendence of a really, really nice stalactite._
_No, you are probably more concerned about our providers and their activities._
I would like to know more about your ... faith?
_You never will. Our sacred secrets will be ever denied to you! Know that, on the cusp of your death, and weep tears of sadness! Enlightenment is ever denied you!_
I am mostly concerned about the lock that keeps me from escaping.
He smiles and lifts a silver chain hanging from around his neck. A crystal key rises from within his robes. _My little magical constructions are a puzzle that is easily solved. By me, not you._
I am very interested in your 'providers.'

_Yes. As we dig deeper, gaining proximity to the holders of Ultimate Wisdom, we need food, supplies, and protection. Certain thuggish Kellem are eager to help us. In return, I protect them, and ..._ He pauses.
_Oh, these arrangements are most tedious to describe. I'm sure you can fill in the details. More interesting, I think, is the punishment you will suffer for your intrusion, blasphemy, and so on._
No! It is I who will punish you!
Audric is thrilled by your words. _A worthy and spirited opponent, you are! The thugs will be very impressed by the destruction of you by me! The thugs who are still alive, I mean._
_Now face my powers, given to me by the Deep Earth!_ He raises his hands and starts to cast a spell. Wispy, insubstantial forms start to appear on the magic circles.
Just let me leave and I won't have to hurt you.
_Ahhh ... You banter for your life. That shows your weakness. You seemed strong, at first, but now I know that you are spent and afraid._
Please! Have mercy upon me! I beg you!
_Ahhh ... You beg for your life. That shows your weakness. You seemed strong, at first, but now I know that you are spent and afraid._
Die, crazy person. (Attack.)
There comes a time when further banter is just irritating. You raise your weapon. _What,_ Audric cries. _We fight already? You show no appreciation for the drama of such things._

A shade appears on one of the circles. It immediately starts to moan. It does nothing else. At first, the deep low keening is only an irritation. As time passes, however, it gets more and more distracting.
The echoing hum of the shade in the circle finally starts to affect you. You find it extremely difficult to concentrate. Everything beyond the simplest blows and defensive moves becomes impossible.
You hear shouting coming from nearby. Some of the brigands have heard the battle, and they are coming to investigate.
Audric casts a spell, and several tottering skeletons appear on the magic circles. They come tottering after you, but they start falling apart pretty much the moment they start to move.

Cultist Audric falls to the floor, mortally wounded. He gasps, _Spirits of the Deep Earth, save me! Destroy the intruders! Show the enlighten ... ten ..._ None of these things happen. He dies, and the remains of all of his constructs fade away.
You take a silver necklace from the body. A delicately carved crystal key hangs from it.
This victory should break the spirit of the bandits here. Once you have rescued Shigaz, you can report your victory back to Castle Vebeaux.

You return to Monitor Shigaz and find that he is not alone. Another shadowwalker kneels at his side, administering first aid. Shigaz will have a hard time traveling to safety, but he is well enough to manage.
Then the shadowwalker rises and bows to you. _I am Harua, of the Honored Forge. When you arrived, I had already begun to infiltrate this lair. Happily, you completed my task for me._
You are of the Honored Forge?
Shigaz looks up at you. _Yes. Your companion. Shima Threespear. I did my investigations. I know of him. I know of his desire for vengeance against the Honored Forge. As, I am sure, do you._
_It is fortunate that Shima is not here, but Harua's presence might ... enrage him._
Shima must know of this.
_I hope you will ... reconsider. I ask ..._ Shigaz winces in pain as he shakes his head. _Time is still short. We are still in the belly of the beast._
_[N], It appears that victory is ours after all. No thanks to me._
I'm not concerned about these squabbles.
_I am pleased, but there is one thing I will still ask. I ..._ Shigaz winces in pain as he shakes his head. _Time is still short. We are still in the belly of the beast._

You return to Monitor Shigaz and find that he is not alone. Harua Honored Forge has discovered him. He kneels at the fallen shadowwalker's side, administering first aid. Shigaz will have a hard time traveling to safety, but he is well enough to manage.
Shigaz looks up at you and smiles weakly. _Ah, [N]. It appears that victory is ours after all. No thanks to me._
Are you doing better?
_I will live. And, no doubt, be sent back to Vebeaux. I am a success, after all._
_With Harua's help, I will return to Holklanda. I will report what happened. They will be ... be ..._ He coughs and groans.
They will be ...
_Surprised and pleased. The Kellem raiders, they are broken. At last. It is a sore spot that ... that ... I am sorry. I grow tired. I ... There is one thing we need to discuss._
_I am bound to give a full report. I will tell my masters all that happened. All my mistakes._ He looks up at Harua. _Everyone I met. This may cause trouble._
How so?
_One of your companions, Shima, he will learn that the Honored Forge are fighting in this area. He hates this clan. He may want to do something rash._
Surely you can leave Harua out of the report?
_I cannot ignore my sworn duties so easily. Perhaps Shima will not read the report. We can hope, but it would be quite a lapse on his part._
Any enemy of Shima's is an enemy of mine.
Harua nods somberly and rests his hand on the pommel of his blade. Shigaz says, _My strength is fading. I must retreat. I will hope ... Hope bloodshed can be averted._
_As soon as the way to the exit is clear, we will retreat. Please hurry and clear the way._
_Now we will retreat. Thank you, [N]. You have saved my life._
Shima is a Hand. He can do what he wishes.
Harua already seems to be planning for the battle. Shigaz says, _Please try to dissuade him. This is not the time for Pact to fight Pact. I hope ... hope what I fear will happen does not happen._
I will try to prevent him from doing violence.
Harua says, _That would be very wise._ Shigaz adds, _I am glad. This is not the time for Pact to fight Pact. I hope ... hope what I fear will happen does not happen._
Withered Drake
Harua Honored Forge
Kellem Sentinel
Shaman Clawfire
The ogre shaman blows on a horn, summoning help.
The ogre shaman blows on a horn again, summoning help.
Brigand Sentry
A sentry has seen you. He starts to raise his horn to his lips.
A sentry blows his horn. You can hear the brigands setting out to hunt you.
Moaning Shade
The moans of Audric's shade are becoming incredibly distracting. You have a hard time concentrating on your attacks.
Kellem Brigand
Shhh.
Come on.
We must act fast.
Kellem Archer
Kellem Marksman
Kellem Rogue
Aubin the Brigand
Arghhh!
Curse them!
Aghh.
Hurry.
Shadowwalker Decoy
The decoy fades away. Then, moments later, another appears to take its place.
Kellem Hunting Wolf
Kellem Hunter
Blademaster Helai
Beraza Tracker
Hunting Hellhound
Kellem Whipmaster
Melisande's Hound
Melisande's Basilisk
Melisande's Drake
Brigand Guard
Brigand Warrior
Minaka
Delbrin
Shelia the Sorceress
Cyclone Bat
Kellem Elite Warrior
Kellem Tracker
Yevena Farsight
Move quickly.
The duke must be very angry.
So many hunters.
Moo.
Mooooo.
Moo!
Mu.
Gavin waits for you.
We mean no harm.
You must move on soon.
Gryfyn's soldiers are everywhere.
I am of Avadon no longer.
I am no traitor.
You can't stay for long.
I buy and sell.
What is 'stolen', really?
Trade before you move on?
You're the hunted one, yes?
Kellem Elite Hunter
At last, after miles of running through the thickets of the Beraza Woods, hounded at every moment by the wolves and basilisks of Castle Vebeaux, you are granted a few moments of peace.
You collapse, panting, on the west shore of a wide, slow-flowing stream. An hour of trudging through its cold water seems to have thrown your pursuers off the scent.
You have some time to digest what has happened to you. Monitor Shigaz murdered. You accused of the crime. Pact soldiers hunting you. Not good.
Sevilin looks north, toward Castle Vebeaux. _Ambushed once again. At least, this time, those with the poor luck to be traveling with me have survived._
Shima looks down the dark path to the west. _We must be alert. Duke Gryfyn clearly has his lapses in judgment, but his warriors are skilled and tireless._
Jenell sniffs the air. _At least we are back in the forest, my preferred territory. Anyone who thinks I will submit peacefully to this injustice will receive an ugly surprise._

Nathalie wraps her damaged arm in a long strip of cloth. The cold water has not been kind to it. She snarls, _I grow tired of running. Any who try to haul me back to Avadon in chains make a fatal error._
Your brief rest comes to an unhappy end. Somehow, someone has picked up your trail. To the north, you hear howls, followed by hisses, followed by horns.

The baying and tumult approaches from that direction. Your pursuers are numerous, close and getting closer, and the woods to the south are too dense for speedy travel. Only the pathway to the west leads away from them.

You are as alert as you can be, given your exhausting journey here. Thus, though the Kellem scout hiding off the path to the north is well concealed, you see her eyes peering at you through the brush.
She steps into view, and you are surprised to see that, though she is armed, she is not a Pact soldier. She nods and raises her blade to you.
_I am Tayce,_ she says. _If you tire of being hunted, I might help you._
Tayce

You reach the edge of the woods and see a wide pathway. This is one of the few roads through the Beraza Woods. It is wild and untended, though in better shape than the rugged paths you have seen to the north.

However, a moment after you step out, you jump back. The road, normally free of travel except for a few brave caravans, is heavily patrolled with guards. Kellem soldiers, wearing plate and bearing greatswords. Horns hang from their belts, ready to call for reinforcements in moments.
Going out there is extremely dangerous. Duke Gryfyn is sparing no expense to catch you and bring you back to his castle.
Once again, you see the road through the Beraza Woods. It is still watched, though less alertly than to the south.

To the east, across the road, you see a large Pact encampment. To the northeast, you see a bridge. Sentries have not been posted at it. They must all be on the road to the south. If you are careful, you might be able to slip across unseen.
You enter this crude tunnel. The low ceiling forces you to bow your head as you walk. You suspect that it is an abandoned tunnel, recently occupied and restored by smugglers.
Except for the dripping of water and the squeaking of rats, it is quiet. Duke Gryfyn's soldiers have not yet discovered it.
You suddenly realize just how determined Duke Gryfyn is to track you down. His hounds are both willing and capable of tracking you under the earth.

The west wall of this old tunnel starts to shake. You hear powerful claws working their way through the dirt. Then the walls both in front of and behind you fall, allowing your hunters to pour into the tunnel.
Woodwalker Unia
Woodwalker Drya

You descend into this dark cellar. The building above was, you suspect, an abandoned farmhouse. When the hunt for you began, Kellem soldiers moved in and did a remarkable job of quickly turning it into a base of operations.
For example, this tunnel was, in the span of hours, cleaned out and turned into pens for the beasts hunting you to rest and be fed. You can hear them in the shadows, snarling and gnawing on bones.
And then, above their grunts, you hear the crack of a whip. The sharp sound of it echoes down the long tunnel to you. It's not just beasts down here. Their trainer is too.

There is a large encampment in this clearing. Not farmers, not lumberjacks. This is a camp of brigands and ne'er-do-wells if you've ever seen one. Several thugs stand guard on the other side of the palisade.
And yet, when they see you, they do nothing. They don't even grab their weapons. They just watch you approach. They seem to be expecting you.

You start to walk down this road, trying to put some distance between you and your pursuers. Then you stop. You realize that you are only taking yourself farther from Castle Vebeaux, its pylon, and your only way back to Avadon.
If you can't find your way back home and clear your name, you will be a fugitive forever. You will be doomed. With great regret, you turn back.

You start to walk down this road, heading back toward Castle Vebeaux. Then you realize that you are making a big mistake. If you take this route, out in plain sight, you will be mobbed and overwhelmed in no time at all.
With great regret, you turn back. You do need to get back to Castle Vebeaux. However, you need to find a better route, and you need a way to get into the castle unseen.
You are at the edge of a large camp of Pact soldiers, the base of operations for the hordes currently hunting for you.
You can't help but note that Hand Gavin's directions led you directly here. Something that might be worth discussing, if you survive to meet him again.
The camp is, fortunately, mostly empty. Most of the soldiers are out hunting for you. However, the commander is still there, with his personal guard.
They are standing at a table in the center of the camp, poring over maps and planning the hunt. They haven't seen you yet, but they will soon.
From this side of the thicket to the east, you can see a concealed pathway through the trees.
The trapdoor is locked. As you try to open it, Tayce watches with interest.
One of the soldiers blows a horn. You instantly hear shouting from the nearby Pact encampment. Duke Gryfyn's soldiers have been alerted to your presence.
If you don't find a place to hide some distance from their camp, you will be in great danger.
One of the Pact soldiers guarding the road sees you. He has a blade in one hand and a horn in the other.
When he realizes that you match the description of one of the fugitives he is hunting, he starts to raise the horn to his lips.

Tender Melisande crumples to the ground, a proud warrior of Kellemderiel to the last. This is another senseless death that Duke Gryfyn is going to have to answer for. Loyal to Avadon or not, any attack on a Hand must be answered.
You try to talk to the brigand, but your efforts to start a conversation fail miserably. The filthy warrior nods to the northwest. _Gavin's waiting. Talk to him._
The brigands in this hall are a dirty, slow lot. They aren't sharpening weapons or planning an ambush. They sit around, play games, drink, and enjoy their huge piles of looted goods.
You try to talk to them about their great fortune, but they only tell you to talk to Minaka.

The brigands here sit in the shadows, armed and alert. They constant look to their leader, who sits at a table in the west end of the hall. They are tense, unsure of what order might come but ready to obey it instantly.
_Moo._
The Wayfarer takes a step back and raises the clay globe in his hand. _Don't get too confident, [N]. I would not travel in these wilds alone._ He drops the globe and smashes it under his boot.
A moment later, a translucent decoy of the Wayfarer appears. Unlike most such enchanted decoys, however, this one can move. And attack.

The Wayfarer is rapidly growing battered and bloodied. _No!_ he shouts, the first time you have heard him raise his voice. _I will not die here, not this way! I will not have my life wasted like this!_
There is a ring on his mailed hand. He grabs it and gives it a sharp twist. It crumbles into dust. A moment later, the Wayfarer begins to slowly fade away.
The Wayfarer vanishes. When he is only a wisp, barely visible in the shadowy grove, he says, _We shall meet again. I plan to buy something far grander with my death ..._
And then he is gone.

The Wayfarer collapses, coughing and spitting blood. He reaches up, grabs his mask, and pulls it off. You get a good look at his battered face. At first, you don't recognize him. Then you realize that he matches the description of Shadow Tarkus, the last of the escaped prisoners from the Avadon dungeons.
Tarkus slumps to the ground, gasping. _What a ... waste ... I was a fool. I wasted my ... my life ... I ..._ And then he is silent. The Wayfarer, quiet at last.
You look at the spire of the rock to the north. Someone has hung a rusty shield from a stone outcropping.
Then you start to pull aside the brush to the east. Behind it, you find a narrow path threading to the east. Beyond, there is a narrow, rotting wooden bridge over the river.

From this side, you easily see the concealed pathway through this dense thicket of brush. You push it aside, revealing the pathway Hand Gavin told you about. Then you realize what his directions left out.
You are at the rear of a huge camp of Pact soldiers. You'll have to move closer to see more. You also suspect that, if you want Hand Gavin to lead you to Castle Vebeaux, you don't have a choice.
Viscount Varoche falls in battle. Another loyal and skilled warrior of the Pact (if a bit arrogant) is dead because of the Duke Gryfyn's treachery.
You need to soon find a way to return to Castle Vebeaux and then to Avadon. Something has to be done.
You hear footsteps to the west. Now that the battle has concluded, Hand Gavin has seen fit to join you.
You walk up to Tayce. She is a young woman, tanned and wearing rough leather clothes. She's obviously lived in these woods for many years, if not her whole life. She watches you with great interest.

She says, in a voice barely above a whisper, _You are looking rather rough, if you don't mind me saying. Wet, dirty, in need of a hot fire. If you don't mind me asking, who are you and where are you from?_
Tayce is still lurking in the underbrush here. She whispers, Say your piece and move on, please. It is hard to be a scout, hidden in the shadows, when you are blundering around nearby._
Why should I tell you anything?
She smiles and says, very softly, _Because you need help, and I can get you to those who can give it. Unless, of course, you would be left to the duke's tender mercies. Not wise, though._
I am [N], a Hand of Avadon, and I demand your help.
When you say this, you hear something to the northwest. Footsteps moving softly over dry leaves. Tayce simply nods.

_We knew that something was amiss, now that the duke's soldiers have flooded the woods. The help you 'demand' might be given, if asked for politely. I can give you directions to the man who might give it._
I am [N], a harmless traveler in these lands.
When you say this, you hear something to the northwest. Footsteps moving softly over dry leaves. Tayce nods and smiles.

_A harmless traveler, you say, but even a blind child could see that you aren't telling the truth. If you wish a moment's shelter and can bring yourself to speak honest, I can give directions to a man you might wish to meet._
I am [N], and I have nothing else to say to you.
When you say this, you hear something to the northwest. Footsteps moving softly over dry leaves. Tayce nods and frowns.

_We knew that something was amiss, now that the duke's soldiers have flooded the woods. We might help you, but you are not making it easy for us to do so. Still, I can give you directions to the man who might give you aid._
Tell me more about you and your people.
_You speak with authority, but I have orders not to give you information. Not until we know more about you. I will give directions. That is all._
_You have met Gavin already. Anything he hasn't told you, I don't want to tell you._
Why are you alone out here?

_Because these woods are now crawling with the duke's soldiers, and he who commands me wishes to know why. I am not the only scout in the shadows, but I am the one lucky enough to have spotted the duke's prey._
Where can I go to find shelter?
Tayce leans close and whispers, _I am glad that you asked. There is a trapdoor in the grove behind me. Descend and go northwest. It is probably safe._
Probably?
_This tunnel is well hidden, but the duke's troops are thorough. None of his hunters lurked within when I passed through, but that was yesterday._
And then?
_Ascend through the ladder at the far end of the tunnel and walk out east to the road. Cross the bridge to the north, but move with care. Soldiers of the Pact are out in force._
How can I evade them?
_Watch from a distance, and cross the bridge when they are away. Last I saw, the bridge had no sentries._
I prefer to fight my way through.
Tayce inspects you with a critical eye. _You seem competent enough, but the duke is going to great lengths to hunt his prey. Even you might find yourself overwhelmed._
And when I am across the bridge?
_Step off the road to the west as quickly as you can, and head north. You will come to our humble settlement soon enough._
_That is up to my master. Go now, and quickly. I must return to my hiding place, to watch and to learn._
She slips back into the undergrowth to the north.
Hand Gavin asked me to slay a huntress and animal trainer.

Tayce winces. _Her. Yes, she is a scourge to my little group. This is the wrong path, though. To get there unseen, pass back through the tunnel to the north end. Then cross the road, hopefully unseen._
And when I am across?
_Look for a path we have marked with a broken jar, resting on its side. Go east from there and you may find the trainer's lair unseen. That is all the help I can give._
Then she slips back into the undergrowth. She is growing better at staying unseen with every passing minute.
I will be going.
_Then I wish you all the fortune you deserve. She slips back into the undergrowth._

Viscount Varoche lets out a stirring battle cry. He seems to have an almost magical effect on his warriors (perhaps aided by actual magic). All of his allies near him attack you with deadly precision and defend themselves with incredible skill.

Hand Gavin reveals another concealed doorway, this one in a large rock outcropping on the east side of the clearing. _This path is seldom traveled. We can follow it all the way to Vebeaux. I will meet you there. Don't delay!_
Then he hastens through the opening and down the path.

As you try to reach Viscount Varoche to do battle with him, you find that his warriors are getting in your way. All of his allies cluster near him, interfering with your blows and blocking your attacks with their shields.
You have to admire the loyalty he inspires in his allies. As long as they are near him, it will be hard to get a good shot in.
You round the corner and see a familiar face. It is Tender Melisande, master trainer of the Vebeaux kennels. Unsurprisingly, she is far less friendly now than she was before.

You round the corner and find the master trainer of the Vebeaux kennels. She is a short, stocky woman who clearly spends a lot of time out in the sun. Her work has left her hands and arms covered with as many scars and claw marks as you would expect.
Two hellhounds and two basilisks stand at her side. They are huge, fierce beasts, the pride of her kennel. Their presence makes her far more confident than she should be.
And then something else edges out from behind her. It is a young drake, barely hatched. It is small, but its fangs are sharp and its fire is hot.

Melisande says, _Ahhh ... [N]. Duke Gryfyn himself told me to hunt you down. You have led to the deaths of many of my prized beasts. I mourn them, and, before this day is out, you will have paid for the loss of each one._
I see you have a drake.
_Yes, hatched from the very egg you brought me. One day, I hope it will grow large and strong. First, it will test itself by fighting the Hand who stole it from its mother._
I have been sent to kill you.
_Have you? By who? The bandits and brigands in these woods? I'm not surprised, considering how many of them have fed my pets._
_I am glad to hear that they have sent you to me. It will make the duke's task so much simpler._
Duke Gryfyn sent you after me?
_He called me to his private chambers and gave me the order personally. He was most determined that you be killed._
Why does he want me dead?
_Don't know. Don't care. My line exists only to serve the lords of Vebeaux._
You should not obey the duke. He is a traitor.
Tender Melisande snorts. _When you say he is a traitor, you mean that he does not obey Avadon. That is true. He told me that I was hunting Hands, and he told me why._
You will be punished for attacking a Hand of Avadon. (Attack.)
Melisande is not intimidated. _Avadon? Avadon will be rubble soon! Duke Gryfyn has promised it to us all!_ She gives the word, and her beasts attack.
And why are you hunting me?
_Because Avadon is too weak and corrupt to protect the Pact. Because the Pact's time is past. Duke Gryfyn has a new path for Kellemderiel. He looks out for our people, and so do I!_
And what is that path?
_I did not ask. I trust him with my life. All I know is that you will not live to see it._
I agree that Avadon's time is past.

Tender Melisande seems surprised, but she does not lower her weapon. _If you truly would leave Avadon and help us, I am sorry. Your death will be a waste. Still, the duke's orders were clear, and he warned me that you would be full of tricks and lies._
_But take heart. You are not alone. Many other servants of Avadon are going to die today._
Duke Gryfyn is either mad or a traitor. Or both.
_If doing what is best for the people of Kellemderiel is treason, than he is a traitor, as am I. Be ready, and take heart. You are not the only servant of Avadon who is about to die._
About to die? What do you mean by that?

Melisande shakes her head. _I can't say, and you will never know. You will not live to warn them. Avadon will be rubble soon! Duke Gryfyn has promised it to us all!_ She gives the word, and her beasts attack.
Melisande, leave this place. This is your last warning.

Melisande shakes her head. _I fear that my death is near, but I will never abandon Kellemderiel! Avadon will be rubble soon! Duke Gryfyn has promised it to us all!_ She gives the word, and her beasts attack.
I have had enough of Duke Gryfyn's treachery. (Attack.)
Melisande is not intimidated. _Then do what you will! Avadon will be rubble soon! Duke Gryfyn has promised it to us all!_ She gives the word, and her beasts attack.
Sevilin suddenly stops walking down the path. He punches a tree with his mailed fist, causing brown leaves to drift down onto him. This act does little to help his foul temper.
Then he turns to you. _Why, [N]? Why was this allowed to happen? I am a loyal servant of Avadon. I always was, even when Avadon wasn't loyal to me. Why am I here now, disgraced and hunted?_
Have faith. Avadon will not abandon us.
Sevilin thinks on this. _I choose to believe that, for now, only because I have no choice. Otherwise, I would despair.._
_And yet, when Avadon tried to pardon a vile murderer, you let him go free. If there is justice left in this world, I don't think it will be received from their hand. Or yours._
He walks on in silence.
It is not just, and someone will have to answer for it.
Sevilin nods. _I am glad to hear it. I have been betrayed often enough._
_And yet, when Avadon tried to pardon a vile murderer, you let him go free. If there is justice left in this world, I don't think it will be received from your hand._
I don't know.
_Does anybody know anything? About anything? Still, I appreciate your honesty, [N]._ He walks on in silence.

As you walk through the woods, Shima says, _[N], tell me, do you think that Avadon is sending anyone to rescue us? Or that they will believe that we are criminals? Perhaps they will simply forget about us?_
I'm sure rescuers are on their way as we speak.
_I admire your trust, but I have learned recently just how little Avadon cares about those it protects. After all, they let the Honored Forge destroy my family for a minor political advantage._
_And you were of no help when I sought revenge. Truly, we all stand alone._
He follows you, lost in thought.
I think, if we don't defend ourselves, Avadon will hunt us too.
_That is what I believe as well. Avadon is deadly and capricious. It is not what I believed when I first went to serve it, but I believe that now._
I think we have already been forgotten.

_Truly, that is the best possible case. We have learned recently just how little Avadon cares about those it protects. After all, they let the Honored Forge destroy my family for a minor political advantage._
Jenell idly runs her hands through the foliage when she walks. She is making no effort to disguise her anger.
Then she turns to you. _When I went into the wilds to help those Wyldrylm fugitives, I did not think I would be a fugitive myself so soon. I should have left with Vid. I curse my foolishness._
We all should have gone with him.

She smiles. Slightly. _What a merry band we would have made, crashing through the wilds of Khemeria. But better that, I think, than to be betrayed and abandoned by our own people._ She adds, darkly, _Maybe even Avadon hunts us now._
Her smile fades, replaced by a grim resolve. She walks through the forest, taking as much comfort from it as she can.
We have a duty to Avadon and to the Pact.
_A duty to the Pact? Where was Avadon's sense of duty when it let my people, people of the Wyldrylm, be driven into Khemeria, hunted and killed?_
_Killing, by the way, that you partook of with great enthusiasm. Don't think I have forgotten._
_No, duty is an idea for children. We of the Wyldrylm should care about only one thing: survival._ She walks through the forest, taking as much comfort from it as she can.
As you walk down the dark passage, you note that Nathalie is muttering angrily to herself. The long, cold journey here has aggravated the problems with her arm. She holds it tight against her chest.
Then you hear her say, _Curse Avadon. They must be behind this. Is there nothing they won't do to keep me down?_
(Stay silent.)
Nathalie realizes that her interior monologue is getting noisy. She starts to mutter far more quietly.
Nathalie, are you all right?
She looks at you angrily. _What? Are you going to pretend to help me, too? If you really were concerned you wouldn't have abandoned me in the woods and let Zhossa Mindtaker go free._
She stops muttering with a start. _I ... I am sorry, [N]. I will regain control. I know that I can trust you when everyone else has abandoned me._
She walks on in silence.
This smoky hall is full of warriors. Hardy, armed people of the woods, all with thick leather jerkins and old but functional weapons. They watch you silently as you pass.

And then there is their leader, sitting at this table. There is no mistaking him. He is an aging man, but muscular and confident. He wears plate mail, and a beautiful steel broadsword hangs from his belt. The chest of his armor bears, faded but recognizable, the symbol of Avadon.
_Welcome, [N],_ he says. _I am Gavin. Once, I was called Hand Gavin. That was before I was forced to flee into these woods._
Hand Gavin sits at the table, his mug and his blade both close to hand. The other warriors watch him nervously, waiting for instruction.
_Well, [N],_ Gavin says, _what else do you need to know?_
How did you know my name?

Gavin takes a deep swig from his mug. _This patch of forest is small and humble, but there is little that happens in it that I don't learn of. Especially when someone comes here dragging a horde of Duke Gryfyn's hunters and trackers behind._
You are a Hand?
_Was. Was a Hand. This is before I was accused falsely of a crime and driven into the wild. Now my only business is survival._
_I will tell you in time, but first, I have a question for you. What are you doing here? And why are so many armed soldiers hunting for you?_
I am still a Hand of Avadon, and I won't be questioned by you.
Hand Gavin is amused. _The arrogance of a Hand. I lost that some time ago. Anyway, I can guess why you are here. The same reason I am. You were betrayed by Duke Gryfyn._
_Tell me. Don't tell me. Doesn't matter. However, if you would see Avadon again, you may want my help._
I am being hunted by Castle Vebeaux. They think me a killer. (Tell the tale.)
Hand Gavin listens with great interest. _A familiar story, one I have been living here for some time. I was betrayed by Duke Gryfyn. It sounds like you suffered the same fate._
_It is good that you told me. If you would see Avadon again, you may want my help._
Someone in Castle Vebeaux has betrayed me. (Tell the tale.)
_Much as you did, I think. Redbeard sent me to Castle Vebeaux. I was going to hunt some brigands in the Beraza Woods. I did not expect to join them._

_However, while I was in the Castle, I intercepted some messages. They were between Duke Gryfyn and the Tawon Empire. That duke, so clever, so seemingly servile, was negotiating in secret with the Farlands._
How did you get those messages?
_I spoke with Eye Acacia, a true servant of Avadon who lives in Castle Vebeaux. She had her suspicions. Once she told me of them, waiting outside the Castle and intercepting the messages was simple._
_Now that the duke's plans seem to be in place, I fear for her safety._
What was Duke Gryfyn trying to do?
_I am not sure. The messages were vague. He was negotiating with the Tawon Empire, the most dangerous of our enemies. I had hoped that we would learn more from him in Avadon's dungeons._
What did he offer to the Tawon Empire?
_I don't know exactly. He seemed to be hinting at an alliance between them and Kellemderiel. And yet, this seems like madness. Such a thing would require Kellemderiel to leave the Pact._
_Does the duke's treason reach that far? I don't know, and it doesn't matter to me anymore._
Duke Gryfyn seemed to be trying to help the Pact.
_With his famed attempts to make peace with Holklanda? Yes, even out here we heard of these overtures._
_Perhaps dealing with the Tawon Empire was a second plan in case the efforts to make peace with Holklanda failed. Which, of course, they would._
What did you do with your information?

_I should have tried to return to Avadon immediately. Instead, I lingered, trying to intercept more messages and make a better case. This gave Duke Gryfyn time to, in turn, fabricate evidence that it was I who was spying for the Tawon._

_When his warriors came to my quarters in the dead of night, it took all my skill and a fair amount of luck to slip by them and escape. I ran out of the west gate with his trackers only minutes behind me._
What did you do after you fled?

_I ran into the Beraza Woods. Duke Gryfyn sent soldiers after me, but I evaded them with ease. Complaints from Holklanda forced him to pull his warriors out of the woods, and I was left free to build a new life for myself._
_During my wanderings, I came here. Once I saw what I had to work with, I took command of this crude band of warriors._
So you command brigands? Rob caravans?

_I do command here, but we do not rob. I know the locations of every cache, safehouse, and other bit of easily taken wealth in the Beraza Woods. These warriors find it far easier and safer to take advantage of my knowledge._
Why haven't you returned to Avadon?
_Because Avadon has abandoned me. They have sent nobody for me. They have not tried to prove my innocence. For all I know, they even aid in the hunt for me._
_No more will I suffer under Redbeard's whims. I give them as much loyalty as they gave me. None._
Does the duke still hunt you?
_Of course, but quietly. Assassins and trackers sometimes roam the woods. He hasn't tried hard, though. No doubt, whatever his plans are, he doesn't have much energy to spare to find me._
_You, however, are clearly different. He obviously fears you greatly._
And what will you do now?
_Now? Now I let the Pact and Avadon and the Farlands carry out their business. I gave them a lifetime of loyal service, and they drove me into the wilds._
_I will stay here. The question is: What happens to you?_
I would like to stay here with you.
Gavin laughs harshly. _There is no chance of that. I am barely tolerated out here as it is. If you stay, we will never be free of trackers and bounty hunters._
_No, we will have to be rid of you soon. And yet, I would not turn you in. We must find another way._
You can't turn your back on Avadon. You must return with me.
_Of course I can turn my back on Avadon. Did they not do the same to me? No, even out here, my life here is quieter and safer._
_As for you, we will have to be rid of you soon. And yet, I would not turn you in. We must find another way._
Do what you want, but I must return to Avadon.
Gavin nods. _On that, we are agreed. You are a true servant of Avadon. I can see that. What is more, you can't stay here, not with all of the hunters on your trail._
I need supplies and protection.
_We are a small group, and we can't protect you. We only want you to be gone._
_You can trade for supplies, though. Speak with Delbrin. He is in the hall to the south._
I need to return to Avadon.
_Then you face the same quandary I did. Your route home is the pylon. The pylon is in the middle of Castle Vebeaux, past all of the gates and the soldiers._

_Impossible to reach it, yes? Unless, of course, you can take advantage of the knowledge of Avadon. I know a secret way into Castle Vebeaux. I will tell it to you if you, in return, slay one of the hunters tracking you._
You require a bribe before you help a fellow Hand?
Gavin and his warriors laugh unkindly. _I am a Hand of Avadon, yes? When has a Hand ever helped anyone, no matter how deserving, without payment?_
Why do you wish this hunter dead?
_She is a tracker and trainer. The beasts the soldiers use to hunt us are trained by her. As long as Duke Gryfyn has her skills, we are not safe. You are not either._
_One day, the other warriors in our woods will leave. Only she is a threat to me._
And if I don't want to kill her?

He thinks on this. _Actually, if you confronted her with the knowledge of the duke's treason and she is truly a loyal servant of the Pact, she might abandon him. That would serve my purposes just as well._
Where can I find her?
_You must go back to the way you came. Cross back over the river to the south. Be wary. There is a camp of Pact soldiers just on the other side, to the east. I suggest you evade them._
Where do I go from there?
_There is a path to the south of the Pact camp. It is marked with a broken pot, on its side. Walk down that path to the east. Our enemy is somewhere in that direction._
_I will send scouts ahead of you to try to lure away some of the sentries on the road. With luck, you will have an easier time slipping past them._
Tender Melisande is dead. (Tell the tale.)

Hand Gavin listens to your tale. He seems surprisingly saddened by it. _I honestly thought that she might be loyal to the Pact. I thought you might convince her to flee. Instead, the duke's treason infected her._

He sits there in silence for some time. He looks at your armor, your weapons, with something that approaches envy. _You acted. Decisively. Sometimes, I miss it. The risk. The ability to make decisions. Yes, the power._
Then he shakes his head. _Those days are lost. I will meet my end of the bargain. I will help you to return to Avadon._
How will you help me to return to Avadon?

_Yes._ He thinks for a moment. _I will help you. But how? Should I tell you ... No. If you clear the way, I will show you to the way into Castle Vebeaux myself. I am still enough of a Hand to do that much._
_Go east and clear the way. I will follow._
Where should I go, exactly?
_East from this encampment, but stay off the main road. Look for a stone spire with a rusty shield hanging from it. There is a concealed path there._
_Continue east from there. There is a clearing beyond. If any guards greet you, you might need to defend yourself. Once the path is clear, my scouts will let me know and I will follow._
You will come back to Castle Vebeaux with me?
_Only long enough to help you to gain entry. I do not think I will help you to fight your way through. The fearlessness of a servant of Avadon has left me._
I need to rest.

Hand Gavin nods. _As long as you don't stay too long, I would not deny a Hand a chance to rest his or her head._ Some of his warriors clear off a few beds and make them as clean as possible. (Which isn't very clean.)
You nap for a few hours and wake up refreshed.
I will be leaving now.
_Then I wish you a safe journey. Though, unless you return to Avadon soon, the hunters of Vebeaux will eventually bring you down._
There is a Holklandan woman sitting on this wooden throne. A gold circlet rests on her head. She looks like a brigand, but one who hasn't actually done any briganding in a while.
Her warriors lounge around, eating and drinking. All of them seem to have put on some pounds during their inactivity. Their armor fits very tightly, and their weapons are poorly maintained.
The bandit queen doesn't seem scared of you. She waves you closer. _Yes, you are [N]. I am Minaka. Hand Gavin told me you would be coming. As long as you behave, you are welcome in our camp._
Minaka, queen of brigands, lounges in her throne. It is old, and battered, and the gilt has mostly worn off. It was probably headed for Castle Vebeaux when it was stolen, many years ago.
Minaka says, _What else do you need, Hand?_
You are ... brigands?
_We are! Proud hunters of Holklanda and Kellemderiel, come together to live a free life. And, of late, a life of ease._
Holklanda and Kellemderiel together? You don't fight?
_Oh, there is an argument from time to time, though I punish anyone who causes real trouble.
_However, we brigands only want the war between Holklanda and Kellemderiel to continue forever. As long as it does, the Beraza Woods stay wild and free!_ She raises a stein. _To war!_
You do all seem comfortable.
_It is all thanks to Hand Gavin. As long as we don't attack caravans or cause trouble, he keeps us all fat and healthy and safe._
So you don't fight anymore?
_Of course not! We fight for survival, not fun. We don't want scars. We don't want to lose limbs. And we don't want to work for a living._
How does Hand Gavin help you?
_He knows where things are in the woods. Caches. Hidden treasures. Safehouses. We live now by looting them. Gavin has no love of Avadon, and he is happy to steal their supplies._
Tell me about Hand Gavin.
_Well, he would want to be called Gavin. Simple Gavin. But he is still a Hand of Avadon, and we don't forget it. He is in charge here. I handed command to him._
What is a Hand of Avadon doing in a camp like this?
_He is disgraced and on the run. Something to do with politics in the Castle. Doesn't matter to me. All I care about is that he is useful._
Why did you hand command to him?

_Because he gives us food and wealth, and we barely have to work for it. He has influence and he knows things about the Castle. What he knows helps us to keep safe and away from the guards. He is so useful that I was happy to put aside command for a while._
And if he becomes less useful?
Minaka gets a vicious gleam in her eye. _Then we will have another discussion._
I was driven out of Castle Vebeaux.
_I guessed. You came here, and you dragged hordes of Vebeaux soldiers after you. We are trapped in this camp now, unable to leave._
_I'm sure you can guess what that means to you._

Her smile vanishes. You can see blood in her eyes. _You have to move on. It is only Gavin's word that kept me from selling you to the soldiers. You only walk free because Gavin wanted to talk to you._
I am a Hand of Avadon. I won't be spoken to like that.
_A Hand? Still? I think not. You are scum now, like us. Go talk to Gavin. Then move on. Otherwise, I will lose my patience._ She waves you away.
I will talk to Gavin.
_He is in the northwest hall. Go see him. Move quickly, or I may lose my patience. I will not have you put us at risk._ She waves you away.

You are surprised to find, in the middle of this lair of brigands, a rather tidy shop. Piles of goods, orderly stacked. A long counter, clean and polished. An attentive proprietor who even combed his hair.
The shopkeeper, a swarthy elderly Dharamite, nods to you from behind the counter. _Welcome, traveler. I am Delbrin, and this is my shop. All who wish to trade peacefully are welcome._
Delbrin, the Dharamite shopkeeper, sits serenely behind the counter. _Is there anything else you need, bold warrior?_
This is a surprisingly tidy shop.
_I thank you. My shop is run in the standard Dharamite manner. In other words, it is clean, efficient, and profitable. We people of the eastern coast take great pride in such things._
Even though you are mainly surrounded by criminals?
_Especially then! That way, I can serve as a good example to them._
You don't worry about thieves and marauders?
_Oh, no. The presence of this trading post is of great value to said marauders. If any of them cause me trouble, Minaka makes sure they get killed to serve as an example to others._
Minaka?
_Our leader, in the past and in the future. She is in the next hall over._
Why are you so useful?

_Well, everyone needs a nice shop nearby, do they not? To buy supplies to deal with the harsh life of the Beraza Woods. And, of course, to turn any excess supplies you might find on hand into practical coinage._
Where do your goods come from?
_Ah, the origin of things. A great and timeless mystery, is it not? I know nothing of what happens outside my doors. Where is a sword from? Was it honestly obtained or taken by force?_
_Yes, we live in a world of mysteries. Contemplating them for too long could drive one mad, so I avoid it._
That seems like an excuse for buying stolen goods.
_No. It seems like a very very good excuse for buying stolen goods. And, since you are a wanted fugitive, I would not spend too much time judging others. What else do you need?_
But how do you know whether the things people bring you are stolen or not?

_Ah, but who is to say whether something is stolen or not? What does it mean for an item to be stolen? Or to be owned? These are complicated philosophical questions, and I am unworthy to even consider them._
_So, now that that issue is completely settled, what else do you need?_
I would like to trade.
_Of course. Would you like to see what I have for sale, or do you have something you wish to sell?_
I want to buy.
Delbrin's Trading Post
Delbrin is a fence of some repute, buying and selling stolen goods with a sharp eye, a smile, and a host of arguments for the morality of his actions.
I want to sell.
_Then I wish you safe travels and the best of luck dealing with your considerable legal problems._

This was perhaps the last place you would expect to see the Wayfarer, but here he is. He stands boldly out in the open, waiting for you. He is not as calm and tireless as he normally appears. He is short on breath, and his robes are dirty and torn.
Also, his hand rests on the pommel of his blade. For the first time, you think that he might be an actual, immediate danger to you.

Still, he manages a smile. _Hello, [N]. I apologize that it took me so long to find you out here. I might have been of use to you sooner. Events are moving quickly, and it has become desperately important that we talk._
How did you manage to find me?
_Our resources are limitless, and our allies are everywhere. I was sure that you would have figured this out by now. You can never escape us, just as Avadon can no longer escape._
Do you know how I came to be hunted like this?

_I know the outline of the details. Duke Gryfyn has declared that you are to be killed on sight. Once he convinces Redbeard of certain untrue statements, you will be unwelcome in Avadon. At that point, you will be doomed._
_And yet, there is hope. That is why I am here._
Do you have a job for me? Even now?
_Not a job. A simple exchange. All I want for you to do is answer a few simple questions. I will ask you to reveal no secret information. I will only ask of your state of mind._
_In return, I may be able to save your life._
I will talk to you, if I must.

_I am flattered by your enthusiasm. I offer a simple exchange. All I want for you to do is answer a few simple questions. I will ask you to reveal no secret information. I will only ask of your state of mind._
All right. Ask your questions.
_All right. Be calm. Things are quiet here. We only need to have a short conversation. Simply relax and answer._
I am through talking to you.

The Wayfarer's hand tightens on the pommel of his weapon. _You should know that you are taking a great risk by not talking to me. There are very few people in Lynaeus now who can help you, and I am one of them._
_You will speak with me. If not, you will not be protected from grim consequences._
Step aside, Wayfarer. Or else.
Was that a threat? I've been waiting for this! (Attack.)
The Wayfarer nods. In an instant, his blade is in one hand, and he holds a small, clay sphere in the other. _I regret this, [N]. Such a valuable waste of material._
Then he prepares to defend himself ...
If you want to stop me, you will have to fight. (Walk by him.)
The lone shadowwalker watches you as you pass. He debates whether to attack you. Finally, he steps back and lets you go. _Your death is inevitable. I do not need to cause it._
You start to walk away. Then you look back. The Wayfarer has vanished.
_Wisely chosen. Let us begin. Be calm. Things are quiet here. We only need to have a short conversation. Simply relax and answer._

_You have seen for yourself a truth the people of the Pact know all too well. The justice of Avadon is for sale. If you give a willing Hand enough money, and you can always find a willing Hand, you can get or do whatever you want._
_Is that just? Is that something you can be a part of?_
That power is a fair reward for the risks we take and the good we do.
_I see. I'm sure most of your fellow Hands would agree with you._
_Now for the second question._
It is unfortunate, but the good Avadon does outweighs the harm.
_Is that true? And, even if it is, will it stay that way forever? How long can Avadon keep its power from corrupting it completely?_
It is wrong, and, if I gain power, I will do my best to correct it.
_Those are dangerous words, and a dangerous path. And yet, Redbeard will not lead Avadon forever._
Avadon is corrupt. I don't need to be convinced of it.
_That is bravely and honestly admitted, more than most would expect from a Hand of Avadon._
Ask away.
_Avadon has been given the power to hunt, interrogate, and destroy any that it thinks threaten the Pact. You have seen for yourself how carelessly and clumsily its power is applied._
_Redbeard expects you to spend your life hunting, killing, crushing, burning. How do you feel about that?_
Those words sound like treason.
_Heh. I think that response answers the question very well._
_Now a third question, if you have the patience for it._
If that is the price to pay to protect the people of the Pact, so be it.
_But is it the best way to protect the Pact? Might not someone else use that power more wisely than Redbeard? It is something to consider._
I don't like it. If I was in charge, it would be different.
_Very brave words. And, perhaps, true ones. Redbeard must, one day, be replaced._
It disgusts me.
_Honestly spoken. It speaks well of you to be unable to withstand such things, even if they benefit you._
Another question, then.
_My final question is about Redbeard. He has been the master of Avadon for many years. The magics he uses to maintain his life will keep him in charge for many years more._
_He holds on by killing any who question him, and yet you follow him. My final question. Are you loyal to him, or has his time passed?_
I swore to obey him. I will continue to do so.
_Your loyalty, even to one who has grown so distant and incapable as Redbeard, does you credit._
_A final question, and then I will reward you._
Redbeard is a great leader.
_Is that true? Does that match what you have seen? Either way, your loyalty does you credit._
Redbeard is distracted. He has let Avadon become weak and corrupt.
_Ahhhh ... And if what you say is true? How will the Pact be protected? Who will finally have the courage to replace Redbeard and bring honor back to Avadon?_
I could do a better job than Redbeard. I should be Keeper.
The Wayfarer nods. _And I might agree with you. Now, the question. Do you have the courage to do what needs to be done?_
One final question.

_You have been abandoned by the Pact. The treachery of the duke has doomed you. Soon, when he has his way, Avadon will proclaim you a criminal. Suppose, however, that you could return to Avadon and clear your name._
_What then? With what you have learned of the Black Fortress, can you still serve it? Or do you have the courage to change it? To replace Redbeard and to rule wisely in his place?_
Before I answer, who are you really?

_I promise, that question will be answered very soon. Soon, I will do something that will elevate me to eternal fame. Or infamy. If you live, you won't have to wait much longer. Now tell me. Are you servile to Avadon, or would you fight to make it better?_
I wish to leave Avadon and never hear of it again.

The Wayfarer shakes his head. _Not an option. You are a Hand. That mark stays on you for life. Now, as the Pact starts to crumble, you must pick a side. The old, crumbling way, or the path of those who would remake Lynaeus._
Your words doom you. You are a traitor! (Attack.)
I am no traitor. I serve Avadon. Leave me and do not seek me again.
The Wayfarer nods somberly. _It is to your credit, I suppose. And yet, I will hold out one final wisp of hope that you can be saved. I will give you your reward: a bit of advice._
My reward is advice? That is all?
_What did you want? Coins? Some dagger? I am giving you a chance to save your life. There is no better reward._

_Redbeard's time is past. If you wish to survive the coming destruction, spare Duke Gryfyn when you have the chance. Then unseat the doddering master of the Black Fortress. Do this, and you might live._
I am sick of your treasonous talk! (Attack.)
I am done with you. (Walk by him.)
I have no more love for Avadon. I would change it if I could.
_Bravely spoken, and I think you will have the chance to change Avadon sooner than you think. In return for your words, I will give you your reward: a bit of advice._
