What is your advice?

_If you want to change Lynaeus for the better, you will soon have the chance. You must do two things. First, should you have the chance, and I suspect you will, spare Duke Gryfyn. This will be of great benefit to you._
And, second?

_Strike down Redbeard. Take his place. Rule Avadon. You are young, strong, and wise. You will be able to restore it to its former glory. That is all I have to say. I must leave. Events have begun, and I will take my part._
You are speaking treason! Now you must die! (Attack.)
Redbeard has served for too long. (Leave.)
_Then I wish you good hunting. Goodbye, [N]._ The lone shadowwalker gives you a final nod. Then he walks back in the direction you came from.
I will decide for myself what is best, but later. (Leave.)
_I can ask for nothing else.  Goodbye, [N]._ The lone shadowwalker gives you a final nod. Then he walks back in the direction you came from.

There is a man in glorious and ornate plate armor standing by the table. Everything about him communicates great wealth and influence. The long, curved blade hanging from his belt also lets you know that he would be dangerous in a duel.

You recognize him from Castle Vebeaux, where you met him briefly and talked to him long enough for him to express his contempt to you. This is Viscount Varoche. He recognizes you too and sneers, _So, you turned out to be a traitor after all. I recognized it the moment I saw you._
He turns to face you. _So, the traitor has come to me. Most convenient. I am Viscount Varoche. Or, as you might call me, your doom._
_I am thankful that you saved us the trouble of hunting you down. You will receive no mercy here. You die now for your treason, and your destruction will only add to my glory._
Step aside, Varoche. I will not be stopped.
He responds by making a chopping motion with his hand. His warriors start to circle to either side, flanking you.
You have heard wrong. I am no traitor.
_[N], you are a Hand of Avadon. If only for the honor of the Black Fortress, you should face your death with dignity. Admit what you have done and quietly accept my blow._
I can see that your mind is made up. I have no choice. (Attack.)
Viscount Varoche draws his blade and salutes you. Then he adopts an intimidating battle stance. His warriors, far less noble and dignified, simply shout and charge.
What exactly is my crime?
_I heard it from Duke Gryfyn's mouth. You are in league with the Tawon Empire. You murdered the Holklandan warriors to prevent him from making peace._
I am innocent.
_Are you? Perhaps. Anything is possible. However, it is not my decision to make. Duke Gryfyn is the lord of these lands, and he has said you are guilty. That ends my thinking about the matter._
What proof did Duke Gryfyn have?
_Proof? He is the duke. His word is all the proof I need. Surely a Hand, used to having your word taken as law, must understand._
Duke Gryfyn is the traitor, not I.

Viscount Varoche, who was calm and dignified until now, is enraged. _Is there no end to your treachery? To your treason? It is not enough to be caught and face death. You have to vomit lies and libel our noble lord! Enough!_
They show no more dignity or care. The warriors charge you, blades out, howling for your blood.
I have no more time. I must get by you.
Viscount Varoche draws his blade and salutes you. Then he adopts an intimidating battle stance. _Then, for one of us, it is the end. I will make sure that it is you._
He prepares for a duel. His warriors, far less noble and dignified, simply shout and charge.

Hand Gavin walks into the grove. He moves up to you quickly, taking in all of the carnage with a businesslike nod. _This is clearly the work of a Hand of Avadon. Quick. Clinical. Lethal. Such efficiency. It makes me feel ... humble. I miss it._
You note that he is armed, armored, and ready for battle. _Now that this lot is gone, the way is clear. We will move quickly now._
You directed me into an ambush.
_Perhaps. I ... Well, yes. I did. However, Varoche, for all of his arrogance, was cunning and deadly. We would have had no chance of slipping into Vebeaux with him and Melisande on the hunt._
_Now they are no longer problems._
Why didn't you help me?
_Because I had my own business to attend to._ He raps the chest of his plate armor with his knuckle. _I had to prepare. Now I am ready._
_After me. You will follow me, and I will lead you to Castle Vebeaux. Then I will guide you to the pylon._
'We' will move quickly?
_Indeed. I have had a change of heart. Words do not suffice. I will lead you to Castle Vebeaux. Then I will guide you to the pylon._
You wish to come with me?
_More than wish it. I will come. I know the route, and that knowledge wins me a place at your side._
Why did you decide to come?
_Because it was easier to live with my shame and disgrace when I only had to face brigands and scum. But seeing you, young, unbowed, the pride of Avadon, showed me how far I had sunk._
You wish to be a Hand again?
_I do. Serving Avadon, for all its flaws and compromises, is the most glorious destiny in all of the world. Someday, I must die. When I do, I will die a Hand._

_Now you follow me. I know all the hidden paths and back roads through these woods. Take the path I will now lead you to. Go to Castle Vebeaux and meet me to the north of the main road. Then we will enter and hunt down the traitor together._
I have been betrayed too much already. Cross me, and you will pay.
Hand Gavin nods and laughs. _Understood._
I am not ready.

Hand Gavin starts to respond, but he is interrupted by the distant sounds of horns and shouting. _Yes you are. You have no choice. There is no time. Come on._ He turns and walks away, expecting you to follow.
Lead on.
Hand Gavin starts to respond, but he is interrupted by the distant sounds of horns and shouting. _Good. We will not be left alone for long. Come on._ He turns and walks away, expecting you to follow.
Sorceress Eponine
Dreya the Farsighted
Sorceress Cosette
Avgard Half-Soul
Kellem Watcher
A sentry blows his horn. You can hear the soldiers setting out to hunt you.
Viscount Varoche lets out a stirring battle cry. All of his nearby allies fight with far greater skill.
Cahil, The Claw
Drake Ssschalor
Ancient Specter
Crumbling Construct
Mining Construct
A construct has taken too much damage. It starts to fall apart before your eyes.
Sandwolf
Wastes Hellhound
Debtbound Guard
Caravan Guard
Debtbound Kva
Mert the Debtbound
Yelisa
Ancient Firebat
Ogre Pit Seer
Cahil's Archer
You are not needed here.
Please go.
I speak for us.
Another Hand comes.
Lots of Hands about.
Someone with money?
Let's trade!
I'm buying and selling.
Kva Brigand
Kva Cultist
From this side, you easily spot a concealed path through the thicket.

You have reached the White Plains, a desolate and remote region of the southern Kva. Something in the sand makes it pale and chalky. The hardy cacti that infest most of the region can grow here. Very little else can.
And yet, the region is far from unsettled. You see the tracks of the occasional predator, enjoying the ability to hunt far from the Pact's hunters.
There is also a path leading to the south. There are bootprints and wagon tracks. Perhaps that is where Sevilin went ...

Behind you, you hear someone shout an angry obscenity. Someone pushed aside a large, dead cactus, revealing a concealed pathway. A thorn in his hand caused him to spoil much of the surprise of the attack.
Several brigands push their way out of the thicket. They must have seen you pass and decided that you were a tempting target.
The pathway curves around a small oasis. Animals from all over the area come here to drink. Their tracks are everywhere, extending to the water and then back into the thickets.

To the east, you can see a small pack of wolves resting near the water. That must be the side favored by predators. On the west side, you see a few sickly cows. A wolf occasionally and half-heartedly crosses sides to snarl at potential prey.
The trail you have been following ends at a small settlement. It's a small cluster of buildings deep in the wastes, far too small to be considered a town.

A few guards hide behind the palisade. They aren't Pact soldiers. Their armor is crude and their weapons are bent and dirty. And yet, it's not a brigand settlement either. They don't move to attack or otherwise hinder you when you approach.
A sign by the entrance says, _Debtbound Colony._ Perhaps someone here can tell you what that means. And, with luck, where Sevilin went.
You find another oasis, of sorts. The nearby stream feeds several pools of stagnant water here. Sickly marsh reeds grow out of the chalky soil. The smell of rot is heavy in the air.
A pathway leads through the fen to the north. There are no signs of human activity to the east. Unless gnawed bones scattered all over the ground count.

There are no human tracks in this area of the fen, only bones and large, clawed footprints. Something large and nasty lurks out this way, a creature the humans have had the wisdom to just leave alone.

You have discovered another of the Kva's old, abandoned mines. There are tracks running along the ground, rotting pilings crossing rusting bars. Blown drifts of dirt have covered most of the piles of ore, and two tents of crumbling canvas are the only sign of the workers who toiled here.
And yet, the mine isn't entirely abandoned. There are fresh footprints running along the trail. And, as you look more closely, one of the trapdoors to the north opens.
A lone man climbs out of it. He rises slowly, because his left hand is crippled and useless. He looks very familiar ...
There is a lone pillar of stone in this clearing. It is old and cracked. It is also covered with intricate carved writing, most of it still legible despite the pillar's great age.
Sevilin says, _It's part of the Stone Code. The part having to do with debts and servitude, most likely. Old. Probably outdated. Who knows how they got it?_
Several of the debtbound cluster around it, reading the law of The Kva and trying to find a way out of their predicament.

You enter the old mines through the northern trapdoor. Abandoned mines are, of course, extremely dangerous. You immediately inspect the support pilings. There are traces of rot, but you think that you can proceed with only a small chance of being buried under hundreds of tons of rock.

There are no signs of the bandits you are hunting. They must be hiding in a different part of the mine, maybe even far below your feet. However, you aren't alone here. There is a powerful reek in the air. Something has settled in here.
Beside you, Sevilin can barely keep still. His enthusiasm for burrowing deep into these crumbling, monster-infested tunnels is worryingly high.
Here, deep in the mines, you find a statue standing in the center of a crude chamber. It is a lumpy, humanoid thing. It is covered with cracks, and something has worn its hands down into crude clubs.
Then the statue slowly turns and looks at you. Bits of stone and dead lichen slough off of it as it moves to face you.

You have heard of constructs like this. Inexpensive, unpredictable magic, used to burrow out deep tunnels without need of fragile humanoids. Pact law requires that such constructs never be left alone, lest the simple magics that control them go awry.
In this case, such laws were clearly not obeyed.
At last, you have found your way down to the hidden lair of Cahil's bandits. A small group of them are standing in this storeroom, sorting through (and arguing over) the results of their raids.

Then one of them sees you, and they instantly leap into action. All but one of them draw their weapons and move to intercept you. The last of their number runs to the east, determined to make sure Cahil knows you have arrived.
Khura the Hunted

The sound of a horn breaks the stillness of the mine. The sound echoes through the tunnels, rapidly proceeding from loud to deafening. The vibrations knock rocks from the ceiling and make the ground vibrate under your feet.

Your training instantly kicks in. You clap your hands over your ears and concentrate on remaining standing. When trapped by offensive magic like this, the most important thing is simply to stay alert and conscious.
Then the sound ceases, leaving you feeling dizzy and confused. And then you hear another, less welcome noise. The shouting of the bandits, coming to make one attempt to drive you from their hideout.
Terah the Hornbearer
The trapdoor is thick oaken beams, held together with steel bands. You try to open it, but it has been barred below. Smashing it open would probably just collapse the aging tunnel underneath.
If you want to hunt Cahil, you'll have to find another way in.
This wheel once pulled a chain that lifted baskets of rubble out of the mine. The mechanism has long since rusted into immobility.
The cows by this oasis are sickly, miserable creatures. However, when a potential threat gets close, you are surprised by how quickly they can move.
The guards of this small settlement are more of a militia. The refugees here take turns taking up weapons and watching the palisades. Any wolf that gets too close is pelted with javelins.

The presence of warriors from outside makes them extremely nervous. They all become very grim and quiet when you get close. They suggest that, if you have any questions, you should talk to Mert, in the center building.

These debtbound are carefully reading, rereading, and rerereading the pillar, which contains a large section of the Stone Code. They are looking for some law, exception, or loophole that would give them some hope of leaving this miserable place.
You try to talk to them, but they avoid your gaze. Living here is a great source of shame to them.

There are several debtbound living in this dirty, remote settlement. Being a debt exile is a source of great shame for members of The Kva. They are cordial to you, but they avoid meeting your gaze. You don't learn anything from them.
There are two caravan guards sitting at this fire, watching hungrily as a merchant pokes at a haunch of roasting, unidentifiable meat. One of them says, _Yelisa does all the trading. Talk to her._
Sevilin approaches you and stands at your side. _[N], I must insist. As long as you hunt Cahil, I must be with you. This is my hunt too, and I will not be shamed by him again._
DEBTBOUND COLONY
All barred by the Code are welcome.
Collectors and criminals stay out!
_MOO!_
A hulking beast rises from the muck on the other side of the nest. Not an animal, oddly enough. It is the corpse of a titan, animated by some careless mage and then left to wander the wastes.

It is covered with moss and vines. Nobody has bothered to disturb it out here for some time. When you get close, it lets out a long, gurgling moan, shakes off the debris, and lurches mindlessly toward you.

When you get close to the stone construct, it turns and lumbers toward you, worn hands outstretched. Somewhere in its simple, magically-created mind, it has mistaken you as a bunch of dirt that needs to be dug out.
What is more worrying is the falling stones and stomping feet you hear to the south. There is more than one construct down here.
The constructs are not alone. There is a creature that lives with them, using them as protection. It is a young drake, and it probably used its own magic to take control of the lumbering statues.
When it sees you, it lets out a long, angry hiss. _Ahssss ... Cahil told me it would keep such pestsss out! When you are dead and eaten, I will have an angry talk with that little human!_
You grab the old, rusting wheel and try to turn it. You get a good grip and pull it as hard as you can.
You turn it around twice, pulling a chain out of a hole in the ground. You hear grinding and feel the floor vibrate.
Nothing else happens, so you turn it the other direction. The chain lowers back into the ground. The ground vibrates again. You hear the sound of flowing water to the west.
The wheel refuses to budge.
An ancient spirit swoops toward you, howling and screeching. Years in this pit have left this creature with a mindless hatred of the living.
The miners and brigands have been wise enough to leave the undead in these tunnels alone. Sadly, you have blundered right into them.
The specter lets out a piercing howl. You feel paralyzed with fear.
The specter waves its arms in a strange, elaborate pattern. A magical barrier surrounds it. It has a strange, reflective quality. You can see yourself in it.

There is an old man sitting in this chair, staring into the fire. He is trying to simply blend into the background, but you note that all of the other people here constantly look to him, hoping for advice or guidance.
When you approach him, he regretfully rises to greet you. _I am Mert. Mert the Debtbound. It is unfortunate that you have come here. I hope that you will depart soon, and leave us to our shame._
Mert the Debtbound stands quietly nearby. His years out here in the wastes have left him tired and thin, and the skin on his face bears the ravages of decades of sun. You try not to look too close.
What is this colony?
_It is what you see. A group of people, poor and desperate, keeping close together in hope of safety. We are lost, and we prefer to be left alone in our shame._
Are you the leader?
_We have no leader. None of us are worthy of commanding others, even others as low as ourselves. However, my many years here have caused my words to be greeted with respect._
How long have you been out here?
_Over thirty years. I have long since given up hope of returning to the respect of The Kva. Instead, I live here and do what I can for other unfortunates._
Who comes here?
_The debtbound, and all who face shame in the eyes of the Stone Code._
Do criminals come here?
_No. Or, when they do, we turn them out. We take those who are shamed by debt, slander, or other causes. There are ways to run afoul of the Stone Code without committing a crime._
Do you think the Stone Code is just?

Mert looks slightly offended. _Of course! It brings stability and safety to our lives! It is not the fault of the Code that I took on the debts that drove me here. It only declared the just punishment for my failings._
Mert looks very uncomfortable. _There is only one thing you can do for us, Hand of Avadon._
_Leave. Leave us to our privacy and our shame._
_And take the other Hand with you too, if you please._
What is a debtbound?
_It is what it looks like. It is one who owes money and cannot repay it. The Stone Code declares punishment for those who fail to pay their debts._
_The Kva has many colonies like this one. The debtbound can then come here to be safe while they decide what to do._
What are the penalties for being in debt?
_The Stone Code, in its wisdom, gives several choices. Repayment. Temporary, absolute servitude. Or shameful exile into the waste until the debt is repaid._
_This is such a colony. For the shamed._
Do you think this is a good way to handle the problem?
_Of course. In Holklanda, those too lost in debt tend to be killed. In Dharam, those in debt are enslaved. Same in Kellemderiel, though the slaves are fed better food._
_Life is harsh here, but it could be worse._
How long do people stay here?
_Not long. Sometimes, they find a way to earn the money to pay back the debt. Others find this life harsh and choose solitude._
_Most only last here a few years before they choose a new path. None here have lasted as long as me._
Why have you stayed here so long?
_My debt is too large. My shame too great. Also, I have a life here helping those who are lost. It is hard, but satisfying. Here I will remain. Here I will die._
I am looking for a Hand of Avadon.
_Yes. Sevilin. I had hoped that someone would come for him. His presence upsets us._
How does he upset you?
_He asks questions we do not want to answer, and he will not respect our silence. Also, the presence of Avadon is never safe. Who among us is truly innocent?_
_In the southern building. Alone. None would share quarters with him. Our shame is too great. Please, I beg you, take him and go._ He waves you away.
I want to find the brigand Cahil. Where is he?
Mert is not surprised by this most unwelcome question. The other debtbound grow silent. Everyone is grim. _Sevilin asked. We would not answer. You ask. We still will not answer._
_I ask you, please go. Do not hunt The Claw._
Sevilin is furious, but he says nothing. He stays back and lets you speak.
The Claw?
_That is what he is called. His hand is burnt and twisted._
Why won't you answer?
_Because Cahil does us no harm, and I fear that he will have revenge on us for betraying him. Also, the presence of The Claw scares away those who would take advantage of our weakness._
That is not good enough.
Mert tries to maintain his composure, but his hands start to shake. _We are low creatures, but we have done nothing to deserve this. Please, I implore you, do not make us betray Cahil._
I am a Hand of Avadon. Tell me what I need to know, or you will all pay.
Mert bows his head, defeated. _We lose our safety and our protector. We have no choice._
He points to the northeast. _There is a hidden trail. By all of the barrels. That path leads to him. That is all I know._
_There. Now you have all. Leave us._ Shaking uncontrollably, he turns away.
All right. I am going. (Leave.)
Mert thanks you. You turn and walk away.
Sevilin says, _I will return to Avadon if you wish, but, if you will not help me avenge what has been done to me and mine, I will not forget it._
All right. I will respect your wishes.
The bandit Cahil is gone.
Mert nods. _We know. Some of his men fled this way. They passed by quickly, and they did nothing more than steal some food. We will not be punished, but we don't have their protection._
_I hope you will go. There is nothing more for you here. Please leave._ He turns away.
There is a merchant sitting by this low, smoky fire, roasting a haunch of some animal or other. It almost smells delicious. She seems surprised to see you.
_Well, it's ... You're a Hand, aren't you? Another one? I don't see what has made the White Plains so terribly important in the eyes of the Pact, but I would be glad to have customers with money._
_I am Yelisa. I would be happy to trade with you._
Yelisa sits by the fire, poking at her stringy, half-burned haunch of meat. _Need anything? A customer with actual money to spend is a rare privilege out here._
_This place? It's for the debtbound. People who owe more money than they can pay. The Stone Code gives them two choices. Servitude, or exile in miserable little pits like this one._
I'd like to know more about the debtbound.
She nods toward the building to the east. _Talk to Mert. He's sort of the leader here. I don't talk about law if I can help it._
Why do you come here?
_It's on my route. It's a safe place to stop. Sometimes, they buy things. Not enough to go out of my way for, but if I'm here ..._
Your customers don't normally have money?
_Not here. This lot is poor, but that doesn't stop them from buying a few things. Tools. Weapons._
What sort of tools?
_Any sort. They use them to make crafts, or to earn money clearing back the cacti for the towns. They hope to earn enough money to pay off their debts and go home. Sometimes, they even succeed._
They buy weapons?
_Yes. That's one of the reasons I come here. No matter how useless or banged up a blade is, I can always get a few coins for it here. Helps them keep the predators back._
She rises and walks over to her wagons. _It would be a pleasure!_
Yelisa's Caravan
Yelisa mainly carries tools and raw supplies, though she occasionally trades in potions and other such items of interest.
_Then I wish you safe travels. Always an honor to meet a Hand._
She nods. _He is here. Makes all the debtbound good and nervous, he does. He's in one of the halls. Don't know which one._
I'm looking for a brigand. Name is Cahil.
Yelisa suddenly becomes a lot less friendly. _Cahil ... Never heard of him. Never. Don't know a thing about him. Can't talk. Need to tend to our meal._
She turns away from you, making a big show of poking at the roasting haunch of meat.
As you leave Cahil's chambers, you look over at Sevilin. He seems stunned. He walks as if he's just received a punishing blow to the head. Which, in a sense, he has.
_Pardoned,_ he mutters. _Pardoned. I saw my friends lying in pools of their own blood. Hands. Members of the brotherhood. Pardoned._
We had to let Cahil go. He had our word.
_Had to? Because of the ... the honor of Avadon? What honor was there in this? You had to let him go. I did not._
_[N], I will fight by your side. I will help you follow orders. But I will never forgive this._ And then he is silent.
But you were avenged.
_Yes. In spite of Avadon, not because of it. Not with the support we needed. Alone, forsaken ..._ He shakes his head.
_[N], thank you for your help. I will be ever grateful. But I have much to think about ..._ And then he is silent.
We must trust Redbeard.
_Must we? Before today, I would have said yes. And now? When he releases our murderers? I ... I don't know anymore._
_[N], thank you for ... for coming with me. Watching my back. But I have much to think about ..._ And then he is silent.
Pardoning him was wrong.
_And yet, it was done. Redbeard did it. Cahil killed Hands and was allowed to run free. Nobody will question it. None will question Redbeard. Except for ... for ..._ He shakes his head.
At last, Cahil lies dead before you. Sevilin's long hunt has come to an end. He gives the body a vicious kick. Then he spits on it.
Then he turns to you. _Thank you, [N]. I could not have done this without you. I am free at last. Ready to ... to ..._
And then he looks at Cahil's scroll of pardon, lying on the floor in a pool of blood. He remembers what he has learned. Confused, he turns and walks away.
Cahil staggers, wounded. He hisses, _Yes, I killed the Hands. I loved it. I would do it again. Curse Avadon! Your Black Fortress will burn soon! I didn't say all I learned!_
Then he takes a potion from his belt. Before you can stop him, he drinks it. _I will take one of you with me,_ he roars!
You challenge one of Cahil's brigands, but she doesn't respond. She stands her ground, aiming an arrow at your chest.
You thrash at the thicket here and find that Mert was not lying. Clearing away the cacti leaves you multiply impaled by sharp spines, but you eventually manage to reveal a narrow, concealed pathway.

Shima Threespear looks down the dark mine shaft with distaste. He mutters, _Years of study in the art of infiltration. A thousand lessons on how best to study a target. Living the dream of the perfect, quick, quiet, stealthy assassination._
_And here we are, blundering through the front entrance as usual. I will never be used to the ways of Avadon._
Jenell puts her hand on Sevilin's shoulder. _I am sorry about what you learned down there. Avadon sometimes ... Avadon does not know who it is supposed to serve._
Sevilin nods. _I thank you, but I ... I have much to ponder. For now, I have made an oath to Avadon. I will continue to follow it. For now._
Then they are silent. There is little else to say.
Nathalie puts her hand on Sevilin's shoulder. _I am sorry. Cahil was our rightful prey, but Redbeard did what he must. I'm sure he has learned of more glorious targets for us to hunt._

Sevilin smiles. _I know you mean those words to be kind, but not all of us are as excited by the hunt as you. There are other principles in play here. Justice, for one. ... I have much to ponder. I have made an oath to Avadon. I will continue to follow it. For now._

This old, dirty hall has enough room for well over a dozen of the debtbound to live here, dry and out of the sun. However, there is only one man here, sitting on a filthy pallet with his back to you. Everyone else has left.
When you get close, he looks over his shoulder at you. His face lights up. Sevilin jumps to his feet and grabs your hand.
_I ... I am not sure what to say. I am ... I am glad you are here, [N]. Pleased, and ashamed as well._
This hall is empty. Where is everyone else?
_They fled. They avoid me wherever I go. They are a beaten, ashamed people. The gaze of Avadon burns too hot for them._
What is this place?
_It is a colony of the debtbound, people of The Kva who owe money and cannot repay it._
_The Stone Code gives them a choice. They can flee to settlements like this, or they can enter harsh servitude. They are given a choice. It is the justice of the Code._
What have you done since you left?
_I tracked Cahil to here. It took cunning, bribery, and harsh questioning, but I found him. He is nearby._
_And yet, that is as close as I have come. He is here. I can smell him. And yet, the people here refuse to give me the final directions I need._
Why are they scared of you?
_They feel that Avadon is looking for any excuse to crush them. As if Avadon cares a whit for these wretches!_
Why won't they help you?
_Because they fear retribution, I think. They are terrified that Cahil will crush them if they speak with Avadon. And, perhaps, they are correct in this._
And now what will you do?
Sevilin rises and walks up to you. _I will hunt down Cahil. The Claw, they call him. I have sworn vengeance on him._
What makes you so sure Cahil is nearby?

_Do not ask me the favors I had to call in, the harsh steps I had to take. From them, I learned he was in this area. Questioning the debtbound here, seeing the fear in their eyes, I know that I am close._
_This is the place, but we must act before he flees._
You still want to hunt Cahil?

_He and his brigands attacked me and my fellow Hands when we were on patrol. Only I survived. For this, he must pay. If Avadon cannot punish such a crime, it can do nothing. And yet, I can't hunt him down alone. [N], will you help me?_
Shima nods. _I understand too well what it is to be unjustly attacked. There are those upon whom I would take revenge if given the chance. I would stand by you, Sevilin._
Jenell looks worried. _I don't believe in increasing the power of Avadon more than I have to. And yet, we do need to hunt down those who would hunt us._
Nathalie grins. _I have spent years rotting away in the Black Fortress, waiting to be called for the hunt. I would love another chance to show my skills._
Cahil has to die for what he has done.
Sevilin nods. _Well said, [N]. Spoken like a true Hand of Avadon._

_I will be honored to have you by my side in the hunt. First, we should speak with Mert. That debtbound might be more willing to tell us what we need to know if he has to face multiple Hands, instead of just one._
We can hunt Cahil. Briefly.
Sevilin nods. _I appreciate that, [N]. And yet, I note your hesitance. I hope this will not take long, but you must know that I will bring Cahil to justice if it is the last thing that I do._
_First, we should speak with Mert. That debtbound might be more willing to tell us what we need to know if he has to face multiple Hands, instead of just one._
We must return to Avadon. You've neglected your duties long enough.
Sevilin looks stricken. _But, [N], I ... I will submit. For now. Know this, though._
_I will bring Cahil to justice if it is the last thing that I do. Until this is done, I will never be able to fully serve Redbeard. Or you, or anyone._
You walk into the thicket of cacti. The path is narrow. The thorny plants rise above your head to either side. Natural territory for an ambush.
And yet, Sevilin seems in high spirits. He has a spring in his step and a smile on his face.
Sevilin, pay close attention.
Sevilin nods. _Do not be fooled. I have never been so alert. When I fought Cahil before, I was young. I made mistakes. We all did._
_Now I am ready. As eager for the hunt as Nathalie. I will never have to be scared of Cahil again._
_Better than all right. Thrilled. Ready. As eager for the hunt as Nathalie. Before Cahil dies, he will see how much I have learned._
_I have dreamed of this day. Soon, I will never have to be scared of Cahil again.
Why are you so happy?
_Because I am on the hunt, and because I am ready. The first time I fought Cahil, I was young. Untrained. Easy prey._
_I know much now that I did not know then. He will not find me to be a safe target now._

You approach the brigand standing by the open trapdoor. It doesn't take long for you to recognize him. He is the thug with the scarred hand that you overheard when you entered the ogre-infested mines in the Jhereth Deeps.
He seems strangely unconcerned when you approach. His good hand rests on the pommel of his blade, but he doesn't draw it. He must not recognize you.

He says, _Ahhh ... The Hands arrive. The debtbound made sure that I knew of it. You have no friends out here. I am Cahil, known as The Claw to some._ He waves his burned hand limply at you. _Why have you come here?_
The debtbound told you that I was coming?
_One of them did. I will not say who. Trust me, those poor fools would much rather see me in their camp than a Hand of Avadon._
The debtbound told me where to find you.
_Of course, and I will not punish them for it. I've already given the word to my allies. I know that they cannot refuse a Hand. I have nothing to worry about from you, anyway._
I am [N], Hand of Avadon, and you will pay for your crimes.
Those words would be enough to inspire pure terror in just about anyone in Lynaeus. And yet, Cahil seems unconcerned. _I admire your determination, Hand, but ... but ..._
Then he looks at Sevilin. His calm exterior fades away, replaced by a look of sudden, great concern. _You ... I know you. Yes. I know you._
You don't recognize us? Any of us?
Cahil smirks. Then, to humor you, he inspects your faces closely.
From when you murdered the Hands with him, perhaps?
Cahil's fear increases visibly with every moment you talk to him. It is very satisfying. _You ... You! The one who lived! And you spent all this time hunting me? Yes ... Of course you did._
_And you came all this way to what? Kill me?_
Keep thinking. It'll come to you.

He doesn't have to think for long. He looks at Sevilin. The arrogance leaves his eyes, replaced by terror. It is very satisfying. _You ... You! The one who lived! And you spent all this time hunting me? Yes ... Of course you did._
(Wait silently.)

You don't have to wait long. He looks at Sevilin. The arrogance leaves his eyes, replaced by terror. It is very satisfying. _You ... You! The one who lived! And you spent all this time hunting me? Yes ... Of course you did._
Or bring you back to Avadon.
_Where I would die, before torture or after. I know what happens to those who kill Hands. But ... You can't. You just can't. You must know that? No ... You obviously don't._
He is talking faster and faster, rapidly working himself up into a panic.
Yes. Killing you was the plan.
_I thought as much. I would not believe you if you said otherwise. But ... You can't. You just can't. You must know that? No ... You obviously don't._
You are babbling.
He keeps talking to himself, ignoring you. _No ... Show them? Tell them? No. It won't matter. Not unless ... No. Better to hide. Safest way. They would tear it up if they saw it._
He looks up at you, about to say something. But then he closes his mouth, takes a step to the right, and falls down through the open trapdoor.
What do you mean, I can't?

_Well, I will tell you. I ... I ... I can't tell you. I can't. You wouldn't believe me. You are here for blood. I see it in your eyes. And if I did show it to you? You would tear it up, and I would be lost. But ... But ..._
He seems to be about to say something else. But then he closes his mouth, takes a step to the right, and falls down through the open trapdoor.
Well, I could just leave. If it was worthwhile.
Cahil nods. _Yes ... Yes ... That is what is supposed to happen. Go. Just go. I will ... Will ...
(Attack him.)
You lunge toward the open trapdoor, but it slams closed moments after Cahil falls down through it.
Sevilin roars in anger. _Coward! I will get you! I'm coming for you! I'm coming!_
Wait!
You shout at Cahil, but he doesn't respond. The trapdoor slams closed moments after Cahil falls down through it.

At last, you corner Cahil in this hall in the lowest level of the mine. It is an odd chamber, centuries old. A small, crumbling throne room, with a rough granite chair and a rotting carpet. The miners probably uncovered it when they were burrowing into the earth.

Cahil is not in the throne. He is standing by the east wall, surrounded by his surviving archers. He is holding a sword in his surviving hand. The twisted stump that is his left arm holds a scroll against his chest.

When you enter his hall, the bandits look terrified, and understandably so. Sevilin is ready to charge into their midst. However, Cahil is not ready to give up hope. He says, _So ... You found us. I knew, the moment I recognized you, that you would not be turned away easily._
_Before you do anything rash, however, there is something you must know._
Speak quickly, and then prepare to die.
Cahil nods. _You are wise to wait. You won't be fighting me today. You can't._
He nods. One of his archers takes the scroll from him and throws it to you. It lands at your feet.
No, no more tricks or delays. (Attack.)
You prepare to charge, only to find that Sevilin is standing still. His weapon is out, but he is staring at Cahil's scroll. He says, _My vengeance can wait a few moments more._
Cahil nods. _Wisely said._ One of his archers takes the scroll from him and throws it to you. It lands at your feet.
What sort of trick is this?
_No trick. No spell. Only a message. From your master._
I am not going to read that.
Now Cahil looks really worried. _You must. It is an order. For you. You must read it! You must!_
Then, before you can respond, Sevilin picks up the scroll and unrolls it.
(Get the scroll.)
You pick up the scroll and unroll it. Sevilin watches you intently.
At the top of the scroll is the seal of Avadon. At the bottom is the mark of Redbeard. Sevilin says, _[N], read it. Please._
Sevilin, don't do it.
Sevilin correctly judges that something is not right here. He ignores you and looks at the scroll. He skims it. Then he looks more closely. Then he gives it to you. His hands are shaking.
At the top of the scroll is the seal of Avadon. At the bottom is the mark of Redbeard. Sevilin says, _[N], read it. You must._
What does it say?
Sevilin skims the scroll. Then he looks more closely. Then he gives it to you. His hands are shaking.
(Read the scroll.)

_Cahil - You are a criminal, the murderer of my Hands. However, the knowledge you have given is of value. The information about the Jhereth Deeps and the presence of the Tawon was worthwhile. Had you joined them, you would be dead now._
_For Avadon to survive, we must aid those who aid us. I pardon you for your crimes, as long as you avoid my servants. Hide, creature. Cross me again, and you will be brought before me. - Redbeard._
(Look at Sevilin.)
The young blademaster trembles. His sword falls from his hand. He looks at Redbeard's seal, pardoning Cahil. _It ..._ He stammers. _It is real. That ... pardon ... It happened._
Cahil almost looks sympathetic. _Yes. I am free. You can't kill me. I have Avadon's word that I will be allowed to live, in return for my service as their spy._
Why didn't you show this to me outside?
_Because I thought you would ignore it. Maybe even tear it up, though I need it to survive. I thought I might evade you. That didn't work._
You killed several Hands.

_I did, but they were young and dumb and clumsy. I hate to say it, but it is true. We would never have been able to defeat competent servants of Avadon. They would have died eventually, one way or another._
Sevilin whispers, _It is true. It doesn't matter. You must answer for it._
I still have to decide what to do with you.
Both Cahil and Sevilin look at you with alarm. Cahil says, _But you saw it yourself. It bears Redbeard's seal! Avadon gave me its word! You can't kill me without giving up your master's honor!_
Sevilin says, _We can't let him go. Redbeard is ... He is wrong. Cahil murdered Hands. Several of them! Avadon's honor is useless if we won't protect our own!_
Cahil hastens to add, _And, if you let me go, I will pay you. A lavish reward. Not that I owe it to you, but I will give it to you anyway in return for our lives._
Sevilin, he does have Avadon's word.
He shakes his head, barely hearing you. _I saw this ... this worm cut down my ... Please, [N]. Don't do this. Don't free him. I could not ... not forgive you._
Sevilin, you say Cahil should be punished?
_Of course he should! Am I the only one who sees it? Am I the only one who is not mad? We are Avadon! We do what we want, we kill who we want, and we must look out for our own!_
Cahil, keep your bribe. Just go.
Cahil and his brigands don't hesitate. They grab their weapons and run through the door to the north. In less than a minute, they are gone.
Surprisingly, Sevilin does nothing to stop them. He stands perfectly still, staring at a point on the floor. He knows that his hope of vengeance is gone. And his faith in Avadon with it.
Finally, you are alone in the crumbling stone hall. There is nothing more to do here.
Cahil, pay me. Then you can go.

Cahil and his brigands don't hesitate. There is a bag on the floor behind him. He picks it up and dumps out a steel breastplate. Then they grab their weapons and run through the door to the north. In less than a minute, they are gone.
No, Cahil. You must die for what you have done.
Sevilin nods. Cahil looks horrified. _But ... A pardon ... From Redbeard himself!_ He spits at you. _Worms you are, no better than wretches. Avadon is nothing but lies! It has no honor! It ..._
He doesn't get to continue his tirade. Sevilin has finally had enough. With one battle howl, he lets out months of bottled up rage and terror. And then he charges ...
Animated Titan
Your blows have had an effect on the animated titan. To the extent that it can think, it is very angry. It swings at you in a berserk rage.
The moss-covered zombie draws energy from the swamp. It seems refreshed.
Dungeon Guard
Dungeon Eye
Eye Mamora
Terrified Prisoner
Ghroz
Snarling Rat
Lexrem
Prisoner
Armed Prisoner
Quennel
Quickghast
Master of Rats
Mad Prisoner
Such a mess!
We need more aid.
Watch for Shadow Tarkus.
Hands, at last.
Four prisoners remain lost.
So much chaos.
This is a mess.
And Tarkus gone? Hrmmm.
The sign says - Arrival Hall. All prisoners must be signed in!
The sign says - Dungeon Kitchen.
The sign says - SCRYING HALL.
The sign says - Recovery Rooms. Give prisoners fifteen minutes of recovery for one hour of scrying!
The sign says - Ceremonial Hall.
The sign says - HALL OF HONORED GUESTS
The sign says - Beast Holding Cells.
The sign says - Southern Cells.
The sign says - SECURE CELLS.
The sign says - To lower cells. CLOSED.
The sign says - LOWER CELLS. Closed by order of the Keeper! Do not proceed without a helmet!
The sign says - HOLDING CAVE 1.
The sign says - HOLDING CAVE 2.
The sign says - HEROM OF THE KVA.
The sign says - TELERA. KEEPER.
The sign says - DIANTHA OF DHARAM.
The sign says - GEERT. KEEPER.

You stand at the doors into the Avadon Dungeons, possibly the most terrifying place in Lynaeus. The most dangerous conspirators against the Pact are brought here. Every once in a while, one of them emerges again.
It is dark down here. In the absence of guards, the lights have gone out. Happily, several lamps have been left on the table nearby.
(Get a lamp. Once it's in your pack, press the Star button next to it to use it. You can use scrolls and potions in the same way.)

You walk into the dungeon. Normally, the torches would be lit and heavily armed guards would be standing at attention. The jailers would be waiting to collect and process new inmates. And there wouldn't be giant rats everywhere.
But the disaster upstairs has left everything abandoned. You can hear shouting and snarling in the distance, but the entry chamber is cold and dark.

But not still. As you step onto the walkway, little pairs of lights appear in the shadows to the south. Then they start to move toward you. With the guards gone, the pests in the tunnels far below Avadon have started to emerge ...
Suddenly, a reassuring light appears to the north. Someone has just lit a torch. He shouts, _Is that support at last? Come here, quickly!_
(This is a good time to save the game if you haven't already.)

You emerge into a large office. A fence rings an area with desks and shelves heavy with records. New inmates are brought here and sat down, while scribes record their arrival, crime, and recommended processing.

There are some chains and cages, usually used for wild beasts and monsters in need of examination. When humans are brought here, they are usually just left on the benches. Few are foolish enough to think they can escape from this place.
There is a man in a leather jerkin standing by the far desk. He waves at you. _A Hand, at last! Hurry!_
As you get close to the exit from the offices, you see that someone has left two healing potions for you. They sit on the table.

(If you are heavily damaged in combat, you can use one of these potions to restore yourself. Put them in your pack. Open your inventory and press the Star button by a potion to use it. You can also place potions in Quick Use slots to use them from the main game screen.)
This is a wide natural cavern. It must have been discovered years after Avadon was constructed. It was then converted into one of the feared workshops of the Black Fortress.
There are about a dozen stone tables scattered about the room. Each has restraints, a glowing, enchanted stone, a chair, and materials for taking notes.

It is here that the prisoners of Avadon are brought, so that the Eyes can use powerful magic to pull the thoughts out of their minds. Once here, a prisoner has no secrets. Everything they planned, everyone they conspired with, all of that precious information goes straight to Redbeard.

This room is far older than the other parts of the dungeon. It looks like it dates back to the earliest days of Avadon. It seems to be some sort of ceremonial chamber. Perhaps rituals of great import, like the swearing in of new Keepers, happen here.
Alas, before it can be used for anything dignified, it will require quite a cleaning. The escaped wretches to the south have been acting in an aggressively disgusting way here.
There is an elaborate, glowing rune carved on the floor in front of this door. Motes of light rise from the rune and float into the door.
This is powerful warding magic. Without some tool to help you pass the rune, this enchantment will make it extremely difficult to open the door.

When you enter this cavern, you stop for a moment, amazed. It is a huge, natural dome, dominated by a strong natural spring. The builders of the Black Fortress must have known this chamber was here. If Avadon is ever under siege, it will not lack for water.

This chamber is not part of the dungeon. There is a wide shaft in the ceiling over the center of the room. Large, dried-up scales litter the floor, and the walkways are covered with deep claw marks. This is a guest room for particularly large and notable visitors to Avadon. Dragons, for example.
No such beasts are in residence at the moment. However, on the stone dome rising in the middle of the spring, you can see a lone human. She watches your approach.

You enter the secure cells of Avadon, where the more cunning and dangerous prisoners are stored. It is deathly quiet. All of the nearby cell doors are open. This area seems to have been evacuated until everything is back under control.

You start to go back upstairs. Then you realize that abandoning a mission in such chaotic circumstances is not a good way to begin your time in Avadon. With regret, you return to the dank corridors of the dungeons.
You should report your successes to Eye Mamora.
Several guards and Eyes have returned to the dungeons. They work on securing the cells, tidying up the records, and getting things functioning again.
They are very busy, however, too much so to talk. They suggest that you speak with Eye Mamora.

There is a pale, shaking prisoner hiding in this room. This inmate has been held here for a while. All desire to fight or escape from the might of Avadon is completely gone. Your attempts at conversation are met with terrified babbling.
The prisoner doesn't match the description of anyone you were sent to find, so you leave.
You hear a loud clattering as you return to the scrying room. A portcullis to the southeast slowly opens.
Odd. It's as if someone was inviting you in.
You hear an ominous clanging sound, echoing through the stone halls.
Several prisoners have been placed back into these cells. They are a pale, twitchy, demoralized lot. There is little to be gained from speaking to them.
There is a wheel in this alcove. Its wood is rotting, and the chains are rusting.
Still, with some effort, you are able to turn it a full rotation before it becomes irreparably stuck. Something creaks loudly to the west.
You try to turn it, but it is stuck.
Hmmm. This corridor ends with a locked gate. Maybe the jailer you passed on the way in can help you to get through it.

The last Eye on duty in the dungeons walks up to you. He is an aging man with a thick leather jerkin and a broadsword held awkwardly in his hand. He nods to you. _I am Eye Mamora of Holklanda, master of the Avadon dungeons._
_I am pleased to see you, though I confess I thought that I might have been aided earlier. And, I might add, with more force. But we will do what we must._
Eye Mamora stands stiffly with his back to the wall, waiting for more aid. He is prepared to defend himself against rats or vengeance-seeking prisoners.
Now that the dungeons are secured, Eye Mamora has gotten to work restoring order to the records. He makes big 'X' marks on the papers for prisoners that were killed.
You are the master of the dungeons?
He nods somberly. _I am. That is why I stayed when the others fled. It is my duty to stay and fight. In safer times, I look out for the prisoners. I keep them safe, which we need to do._
_And I pull from them the information that Redbeard requires to protect the Pact._
You keep the prisoners safe?
_Of course. We protect them while we learn what we must from them. We don't starve them or put them in unsafe circumstances. And then, if we don't need to execute them, we leave them untouched._
_The ordered way that I run these dungeons is a great point of pride for me._
Do prisoners ever leave?

He nods. _Of course. We always make it clear to our prisoners they have a chance to leave unharmed. All we need is all useful information they possess. And, of course, we need to believe that they no longer threaten the Pact._
_If this is the case, we send them home to serve as a valuable example of the might of Avadon._
And if you don't send them back?
_All true threats to the Pact are slain in a quick and merciful manner. Their ashes are then promptly returned to their families, so that they are not left in an unpleasant state of doubt._
Do you supervise the torture of the prisoners?
Eye Mamora looks shocked. _Torture? Where do you think you are? The Tawon Empire? Svorgald? Do I look like an ogre to you? Torture is crude and ineffective._
_Under torture, prisoners say whatever they must to make the pain stop. This is, often, not the truth. Redbeard requires truth._
How do you get information from prisoners?
_We secure them firmly to a table. Then we use the scrying magic developed by Avadon's finest mages to extract their thoughts. There is no lying, no escape._

_We read prisoners until we know all we must. And we look deep within the inmate's soul to see if he or she has been properly terrified and broken. Or, alternately, if the prisoner is still a threat._
How long does the process take?
_Weeks. Even months. The soul is large and dark and full of hidden corners. Happily, the masters of the dungeon work hard._
_Hopefully,_ he adds bitterly, _they will soon return to get back to their work. They fled after the disaster._
Does this harm the prisoner?

_No. Not at all. Now, some are a bit dazed when they leave here. Easily distracted. In a word, broken. But I think that is the result of their total defeat at the hands of Avadon, not of any actual harm suffered at our hands._
_But it does not matter. The safety of the Pact is at stake._
Are innocent people ever sent here?

_All the time. Many is the noble who has tried to rid himself of a rival by forging evidence and having the victim sent to Avadon. However, outsiders do not know of the effectiveness of our techniques. It is a closely held secret._
_In these cases, the victim is released, and the noble is cordially invited to spend some time on one of our tables._
What happens if you see that the prisoner will always fight you?
_Once we are sure? Death. Often, I simply don't allow them to wake up from the scrying. I direct one of the Eyes to simply end their thoughts. It is the quickest and most merciful of deaths._
Eye Mamora's absolute pride and confidence in his work is awe-inspiring. And slightly unnerving.
What happened down here?
_I am not sure. It is the result of something that happened above, something I still have not been informed about._
_There was an explosion upstairs, of a magical nature._

_A pulse of energy from upstairs disrupted our magical wards, enabling some prisoners and held creatures to escape. They, in turn, helped others out. There was, as you might expect, a fierce battle. Some prisoners fled._
Where is everyone now?
_Many of the prisoners are dead or were returned to their cells. Some keepers were slain. Others went upstairs to safety._
What threats remain?
_There are abandoned tunnels under Avadon, and some pests have taken this chance to emerge. They will need to be slain._
_Also, some prisoners are still loose on this level. Many of them will have been devoured by the pests. Others, however, will have to be hunted._
Have you had any progress finding the escaped prisoners?
_All is under control. I am proud to say that only one has escaped. There has been no sign of Shadow Tarkus. And yet, I am sure we will find him. None have ever escaped these dungeons for long._
Where did all the rats come from?
_The deep cells. There is a network of old tunnels and cells below the main dungeon that was abandoned and sealed off. It is a home for pests. Rats, spiders, other beasts that are sure to emerge._
Why haven't those cells been sealed off?
_We have considered expanding into them. Rebuilding, and so on. This disaster is making me reconsider those plans._
How can I go down there?
Eye Mamora points to the southeast. _The stairway down to the old tunnels is in the secure cells._
_However, I can't give you the key to the cells. You must obtain it from a superior. Such as, say, Hand Callan._
Miranda sent me to help you.

Eye Mamora nods. _It is overdue. Now that we are regaining full control of Avadon, it is time to retake the tunnels. They are infested by a wide variety of pests. Rats, spiders, nothing surprising. These must be slain._

_Also, I have been questioning the keepers as they emerge from the tunnels and go upstairs to safety. There are four prisoners who are unaccounted for. These should still be out there in the shadows. You must find them, or verify that they have left this level._
_I closed the gate to the inner caves when I saw that the prisoners were loose. I will try to open it for you._
Must those prisoners be slain?
_They must be found. As long as they are located and don't seem inclined to leave, you may spare them. Or not. As a Hand, you have the authority to decide their fates._
Who are the prisoners I need to find?
_There are four._ He consults a scroll. _A wretch named Ghroz. A Khemerian savage named Hansi. A tricky young mage from the Tawon Empire named Quiria._
_And, most dangerously, Shadow Tarkus. Of course, that treacherous creature did not hesitate to try to slip away._
_As the keepers emerged, they told me where they last saw the lost prisoners._ (There are now markings on your map.)
Tell me about the wretch.

_Ghroz is a sniveling little creature. We were trying to learn who was selling weaponry in the Wretch Lands. He knew nothing. We were going to release him, though he may have jeopardized that mercy by trying to escape._
Tell me about the Khemerian.
_Khemerians are barbarians, shamans and warriors of the plains. Truly savage and cruel, not like our allies in the Wyldrylm._

_Hansi was leading raiding parties into Wyldrylm Lands. Happens often, but we need to make an example of them occasionally. Hansi surrendered all of his information to us freely, so we were planning to release him._
Who is the Tawon mage?
_A particularly vicious rebel. Truly filled with hate for us. She was spying in Kellemderiel when we caught her._
_I hope she can be spared. The scrying of her mind was going well. We had found the existence of some conspirator named Dheless in the Tawon Empire. I am eager to find more._
Who is Shadow Tarkus?
_A spy and assassin. A blade for hire, a killer for coin. However, he only works to harm the Pact and the warriors of Avadon. Capturing him was very difficult and required a good deal of luck._
_If you find him, you may wish to get help as quickly as possible. By now, he is sure to have armed himself. He is very dangerous._
Might he be responsible for your problems?
_The possibility has occurred to me. However, it is unlikely. He has been continuously chained with our most secure spells. Whoever caused this disaster, it was not him._
I have information on your four prisoners.
You tell Eye Mamora what happened with the prisoners. He takes notes on your findings. _Yes. Well. None of these results are surprising._

_The death of Quiria is most unfortunate. I believe that we could have learned much from her. Another unfortunate result of the accident upstairs. And, as for Shadow Tarkus ..._ He shakes his head. _I will inform Hand Callan._
_As for you, please convey my gratitude to Heart Miranda, and let her know that my need for aid has not ended. I wish you a productive time here at Avadon._
I was in the lower cells and learned something very interesting about one of Avadon's officials.
Eye Mamora raises a hand to stop you. _Do not say. I do not want to know. And, if you are wise, you will forget as well. That knowledge was hidden in the low tunnels for a reason._
I need to find a prisoner named Quennel.
_Quennel ... Quennel ... Wait._ He pulls a scroll out of a bookshelf and reads it. _Yes. Odd case. He is quite broken. Free to leave. But he refuses._
_He is a noble of the Pact, so we will not force him to go, but he is broken, so I will not execute him. He is in the southern cells. If you can relieve us of his presence, I would appreciate it._

There is a pen to the south. Livestock was recently held there, perhaps to serve as food for something much fiercer and larger. Now there are rats in the pen, gnawing bones and drinking from the watering trough. They haven't noticed you.
(Sometimes, a creature will be inattentive. You can sneak past it. If you get too close, a '?' will appear over its head. If you stay close to it for too much longer, it will notice you.)

You enter the lower level of the Avadon dungeons. These chambers have been abandoned for at least a century. The walls are crumbling, and the smell of decay is heavy in the air. Some pests have infested these tunnels. You see little piles of moldering droppings in the corners.
You look for signs that anyone has come down here recently. It is hard to tell on the rotting planks, but you think that you can see some recent footprints. At least one pair of bare feet.

There is a fresh body here, a pale, aging human in torn robes. He has been here for several weeks. He must have escaped from the cells above, somehow slipped into this abandoned level, and immediately blundered into a pack of rats.

These corridors are bitter cold, but a refreshing draft of warm air comes from the holding cavern to the west. Refreshing, that is, until the cloud of sulfur stink wafts out at you. Something unpleasant is in there.
You emerge into a new set of caverns. You are surprised to find that they are not abandoned. In fact, it looks like workers have been down here very recently.

Peering into the side caves, you can see stone sarcophagi. Some are sealed and some are open, awaiting their permanent residents. This must be the burial place for servants of Avadon of great distinction.
You are in the lowest chamber of Avadon. It is completely freezing, and you can sense the countless tons of rock over your head.
The alcoves here, as on the floor above, contain sarcophagi. They are much nicer than the ones above. Some of them are also much older.
It isn't immediately clear what this place is. Then you see, in the shadows to the south, someone standing with his back to you. Maybe he can tell you more.

There is a wretch hiding behind this cabinet, shivering and whimpering. Based on his size, tattoos, and scars, you suspect that he has a high status among his people. And yet, Avadon has reduced this proud creature to a pool of jelly.
When he sees you, he shouts, _Aieee! Not hurt! No hurt! I give up! Ghroz is good wretch. Not hurt, not fight. Take me to cell, please!_
_Hiding. Bad spiders, they wrap me up. Me alive and stuck in webs and waiting to be ate. Bad, bad! Please save me!_
Why did you escape your cell?
_Escape? Not escape! Run! I run or be eaten. Too many rats. They swarm me if I stay, with biting. Had to go._
I was sent to look for you.
_Yes. Yes. Take me to safety. I not do the bad things they say. No, I don't. They say they let me go. Go back to tribe! Want tribe! Please no hurt!_
You are going home?
_Jailers say, yes! Go home, be great! Ghroz go to Avadon and live! Be great thing, if only I live._
What did they think you did?
_Weapons. Think I get weapons to give to wretches to fight Avadon. I hear rumors about that. I tell them that all. Just rumors. Wretches flapping big dumb lips. I know nothing real. They believe me!_
I need to do something with you.
Ghroz looks hopeful, and then terrified. _Just take me to cell. Or leave me alone. No hurt Ghroz, please._
Come with me. You can help me fight the pests.
_What? Fight? No! Me not fighter! Well, was fighter. Not now. Too stringy. Too weak. Just leave here, please!_
Stay here. Someone will be here for you soon.
_Yes. Ghroz stay. Ghroz hide. You kill pests. Thank you. Thank you. Ghroz be safe now._ He returns to his hiding spot.
(The first part of your mission is complete. Now hunt for the other missing prisoners.)
I don't trust you. I'd better kill you.
_What? No! They say Ghroz free. They say ... say ..._ Then he sees you advance upon him, weapon ready. He lets out a long hiss. _Traitors! Bad Avadon! I not let you kill me!_
He leaps out of his corner, claws out. He moves surprisingly quickly.
(The first part of your mission is complete. Once Ghroz is dead, you can hunt for the other missing prisoners.)
Ghroz hides in his corner, whimpering quietly and waiting for rescue.
Ghroz is still here, gnawing on the bones of rats he caught while waiting for rescue. He mutters, _Ghroz good. Ghroz waiting to be took to cell. Didn't think would wait so long._
There is a prisoner being held in this room. He is a young man, dressed in torn clothes of an unfamiliar style. He stands in the middle of a magic circle, surrounded by a translucent field of energy.
He is staring off into space, and yet he seems to sense that you are there. Inside the field, he moves and talks very slowly.
He says, in his odd, painfully drawn out way, _I ... I ammmm Lexrem. I ammmm here toooo teach._
Lexrem stands upright, trapped in the field of energy. He moves very slowly, and his words come out as a long, ghastly moan.
His clothes have a very peculiar style. You start to suspect that they went out of fashion years before you were born.
(Pull Lexrem out of the field.)
The moment you touch the field, you are harshly thrown back. It takes several minutes for the numbness in your arms to disappear, only to be replaced by a painful ache.
Lexrem says, _Don't dooooo that._
Who put you here?
_Rrrredbeard. It issss my fate. Forrrr ... Forrrrr ... What year is it?_
_Ahhh ... Ahhhh ... Everyone I ever loved issss dead._
When did you come here?
_It was ... 6263. A long time._ If he is telling the truth, a very long time.
You said you are here to teach?
_I ammmm ... an example. I had a choice. I could choose death. Orrrr to teach. I teach. So I was frozen here._
Frozen? Is that the field around you?
_Yes. It keeps meeeee alive. And you ... You move very very fast. It is hard to focussss on you. To understand._
Is it painful to be in there?
_No. I am ... numb. Time goes by. I am ..._ He sort of drifts off.
What are you here to teach me?
_Neverrrr fight Redbeard. Do not try to assasssssinate him. You will be dead. Or like me._
Redbeard keeps you here as an example?
_He bringssss new servants to seeeee me. So they know not to revolt._
You tried to kill Redbeard?
_I came from Dharammmm. I thought Avadonnn had tooooo much power. I had a poison. I thought Redbeard would not detect it. I wasss wrong._
Why did you choose to live?
_Hope. Someday I might be free. I thought this issss betterrrr than the void. I was wrong._
Maybe I can free you.
_Do not try. You willll end up like me. Someday Redbeard willll die, and maybe his follower will have mercy._
This is unjust. Nobody should be punished like this.
Lexrem makes a hideous, gurgling noise. You soon realize that he is laughing. _You sound like I did. And look where I ammmm now._
_You have heard what I say. I returnnn to silence._ He closes his eyes.
This is a just punishment for trying to strike down the Keeper.
_It is a punishment. I willll not say if it is just. You decide that. And take the consequences._
All right. Consider me taught. I am going.
With painful, glacial slowness, Lexrem nods inside his magical shell. _Yessss. Keep your thoughts close, and they will not hurt you._
There are three escaped prisoners standing by the southern passage. They have scavenged leather armor and blades, and they look understandably desperate.

One of them steps forward. He salutes you with his stolen blade. _I am Hansi, and we are warriors of Khemeria! We will not lose this chance to fight your kind._ He looks you over. _Though we thought more would come for us._
We don't need more help to slay a Farlander like you.
Hansi nods. _That is the spirit of Avadon. It is courage that crushes our people, but we do admire it._
The two warriors by his side start to look nervous. Hansi says, _Be strong. A death fighting the Pact is a death with honor._
I will bring you to justice just the same.
Hansi nods. _You are outnumbered and, from what I see, untrained. And you give us the chance to bring one of your kind down before we die. It is courage that crushes our people, but we do admire it._
I was actually hoping that you would just surrender.
Hansi slowly shakes his head. _It is not possible. It simply can't be done. This chance must not be lost._
The two warriors by his side start to look nervous. The chance to surrender tempts them. Hansi says, _Be strong. A death fighting the Pact is a death with honor._
You are from Khemeria?

_Yes! We are warriors of the northern plains, the terror of the Wyldrylm and the Pact. You of the Pact call us barbarians, savages. And perhaps that is true. We will take any chance to slay one of your kind before we are brought down._
Why are you imprisoned here?

_I can't speak for my brothers._ He nods at the increasingly terrified warriors to either side. _I was caught raiding the villages of the Wyldrylm. Your kind calls it attacking the Pact. But it is what we Khemerians are born to do!_
This is your last chance. Surrender.
Hansi shakes his head. _It is not possible. If you were Khemerian, your clan would take me prisoner and ransom me back._
_But this is Avadon. Here, you will force betrayal from me. All that will be left to me is death or returning in shame, knowing that I submitted to the Pact._
You are an enemy of the Pact. You will pay for your crimes. (Attack.)
Sevilin nods grimly. He mutters to himself, _Stand strong. I will not falter this time._
Nathalie nods approvingly. She mutters, _This is what I have waited for. A fight, at last. Let us destroy them._
Hansi looks quickly at the warriors standing to either side. _I have only just met you, but, in these last moments, I will call you my clan brothers. Be strong, like a true Khemerian, and ..._
Happily, your charge interrupts his speech.
Perhaps you can simply sneak out.
Sevilin looks shocked. _[N], we can't let a prisoner escape. I will not let this be counted against me._
Your suggestion annoys Nathalie. _I have not waited to fight this long only to let a prisoner escape. Do what you want. I will fight._
Hansi says, _Such an escape is not possible._ The three of them raise their blades. _This is our last chance to slay a warrior of Avadon. We will take it._
Then, if you will not surrender, we must fight.
Hansi says, _This is inevitable._ The three of them raise their blades. _This is our last chance to slay a warrior of Avadon. We will take it._
Hansi collapses to the floor, mortally wounded. _The fields ... of Khemeria ... I see them. I slew a Hand ... Yes ... Victory. Victory._
Then he closes his eyes. Whatever fantasy this foe of Avadon entertained in the last moments of his life, it is over now.
This island is where creatures like dragons rest when they visit Avadon. They enter through the shaft in the ceiling directly above you.
The only person on the island now is a middle-aged woman. She wears long, torn robes. She is not yet pale and twitchy. She must have been a prisoner here for only a short time.
She looks at you wryly. _So this is who they send to bring down Quiria? This is all? Tarkus said there would be more before he left. But that is my punishment for trusting him._
You saw Shadow Tarkus? Where is he?
_Gone, fool. You think that, given such a chance, you would be able to hold him? He said he would return to help me, but I knew that he would take no risk on my behalf._
Why were you brought here?
_Why did your spies in the Tawon Empire bring me here? They thought I and others were conspiring against the Pact. Is it true? You will never know. Soon, I will be dead._
I am here to find you. Return to your cell, or you will die.
Sevilin quietly watches her, prepared to charge the moment she does anything suspicious. Maybe it's your imagination, but he seems to be shaking slightly.
Nathalie quietly says, _Please don't let her make a speech. I've heard enough Farlander garbage today._
Quiria maintains a calm composure. _No. A chance to die before my soul is invaded is a gift. I will accept my death like a daughter of the Tawon Empire._
You sound like a Khemerian I just met.

Her composure breaks for a moment. She is offended. _I am from the Tawon Empire, the core of civilization, that once ruled most of Lynaeus. And you compare me to those barbarians? All we have in common is hatred for you. Nothing else!_
You Farlanders throw your lives away easily.
_Our lives are as valuable as yours. I die proud, with the satisfaction of knowing what will happen to your kind after I am gone._
This is your last chance to surrender.
_No. My time is done._ She holds her hands out to either side. A nimbus of light appears around them. _I am prepared. I only wish to kill one of your kind before I die._
The mist at the edges of the island starts to coalesce into translucent forms. She holds her hand out, and a bolt of fire flies toward you.
It is time. Defend yourself. (Attack.)
She holds her hands out to either side. A nimbus of light appears around them. _I am prepared. I only wish to kill one of your kind before I die._
Quiria collapses to the ground. She is not long for this world. She starts to whisper. You have to lean close to hear what she says. _Tarkus. Dheless. Avenge me._
Where is Shadow Tarkus?
_Gone ... Gone from here ... The honor of the Tawon,_ she whispers. Then she closes her eyes for the last time.

You notice that she has a key hanging from her belt, stolen during her escape from her cell. You take it. Through the mists to the southwest, you can just make out a closed door in the wall of this huge chamber.
Who is Dheless?
_You will learn ... You ... The honor of the Tawon,_ she whispers. Then she closes her eyes for the last time.
Die, enemy of the Pact.
She hears your words and smiles. _The honor of the Tawon,_ she whispers. Then she closes her eyes for the last time.
As you explore, you notice that Sevilin is shaking slightly. Every noise makes him jump a little. For a Hand of Avadon, armed and armored, it's odd behavior.
Is something wrong?
_What? Oh ... I apologize. It has been some time since I was on a mission. I am not used to it. Do not worry. I will fight in a way that does honor to my training._
Stop being so jumpy. You're making me nervous.
_Am I? After waiting for so long, to ... I apologize. It has been some time since I was on a mission. I am not used to it. Do not worry. I will fight in a way that does honor to my training._
Why haven't you been selected for a mission?
_Perhaps this is not the best time to discuss it. Later. For now, I will calm and prepare myself._ He takes a deep breath and walks forward, a bit more composed than before.
I expect no less. Don't disappoint me.
He nods. _Yes. Of course. I will calm and prepare myself._ He takes a deep breath and walks forward, a bit more composed than before.

Sevilin turns to you. His face glows with enthusiasm. _We have succeeded. I admit, I was concerned. I did not think I could fight well. I thought I would be of no use. And yet, those foes of the Pact, they fell before us!_
_I am grateful that you chose me. My dark time is done. I am a warrior of Avadon._

Nathalie turns to you. She is literally shaking with excitement. _At last! After all this waiting! I was chosen, I went out, I slew the enemies of the Pact. All of my doubts were wrong. They should have sent me out long ago._
_I am grateful that you chose me. My wasted years are behind me. I am a warrior of Avadon._
What about Shadow Tarkus?
_From what the Tawon mage said, the fourth prisoner is gone. We should report back to the jailer quickly._
Be ready. We are not safe yet.
_Of course. Let us get back to Eye Mamora and report what we have learned._ The Hand's enthusiasm does not fade.
Let's find our way back to Eye Mamora.
_Of course. We should report our victory as soon as we can._ The Hand's enthusiasm does not fade.
Nathalie stops walking. You turn to see what is wrong, only to see that she looks thrilled. There is not a touch of doubt or fear in her expression.
Why have you stopped? Is something wrong?
_No. Nothing is wrong. Nothing at all. I am finally acting. No more lessons, no more the tedium of being a student. I am doing what I was born to do!_
Keep up!
_What? Of course. I just needed a moment to reflect and enjoy this moment. To fight, to use my training at last!_
I understand. It is thrilling.
_Yes! It is as exciting as I thought it would be. 'Destiny' is a foolish word, but ... No. There will be time for this later. I must concentrate. Let us proceed._ She walks forward into the shadows.
Enough of that. You need to focus.
She seems slightly embarrassed. _Of course. I apologize and will improve. Let us proceed._ She walks forward into the shadows.
There is a prisoner sitting on a chair in this cell, his back against the wall. He is very thin and pale. He has been here for months, if not years.
He must know that you are staring in at him, but he ignores you.
The prisoner is still sitting in his cell, doing his best to ignore you.
Quennel is still sitting in his cell. He stares intently at the opposite wall.
The prisoner ignores you.
Are you all right in there?
The prisoner doesn't say anything. Maybe repeated readings of his mind have left him a little damaged.
Are you Quennel?
At first, the man is silent. Then his head slowly turns toward you. _I ... You know me? You came for me?_ His voice is raspy with disuse. _None have come for me for a while. What do you want?_
You walk away from the window, thinking that the man might call you to return. He doesn't.
Do you need anything in there?
_I am safe. The door stayed locked, protecting me from the wretches and pests. I am content to remain._
Why are you held here?
_Since you know my name, you must know what I did. My guilt is known. I have been punished. I am no more threat to Avadon._
Why don't you say what you did?

He looks at you briefly. Then he faces the back wall. _I repeat my crime as part of my penance. I am of a noble family. A Hand of Avadon was making decisions that took our lands, for the benefit of another family._
_To save our fortunes, I and three cousins abducted that Hand and killed him._
Why was this Hand acting against you?
_I imagine the other family convinced him that it was for the good of the Pact. And removed his doubts with a large sack of coins._
What happened to your cousins?

_Avadon soon deduced what happened and sent Hands after us. We were not experienced assassins, after all. One cousin was killed when fleeing the Hands. Another was brought to Avadon and showed insufficient remorse. He was executed._
What was your penalty?
_It is paid. They looked through my thoughts and found all they needed. They know I will never act against them again. And yet ... How can I return? The shame. The shame._
Your family wishes for you to return from Avadon.
_I know. And yet, I cannot. I do not favor this cell. I long for Kellemderiel. And yet, how can I face them?_
I want to ask you about your return to Kellemderiel.
_I have already made up my mind. I have nothing else to say. Please leave me._
Why can't you return?
_Our foolish plan killed two of our family. Shamed our family. Probably cost us great wealth and fame. Our rash actions did great harm. I can never let them see me like this._
_One day, I will leave, when I determine where I can go. But I can never go home._
That is understandable. You should just stay here.
He nods. _At last, someone understands me. I am a noble of the Kellem, and I will stay here until I am ready to go. Please leave me._
Your staying away from your family just punishes them more.
_So you say. But you do not understand them or us. It is not your affair._
You are being forced to leave. You must decide now. (Lie.)
He turns to look at you. _But I am a noble of the Kellem. You cannot deny me! Avadon would deny me a room? You would not dare!_
I am through dealing with this affair.
He nods. _I appreciate your effort, but it is not your affair. I am a noble of the Kellem, and I will stay here until I am ready to go. Please leave me._
These are not normal times. After the disaster, everyone who can go must.
_But ... But ... Where will I go? I am still weak. I am not ready. I can't go home. I won't survive the shame. But I can't go anywhere else!_
You will have to go home, until you can find somewhere else to live.

_If I must ... I see that I have no choice. Their shame, their disappointment, I will survive it as long as I can. I will go soon. I must prepare. Excuse me._ The young man, prematurely aged, stares at the wall and tries to concentrate on a plan.
Go somewhere else in the Pact. You will find a way to settle in.

_If I must ... I see that I have no choice. Perhaps I will go to Dharam. They lack our culture, but they do know how to think. I will go soon. I must prepare. Excuse me._ The young man, prematurely aged, stares at the wall and tries to plan.
