There is only one prisoner left in these cells. He sits cross-legged in the back of his chamber, spear stolen from a guard across his lap, eyes closed, meditating.
Then, in a remarkably quick movement, he is on his feet, weapon in hand. _Your arrival was easy to detect. You servants of Avadon are very loud._

The prisoner waits calmly in his cell, spear in hand. Under his ragged shirt, you can see armor stolen from a storeroom somewhere. _I ask to be left alone. I am not a threat, and I remain in my cell._
_A prisoner of Avadon. Humble and defeated. That is all. I only wait for my chance to prove my harmlessness and be released._

_Waiting in my cell, calmly, for help to come. I took some food and a spear from the nearby stores, and I wait for the Eyes to come and secure me. I mean no harm, and the pests that remain are unable to harm me._
But why are you being held?
_Suspicions. That is all. My next session on the Eyes' tables will show that I am only here through the treachery of another. Then I will be freed._
Are you Shadow Tarkus?

He laughs. _That assassin? That famed bloodletter of the loyal servants of the Pact? Nonsense. He was held in these cells, but I have no idea where he is. He is probably a thousand miles away by now._
Are you Spiridon?

The prisoner's calm suddenly fades. _That is my name. Not my real name. The name I gave to a group of Wyldrylm barbarians. I am a citizen of the Pact, a skilled mercenary from Dharam._ His grip tightens on his spear.

_I was doing honest work in the Wyldrylm, but I was brought to this place through well-placed bribes of corrupt Hands. I'm sure of it. I've been waiting for the barbarians to send someone to silence me._ He takes a step forward.
Jenell shakes her head. _Don't try to fool us. You lie to play upon our sympathies. You were an assassin, killing the good people of the Wyldrylm woods for pay. Now you will pay your debt._
Spiridon
I will leave you.
He nods. _Thank you for the visit._
Say your last words. I came here to kill you.
_This is what I expected. I have been waiting for you, armed and ready. I will end you, and then I will find those who betrayed Spiridon and end them too!_ He lowers his spear and charges.
I did come to kill you, but I don't have to.

_Oh, no! Don't back away now! Why is it that, when you Hands become corrupt, you become cowards as well. I have been waiting for you, armed and ready. I will end you, and then I will find those who betrayed Spiridon and end them too!_ He lowers his spear and charges.
I mean you no harm. I'll be going.
_What, coward? You did not expect me to be armed? Awake? I will end you, and then I will find those who betrayed Spiridon and end them too!_ He lowers his spear and charges.
You find some old records here. This is not surprising. The Avadon dungeons are full of the records of prisoners, the things they confessed, and their final fates.

What is odd is that this ledger seems to be only a few decades old. It's as if it was placed here in the hope that it would rot away and be forgotten. Such papers tend to contain information one is better off not knowing.
You find the old records. You have already read them, for better or worse.
Look through the book.
You flip through the records. They date from about forty years ago. Moisture and mold have left most of the writing illegible. One entry, halfway through, catches your attention.
It concerns a Hand who attempted to assassinate Redbeard. He tried to stab the Keeper, but the result was a minor wound. Once the Hand's mind was stripped of all knowledge, he was executed.

Oddly, it notes that he was married to one of the Eyes. Her mind was also searched extensively, but nothing was found that implicated her. She was allowed to return to her work. A widow, but one of unquestioned loyalty.
Her name was Miranda. And the cursory description given of her in the records matches very closely with the appearance of the Heart who has been giving you orders. Interesting.
Leave it alone.
Sometimes, a little bit of discretion contributes directly to one's survival. You leave the book alone.
You flip through the records. They date from about thirty years ago. Moisture and mold have left most of the writing illegible. One entry, halfway through, catches your attention.

It concerns three new arrivals at Avadon, two Hands and one Eye. As often happens, they had great skill and ambition, enough to want to take control of the Black Fortress. And thus, they planned to overthrow Redbeard.

The Eye, however, lost interest in the plan. She betrayed the plot to Redbeard, and all three ended up in the dungeon. The Hands were executed. The Eye was allowed to return to the library, broken, as a warning to others.
The pages describing the dead Hands have rotted away, but you do find the name of the Eye who betrayed them. It is Leira.
There are several people hiding in the tunnels here. They are not recent escapees. Their tattered clothes and emaciated figures make you think that they have been hiding down here for years.
One of them steps forward, brandishing a long, curved blade. _You ... You came for us ... Came to hunt us at last. You will never get Kano back to your tables. Never. Ever._
How long have you been down here?
_We ..._ Kano looks to the warriors to either side. They shake their heads. _So long. So dark. Hunting so many rats. We ... hate rats._
Are you escaped prisoners?
_We ... Wait? You don't know? You mean ... Those above don't know we're here? So, if you disappeared ..._ Kano, with some effort, works through some thoughts.
How did you escape?
_Was an uprising. Others ... did something. Fighting. They opened our gates. We ran ... down stairs. Don't remember much. Lots of ... Time in the dark. Nobody else came with us._
What crime did you commit?
_A crime of justice. We fought against ... fought for ... I have no idea._
I'm looking for a prisoner. Just escaped. Shadow Tarkus.
_A prisoner? No. No escaped prisoners anywhere down here. None came past us. No, no shadow down here. Just ..._ Well, that answers that question.
One of the other men nudges Kano. _No. Need to stop you. None can know we are here. Life or death. Take no offense._
Wait. You want to attack me?
_Yes ... Yes. You must see we have no choice. Avadon will destroy us if it finds us. The only ... only reasonable course is for you to die. You must be reasonable._
I'll just slip away now. Goodbye.
Kano says, _I am sorry. You have to die._ The men produce a remarkable array of rusty old weapons. They lurch forward.
You are prisoners of Avadon. You will come with me or die.

Kano shakes his head. _Avadon does ... horrible things to those who escape. It is better to live in the dark and eat rats. After you die._ The men produce a remarkable array of rusty old weapons. They lurch forward.

As you edge closer to the figure in the shadows, he turns to face you. You immediately recognize the muscular form, the unnaturally young face. It only took extra time to recognize him because you aren't used to seeing him outside of his throne room. It is Redbeard.
For once, he is not smiling. He says, somberly, _Ahhhh ... You found your way down here. Most do. All servants of Avadon should come here often._
I did not expect to find you here.
_I find it is good to turn up unexpectedly. Makes everyone stay constantly alert. A good thing, when one has our massive responsibilities._
_But that is not why I am here now._
You should return to safety. This area is not secure.
_What? You mean the pests above? Even they know not to touch the Keeper of Avadon._
_This is the burial chamber for Keepers of Avadon. Keepers of distinction, that is. All the lasting Keepers since the first days of the Black Fortress are kept here._
Are all Keepers left here?

_No. The tradition is that only the Keepers who lasted two score days in the post without being assassinated are given the honor of interment here. That reduces the number of coffins needed considerably._
It looks like this room is still under construction.
_And, as long as there is need for more tombs for the Keepers, it always will be. The roughness is an act of faith in the future of Avadon._
How many Keepers are buried here?

_In the seventy years Avadon has protected the Pact since the end of the Black Age, four Keepers have been buried here. Most of those years, I have been Keeper. It has been a long time since there was a funeral here._
_To pay honor to those who created this place. Who gave their lives for the Pact, before falling to the assassin's blade._
_And I come here to think. It is a place where I can be alone in the quiet. Diplomats and courtiers know not to disturb me here. Not if they value their lives._
They were all assassinated?

_Every day spent as Keeper, every day fighting those who would disrupt the Pact, a Keeper gains another enemy. Clanmates seeking vengeance. Those who would give all for power. Ambitious Hands._ He raises an eyebrow at you.
_Attempts on a Keeper's life are constant. And, eventually, one will succeed._
What are you thinking about now?

_So many troubles, so quickly. Am I paranoid? Is it only chance? Or is it more than coincidence? And the Tawon Empire. It keeps being mentioned. The Empire, and the name 'Dheless.' What does it mean? How should I react?_
He is silent. He doesn't seem to have heard you. _I have been alone enough. And, anyway, my solitude has been disrupted. I should return to my duties. As should you._
He turns and strides out of the chamber.
Is there anything I should do?
It is likely only coincidence.
Hansi
Kano
Escaped Prisoner
Quiria

Wyldrylm Warrior
Wyldrylm Archer
Mossy Bones
Shaman Essela

I expected you.
You have saved us.
Jenell is well.
Look after Jenell.
We must go.
Back to the road.
Vine-Wrapped Flesh
Deep Woods Horror

You followed the directions you received in Dhorl Stead and arrive at Jarlswood. It is a remote region of eastern Khemeria, far from any large settlements. It is mainly settled by hunters and clanless warriors.

There is a stone circle to the east. It has been abandoned for many years. Some of the stones have been smashed apart for building materials. If Jenell was here, she would no doubt have some angry comments about this.

One thing you don't need Jenell to tell you is that this pathway has received a lot of recent use. There are lots of recent footprints in the dirt and the mud. Some of the travelers were pulling wagons and sledges. You suspect that you are in the right area.
This road has been blocked. Someone has recently assembled huge piles of logs and debris here. This barrier would be very easy to defend with a handful of warriors, but nobody is here.

As you start to clear a path through, you hear someone talking behind you. You turn around and see a group of Wyldrylm warriors. They have emerged from the woods and are walking down the road to the west.
Then one of them sees you. He points and shouts, _Scouts! We've been found! Get them!_ And, before you have a chance to explain yourself, they attack ...
You walk down this concealed path, shaken by your encounter with the warriors of the Pact. You didn't recognize any of them, but they must have been part of the group that fled north.
They were probably going out to hunt game or to raid nearby Khemerian settlements. The rest of the rogue warriors must be nearby.
Jenell looks around at the dark forest. _I should be able to find tracks that lead back to Theresia's hall. Let's look around. If we wander enough, we should find what we are looking for._

You emerge from the valley and see a pair of halls behind a palisade. They are built out of rough-hewn logs. They have been here for a long time. The wood is afflicted with rot and covered with moss. Only recent repair work has kept them from collapsing.

Jenell says, _This is the place. I was brought here. It is where I was held. I met Theresia in the south hall. I asked her to see reason and leave this area before Avadon came. The meeting did not go well._
There are several guards keeping watch behind the palisade. If they choose to attack you, you will have no choice but to defend yourself.

A lot of humanoid bones have been discarded along the path to the north and south. They are overgrown with moss and vines. A few of the skeletons are human, but most of the bones are from wretches and ogres.

As you pass, you hear crackling and rustling from the bones. They start to move. The vines come to life, pull them together, and lift them up, forming unpleasant hybrids of plant and bone. The bizarre creatures shamble toward you.
Jenell shakes her head. _Theresia ... What monstrosities have you been creating? Is this how a shaman acts?_
Slime-Covered Bones
There are several posts in the alcove to the east. Rusty shackles rest on the floor next to them.
Jenell shudders. _That is where I was held. To think that I almost died there._
She looks to the north. _There is a ladder up there. Theresia will probably be waiting at the top of it._

You recognize this warrior from the road through the Dhorla Woods. This is another of the refugees from the Pact, hiding in Khemeria. _Thank you for saving us. Speak with Vid. He speaks for us. We must prepare to flee._
As you explore the Jarlswood, someone runs along the path to join you. It is Jenell.
She seems annoyed. _Until the matter of Shaman Theresia is settled, I insist on traveling with you in this area._
This door has been securely barred from the inside. You fail to get it open.
Shaman Theresia falls to the ground, slain. She tried to kill a Hand of Avadon. She has paid the price.
You look at Jenell. She looks miserable. _It had to be done, but ... To kill a shaman? These are dark times. Truly dark times. Still, I am grateful for your help. Thank you, [N]. I owe you a debt._
You look at Jenell. She averts her gaze, devastated by the need to battle her own people. She says nothing to you.

Shaman Theresia lets out a growl. Not a human growl. A long, low, feral animal sound, terribly alien coming out of her throat. A strange, faint vision appears over her form. It looks like a bear, standing upright.
Then it is gone, but some power of the image remains. Suddenly, it takes great strength and resolve to keep from fleeing in terror.
Once again, the image of the bear appears over Shaman Theresia. This time, instead of sending out waves of terror, it reinforces her strength. She seems partially restored by the power of the beast.
Jenell looks back down the path. _Those creatures ... Those horrors ... Shamans revere nature. It is not our way to release such disgusting things into it. Not our way._
Theresia will pay.
_Yes, but I take no satisfaction in it. I am sure we will see more such things before we are done here. Let us move on._
Shamans never engage in necromancy?
_That is not what we just saw. They were not truly undead. Just dead bones, maneuvered by plants. The magic was used on the plants, not the bones._
_Still, that sort of thing is ... not wise. It is a sign of desperation, or worse. I am not proud of our arts today. Let us move on._
Sevilin looks at the blocked roadway to the southwest. _The woods ... The ambush ... We are walking into an ambush. I am sure of it. It is just like what happened in The Kva. I ... Will I ..._
Jenell reaches out and puts a hand on his arm. He calms down.
_It makes me angry. I wonder if I will ever be free of what happened to me and my friends. I will be all right._
Shima seems lost in thought as you enter the dank cellar. Jenell looks over at him. _Something to say, Holklandan?_

He responds, _I am surprised to see so much confusion and argument about membership in the Pact. The Wyldrylm has had to make adjustments. We all have. And yet, the safety we have gained ... There are many in the Farlands who would give all to join the Pact._
Jenell says, _The Wyldrylm is attached to its ways. We value safety, but our traditions are ... They are very important._
Shima thinks on this. He quietly says, _It is possible that the other lands of Lynaeus value their ways too. And yet ..._ And then he is silent.

Nathalie looks around the clearing with distaste. _We have come all the way out here, neglecting our missions and leaving good prey unhunted. Why? Because the barbarian decides to run off into the wild. Such unreliability from their kind is not a surprise._
Before you can respond, she walks off through the grass, viciously kicking a stone as she goes.

This grove contains a group of Wyldrylm warriors, standing among the ruins of a looted caravan. They are armed, armored and ready for battle. They were watching the pathway to the north. They have someone trapped up there, and they are preparing an attack.
Then their leader sees you. She is a hunter of the Wyldrylm, tall and muscular. She steps forward, her blade drawn. _Hold, there!_
_I am Flos, runner of the deep woods. Why have you come here, warrior?_
Who is up that northern path?
She taps her blade against the palm of her hand. _This land is claimed by us. You have no right to ask questions here. It is a private disagreement._
I am [N] of Avadon. I am looking for an associate of mine.
Flos nods. _Yes. Shaman Theresia told us to expect you. That Avadon would come and expect obedience from those they drove from their homes._
_But you are far from home, Avadon. And outnumbered._ Her warriors turn toward you, weapons out.
I am simply a traveler passing through.
Flos smiles. The others laugh. _Of course. Warriors of the Pact well-equipped and ready to fight, going for a leisurely stroll deep in the most savage reaches of the Farlands._
_I suggest you come up with a better excuse for your presence._
I need no excuse. I am [N] of Avadon, and you will mind your tone.
It is as I said. I am lost. Can you give me directions?

Flos laughs, but it is a dry, mirthless sound. _Shaman Theresia warned us. Warned us to watch for spies from the Pact. They are easy to spot. There is no other reason for a warrior of the Pact to be here._
_I regret this. If you were innocent, my spirit will apologize to yours in the realms beyond._ Her warriors turn toward you, weapons out.
I have nothing to say to you.
_Then we have no choice. Shaman Theresia's orders were clear. None from the Pact leave to betray our presence._
What do you think you are doing?
The warriors do not shout or do anything that might alert whoever is up the road to the north. They pull out their blades and silently charge.
They hope to subdue you and slit your throat before you can make a fuss. They are in for a real shock.
There is another group of warriors of the Wyldrylm in this camp. They stand in a semicircle behind their fire, blades drawn, ready to defend themselves.
They watch you as you enter the grove. Then one of them steps forward, lowers his weapon, and shouts, _Wait! Don't attack!_
You actually recognize him. It is Vid, the raider you met while exploring the Dhorla Woods. He actually seems pleased to see you. _We knew you were coming. We don't want to fight you._
Vid speaks with you, though he is constantly watching the pathway to the south. He seems to expect an attack at any moment.
What has been going on here?
_There has been ... an argument. There are many of us gathered together here, but ... my group has been cast out._ You look at them. They look like the warriors you met in the Dhorla Woods.
_It was because of Jenell. She is in there._ He points into the cave to the east. _She is well. You should speak with her._
I am here to find Jenell.

Vid nods. _She is here and well. However, there has been a disagreement over her. There are many warriors of the Wyldrylm hiding here, but ... my group has been cast out._ You look at them. They look like the warriors you met in the Dhorla Woods.
What has been happening here? Why were Wyldrylm warriors attacking me?
Vid shakes his head. _It is a ... mess. After our group fled the Wyldrylm, we came here. We heard that a number of warriors from our land had bound together here. We came to join them._
_Then Jenell arrived to find us, and things became difficult._
Remind me why you left the Wyldrylm?
_A rival tribe was using the free roads to attack us. We attacked some of their warriors on the same free road. This broke one of the unjust laws of the Pact, so we were forced to flee._
What happened when Jenell came?
_She walked into our camp and told us that we had to flee. She said that the Pact knew we were here and that we would have to leave._
_This angered Shaman Theresia, the leader here. She took Jenell prisoner. When they began to debate whether to kill her, I had to step in._
So what did you do?
_We helped her to slip away in the night. We had to leave with her, of course. We knew Theresia would not forgive us._
Why didn't you agree with them?
_I do not follow the laws of the Pact. But kill a warrior of Avadon? And a shaman of the Wyldrylm? A woman bound in a cell?_
_There is nothing about that plan that isn't mad._
And you brought Jenell here?
_Yes. We fled as quickly as we could, but Theresia was faster. She trapped us here. We have been here for a few days. My friends. Me. And Jenell._
_They would have killed us soon, had you not come._
How many of you are out here?
_My band? Me and my friends? All that is left is what you see here. One was killed by a Khemerian. Another stayed with Theresia. Perhaps he is the one who said that we were going to flee._
_As for Shaman Theresia's band, there are over forty of them now, plus livestock and wolves. A powerful band._
Where did they all come from?
_The same place we did. They hate the Pact. They hate the way it interferes with the old ways of the Wyldrylm. They came here to live as they choose and to hunt Khemerians._
Where do they get their supplies from?
_Khemerians and the merchants who sell to them. We raid the villages of the enemy. It is an honorable path._
Why haven't the Khemerians hunted you down yet?
_Shaman Theresia and her warriors are wily. They are fast, they cover their tracks, and they take advantage of the constant warfare between the Steads._
_I'm not sure that the nearby Khemerians even know that they are camped here._
You have been looking after Jenell?
_I had no choice. When I saw that they were going to kill Jenell ... Shaman Jenell, I knew that I could not allow it. My friends chose to stay with me. Well, most of them._
_We took turns standing guard. The rest of us waited in the cave. I looked after her to make sure she was all right._
You risked much for her.
_I knew, the moment I saw her in the Dhorla Woods, that she was an honorable Shaman of the Wyldrylm. I knew she was not my enemy, whatever happens._
Jenell is thoroughly embarrassed. She starts finding other directions in which to look.
How did you spend your time together?
Vid looks annoyed. His face flushed slightly. _That is a private matter between two warriors of the Wyldrylm._
Tell me about Shaman Theresia.
_Perhaps you should see Jenell first. I'm sure she will have much to tell you._
I need to know more about Shaman Theresia.

_She says little of her past. I don't know where she is from, what drove her here, or even how old she is. All I know is that she is powerful, and that she hates the Pact. She wants the Wyldrylm to stand free again._
Do you agree with her?
He looks disturbed. _I ... Once, I would have said yes. But I have seen much in the last few months. I have seen how strong and vicious Khemeria is. I've seen how hard life is without protection._
_Now, I am not sure. I can see wisdom in having allies._
What do you think should be done about her?
_I don't know. Her time out here has made her hard and cruel, if she wasn't so already. I have learned in my time in the wilds that I know little._
So what do you think I should do?
_I will not give advice to Avadon. I am happy that I don't have to make the sort of decisions you do._
Shaman Theresia is dead.
_I am sad to hear it. The death of a shaman is always a loss. And yet, I knew that this was how this tale would end._
_We will leave this place, immediately. It is painful. We will be alone again, in a hostile land. I don't think we have any other choice._
You must return. You need to be brought to justice.
Jenell shakes her head slightly when she hears your words, but she doesn't speak.
Vid looks very tired. _We will walk for a time, we will speak, and we will see. It is not cowardly to face your enemies, and life here among enemies is hard._
_Thank you for saving our lives. Now we have much to decide._ He nods to you and walks back to rejoin his fellows.
You should return and face your punishment, but know that someone in Avadon will speak on your behalf.
Jenell looks at you, surprised and grateful.

Vid looks very tired. _We will walk for a time, we will speak, and we will see. It is not cowardly to face your enemies, and life here among enemies is hard. At least, thanks to your honorable words, we have hope._
You should stay in Khemeria.
Jenell nods at this advice, though it clearly pains her.
_Then we will be brave. We will stay in this cruel place until they hunt us down. It is what honor has forced us to, and we will accept it._
Jenell looks carefully at the faint tracks on the ground. _Every Wyldrylm warrior knows how to travel while leaving only the faintest trace. And yet, when enough people walk in and out ... There!_
She walks up to the stone wall, gives it a heavy shove, and watches with satisfaction as a section of it swings away.
The path dead-ends in a small grove. Jenell smiles. _As if this path would simply end. Look for ... there is the path._ She points to the south.

Jenell looks around. _This is a dark forest, and the path is faint. Still, with so many warriors ..._ She walks to the end of this clear space and kicks aside some of the underbrush. There is a narrow path on the other side, winding through the trees.
The shaman sniffs the air. _We are close. Be ready. I do not want to kill warriors of the Wyldrylm, but I will defend myself from any who attack me._
There is a small thicket of trees growing at the base of this cliff. Jenell is not fooled for a moment. She shoves some brown brush away, revealing a crack in the stone.
Alas, the narrow valley beyond has been piled high with debris and logs, forming an impassable barrier. Jenell snorts and turns away.
The pathway on the other side is clear. Jenell smiles. _I knew that they wouldn't plug up every pathway. They need to get in and out, after all._
_Theresia is going to pay for the insult she gave me. I hope that we can spare the others._

Jenell is waiting for you in this cell. She is dirty and exhausted, but unharmed. She jumps to her feet when you enter, smiling. Then she sees that it is you. For a moment, you think that she is slightly disappointed.
The moment passes. _I see that you received my message. It is a relief. My visit here did not go as well as I expected._
_I came back to Dhorl Stead and spoke with Runner Faiga. I learned where she thought the raiders were. Then I came here._

_It was not difficult to track them for a woman of the woods, one who follows the old ways. I came to them. Their warriors found me, blindfolded me, and brought me to their halls. There, I warned Shaman Theresia._
What warning did you give?
_That Avadon knew where they were and that they were spreading unrest in Khemeria. That was not something Avadon can tolerate. They can't be allowed to stir up the Khemerians against us._
How did this Shaman Theresia react?
_She was ... It pains me to admit this, but not all shamans are wise. Some are arrogant. Some love war overmuch. Theresia suffers from both flaws._
_They took me prisoner. They chained me and put me in a cell. Warriors of the Wyldrylm! Treating a shaman thus! Their time out here has made them ... wild._
_I feared for my life. Throat slit in some filthy cave in this horrid land. Then, in the night, Vid and his warriors came for me._
They rescued you.

_They tried to. We fled in the night, but we didn't get far before Theresia sensed our departure. They trapped us here for days, trying to decide whether to kill us. They demanded that we surrender, but we didn't._
_The end came fast, but then you came._
How did Theresia learn that you left?
_We don't know. One of Vid's men stayed behind. He might have informed on us. But then, that shaman has eyes all throughout these woods. We would have been discovered soon in any event._
You were with Vid and his men?
_Yes. I spent much time with Vid. After my years in Avadon, it was good to spend time with one of my own people again. A true member of our people._
She suddenly seems very self-conscious. _But we don't need to talk about that. About Vid. It isn't important. We need to decide what to do next._
What do we do now?
_It is a difficult decision. It is no longer only my affair, but yours too. We both need to decide what to do next._
We need to return to Avadon. You have shirked your duties long enough.
Jenell looks down at the stone floor. She is far from contrite. _I admit, my journey here did not end well. But ... we will discuss this later._
She steps forward. _I will travel with you. There are things that must be said. Let us go._
(Until Jenell's business in the Jarlswood is resolved, she will always insist on traveling with you.)
You did what you thought was right, but we still need to return to Avadon.
Jenell says, _We do need to return at some point. We have duties here, too. We ... we will discuss this later._
I think we still have business to attend to here.
Jenell says, _I agree. We have pressing business back at Avadon, but we have duties here, too. We ... we will discuss this later._
You enter the grove where you fought the other Wyldrylm warriors. Jenell looks at the carnage. She looks sick.
_To see the people of my land ... to see them end this way ... It sickens me. And yet, you had no choice._
_This is the fault of one woman. Shaman Theresia. She is in charge. She controls them. She is responsible._
This is not our concern.
_Not our concern? A mad Shaman of the Wyldrylm spreading unrest all along the border? That is the definition of what we should be concerned about!_
And she tried to kill a Hand of Avadon.
_That is more important to you than to me, but, if it convinces you to act, then yes. That is true. She is an enemy of Avadon in the truest, most direct sense of the term._
She needs to be stopped.
_Indeed. She is a mad Shaman of the Wyldrylm spreading unrest all along the border. That is the definition of what we should be concerned about._
What do you think should be done?
_We need to hunt her down. When I traveled in this area, I was blindfolded or running in the dark, but she is close. I can use my skills to find her._
_She and any who oppose us must be stopped. The other Wyldrylm warriors must be allowed to flee. They have done no wrong._
Sevilin frowns at this last part. _The servant of an enemy of Avadon is equally guilty. What should happen to them is not important but it is clear._
Shima is with her up until the last part. _You do not understand the dangers of letting foes live. Holklandans do not let nests of vipers remain, no matter how small they are._
Nathalie is irritated. _Yes, the crazy shaman needs to die. However, I don't fight for Avadon to allow enemies to escape. That is not my purpose. Quite the opposite._
I'd like to know more about Vid.
Jenell looks, for the first time that you have seen, truly sad. _Meeting him reminded me of things I have forgotten. Our ways. Our people. The paths I ... I chose not to follow._
Sevilin looks away quietly.
Shima looks away quietly.
Nathalie watches the older woman's difficulty with silent fascination.
_I met him. We spent ... time together. He is going. I am going. I will speak no more of him._
Let's go find Shaman Theresia. She must be removed.
_I am pleased. We indeed need to save my fellow warriors of the Wyldrylm from the influence of that madwoman. If you can help me with this, I will owe you a debt._
_We should travel to the east. They have covered their tracks well, but they will not evade a true shaman!_ She looks down the path, eager to begin.
Shaman Theresia and all of her followers must be wiped out. Let's go.

Jenell looks nervous. _Shaman Theresia must be dealt with, but we also need to save my fellow warriors of the Wyldrylm from the influence of that madwoman. If you can help me with this, I will owe you a debt. If not, I will not forget how you turned from me._
No more delays. We return to Avadon. Now.

Jenell stands up straight. She looks furious. _I will not argue. I will return. However, until we come back here and save my fellow warriors of the Wyldrylm from the influence of that madwoman, I will be displeased. Remember that._
She walks away.
Jenell walks out of the cave, blinking as her eyes adjust to the light. When she sees Vid, she smiles at him and nods.
As the other warriors watch, she walks up to Vid and they look into each other's eyes.
I need to talk to you, Vid.
Jenell says, _In a moment._ The two of them walk off to the side of the grove.
Come on, Jenell. We've lost enough time.
Jenell shoots you a particularly nasty glance. _You will lose a minute more._ The two of them walk off to the side of the grove.
Jenell looks at you. _One moment, [N]._ The two of them walk off to the side of the grove.
(Wait for them.)

Jenell and Vid talk for a short time. Their voices are very quiet. You can't hear a word. He puts his hand on her arm. They lean close together. Their foreheads touch. And then the two of them return. Jenell takes her place by your side.
She says, extremely formally, _Vid, I thank you for your aid. Your service to Avadon will not be forgotten. Now we will go._
Vid, you are still a wanted man.
Jenell looks over at you. _I have told him that, for saving my life, he will be afforded free passage. You will not make a liar of me._
I need to talk to Vid.
Vid says, _We will stay here a short time. I will tell you what I can. Excuse me. We must prepare to leave. It is not safe for us here._ With a final nod to Jenell, he returns to his camp.

Vid says, _We will stay here a short time. If you require information, I will tell you what I can. Excuse me. We must prepare to leave. It is not safe for us here._ With a final nod to Jenell, he returns to his camp.
These are the barracks for a band of Wyldrylm brigands. As you enter, they are engaged in a spirited argument. They know that Avadon has found them. A few want to stay and fight. Most want to leave.
Then they see you. Things become very quiet and tense. Their leader, a massive warrior, turns and faces you. He must have been very important in some tribe before something forced him to flee.

_I am Hunter Merten,_ he says, in a deep, halting voice. _We have decided that Theresia has gone too far. We want to flee. We will go deep into Khemeria and you will never hear from us again. I ask ..._ His voice catches a little. _I ask that you spare us._
Jenell, what do you think?
Jenell looks grim. _Merten ... He was not exceptionally cruel to me when I was held here. He only struck me in the head to subdue me. Once. Or twice. He certainly said nothing on my behalf._
_I will let you decide how to proceed._
Your men can go, but you can stay.
Merten starts to agree to your terms, but his warriors step forward. It is clear that they will fight to protect him.
Why should I trust you?
_You have the word of a warrior of the Wyldrylm. I can give no more._
You can go.
Merten nods. _We will be true to our words. Avadon will have no more complaint about us._ Then, before you can change your mind, they leave.
You have broken the laws of the Pact and assaulted one of its servants. You must pay. (Attack.)
Merten nods. _I will not deny the charge, but I will not die meekly._

This hall is claimed by Shaman Theresia and her inner circle. They have a circle here for discussions and ceremonies. They stand around it, waiting for you. You have to admire their courage and resolve, here in the face of impending doom.
Their leader steps forward. _I am Theresia. I'm sure you have heard of me. So. Avadon came to us. This is the fate I sought to prevent, and yet it has come._

_I assure you that I have committed all of the crimes I have been accused of. I am not ashamed. I hate the laws of the Pact. I will happily die defying them. Yet, before the end, I must ask for a boon._
Why do you hate the Pact so?
_You should ask your friend._ She nods at Jenell. _She believes in my cause, but she is not strong enough to follow it._
_The old ways of the Wyldrylm are good ways. Just ways. All who would ask us to abandon them, no matter how good their intentions are, are our enemy._
You hate the Pact enough to kill a shaman? To create hideous monsters and let them loose in the woods?
_I do. I make no excuses. I have no regrets._
What drove you to come out here?

_A Hand of Avadon visited my tribe, hunting one who sought sanctuary in our village circle. I will not bore you with the details of our ways. I will only say that the Hand's offenses forced me to kill him, before further defilements could occur._
_Then I fled my home._
What would you ask?

Shaman Theresia's defenders look increasingly miserable as she speaks. _All here in this little colony are blameless. Loyal servants of the Wyldrylm, driven from the Pact. They did not want me to kill Jenell. In that, I would have acted alone._
_I ask you to spare them. Let them flee deep into Khemeria. I think Jenell would not object._
Jenell inspects them carefully. _Yes. Theresia speaks the truth. [N], they should be spared. It is just._
Jenell, I can't let them go.
_You must. I demand it. If you refuse me this request, I ... I will fight with you, but I will never be loyal to you._
What sort of crimes have they committed?
_We will not beg and scrape more than we have to. They are not killers. They do not deserve to die here by my side, as much as they want to._
All right, Theresia. They can go.
Jenell lets out a long breath, greatly relieved. Shaman Theresia turns to them. She says nothing. She just points toward the door.
There is a long pause. None of them move. Finally, she says, in a voice of great authority, _Go!_
All of them leave but two. They stand perfectly still, sweat running down their faces. Theresia turns to you. _I am grateful._
Shaman, whatever punishment you suffer, they all must share it.
Jenell lets out a long breath, realizing what she has brought about. You look at her, but she does not meet your gaze.
All of the Wyldrylm warriors face you. They are resolute, but sweat runs down their faces. Theresia looks at Jenell. _You see? Everything I told you? It was all true._ Jenell nods.
Then Theresia looks at you. _I hope you realize what you have lost. Now, let there be no more delay._
Now we must decide what to do with you.
Shaman Theresia says, _Yes. We ..._ And then she raises her staff. It starts to glow. In an instant, all of your foes leap forward, trying to catch you by surprise.
Hunter Merten
Talking: The warriors are leaving.
Runner Vid
Valley Ogre
Seer Bhat'Ul
Valley Titan
Slavering Hellhound
Seer Tyruh
Seer Corahl
Chief Tyranika
Harua
Honored Forge Warrior
Shadowwalker Rai
Honored Forge Sage
Rocks fall from overhead!
Come closer!
Do what you must.
Holklandan War Wolf

You arrive at the place marked on Shima's map, about a day's journey into Holklandan territory. Since you are a Hand of Avadon, you are allowed to travel wherever you want, both in and out of the Pact. However, the fact that Shima came here to kill Holklandans makes your position a little more awkward.
Nathalie should also be very nervous, as people from Kellemderiel are unwelcome on this side of the border. Of course, she is entirely cheery and unconcerned.
Steep hills rise to the north. Several narrow ravines run up into them. At the top, you can see the smoke from cookfires. A large group is camped up there.

At the base of the hill, however, less friendly creatures have taken up residence. You see a crude totem nearby, and massive footprints are visible along the pathways. There are ogres camped nearby. Or something larger.

You are at the base of a large ravine, rising into the hills to the north. There is a meeting place just ahead, or some sort of ceremonial site. You aren't sure. It has two rows of standing stones, with two pairs of benches facing each other between them.
A lone shadowwalker stands at the north end of the meeting place. He watches you silently as you approach. His sword is still in its sheath, but you doubt that he is alone.
Sevilin says, _Remember. We are all still of the Pact. Perhaps it is possible to avoid bloodshed._
Jenell says, _Remember. We are all still of the Pact. Perhaps it is possible to avoid bloodshed._
The ravine to the north is strangely unguarded and barren. All you find are a few old totems and a scattering of patches of rubble and bleached bones. Moving on seems perfectly safe.

And yet, Shima stops and shakes his head. _Looks are deceiving, [N]. The path ahead is sure to be full of traps and ambushes. Shadowwalkers believe in strong defenses. I strongly suggest that we look for another way in._
Another way in?

_We Holklandans always believe in having concealed routes in and out of danger. Very well hidden, but I should be able to spot the signs. We should go south and search the other ravines. At least, that is my humble opinion._
I do not fear their traps. We press on.
Shima is clearly not happy to hear this, but he says nothing. He simply walks behind you, watching the cliffs above you closely as you proceed.
I believe you. Let's turn back.
Shima nods. _Wise as always. Let us follow the cliff wall closely. With luck, I will see something of interest._

You reach the Holklandan camp, perched halfway up a large hill. There are rows of tents and generous piles of supplies. The camp has only just been established, but it seems that the Holklandans are preparing to make it much larger.
This is odd, as you are a good distance from the Farlands. The only reason to make a camp here is to have more forces near the Beraza Woods. That is interesting, and perhaps worrying.
But there will be time to think about politics later. For now, if Harua is to be believed, the Holklandans are likely to treat you as dangerous intruders. Avadon or not.

To the east, you can see that a small group of ogres have made the inevitably fatal error of thinking that they can set up a small village inside Pact territory. With typical ogre ego and lack of foresight, they have built a palisade and set up totems along the pathways.
While Holklandan soldiers will probably soon find these arrogant creatures and drive them out, you have the opportunity to take all that fun for yourself.
Nathalie looks up at you with a wicked gleam in her eye, the pain from her wounded arm temporarily forgotten. _Can we destroy them, [N]? Can we? Can we?_
An icy wind blows down the ravine, making you shudder. This is very odd, considering that it's not actually that cold a day.
Shima looks around, suddenly very alert. _This would probably be a good time to mention that Holklandans often create decoy hidden paths that lead into traps. Just so you know._
Burning Bones

When you step onto the platform, you trigger one of the Holklandan traps. Three piles of rubble begin to move around, forming several huge, lumbering stone figures. Predictably, they lunge toward you.
As they walk, the ground shakes under their feet, shaking loose rubble from the cliffs above.
Shima says, _Beware. Harua's traps are sure to be deadly. As I warned you._
Lumbering Defender
Shima says, _Wait._ He walks up to the cliff wall and examines it. _Yes ... Here._ He pushes on a section of the stone and it swings away, revealing a narrow crack in the wall.
_This path might lead us to the Holklandan camp._
_It will be interesting, I think, to see where this pathway leads._
_I think we are very close to the Holklandan camp. This does not feel like a decoy passage._
You round the corner of the ravine and find that you have reached a dead end. The pathway up is blocked by many tons of rubble. As you turn back, things suddenly get very noisy.
You walk down the narrow, rubble-choked ravine. It's tight quarters, and you start to feel very vulnerable. With good reason. When you are halfway down the pathway, things suddenly get very noisy.

Rocks start raining down on you from overhead. Multiple small avalanches pelt you with debris. The roar is almost deafening, but not loud enough to keep you from hearing the howling. The wolves of the Holklandans have been unleashed.
Shima shakes his head, but he is kind enough to not mention that he warned you.
Harua Honored Forge collapses. He looks up at the sky for one final time. As the life fades from his eyes, he whispers, _My brothers and sisters ... avenge me ... Shima must ... must ..._
And then he dies. With luck, Avadon will not learn all the details of what happened here today. They would not be pleased.

Harua is bruised and bloodied, but he refuses to bow to the inevitable. _We are allies of Avadon, and they have granted us the aid of Craftmaster Nicodemus. His weapons are powerful, and I will turn them against you!_
He mutters a word of command, and his blade begins to glow.

Shima Threespear approaches you and stands at your side. _[N], I must insist. As long as there is a chance you might hunt Harua, I must be with you. This is my hunt too, and I will not be shamed by him again._

You approach the meeting place and are close enough to get a close look at the shadowwalker waiting for you. Even though little of his face is visible, you recognize his build, demeanor, and the monitor's insignia pinned to his shoulder.
It is Harua Honored Forge, the shadowwalker you met in the pit to the east. He nods to you and waves you forward.
Harua holds up his hand. _Please stop, [N]. You are close enough. I have met with you in this place to parley. I do not know that you mean me well._
_I am doing the business of Holklanda of the Pact, loyally, tirelessly, and legally. Or, I was doing such work, before I was interrupted._
_You mean this little circle?_ He waves at the pillars and the benches. _A peaceful meeting place, for calm negotiation without fear of assassination. You will find such throughout Holklanda._
_Very handy for settling disputes. Pity Shima did not think to use it._
I am looking for Shima.
Harua Honored Forge nods slowly. _Of course you are. That is why I set sentries on the roads to watch for your approach. I knew you would follow your fellow Hand soon enough._
He claps his hands ...

Two of Harua's warriors walk down the path from the north. Shima is between them. He is unarmed. His hands are bound behind his back. Though he looks like he has taken a fierce beating, he lacks serious injuries.
The warriors haul Shima forward and throw him to the ground at Harua's feet. He looks down at Shima and then up at you. _Here is your companion. _
Shima is conscious, but he does not move. He silently stares at the dirt inches from his face.
Shima, are you all right?
He doesn't respond. Though he still wears his mask, you can see that his cheeks are burning with shame.
Is he injured?
_No. We have saved him for you and administered only enough punishment to keep him from lashing out at us._
What happened to him?

_He slipped into our camp and tried to murder me. Then, when I deflected his feeble assault, he attacked my men._ For a moment, Harua's voice betrays his considerable anger. _All loyal servants of the Pact, all innocent of any crime, and he tries to slay them._
_I assure you that my soldiers urged me to kill him. And yet, I did not. You should mark that in my favor._
They urged you to kill him?
_I am not the only warrior of the Honored Forge in this camp. Many of us are here. Not all of them are as capable of rising above tribal disagreements as I am._
Why didn't you kill him?
_Well, it was my right. You must understand that. Were he not under Avadon's protection, I would have had him hung from his foolish neck, and smiled as I ordered it._
_But I do not wish enemies in Avadon. So I return him to you._
Now what happens?

Harua kneels down, draws a dagger, and cuts the ropes binding Shima's hands. A soldier leaves to the north and soon returns with Shima's weapons, which he throws onto the dirt by the young shadowwalker's feet. Shima doesn't rise.
Harua says, _He is yours. I return to my work now. Before I go, there are two things you should know._
I don't care to hear what you have to say.
_But you will. You owe me that much._
_You should know that Redbeard will not appreciate your attacking the Honored Forge. We are elevated in his eyes._

_I mean that my clan has been tireless in helping Avadon to achieve its ends. Many fear and resent the power of Avadon. The Honored Forge does not. We respect it, and we have acted to increase it. During Shima's short time here, we convinced him of as much._
Shima closes his eyes. Whatever he has seen, he believes that Harua's words are true.
And what else do you have to say?

Harua looks you in the eye. His fury is starting to escape his control. _Out of respect for Avadon, I have let this fool go, but I promise you this. If any try to kill my warriors or clanmates, I will destroy them._
_This includes Hands of Avadon. And, [N], this includes you. Is that understood?_
It is understood.
Harua nods. _I am glad to hear it. You can go and fight for the Pact in your way, and I will fight for them in mine._
He gives you a brief, sharp salute. Then he and his warriors turn and leave the clearing. When they are gone, Shima rises and reclaims his weapons. He doesn't meet your gaze.
I am a Hand of Avadon. I can do what I wish.
_Sometimes, Hands misuse their power. The Honored Forge supports Avadon because we know that this is only rarely the case. Do not make us doubt our decision._
Harua gives you a brief, sharp salute. Then he and his warriors turn and leave the clearing. When they are gone, Shima rises and reclaims his weapons. He doesn't meet your gaze.
Shima is my friend. I will stand by him.
Harua nods. _You will do what you must, and I will do what I must. Only, know this. The Honored Forge has chosen to support Avadon. Do not make us doubt our decision._
Shima looks at the piles of supplies. _It is odd. An armed camp, so close to the Beraza Woods. Duke Gryfyn is seeking peace with my people. Perhaps not all of them welcome it._
What do you think they are planning?
_Even I do not understand the layers within layers within plans within schemes that make up Holklandan politics. I will say, however, that it is worrying._ He walks on, lost in thought.
You think the Holklandans prepare for war with Kellemderiel?

_I wouldn't want to make a guess. However, as my grandfather said, if it looks like a goose, and sounds like a goose, and bites you like a goose, and voids its waste in your beloved pond like a goose, it is a goose._
He looks slightly embarrassed. _He did have better sayings._
You look at Shima. He walks in silence. He is still stunned by what he has learned.
What is it, Shima?
_I had two things left in my life. Avadon and you. Both have betrayed me. I feel ... alone._
_I wish to go home. I need much time to think._

_I had two things left in my life. Avadon and you. Avadon has betrayed me. I feel ... alone. All I have left is those who fight at my side. When I was abandoned by all, you stood by me. [N], I will never forget that._
_And, as for what I have learned, I wish to go home. I need much time to think._
Shima looks over at Nathalie. _Are you not worried about traveling in Holklanda? People of Kellemderiel are not usually welcome here._
Nathalie looks back at Shima. _I am not of Kellemderiel. I am of Avadon, and I will go where I choose._ There is no trace of a smile on her face.
Shima nods. _Well spoken, but perhaps not all of my people have as much respect for the Black Fortress as you do._
Sevilin puts his hand on Shima's shoulder. _I understand what it is to be abandoned by Avadon. You have my sympathy and my support._
Shima nods. _I do not require sympathy, but your support is most welcome. I thank you, Sevilin._
Jenell looks at Shima with concern. The things Harua said still weigh heavily on the young shadowwalker. She says, _Avadon is not always wise. That is why I had to go on my own journey._
Shima responds, _Thank you for your words. I did not understand before. I did not approve of your departure. I see things more clearly now._
Jenell nods, and they walk on in silence.
You approach Shima. He has collected his weaponry and other equipment. Despite all of his bruises and the odd sprain or two, he is uninjured. He lets out a deep, ragged sigh. Then he looks at you.
_I am glad to see you, [N]. I am also glad that you came for me. I doubt that I would have the courage to track you down and face you myself._
Of course I came for you.
Shima nods. _I am grateful to you. I only hope that I can live up to the debt I owe you._
I didn't want to come for you, but I had no choice.
Shima flinches. _I deserve that, [N]. You must know that I have tried to serve Avadon as well as I could. However, I have another duty, and I could not ignore it._
I am glad that you are safe.
_Not that I deserve to be. My assault was poorly considered from the beginning._
Tell me what happened here?
_I spent a few days circling and scouting the Honored Forge camp. In the end, I decided to attack from the rear, climbing down the sheer cliffs above them._
For the first time, he smiles. _You should have seen Harua's face when he realized that I infiltrated his camp unseen. It will haunt his nightmares._

_Then I realized what I should have known from the start. Whatever my skills, I could not beat all of them alone. I almost killed Harua. My blade came a hair's breadth from his throat. Then he shouted the alarm, and I was swarmed and overwhelmed._
Did you kill any of them?

_No. I did not realize, at that point, how many of the Honored Forge are in their camp. Had I been aware of that, I would have killed as many of them as I could. And, trust me, that would have been a hearty tally._
How did they subdue you?
_Harua was kind enough to tell them to beat me into unconsciousness. It was his own shadowwalker weapons, in the end, that drove me to the ground. Then they bound me._
We must decide what to do now.
Shima turns away from you. He looks up the hill toward the Holklandan camp. _Harua did not lie. The Honored Forge is beloved of Avadon. He showed me letters. One of them even bore Redbeard's seal._
_And yet, I ... I cannot simply abandon my vendetta. Not after all they have taken away from me._
Why is this so important to you?

He continues to look up the hill. _They destroyed my family. They took our honor, our ancestral lands. Their machinations resulted in the death of many of us, including my father. The rest fled our beloved homeland, entering a pitiful exile._
_Harua and his clanmates were a part of that. They are up there now. If I don't face them today, it only delays our final reckoning._
What do you want to do?

He turns back to you, fire in his eyes. _If I had my way, I would travel up there and slay them all, the Honored Forge and their allies. This time, however, I would not be alone. You, [N], would be at my side._
Nathalie nods. _I don't care about Holklandan matters one way or the other, but I know what it is to be abandoned by Avadon. I would aid you._
Jenell says, _Were my family to suffer what yours did, I would do no less, Avadon or no._
Sevilin looks up the hill. _When I was alone with my own vendetta, I was not left alone. I would not deny the same to you._
Is everyone in that camp part of the Honored Forge?
_Yes, or else one of their hirelings. This is a harsh thing I wish to do, but it is the way of Holklanda. If you fight for a clan, you are, in part, culpable for their crimes._
I will not fight an ally of Avadon. Shima, forget this and return to Avadon.
_No, [N]. You must realize that I can delay, but I can never forget, no matter what they do for Redbeard. I will return to Avadon, but my loyalties will always be, in part, elsewhere._
He walks to your side. _I follow you. For now._
Vengeance must be had, but this is not the time.
_Then I will leave Holklanda, but only for now. You must realize that I can delay, but I can never forget. I will return to Avadon, but my loyalties will always be, in part, elsewhere._
I will help you to gain vengeance.
_I thank you, [N]. To their camp we go. I can help you find the hidden ways that will enable us to gain entry. I thank you. If we are successful, you will ever have my loyalty._
Shadowwalker Harua of the Honored Forge comes walking out from behind the barricade, his blade drawn. _Hold,_ he shouts. _Cease this madness! Are we not all of the Pact!_

He looks at you. There is fury in his eyes, but, even now, he maintains control. _[N], this murder of my clanmates and allies must cease. You must leave this place, or you will do great harm to your own cause._
You know that it is too late for that.
_It is not too late, not while I live. You can still leave this place and prevent a disaster._
_There was something I did not tell you earlier. Now I see that I must say all I have to say._
No. I stand with Shima.
_Of course. I think I knew you would all along. Avadon, in the end, only ever looks out for Avadon. And yet, I must speak, so that we might prevent a fresh disaster._
I am a Hand of Avadon. I will do what I wish.
_Of course. I never thought otherwise. And yet, perhaps, I might appeal to what few shreds of sanity are left within you. I must speak, so that we might prevent a fresh disaster._
More talking? If you must.
Harua nods. _I will be brief. My clan destroyed Shima's. It is true. And yet, we did not fight alone._
Harua doesn't hesitate. _My clan destroyed Shima's. It is true. And yet, we did not fight alone._
I have heard enough from you.
You start to raise your weapon, but Shima grabs your arm. _We will hear what he has to say,_ he says.

_Such a shift in power within the Pact does not happen without the approval of Avadon. What is more, Avadon sent several Eyes and Hands to aid us in the destruction of the Threespear Clan. Yes, Avadon aided us._
Why did Avadon help you?
_The Honored Forge has helped Avadon for decades. The Black Fortress realized, correctly, that elevating us would help its ends greatly, and thus help the Pact._
_The Threespear Clan was always too proud to earn influence with Avadon. And thus, they were punished._
Why did you want to destroy the Threespear Clan in the first place?

_Some time, if you have several weeks to spare, someone can explain the centuries of history and politics and grudges that govern the relationships between the clans of Holklanda. Now is not the time._
Why should I believe you?

Shima answers the question. _This is the thing I always wondered. The Honored Forge was always weaker than we were. Pathetic, in fact. And yet, in a short time, they destroyed us. I never understood why._
Harua nods. _No offense is taken. We spent centuries trying to supplant the Threespear Clan, always meeting failure. Only with Redbeard's help could we finally triumph._
_And yet, now that you know all, you must see why you should stop attacking us and leave this place._
So why did Avadon take Shima in?
Harua shrugs. _Who knows? Guilt, perhaps, for what they did to his clan. I'm sure some in Avadon are still capable of human emotions._
Explain. Why should I leave?
_Because, if it comes out that Hands of Avadon attacked my clan, the Honored Forge will turn from you. In this dark time, Avadon cannot afford to lose a single ally._
_Instead, you should listen to my offer._
Shima stands beside you, every muscle tense, barely able to keep himself from leaping for Harua.
Perhaps your clan will never learn what happened here.
_Perhaps. However, you can't afford the gamble. Think. We are talking of the future of the Pact, of the lives of millions! Our little squabbles are of no importance._
You want me to turn my back on Shima?
_Of course! Who cares about Shima? Or you? Or me? You must only do what is best for the Pact._
Tell me your offer.

_I will pay you gold and a suit of the finest ceremonial Holklandan armor. I will leave this place, taking the surviving members of my clan with me. You will leave behind this foolish vendetta and join me in protecting the Pact._
_In return, we will not punish you for the lives you have taken here today. A punishment you truly deserve._
Shima, what do you think of his offer?
_I think the treacherous creature means what he says. And yet, he expects me to forgive his kind for all that were lost. I can never do this._
Shima, do you think that letting him go would be better for the Pact?
Shima looks away. He says, very quietly, _Whether it is or not, my honor commands vengeance._
Harua, you may go.
Shima loks at you with disbelief. He shakes his head. Then he sheathes his blade. _[N], I will fight with you, but we are friends no longer._
Harua Honored Forge nods. _I am sorry for all that has happened, but we must live in the world as it is._ He brings you a suit of fine armor and a pouch of gold coins.
_Now, [N], I depart. The secret of your actions here will stay with us. Go indulge your bloodlust elsewhere._ Then he walks away, taking the survivors with him.
Harua, you must die.
Shima nods. _You see, Harua? Not all have lost their honor._
Harua responds, _You are fools. There is no honor in this. I weep for Avadon and for the Pact._ He steps forward. _I will die now as a warrior. Come, [N]. Slay a true servant of this land!_
And then he charges ...

You feel a strange, warm sensation, that seems to crawl over your skin in waves.
