You have reached a forest, high up in the mountains on the border between the Beraza Woods and the Tawon Empire. These cold, windy woods are in the valley between two high peaks.
The air is crisp and clean, but, as you smell, you detect a hint of smoke. You look for tracks, but, if Nathalie came by here, recent rains erased all trace of it.
There is a structure up here, though. To the west, you see a squat, mossy stone tower, perched on an island in the middle of a mountain lake.

As you look around, you start to feel dizzy and distracted. Someone else might think the sensation was brought on by the thin air up here. You, however, recognize the feeling intimately. The last time you felt it, you were near Zhossa the Mindtaker.

You enter the main hall of this small tower. The building looks like it is at least a century old. This chamber is full of coffins, rubble, and refuse. Everything is cold and still. Spiderwebs hang from the wall.

It doesn't look like anyone has come here for years. Or decades. And yet, the feeling of confusion caused by the Mindtaker's presence is far stronger here. You can almost imagine that he is watching you. Right now.
Maybe this tower has been completely abandoned. Or maybe it is just another of the drake's cunning illusions. You can't be sure.
As you get closer to the tower, the feeling of confusion and distraction intensifies. It is growing harder to concentrate, though, with time, the drake's spells are slowly becoming easier to resist.
You look at the tower and ... and ...
What was that? For a moment, you were sure you heard an explosion, followed by a howl of anger. The sound was very faint though, as if it came from far away. Probably just your imagination.
Shima says, _Stop. Did you hear that? It sounded like ... fire. And screaming. I ..._ He shakes his head. _Never mind. Was just my imagination._
Sevilin says, _Stop. Did you hear that? It sounded like ... fire. And screaming. I ..._ He shakes his head. _Never mind. Was just my imagination._
Jenell says, _Stop. Did you hear that? It sounded like ... fire. And screaming. I ..._ She shakes her head. _Never mind. Was just my imagination._

You walk out of the abandoned tower, frustrated by your continued inability to find any trace of Nathalie. But then ... It's just at the edge of your perception, but you don't let it drift away. You concentrate on it.
Suddenly, Sevilin shouts, _Wait! There!_ He points to the northwest. _I heard it. A scream. It was ... Nathalie._
Suddenly, Shima shouts, _Wait! There!_ He points to the northwest. _I heard it. A scream. It was ... Nathalie._
Suddenly, Jenell shouts, _Wait! There!_ She points to the northwest. _I heard it. A scream. It was ... Nathalie._
It was a scream. A young woman, you would guess. It came from the northwest.
As you get farther from the tower, your senses start to clear. That is why it only takes a small amount of concentration to see what, once you focus on it, is so obvious.

There has been a battle here. The ground is covered with scorchmarks. There are bloodstains and ... bodies. Dead wretches. The air is heavy with the reek of blood and smoke. How did you not notice it before?
And yet, it sounds peaceful. All you hear is a light breeze and the calming sounds of birdsong.
Jenell looks at the scorch marks and nods approvingly. _I think Nathalie has been through here. Recently, by my guess. We should hurry._
Sevilin looks at the scorch marks and nods approvingly. _I think Nathalie has been through here. Recently, by my guess. We should hurry._
Shima looks at the scorch marks and nods approvingly. _I think Nathalie has been through here. Recently, by my guess. We should hurry._

You walk round a thick copse of trees and stumble into several ogres and their wretch servants. They gawk at you silently. They have strange, glassy stares. The drake has a powerful hold on their minds.
Then, as they raise their weapons and mindlessly shuffle toward you, you hear a scream. A single, piercing cry, the same young woman you heard before. It came from the south.
You hear a fiery explosion to the east, close enough that, moments later, a warm, sulfurous draft blows past you. Concentrating, you manage to hear the gibbering roars of infuriated ogres.
Either this is a cunning illusion, or you are very close to Nathalie and she is under attack.

You enter a grove and stumble upon a battle in progress. Nathalie is at the south end of the grove, backed up against a tree. Several ogres and wretches face her, closing in from all sides. She is outnumbered and, after the long running battle she fought to get here, exhausted.

And yet, her powers seem, if anything, even sharper. An ogre tries to close in on her right. She turns, points her right finger, and a jet of flame engulfs the creature. It flees off into the brush, screaming and smoking. It won't be alive long.
And yet, something is not right. She holds her left arm against her chest. It has been injured. And, as powerful as she is, she is young and alone. Without help, she may not last long ...
That's odd. You are sure that you have been in this corridor before. And yet, you never stopped going downstairs. There is something strange happening here.

Nathalie walks up to a wall, touches it with her uninjured hand, and grimaces. She is in pain. _This is as far ... as far as I got before the ogres found me. Had to flee. But ... Let us continue downward. It is an ... an illusion. I can break it, given time._
Nathalie stops again. At first, you think that her injured arm is bothering her. It is, but that's not why she stopped.
She walks up to a wall and touches it. Nothing happens. She walks across the hall and touches the opposite wall. Nothing happens. She smiles.

Then she mutters a word. The wall vanishes in an instant, revealing a natural tunnel beyond. _Every hour I spend here, I can see through more of the drake's tricks. Others may fear it. I am a hunter._
You finish your loop around the circle and step into the magic circle. There is a brief draft of cool air.
You look at the north wall. Where before there was an obelisk, now there is only a gap in the wall.

You enter another large hall. The smells of dust and decay are heavy in the air. You can see several coffins lining the walls. Someone has smashed the lids of most of them. There are no signs of the drake.
There are, however, trapdoors. Dozens of them, all arranged in rows on the floor. Continuing downstairs seems deceptively easy.

Nathalie leans against the wall, exhausted but determined to continue. She says, _Odd. This ... Don't feel the drake as strongly here. These might be the tower's defenses ... not the beast's. Still dangerous. Still need to pass._
There is an obelisk by the pathway leading to the tower. It has been here for a long time. You scrape away the moss, only to find that, whatever words were inscribed here, they have faded away.
You look at the obelisk. A recent burst of fire recently struck the surface. Whatever message was written here, it has been destroyed.
_My fault,_ Nathalie mutters. _A spell went awry when I was fighting my way out. Was just a list of names and dates. Nothing important._
At last, victorious, you emerge from the tower. The drake that infested it is gone, and the tombs are free to crumble in peace.
You look across the water at the tree line. Now that the drake is gone, the woods look different. You wonder what had been concealed and is now exposed.

As you walk out into the cool, fresh air, Nathalie makes a strange, choking noise. She comes close to being overcome with emotion, but she maintains control. _I need to return to Avadon. My arm requires tending._

She mutters, _It should not ... not have happened ... had Avadon done its duty. I was left ... to hunt it ... alone. Their fault. Their ..._ She turns and sees that you are listening. She continues to mutter, but far more quietly.
The leader of the lost band of titans lets out a roar and charges you. Now that the drake is dead, these brutal creatures have found themselves in a remote forest with no idea how they got there.
They are thus dealing with their confusion in the time-tested titan fashion: Looking for something smaller than them and throwing rocks at it. It's worked for them so far.
The writing on this obelisk is in a language you can't understand. You look at it briefly and then ... Oh, wait. It's entirely readable. It was hard to tell in the shadows. It says:
You look at the obelisk. The writing on it is clear and in a language you understand. It says:
Into the circle.
Circle to the circle, with the altar on your left.
Circle on to the circle and reverse.
Circle to the circle, with the altar on your right.
Circle on to the circle, and to the darkness.

You look around this empty crypt, trying to find a way down. The stairway behind you is the only exit. The sensation of the drake being nearby is completely gone. This icy hall must be the lowest level of the crypt.
Nathalie looks at the throne intently. _No. There is something I've missed. I ... I ... Something is coming._
You feel it too. A hidden, malevolent presence in the center of the room. It is the specter of a figure in black robes. The clothes look like the garb of a shadowwalker, but many years out of date.

As the spirit draws its spectral blade and stalks toward you, the rubble in the side alcoves begins to shift under its own power. The bricks reform themselves into golems. However, the constructs don't move. They stand guard in the alcoves. Odd.
Nathalie approaches you and stands at your side. _[N], I must insist. As long as you hunt the drake, I must be with you. This is my hunt and my prey, and I must share in the glory._
As you engage the shade in battle, the spirits in the alcove begin to chant. It's a low, monotonous hum that makes the stone vibrate under your feet.
A faint, glowing membrane appears around the ghostly shadowwalker. You find that your blows are sliding off of your foe, barely damaging it.
The faint, glowing protective shield that surrounded the ghost flashes brightly. Then it fades. Something has caused the protective aura to grow weaker.
With a final blow, you cleave through the spectral energy holding the spirit together. The entire shade crumbles up, as if it was as thin as a piece of paper, and then fades away.
Its remaining servants crumble as well, leaving you surrounded by piles of smoking rubble.
And yet, despite all of your efforts, Zhossa Mindtaker is still nowhere to be seen.

Now that the spectral distractions have been cleared away, Nathalie is free to concentrate. She turns to you. _As I was saying before I was interrupted, I know now! I know what the drake is doing! Where it is hiding!_
_We must go back upstairs! To the entry hall! And hurry ... there may be little time!_
As you walk through this crumbling hall, Nathalie looks around intently. _Yes ... Yes ... Here. I feel him ... There!_ She points at the circle to the north.
You look at the circle. It's empty and dusty, as before. Nathalie says, _Am I the only one who can see past the creature's lies? Look again!_

And you do. You concentrate. Then you see the vague, translucent, shifting form. You concentrate directly upon it. Little by little, your mind pierces the illusion. Zhossa Mindtaker was here all along, standing perfectly still, concealing itself.
Zhossa lets out a long, low, disgusted growl. _Gharrrr ... I have been found. I suspected as much, that I must face you. Come. I am ready._
You return to the stone hall and look around. Zhossa is still concealed in the northern circle.
_Ahssss,_ he says. _Why flee? I know I will be tracked. Confront me, or leave me be._
You approach Nathalie. She is exhausted and panting with exertion. She looks up at you, and while her face looks painfully young, her eyes look far, far older.

Her left arm has been burned. Not with fire, but with acid. A potion and a bit of healing have sealed the wounds and left the limb functional, but the injury clearly still pains her. You have the grim suspicion that the damage will be permanent.
For a moment, she barely seems to see you. Then she starts to cast a spell, determined to attack you. Then she stops and looks at you again. _[N]? [N]? It ..._ She looks harder. _Yes. You are real._
Yes, I am real.
She relaxes slightly and pokes you in the chest, verifying that you are solid. Then she laughs. A shrill sound, that seems to leech out of her some of the terror of her ordeal.
_I almost didn't leave directions for you. You know that? Wanted the ... the hunt for myself. Perhaps not ... wise. But I do have a glorious tale to tell._
I have come to bring you back to Avadon.
She relaxes slightly and pokes you in the chest, verifying that you are solid. Then she laughs, a bitter, angry sound. _Avadon? There is no Avadon, not really. Not anymore. Just you. You saved me._
Nathalie, you've been injured.
She smiles at that, a pained, bitter grimace. _Now I know you are real. None of the drake's pets can think about ... such things. They just obey. And die. Simple things. But you ... You came for me._
What happened to you?

_I ..._ She struggles to recall. _It seems long ago, you know? I returned to the pit where we fought the drake. I ... I sensed it. Power like that, it leaves a trail. Faint, but I was fast on my feet._
_I got here. I entered the tower. It seemed empty, an old crypt with a few fading magical traps. But ... I knew ... Then the drake's servants came in behind me._
_They followed down the stairs after me. They thought I was ... Easy prey. Meat. I broke through their circle easily. Fled the tower._
And when you got outside?

_They followed. Many of them. And it ... It would have been easy to escape. Down the path. Burn any that followed. But the paths ... they shifted. Twisted. I had to fight, so I couldn't concentrate. I was confused._
_They chased me round and round the lake. I burned some. More appeared, some real, some not. They cornered me here. They might even have worn me down eventually, but you saved me._
What happened to your arm?
_A shaman. An ogre. A spray of burning bile, backed by a curse._ She looks down at her arm. _I treated it. It's not infected. It just ... It burns. It won't stop burning._
She looks up at you defiantly. _Ignore it. I can. We must finish our work here._
How many did you kill?
_How many? Many! [N], it was glorious! The sort of battle I dreamed of. I lived it. I even might have survived. Probably? Maybe?_
_I only thought ... I wish I had not faced it alone. Instead, Avadon abandoned me. Again._
_Can there be any question? Zhossa Mindtaker is my prey. Our prey! We must return to the tower. We must slay the beast. It is a menace, to Hands and to the Pact._
_We must kill it and bring its head to Avadon. We will receive the glory that is our due._
We are returning to Avadon. Now. (Leave.)

Nathalie looks stunned. _No! After all I've done? After what the drake did? It cannot live!_ Her voice is shrill and furious. _This is not the end of it. It is not! I will not rest until I have the glory of the drake's destruction._
_If you don't help me in this, I will not forgive it!_ But, by this time, you have left the grove. Nathalie, seething with rage, moves to follow.
The glory?

She looks down at her seared arm bitterly. _I came to Avadon to win glory and to fight for the Pact. They ignored me. Pushed me aside. And, when I saw a monster that needed to be slain, I had to face it alone._
_It must die. They must see that I was worthy. Am worthy._
Where is the drake?

_The drake? The tricky serpent, with its spells and illusions? It is where I encountered it at first. In the tower. Hiding in the crypt. I can feel it. Can't you? That is where we must go. Now, before the worm escapes._
You think you can find it?
_I ... I ..._ The next words come very hard for her. _No. I can't find it. But we, we can find it! [N], I will share this hunt with you. Not with Avadon that abandoned me. With you._
No. Our work is not here. We return to Avadon. (Leave.)
All right. Let's hunt the beast.

Nathalie smiles. Then she winces with pain. Then she smiles again, a tired, wispy attempt at bravado. _Yes. At last. Someone sees my value. Come on. The tower awaits. Let's teach that monster what Avadon can do._

Zhossa Mindtaker watches you as you approach. The creature is visibly weaker than he was when you first fought him. His scales are cracked and losing their color, and his eyes are losing some of their glow.
His battles, first with you and then with Nathalie, have taken a harsh toll. At last, he has no choice but to face you directly.
_Hsssss ... Avadon found me. I thought you would leave me behind. I thought you had worse foesss to fight. Your young mage ... She is persistent. Now I will parley for my life._
You think I will let you live?
_You are a Hand of Avadon. All Hands have their price._ Nathalie snorts.
All right. Let's parley.
Nathalie looks at you with alarm. She whispers, _What are you doing? This is a trick to throw him off his guard? Right? Right?_
Zhossa smiles. _No, young one. You are strong, but you have much to learn. This is where you learn your harsh lessonsss about life._
He looks at you. _[N], this is not the first time I have run afoul of the powersss. I spent my hoard to buy my life before. I will do it now._
No more tricks. You are too dangerous to live. (Attack.)
The weary drake instantly adopts a battle stance. _Yessss ... I will face you. I am tired but not so worn that I will reject a proper challenge._

As you advance on the creature, its form starts to blur. Other drakes, perfect copies of Zhossa, begin to appear on the circle. _Sssss ... Now you will both fight me and the images of me in your own mind ..._
You would surrender your hoard?
_Yesss. I know. For my kind, that bringsss great pain. Great dishonor. These are both true. I am, in their eyes, a wretched thing, for all my skill._
_But I outlive them all, because I know that no amount of gold is worth my own life._
You need to pay for your attacks on the Pact.
_And I will. I will pay you all that I have. I will also flee to the Corruption, a dark and dismal place, where you will not hear from me for the rest of your lifetime. That isss payment._
What exactly are you offering?

_I will flee the landsss of the Pact for fifty yearsss. None of your faction will see or hear of me. I will give you gold and a pair of valuable magical itemsss. I offer these thingsss with my solemn word._
_Also, I must add, if you take my offer, you will not need to fight me. I am tired, but I am still dangerousss._
Nathalie smirks at the creature. _Your words are in vain, worm. You are our rightful prey, and your life is forfeit._
Zhossa, in response, turns to look at you.
It is dangerous to let you live.
_Yessss ... It isss, but I will not emerge from the Corruption until after you are gone. So it isss not your problem._
_I doubt the Pact will even exist by that time, anyway._
My associate demands your life.
_She is young. She hasss many yearsss of life in which to overcome her disappointment. And yet, her foolish bloodthirstinessss should not be indulged._
I can just kill you and take the hoard.
_Not my full hoard. Much of it is hidden by illusionsss. They will last after I am gone. You will only find it with my help._
No deal. You must be destroyed. (Attack.)
Nathalie is stunned into silence. Zhossa gives a smug little smile and nods. _Go down the stairsss. Keep going down, and my hoard will be clear to you._

_Now I will leave. I give my word that I will live up to my end of the bargain._ He lets out a weary sigh. _And to the Corruption I go. Again. It isss a dreary pl_ And, in the middle of the word, he vanishes.

A moment later, a lance of fire strikes where the drake was standing. You turn and see Nathalie, incoherent with rage. She flings bolts of fire around the hall, hoping to strike the concealed drake. It doesn't work. The creature is gone.
You start to speak with her, but she turns away, seared arm clutched to her chest, tears streaming down her face.

Copies of Zhossa Mindtaker begin to proliferate around the room. They all seem completely real and solid, and yet some of them must be illusions. Zhossa's ability to affect your mind has weakened, but it is still very potent.

The copies begin to stalk you. Since they aren't real, all they can do is convince your mind that you have been wounded (or killed). Sadly, you suspect that this will be more than enough to be the end of you.
You heavily damage one of the copies of Zhossa. It pops like a bubble. There is no trace of it, or its tracks, or the blood it has spilled.
All of Zhossa's other images cackle in perfect unison.
You strike one of Zhossa's copies with a savage blow. The creature roars in anger. Droplets of blood strike the stone floor and start to hiss. They don't disappear.

You realize that the Zhossa you struck is the real one. He roars in anger. Then the images of the creature shift and flow together. The real version vanishes. You suddenly are no longer sure where the true Zhossa is.
Once again, you have struck and wounded the true Zhossa. He lets out a long, low moan of pain. Your blows are starting to wear him down.
However, his powers remain. The true image vanishes, and the other shades flow together and split apart.

You deliver a vicious blow to the true Zhossa. The illusion covering his body fades, and you can see how grievously you have wounded him. The pain and loss of blood prevent him from maintaining the illusions.
The shades fade away, and you are left with the drake himself, alone and pathetic. _My last ..._ He gasps. _My last powersss ... they remain._

With a final blow, Zhossa Mindtaker falls to the ground, slain. You barely have time to approach the body before a lance of fire strikes it. And then a bolt of ice. And then more fire. Nathalie screams in fury as she blasts the corpse, incinerating it.
Then she turns away, gasping for breath. _I ... I won. I won. The ... glory? My arm. It hurts. I ... Thank you, [N]. I am ever in your debt. Let us go home. To Avadon._

As you walk down the path toward the tower, Jenell silently seethes with anger. Finally, she can take it no more. _This is madness, following that young, impetuous ... She is putting us at risk, all for her own, private goals._
Wait. Didn't you do exactly the same thing?
This brings her up short. _I ... That was entirely different. It was a matter of Pact business. And ... of honor ..._ Then she decides, wisely, to stop talking.
Nathalie is right. We should hunt the drake down.
_Avadon does not appear to agree with you. Nor do I. However, she is a Hand, and we must support her. No matter on what foolish errands she drags us._
We will find her, save her, and bring her back.
Jenell nods. _Agreed. In normal times, I would be eager to hunt Zhossa down. However, these are not normal times, not in the slightest._

Shima looks at the carnage and destruction left by Nathalie with interest. _Raw power. Quite impressive. But there is a lack of control. A Kellem trait, perhaps. Not the sort of thing you would see in Holklanda._
You think all Kellem mages are like Nathalie?
_I am not sure. I suspect not._ He smiles. _I hope not. I am not sure that Lynaeus could survive the ambition of more than one Nathalie.
Does Holklanda have mages?

_Of course! We are as learned and skilled in the magical arts as any in the known lands. However, my people prize subtlety as well as power. A Holklandan mage can kill with great competence. Only quietly, and with less fire._
What do you think of Nathalie?
_Great skill. Even greater ambition. Questionable self-control. She can be ... worrying._
Shima notes the old, slightly-tarnished razordisks on the floor nearby. _Interesting. That would indicate that this building is of archaic Holklandan construction._
_This would be interesting evidence to support my people's claim that these woods were originally ours. I would report it to my homeland, were I still welcome there._
Demo Demon
You return to Avadon.
Odd. This person's head appears to have exploded.
You find yourself in a fiery, infernal hall, face to face with the dreaded demo demon. He shakes his head apologetically.
_Alas,_ he intones, _there is a problem with the registration code you are using. It is not valid._
_Please let me ask you a question. Did you, in fact, purchase it from Spiderweb Software?_
Yes! I paid for it!

_Then I apologize profoundly for the inconvenience. Write support@spiderwebsoftware.com and ask for a new key. Include the game you registered and the address you ordered from. A replacement will be provided immediately and for free._
_Until then, you may use the portal behind me to return to Avadon again. Again, I am very sorry for the inconvenience._
The demon waves a hand, and a gap appears in the wall behind it.
No. I did not.
The demo demon nods. _I understand. It is very tempting to get a game for free. Everyone loves free things, after all._

_However, the people who spent a huge amount of time making this game need registration fees to do things like feed their families. This is an Indie game. It's not made by some huge company but by a handful of hard-working people who simply love to make games._
_And, while I'm sure you think you had a good reason to not pay for it, someone needs to pay for games. If they don't, there will be far, far fewer games to play._
But it's too expensive!
_We respectfully disagree. This game is quite large and provides many, many hours of entertainment for the fairly modest price we ask for it._
_If you enjoyed this game enough to spend the hours you spent getting to this point, won't you consider enabling the people who made it to make more like it?_
I can't afford it!

_Rest assured that we sympathize. Nobody likes being unable to afford everything they want. However, the hard facts of the situation are unchanged. If people don't pay for games like this, there won't be new games like this._
I don't believe in paying for software.
_We're sure you have your reasons. Copyright law IS abused by large corporations. Many games from other companies are sold with obnoxious DRM that abuses paying customers._
_However, the hard facts of the situation are unchanged. If people don't pay for games like this, there won't be new games like this. No reason for not paying for software changes this fact._
I'm just playing the game until I'm sure that I like it.
The demo demon raises his bushy eyebrows. _Surely, by this point, you can be confident that this is an enjoyable game that functions properly on your computer?_
Now what?
_Now you decide whether or not you wish to purchase this game. It has become very difficult in recent years for small PC and Mac developers to make a living, in large part due to piracy._
_Will you be part of the solution?_
No. I'm not paying. Nyeah!
The demo demo nods sadly. _I am very sorry to hear it. Alas, we are at an impasse. I therefore must free you, so that you can go and enjoy some other entertainment._
The demon waves a hand. In a spectacular display of pyrotechnics, your head explodes.
Sure. I'll buy the game.

_We are very grateful. We feel lucky to have honest customers who believe in supporting what we do. Quit Avadon and restart, and, when the registration screen comes up, choose to go to the Spiderweb Software online store._
_Thank you again. Until then, you can return to Avadon._

A new recruit.
Let me see you.

Another report?
More losses.

I've had enough of this.
More forces to the Wyldrylm.
I need the Eyes' report!

Fabron
Will he see me?
I won't leave without help.
My brother was lost.
Is it time?
Thank you so much.
My brother is avenged.
I will leave soon.
He seeing me yet?
Chomp! Slump!
Gnaw.
Uuuuurp.
I will be heard!
They are hunting us.
A new mission awaits.
Where are those maps?
Redbeard will be furious!
Where's that Khemerian survey?
I need a map of the Svorgald coast.
To see culture again.
Almost lovely.
A Hand visits me?
To be home again.
Die, tyrant!
You have no hope.
We are legion!
This is the end.
The sign says - KEEPER'S TOWER.
The sign says - KEEPER'S HALL.
The sign says - TO CEREMONIAL HALL.
The sign says - GYMNASIUM.

You step into Redbeard's audience chamber, the place where the Keeper of Avadon greets outsiders. And, for the first time, you lay eyes on the master of the Black Fortress, the man who has kept Lynaeus trembling in fear since decades before you were born.
He sets down a goblet, casually wipes his mouth with his sleeve, grins, and waves you forward. _A new Hand, and a good time for it too. Step in here! Let me have a look at you!_

This is a small gymnasium. Here, Redbeard can exercise, practice with his blade, and keep himself in the sort of shape he needs to be in to fend off assassins. Being invited to train here with him is probably a great honor. And a dangerous one.

You ascend to the next level in Redbeard's tower. There is nobody up here. No guards, no couriers, no diplomats. These are Redbeard's private chambers. Exploring them without permission might be a very dangerous activity.
The chamber itself seems to be a combination of a magical workshop and a theater for displaying ... something. There is a magical circle in the center of the room, surrounded by benches.

As you enter the room, pairs of red lights appear in the shadowy alcoves. Six pairs, each seven feet up. You soon realize that these are the glowing eyes of statues, one in each alcove. Their heads swivel to watch you as you move.
These massive slabs of sentient rock must be the defenders of Redbeard's hall. Proceeding might be very dangerous.
This chamber is very disorienting. It seems like it should be deep under the earth, instead of high up in Redbeard's Tower.

The ground is raw basalt, that crunches under your boots. Caldera of bubbling magma surround you, blasting you with heat and sulfurous gasses and making you feel like you might pass out at any moment.
In the center of the chamber, you see a stone basin. The clear water within sparkles like diamonds, tempting you with a soothing respite from the heat.
At last, you reach the highest level in all of Avadon. Windows look out on all sides, giving a spectacular view of the Wyldrylm to the west and Holklanda to the east.

These are Redbeard's private chambers. There are no guards and no signs that anyone but Redbeard ever comes here. The only sounds are the echoes of the winds outside. Despite the great luxury of these chambers, there is something powerfully depressing about them.
You get close to the pool in the center of this chamber. The heat from the magma is overpowering. The water in the basin beckons to you.

This is the first floor of Redbeard's Tower, where the Keeper of Avadon meets with the Hands, Eyes, and Hearts, as well as the assorted diplomats, supplicants, and courtiers who come to ask for help or mercy.
It is far quieter up here than downstairs. Nobody wants to be the loudmouth who irritates Redbeard. That can be very dangerous.

You can see his hall to the east. Several people wait patiently outside his chambers, hoping that he will decide to spend a few minutes hearing petitions. He usually doesn't, especially in these chaotic times, but they wait anyway. For day after day.
You enter an old, stately hall, one that is usually locked away. It is both lovely and imposing, and someone recently went to the effort of lighting candles all along its length.
It stretches off into the shadows to the east. You see another exit at the far end. Perhaps Redbeard retreated here when the attack happened.
Then someone steps out from behind a pillar. The hall is not empty. You see one of your companions ahead, waiting for you and eager to talk.
As you walk farther east, the halls get darker and dirtier. The gate ahead is open. The ceremonial hall doesn't look like it has been used for many years.
Perhaps it is used for the coronation of a new Keeper. Since Redbeard has been in charge for many decades that would explain why it has been left sealed.

But it is open now, and someone is fighting within. As you approach, you see flashes of light and hear the clash of steel on steel. You see the shadows of two people, one smaller, one larger, fighting to the death. You are just in time to interrupt a savage duel.

Redbeard's tower, unsurprisingly, has a number of guards. They are different from the warriors downstairs. They are far larger, far stronger, and far dumber. Redbeard chooses as his personal guard those who could entertain no thoughts of ambition.
Their eyes follow you as you pass. They are ready to crush you at the slightest sign of treachery. Enlightened conversation is completely out of the question.

Their eyes follow you as you pass. They are ready to crush you at the slightest sign of treachery. However, you think you detect signs of envy and admiration. News of your growing success in Redbeard's service must be getting around.
The stone sentinel's head turns to follow you as you walk around the laboratory. A palpable sense of menace radiates off of these creatures.
You try to talk to them, but they are mindless automatons. The only question is what you have to do to get them to attack you.

You open the cabinet and find stacks of papyrus sheets, covered with Redbeard's sloppy handwriting. Some of the pages are yellowed and crumbling. The Keeper has been writing notes and stowing them in here for fifty years.
One sheet, on the top of one of the piles, catches your attention.
_[N] showed early promise. And yet, is working with some of our most questionable Hands. Helpful pair of eyes watching them? Or source of corruption?_
_So far, [N] shows no signs of disloyalty. Surprising skills. Will leave where is._
_Recently, [N] showed signs of disloyalty. When things calm, time in dungeon may be necessary. Simple scrying, to make sure no problem._

There is a Hand here, waiting to see Redbeard. He furiously stalks back and forth, muttering to himself. He must have just returned from a mission. The dents in his armor haven't been repaired yet, and there is a red-stained bandage wrapped around his leg.
When he sees you, he nods in greeting. _Haven't seen you before. Been out in the wilds. Welcome to Avadon. I'm Hand Barne. You're not catching me on the best day._
Hand Barne continues to pace around the hall. He really should be resting and letting his leg heal, but he is far too agitated to stay still. He mutters, _When will he call me in?_
I haven't seen you around.
_I've been out in the wilds. The Farlands. We've all been. I've never seen Avadon with so few Hands. It's worrying._
Why are all the Hands away?
_Sometimes it happens that way. Weeks of quiet and boredom, and then twenty things go wrong and we go mad hunting down the malefactors._
_But lately ... It's been ... I don't want to say more until I talk to Redbeard._
You have been on a mission?
_Yes, and I'll go out again as soon as I see Redbeard._ He looks down at his leg. _Not enough time to get over this scratch. But a few potions, and I'll be ready to do my duty._
_Others, they weren't so lucky as me. Things went wrong._
How did your leg get hurt?
_I was slow. A bandit grazed me with his spear. Don't worry. He didn't live to boast of it. None of the Tawon will think they can attack our Hands without suffering for it._
What was your mission?
_A mess. That's what it was. We've been seeing signs for months of trouble in the Tawon Empire. Four of us were going to a village out there. We were going to collect someone with information._
What happened in the village?

_We never got there! Five miles outside of it, brigands ambushed us. Twenty of them, five for each one of us! And it was no disorganized rabble either. They were prepared, and they didn't stop when they knew we were from Avadon._
You think they were expecting you.
_I won't be coy about it. They knew we were coming._
_We butchered them, but two Hands died. Two! Four of the brigands tried to surrender, but we weren't having that, not after they killed some of our own._
_We had to retreat. We grabbed a passing horse and cart and fled back to the pylon. But Redbeard will hear of this, I will make sure of it! This insult must be answered_
What do you need to say to Redbeard?
_Someone in the Tawon Empire was hunting Hands. Two of my friends were just killed, left dead in the dirt on the road. We barely brought their bodies back._
_I am not setting foot out of this hall until I know Redbeard has heard personally what happened. And what else is happening._
Well, what else is happening?
He shakes his head. _I'm not going to be known as a spreader of rumors. But if half of what I've heard from the other Hands is true, someone is hunting us._
_Be very wary. Someone tried to kill us. They will soon do the same to you._ Something occurs to him. _You've been out, haven't you? Seen anything unusual?_
Nothing I didn't kill myself.
He grins. _I only just met you, and I like you already. But stay wary all the same._
There is a shadowwalker who keeps contacting me. (Describe him.)
Barne thinks about this. _Hmmm. Spies and diplomats are always approaching us Hands, offering us this or that for this or that. This fellow sounds ... unusual. But not that unusual._
_He hasn't tried to kill you yet, so he's probably just trying to use Avadon to his advantage. Just don't trust him._
No. Nothing.
He nods. _I'm glad to hear it but stay wary. Your turn will come soon enough._
The closer you get to the crystalline pool in the basin, the stronger your desire to drink from it. You stumble to the edge and put your hands on the sides.
As you prepare to plunge your head in, you notice words on the side. _FOR THE SUSTENANCE OF THE KEEPER_
Drink.
You plunge your head into Redbeard's basin and drink deep. The water is amazing. It's cool and fresh and ... it ... it is infused with power. There is a powerful enchantment on the basin, that ...

That you have not been prepared to receive. The water burns in your stomach, releasing its power. You can't withstand Redbeard's magic. You wither away, from the inside out, and die writhing on the basalt floor.
Back away.
There is something about the words on the side that seems like a warning. With a supreme exercise of self-control, you back away from the basin.
There is powerful magic at work here, but it is for Redbeard's benefit, not yours.
There is one person in this library. She is an old woman with graying hair and the garb of the Wyldrylm. She runs from bookshelf to bookshelf, desperately hunting for scrolls and records.
When she sees you, she says, without breaking stride, _I am Heart Jarvina. I don't know you, and I don't have time to properly meet you yet. Soon, when these troubles are over._
Heart Jarvina continues to run around the library, searching for records and maps.
You are a Heart?
_Yes. One of Redbeard's trusted advisors. Not that anyone has explained those things to you. You are new, and we are busy._
What can you tell me about Redbeard?

_The Keeper? Talk to him yourself. He will want to meet you. He meets all Hands before they go out into the wilds. He might even talk to you later. You should visit him from time to time. He might have more work for you._
What are you looking for?
_Information. There are many things happening, things that must be addressed. I am finding the maps and histories and so on so that I can suggest where Redbeard should send Hands next._
What sort of things are happening?
_Riots. Raids. Signs of unrest. Rumors of ... Things have become very upset lately, and the problems in the dungeons have not helped._
_Do not concern yourself with the why and the how. Just do what the Hearts and the Keeper tell you, to the letter, and you will prosper._
You tell Redbeard what to do?
_I give my advice. That is the task of a Heart. I spent many years fighting as a Hand and proving my wisdom. That is how I earned this rank._
How can I help you?
_Please. Just leave me. I need ... There!_ She grabs a map off of a shelf. _Excuse me. Much to do._ She runs off.

There is a young man wandering through the library, lost in thought. His hair and clothes are immaculate, done in all the latest styles. You guess that he is from Kellemderiel before he even opens his mouth to speak.
He turns to you and gives a tight little smile. _So there are still Hands in Avadon. I was starting to think that they had all retired. I am Fabron, the envoy from Kellemderiel._
_There is much you can do for us. And we will give proper consideration, of course._
Fabron examines you, wondering how best you can be used to the advantage of Kellemderiel. _Yes? What else do you wish to know, warrior of Avadon?_
You are an envoy?
_Of course. All powers in Lynaeus send envoys to Avadon. There are some tasks that can only be done by Redbeard's warriors._
_Nobles send me requests, and I pass them on. With, of course, massive rewards. It is the only way we can keep even with our enemies._
Our help is always expensive?
_Of course. Avadon provides powerful justice, but expensive._
And who are your enemies?
_Do not be naive. The enemies of Kellemderiel are all that are not Kellemderiel. Such as the greedy and vengeful creatures of Holklanda._
Isn't Holklanda part of the Pact?
_Unfortunately, yes. We are sworn to fight to defend them. When they are not scheming to steal from us and to keep the territories they stole from us in the Black Age._
_But this is not the time to discuss such things._
How long have you been in Avadon?
_Months. An eternity. I am not to be relieved for a season._
You do not care for Avadon?
_Do not be offended. Avadon is cultured by the standard of Lynaeus. However, it is crude and barbaric compared to what we are used to._
Tell me about Kellemderiel's culture.
_Of course, it is the envy of all the known lands. Our food, our clothes, our bards. Being away from it pains me. But these tiresome discussions are drawing us away from my purpose._
What would you hire me to do?

_So much to do. Hmmm. Ah, yes. You would have access to the dungeons, wouldn't you? I believe there is someone named Quennel down there. At least, he was taken down there, and his body was never returned to his family's keep._
_We have had word from Avadon that he could be freed, but he has not been. We will pay well if you go down there and find out what happened to him._
Why was he put in the dungeon?

He waves his hand airily. _Oh, I don't know for sure. He was part of some conspiracy that angered Avadon. He was caught and brought here. Based on what they learned, all of the conspirators were killed._
_Just an unimportant, tiny bit of history._
He could leave, but he hasn't?
_So our sources have told us. It is most unusual, and his family very much wants him back._
Quennel has agreed to return to Kellemderiel.
_Oh, really? That is a surprise. I imagine he has been thoroughly broken. His nobles will be very pleased._
He gives you a pouch of coins and a wand. _That is the sort of thing you Hands need, isn't it? Money and things that make fire? We appreciate your help._
I met Quennel. He is alive, but he will not return.
_Ahhh. That is unfortunate. Well, not for me. I never met the man. Of no interest to me. But his nobles will be displeased. Still, he is alive, and they will be happy to hear that._
Is there anything else you want done?
_There is. And you will be very well paid. There is an exile from Kellemderiel. Her name is Angevine. She is hiding in The Kva, somewhere near Goldcrag._
_I'm afraid that she needs to be killed. It absolutely needs to be done. Or so I am told._
Why don't you kill her yourself?
_Because The Kva would be very angry if we sent our armed troops wandering around in their lands. There is still much anger from the Black Age._
Why does she need to die?
_I have no idea, really. I imagine she has a claim on some piece of land or other, and the nobles currently on that land want to make sure she won't return to take it._
_It is a depressing business, unrelated to the health of the Pact, but it is the sort of thing only Avadon can do properly._
Where is she?
_She travels a lot, but the spies of our nobles have seen her in the lands around Goldcrag. I don't believe that she will be there for long._
Angevine is dead.
You tell Fabron the story. He is quite pleased. _Then I am able to pay you, and I have earned my portion of the fee as well._
He gives you a pouch. It contains gold coins and an old, scratched scarab. _That scarab belonged to the nobles who hired you. Does them no good, of course, but it can aid you._
Angevine is dead. (Lie.)

You tell Fabron a fabrication. He doesn't seem to believe you. He also doesn't care whether you are telling the truth or not. _Then I am able to pay you, and I have earned my portion of the fee as well._
Angevine has fled. (Lie.)
You tell Fabron a fabrication. He is displeased. _Then I am unable to pay you, and thus I do not get a portion of the fee. I am disappointed._
_But never mind. She will be found and killed. The nobles seemed very determined in that regard._
I decided to leave Angevine alone.
You tell Fabron the story. He is displeased. _Then I am unable to pay you, and thus I do not get a portion of the fee. I am disappointed._
Do you want me to do anything else?
He thinks. _Perhaps, but not yet. I need more time to evaluate what is happening to Avadon before I can make a judgment. Now excuse me._ He wanders off, lost in thought.

There is a young woman, probably not even eighteen, sitting on the bench and chewing on a roll. She looks completely out of place in the grandeur of Avadon. Her dress is rough, humble, and torn, and her feet are bare.

When you get close, she immediately leaps to her feet and bows to you. _I humbly greet you, warrior of Avadon. I am Laurella of Dhorl Stead, in Khemeria. I have come to ask mighty Avadon for your help._
Laurella sits at the table, picking at her bread and dried fruit and sipping her tea. She is clearly overawed by her surroundings, but she does a good job of concealing it. She is very brave.
You note that there is a pack at her feet. It seems that she is about to depart.
_I thank you for your attention. I have come far to ask for help for my tribe, in Khemeria. Have you been assigned to aid us?_
I know nothing of that.
_Then I am sorry for taking your time. Excuse me._ She returns to her meal.
Perhaps I can help you.
_I am sorry, but I was told that only the ... The Hearts, they are called? Only they can order help for us. Have you been sent from them?_ You say that you haven't.
I am going to Khemeria now to deal with your problem.
Her face lights up. _Really? You are really going to help us? I ... Thank you. I thank you. And have you come to me to hear my tale? I will tell you what I can._
It is strange that she has so little fear of you. Khemeria is one of the Farlands, a sworn enemy of the Pact. She must have had a very good reason to come here.
Tell me about Khemeria.

She smiles sadly. She clearly misses her home. _It is my home. It is beautiful, and the lands are rich. Our warriors and shamans are mighty._ She hastens to add, _Though we have no intention of angering the Pact._
_And our spires, they are truly ..._ She is speechless with awe. _I long to see them again._
How did Khemeria come to oppose the Pact?
She seems nervous. _I only know what I was taught. I do not wish to give offense. Once the Wyldrylm and Khemeria were one. Tribes living near each other, sometimes trading, sometimes fighting._
_But, while the Wyldrylm was content to stay barbarians, we of Khemeria saw the stone spires and cities of the other lands, and we wanted them for ourselves._
So you began to move into cities?
_Yes, with mighty walls and towers of stone. These tribes were in the north, and came to be called Khemeria._
_And the bar ..._ She chokes off the word 'barbaric.' _The southern tribes joined the Pact to avoid our might. And ..._ She stops herself once again.
_I am sorry. The Pact is mighty, and we obey their laws. I do not want to anger you._
Tell me about your spires.
_We make towers and castles of stone. Not delicate or weak, but massive. Huge blocks of granite, moved with muscle and magic._ Her eyes gleam with awe. _And ..._
She stops. _I am sorry. They are nothing to compare with the works of the Pact._

She recalls her journey. You can see on her face how difficult it was. _I walked. Through the Wyldrylm. It was difficult. And dangerous. If I was found ... It would have been ... I am glad to be here._
How did you evade detection?
_I only traveled at night. I hid in undergrowth and piles of refuse during the day. There was little to eat. It was slow. But I had to come here. I had to! Only Avadon could help us!_
What would have happened if you were caught?
_If a Wyldrylm tribe found me and realized I was from Khemeria? I ... I took a great risk coming here. But I had to._
How will you get home?

She smiles. _Heart Miranda came to see me. She is very kind. She has given me papers of passage, with the seal of Avadon. Not even the Wyldrylm tribes would touch me with this paper._ That much is true. Even the most foolish bandit would not bother one under the protection of Avadon.
_I will walk back proudly! On the roads!_
I am going to Dhorl Stead. I wish to learn what has been happening.
She is eager to tell you, though the memory of it is very clearly painful. _It took three months to get here, so my tale is old, but I will say what I can._
_I am from the village of Dhorl Stead, in Khemeria. We serve lord Carsta'Arl, who lives in the mighty stone fortress of Oghrym'Tor, whose stone walls block out the sun._
_But, a year ago, our village was stalked. A beast roams the night, a horror of shadow and blood._
The creature hunting your people has been destroyed.
Laurella nods, grinning broadly. _I have heard. You were victorious. My brother was avenged. I will spend my life telling all who will listen of the mercy and strength of Avadon._
How long will you stay here?

_Not much longer. I am gathering supplies and regaining my strength for the long walk back. And, I confess, meeting as many Hands as I can. I would like to do what I can to join my Stead to Avadon. You are a mighty ally, and perhaps there are things we can offer you._
_Knowledge. Warriors. I do not know. Our lord failed us, but you did not. Perhaps our fear of you all these years was misplaced._
I am returning to Dhorl Stead.
Laurella stops smiling. Her brow wrinkles. _Returning? But ... The beast is dead. Why do you need to return? Do you ... have doubts about us?_
We are investigating the creation of the beast, to make sure no other such creatures are created.

She smiles, relieved. _Well then. The justice of Avadon was even greater than I suspected. I will return home soon, so that I can help you if need be. Excuse me. I must prepare._ She sits down and eats more quickly, eager to leave.
I can't tell you, but there are a few minor issues I need to deal with.

She is still skeptical. _All right. I will return home soon, so that I can help you. Or speak for my people, if need be. Excuse me. I must prepare._ She sits down and eats more quickly, eager to leave.
The works of Avadon are none of your business, Farlander.

She looks at you with wide eyes. For the first time, she has a flicker of doubt about the wisdom of her actions. _Well, I ... I ... I will be leaving soon. To return to my people. I thank you for your past help. I ... Excuse me._  She sits down and eats more quickly, eager to leave.
Its walls block out the sun?
_Excuse me. We of the western tribes have our own way of telling tales. I will restrain myself._
Tell me about this beast.

_It is large, tall as a mighty warrior. It moves like the wind, in a cloud of rot and shadow. It circles our homes and farms in the night, tearing apart any traveler it can find in its lust for our flesh._
_And then, the following morning, it is gone, leaving us with nothing but tears and what is left of our loved ones._
How many has it killed?
_We do not know for sure. We do not know how many Steads it feeds upon. We have lost dozens._ She swallows, hard. _Including my dear brother. It was his loss that moved me to act._
Why come to us? Why doesn't this Carsta'Arl help you?

_We beg for his help. He does not answer. He shuts himself up in his fortress and is deaf to our pleas. We do not understand it. Thus, I come to you. Since we pay so much to the Pact in tribute, we thought you would have reason to protect us._
And you know nothing else about this beast?
_No, nothing. We sent warriors into the woods to find it, but they never returned. Thus, I ask for your help. And that is all I have to tell you. I am so grateful for your aid._

You are surprised to find a wretch sitting here in Avadon. He sits in a shadowy corridor of Redbeard's glorious hall and gnaws on a bone. His robes are torn and stained, and his chin and jowls are covered with sauce.
He gives you a wave when you approach, though he doesn't rise. _I, Lord Svarl, envoy of High Lord Deathskull, greet you. And I ..._ He loses track of his speech, shrugs, and returns to his gnawing.

Lord Svarl continues to messily gnaw his way through an unending dinner. Occasionally, he breaks through a bone to a nice pocket of marrow and makes some happy slurping noises. The disgusted looks of Redbeard's supplicants are lost upon him.
He looks up at you, considers saying something, and then returns to his chomping.
What is a wretch doing in Avadon?
_Eating._ He belches. _Your food. Very good. And I get all I want._
_We wretches are not all stupid. Most. Not all. Some in Wretch Lands wise enough to use Avadon. Good, strong ally, you are._
_We ride, me and my guards. All are allowed to travel on the main roads. Is the law of the Pact. Then all can come to Avadon._
And you are an example of a smart wretch?

_Yes! Look at this!_ He waves a bone at you. _Could be in Wretch Lands, hunting rats, fighting other tribe. Instead, I, Lord Svarl, am here, safe and with meat! Not all wretches as smart as me. They fight Pact. Not smart._
And you are a lord?
_Yes! High Lord Deathskull says so! Lord among wretches, Svarl is!_
You are an envoy here?
_Yes! All smart peoples send envoys to Avadon! Must be friends with Avadon. Then Avadon hurts others and not you. High Lord Deathskull is strong and wise, so he sends me._
Tell me about High Lord Deathskull.
_Is mightiest leader of mightiest tribe, and talking to Avadon will make him mightier still. Only Avadon and the Pact stronger than him!_
What do you want from Avadon?
The wretch gets a cagey look. _We have plans. Messages and offers. To get to those who can make decisions. The Hearts. And Redbeard. We have plans._
But you want nothing from me?
_We do! You are Hand. Hands who help us, we will pay them. We know Hands do great things. For right price._
Are you here to get help?
Svarl nods. _We are. We try to get message to Redbeard. None take it. They look down on us. They don't let me in. But you ..._
He presses a folded up piece of paper, wrinkled and stained with wine, into your hand. Then he points down the hall to the east.
_Give letter to Redbeard. I pay you. Redbeard is helped. Things better for all._
What is in that letter?
_Offer. Good offer. Not a waste of time. You take!_
I delivered your letter.
Svarl nods. _And answer comes back. 'No.' Not happy. Redbeard misses good opportunity. But I am not done. Other ways we can help Avadon. Ways they help us._
_Oh, and reward. Here is thing. Thing we ... uhhh ... Thing we found on path. Want you to have. Not good for us. Too delicate for hacking._ He gives you a long rapier, still in its sheath.
I can't deliver your letter.
Svarl nods. _No surprise. None help the wretches. Afraid of Redbeard. Should be afraid. But no reward for you. I give reward to foolish Hand who does take letter._
Is there anything else you would pay me to do?
_Hmmm._ He looks you over. _Maybe. But I think you not ready. Get bigger swords for hitting. Then we see._
Lord Svarl nods eagerly. _Is good! Wretches and Avadon, working together! Natural allies!_
_I get message from High Lord Deathskull. You in Jhereth Deeps, yes? Bad place for my clan. Is where Hegra Clan is. Long-time enemies. Want to see them on stakes. Impaling, I mean._
_Get our vengeance! Slay leader of Hegra Clan. For that, get valuable things we found. And treasure of Hegra Clan. Much treasure._
Why should I get involved in this dispute?
_For pay! We pay! What better reason to do anything?_
How does this help the Pact?
_You do this, there are less wretches. What makes you humans happier than less wretches?_ He smiles bitterly and crunches a bit of femur between his teeth.
How can I find them?
_Go to Jhereth Deeps. They try to rob you soon enough._
The chieftain of the Hegra Clan is dead.
Lord Svarl bounces around in his chair, almost childlike in his enthusiasm. _And the other wretches? Many dead, yes? Is a good day! Happy day for Lord Svarl and High Lord Deathskull!_

He rises from his chair with difficulty, laden down by an abdomen full of meat. Soon he returns with a beautiful longbow, that he presents to you. _Another thing we ... found. By the road. Good reward, sign of union between wretches and Avadon!_
Anything else you would pay me to do?
_Not yet. Lord Svarl out of rewards. Send back to Wretch Land for more. Need to ... find more treasures in road. Maybe soon have more._
I am looking for someone near Goldcrag who is smuggling blades to the wretches.

Lord Svarl's mouth hangs open. The bone drops from his hand. For a diplomat, his poker face is definitely subpar. _You want ... I ... Weapons for wretches? Shocking! Nothing about it ... I know nothing._
All right. Sorry for bothering you.
_Well, I ... I forgive you. No harm done._ Relieved, Lord Svarl returns to his endless meal.
Tell me what you know, or I'll have the dungeons pull it out of you.
Lord Svarl looks pained. _Please, don't tell High Lord Deathskull. If he knows I told, I ... Avadon! Always their gaze brings pain._

_Yes, we buy weapons. Merchant is Neray. Blame her. Not me. I know nothing. Well, nothing but that._ He starts to shake in terror. _Please! Please don't kill me!_ You leave the pitiful creature alone to regain his composure.
At last, you stand before Redbeard, who is alone in his enormous stone hall. He is not what you expected.

He is a massive man, over six feet tall and broad of shoulder. The hair and beard that are his namesake are, as expected, bushy and fiery red. He looks like he is only a few years older than you. Which, considering that he has been the Keeper of Avadon for almost sixty years, is a little odd.

But the strangest thing is his mood. Despite the chaos inside and outside his fort, he seems strangely jolly. A genuine grin doesn't seem to leave his face for a moment. He steps forward to clap you on the shoulder. _Welcome, new Hand. Welcome to Avadon._
I thank you for your welcome.
He nods. _Politeness. Good. Manners are a valuable thing to have out in the wilds. A good blade, of course. And knowledge of the rightness of our cause. But calm and a kind word can do so much, eh?_
_Even in these chaotic times, I always greet my new recruits. I never send anyone to risk their lives without at least that little honor. And, of course, there is one small bit of business._
I would have been here sooner, but I was sent into the dungeons.

_Yes. Of course. Miranda sent word ahead. Unfortunate that you aren't getting time to settle in. But then, nobody volunteers to serve Avadon because they want time to relax. No sipping wine and eating grapes for us, eh?_
I humbly offer myself to your service.
He takes a step back, feigning shock. _Of course! Such eagerness! Such obedience! Avadon never seeks anyone but the meek, yes? Well, your kind offer is accepted._
What is that?
He stands up straight and adopts an air of bemused self-righteousness. _I, Redbeard, Keeper of Avadon and defender of the Pact, offer you the honor of being a Hand of the Black Fortress._
_Do you swear to obey our orders and give all for the safety and security of the Pact?_
I do so swear.
Redbeard nods. _Good to hear it. I guess now you have no chance of being a spy or assassin. Not if you swore an oath!_ He winks at you.
_Now, I have a question for you._
I will give all I can to protect the Pact.
Redbeard nods. _But you won't swear, eh? Noted. I have never had much faith in oaths. Seen too many of them broken. But I do love tradition. Ceremony. Yes?_ He laughs.
I will follow your orders as I see fit.

Redbeard nods, but you see in his eyes, for the first time, a dangerous glint of annoyance. _I admire independence. Require it, in fact. But I also expect obedience. Forget that, and you may find yourself back in the dungeon sooner than you think._
Then his dark mood passes. _Now, I have a question for you._
_All come here to serve the Pact. Though they have very different ways to do it. Some that involve serving me. And some that ... oppose me._
_But service is never the only reason. Not with so much wealth and power available, eh? So tell me. And I assure you, I have heard everything. What do you want here?_
I only want to serve the Pact.

_Of course. A paragon of virtue. A creature of pure, undiluted duty. We get those from time to time. It never lasts. There will be plenty of temptations. I suggest you decide which one to succumb to first._
_I suppose, then, that is all. I must return to work ..._
I want the glory of battle.

He nods. _Bloodlust. The rawest form of power. It is a delight, isn't it? I confess that is why I came to Avadon myself. I had a true talent for it. Really ascended in the ranks._ He kicks his throne with the back of his foot.
_I suppose, then, that is all. I must return to my work ..._
Wealth and power sound good.

He grins. _I admire your honesty. And I would not believe you if you said otherwise. When you are here, your life will be in constant danger. Your wealth and power will be earned. Just don't be greedy. That is a path to the dungeons._
I haven't really thought about it.
_Really? All the work to come here, and you have no idea what you wish from your life? Fascinating. And not the slightest bit suspicious. Still, focus on duty is appreciated._
Where should I go then?
_Back to Miranda, and quickly. She will have much for you to do, and I must do my best to hold back the limitless chaos out there._ He makes a grand wave with his hand.
Then one of the Hearts comes in, her arms full of maps and scrolls, and he returns to work.
Wait! There is something I need to know.
Redbeard sighs. _Curiosity. Inquisitiveness. Those are such a trial. All right. One question._
What has been happening? Where are the Hands?

_There have been an unusual number of problems happening lately. It happens from time to time. The sort of thing that keeps life interesting. Just get to work, and everything will be calm soon. We can sit around, eat grapes, and ..._

Then one of the Hearts comes in, her arms full of maps and scrolls, _Ahhh ... This will have to wait until later. Such a shame. Return to Heart Miranda. Time to begin your labors._ He waves you away and returns to work.
I have heard many rumors about you. That you have three wives. That ...

He holds up a hand. _Stop right there. The outside world is full of mad ideas about me. I am a humble servant of the Pact, nothing more. I am not married. My three most loyal assistants in Avadon are called my wives. A simple nickname. That is ..._
I saw a prisoner in the dungeons. He was held in place with magical bonds.

He laughs. _Oh, old Lexrem. He tried to assassinate me once. So very long ago. He has had time to regret it. I assure you of that. He is there as an example to all those who would try to unseat me. None can succeed, and the punishments are ..._

You approach Redbeard and try to speak with him. However, with the Hands coming for orders, Hearts delivering information and advice, and his own need to plan Avadon's actions, he has no time to speak with you.
_What, you?_ he says. _Return later. I will have time to speak with you soon._ He waves you away.
You return to Redbeard's chamber and find the Keeper sitting in his throne, hands in his lap. Eyes closed. Scrolls and reports scattered on the floor to either side.

At first, you think he is asleep. That, or simply unaware of your presence. Then, as you turn to leave, he says, _I never really thought it would be like this. In the beginning. Oh ... Must be sixty years ago now._
Sorry. I didn't mean to disturb you.

He continues as if you hadn't said anything. _I was a farmer's child. Could have spent my life threshing wheat. Shearing sheep. That sort of life. But there was still unfinished business from the Black Age. Pulled me away._
Is that when you came to Avadon?

He nods, eyes still closed. _I was a farmer's child. Could have spent my life threshing wheat. Shearing sheep. That sort of life. But there was still unfinished business from the Black Age. Pulled me away._

He opens his eyes and smiles. _Sometimes, I ramble. Look back on the past. Gives good perspective, especially in difficult times. And you, of course, are forced to listen. One of the privileges of my post._
You grew up on the farm?
_Of course. I had to grow up somewhere. Out in the fields, far from anything. Hearing my parents tell tales of the Black Age. Of the kin that died. Seeing the bones in the dirt._
_And, of course, the unending boredom. The wheat. The sheep. Not surprising that some of us were determined to leave._
The Black Age?
_The civil war, inside the Pact. The lands of the east versus the lands of the west, and the Farlands taking advantage of our confusion to hack at us any chance they got._
_It was at the end of the Black Age that Avadon was built, to help prevent such chaos from ever happening again._
You left to fight?

_There was a need. By the time I came of age, the civil war was over, but some pockets of resistance remained. Armies of mercenaries and rogues, living in the wild lands and doing whatever they wanted._
_Hanvar's Council recruited young warriors into the legion, bundled us up into Forces, a thousand warriors to a Force, and threw us into the wilds._
Who did you hunt?
_The sort of scum that thrives in chaos and feeds off the weak. I got a good, long look at the sort of vileness that comes about when leadership is absent and chaos is allowed._
Did you suffer heavy casualties?

_Oh, yes. The Pact in the decades after the Black Age was a poor and weakened thing. Such luxuries as proper training and equipment were not always available. A lot of those bored young people never returned to the tedium of farm life._
And how did things go for you?
_I was a natural, of course. I saw how low people could sink when the law was not enforced, and I showed great skill with the blade and spear._

He looks down at the piles of scrolls surrounding him. Eyes and Hearts lurk in the shadows, waiting for Redbeard's orders. _But I suppose I should end this reverie soon. My skill and effectiveness drew the attention of Avadon, and they soon plucked me from the wastes and brought me here._
Tell me about your time in Avadon.
_Later, perhaps. I should reach the inspiring conclusion of the tale, my ascension to Keeper._
How did you become Keeper?

_The old Keeper was Telera. Truly an inspiration. Effective, and lethal. Then she disappeared. Avadon was in chaos. Keepers would rise, only to be assassinated within weeks. Telera's body was found. More Keepers died. Hanvar's Council even debated whether Avadon should continue to exist._
_The confusion disgusted me. I saw my opportunity. I gathered my friends and allies, I watched for my opportunity, and I struck._
Did you kill the previous Keeper?
He grins. _You know, I can't remember. Was such a long time ago. But whoever was Keeper before me, well, I'm sure he or she was a non-entity and not to be missed._
And Avadon was allowed to survive?

_Of course. And anyone who said otherwise soon drew my attention, and I made sure to win their agreement. Or silence, by whatever means were necessary. Any who oppose Avadon are agents of chaos, and must be dealt with appropriately._
Did anyone try to kill you?

_Of course. Attempts on my life came fast and furious in the first few years. They slowed later on, as my foes saw the gruesome fates of those who interfered with me. But they have never stopped. And they have never come close to succeeding._

You start to ask another question, but he raises his hand. _The time for rambling is done. I must return to work. But first, young and ambitious Hand, I have a question for you. Why do you think, in this perilous time, I have expended this time to tell you my tale?_
You want me to understand why Avadon exists.

_Yes. Sometimes we are called to do horrible things and make difficult choices. We are reviled. And yet, remember the fragility of life in the Pact. The people accept our power because they know they need us to stay safe._
He motions for one of the Hearts to approach. Your audience has come to an end.
You are warning me.

_Well, there is that. I am frank about these matters. Every servant of Avadon, from time to time, thinks how much better things would be if they controlled the Black Fortress. However, to seize Avadon, you must defeat me. And, I promise, you are not capable._
You are advanced in years, and that leads to rambling speeches.
Redbeard is delighted. He laughs uproariously. _Oh, I think you will find that I am not as senile as that. But your honesty is appreciated!_
As you walk through Redbeard's hall, he suddenly points at you. _You! Hand! Come here. I require an opinion. A fresh pair of eyes for a problem. You will give me your advice._
The gaze of the Eyes and Hearts walking through the chamber fall upon you. You step forward.
I am not worthy to give advice.
Redbeard approves of your modesty. _Knowing the limits of your wisdom. Control and humility. That is good. The sort of discipline that can make a good Heart._
_Here is the problem that faces me._
Sure. What do you need to know?
Redbeard approves of your enthusiasm. _Ahhhh ... You see the opportunity to prove your wisdom. Get my attention. Maybe become a Heart someday. Good._
_There has been a good deal of unrest in Lynaeus lately. There have been several incidents of attackers trying to kill our Hands._
_About a week ago, three Hands just died in a small village in Kellemderiel. They were traveling through, stayed in an inn, and were murdered in their sleep._
_We sent a large force there, of course. Questioned anyone we could find. All of the scared people there, peasants and gentry alike, claimed to know nothing. And I find that rather dubious._
I'd like to know more about these attacks on the Hands.
_That is not your concern. The problem is being given the greatest of attention. All you need to do is keep alert and never lower your defenses._
Can I go and question them myself?

_Not possible. And, trust me, if my hand-picked Eyes and Hands could not elicit the truth from them, you could not either. They are refusing to say what they know, and I can't haul the whole lot back to our dungeons._
_An attack on Avadon's warriors requires a response. We can never just do nothing. So, tell me. This village, where the Hands were murdered. What should happen to it?_
I honestly don't know enough to say.
_Of course. Because every problem that faces us gives us perfect knowledge, so that we may apply our wisdom with the purity of angels._
_Nonsense. You know little more than I do, but action is still required. I will have your answer._
The village should be razed to the ground as an example.

Redbeard looks pleased. _Yes. You show wisdom. Sometimes, the most important thing is not justice, but stability. For Avadon to function, our warriors must be able to travel freely. Interference cannot be tolerated._
_You will be pleased to know that this is what has happened._
The village should be taxed and harassed until someone comes forward.
Redbeard nods. _In normal times, a feasible solution. Punish. Let the word spread of the punishment. Sadly, during these troubles, we lack the forces and the time to make this solution work._
_So we have had to choose a different path._
We can't be sure the village is guilty. We can't do anything to it.

Redbeard looks disappointed. _All of the Pact look to Avadon to bring safety. There is no room for gentleness. Sometimes, the most important thing is not justice, but stability. For Avadon to function, our warriors must be able to travel freely. Interference cannot be tolerated._
You mean the decision was already made?

_I sent word yesterday. All of the buildings in the village will be burned to the ground. The fields will be salted. The people of the village will be sent out in all directions, refugees, to spread word of what happens when Avadon is defied._
He smiles wryly. _You should be grateful. This was done for your safety, so that your throat is not slit in the night. You are welcome._
_I appreciate your words. I think I understand you a little better. Now I must return to my work._ He waves you away.

You return to Redbeard's chamber. He seems pleased to see you. Even eager. He sits on the edge of his chair, his enthusiasm palpable. _Yes, the new Hand. Come here. You are receiving a true opportunity, one the older Hands would kill for._
_I have a mission of true importance for you. You are going to Kellemderiel. Near the Beraza Woods!_
Redbeard says, _Yes? Do you need to know anything else? Speak quickly ... I need you in Kellemderiel as soon as possible._
Why have I been selected for this mission?

He laughs. _Why lie? More experienced Hands are out in the wilds, dealing with the limitless problems that face us. I need to use the most promising Hand available for this task. Which is, I'm afraid, you._
Why is this mission so important?
_Because it deals with the entire future of the Pact, with bringing peace and tranquility where there has been none for a century._
_Since the Black Age, Holklanda and Kellemderiel have, frankly, hated each other, and it is the dispute over the Beraza Woods that has kept this hatred alive._
Do they fight each other?

_Anyone who tries to cause trouble there attracts the gaze of Avadon. Keeping the peace between the two has been a huge amount of my work for the last fifty years, and I will take any chance to reconcile the two._
_And all for the sake of one miserable and useless patch of forest._
Tell me about the Beraza Woods.

_There is little to tell. A patch of woods near the Tawon Empire. Both Holklanda and Kellemderiel claim it. When the peace at the end of the Black Age was declared, it was given to neither of them. Brilliant diplomacy, that._
_Since neither can send their forces into it without enraging the other, it is uncontrolled territory, full of brigands and similar pests. So much strife, over so little._
What do you wish of me?

_There are signs that Holklanda is willing to begin working with Kellemderiel to decide what will happen to the Beraza Woods. Holklanda has sent warriors to Castle Vebeaux. You are to go there to be Avadon's eyes, and to do what you can to bring peace between the two._
Redbeard takes your sapphire symbol and replaces it with one with a pearl hanging from a gold chain. _That will allow you to reach the portal to Castle Vebeaux._
_Current chaos be damned, we can't let an opportunity pass to bring peace between the powers of the Pact._
Why are they working together now?

_Neither Holklanda nor Kellemderiel can send soldiers into the Beraza Woods without enraging the other side. As a result, the place is a haven for thugs and spies. I believe it has become such a problem that neither of them can tolerate it anymore._
Tell me about Castle Vebeaux.
_It is a keep at the west edge of Kellemderiel, overlooking the Beraza Woods. It is commanded by Duke Gryfyn, a young but promising power in the east._
And what do I need to do?

_Go to Castle Vebeaux. The portal to there is east of the library. Speak with Lord Gryfyn. Meet with the emissaries from Holklanda. Be my eyes, and do whatever you can to help the two forces fight the brigands of the Beraza Woods._
_Perhaps, if the two sides can work together, this can lead to settling this issue. This is a great opportunity. Do not disappoint me._
I am back from Castle Vebeaux. (Describe what happened.)

You tell Redbeard how Kellemderiel and Holklanda worked together to rid the Beraza Woods of a dangerous monster. He is pleased. _A small beginning, but better cooperation between the two than we have seen since the Black Age._
Redbeard presents you with a scarab. _I will send word to Lord Gryfyn, encouraging him. That lord has much potential. Perhaps we can build on this auspicious beginning._
_You have done well. Return to Heart Miranda. Perhaps she will have more work for you. If not, you will have a much deserved rest._
Redbeard nods as you approach. _Here to ask about Kellemderiel and Holklanda? No news yet, but I have sent envoys to encourage them to continue to work together._

He sets aside a sheaf of reports, sits back in his chairs, and grins. He is trying to look carefree, but recent events are clearly wearing on him. _You have arrived at Avadon in an unusual time. I am wondering something._

_It is valuable to have a fresh pair of eyes from time to time. After years of labor and training, you made it to Avadon. You have seen what we do. You have fought and killed to bring our will about._
_What is your ambition? Where do you wish to be in the future. If you survive, I mean._
I want to leave. I wish I had never come here.
_I am surprised. And you showed such promise. Someday, you will be allowed to depart. But not as long as we have need of you, and we do._
Being a Hand is all I ask for. I long to fight for Avadon.
Redbeard nods. _That is possible. Some stay in the Hands their entire lives, serving Avadon, doing good, gaining influence. It is a good life, one I sometimes wish that I chose._
I would be an Eye, seeking and sorting the knowledge of Avadon.
Redbeard seems surprised. _It does not seem to be a good use of your talents, your skill and cunning. But then, when our foes are defeated, I think you may have earned it._
I want to be a Heart, an advisor to you.
Redbeard nods. _And you may well be. You have done much for Avadon, but, what is more, you have showed true judgment. Someday, with ten more years of experience, I may take you into my inner circle._
I think I would make a good Keeper. When you retire, of course.

Redbeard smirks. _Retire? Keepers only stop being Keepers one way. Death. And none will ever slay me. So many have tried. They have all failed. And, as long as a threat to the Pact remains, I will never leave._
_Make your peace with that. Whatever happens in Avadon, you will always follow my orders. Always._
Is there anything else?
He waves a hand. _I feel generous. I will answer a question. One thing you would know of me, if you wish._
Why do you still look so young?

_Because I am young. The Keeper of Avadon has all the power of Lynaeus to draw from, if he wishes. I have found powerful magic, and I have used it. Do not try to find it for your own gain. Only I command it._
What has been going on lately? Really?
_I am not sure. I admit that. I believe that someone is attacking Avadon. Someone who wishes the Pact harm. That is all I know now, but I will know more soon._
Do you believe that there are traitors in Avadon?
_There are always traitors in Avadon. And spies, and those who would kill me and take my post. Are any of them acting now? I believe so. The accidents that have occurred ..._
_But I am still trying to learn. I hope to know more soon._
Will I ever be allowed to rest?
Redbeard laughs uproariously. _Of course! When you are dead! This is the life of Avadon. An unending trial, but the greatest of honors._
