I need to know something else.
_Then go elsewhere. I have spent enough time bantering. My work awaits._ He picks up a scroll and uses it to wave you away.
As you pass, Redbeard points at you and shouts, _You! Come here!_ You've come to recognize that tone of voice.
As you approach, he says, _I need your opinion once again. A problem that faces us, and an opportunity. You will tell me what you think._

_Khemeria is, of course, the Farlands. Our enemy. But one of its clans wishes to join us. Somehow, through all of the chaos, its chieftain has gotten a message through to me. It and its people will join the Wyldrylm. Obey Hanvar's Council. Follow our laws, pay our taxes._
_We have watched this chieftain for some time. We believe that the offer is genuine._
_Should we accept it?_
Perhaps. We should wait and watch him.

Redbeard seems amused. _A diplomatic answer, but not a valuable one. To survive, the Pact must act quickly and decisively. Now that these overtures are made, if the protection of the Pact is to be given, it must be given soon. Otherwise, the other lords of Khemeria will discover this treachery and destroy this potential ally._
_Try again. What should we do?_
No. The Farlands are ever our enemy.
Redbeard nods. _That is correct. The goal of the Pact and Avadon is clear. Protect our own. Fight the enemy. Open Arms Within. Stone Wall Without._

_This clarity, friend and foe, is what makes our mission possible. We can't constantly wonder which outsider is good and which is bad, and we will never expel any lands from the Pact. Farlanders can help us if they want, but they are never one of us._
Yes.

Redbeard looks disappointed. _That is an error, one often made by the young. But no matter. You can be educated. The goal of the Pact and Avadon is clear. Protect our own. Fight the enemy. Open Arms Within. Stone Wall Without._
Is this something that actually happened?
_This is something that happens all the time. Parts of the Farlands see the power of the Pact, and they try to join us. It happens constantly._
That is an overly simple way of looking at it.

_Really? Then consider this. Any who would abandon their own land to follow us is a traitor. No matter how loudly they swear fealty to us, we do not need traitors. They only look out for their own gain._

_But I appreciate your response. The honesty and the thought behind it. There is no shame in error, as long as the error is not repeated. Now you should return to your duties. Go._ He returns to work.
I understand. It is good to have clarity.

_Yes. This person is family, that person is the enemy. It is not good, or wise. Those words don't even mean anything, really. But it does keep us safe, keep us alive, and those words do have a true meaning._
_I appreciate your response. The honesty and the thought behind it. Now you should return to your duties. Go._ He returns to work.
Is that all? I should return to my labors.
Redbeard frowns. _I expected more of a response, but no matter. It is good to attend to one's duties. Go._ He returns to work.

Someone has recently placed a fresh lamp in Redbeard's hall. In this newly bright light, you can see how worn down and exhausted the Keeper of Avadon is becoming. His skin is pale, and there are dark circles under his eyes.
And you think for a moment, you can see wrinkles. It is as if, slowly, his true age is returning. Then he notices that you are staring, and you hurriedly turn away.
_You are finally here,_ he grumbles. _I need your efforts. Set aside your other work. You must return to Castle Vebeaux. Curse the Pact states and their eternal squabbling._
Redbeard says, _What else do you wish to know? Speak quickly. I want you to return to Castle Vebeaux before someone gets stabbed and ends this whole negotiation._
Are you feeling well?
Redbeard surprises you by starting to lose his temper, his jolly exterior temporarily broken. _That is none of ... none of ..._ He calms down. _I am fine. Look after yourself, not me._
Why do the states of the Pact fight?
_Because they do not like each other. It is simple enough. One thing binds them: a desire for survival. It is why the Pact exists, and why Avadon is necessary._
Can the Pact survive so much strife?
_Of course. It is a family. And you must be aware of how much the members of a family can hate each other. And yet, they stay together. Usually._
What does Avadon do?
_We watch for people who are trying too hard to disrupt the delicate peace we have attained, who foment warfare inside the Pact. And then we kill them._
_What Avadon says is simple: 'Hate as much as you want, but do not let your resentment turn into action. Otherwise, we will destroy you.' It works._

_Lord Gryfyn has sent word to me. Somehow, his good relations with the Holklandans have not been progressing. Go back there, find him, and do what you need to do to get those temperamental children working together again._
_And, by the way, you should be honored._
What went wrong, exactly?
_I am not sure. The message was painfully vague in that regard. Lord Gryfyn will tell you more, I am sure._

_You should use your wisdom and the authority of Avadon to bring better relations between Kellemderiel and Holklanda. If that means finding someone who is fomenting discontent and using your blade, well, I have given you great freedom._
_I want greater peace between the Pact states. It is my life's work. Do whatever is necessary._
Why should I be honored?
_Lord Gryfyn requested you personally. It seems that you made quite an impression on him. Be pleased. It is from such steps that great influence is won._
I have returned from Castle Vebeaux. (Describe what happened.)
Despite Redbeard's exhaustion, he listens raptly to your words. _A bunch of Kellem bandits, eh? They were the sole obstacle to negotiations? And they are dead. Good. The work can continue._

Redbeard presents you with a scarab. _A true honor, this one. It is from my private collection. Wear it well. I must send messages to Kellemderiel. I will do what I can to bring this peace about. As for you, return to Miranda. You have done well._

You return to Redbeard's chambers and find the Keeper of Avadon sitting slumped in his chair. The confidence and energy he had when you first arrived are completely gone. It's hard to tell in the shadows, but you think that you can see streaks of gray in his hair and beard.

He holds a list of names in his lap. The word 'Casualties' is at the top. He crumples it up, casts it aside, and says, _Ah. It is you. I hope that you are aiding Heart Miranda. We have few Hands to spare._
What was that list?
_It was the lost. More every day. We are provoked and must send out Hands. And then ..._ He shakes his head.
I am doing well.
He nods. _Then we have chosen well, placing as much trust in you as we have. But do not be complacent. It seems, of late, that Avadon is losing its greatest weapon and its greatest shield._
I am finding it difficult to continue.

He chuckles bitterly. _Oh, but I understand that. I do not remember when I have been so sorely tried. And yet, we must ask more of you still. It seems, of late, that Avadon is losing its greatest weapon and its greatest shield._
_We have lost our aura of invulnerability. The terror our name brings. There can be no denying it. Someone is murdering our Hands. If one is killed, we will bring horrible vengeance upon the killer._
_But our enemies, whoever they are, know that we cannot fight the entire world. But we will recover. We ..._
Finally, he says, _I would ask something._
_You have seen much of Avadon now. Our purpose. Our goals. How we work, how we fight. What is your impression of us?_
Avadon is corrupt, and its influence is entirely for sale.

Redbeard nods, but you can see that your words have angered him. _Corrupt? Us? Some say so. But what do they know of what it takes to hold the savages at bay. How dare they depend on us for their lives, and then judge us. Have we earned no trust?_
_This is a crisis! We have no time to worry over such trivia. Leave me. Go and do what you are told. We will uncover our enemies yet!_ You back away before Redbeard can completely lose his temper.
Avadon, whatever its flaws, is the best hope for keeping our people safe.

Redbeard is still for a long moment. Then he nods. _Of course. Whatever the ... the accusations ... We are just. We fight for our peoples' safety. That justifies much, no matter what the naysayers say, those who sleep soundly ... soundly in their beds ... I ..._ He pauses.
Avadon is doomed. It is only a matter of time before its foes destroy it.

Redbeard glares at you. You imagine you can see in his eyes reflections of the multitudes who have died at his command. _You say that? To me?_ His voice is soft, but full of rage. _You dare? After all we have done?_
_You are lucky they still have need of you in Kellemderiel, or I would have you in the dungeons. I may still. Follow your orders, and get out of my sight._

_We will find those who work against us, and their suffering will be without limit. I promise you that. Your dead brothers and sisters will be avenged. I will make sure of it. Now go. There is much to do. The real work is only beginning._

You return to Redbeard's hall and find that the Keeper is full of energy. He seems much recovered from his recent exhaustion. Something has made him cheery, almost playful. _Come in, come in!_ he shouts. _This is a good day, the first in some time._

_There is fresh word from Castle Vebeaux. Lord Gryfyn tells me that he has had envoys from Holklanda. They are there to begin to negotiate a peace! It is hard to believe. Something good coming from all this chaos._

Redbeard is still in high spirits. _Still here? When an opportunity awaits in Kellemderiel? Do not waste your time here. Go. Aid Lord Gryfyn in his negotiations. You will receive great advantage from this, I promise you._
Negotiations? Over what?
_The Beraza Woods. At last, both sides have realized that that wild land does not justify the perpetual threat of war._
So what will happen?
_That is up to the negotiators. For once, not our business. Perhaps a payment. Perhaps a partition. Whatever is necessary to enable each side to save face._
What is required of me?
_Not all wish peace. In fact, some have a great interest in preventing it. Lord Gryfyn asked for you personally to come and provide security for the negotiations._
_Return to him. He will tell you more. This is a great day._
_And, before you go, I have a gift for you._
Who opposes peace?
_Fanatics, who cannot accept even the slightest surrender by their people. War profiteers, who make their fortunes selling the tools of war. And a variety of other zealots and fools._
_They are the enemies of Avadon and of the Pact. Treat them accordingly._
And I should do whatever Lord Gryfyn says?
_No. You are a warrior of Avadon. You do not answer to him._
_That said, you should do anything he requires, within reason, to keep the diplomats safe._
What is your gift for me?
He removes a scarab from his pouch and hands it to you. _It is mine. No castoff, that. It is the most powerful scarab I own._

_I will forgive you for certain foolish words you have said in the past. Remember, we have the same goal. Also ..._ He removes a scarab from his pouch and hands it to you. _It is mine. No castoff, that. It is the most powerful scarab I own._
_Let that be an expression of my gratitude toward you, and may it protect you as you fight for a peace that will benefit the Pact long after we are dead._
Have you had any success finding out who is attacking Avadon?

He slaps the arm of his chair. _Yes! Everything that happens, all the clues, they lead us to the Tawon Empire. Not to their leaders or their diplomats, but someone else. Someone hiding there, who has a long reach._
What are you going to do?

_I will not say. Our plans are wrapped in secrets. But we will act soon, and decisively. Within days, I think. They hit us. They bloodied us. But we found them too quickly. Before they can strike a mortal blow ..._ He stops talking and laughs.
_I am letting my high spirits get the best of me. Concentrate on your work, on the peace. You will learn of our other victories soon enough._
As you approach Redbeard and he looks up from his papers, you can see that his normal jovial attitude is gone. He sets aside a scroll, clears his throat, and waves you forward.
_I have been waiting for you. Something has happened. I want to know if you know something about it._
_There is always a guard posted at the stairs up to my private chambers. Recently, they disappeared. The gate to my tower was left open._
_Do you know anything about this?_
No. Nothing at all.
Redbeard nods. His smile returns. You can see no sign of if he knows that you searched his tower.
He says, _That is all. You may return to your duties._ He waves you away.
I went into your tower, but I had nothing to do with the gate.
Redbeard nods. _You saw the chance to poke around, and you took it. Such curiosity. An excellent trait in a Hand, within reason._
He adds, _No harm was done. The gate will be secured. That is all. You may return to your duties._ He waves you away.
I found the gate open and decided to investigate.
Redbeard's grin returns. _Ahhh .. An investigation. A simple desire to help me. Make sure there were no intruders. Unnecessary, but admirable._
As you approach Redbeard, he looks up at you with annoyance. You remember the letter that the wretch to the west gave you.
Redbeard says, _What is it? I would love to banter with you all day, but there is very much to do._
Sorry. Nothing. (Throw the letter away.)
You make your excuses, back away, and discreetly discard the wretch's letter. Redbeard returns to work.
I was asked to give this to you.
Redbeard impatiently takes the letter. He reads it. Then he crumples it up and throws it away. _Listen carefully,_ he intones. _You are allowed one error in this area, and you have just made it._

_Many people will offer you rewards for your aid. I give you some latitude in accepting them. It is a reward for the many risks you take. But you may not sell access to me, and your projects are not allowed to waste my time!_
_Now get away before I lose my temper._ He waves you away.

At the top of the stairs, you see a familiar face. Hand Callan runs up to you, trailed by several warriors. Her blade is drawn and shows signs of recent use. She pants, _[N], you have returned. I am glad to see it. This is a dark day for Avadon._

At the top of the stairs, a Hand of Avadon runs up to you, trailed by several warriors. Her blade is drawn and shows signs of recent use. She pants, _[N], I am Hand Callan. It is unfortunate I have not been able to speak with you before now. I am glad to see you. This is a dark day for Avadon._
_We have been trying to reach Redbeard, but without success. Now we are going back downstairs to drive the invaders from our fortress._
I am looking for my companions.
Callan nods. _They were helping me to find Redbeard. You will find them to the north._
You could not find Redbeard?

_No, and it makes no sense! This is the darkest day for Avadon in recent memory. Why is he not out here, rallying the troops and fighting by our side! Many loyal servants of the Black Fortress have died today._
I will go back down with you.
She shakes her head. _No. You must find Redbeard. Until we know what has happened to him, we will be unable to make a proper plan. After the attack, we need a leader!_
I need to know what happened here.
_We were attacked, by surprise and from within. And ..._ She shakes her head. _It has been a disaster._
Tell me more about the attack.

_There is still little that I know. Somehow, dozens of assassins gained entrance to the Black Fortress in the middle of the night. With the advantage of surprise and darkness, many of our best were dead before they had a chance to draw their blades._
Who has been lost?
_I can't yet be sure. The librarian, Eye Leira, fell under their blades while weaving a spell to save herself. I saw it with my own eyes._
_As for the others lost? The time to make a tally is after the assassins are gone._
How did you survive?
_Pure luck. One of my guards let out a scream as the assassins tried to kill her in her bed. She was slain, but the sound woke some of us up._
_You should stay up here and find Redbeard. We will go downstairs, kill all of the invaders we can find, and locate Heart Miranda. In Redbeard's absence, she can take command._
Good luck with that. I'm sure she'd love to help. (Lie.)
_Yes. Heart Miranda is a rock. If anyone can help us to drive out the attackers, she can._
Um, there's something you should know. (Tell her about Miranda.)
You quickly tell Hand Callan what transpired down below. She is, predictably, stunned. _Can this be true? Even Heart Miranda ... I mean, Miranda, even she has turned against us?_
_No matter. I am loyal, and I am ready to fight. The battle awaits us below._
Miranda has left Avadon.
Good luck. I will look around up here.
_Good luck to you, [N]. If we survive, a long, hard job of rebuilding awaits us._
Hand Callan runs downstairs, eager to fight. Her warriors follow.
I will find Redbeard.
_Find him and bring him to us. We need him now more than ever. Good luck to you, [N]. If we survive, a long, hard job of rebuilding awaits us._
I will look for Redbeard. He must pay for his incompetence.
_I ... Even now, in all of this chaos, it is unwise to sound disloyal. We still serve Redbeard. And, I suppose, the Pact. Remember that. Good luck to you, [N]._
Several warriors, grim and battered, follow behind Hand Callan. They have been fighting continuously since the invaders came and are too exhausted to talk.

You walk unnoticed into the ceremonial hall. To the southeast, in the middle of an enchanted circle, you see Redbeard. He is in furious single combat with a shadowwalker. At least, he is dressed like a shadowwalker.

The two of them are dueling both with blades and with magic. Redbeard wears many enchanted pieces of jewelry. These constantly provide him with protective spells and spit fire and lightning where he desires.
The shadowwalker, in turn, has many of the tricks of his kind. Decoys flicker into being, attack, and fade away. He constantly produces pods, potions, and pouches of dust from his robes.
You move into the hall, hoping for a closer view.
As you move into the hall, Redbeard finally gets the upper hand in the battle. The Keeper of Avadon, unwounded and barely breathing hard, summons a blast of energy.

Just as you finally recognize the shadowwalker, Redbeard's spell flies toward his chest. He dodges the blast, but it grazes him. The Wayfarer, attempted assassin of the Keeper of the Black Fortress, flies back across the room.
The assassin manages to dodge it, but only barely. It still grazes him, knocking him back across the room. Whoever sent him would have been far better off sending someone competent.
The assassin collapses, coughing and spitting blood. _What a ... waste ... I was a fool. I wasted my life on this attempt ... I might ... might ..._ And then he is silent.
Redbeard turns to you. _Now that that ugly business is settled, I need your report. There is much to discuss, plan, and do._
Redbeard turns to you and smiles. _Now, my treacherous servant, I need your report. There is much to discuss, plan, and do. Perhaps, if you please me, you might survive this day._
At last, Redbeard's aging body, sustained by powerful and unreliable magic, gives out. In the end, it is not a wound that kills him, or poison, or even old age. He grabs his chest. His heart stops.

He gives you one final look. He is in great pain, but there is still a smile on his face. He whispers, _Now it is all on you ... on you ..._ Then he falls sideways and hits the floor with a mighty clatter of steel armor.
You stare down at his body, barely able to stay on your feet, trying to take in the enormity of what just happened. You are still that way when the Hands of Avadon finally find you ...
The Wayfarer takes a step back and raises the clay globe in his hand. _Don't get too confident, [N]. I still have plenty of tricks left._ He drops the globe and smashes it under his boot.
The assassin's luck runs out. He stumbles on a bit of broken masonry, and, before he can recover his balance, Redbeard hits him with an intense blast of flame ...
Redbeard mutters a word of power. Then he grunts in pain. A wisp of insubstantial light floats out of his chest. With a spasmodic motion, it rips loose, floats to the south, and fades away.
_That hurts,_ he roars, _but if you want to kill me, you have to kill all the parts of me!_
As you look for where the wisp went, you realize that something seems slightly different about the room. You try to figure out what, but you can't quite put your finger on it.

As you slip into the room, Redbeard and the assassin continue their duel. Vicious blows and spells fly back and forth at blinding speed. You stand a safe distance away. If you try to get involved you could easily hit the wrong target.
Sevilin walks up to you. _[N], it is a relief to see you. When you didn't emerge from the portal at the same time I did, I assumed you were lost._

_Everything has gone mad here. Avadon once played so casually with everyone's lives. My life. Now, it can barely protect itself. And yet, here we are, sworn to protect it. I follow the Stone Code. I am no oath-breaker._
_And yet, how am I best to serve Avadon? I think that our time following Miranda's orders is done. Do you still have need of me?_
I am looking for Redbeard.
He looks to the east. _I think that the Keeper is back there, behind a locked gate. He has not let me in. For you, it might be different._
No. Go back downstairs and help to drive out the invaders. I will continue without you.

Sevilin is surprised by this, but he nods calmly. _I hope I have given you no reason to doubt my competence. I bid you farewell, [N], and good luck in your hunt for Redbeard. We are at the beginning of dark times._
He salutes you with his blade and walks to the south, ready to do battle.
I want to fight with you at my side.

Sevilin thinks about this. It is a long and tense moment. Finally, he says, _I must think about this, [N]. You let Cahil, the murderer of my friends, go. Perhaps I can forgive you for this, but it will take time._
_I will go below now and fight to drive the invaders from Avadon. I bid you farewell, [N], and good luck in your hunt for Redbeard. We are at the beginning of dark times._
He salutes you with his blade a final time and walks to the south, ready to do battle.
Sevilin nods. _It will be an honor. You helped me to hunt down Cahil and have vengeance upon him. In return, I owe you an awesome debt. I will do whatever you require._

_Now we must find Redbeard._ He stops to think about this, remembering all he has been through, all he has learned. The pardon of Cahil weighs heavily upon him. _Though I do not know what we should do when we find him._
We will do whatever he commands. He is the Keeper of Avadon.

Sevilin thinks about your words. _I have no more respect for Redbeard, not after his pardon of Cahil. Your words pain me. You ask me to follow a Keeper who ... who ... But I remember how much I owe you, and I submit._
_Lead on, [N]. I will follow your lead, whatever you decide. Even if you change your mind._
We do what is best for the Pact. Today, that means following Redbeard's orders.

Sevilin thinks about your words. _I have no more respect for Redbeard, not after his pardon of Cahil. And yet, today, I must forget my grudge and do my best for the Pact. I wish it did not have to be so._
We will make Redbeard step down, by force if necessary. Avadon needs a new Keeper.

There is a long silence after you say these words. Sevilin thinks about them. Finally, gravely, he nods. _These halls have gone without justice for too long. A Keeper who would pardon Cahil is not worthy of the title. Even if it means my doom, I will do what you command._
_Lead on, [N]. I am ready. I only hope that I can be forgiven._

Shima emerges from the shadows. He is clearly relieved to see you. _Welcome, [N]. You have missed eventful times. The portal had been disrupted during the attack. We were afraid that you would be unable to return._
_The attack is almost over. Soon, I think the assassins will be destroyed. We will count and bury our dead. I have been tasked to find what has happened to Redbeard. I may do this._
_But then, what? I can no longer put my full faith in his leadership, not after all I have learned. Where should I go? What should I do?_
You should go downstairs and help to drive out the invaders. I have no more need of you.

Shima nods, his face betraying not a hint of emotion. _I hope I have done nothing to give offense. I have tried to aid you to the best of my ability. Still, [N], if this is what you think is best, I wish you good hunting._
With one final nod, he leaves to the south.
I want you to continue to fight at my side.

Shima does not hesitate. He shakes his head. _These last months have been a great struggle for me. After my family was destroyed, I began to hunt for a place where I could belong. I need companions whom I can support, and who will support me when needed._
_I will go below now and help to drive the invaders from Avadon. Then I will leave this place forever and begin my hunt for a new home. Goodbye, [N]. I truly wish you the best of fortune._
_I would be honored to, [N]. After all you have done for me, I would be ashamed to do otherwise. We need to find Redbeard. Those are our orders, and the Black Fortress seems to need him._
_And yet, after all we have seen and learned, I confess that I am not sure if he is still worthy of leadership here. Lynaeus is in chaos, and Avadon's behavior of late has been simply dishonorable._
We have sworn to serve Redbeard. Though it is difficult, we will continue to do so.

_Your words are hard, and the burden of duty is harder still. I wish to serve the Pact, and this is a place where I can fight for it. Whatever Redbeard says, I will always do what is best for our people._
_Lead on, [N]. I trust you. Whatever you decide, even if you change your mind, I will support you._
This is not the time for strife. Today, we all stand together. Tomorrow, we can judge Redbeard.
Shima looks to the east. His shoulders slump. _This delay ... it pains me. And yet, you are, of course, correct. There is going to be enough bloodshed soon. More will not help._
You are correct. If the Pact is to be helped, Redbeard needs to go.
Shima Threespear nods gravely. _I think, together, we plot our own deaths. And yet, we swore to sacrifice all for the Pact. If removing Redbeard is the task that falls to us, we must not shirk it._

Jenell is sitting on a marble bench, feeding a tiny salamander. When she sees you, she dispels it with a wave of her hand. She rises and puts her hand on your arm. _[N], I had feared that you were dead, lost in the mad flight from Castle Vebeaux._
_It is good to have you here. You can help us in the hunt for Redbeard. The enemy seems to be defeated, but our leader remains at large. Dead? Hiding? Cowering? We should find out._

She sighs. _Then I have to decide where to go. I have learned too much about Avadon over the last few months. Is the Pact even good for my people? I am no longer sure. What little certainty I had has faded away._
She looks to the east. _I think that the Keeper is back there, behind a locked gate. He has not let me in. For you, it might be different._
If you are confused, I can give you some clarity. There is a battle downstairs. Go down and drive out the invaders.

She seems taken aback. _But ... I did not expect that you would want to go on without me. [N], I will never go where I am not wanted. I will do as you ask. I still have much to offer the Pact. Only, perhaps, not here._
With one final wave, she turns and leaves to the south.

Jenell thinks hard about this. Finally, she looks you in the eye. _You are a skilled warrior, one of the best I have ever seen. And yet, I watched as you used those skills to slay my countrymen. Warriors that you could have spared, had you chosen to._

_I will go below and help to drive the invaders from Avadon. Then I will leave this place. I have been forced to chose between Avadon and the Wyldrylm. I choose my true home, and I will return there. Good luck, [N]. I wish you well._
With one final nod, she turns and leaves to the south.

Jenell thinks hard about this. Finally, she looks you in the eye. _When my fellow warriors of the Wyldrylm were threatened, you helped me to save them. When you could have killed them, you spared them. I offered you my gratitude, and I am still in your debt._
_Before we continue, I have a question for you. [N], based on all you have seen, is Redbeard still the right man to command Avadon? Is he making Avadon do what is best for the Pact?_
He is not perfect, but he is doing the best one leader could possibly do.
_One leader? Yes, we are all at the mercy of that one man. One immortal, arrogant, capricious man. The state of things was decided by wiser heads than me, and yet I can't help but question it._
_Let us go, [N], and find Redbeard. I will discharge my debt to you. Whatever you decide in the end, I will be at your side._
Now is not the time to question our leaders. Now is the time to band together against our enemies.
She thinks about this, and then she nods. _I see much wisdom in what you say. And yet, if our leaders are not capable of bringing us together and saving us, what then?_
The time of Redbeard is past. I intend to challenge and replace him.
She smiles. _So we must fight the most dangerous man in Lynaeus? When I incurred my debt to you, I did not think I would have to pay so much. It is the right thing to do. I will not shrink from it._

Nathalie is waiting for you at the east end of the hall. For once, her arm doesn't seem to be bothering her. It hangs, relaxed, at her side. Right now, the look in her eyes is a source of more concern. She looks wild, almost out of control. Her hands are shaking.
She turns to look at you. For a moment, she doesn't seem to recognize you. Then, finally, something clicks. She runs up and embraces you. _[N], you have returned. You are well. I am pleased._

_Avadon has gone mad. It ... It is crumbling. Surely you have seen it for yourself. I have been standing here, unsure what to do. Should I even stay here? I wanted to hear what you had to say. Of all of Avadon, you are the only one who saw my potential._
Your skills are great. Go downstairs and use them to drive the invaders out.
Nathalie is not thrilled by this suggestion. _You know that I never want to back from a fight, but you ... you ... You are abandoning me? You cast me aside, like all the rest?_

She looks at you with loathing. _I will do as you say. Then I will leave this place. I will find a place where my power is properly respected! [N], you can be sure of that!_ Then she turns and leaves without even a backward glance.
I want to put your skills to use. Continue to fight at my side.

At first, your offer tempts her. Then something starts to bother her. She scratches at her injured arm. _Even since I came here, my power has not been respected. All I wanted to do was destroy foes of the Pact, and, when we had one cornered, even you let it flee._

_I am going to go below and fight the invaders. Then I am leaving this place. I will find Zhossa Mindtaker and have my vengeance. Then I will find a place where my power is properly respected. [N], you can be sure of that!_
Then she turns and walks away. At the door, she gives you one final, rueful glance. Then she is gone.

_Of course. [N], you are the only one who ever seemed to recognize my power. These other fools, they ignored me, and look at what a mess Avadon is in now. You saved my life, and I will do as you say._

_I wish I could say the same for Redbeard, but his time is ending. He has allowed everything to crumble around him. He commands no fear. Hands being murdered. Me, abandoned, my arm ruined. It always hurts. His power is fading. Perhaps ... someone might replace him._
She looks at you with a gleam in her eye, perhaps already picturing the day when you make her a Heart.
Redbeard rules here. You must make your peace with it.

Nathalie goes from pleased to furious in a moment. _Then I must continue to labor under him? All of my power and skill, held back and left to gather dust? But we did swear an oath, I suppose. I owe you much. I will trust you in this._
_I owe you my life, and you know how to make use of my power. Whatever you decide in the end, I will follow you._
This is not the day to make such decisions. Today, we must all fight together.
_The only day is today! My powers are here! They are ready, waiting to serve you. Why delay? I ..._ She lowers her head, defeated. _I owe you too much. I will do what you say._
With your help, I can destroy Redbeard.

She grins. She shows no worry or hesitation. _Yes. We will make him pay for his incompetence. At last, someone has the courage to confront him. I can't wait to see the look on his face when he sees that all is lost!_
Redbeard doesn't leave his protective circle. He points a mailed hand at the Wayfarer, ready to deliver another spell. The Wayfarer slowly rises to his feet. Then he sees you.
He reaches up and pulls off his mask. You see that he is a middle-aged man of eastern Lynaeus. He is a skilled warrior and assassin, but he is no Holklandan at all.

Redbeard flicks his eyes toward you, takes in your presence, and then returns his attention to his foe. _Shadow Tarkus,_ he says. _I knew you would return here in time. As a prisoner or my victim, it is all the same to me._
Shadow Tarkus?
Redbeard nods. _An assassin and spy for the Farlands. If a Khemerian or Tawon or warrior of Svorgald wants a loyal citizen of the Pact killed, Tarkus will do it. For a price._
From your vantage point, you can see that Tarkus's hand is inching slowly toward one of the pouches on his belt.
I know this man.
Redbeard's eyebrows go up. _Really? Interesting. We can discuss it after we have disposed of him._
Redbeard, he's reaching for something.
Tarkus's hand darts toward his pouch. Redbeard mutters a word of command. The muscles in the assassin's arm seize up. He shouts in pain. _Thank you,_ Redbeard says.
Tarkus turns his head to face you. He is furious.

Tarkus slips his fingers into the pouch. He starts to draw out a small clay globe. As he tries to bring the weapon around, Redbeard mutters a word of command. The muscles in the assassin's arm seize up. He shouts in pain. Redbeard looks over at you, though you can't read his expression.
Tarkus turns his head to face you. There is still a flicker of hope in his eyes.
(Listen to Tarkus.)
_So you are finally here, [N]. Made it through Vebeaux, I see. Knew you would._
_Now is your chance. Do what you told me you would. Strike down Redbeard, now that he is weak!_ Of course, Redbeard is listening to this with great interest.
_Now I suppose you will watch me die, grinning and gloating all the while. Watch as the cowardly tyrant of Lynaeus claims another victim!_
Redbeard, I will kill Tarkus myself.
Redbeard nods approvingly. Then he takes a step back. _Well done, [N]. That is the spirit I like to see in my Hands. Be my guest._
Shadow Tarkus turns and, with a snarl of fury, leaps at you. _My time with you was wasted. How I have longed to do this ..._
Tarkus, we will kill Redbeard together! (Attack.)

Redbeard looks surprised, but not alarmed. _What a strange and unfortunately timed bit of resistance, [N]. I expected better of you. If nothing else, I would have expected you to select a more durable ally._
He turns to Shadow Tarkus, who is already leaping forward for one final attack. A gout of flame flies from Redbeard's gauntlet ...
Redbeard, spare him.
Redbeard looks surprised and amused. _Spare him? A lifelong foe of the Pact? This assassin? This vermin? [N], you are not showing the true spirit of Avadon._
(Just watch.)
Shadow Tarkus spits at you. Then he turns to Redbeard. _The end is upon you, Keeper. The assault has already begun, and soon ..._
Redbeard cuts him off. _Enough, Tarkus. I've heard a thousand such speeches. They bore me._ He says a word of command. A gout of flame flies from his gauntlet ...
Redbeard looks at the crumpled body on the floor before him with clinical detachment. _That was a long-delayed bit of business. Were this a happier day, I would take some satisfaction in it._
_As it is, he has distracted me at a time when I couldn't afford it. What gets my attention, however, is that you seem to have spoken to him already._
_And, judging from your actions, seems to have had some luck planting disloyalty in your soft head._
Redbeard looks at you intently. _Tell me, how did you know this creature?_ You suspect that your answers to his questions will make a huge difference in how things go for you ...
How did he distract you?

_All sorts of trickery. When I realized that we were under attack, I found gates locked and passages full of traps and hostile shades. When I was about to return to the main floor of the fortress, that was when Shadow Tarkus stepped out to attack._
_That creature truly thought he had a chance to best me. Humorous._
I have no idea what he was talking about.
_Interesting. It has been some years since someone has lied to my face so blatantly. It is a fascinating sensation._
_I will not waste more time bantering about this. I need your report. Try to lie more convincingly this time._
He tried to turn me against you. He failed.
_I saw that. He is a cunning fellow. Better Hands than you have been turned by his wiles. He must have seen great potential in you._
_But enough about this refuse. He has wasted enough time. I need your report. Speak quickly._
He convinced me that we would all be better off without you.
_I saw that. He is a cunning fellow. You are not the first Hand to be turned by his wiles. He must have seen great potential in you. Pity for you that he has put you in so much peril now._
He constantly contacted me as I traveled. He was a bit of a pest.

_I can imagine how irritating that was. He was a cunning and persistent fellow. Better Hands than you have been turned by his wiles. He must have seen great potential in you, but you seem to have resisted. A mark in your favor._
(Tell Redbeard the whole truth.)

You give Redbeard a quick summary of your interactions with Tarkus, trying as much as possible to keep you from sounding like a traitor. _He was a cunning and persistent fellow. Better Hands than you have been turned by his wiles._
_He must have seen great potential in you, but you seem to have resisted. A mark in your favor. But enough about this refuse. He has wasted enough time. I need your report. Speak quickly._
Report what, exactly?

You stumble out into the hot sun. After the cool and darkness of Avadon, the hot, dry air of the deserts of The Kva immediately starts to wear you down. Sweat rolls down your face and grit starts to work its way into your armor.
The ground is arid and dusty. The only plant life visible nearby is in the form of huge thickets of cactus, bearing vicious thorns. The dragon Zhethron picked a home truly inhospitable to humans.
When you emerge, someone shouts to you. A woman is waiting for you by the path to the north.
Once again, you approach Goldcrag. The pylon still made you feel desperately ill, but at least you kept standing this time.

As you look around, something seems different. The town is quieter. There are fewer guards on duty and fewer people wandering the streets of the town. Several freshly severed ogre heads hang from the western gate. Ogres? What are they doing here?
There is an unmistakable tension in the air. Things have gotten worse since you hunted wretches for Zhethron.

You enter the town of Goldcrag. It is not a large settlement. There are a meeting hall and barracks in the center of the town. You can see shops and an inn to the north and a few quiet buildings to the south.

Normally, in this remote, arid land, you would only find small clusters of nomads. However, the people who come out here to see the dragon and try to purchase its aid need a place to sleep and get supplies for the journey back.

When you enter, the few people out in the hot sun nearby look very nervous. The presence of a Hand of Avadon always causes fear. Everyone wonders what they have done wrong recently and how much you know about it. And Avadon does all it can to encourage that paranoia.

From here, you can see the fields east of Goldcrag. There is a small oasis and, nearby, a few patches of arable land. There are enough crops grown here to feed a small village, though Goldcrag is large enough to need to bring a lot of food from outside.
The thickets of cacti are constantly growing, and the town must wage a constant war to hack them back. The smell of burning cactus is constant. The smoke makes your skin itch and your eyes water.

This courtyard has several sets of stocks, set here to punish those who run afoul of the Stone Code. Two of them are occupied, and what little rotten fruit the village can spare has been used to pelt them.
Fines and the stocks are only two of the possible punishments called for by the Stone Code. Shunning, branding, amputation, and execution are also covered.
Sevilin nods approvingly. _A good place for punishment. But note the buckets of water, to ensure nobody dies of heat or thirst. Harsh, but just._
Shima frowns. _They must have done something very serious to have their dignity stripped away. This sort of thing should be kept private._
Seeing the people bound like that makes Jenell shiver in horror.

There are four black stones set upright in the middle of Goldcrag. Closer inspection reveals that they are covered with dense writing. Townsfolk circle them, reading the writing and making notes of it. Those who are illiterate ask those who can read for help.
These stones bear the core of the Stone Code, the law that governs life in The Kva. They are traditionally set here so that all can see them.

Sevilin looks at the stones with interest. _It is interesting to see them in a town so small. Getting the stones is a sign of great achievement, signifying that the settlement is a place of importance._
Jenell seems fascinated. _It would be interesting to read them. Perhaps later. See if The Kva is as savage as we have heard._

There are two young Kva farmers in here, dozing in the cool and shade. They probably emerge to work in the early morning and evening, when it is cooler.

The customers in this inn are a motley bunch of caravan guards, merchants, and people of influence who seek to see the dragon. They stay in the shadows, drink lots of liquids, and do their best to keep a Hand of Avadon from hearing any of their business.
These scribes are recording the judgments of Overseer Levent. When the leaders of The Kva make judgments regarding the Stone Code, they are carefully transcribed for future reference.

_Every once in a while, for huge troves of money and artifacts, they can also be hired to fight, but this is rare and expensive. Dragons do not grow to be old by taking unnecessary risks._
Tell me about Zhethron.
_He is a young adult specimen, about five hundred years old. He remembers well even the days before the Pact. He is wily, wealthy, arrogant, and near the height of his power._
_Thus, we want to keep him happy. He is a valuable ally for the Pact._
_Still powerful, still arrogant, and increasingly unbalanced. The attacks of the lesser humanoids are enraging him, and Avadon has been unable to keep him calm. Thus, you must do your best._
How can I get to Zhethron?
_Go to the road and head west. Follow the signs._
_First, however, I would visit Goldcrag. There are profitable opportunities for a new Hand, and you might want to gain some experience before undertaking one of Miranda's tasks._
I need supplies.
_And you want them from me. I am no quartermaster. You should travel into Goldcrag. Merchants there will give you a fair deal. They know how dangerous it would be to do otherwise._
Can't I just take what I want?
She shakes her head. _It would be unwise. The job of Avadon is to make the Pact more stable. Looting and theft will invite rebellion and thus anger Redbeard. So I would behave._
I need to help Zhethron again. Is there nothing you can give me?
She sighs. _In these turbulent times, I think I should give you what I can. Too many Hands have been lost. I will unlock the storeroom in my home for you._
_I have been stationed here for many a year._ She looks around at the parched land and the vicious thickets of cactus. _It is Redbeard's pleasure that I serve in my homeland._
Is this where you wanted to be stationed?

She smiles wryly. _Why would anyone choose to expend their short lives anywhere else? I may have been on the wrong end of a political disagreement before I was sent here, but I'm sure that was not involved._
_But this is where Redbeard sent me, and this is where I will serve._
What do you do besides assist Hands?
_I watch. I gather information. I carry messages directly from the dragons to Redbeard and back._
_It is the work of the Eyes._
Are you from The Kva?
_I am. A more pleasant part of it. Most of The Kva is not so ... arid. Some areas even have plants that aren't cacti._
Is everything all right here?
She looks at the ground, debating what to say. Then she looks up at you. _You deserve to know. You are a Hand, after all. Things are not well out here._
_Hands have been sent out on missions here. Hunting the wretches and titans that have been encroaching from the wilds. Few Hands have returned. Some have been killed. Others are missing._
Does Redbeard know?
_I have sent messages. I have received no response. But he must know._

_You should be wary. The enemies of Avadon, the wretches, the ogres, they are emboldened. They are emerging from the Farlands and defying the Pact, and we have not been stopping them. This will only get worse._
You are approached by an elderly man of The Kva. His robes are long, brightly colored, and immaculate, though they are rapidly picking up dust from the road. He must not come outside much.

For you, however, he made an exception. He greets you with a broad, fake smile. _An envoy from Avadon! A ... Hand, if I guess correctly? We are most honored and pleased to meet you in our humble town._

_I am Overseer Levent, and I wanted to greet you personally, here, before the stone. Welcome to Goldcrag. Anything we can do for you, we will._ Sweat begins to bead on his forehead. He glances briefly at the city hall, clearly eager to return to its shelter.
Overseer Levent nods to you, showing a broad smile that does not reach his eyes. _The Hand of Avadon wishes more of my time? I am thrilled to be able to help you._
Once again, Overseer Levent has emerged from his hall to meet you. His smile seems even more forced than usual. You can clearly see the worry in his eyes.
_Ahhhh ... The Hand. Yes. Once again, I greet you. And I wish to speak with you briefly. About the ... The unrest. I hope you can spare me a moment of your time._
I am here to see the dragon Zhethron.
He nods. _I have heard that the mighty dragon is dissatisfied. Wretches, yes? Such pests. We have had increased difficulties with them lately._
Why haven't you done more to rid yourself of them?
Levent's smile remains, but his eyes grow very cold. _We do what we can, but my humble town cannot restrain all of the Wretch Lands without aid. Aid which has not come._
_What else would you like to know about?_
Perhaps I can be of assistance.
For a moment, Levent's smile seems genuine. _We have asked, and Avadon has provided. We are most grateful._
I'm sure the problem will be solved soon.

_So we have been told. And told. For months, more and more wretches have assailed us, and now they even pester the dragon. We don't have the strength to deal with them ourselves. I hope someone bothers to aid us soon._
I want to know more about Goldcrag.
_A modest town, as you can see, in a harsh part of The Kva. We have little land that can be farmed._
_And yet, thanks to the dragons, we have value for the Pact and for travelers. And, thus, honor has been given to us._
_But we have also drawn attention. Since you were here last, we have been attacked._
How many dragons are near here?
_One currently. Zhethron. Sometimes, there are more. They move around. They come here when they have the urge to grow their hoards, so that the sages and leaders of the Pact can bribe them._
_However, if the problems with ogres and titans continue, I fear that these creatures may depart for the remote parts of the Titan Peaks. This would be a disaster for us, and for the Pact._
You don't fear the dragons?
_We do not. Goldcrag is part of the Pact. If the dragons attacked us, they would attack all of the Pact. They are not foolish enough to want war._
_However, it was not always thus. Once, the dragons hunted at will. These are better days._
What honor have you received?
_Because of our increasing wealth and the attention Avadon has given us, the leaders of The Kva have bestowed upon us our own copy of The Stone Code. It is just outside the city hall._
_This marks us as a town of importance and prestige. Small villages are not so honored._
Tell me about the attack.

_Ten ogres rushed out of the thickets and charged our gates. Ogres, here! We slew half of them, and the rest fled. But what are ogres doing here? Do they have no more fear of the Pact? And when will they return?_
You are an Overseer?
He nods and brushes some dust off his sleeve. _It is the title of one who leads a village or small town. I was appointed to direct affairs and to make judgments of law._
_I am interpreter of The Stone Code. Both master and servant._
How did you come to be Overseer?
_I was chosen by our king and approved by his Council. It was a true honor._
How long will you stay in this post?
_Until my masters think my services are better used elsewhere. Or until I draw the anger of Avadon or Hanvar's Council. Or until I myself break the laws of the Stone Code and must be ... removed._
So you are the judge here?
_Yes. I have memorized all of the Code, both the words on the stones and the expanded version on the scrolls in this hall. I pass judgment and declare punishments._
_You may have seen the stocks and the place of execution. The law is harsh, but it is fixed. All know what is expected of them, even me._
It is a just way to settle disputes.
He nods. _It is always gratifying to hear one from Avadon say so. Your kind has such power, it is a relief to hear that you respect our ways._
_But what else would you discuss?_
Your laws are savage.

His smile fades, but only for a moment. _Savage? No, being subject to arbitrary whims of the monarch is savage. You think our law contains evil? It is but words. The worst evils come from a mad leader._
With effort, he calms down. _But what else would you discuss?_
You would be better served to decide cases for yourself, no matter what some stone says.
_Outsiders often do not understand our ways. I am flesh, and flesh is weak. We put our trust in unchanging stone._
I haven't seen enough of your laws to say.
_A diplomatic response. I hope you become more familiar with them. When you are in our lands, you should obey them, even though you serve Avadon._
_But what else would you like to know?_
I require assistance.
He nods, but he is slightly nervous. _Of course. Avadon may request whatever it wishes. What do you need?_
I need soldiers to help me hunt the humanoids in the wilds.

_Ahhhh ... If we had the soldiers to spare, we would have hunted those pests already. But our town is small and poor, depending on the coppers spent by pilgrims and officials passing through. We have no army to put at your disposal._
_But, if I ever get an army, I will put it at your disposal with enthusiasm._
I need information.
_I could tell you much, but you would be better served by speaking to Eye Tamaria, near where you arrived. She knows all I do, and more._
_Then talk to our merchants. They will be eager to help you. They can be found in the north end of town._
No, you will give me supplies.

The Overseer is not the slightest bit intimidated. _Young Hands often make such demands, before they learn not to unnecessarily anger the people of the Pact. If you feel anyone here treats you unfairly, speak with your superiors in the Black Fortress._
_Do you need anything else?_
I will speak with them.
_Of course. I hope they have something to your liking. Do you need anything else?_
You wanted to discuss the recent unrest?
_Yes. As you know, we have faced increasing raids from wretches over the last year or two. But, recently, they have been joined by ogres. And titans._
_They are starting to seem ... organized. And I want Avadon to know that I have had no part of it._
You think they are organized?
_I thought so. Now, I am sure of it. These are wild, unintelligent creatures. They do not trust each other. For so many of them to move toward us, in unity ... It is more than just bad fortune._
_I have sent messages saying as much to Avadon and to Hanvar's Council. I await a reply._
Who is organizing them?
He stops smiling. _I am an aging mayor of a small town, precariously placed in the middle of the wilds. I have no agents, no Eyes, no spies. I have no answers._
You think you will be blamed?

_I know that someone will be blamed. Someone must be blamed. It is the way of things. But I have spent my whole life serving the Pact loyally. I simply wanted a chance to say that before whatever happens ... happens._
_And, to show my loyalty, there is something you might want to know about._
_There is someone in the inn. Someone suspicious. From the Wyldrylm. Name, I hear, is Alfans. Always watching. Too quiet. A natural spy. Might be worth talking to. Remember it was me who told you._

Sevilin walks up to the central pillar of the Stone Code. He touches it reverently and looks at the writing. _Always the same,_ he says. _Everywhere in The Kva, even out in these wastes, it is constant._
A wasteland? Aren't you from here?
_I am from The Kva. The northern reaches. More rain, more plants. And more learning._
_But the Code is the same._
So the law is the same wherever we go?
_Yes. Our leaders interpret it and expand it, but they can't change it. They are subject to it. It is our way._
Jenell says, _We trust our chieftains. We choose them, and they have more wisdom than a mere stone._
Shima frowns. _There is no honor in a stone. Mere writing can not tell us how it is proper to behave._
Sevilin is unmoved. _It is not wise, but it is constant, and it protects us from the worst within a leader. You tell me there has never been a tyrant where you are from?_ The response is silence.
_Of course._ He returns to your side.
Shima seems lost in thought. Something about the nearby stones seems to have shaken him.
_[N], the way of Holklanda is one of honor. And that is something in here._ He pats himself on the chest. _But there is something I am wondering._
Sevilin listens with interest.
_Each nation needs a way to control the people, so they do not rob, or kill, or run wild. Without control, we are no different from wretches._
_But does that control best come from a sense of honor or from a set of laws?_
Let's discuss this later. We have work to do.
Shima nods, but he still seems disturbed.
I trust in honor and teaching the young to do right.
Shima nods. _That is wise. The people of Holklanda feel much the same. Thank you, [N]. I feel more at peace._
I trust in a set of rules all must obey.

_Thank you for your honesty, [N]. I can see why those laws would give a sense of comfort. But what value is a people if that within them is rotten, and they only act as they do because of fear of a stone?_ He walks on in silence.
Any sense of control is an illusion.
_I see. [N], I hope that you are wrong. For our own sake._ He walks on in silence.
Shima smiles. _Then I envy you your tranquility. Though I hope never to share it._ He walks on in silence.
Jenell looks more comfortable out in the fields. _I am not fond of towns. Even small ones like Goldcrag. These dry lands remind me of home. Except for the cacti, I suppose._
Nathalie looks over at her. _A servant of Avadon must be comfortable going anywhere. Fighting anywhere. I will climb an erupting volcano if Redbeard asks it of me._
Shima looks around. _It is not so bad. I have been in worse places. As long as we stay out of the cacti._
Jenell's cheeks are flushed, though it might be the heat. _I will go anywhere and fight anywhere. But all have places where they would prefer to be, and this is mine._
Nathalie looks around the inn, but she seems disappointed. _Inns are normally a fine place to find work for hire, but this does not look promising. Still, we might ask around._
Sevilin is amused. _And pacifying a dissatisfied dragon is not enough work for you?_
She shakes her head. _It is not. I have spent too long waiting to be sent back out into the world. I will not refuse any chance to show my talents to those who have ignored them._

There is an archer of The Kva sitting at this desk, reviewing reports of wretch sightings and shaking her head. She wears the insignia of a Monitor on her shoulder. She must have a fair amount of influence in this remote land.

She rises to shake your hand. _Heard a new Hand was here. I am Monitor Sibel, of Goldcrag. I knew, when fresh faces arrived from Avadon, that my Lance's cashbox would be looted soon enough._ She laughs, not unkindly.
Monitor Sibel says, _Anything else you need before I get back to this mess?_ She jabs at the piles of incident reports with distaste.
A lot of trouble with wretches?
She nods. _You leave town, you will see. They have been coming out of the Wretch Lands, and coming. Suspicious, but nothing my Lance can't handle._
She looks grim. _It has gotten worse and worse. Wretches. Ogres. Even sightings of titans. Something is happening out there in the wilds, something bad. Something too big for my Lance to deal with._
You are a Monitor?
She pats her insignia proudly. _Commanded the Lance here for three years. Three good years. Heads of lots of wretches and brigands on pikes. Enough to justify putting a Lance in this small town._
She looks at her bow sadly. _Though I do miss getting out there in the thickets._
What is a Lance?

_In the army of the Pact, ten warriors is a Blade, led by a Watcher. Ten Blades is a Lance, led by a Monitor. That puts a hundred trained, bloodthirsty killers under my command, plus support staff, mounts, and so on._
You spent a lot of time out on patrol?

_Years._ She rolls up her sleeve and shows you an arm covered with a dense web of long, pale scars. _From chasing the enemy through the cactus fields. Every warrior of The Kva gets like this in time._
She rolls her sleeve back down. _We call it 'earning our marks.' A point of pride with us._
Why are so many soldiers here?
_The dragon and the wretches are enough to justify it. We have to control this area. Part of our debt to the Pact._
Your debt?

_Hanvar's Council expects every nation in the Pact to keep a Vanguard ready at all times. That's ten thousand soldiers, ready to move at a moment's notice. The Pact protects us, and, in return, we have a debt. And The Kva pays its debts._
Do you have many dealings with Hands of Avadon?
_The Hands, yes, because they always have their hands out._ She laughs. _Just a little joke. No offense intended._
_There are always lots of things we need done, brigands we need hunted, and we sometimes ask Hands to do it. And there is always a fee._
You pay us for our help?

_That is the old way. Anything you do for us instead of Redbeard, we have to pay. Always been that way. Some resent it, say that you can only get justice if you pay. I'm all right with it, though. Just the way of the world._
And might you have some work for me?
_With the wretches (and worse) coming out of the thickets, we need the help, and we can afford it. Check in with me from time to time. I have work, and I pay my debts._

_Most of my soldiers are on patrol now, watching for the wretches that haunt us. That has kept us from dealing with other problems, like the packs of wolves that are harassing the farms in the lands to the west._
_A new pack stalks the roads between here and Zhethron's Aerie. They are a vicious breed, with long fangs and red-tinged fur._
_Kill eight of these wolves, and I will reward you from our coffers._
Where can I find these wolves?
_Take the road west to Zhethron's Aerie. When you approach the dragon's lair, hunt along the road and in the thickets near it. The bloodthirsty creatures will locate you soon enough._
I have hunted down the wolves of which we spoke.
You describe the hunt. Sibel nods approvingly. She sends a soldier to fetch a pouch of coins and a crude leather bracelet from her Lance's supply room.

_I thank you for your aid, Hand of Avadon, and I will also unlock one of the boxes in the storeroom for you. If you are looking for work in the future, please ask me. I'm sure I will have plenty that needs to be done._
I am still available for hire.
She looks you over skeptically. _I have a task in mind, but you might want to gain some more experience before you undertake it. It is very dangerous._
I am available for hire.

_I am glad you have returned. While one pack of wolves has been purged, another has appeared. Dire wolves, unfortunately, bloodthirsty beasts. They have destroyed three farms already, and I think it has only whetted their appetites._
_The pack is in the lands east of Zhethron's Aerie. Hunt them down, and you will be paid well._
Any ideas on where to look?
_Wander among the thickets due east from Zhethron's Aerie. That is where they have been sighted. It may take some looking to find a route into the cactus fields._
What is a dire wolf?
_A huge wolf, touched by the foul magic of the Corruption. Vicious, ever hungry, and with a touch of intelligence. The Pact does not tolerate those creatures in our lands._
That pack of dire wolves has been destroyed.
You describe the hunt. Sibel and the other soldiers listen with fascination. She sends a soldier to fetch a pouch of coins and a polished oak stave from her Lance's supply room.

_I thank you for your additional aid, Hand of Avadon, and I will also unlock one of the boxes in the storeroom for you. If you are looking for work in the future, please ask me. I'm sure I will have plenty that needs to be done._

_Hungry for more, eh? More wolves, I am afraid. But these ... They are different. Dire wolves, as before, but led by a special specimen. Truly cunning, and black as night. My soldiers have taken to calling it Nightshade. Those few who survived meeting it._
_It has killed five under my command, and wounded more. I want the thing dead._
Killed five? A wolf?
_No ordinary wolf. This one has been touched by dark magic and sent to harry us, I am sure of it. Though I do not know what crime we have committed to merit such a punishment._
Where can I find Nightshade?
_All of the attacks have been in the lands near Zhethron's Aerie, to the south of the entrance. Search the thickets down there._
Nightshade has been hunted down and destroyed.

All activity stops as everyone gathers round to hear the tale of your hunt. They all appear genuinely grateful for the aid. One of them gets a pouch of coins and a pair of silken pants from the Blade's stores. _This drains our resources, but it was worth it if it saves the life of even one of my men._
_I thank you for your additional aid, Hand of Avadon, and we will also unlock the final box in the storeroom for you._

_I am gratified to hear it, Hand of Avadon, but our coffers are drained and our problems are many. At this point, only intervention from the army can help us, and I have heard no news of its coming. So all we can do now is watch the gates and hope._
This inn is surprisingly luxurious for its location, far out in the wilds of The Kva. The travelers who go to visit the dragon must demand quality accommodations.
The bar is being tended by a young woman, who is wiping out pewter mugs with a mostly clean towel. She nods to you. _Welcome, Hand of Avadon. I am Methe, and this is our inn._
Methe wipes out mugs and fills orders for ale. The inn has several varieties on tap, most of them expensively imported from greener climes. _Can I help you?_
Can I get a room?
_I am sorry, but they are all full. Even the common room. It is because of the troubles._
(Return to the arrival pylon to rest. Your vitality will be restored when you use it.)
Troubles?
_With the wretches. Merchants and travelers wait here for longer so that they can band into larger groups before they travel._
I could use a drink.
The Soggy Cactus
Methe has a variety of quality wines and beers available.
Have you heard any rumors?
She suddenly appears rather cagey. _Oh, I hear many things. It's so hard to tell what might be useful._
Well, tell me something you think might be helpful. (Give a tip.)

She thinks. _I overheard someone recently who had just returned from the dragon's cave. He said that a shadowy human was hiding in the thickets. Didn't get a good look. The fellow looked him over and ran off._
_Might be a bandit. You should watch out if you head out there._
She thinks. _One of the soldiers was in recently. Said she saw a dragon flying overhead. Everyone else thought it must have been Zhethron, but she said she was sure it wasn't._
_A second dragon? Fancy that! It would be wonderful for business._
She thinks. _I've heard news, but it isn't good. First, there were wretches, then ogres, and now I hear that titans have been sighted two day's travel to the southwest. Titans!_
_That's what the Pact is supposed to be protecting us from, isn't it? Some people, and I'm not naming names, are not happy about it._
Never mind then.
She nods, smiles and walks off to dish up some stew for an impatient courtier.

You meet the blacksmith of Goldcrag. He is a massively built, swarthy man, and a set of tools hangs from his belt. He is tending to his shop right now, not his forge. You can understand his not wanting to be hammering red-hot metal in this heat.
He shakes your hand. _Welcome, Hand of Avadon. I am Berak. I am more than happy to supply your kind. I have been doing it for years._
Berak says, _Is there anything else I can do to help you, honored Hand? I've a good supply of arms and armor._
Who is tending to your forge?
_Nobody, right now. I can do work in the hot sun, but I prefer to labor at the forge in twilight or early morning._
_In midday, I trade the goods I have made._
You deal with people from Avadon frequently?

_I help the Hands with their equipment. Also caravan guards, and the warriors who come to meet the dragon. I also make equipment for the farmers, what few there are, but all of my work changed when the dragon came._
_I also hire the Hands for help, when they would accept missions from one as humble as me._
How long has the dragon been here?
_Zhethron first flew to his Aerie nearby about twenty years ago. His presence has changed the lives of all here, much for the better. This was a poor place, before the dragon came._
Have many Hands been here recently?
He looks nervous. _Several have been through here recently, going to calm the humanoids on the borders._
_Few have come back, but I imagine they will return soon._
_I hope more are sent. I ... I would never criticize Avadon, but there have been more attacks nearby. Ogres, and even titans. We need help, and it is not being sent._
You can make arms and armor?
_Once, I couldn't, but I learned quickly. I can't match the masters of Dharam and Holklanda, but I can maintain the weapons of the guards who escort the caravans out here._
You hire Hands to help you?
_Many Hands are willing to aid humble citizens of the Pact. In return for pay, of course. Some have a problem with that. I would never question the ways of Avadon._
_I have lost a caravan of my own, which was carrying my goods to Zhethron's Aerie. I want to recover it, or as much as I can. If you can find it for me, I will pay a bounty from my wares._

_There were wretches, led by an ogre. The attack happened on the road just south of the entrance to the dragon's lair. None of the guards were killed. The creatures let them go once all of my goods were taken._
_I would not ever presume to question the way of Avadon, but I hope that Keeper Redbeard is aware that wretch brigands are attacking caravans on the free roads of the Pact._
Where should I look for the goods?

_The goods within it were heavy, so it may take some time for the creatures who stole them to spirit them away. They may still be near where the caravan was taken, southeast of Zhethron's cave. More than that, I can't say._
_Of course! I can sell you my humble crafts, and I can purchase equipment you recover in your travels. All of my prices are, I think you will find, very fair._
That seems fair.
He nods. _Let me know when I can show you what I have._
Prices? I think you should give me what I need.

His mouth opens, but no sounds comes out. _I ... It ... It is an honor to aid Avadon, but I must charge. That has ... Always been the way. But ... I will lower my prices. I will take a loss on everything I sell you. It is all I can do._
Berak's Smithy
Berak is not an accomplished crafter of arms and armor. His wares are lower quality than you are used to. He is helped, out here in the wilds, by the lack of competition.
I found your stolen goods. (Say where they are.)

You carefully describe the location of the ogre's cache. Berak is pleased. _I will hire some guards soon and go to recover my goods. It is such a pleasure to see someone finally strike down the invaders that torment us._

He gives you a pouch of coins and a pair of steel greaves. _I made those myself, and I trust you will find the quality adequate._ After some thought, he adds, _And there is something else I require, though I hesitate to ask._
_I hesitate to ask, since I do not know how far you will be traveling into the wilds. However, the wild, dry mountains to the south are known for a special iron ore, with a bluish tinge._
_I need a large sack of it to begin work with it. I am sure some can be found, as it was once thought useless._
You thought that it was useless?
_That is so. Then the alchemists of Dharam found how to turn it into steel of unusual strength. I wish to try to adapt their techniques to The Kva's benefit. First, however, I need the ore._
I found some of the blue ore you wanted. (Show it to him.)
He inspects the ore eagerly, but his face soon betrays his disappointment. _That is the ore, but not in enough quantity for me to begin my work._
I found a lot of the blue ore you wanted. (Show it to him.)

He inspects the ore eagerly. He takes the sack and conceals it in his storeroom. He looks almost giddy with excitement. _Soon I can try the new techniques for myself. Maybe I can improve the blades of The Kva. That would ..._
_I am sorry. That is not important to you. Here ..._ He brings you a pouch of coins and a pair of plate boots. _These are the finest boots I have ever made. I want you to have them._

He shakes his head. _I very much doubt it. My work with the blue ore has begun, but there is one other thing that could help me. The ceremonial club of a titan. One with a head of steel, not bone or wood._
_I would pay well for such a treasure, but I think that finding one would be impossible._
Why do you want it?

_Because titans, crude as they are, have their own ways of working steel. They need to be very skilled, to make weapons usable by one of their size and strength. Their ceremonial clubs are only made by the most talented of their smiths._
_I think, if I had one, I could learn much about steelworking._
Why is it impossible to get one?
_Because there are no titans near here. And, if there were, well, you would have to get the club from the titans, and they would kill any who tried to steal one._
I found a titan's warclub. (Show it to him.)

You take the massive object from your pack and hand it to him. _Astonishing! And lovely! The workmanship is exactly what I expected. I will spend many hours examining it._ He carries it (with difficulty) into the back room.

He returns with a pouch of gold coins and a broadsword. The blade is touched with rust and pitted with unwholesome green patches. _Do not discount this blade. It is unpleasant to look upon, but it contains powerful magic. I did not make it. I purchased it. I think it might serve you well._ He gives the sword and the pouch to you.

He shakes his head. _I will have to be in business for some time before I can afford to hire you to do more. But, considering how much chaos there is in the wilds, I will soon be able to sell many weapons._
_I was honored to have you in my store. Good day._
A small, nervous man emerges from behind a rack of luxurious robes and cloaks. He is very pale, unusual for this desert. The presence of a Hand of Avadon has given him a facial tic.

_Hello ... Hello. I am Tanner. This is my ... my shop. Fine goods, as you can see. Quality, brought from as far away as Kellemderiel. Just the thing for seeing a dragon._ He lets out a strained, high-pitched laugh.
Tanner stands obsequiously off to the side, ready to swoop in if you need to buy something. He occasionally brushes the desert sand off of the cloaks and other fine goods in his store.
What sort of goods do you sell here?
_Fine goods, as you see. Imported. Brought here on caravans, at great risk and expense. These are the finest garments you can find within two hundred miles. Not a boast, just a statement of fact._
Do you do much business with the locals?
_Oh, no. They are but simple desert folk. Not that I would ever insult them. My market is the travelers._
What use do such luxuries have in the desert?

_Many come to see the dragon. Important people. Courtiers and diplomats. Sages. They come with garments worn and dirtied by the long journey. I help them to look their best before they ask mighty Zhethron for aid._
It's dangerous to bring goods here?
_The free roads were the pride of the Pact, but, in the last few months, they have been swarmed by wretches._
_And, of late, it has only gotten worse, despite the Hands sent to investigate the problem. I would never criticize Avadon, but I thought that you should know._
He looks down at his pale hands. _From The Kva. The northern reaches of The Kva. We are a paler, more civilized folk._
He looks at Sevilin. _Like your companion. He is northern Kva, yes?_ Sevilin nods.
_To open this shop. I followed my fortune, which flew on dragon's wings._
_As long as I can stand. There is blood of Kellemderiel in my veins, and it does not agree with this harsh land._
_Of course. I have much to sell, or I can buy from you. Goods of quality, of course._
Tanner's Goods
Tanner's goods and fashions would be considered very crude in Kellemderiel, but they are by far the best available in this desert.
I want to sell something.
_Of course. I hope I was of aid._
Do you deal with many Hands?
_A few. I do stock some potions and similar goods, but they tend to be more interested in Berak. The smithy. But you are a valued customer, and I will charge you a fair price for all goods._
That is all I ask.
Tanner nods and seems to calm down slightly.
You will lower your prices more than that, or I will make trouble for you.
Tanner takes a step back. He realizes that his fears about your arrival were entirely justified. _But my ... The difficulty ... The expense ..._
He sighs. _Of course. It is the way of Avadon. I will charge as little as I possibly can for my goods._
He seems relieved. _Of course. It was an honor to have you in my store._ He shuffles off.
There is an old man sitting on a log, staring into the fire. His dark skin bears countless thin scars from encounters with the cactus thickets, and the sweltering heat barely affects him.
He shelters his eyes with his hands and inspects you. He looks cautious, but not afraid. He's dealt with your kind before.
_Excuse my not rising. I am an old man. I am called Elder Okan. It is rare for your kind to come out here in the thickets. Rare and, at times, welcome._
Elder Okan pokes at his cooking fire with a stick. He constantly brews cups of dark, acrid cactus tea for himself. _I always have time to talk with a Hand. What else do you need?_
You are an Elder?
_It is not a rank, nothing carved on the stones that bear our laws. It is what the others call me. They respect me. That is all._ He takes a sip of bitter tea.
And what do you do for them?
_I give advice. And, sometimes, I deal with Hands on their behalf. When they come out here._
Do Hands come here often?

He takes a slow sip of tea and smiles wryly. _Why should they? We are poor. We are the natives, here before they came, here after they go. Hands do not think we have the money it takes to buy safety and justice._
Perhaps I am different.
_We will see. What else would you speak of?_
You have a problem with Avadon?
_No. None at all. Or, at least, no problem with the Pact that protects us. What else would you speak of?_
You sound dangerously close to criticizing Avadon, old man.
_Then I take back what I said. I will not speak ill of those who hold power in our land, no matter how they use it. What else would you speak of?_
Tell me about your farms.
_The people of the southern Kva are nomads, not farmers. Mostly. There is a small oasis here, and we grow crops. Some for us, not enough to feed all here. And some are grown for the other._
You don't raise enough food to support yourselves?
_It is brought in on caravans. We can afford it. Being near the dragon brings wealth to all. But, if the dragon was gone, most would leave as well._
Grown for the other? What do you mean?
_Cows are raised here. They are to feed Zhethron. The dragon is always hungry. We are paid well for them. The Pact makes sure of that._
You have dealt with Hands before?
_I have. Sometimes, we have need of them, when the soldiers of the Pact will not help us. We save up a small amount to pay for aid, and I find a Hand who can aid us._
_We need help now, and the soldiers are off hunting the wretches. We can pay little. Can you aid us?_
Nathalie is instantly intrigued. She shuffles excitedly from foot to foot. The chance to fight outweighs the modesty of the reward.
I am too busy.
_I thought so. Then please leave me to my rest. I am an old man._ He goes back to sipping his tea.
Nathalie is obviously disappointed. She mutters something quietly to herself.
I might be able to help you.
He nods. _I thought you might. You seemed ... eager. There is a cave to the southeast, in the thickets. Cool and shadowy. We have used it for storage, in the past._
_However, it is full of rats. Big ones. We tried to get rid of them. Two farmers, one my nephew, are still hurt._
_Slay them, and we will pay you what we can._
I have hunted down some of the rats.
You tell Elder Okan the tale. He shakes his head. _No, there are still too many in the caves. We need more of the dirty things dead._
Your cave is free of rats.
You tell Elder Okan the tale. He nods and sends a boy into his home to fetch a pouch. Okan gives the pouch to you. It is, unsurprisingly, fairly light.
_We thank you. If they were not killed, they would spread. To our silos. Then our homes. You have our thanks, and what little money we have._
Need me to do anything else?
He nods. _It is sad. We do. But we have not saved up enough money. Come back later. We will scrape together what we can for you._
