_We do, and we have saved more money. The problem is in a cellar, just behind my home. Not finished. We were using it for brewing._ He points to the west.

_It is spiders, this time. Many of them. It is very strange. Again, we need them dead, before they start to come out at night and hunt our children. I will have someone clear a path through the thicket for you._
What is odd about them?
_One night, there was one of them. The next night, a swarm. It is strange. Odd enough to keep us out of there._
I found a particularly nasty spider in that cellar. It's gone.
You tell him the tale. He seems relieved, but not entirely. _What is bringing these things to our town? Normally, they fear us. They stay away. Why do they come?_
He has a pouch of coins fetched for you. _That is a lot of money for us, but we are happy to spend it. One less thing to kill us in our sleep._
He nods. _We do. But we have not saved up more money, and it is becoming difficult. Come back later. We will scrape together what we can for you._

_Since you first helped us, a small problem has become a big one. There have always been lizards living in the cacti. Big ones. But they have stayed far from town, until now. Now they have come as close as the south fields, and nobody helps us._
_It has been hard, but we have gotten enough money to hire you again. Kill all of the lizards in the thickets to the south. We will be even more poor than before, but we will be safe._
Keep your money. I will help you without pay.
Okan nods solemnly. _This is the first time a Hand of Avadon has helped us without pay. We are grateful._
Whatever you have saved up so far for payment will be fine.
Okan nods. _We are grateful._
I have rid the thickets of lizards.

Elder Okan nods, but he is not as happy as you thought he would be. _We are safe, then. For now. But the guards don't help us. The Hands, besides you, have stopped coming. I thank you, but we fear the future._
_Why do we pay taxes and help the Pact if it can't help us?_
_Oh, and your reward ..._ A pouch of coins is brought to you. They are silver. It must have been a real challenge for these farmers to scrape together so much money.

There is a Holklandan mage sitting at this long table, sipping a goblet of wine and reading a scroll. When you get close, she inspects you. Lacking an obvious reason to dismiss you, she motions for you to sit.
_I am Seeker Azarni,_ she says. _Normally I prefer solitude on my journey, but it is always wise to curry favor with Hands when you have the chance._
Seeker Azarni sips her wine and reads her scroll. She occasionally looks up at you and gives a little nod. She doesn't mind your presence, but she's not much for conversation.
_I am._ Sip.
How was the journey?
_Long. Many miles on free roads. At one point, I had to use my talents to burn away some attacking wretches foolish enough to try to rob us._
Why did you come?
_The dragon. There is no other possible reason to come here._
What are you reading?
_Magical formulae that are, I am sure, of no interest or value to you._
Have you come to see the dragon?
_I have. I will join a caravan to Zhethron's Aerie soon. I will ask the dragon for help._
Will the dragon help you?
_If the wealth I offer is sufficient. Dragons are creatures of pure avarice. Only two things ever drive them to act: fear and greed. And the only thing they fear is the full enmity of the Pact._
What are you trying to learn?
She frowns. _That is an impolite question. None ever reveal why they seek the dragon unless they have to. To do so would remove some of the advantage gained._
Azarni has no interest in talking to you right now. A few more weeks in this wasteland might make her more willing to talk.
Have you seen the dragon?
She frowns and runs her finger around the lip of her glass. _I did. The dragon refused to aid me. All I offered, and he would not help. Or could not. I am unsure. It is most vexing._
I would like to know more of Holklanda.
She looks at Shima and curls her lip in distaste. _Ask him. I'm sure the banished one can tell you all you need to know._ Shima remains completely expressionless.
_Yes, some of us pay close attention to who of our land joins with Avadon. I know of you, all that I wish to._
Sorry to hear that. I'll be going, then.
_Yes ... And I will return to planning. I will not return home without the knowledge I seek._

She thinks on this. _Perhaps ... I know you have seen the dragon. And you can return, I am sure. I am looking for something from Zhethron's library. If you can find it for me, I will give you the reward I promised the lizard._
_I believe a tome in Zhethron's library contains the secrets of the Sixth Ritual of Inner Vision. I want that tome. I have risked all to come here for it. I must have it!_
What is the Sixth Ritual?
_The Rituals of Inner Vision have been the secrets of Holklandan wizardry for centuries. The peace and calm they bring are what enable our mages to surpass all others in skill._
Nathalie makes a gentle snorting noise. Azarni ignores her.
_We know of five such rituals. It is said that there was once a sixth, and very few mages were allowed to learn it. Alas, those mages all died in battle during the Black Age._

_Ever since, we have quested for any scroll or tome that might contain the secrets necessary to reconstruct the Sixth Ritual. Since those who knew the secret were forbidden to ever write down its contents, this has been difficult._
Why won't the dragon help you?

_Zhethron said he possessed no such secret. I believe that the lizard lies and that he felt the price I offered inadequate. I hope that you, a Hand of Avadon, can enter the creature's library and look on my behalf._
What in the library should I look for?
_If there is any organization, there will be a section on Holklandan magic. Look there._
_A small section, of thin books with many pictures,_ Nathalie mutters. Holklanda and Kellemderiel do not generally get along.
I searched the dragon's library. The ritual is not there.

Seeker Azarni does not take the news well. There is a long period of despondency and drinking. _Ruined,_ she mutters. _I promised. I boasted. How could I have been so foolish? What will happen to my honor?_
_But there is another ... Another dragon. I will seek it. It ... It may know._
_And you. A reward. I will give you a reward._ She fetches several jewels and a pendant from the hoard she was taking to Zhethron. _For your help. Now I will try again. There is still hope._
Where will you go now?

_I have heard that there is a new dragon out there in the wilds, to the south. It only just arrived. I will see it. Perhaps, if you visit it, we will meet again. When I am sober, I will leave this place._
_Now, excuse me. I must prepare._ She waves you away, though she has not yet risen from her table.

This man is sitting in the shadows in the back room of the inn, sipping water from a wooden bowl. A half-eaten loaf of bread sits on a nearby table. His leather clothes and bone pendants mark him as from the Wyldrylm. He's come a long way.
He looks up at you and says, _Greetings._ You ask his name. _Alfans._ You ask if you can sit. He says, simply, _I wish to be alone._
Alfans sits here in solitude, sipping water and thinking quietly. The room is as luxurious as you can find in Goldcrag. His Wyldrylm garb makes him look comically out of place.
Jenell, do you know him?
Jenell smiles. _The Wyldrylm is large. Why would I know him? He looks to be from the south. I am from the north._
He nods to her. She nods back. _And his privacy should be respected._
Can we talk?
_I prefer solitude. I mean no offense. Please leave me._ There is nothing to say to that. You leave him alone.
I have heard some say that you seem suspicious.

You now have his attention. He inspects you carefully, looking for signs of danger or imminent arrest. Finally, he says, _We of the southern woods of Wyldrylm welcome solitude and thought. It is a dangerous time when that can be mistaken for treason._
_But, if it puts me out of danger, I will speak with you. Especially since I am in need of help._
_I sought the help of the dragon. It took two months to see the creature, and two minutes for it to hear my plea and dismiss it._
Was the journey hard?
_Harder than you know. To leave the cool of my forest to walk hundreds of miles on the free roads to this place ... But duty required it._
Jenell nods in sympathy. _You do honor to your tribe._
What did you do then?
_I came here. I spend my money slowly, living on what little I can, while I try to form a plan. I have had no luck. And now they think me a spy._
Will you go home soon?
_Not until I have no hope of getting what I came for. If I must, I will slip into the wild lands to the south and hunt alone._
_I will leave tomorrow, and I will run to the Wyldrylm as fast as my feet can carry me._
You need my help?
_I am ashamed, but I do. My people have a sickness. It is spreading. When I left, there had been many deaths. Now I am sure there are more._
_I came here to talk to the dragon. To look for a cure. The Pact was of no help._
Jenell, what do you think of this story?
_His tribe is from the other side of the mountains from mine, so I have heard nothing of them or their disease. But such things do happen, and I definitely believe that the Pact would not help._
_In such difficult times, no help for savages, yes?_ Alfans nods.
What did the dragon say?

_That it knew of the disease. It had seen humans dying of it before, when he ravaged their weakened cities. And he knew that it could be cured with a brew made with but the tiniest pinch of dragon's fang._

_And that was all. Zhethron never helps anyone to obtain the parts of the bodies of dragons. He doesn't want to 'Create a demand for it,' whatever that means. So now I must find a way to get such a tooth on my own._
Zhethron wouldn't give you one of his teeth?
_No. Apparently, they aren't like scales. They don't grow back._

_I have seen you walking around. I know you travel into the wilds. There are dragons out there, and maybe bodies of dragons. If you can find such a tooth for me, I will give you the treasure I brought for Zhethron._
_That is all I can say. I hope you can help me, or I will need to enter the wilds myself. I do not think I can survive in that desert, but I have no choice._
I have a dragon's tooth. (Give it to him.)
Alfans takes the tooth and examines it. Then he stands and bows deeply to you. _It is real. And ... fresh. The magic in it is strong. It will save many lives._

In return, he gives you what looks like a dragon's fang. It is carved of ivory and inscribed with many lines of intricate runes. _We offered a fang for a fang. This charm has magic in it strong enough to even help a dragon. Bear it well, with our thanks._

There is a merchant sitting by this small cookfire, fanning herself with a torn piece of parchment and eating lunch. Her face has been tanned by the scorching sun of the Kva desert, but she is not from around here.

She nods as you approach and motions for you to sit. _Welcome, Hand. I am Marmara of Dharam. I have only just arrived with a new shipment of goods. I would be happy to give you the first choice from them._
Marmara is still sitting by the fire, fanning herself. _I should get in from the sun, I suppose, but I find that I like it. It is cool and windy in Dharam so much of the time._
What brings your caravan here?
She laughs. _Money! Power and influence follows the dragon, and they bring money with them. So I bring fine luxury goods out here to the middle of this wasteland._
_Happily, I will be returning home soon, before things get worse here._
What sort of things do you sell?
_Fine wines and ales. Fashionable clothes. And weapons to protect them from wretches and ogres for the journey home._
What do they ask the dragon for?
She laughs. _What could a wise, immortal, invulnerable, fire-breathing beast do for someone? I think you can puzzle that out for yourself._
The roads are dangerous?
_The free roads have been infested with brigands and wretches of late. I know that Avadon is ever loath to admit that something might be wrong in the Pact, but that is the hard truth._
You don't mind the heat?
_Not yet, though it will wear upon us soon enough. The cactus fields are worse. I'm amazed that it still hasn't overgrown this miserable town._
There is a lot of cactus.
_Yes. It's vicious stuff. When a cow gets stuck in it, you need to put armor on to retrieve it._
Goldcrag could be overgrown?
_If they don't keep cutting it back. But they won't get rid of it because it protects the town. That is the way of the southern Kva._
_They have a name for the cactus. They call it the Cruel Shelter. That is the truth._
I can trade with you?
_Of course. I have dealt with Hands many times in the past. A new blade? Or a fashionable robe for a state dinner? I can help, and for a fair price._
I appreciate the help.
She nods. _Let me know when you want to trade._
I am a Hand of Avadon. I should not need to pay for equipment.
She is not intimidated. In fact, she laughs. _You must be new. Only one so young would make such a mistake._

_I will charge a fair price for my wares. If you have a problem with that, complain at the Black Fortress. See how Redbeard reacts when he learns that you are intimidating and angering merchants loyal to the Pact._
_Of course. I can sell what I have and buy what I need._
Marmara's Caravan
Marmara has brought the best goods from the north. They are being sold at a generous mark-up.
_All right. Safe travels to you._ She returns to her stew.
She nods. _Safe travels to you._ She returns to her stew.
You approach the runed pylon. It senses the amulet around your neck, that marks you as a servant of Avadon. The glowing stone sends out a wave of restoring energy, erasing your fatigue in an instant.
You touch the pylon. In an instant, you are surrounded by a cloud of energy, that wrenches you back to Avadon ...
Angevine
Watcher Zaren
Kva Soldier
Halrik
Kallia
Tolia
Redfur Wolf
Dire Blasthound
Dire Wolf Howler
Wolfrider Prozz
Prozz's Pet
Tartam
Ogre Graybeard
Runed Sentinel
Hold it.
Identify yourself.
We need support.
The road isn't safe.
I need your help.
I thank you.
The Pact won't help us.
The soldiers are useless.
A warrior!
Accursed cows!
Stay with me!
Do you want to be eaten?
Stay out.
Go away.
This mine, human!
Heh.
I have fine wares.
Abi needs to be quiet.
I need assistance.
We are not safe.
You hear howling from the path behind you.
Dire Wolf Hunter

The road rises steeply to the northwest. It is lined to either side by massive, pointed spires of stone. Granite fangs, crudely shaped with magic and brute force. The path to Zhethron's Aerie is meant to inspire awe.

And yet, it has not kept the wretches away. You can hear their cackling laughter ahead. There are many of the aggravating creatures loitering before the dragon's lair. You wonder why the guards are tolerating that.

As you advance, a figure steps out from behind one of the stone fangs. A shadowwalker, from his garb. His face is completely obscured. He is armed, but his long, curved blade stays sheathed at his side. He walks toward you ...

A vile smell assaults your nose. Rotting, and other odors even more vile. It is not the reek of a dungeon. Worse, it's the smell of a tannery. You can guess why it is out here. Tanneries are commonly forced to locate themselves far from human settlements.
As you walk up the path, you see that the door to the central building is cracked open. Then it closes. Someone was watching you.
You enter a clearing in the middle of a particularly tall and wild thicket of cacti. There is a tower in the center. Several floors, made of huge blocks of rough stone securely mortared together.
When you get close, your hair stands on end. There is power within this tower, raw magic barely controlled.
There are no guards in sight. And yet, you suspect that the owner of this tower has powerful defenses.

One of the most important tasks of the Pact is to maintain the free roads, a network of stone roadways that spans Lynaeus. All people of the Pact are able to travel on the free roads without tolls or hindrance.
Thus, using one of the free roads, you are able to reach the valley below Zhethron's Aerie quickly and without difficulty. However, your easy journey seems to be about to end.

The road here is crumbling and poorly maintained. There are wolf tracks plainly visible in the dirt all around you, and there is an eerie quiet in the air. It is a sense of danger and unease Hands quickly learn to pay attention to if they want to survive.
To the northwest, you can see the massive pillars of Zhethron's Aerie rising above the cactus thickets. Even if you get there, you will still have to face the dragon ...
There is an abandoned farmhouse at the side of the road. It is quiet and empty, and the walls are crumbling.
There is an odd chill in the air here, making you shiver despite the desert heat. There are no tracks on the ground, not even of wolves. Odd.
The cellar of the abandoned farmhouse is littered with bones. Some animal, some wretch. It's icy cold down here. You feel like you are being watched.
Bones. Cold. Paranoia. During your extensive training, these were clearly listed as the three main symptoms of monstrous infestation.

You hear a sound behind you. Bones scraping across stone. The skeletons behind you rapidly begin to reassemble themselves. You kick a few of them apart before they can complete themselves, but you can't stop all of them in time.
This is convenient. The infestation here is going to come to you, making it much more convenient for you to purge it.
Wretch Bones
Accursed Skeleton

This pathway is lined with totems, marking this crevice as claimed by wretches. All of the skulls on the totems, you note, are either from other wretches or made of clay. Wretches are not mighty creatures in battle.

Of course, that doesn't stop them from trying. The moment you set foot on their path, you hear a shrill scream. A wretch guard in the distance has spotted you and released several mangy wolves to attack you. He chases after them, clearly having no idea who you are.
This shouldn't be difficult.
Wretched Wolf
Hunter Gvarl
You have discovered the hideout of a small tribe of wretches. It is a small series of underground chambers, full of mud, trash, and a truly foul smell.
Many pairs of eyes silently track you from the shadows. They hold on to their crude weapons, unsure whether you are going to attack them.
Zhethron's Aerie - Northwest
Angevine - Sage
All who come in peace are welcome.
TANNERY
AERIE OF THE MIGHTY ZHETHRON
Pleas for aid will be heard.
Tribute must be presented.
Halrik's Freehold
There is a lone woman sitting back here, doing some repair work on a thick leather jerkin. Even with the fire unlit, it is very hot in this room, but it doesn't seem to bother her.
The presence of armed warriors in her home does seem to bother her. She politely suggests that you return to the common room and speak with Halrik.

There is a small herd of cattle at this farm, waiting unhappily to meet their final hands of fate between a dragon's jaws. Their simple bovine minds have, in their vague way, recognized this fact, and they are coping with it by making the lives of the humans around them as difficult as possible.
Looking down this corridor gives you a strange feeling of vertigo. You would swear that this corridor is too long to fit inside the tower. There is strange magic at work here.
You have the feeling that you are being watched. And, considering the circumstances, you very likely are being watched.

These boxes are full of supplies. Tools. Bars of iron. Even a few finished bronze and iron weapons. The boxes are moldy and rotten enough to have been down here for a long time. They were probably stolen from a passing caravan.

There is nothing of high enough quality to be useful to you, and there is too much stuff for you to carry out. You suspect there is a merchant somewhere who would be very interested to hear that all of this was found.
The wretches are all cowering in their alcoves, hoping that you will just walk by.
Leave them alone.
They sigh with relief as you walk away.
Attack them.
The wretches let out a pitiful howl and try to defend themselves.

There is a Kva soldier sitting by the fire sipping tea. His helmet is off, and the harsh sun doesn't seem to bother him. His jerkin bears the symbol of a Watcher, which means that he commands a Blade of ten soldiers.

When you approach, he spits into the fire and rises to greet you. _A warrior, yes, but not of the Legion. I am Watcher Zaren. Since your face is not familiar, mind telling me what brings you onto the free road?_
Watcher Zaren sits by the fire. He watches you suspiciously. _Anything else to say before you move on?_
It is none of your business what I do here.
Watcher Zaren's face grows flushed, but he says nothing. _This is a free road. Until you break the laws of the Pact, I can do nothing to you. But I will be watching you._
I am a Hand of Avadon.

Watcher Zaren slowly swallows a mouthful of tea and inspects you. _I suppose I can believe that. You have the look. Welcome to the free road of this valley. My Blade is trying to keep it secure and having little luck. Watch yourself._
_We were sent here by Monitor Sibel of Goldcrag. This Blade is tasked to keep this road as safe as possible._
Tell me about this road.
_It's in bad shape. Bandits and wolves everywhere. Nasty wolves, the sort that doesn't fear anything on two legs. And, with only ten soldiers, all we can watch is this short section._
Why don't you have more support?
_Because Goldcrag only has a hundred soldiers to watch the town and miles of road, and there are wretches everywhere._
_And ogres. And maybe even titans, if the rumors are right._
_If we try to watch a longer stretch than this, we'll be too spread out. And then we'll be killed._
Shima frowns. _You have a duty to the Pact. All I hear are excuses._
Zaren snorts. _And Avadon has a duty to us. Where are you? The wretches are everywhere now!_ Shima doesn't seem impressed.
I'm sure you are doing all you can.

_We sure are. And I don't know what happened to those Hands Avadon sent here. We saw them pass on the road. We thought they would help, but we never saw them come back. I hope you can do what they didn't._
_Need anything else?_
Avadon expects these roads to be kept safe.
_Then tell Redbeard what a terrible job we're doing. He can put us in his dungeons. Can't be worse than being left out here, waiting for an ambush in the middle of the night._
I'd like to know more about the dragon.
He snorts. _I'm only a Watcher. I've never been anywhere near the dragon, and I hope never to be. All I hear are rumors._
What have you heard?
_That the dragon's lair is infested with wretches. The creature's own cave. Now, I ask you, what use is it to be a dragon if you can't even rid your own lair of pests?_
He thinks. _Or maybe the creature is so arrogant that it lets humans do the work. Wouldn't surprise me._
_Nothing lately. It's been quiet. But, since you're here, the dragon must be angry about something._
Zaren looks worried. _I've heard that the dragon was hurt. Seriously. Don't know by what._
_That would mean there's something around here that would scare a dragon. And we're here, camped out in the open by a free road._
Anything I can do to help you?
He shakes his head. _I don't have any way to pay you. If you would help us anyway, it would be a nice change. See a wolf or a wretch? Get rid of it. That's the help we need._
He points to the east. _There's a farmer that way that's been begging us for help for weeks. Name is Halrik. Want to help me? Shut him up._
_Well, watch yourself. This road is free, but, once you're out of sight of this camp, it's not safe._
You meet a Kva soldier, one of several stationed here to watch the free road. You try to talk to him, but he says, _You should talk to our Watcher. That's Zaren. He'll want to see you too._
This soldier is dozing fitfully in the shadow of this tent. Probably stuck with the night patrols. You walk away quietly.
You enter a cool, shadowy crevice in the side of the mountain to the west. There are bones everywhere, and the smell of rot is heavy in the air.
The west side of the clearing is very dark, unnaturally so. You struggle to see what is back there. And then you realize that the darkness is slowly moving toward you.

A pair of glowing red spots appears in the shadows. Eyes. The blackness surrounds the insubstantial figure of a wolf. Some horrible magic, perhaps even the touch of The Corruption, has warped this creature.
It stalks toward you. The foul stench of its breath reaches you. You grip your weapon, trying to keep from retching.

Your blades have actually drawn blood from this foul beast. It lets out an angry snarl. Two bits of the blackness break off and float nearby. They grow solid and take on the form of wolves. Nightshade now has allies to fight at its side.
It is hard to focus your eyes on the wolf shades. Each appears to be four shadows, superimposed on each other and barely held together. A strong force might only serve to break them apart.
Nightshade opens its mouth again. Green drool oozes out of it, hissing as it strikes the ground below. It lunges at you, its speed doubled.

You deal a final blow to the hideous wolf-thing Nightshade. In an instant, the sun breaks apart the shadows that surrounded it. Its body collapses and rots away before your eyes, leaving a pool of searing green ichor behind.
The farms around here will be free from wolf attacks for some time.

There is a young woman standing by the side of the road, pulling on a cow. She has a rope around its neck and is trying to drag it toward the farm to the north, but it seems content to remain where it is.
Then she sees you. She turns to greet you (holding on to the rope with one hand) and curtsies. _Welcome, warrior. You are a warrior, right? You look like it! I am Tolia. Hello!_

Tolia continues to look after her cows, trying to keep them from wandering off where the wolves can get them. She is a small person, and the cows don't treat her with the respect and obedience she deserves.
She waits for you to say more. _Oh. You didn't say if you're a warrior or not. I guess you ... You must be, but it's secret._ She smiles, excited. _A secret warrior! I won't ask anything else!_
_It's too bad, though. My father told me that I was supposed to tell any warriors I saw that he might hire them._
Greetings. I am a Hand of Avadon.
Her jaw drops. _Really? Wow! That's ... Wow. I've heard that Hands go by, but I've never seen one. One of the warriors that protects the Pact! My father would love to hear ..._
_Oh! I almost forgot! My father told me that I was supposed to tell any warriors I saw that he might hire them._
Hello. I am, as you said, a warrior.
_Really? I knew it! I'm sure you've traveled everywhere, fighting Farlanders and bandits and wretches. And you have lots of stories! Exciting stories! My father would love to hear ..._
Tell me about your father.

_His name is Halrik._ She points at the large, nearby farm. _He is in there. He needs help, but none of the soldiers give it. He told me, if I saw any warriors, that I should let them know. And then get away from them._
_Oh. I don't think I was supposed to say the last part._
Jenell says, _That is all right. Your father sounds wise to have said it._
Nathalie says, _That is all right. Your father sounds wise to have said it._
I would be glad to help your father.
She grins. Her teeth are blindingly white in her deeply tanned face. _He is inside. He would be happy to see you._
_Now I ... I have to go. I'm sorry if I'm rude. Goodbye._ She turns and leaves, dragging a cow after her.
Assistance is not free.
She grins. Her teeth are blindingly white in her deeply tanned face. _I know! My father said everything about how all this works! He will still be happy to see you!_
I am too busy to help.
_Oh. Well ... I have to go. Goodbye._ She turns and leaves, dragging a cow after her.
I am going to help your father.
_Really? You met him and you'll help us? That's wonderful!_
I have helped your father.

_Really? The wretches won't bother us anymore?_ She leaps forward and gives you a painfully tight hug. _Thank you! Thank you!_ You wince at the pain in your ribs. Years of dragging cows has left her arms very strong.
You note that Jenell has turned away, so that Tolia can't see her giggling.
You note that Nathalie has turned away, so that Tolia can't see her smiling.
Tell me about your farm.
_Oh ... I'm sorry. My father told me not to. Talk to Halrik. He will tell you things._
Having trouble with your cows?

She frowns at the recalcitrant creatures. _Always. I hate them. And they hate me. My father makes me keep them by the farm and safe. But they make it so difficult, I'm glad for what will happen to them._
Are they in danger?
_Yes. From the wolves and the wretches, who always want to steal them away. They won't bother me as long as I stay close to home, but they love to take our cows._
What will happen to them?
_They'll be sold to the soldiers and Zhethron's Aerie. Then they'll be fed to the dragon. And good riddance._
She curtsies. _Then good day to you. I have to get back to ..._ She looks at a cow and sighs. _Come on, you._ She starts to drag it off.
You approach the aerie of Zhethron, one of the oldest and most feared dragons in all of Lynaeus. Before you can enter, however, the fearsome Demo Demon appears before you in a cloud of vile smoke!
_Haw! Haw! Haw!_ he roars. _The lair of the dragon ahead is the last section in the demo! Until you purchase this game, the exciting adventures beyond will ever be denied to you! Bwah! Hah! Hah!_
_To purchase Avadon, visit the Spiderweb Software online store. You will be given a chance to go there every time you run or quit the game! Hisssss!_
And then, its message of woe delivered, the Demo Demon vanishes.

Sevilin looks up the hill toward the dragon's lair to the northwest. He shakes his head. _Dragons. They live in our land. Eat our food. And yet, they are not required to follow the Stone Code. It is ... bothersome._
Jenell sighs. _The Stone Code again? Here we go._
Sevilin looks at her. _I know it is bothersome for you to be in a land with laws. Not constant chaos, like in the Wyldrylm._ Happily, she ignores his response.
It's just a few creatures. Does it matter?
Sevilin says, _The meaning of the Code is that it applies to all. Once something lives in The Kva and doesn't have to follow it, it weakens the whole thing._
_But I will remain quiet about it. I know that we have a task to do._ He walks on in silence.
If they live in your lands, they should follow your laws.
Sevilin laughs. _I agree. But I would like to see someone tell that to the dragons._
Jenell smiles. _On that, we agree. It would be an amusing sight._
Do we have to discuss this now?
Sevilin is annoyed, but he walks on in silence.

As you cross the bridge, you receive a brief, cool breeze. Shima, who is sweltering in his black garb, sighs in relief. _It is a great honor to wear the black of a shadowwalker, but it can sometimes be ... wearying._
Sevilin, who is also miserable, looks over at him. _We both need to wear armor, but couldn't you wear something white over it? It wards off the heat._
Jenell looks at him. _We of the Wyldrylm dress to match the weather, not fight it. Something you might consider._
Nathalie smiles. _Why not wear a robe? Something nice and flowing and airy? Does your garb always need to be so thick? And black in this weather is unwise._
Shima chuckles. _This is one point where our traditions might be ... poorly chosen. But I wear these garments with pride anyway. They are all that I have left of home._
Jenell looks down at the free road. Surprisingly, she is frowning. _The free roads. So they are called. But they make my people less free, not more._

_The tribes of the Wyldrylm have traditionally charged a toll to those who cross our lands. It is a right of ownership, almost sacred. The Pact took that from us, made our lands not our own. There is little free about it._
Nathalie seems confused. _But, in return, you can travel on the roads of others without paying, and you can travel farther and safer than you would have been able to before._
Sevilin is not impressed. _We had to compromise our ways too. Change the Stone Code to match the laws of the Pact. But what we gain is more than what we lose._
Jenell responds, _I am sorry we are not as happy about losing the old ways as you are. I came to Avadon in the hope that ..._ She shakes her head. _Never mind. It is hot. Let us travel toward shade._
Nathalie walks up to one of the tapestries and touches it lovingly. _Kellem work. Someone here is from Kellemderiel. Or just likes fine things. It is enough to make me miss home._
Then she returns to your side. _But only for a moment._

There is an old farmer sitting at the table, eating stew. His skin is dark and leathery, the result of decades of exposure to the harsh sun of The Kva. When he raises his spoon to his mouth, you see that he is missing two fingers on his left hand.
He watches you calmly as you enter his home. _Ahhh ... A Hand. I recognize the look._ He stands and shakes your hand. _I am Halrik. I welcome you to my home._
_These are hard times, and these lands have grown wild. I am forced to pay for that which should have been given. If you have time, I have an offer for you._

Halrik sits at the long table, eating stew. You have time to see what a nice farmhouse this is. Decades of hard work have gone into building it, and you can see why Halrik refuses to be scared away by mere wretches.
_I farm this land. The river has left a few patches of land that can grow crops, and I can feed and look after cows until I can sell them to the Aerie._
Zhethron's Aerie buys cows from you?
_Yes. The humans buy them to feed the dragon. My job is to keep them fed and safe until then._

_For thirty years. Built this home with my own hands, and then made it bigger. And bigger again. Raised five children. This is my land, and I won't be driven off of it._ He looks up at the weapons on the wall to either side of the fireplace and nods.
Have you been a farmer your entire life?
_No._ He looks down at his mutilated left hand. _I was a soldier. Did well, until I was forced out of the Legion. Good thing for me I had enough money saved to buy the land here._
Did you lose one of those fingers in battle?
_Yes, one of them. Bitten off by a wretch. But not the other._
What happened to it?
_Lost it to the Stone Code. Disobeyed an order. Penalty was discharge, and a finger. But they let me choose which finger to lose. Smallest one on my left hand. Code is harsh, but fair._
These lands have grown wild?
_Look around for yourself. Wolves and wretches everywhere, and it's getting worse._ He looks down at his stew and frowns. _My family can't feel safe anymore. Nobody's can. And we know who to blame._
How long has it been like this?
_The wretches starting coming in greater numbers about six months ago, and it started getting worse from there. We farmers ask why they are coming, but nobody knows._
_And now there have been ogres sighted. Ogres! I've always said I'll be taken out of here feet first, but I never thought it would come to that. If your lot doesn't do something soon, it will!_
And who do you blame?

He looks you right in the eye. _The Pact. And Avadon. We pay so much in taxes. We provide warriors. In return, we're supposed to be kept safe. Well, where are you? Where are the warriors? Where is our safety?_
Sevilin turns and looks at you, interested in how you will react to this blatant insubordination.
Shima turns and looks at you, interested in how you will react to this blatant insubordination.
Jenell turns and looks at you, interested in how you will react to this blatant insubordination.
You are right. Something should be done. And I'm sure something will be done.
Halrik seems surprised. _I'm glad to hear that from one of your kind. I just wish I still had that kind of help. Anything else you want?_
The Pact is doing what it can.
Halrik shakes his head. _Not true. I know what the Pact can do. I fought for the Pact. I saw it myself. The Pact could fight back the wretches. It just isn't doing it. Why, I don't know._
He mutters, _Anything else you want?_
Watch your tongue, old man. Remember who you are talking to.
Halrik calms down. He looks sullenly away from you and mutters, _Oh, I remember. And I will keep remembering. What else do you want?_

_I do. And I will pay for it. Due west of here, over the river, there is a gang of wretches. They keep a few wolves with them. They come at night and steal my cows. And they're getting bolder. I fear they will do more soon._
_The soldiers outside are useless. They refuse to help. So I will pay you if you get rid of them._
What will you pay me?
_Money, and two handy trinkets from my soldiering days. It will be worth your time, I promise you._
No. I am too busy.

_Of course you are. Well, I will be here if you change your mind. I'm sure the job will still be open. Nobody else will help me. Now, I must return to work. Good day._ Greatly incensed, he stands and walks away.
I can do it.
_I'm glad. As I said, go west and a little south. There will be a bridge over the river. Cross it and the scum will be to the west._
I found those wretches and drove them off.

You say what happened to Halrik. He seems satisfied. _Some deed. Word will get around about this. The wretches will learn that a Hand helped us. They will leave before you can get them. This valley will be much safer now._
_That is all it takes to keep us safe. An hour's work, and the word of Avadon. If only more of your kind would help us._
_And I will unlock a box in my storeroom. Your reward is in there. I thank you, [N]._
Do you need anything else?
_No. I have no problem I can't take care of myself. And I can't afford any more of your sort of help._

There is an ogre in the western alcove, going through a wooden crate. He is a pitiful specimen for his kind, old, thin, and stooped over. Being in this pit, lording over a handful of filthy wretches, is a humiliating fate.
When he sees you, he turns and snarls. _Stupid wretches! Worthless! Why you no kill human! Why human here? Come! Kill it! Kill it!_
The ogre grabs a club and lumbers toward you. The wretches give an unenthusiastic battle cry and rise to their feet.
The wretches have stolen a pair of cows. They hide in the back of their muddy pen and moo unhappily.
There is a wretch warrior standing at this crude palisade, bravely placing himself between you and their pathetic little village. He wears a necklace heavy with wolf fangs around his neck.
He points his blade at you. _Stop there, human! I am Wolfrider Prozz! This our land! You no take! We no want fight. You go!_
Wolfrider Prozz, showing an unusual amount of courage for his kind, continues to stand guard at the palisade. _You here? You go! We stay! This ours!_
You claim this land?
_We come. It dry. It empty. Nobody here. We take! Ours now. We no go._
_And what Avadon care? This dry land. Dusty. Why you care if we here?_
I want to know something.
_No talk. We wretch. You human. I stay, you go._
The farmer Halrik sent me. You have been pestering him.
Prozz thinks for a bit. _Oh. Farmer? Yes! Big farm! So many cows. They no need so many cows. We need cows too! We leave them alone. Take cows. Is ... What humans say? Fair? Fair!_
_But farmer send you? For what?_
You need to cease your stealing.
_But we want cows! We no take cows, we no have cows. And we can take cows! So it is right to take cows! See? I think like a human!_
_So you go away._
If you want to stay here, you aren't allowed to steal.
Wolfrider Prozz shakes his head. _I already say, right to take cows, whatever you call it. Go away, human. You come in, we kill you!_ He gives you a raspberry and turns away.
I can't argue with that logic. I'll go.
Wolfrider Prozz nods. _That right! Wretches are strong and have logic! Go away, human. You come in, we kill you!_ He gives you a raspberry as you turn away.
I am a Hand of Avadon, and I say you will stop or die.

One of the few things capable of deflating wretch arrogance is the word 'Avadon.' Wolfrider Prozz takes a step back. _Av ... Avadon? Avadon sends you? Sends a Hand to deal with Prozz? Prozz is mighty! This is honor for us!_
_But ... Oh. You kill us? No. We stop with taking. We leave humans. Alone. I will tell others Avadon talk to Prozz!_ He turns away from you, bursting with pride.
Oh, this is getting us nowhere. (Attack.)

Wolfrider Prozz nods solemnly. The idea that you might completely outclass them has not at all occurred to him. _My logic defeats you! Now we fight! Come friends! Drive out the tall one! Hrrrarrrr!_ He charges you.
If you won't go, I'll drive you out. (Attack.)
Wolfrider Prozz nods solemnly. The idea that you might completely outclass them has not at all occurred to him. _Then we fight! Come! Drive out the tall one! Hrrrarrrr!_ He charges you.
All right. I'll go.
Prozz takes a step back, but he doesn't sheathe his weapon._
_I know you from Avadon. Still, this our lands. We still keep!_
_You stay out. You step in our gates, we fight!_ Ah, wretches. They are weak and generally foolish, but you have to admire their courage. And they don't know how to bluff.

You are now inside the tannery, where the skins are trimmed and processed. At least, it looks like a tannery. The vats are empty and the furs and skins on display are dusty. The reek that assaulted you outside is still present, but faint. The building is strangely cool and pleasant.

There is a lone man here, in a leather jerkin. He wears a long, thin blade at his side. _Welcome, traveler,_ he says. _I am Tartam. I welcome you. Have you come here to purchase fine leather goods? Because, if so, I can aid you._
He has a faint smile on his face, as if something is amusing him. You aren't sure what.
Tartam says, _Is there any other way I can help you?_ He still has a faint, cocksure smile. His hand rests on the pommel of his blade.
You notice that his hands lack the stains and burns you would expect to see on a tanner. Odd.
You notice that his hands lack the stains and burns you would expect to see on a tanner. His disguise is less convincing than it could be.
You are a tanner here?
He nods. _Oh, yes. I just kept moving away from Goldcrag until they stopped telling me to keep moving. Then I built my tannery here._
It doesn't look like you're doing much in here.
_Well, there aren't many traders out here, are there?_ He smiles.
Who buys your wares?
_Why you, hopefully. And merchants supplying the dragon's cave, sometimes. It is quiet here. Except for the wolves, of course._
I would like to know something about the area.
_Why, I would be happy to help. I don't walk outside much. Too warm. But if there is something you are looking for, you can ask._
_Tartam nods. _I'll tell you what I can. I'm only one pair of eyes, but I have seen some things._
Tell me about the dragon's lair.
_I can't. I've never been inside._
_I've heard, however, that the dragon has been hunting titans. And was injured doing it. If something isn't done soon, the Pact will lose a valuable ally._
There are a lot of wolves on the road.
_There are, indeed. Makes me wish something would be done about it. Yes, indeed._ His tranquil smile is starting to bother you.
_And wretches as well. They have been advancing, and the Pact hasn't sent enough soldiers to deal with them._
_Avadon has sent Hands to investigate, but ..._
_They have been out in the wilds longer than they should have been. I am worried, and so is Avadon. I have been watching my back, and you should do the same._
A caravan was robbed near here. I'm trying to find what was stolen.
_Really? How noble of you. I think I can help._
_Really? Earning a little extra money in a time like this? Well, I suppose I can't blame you. I think I can help._
_There is an opening in the cliff face to the north. A lot of garbage there. I've seen an ogre and some wretches going in and out of there. It is odd._
Odd? Why?
_Because that passage ends in a dead end. If I didn't mind the risk, I would investigate. There may be a secret passage, though you would have to look very closely to find it._
Can I see your wares?
Tartam's Tannery
Tartam shows you his wares. The quality is good, but the items have a layer of dust on them, as if they've just been sitting here for some time.
Tartam shows you his wares. He brought them out here to help with his disguise as a simple tanner. The prices are low, and the quality is good.
I am a Hand of Avadon, and I need to question you.
He seems very amused by this. _Oh, really?_ He holds his hands wide. _I would so hate to have Avadon suspect me. I am eager to help. Please tell me, what is the problem?_
Someone has been selling weapons to the wretches.

His smile fades. Tartam looks genuinely irritated. _Have they? Really? I suspect you are correct. Very perceptive, Hand of Avadon. And, tell me, please. What insightful soul told you that I was responsible?_
I am asking the questions.
_Really? Then let me guess. It was Abi. I knew this would happen the moment I heard that fool went to Avadon. Spilling out words. Letting anyone who cares to listen know what we know._
_And now he wastes your time as well, sending you to question me, a fellow servant of Avadon._
His name is Abi.
_But of course. I knew this would happen the moment I heard that fool went to Avadon. Spilling out words. Letting anyone who cares to listen know what we know._

_An Eye, actually. Sent out here by Heart Miranda to find out who was supplying the wretches with weapons. My identity was to be a secret. No longer, apparently. I will have to leave soon, before I wake up with my throat cut._
_Since you know who I am, I will help you if I can. I will unlock my safehouse for you. And, now that you know who I am, I suppose you have some questions for me._

_Someone is selling steel weapons to the wretches. That is the sort of thing that could cause real problems. I think I have learned who is dealing with them. However, she is usually out in the wild lands to the south._
_Preparing to leave. As soon as I am sure that nobody is giving good steel to the wretches, I will return to the safety of Avadon. I don't think we are safe anymore. I think someone is hunting us._
That is unfortunate. I don't think I can help.
Tartam looks even more irritated. _Of course. Everyone can take the time to gossip about me, but nobody can actually help._
_Just leave me. I will find a way to reach the smuggler, with or without you._ He stalks off.
Perhaps I can help.
_I thought you might. You are a Hand, after all. I believe that the smuggler's name is Neray. She pretends to be a trapper, but I think she is much more. You might meet her if you travel south._
_If you do and can find proof that she is helping the wretches, she should be brought to justice. Otherwise, the problems we're having with the wretches here will only get worse._
What makes you think she is responsible?
_Just guesswork. I watch the roads to see who goes where and when. When Neray has been to an area, wretch attacks soon follow, and the wretches are wielding new, quality blades._
_Selling anything to the Farlands that would enable them to threaten the Pact is a crime. Steel, knowledge, magic. A serious crime, one of the worst._
Why do I need proof?
He gives you an evil smile. _Well, you are a Hand of Avadon, so you need no proof at all. But I like to avoid killing the innocent. A matter of ... craftsmanship, I suppose._
How should I bring her to justice?
_She should spend a long time in Avadon's dungeons. Eye Mamora could learn much from her. But that does not seem practical. So, if she is truly guilty, death is probably the best option._
I tracked down Neray, but she escaped.
You tell the tale. Tartam is both pleased and annoyed. _Well, at least we know that she is the one. And she knows we know, so she will be hiding in the wild lands for some time._
_Watch for her. If you travel down south for long enough, you might meet her again._
I have found and killed Neray.
You tell the tale. Tartam is pleased. _Then my mission is complete. The Heart sent, the Eye watched, and the Hand acted. This is how things are supposed to work._
_Since I am leaving, I don't need my records and notes anymore. I will open the back room for you. Please take anything you find that seems of use._
_Soon I will return. And give Abi a good, sharp kick._
I'll be going then.
Tartam smiles at some secret joke. _Then I bid you safe travels, Hand of Avadon. The free roads are not safe. Watch yourself._ You think back, unsure. Did you ever mention that you were a Hand?
_Then safe travels, and be wary. Of late, the roads are not safe for our kind._

There is a woman sitting in this throne, watching you enter. She is very small, thin, and pale. Her robes are long and elegant. They flow to the base of the throne and curl along the floor almost to where you are standing.

She touches her fingertips to her forehead in greeting. _Welcome, [N], Hand of Avadon. I am Angevine, of the Kellem. I sensed your presence, and I allowed you to enter. Our kind should always be hunting for allies. And trading partners._

Angevine curls up in her throne, her slender legs folded up underneath her. You might be fooled by her girlish exterior, if you couldn't sense the power that flows from her. And if her stone guardians weren't staring at you.
_Little bits of the parlor trickery. I have watchers, you know. Pay it no mind._

_It is a humble thing, is it not? And in such a dry and unpleasant place. But, with the aid of my helpers, I will expand it. It will never be fashionable, but it should at least have the comforts, yes?_
Nathalie says, _You came directly from Kellemderiel to this place? How dreadful._
_Yes,_ she responds, _though the icy peaks of Avadon are unpleasant as well. Nowhere on Lynaeus is as lovely as home._
You built all of this yourself?
_In a sense. My helpers made it. But I made them, so yes, I suppose I did. And yet, I take no pride. It is a stony and lumpy place._
_Ah, who knows? Time does such funny things. I think I have been inside this tower for a year. But I can't say how much time has passed outside._
Who are your helpers?
She waves at the stone men standing in the alcoves. _The servants of rock. I make them. It is my specialty. They are very helpful for construction. And light cleaning._
She gives you a little wink. _And for crushing into jelly those with no manners._
They are quite impressive.
_I thank you, but I am sure my housekeeping is not what you came to discuss, yes? What do you need?_
Can I buy one from you?

She giggles, a carefree, lilting sound. _Oh, no. Not that I would object to your taking a pile of rocks, but the magic that sustains them would fade the moment you left my tower. And then you would feel angry and cheated. But maybe you have something else you want from me, yes?_
You are from Kellemderiel?
_I am. A beautiful land._ She sighs wistfully. _The food, the music, the dancing. Also, no cacti. 'Twas my home. No longer._
What did you do there?
_I made my talents available to the nobles, for a price. One with my natural talents is always found to be of value._
_Alas, working for one may made me the enemy of another. Alas. A soldier in a war started by others, that was me._
Why did you leave?
Angevine looks mildly shocked by the question.
Angevine looks mildly shocked by the question. Nathalie suddenly develops an intense interest in the tilework on the walls.
_Such direct questions about matters of politics and alliances are felt to be rude._

_Though, since you were kind enough not to attack me, I will simply say that I was in the employ of one party, and another party, foe of the first party, decided to deny the first party my services. And so here I am. In a desert._
You wish to trade with me?
_Indeed. I spend my long hours here making crafts of some value, and I purchase from travelers materials for my work._
_In addition, there is a certain item I would like to obtain. I would reward well whoever could bring it to me._
Angevine's Crafts
Angevine shows you the items she has made. She is remarkably skilled at magical crafts.
I would like to sell something.
What are you trying to obtain?
_A libram. A magical journal, full of notes and minor works of spellcraft, by a Kva mage named Ahmed. It currently rots, unused and unread, in a library near here. I could make use of it._
_In fact, I believe it is in the library of Zhethron. The dragon._
How might I get the book?
_Your travels include the lair of the dragon, correct? You might trade for it. You might sneak it out. I trust your judgment._
You want me to steal a book from a dragon?

_Oh, crude theft might not be necessary. Well, it probably will. But the dragon would never notice. If you stole a single coin from its hoard, it would be furious. But books? I doubt that the wyrm cares._
She smiles and flutters her eyelashes. _But of course! I welcome civilized conversation._
Fabron has sent me to find you.
She tenses up in her seat. There is the sound of grinding stone from the sentinels in the alcoves. They have leaned forward slightly.
_Ah. Fabron. A toady and a worm. And one who hires others to fight his battles for him._
_I worked for some nobles who happened to be the foes of his family. It is true. And they were then imprisoned, and some were executed. Also true._
_But why does he now send you to hunt me?_
I found Ahmed's Libram. (Give it to her.)

She takes the book and flips through the pages. _Yes. This is what I needed. How sweet of you to bring it to me!_ She leaves the throne room and goes upstairs. Soon she returns with a spear and a pouch of coins. She gives both to you.
_The pouch of gold is not enchanted, but the spear has received the benefit of my spellcraft. I hope these gifts are to your liking._
She nods. _Then I trust you can find your way out. Thank you for alleviating the boredom of my exile._
He didn't go into details.

_Well, I am already brought low, a miserable exile. All for performing mere ... errands. Of course ..._ She flutters her eyelashes. _You could simply tell him that I am dead. He would never come out here to check, indolent worm that he is._
_I can be more useful to you alive, I think. Please, let us help each other?_
Just errands? Really?
_Well, some of those errands may have resulted in bloodletting. Politics in Kellemderiel is that way, after all. But to still hunt me after his side was victorious? It is so ungracious!_
I will spare you and say that I killed you.
She is trying to seem calm, but she is clearly relieved. _You are so kind. I will stay here in my pathetic exile, but alive._
_Now let us speak of this ugly business no more._
I will spare you, as long as you flee and never return.

She thinks this over. _You are very kind to allow me to continue my pathetic exile, alive. But I will not be driven from my home, not until I am ready. Tell the cur who sent you that I have fled if you wish, but I will not leave here until I am ready._
I will spare you, if you pay me. Well.
_What? You play both against each other? You would take two payments for the same task? How rude!_ She sighs and smiles wearily. _But understandable. Even admirable, in its way._
She makes a motion with her hand. A moment later, she holds a pair of gemstones. She hands them to you. _In return for your ... kindness. Now let us speak of this ugly business no more._
I took this job. I will complete it. (Attack.)

_I am so sorry to hear that. And we could have been such valuable allies. Ah, well ..._ As you advance toward her throne, she waves a hand, In an instant, she is gone. And her stone guardians begin to lumber toward you ...
When you put your foot on the first step, you suddenly feel very dizzy. The feeling of vertigo starts to overwhelm you, so you back away.
When you get close to this stone figure, it turns slowly to look at you. Its eyes glow a dim red. Then it turns back and is still. They don't seem to be able to talk.

Angevine crumples to the ground, a pitiful heap. The stone of the tower shudders under your feet. Cracks appear in the walls. For a moment, you think you are doomed, as the magic that holds the tower together starts to fade.
Then things quiet down. You feel a little dizzy, but the corridors and chambers stay intact. You can't be sure how long they will still exist, however.

Angevine is waiting for you in her living quarters. She gives you one of her playful winks, but you can see the loathing in her eyes. _So it is true. You are a murderer for hire, lackey of the fools who rule Kellemderiel?_
_Well, I have killed to defend myself before, when I fled my beloved homeland. And I will kill you now!_
The hooded man stands in the middle of the road, blocking your path. He doesn't draw his weapon, though. He inspects you carefully. _Yes. You are [N]. It is my purpose to know such things._
_I have been waiting for you. I need to speak with you. It will only take a moment of your time._
Are you from Avadon?
_No, though I deal with Hands and Eyes frequently. To some of them, I am a welcome visitor. As, I hope, I will be for you._
Get out of my way.

The man doesn't move. _I mean you no harm, I assure you. In fact, I offer you an opportunity. But I am persistent, and my work requires that I speak with you._ Apparently, unless you chop him down in the road, he is determined to speak.
I will speak with you, but make it quick.
_Of course. I will be brief. I have a unique opportunity for you._
All right. Let's talk.
He nods. _I would introduce myself, but I would prefer to keep my name private for now. For now, just think of me as the Wayfarer._
_I often contact Hands and Eyes of Avadon and offer them work. Easy tasks, great pay. The sort of thing only servants of Avadon can do. That only servants of Avadon are allowed to do._
And this is permitted?
_Of course. All is permitted to Hands of Avadon, as long as Redbeard approves. Or never hears of it._
_Why do you think there is such demand to work in a place that requires so much work and so much risk? It is the authority. The freedom. The power. And, from that, the wealth._
What can only servants of Avadon do?

_Whatever they want. It is the little secret of Avadon, the secret everyone knows. You are rewarded with the ability to use your influence for great reward. Now it is time for you to claim your reward._

_It is simple. Recently, a Holklandan named Ryozo came to Zhethron's Aerie. He wants something from the dragon. I need to find out what that is. Enter the caves, obtain this information, and deliver it to me._
Why can't you find this out?
_Because the dragon keeps all dealings between him and his supplicants secret. Thus, I require someone with influence, one who can wander the dragon's caves and investigate with discretion._
Why do you want to know?

You can't see the Wayfarer's expression, but he sounds amused. _I'm sure you realize that such things are closely guarded secrets. It is a small piece of information, and you will be paid well. That is all you need to know._
I won't do this.

He nods. _Fair enough. I will simply give this profitable task to one of your fellow Hands. I will go and let you spend more time risking your life for minimal pay. Then I will contact you again. Perhaps you will feel differently then._
Before you can give a stinging retort, The Wayfarer leaves. He walks down the road to the east.
I will do what you ask.

_I am pleased. It takes some Hands much longer to see wisdom._ He points to the north. _There is a barrel behind this spire. When you have learned what Ryozo wanted, write it down and leave it in the sand under the barrel. Once I have retrieved it, I will leave your reward._
_Now I must depart. I have much to do and far to travel. Excuse me._ Before you can ask any more questions, The Wayfarer leaves. He walks down the road to the east.
There is an old, weather-beaten barrel behind the stone spire.
You look inside it. It's empty.
You can leave the message to the Wayfarer here if you want.
You look under it. There is a leather pouch. You take it and look inside. There is a ring and two gemstones.
Don't leave the message.
You leave.
Leave the message.
You slide the message under the barrel.
Nightshade
Nightshade howls for help!
Incarnus
Walking Fire
Talking: Zhethron roars, 'Kill the ogres!'
Fyrassa
The magma pool to the north is starting to bubble menacingly.
The magma pool to the north sprays out lava!
The pool to the southeast is starting to bubble menacingly.
The magma pool to the southeast sprays out lava!
The pool to the southwest is starting to bubble menacingly.
The magma pool to the southwest sprays out lava!
calls several salamanders out of the lava.
doesn't want to talk until the valley is reclaimed.
Crypt Specter
commands some bones to awaken.
Watcher Harissa
Aerie Guard
Aerie Worker
Teria
Commander Ryozo
Keeper Ilhan
Shaman Thrale
Zhethron
Keeper Thara
Scaled Thrasher
Fire Lizard
Stone Guardian
Slime Lizard
Raider Thrat
Slime Lizard Hunter
Vicious Salamander
Cursed Imp
Warped Imp
Unbelievable.
They came right in.
We need more help.
Will you kill them?
Wretches!
Need more cows!
Fix that fence!
Need more help.
So much trash.
Gates are secure.
I need more soldiers.
I am losing scouts.
The dragon will see you.
Leave me.
I need privacy.
Always so hot.
No help for us.
Obstinate creature.
It never listens.
We need your help.
The Pact is failing us.
Hrrrr.
Hssssss.
Ahrrrr.
Ahssssss.
I am the mighty Fyrassa.
I am Zhethron's partner.
This is my cave.
Do you bring me tribute?
I have been found.
I desire privacy.
I won't tolerate it!
You have no choice.
They can't even secure the gate!
You must be patient.
Pfaugh! Leave me!
I have called for you. I ...
What!?
The sign says - GUEST QUARTERS.
The sign says - Aerie Workshops.
The sign says - Warning! Lizards are not tame!
The sign says - PACT RECORDS.
You look through the shelves, but you don't find Seeker Azarni's book.

You walk into the cavernous halls of Zhethron's Aerie, home to this region's most powerful and cooperative dragon. His lair must be set on top of a volcanic vent. The stifling heat within is enough to instantly make you miss the desert outside.

There are piles of crates, supplies, and gifts all around you. Keeping the dragon happy means a constant stream of food and other creature comforts, and earning his help requires a bribe of great magnitude.

Not surprisingly, things don't seem to be under control here. There are no guards posted. Looking to the northwest, you can see several people cowering in a storeroom. And, to the south, above the sounds of rumbling and hissing, you can hear the cackle of wretches.

The corridor opens up into a small valley. The ceiling opens up, revealing the clear sky. The sun is beating down on you again, but fresh air is a great relief after the sulfurous stink of the dragon's caves.
There are several pens, each full of cows awaiting their dinner engagement with the dragon. Some of the humans that work here have also planted some modest crops by the pool to the south.

However, no people are visible here now. The wretches have overrun the area. They are looting the boxes, chasing the cows, and being an incredible nuisance. It is shameful that the warriors here have allowed themselves to lose control like this. Someone will have to answer for it.
The dragon Zhethron has accumulated an enormous library. Shelves of books stretch into the shadows, dimly illuminated by the river of magma to the north.

The tomes and scrolls are covered with a thick layer of ash. Few of them show signs of having been read. Zhethron charges handsomely for access to his collection, but he has no interest in consulting or maintaining it himself.
Behind you, the floor is etched with a web of enchanted runes. For decoration? Theft-prevention? You aren't sure.

This is an enormous hall of records, where all human interactions with the dragon have been noted and stored away. These records are kept by Avadon. The dragon himself doesn't care about humans enough to remember dealing with them.
Zhethron has only been here a few decades, and yet the piles of records and transcripts are enormous. The pleas for his aid must be constant.

At last, you enter Zhethron's chamber. It is an enormous cavern, strewn with debris. It is divided into several sections by slow-moving streams of magma, which keep the cavern at a nice, constant level of excruciating heat.

On a basalt spire in the middle of the cavern, you can see the dragon himself, arguing with a human. Zhethron is smaller than you expected, but, even from here, you can sense the power that radiates off of him.

Zhethron is a dragon. These creatures, more than any other, are infused with raw magical power. They are arrogant, greedy, long-lived, and extremely dangerous. But even they must bow to the power of the Pact. Their days of raiding your colonies are over. Now they gain wealth by exchanging it for power and knowledge.
Normally, it's a smooth and simple operation, but now, judging by how furious the dragon is, things have gone very wrong. And thus they sent you ...
These back corridors are slightly cooler, but an animal reek is heavy in the air. You can hear the hisses of lizards and the echoing sound of claws scrabbling over stone floors.
It must amuse Zhethron to keep a lounge of vicious lizards around, to pester the humans and to serve as pets. And occasionally food.
You step out into a huge, spectacular caldera. This is the source of the raging heat that fills these caves. You won't be able to stay here for long. The heat is devastating.
You can dimly see spires of rock emerging from the magma. Each has a chest sitting on top of it. Zhethron has found a marvelously secure way to protect his valuables.
An extensive set of tunnels runs under Zhethron's lair. It is far hotter and muggier down here, and the ground is covered with discarded scales and claw marks.
Humans once came down here to try to build more quarters and workshops, but the effort didn't last long. The ruins and discarded tools are still visible. Down here, you are on your own.
As you get closer to the ruin to the south, the air suddenly develops a slight chill. You shiver.
The structure ahead is old, far older than the rest of the complex. There are no scales or tracks here. The lizards avoid this place. Adventurers are probably not so cautious.
LAIR OF ZHETHRON
Deliver all tributes here.
Supplicant Records - North
Dragon's Lair - West
Guest Quarters - West
ZHETHRON'S CHAMBER
ZHETHRON'S LIBRARY
No withdrawals.
Caution! Lower tunnels are not secured! Proceed with caution! Wear proper headgear!
The writing on this sign has mostly worn away. What remains says:
Stop! This ... bones ... devouring ... forever! ... undying horror.
Sounds fun!
Records Hall - South
Warning! Defenders are active! Use main entrance!

You flip through the records on this pedestal. They are accounts of recent meetings between envoys and Zhethron. Who came. What they wanted. What they offered. The dragon's response (which was usually 'no').
The amounts offered were quite lavish and the desires were evenly split between requests for information and aid in destroying someone or other. Zhethron was much more likely to provide information.
Interesting. A recent request came from someone named _Commander Ryozo._ Apparently, he believes that someone in the Tawon Empire, one of the Farlands, is plotting against the Pact.
He offered a considerable amount of gold if Zhethron would fly over parts of the Tawon Empire and report what he saw. The offer was denied.
You grab a pen and sheet of parchment and write this information down. You can decide what to do with it later.
LAIR OF FYRASSA
No non-dragons may enter!

You search through the papers in this desk. They are the letters and notes of a Holklandan Commander named Ryozo. Though these are private notes, being a Hand of Avadon, you have every right to look through them.
However, you find nothing but some supply ledgers and personal correspondence. Nothing about Ryozo's plans or reasons for coming here.
At first, you find nothing but supply ledgers and personal correspondence. Then you find a false bottom in one of the drawers. Underneath it, you discover several letters.

They appear to be from the Tawon Empire, one of the northern Farlands. The letters indicate that Ryozo has, in return for generous payments, agreed to try on their behalf to convince Zhethron to leave the Pact and go north. Interesting. You keep the papers.
You find nothing else of interest.
When you step over these runes, you feel slightly dizzy. When you recover, you realize that your pack feels lighter.
You look inside and, sure enough, Ahmed's Libram is gone. This library has elaborate, magical anti-theft measures.
When you open this chest, a cloud of dust flies into the air. It is full of old journals. Some are diaries. Some describe long journeys of exploration. And some describe magical research.
You look through them briefly, but you don't find anything of value. You close the box.
You look through them briefly, and, before long, you find a leather-bound journal. A note inside the front cover indicates that it belonged to, _Ahmed, Seeker of Truth._
Take the book.
Bracing yourself for traps, you gingerly pick up the book and put it into your pack. Nothing happens. Phew! You close the box.
Close the box.
This might not be the right time to steal from the dragon. You close the box.
This thick book is a catalog of the holdings of the library, written in a cramped, illegible script and organized in the least convenient way possible.
Only a few minutes of flipping through the catalog gives you a splitting headache. You close it again.

You look through the catalog for anything related to the ritual Seeker Azarni was hunting for. Eventually, when you are about to give up, you find something. The library has a book called 'The Focus of the Holklandan Spellcrafter.' Interesting.
The book is listed as being on one of the northern bookshelves, but it is not clear which one.
You look through the shelves and find, shoved behind a pile of scrolls, 'The Focus of the Holklandan Spellcrafter.' You sit down with it.
The pages are stained and hard to read, but you don't have to read it for long.

Early on, you find the following passage: _Though the Sixth Ritual of Inner Vision is lost, if indeed it ever existed, the first five rituals are an invaluable tool and worthy of study. This book describes them in extreme detail, so that ..._ and so on.
You replace the book. You doubt that Azarni will find what she seeks here, and she won't welcome the news.
It looks like most of the human staff of the dragon's lair is hiding in this cavern. Some of them have been wounded, probably when trying to fend off the wretch invasion.
When you enter, a Watcher, the commander of the soldiers here, walks up to you. She looks understandably agitated. _You must be [N]. At last! Someone has finally come to help us!_
_I am Watcher Harissa, of The Kva. The wretches have overrun the outer valley, and I don't have enough soldiers left to drive them out. You need to help us!_
Watcher Harissa looks at you impatiently. _Well? The wretches? Are they gone yet?_
Did you know I was coming?
_Yes. Avadon sent word days ago that you were coming. Unless it's a surprise inspection, they always let us know that Hands are coming. So we can be prepared._
_Not that it helped this time._
There is something I need to know.
_And there will be time to talk later! For now, we need to drive those wretches out before Zhethron starts roaring for his daily cow. The creature is in a bad enough mood already._
What do you need from me?
_This morning, we were attacked by wretches. There must have been a hundred of them. They ran right in through the gate! Couldn't believe it! We killed about half of them and then retreated._
_We were preparing to attack them again, but then you showed up. It's about time Avadon came to help us._
You couldn't fight off the wretches yourself?
_There were a lot of them._ She shoots a nasty look at a man sitting by the cave wall. _And Keeper Ilhan had me send most of my soldiers out to hunt the things. To keep the dragon happy._
_We never thought they would dare attack us here._
You can't get rid of wretches? But there's a dragon here!
She snorts. _That beast? When they came in, he closed the gates and said that it was our job to deal with them. If you don't have a chest of gold, the dragon won't lift a claw for you._
I'd love to help, but I'm very busy. I'll just go in to see the dragon.
Harissa laughs harshly. _Well, I don't know how you will do that. The gate to the dragon is locked. But I would be happy to open it for you. As soon as the wretches are dead._
She points to the south. _They're that way._ She turns to tend to a wounded soldier.
I'll solve your problem.
She nods. _I appreciate it, and, as soon as I can get in there, I'll unlock the gate to the dragon for you._
The wretches are gone.
You immediately have everyone's attention. _It's clear? We can go back in? Thank you, Hand of Avadon._
_Once inside, I'll unlock the doors to the dragon's gatehouse. Good luck with that creature. And come talk to me later. I have paying work, if you're interested._
She gives you a nod and starts rousing everyone. Soon, they are on their feet, ready to reclaim the lair.

There is a mix of soldiers, envoys, and dragon tenders sitting around this cave, bruised, humiliated, and miserable. They are waiting patiently for someone to get rid of the wretches so that they can reclaim their home.
As you try to talk to them, they point at Watcher Harissa, who is standing just inside the cavern. _She is in charge until the wretches are gone._

This man introduces himself as Keeper Ilhan. He sits in the corner, humiliated and furious. _I am in charge of the chambers outside the dragon's lair. Or I would be, if our Watcher hadn't been so careless as to lose control. To wretches!_

_I can help you when we have control of the outer valley. Until then, perhaps your time should be spent tending to the wretches._ He points at a woman watching you nearby. _When they are dead, report to Watcher Harissa._
He returns to what he was doing before: sitting there, quiet and miserable.

There are a handful of warriors of the Pact on duty now, a sadly inadequate force to defend against any sort of attack. You have a brief, half-hearted conversation with them. Between the heat and the low morale, they have very little to say.

There are several Kva workers here, put in charge of getting food to the dragon in a timely manner and cleaning away the mess when the creature is done. The presence of a Hand makes them nervous. When you approach, they get very quiet until you go away.
You meet another unfortunate unit of dragon food. Zhethron seems to have developed a taste for fresh, delicious bovinity.

You meet Watcher Harissa again. She seems very relived to be back guarding the dragon's gate. _Ah ... [N]. As you can see, we're back in, thanks to you. We could have retaken the caves ourselves, I'm sure, but only with losses._
_I know Hands, like dragons, offer their services for a fee. I could use your help. As you saw, we don't have the soldiers we need to keep these lands safe._
Watcher Harissa says, _Is there anything else you need?_ She pats the bow on her shoulder. _I'm ready to fight, but it's good to have other warriors around._
Tell me about the forces under your control.
_I have three blades here under my command. That's thirty fine Kva soldiers, well-trained, all tasked to protect the dragon. But not enough._
_And things are getting worse every day._
Protect the dragon? Does it need protecting?
_Not really. It insists on the soldiers though, as tribute. And we kill the pests the dragon can't be bothered to hunt._
_Wretches can't hurt that beast, but they can slay the envoys. And the envoys are important people. Or at least they think they are._
Where are your soldiers?

_Out scouting the wilds and hunting wretches. The Pact army hasn't been doing it. Avadon hasn't either. So Keeper Ilhan pesters me. Makes me send my warriors out with no regard for their safety. And not all are coming back._
_And it is getting worse all the time. Now it's not just wretches, but ogres as well._
_And it is getting worse all the time. Now it's not just wretches, but ogres and titans. We are skilled and well-armed, but we can't fight titans!_
How are things getting worse?

_Ogres are moving in. Wretches are pests, but ogres are dangerous. They even snuck in somehow and attacked the dragon! Zhethron is furious! We can't hunt down ogres without help from outside. I hope you have come to kill them, because we are spread too thin as it is._
Why are so many ogres coming here?
_I have my ideas, but I'm keeping my mouth shut. Not until I learn more._
_Titans! We can't fight titans. And we just saw that not even Zhethron can handle titans when they come in large numbers. But what are titans doing here? Their lands are a long march to the west._
What do you think is happening?
_The only explanation I can think of is invasion. Or preparations for one. I hope Avadon is aware. The Pact seems to be asleep._
How is the dragon doing?
_Angry, and getting angrier every day. I don't want to say more. I stay as far from that beast as I can._ She grins evilly. _You can go see him. That is your job._

She looks genuinely disturbed. _Wounded. He went to hunt titans, and, from what I hear, they threw hundreds of rocks at him. Almost knocked him from the sky. Hundreds of years thinking he can never die, and then ..._ She shakes her head.
_This is getting to be very bad._
Why is the dragon so angry?

_Because wretches keep sneaking into its lair. Some slip in through the gate. Others burrow tunnels. Now they are attacking blatantly. It doesn't threaten Zhethron, of course, but he sees it as an insult._
_If dragons have anything, it is pride._
_Happily, there have been a lot fewer wretches underfoot recently. Some of us are even getting sleep now._
_Somehow, ogres burrowed into its lair. They attacked it in its home. Zhethron slew them easily, of course, but he is furious. Understandably, I think._
_Why should it respect the Pact if we can't even keep a handful of ogres at bay?_
How bad are its injuries?
_Broken bones, a damaged wing. It will recover soon. But the current arrangement? Its respect for the Pact? Working for us instead of hunting us? That may not recover._
_We do not want a dragon as an enemy, but, if we can't prove our strength, we may have one soon._
You are in need of my help?
_I am. Well, not me. My men. I have had to send them out on patrols and raids, trying to hold back the wretches. Some have not returned._

_If you go to attack the Hegra clan, I sent four warriors there not long ago. They have not returned, and I can't risk more to hunt them. Not with the raids coming to our own gate. If you let me know what happened to them, you will be compensated._
You would pay me for this service?
_Hands of Avadon have only ever helped us lowly soldiers for pay. Sometimes, they are generous and ask little, but, other times ... It is the way of things. I must accept it._
What will my reward be?
_We have some workshops and barracks that have fallen into disuse. They still contain valuable supplies. I can unlock them and let you take whatever you need._
Tell me more about them.
_As I said, there are four of them. A small scouting party, though they wouldn't mind killing a few wretches if a good chance came._
