_They are led by a woman named Ayse. My cousin, and as skilled a scout as ever roamed the thickets. I do not think they are dead, but they might need help. And I want news._ She smiles sadly. _My uncle would be furious if he found that I sent Ayse into danger without looking after her._
I met three of your soldiers in the Jhereth Deeps.

You tell her how you met Ayse and two others. She grows more furious with every passing moment. _But Yevner is lost? The wretches have him? And they are doing ... Who knows what? And I can't rescue him. I don't have the men._ She smacks a gloved hand into the wall.
Then she turns back to you, a wild look in her eyes. _I said the reward was for all four of them. Find out what happened to Yevner too. I can't leave him in wretch hands._
All of your soldiers in the Hegra lands are accounted for.
You tell her the full story of meeting Ayse and of Yevner.
She nods, pleased. _Yevner is alive, but I sent him back to Goldcrag. It will take some time for him to recover from his ordeal. You have done us a great kindness._
_Yevner was a good soldier. I'm sure you did all you could for him, and he has been avenged. Thank you for that._
_I will unlock the southern barracks for you. Please take anything you need from there. And, in time, I might need more help from you. Please, if you can, come see me later._
You have more work for me?
_Not yet, but I'm sure I will soon. As long as there are more invaders in the hills, not less, I will need your aid._
I am ready to do more work for you.

Watcher Harissa seems disturbed. _I am glad, because, once again, I need you to check on one of my scouting parties. I sent them to the Jhereth Deeps. Some miners said they saw ogres there, so I sent them to investigate._
_That was some days ago. I haven't heard from them since. Should you go there, please watch for them and aid them if they need it._
You lose a lot of scouting parties?
_No, actually, I have lost no scouting parties. Ever. That is because I send help for them when they need it._
You don't have soldiers of your own to send?
_No. We have too much to do and far too few warriors. But we are fighters of The Kva. We will do whatever we need to do to prevail._
I met your soldiers. They were trapped by some ogres.
Harissa listens attentively as you tell her the tale of what happened.

_And none survived?_ she asks. You shake your head. _This is the first such group I have lost. I wish you could have done better. I will unlock a workshop for you. It might not be what you deserve, but it is what I promised._
_There were losses, but some survived. I thank you. Without your help, all would have been lost. I will unlock a workshop for you. Take what you need._
_You rescued all of them. I am most grateful. That was bravely done. I will unlock a workshop for you. Take what you need. Also ..._ She gives you a glittering gemstone. _An extra reward for you._
_And, in time, I might need more help from you. Please, if you survive, come see me later._
Do you have more work for me?
_I do. All of my soldiers are safe, happily. Until I get reinforcements or direct orders, I am keeping them close. This is a simple hunt, for bounty._
_There are titans in the hills. Some are new arrivals, but one has been here for some time. A vicious old creature named Splinterbone. It is time for him to die. Slay him, and I will pay you well._
He has been here for some time?
_Yes, years, in a cave out in the hills. Until now, he lived alone, hunting game and wretches. He was scared enough to behave. That was then._
Why hunt him now?
_Because, after years of good behavior, the presence of other titans has made him bold. We have seen him stalking our patrols. Soon, he will attack._
Where can I find him?
_I have heard rumors that you will soon go to attack the titan stronghold. Splinterbone stays close to them, in a cave nearby. They don't take him in, but they don't drive him off either._
_You might encounter him as you scout the titans' keep. Or he might hunt you._
Splinterbone is dead.

You tell Harissa of the titan's death. _Unfortunate, but this was probably inevitable. The moment the Pact seemed weak, one foe after another began to emerge, ready to hunt us. This is the penalty for our confusion._
_I will have another workshop unlocked for you. Take what you need, with my gratitude._
I'd like to talk to you about Ryozo.
_Ah, the Holklandan, yes? Came to the dragon for something. Angry. About to leave. Arrogant, but that's not unusual for an envoy._
_What about him?_
I have evidence that he is a traitor. These papers were in his chambers. (Give the papers.)

Watcher Harissa takes the papers and inspects them. She seems stunned. _I never would have expected this. Letters to the Tawon Empire? Attempting to seduce the dragon away from us? This is ... It seems strange. But these papers ..._

_I will have Ryozo arrested immediately. He will be sent to Avadon, or submitted to the justice of the Stone Code. Either way, he will threaten us no longer. Excuse me._ She walks to a nearby guard and begins to whisper orders.
Nothing. It is not important. (Get rid of the papers.)
Watcher Harissa seems confused, but she says nothing. _All right. Good day._ You take the papers away and discreetly dispose of them.
As you walk toward the dragon's lair, Sevilin laughs.

_Oh, it is just strange. My homeland has dragons. They can ignore our laws, and that bothers me, but ... To meet one. To have heard tales of them in childhood. To dream of them, of fighting them, of their treasure ..._
_Now I am meeting one. It is strange, but ... uplifting? I don't know how else to say it._
Jenell says, _I understand. We shamans are attuned to the beasts of the wild, and a dragon ... it is the mightiest of beasts. I feel unworthy, somehow._
Shima notes the piles of supplies with amusement. _So much expense and effort to hire a dragon. It is a strange thing._
Do Holklandans think that is honorable?
_Honorable? No, but having a dragon ally brings great prestige, which is just as good. This Ryozo ... If he succeeds in hiring a dragon, it will lead to great elevation for him._
_Politics,_ Jenell says with distaste.
_Yes,_ Shima responds. _An ugly, ugly business._
You don't approve?
He lets out a pained sigh. _If my family were able to buy the support of a dragon, my life would be very different. But we were not wealthy, and ..._ He shakes his head.
Nathalie looks at him with interest. _Holklandan politics. Like in Kellemderiel. Vicious and bloody. But far more crude._
Shima doesn't respond.
Jenell stops walking. She seems slightly dizzy. _I am sorry. The heat. The caverns. It is not what I trained for._
Nathalie, who is barely sweating, says, _You should seek out difficult territory. Spend time there. Grow used to it. Then you will always be prepared. That is what I do._
Jenell says, _I don't doubt it._
We can wait a moment.
Jenell shakes her head, sweat pouring down her face. _That is kind, but keep walking. I will not slow you down._
Sevilin offers a hand to steady her. Irritated, she shakes him off.
Shima offers a hand to steady her. Irritated, she shakes him off.
Hurry up, will you?
Jenell nods, sweat pouring down her face. _Just keep walking. You won't lose me._
Nathalie stops for a moment. She stares at the dragon, a faint smile on her face. _Look at it. Imagine what it must be like in battle? What weaknesses do you think it has?_
Sevilin smiles knowingly. _I know. You want to fight it. Calm yourself. It is an ally._
Shima shakes his head. _It is not part of our task. Don't distract yourself, not until Redbeard tells us to go dragon hunting. Anyway, it is an ally._
Jenell looks slightly disgusted. _How can you fantasize about striking down such a fantastic beast? Anyway, it is our ally._

Nathalie shrugs. _Read your history. A creature like that can never be our ally. Zhethron hunted humans for game in the Black Age. We grew weak, and it stalked us. Useful, perhaps, but no ally._ She starts walking again.

There is an old wizened man walking in the clearing, shouting orders, inspecting the damage and occasionally repairing a bit of fence or gathering up some trash. When you get close, he turns and bows to you.

_Greetings, [N]. I am Keeper Ilhan,_ he says, _master of the outer valley. This is a precarious time for us, and for our relations with the dragon. We are overwhelmed, and the help you are giving us is most welcome._
Keeper Ilhan continues to walk around the valley, a frenzy of activity and shouted orders. He takes the debris and disarray left behind by the repeated humanoid attacks as a deep personal insult.
_I have a vital job, not that it is appreciated. I am the master of this little valley. I make sure that the dragon's needs are properly filled, so that he does not grow angry._
_We also provide security. This has led to many an argument between me and Watcher Harissa._
Why aren't you appreciated?
_The warriors are in love with their weapons and themselves. The scribes work with paper instead of their hands so they think that makes them superior._
_But I keep the dragon happy. Without my work, there is nothing._
Tell me about Watcher Harissa.

_She loathes me, because I press her to do what is needed to keep the dragon content. She doesn't have enough warriors? Yes. Not enough weapons? Yes. But get her to do what must be done? Then she blames me._
_The disaster with the wretches is not my fault, whatever she says._
What are the dragon's needs?
_Well, there are the basics. Fresh water. Cleaning. And a cow a day. And, if there are any delays, the creature grows angry._
Is that all the dragon wants?
_Also, security. Flattery. Groveling. That is what it takes to get it to live here in peace. For Zhethron to actually help us? That requires much more lavish tribute._
Why doesn't it hunt its own food?
_Because dragons are arrogant. It feels that being fed is a tribute it is due. Plus, Zhethron seems to have developed a taste for cow._
Can you tell me about the dragon?

He shrugs. _I know as little as I can. I am told its needs, and I provide them. Otherwise, I keep as far away from the creature as I can. That is the wisest course, I think, when dealing with dragons._
_All I know is that it must be kept happy. And we are failing at it._
Why must it be kept happy?
_Because otherwise it will not respect the Pact. And then it will hunt our people, instead of helping them._
_And I fear that it will turn on us any day now, unless something is done._
How does the dragon feel now?
_Furious. Insulted. Humanoids have attacked it, and in its own lair! Still, as long as it feels safe, I think it will be content._

_From what I hear, after the fight with the titans, Zhethron is feeling something it has never felt before. Fear. Its own mortality. That makes the creature unpredictable. And that will be very bad for the Pact, unless something is done._
_Alas, I do. There are some pests that Zhethron allows in his lair, because they amuse him. And sometimes those pests attack our cows, or our people. Then we must rid ourselves of them._
_There is a small infestation of fire lizards in the northern tunnels. If you were to kill them, I could give you a few stray bits of dragon tribute I kept to myself for this purpose._
I am too busy for that.
_Ahhh. Not surprising. Well, I will just tell my workers to be more careful._
_I am pleased. Kill a half-dozen of the fire lizards, and that will reduce their numbers enough. You can reach their tunnels through the back of Zhethron's lair._
_I will speak with Keeper Thara and make sure that the gate to their tunnels is unlocked._
I got rid of your fire lizards.

_I thought I have been hearing less screaming. I am happy that it was not my imagination._ He fetches a pouch of coins and a fine cloak of drakeskin. _Here is a bit of genuine dragon tribute, set aside to hire aid for us._
_I thank you. Perhaps, if you visit me later, I can offer a new bounty._
Anything else you need killed?
He inspects you and thinks about it. _I would not have Avadon thinking I delivered one of their Hands to an untimely death. Perhaps return when you have more experience._

He smirks. He seems to be genuinely enjoying this. _A few years ago, Zhethron, in a moment of unusual generosity, allowed a drake named Fyrassa to take up residence in the low caves. The creature amused the dragon once. No longer._
_Fyrassa has taken to emerging and pestering us. I will have the gate to his tunnels unlocked. Please go downstairs and deliver the message that the drake must leave._
Zhethron won't mind?
_Zhethron has forgotten all about the drake. It is his way._
What if the drake won't leave peacefully?
_Then evict it. By force, if necessary. Oh, I do wish I could be there to see it._
Fyrassa is dead.
Ilhan makes a show of mock sympathy. _Oh? That arrogant, thuggish creature met an untimely end? How very, very sad._ He fetches a pouch of coins and a fine belt of drakeskin.
_I am most grateful, and hope certain other pests see Fyrassa as an example. Thank you._
There is a Holklandan man sitting alone in this chamber. He is reading next to a dark fireplace. You aren't sure why the Pact built fireplaces in these quarters. Maybe it was cooler once.
The man looks up at you, but he doesn't rise. He is noticeably tense. He says, _Greetings, Hand of Avadon. I am Commander Ryozo. Excuse me if I don't rise. I prefer to be alone._
If he is a Commander, that means that he leads a Force, a full thousand soldiers. He must have some influence in Holklanda.
Commander Ryozo continues to read his scroll, holding it in a way that you can't see it. He is doing a good job of concealing it, but he is definitely nervous.
_I am,_ he says, without looking up from his scroll.
Can you tell me anything about it?
He doesn't look up. _As I said, I am too busy to talk._
_All I can tell you about Holklanda is that we know enough to be rid of those without honor._ He doesn't elaborate, but Shima takes a step back.
You are here to see the dragon?
_There is no other reason to come to this miserable place._
He says, calmly, _That is private. A foolish thing to ask to an envoy of his people. Go away. I will not say another word._ And he doesn't.
You want the dragon to spy on the Tawon Empire?
His fists clench, crumpling the scroll. He looks up at you, furious. _That is private. That knowledge is private. I know. You are a Hand, [N]. You have the right. But I ..._
He makes a disgusted noise and turns away.
I want to know something else.
_I'm sure you do. Go ask someone else. I would be alone._ And he turns away.
I found these papers in your quarters. (Show them.)

Ryozo looks confused. He takes the papers and reads them. He looks up at you, stunned. He is arrogant no longer. He looks confused and terrified. _I ... I ... Where did you get these? Who placed ... I have never seen ... But you are a Hand. You can have me killed for no reason._
You deny that they are yours?
_I live for the Pact! I would never betray it! And in so clumsy a fashion? It is pure foolishness!_
That is exactly the response I would expect from a traitor.
Ryozo starts to open his mouth, but then he decides to remain silent. He looks at you with pure loathing.
I suspect that they are fake.
_Of course they are! I live for the Pact! I would never betray it! And in so clumsy a fashion? It is pure foolishness!_
So now what happens?
_You are a Hand. You can do what you want, even inflict such an injustice. Leave me and do what you will. I will compose myself._
He hands the papers back and turns away, shuddering with anger. Or fear.
I'll be going.
_I am so disappointed to hear it._ He turns away.
I need to speak with you.
_Speaking with you is a good way to be falsely accused of treason. Leave me._ He turns away.

There is a woman of the Wyldrylm sitting at this table, looking warm, cooped up, and very uncomfortable. When she sees you, she nods. _The Hand, yes? [N]? The one who killed the wretches? I am grateful._
_I am Teria, of the southern tribes. Excuse me if I seem distracted. The heat is difficult for me._
Jenell smiles. _Agreed, sister._
Teria sits at the table, a bowl of water in front of her. She alternates between sipping it and dipping a towel in it and applying it to her forehead.
You are a long way from home.
_Indeed. The free roads made the journey easier. They give, as well as take away. I am still eager to return home._
She sighs. _And doubly so, now that titans have been seen on the roads._
You don't like the free roads?
_We of the Wyldrylm feel that they take our land. But that is not something to talk of when it is so warm._
She thinks about it. _To see the dragon. The reason why is a guarded secret around here. I don't really understand why, but I will follow custom and keep my privacy for now._
Can you tell me anything about the dragon?
_I have not yet seen mighty Zhethron, though I hear him roaring and complaining day and night. I will be in to see him soon, I hope._
_He is smaller than I thought he would be, and yet more powerful. I am not ashamed to admit that I was afraid. And he refused me._

_I offered gold and enchanted trinkets from our tribe. All we could afford, and then some. But the dragon did not want to travel all the way to our land, and his hunger for gold was greater than we could satisfy._
She thinks about it. _To see the dragon. The reason why is a guarded secret around here. I do not need to keep the secret longer, I think._
_I was trying to hire the dragon to help us fight another tribe of the Wyldrylm. Our neighboring tribe, that has stepped beyond honor in its hunger for our hunting grounds._
Jenell looks confused by this.
Is that common?
_No. It is very rare. Normally we fight our battles ourselves. But ..._
Jenell exclaims, _That is right! To bring a dragon to the Wyldrylm to settle a dispute with another tribe? It is unheard of!_
Teria responds, _It is unusual, sister, I know, but it is a fair response to the assassins they have hired._
_We have been grievously provoked. We respond as best we can._
Why is this tribe attacking you?
_Greed. Madness. A young chief that respects our traditions not at all. Such chieftains are rare, happily, but they are a disease._
Sevilin says, _This is why we follow The Stone Code. Then we are not at the mercy of such individuals._ Teria, unsurprisingly, does not appreciate this advice.
How has this tribe attacked you?
_They hired an assassin from the Farlands. Can you imagine! He killed five of us before he fled! Young warriors, two only just bonded, another a father!_
_And then we were denied revenge. Hands of Avadon learned of this affair, captured Spiridon, and took him away. But no other punishment befell the tribe that hired him._
Jenell seems as disgusted by this as Teria is. _That is Avadon's usual respect for our ways._
Spiridon? I have met him.
_And did he mention that he is a coward and an assassin? I imagine not._
Avadon took Spiridon away, you say?
_Yes._ An idea occurs to her. _And if you return there, find Spiridon, and cause him to suffer an ... accident, you could share in the wealth the dragon refused._
_Now please excuse me. I think I have said too much already._ You leave her alone.
Spiridon is dead.
_I am pleased, and my people will be too. I will return the news to them. And not ask any questions about how it happened._
She gives you a pouch of coins and a small charm. _The wealth and handiwork of my people, and you have earned it._
I will leave you be.
She nods. _I thank you for your company._
This young woman looks surprisingly calm for someone who just had a furious argument with a dragon while standing by a river of magma. She is still mildly irritated, though.

But then she sees you and favors you with a broad grin. _Zhethron is obnoxious, as usual, but I will give you a civilized greeting. I am Keeper Thara, assistant to the big lizard. And advisor, as the creature needs constant wisdom. It lacks its own, you see._
Zhethron roars, _Thara, need I remind you how sharp my hearing is?_ She smirks.
Keeper Thara says, _Do you need anything else? I am ever required to meet the needs of the dragon. Who can't look after itself._
What is your purpose here?
_I am the dragon's assistant. I show envoys in to see him. I relay his demands to the unfortunates outside. And I give him advice when he asks. Which is not often enough._
_You should ask him. Once he decides that you are of value to him, he will tell you ceaselessly of the might of dragons. And the tale of his life. And so on._

_But dragons are similar to humans. They want everything they can get, and they have enormously inflated opinions of their own value. And they are powerful enough to do much, but not all, so they hire others to do their dirty work._
Do you not fear the dragon?
She smiles. _Because it could kill me in an instant? Of course I fear him, in the way that you fear Redbeard, and any soldier fears his commander._
_And yet, I rest easy in my utter indispensability._
She looks at Zhethron wryly. _Who else will advise the dragon not to get himself killed by titans. Even though he ignored my wise advice.
Tell me about the envoys.
_Wealthy and arrogant officials from all over Lynaeus, who come here thinking a dragon is just another bauble to be purchased to show off to their rivals._
_They come with their bribes. Most of them are rejected, but he aids a fortunate few._
How does he decide who to help?
_Lots of gold helps. Magical artifacts. And, of course, he relies on my advice._
She winks. _So, if you ever come here trying to hire a dragon, don't be rude to the help._
What does the dragon demand?
_More cows. Fatter cows. Someone to clean up after him. The sort of things asked for by dragons, the lazy, and invalids._
Zhethron cries out, _I hear every word of this! I shall devour you the next time you return to me!_
She tilts her head, expecting a rejoinder from the dragon. The creature is silent. Thara looks worried.
Is that the response you expected?
_Yes. It is fortunate to me that I am so valuable to the creature._
She looks genuinely disturbed. _Zhethron is ... unwell. Since the battle with the titans ..._ She shakes her head.
You give the dragon advice?
_Yes. Zhethron is, like all of his kind, proud and arrogant. But he is also smart enough to realize that, when dealing with the Pact and Avadon, an occasional touch of humility and care is helpful._
_So he asked my advice. As a human, I almost understand other humans._
And what are you advising him to do?
_Be patient. I tell him to give the Pact time to send forces and beat back the wretches._

She lowers her voice. _But now that they have been joined by ogres? And the ogres are coming here? It is growing harder to keep the dragon calm. I hope that you are planning to send a proper force here soon. Otherwise, the Pact will lose a valuable ally._
And yet he fought the titans?
She looks furious. _I did everything but beg and try to hold him down! And yet he goes and tries to get himself killed! Dragons have great power, but it is not without limits!_
_You must do something about the titans, or the Pact will lose his goodwill. And that, in these troubled times ..._ She shakes her head.
How old is Zhethron?
_About five hundred years. He is in the prime of his life._
How arrogant are dragons?
_They are as arrogant as it is possible to be. However, they do realize that if they fought the Pact they could all still be hunted down and destroyed._
_Thus, all dragons either hide deep in the Farlands or emerge to trade with the Pact._
Is Zhethron hiring anyone now?

_No, but I am. I will give you samples from the dragon's hoard if some papers can be recovered for me. Three leather binders that were stolen by the wretches. Not all of the creatures stayed here to be killed. Some of them fled with my papers._
_It would be wise for me to get them back._
Why did they steal the papers?

_I am not sure. They are records of the requests envoys made of the dragon, and the responses, taken while they were being carried to storage. I don't know why the creatures would seek them and take them away._
_However, I do want them back, in part because the wretches wanted them so badly._
How well will I be paid?
She gives you an evil grin. _Oh, lavishly! Pounds of gold for your help!_ On his island, Zhethron furiously snorts out a gout of flame. _You can negotiate a better deal than that,_ he roars.
I found the stolen records. (Give them to her.)
She takes them and looks inside. _Hmmph. Not read. Not even opened. I wonder who wanted them, or why._
_I will tell the dragon to unlock one of his chests. Ignore his protests and help yourself._
Does the dragon require any more help?
_Not yet, but I'm sure he appreciates your concern._ She smiles.
_In fact, he does. We have learned that a new dragon has taken up residence near here. The interplay between dragons is very complicated, and Zhethron does not know how to regard his new neighbor._
_Thus, if you would drop by Zephyrine's lair and ask her future intentions, Zhethron would be most grateful. And pay you._
Ask her intentions? That is all?
_That is what Zhethron said. Though I would be very cautious. The interplay between dragons is extremely complicated, and we humans know very little of how it works._
I asked Zephyrine for her intentions. She attacked me. (Describe what happened.)
_Ah. I was afraid of that. Dragons tend to prove themselves with violence. Against each other, or their envoys. Another unpleasant job the creature leaves to us humans._
_Well, the rest is left to Zhethron. I will tell the dragon to unlock one of his chests. Ignore his protests and help yourself. You have definitely earned it._
You don't need to worry about Zephyrine's intentions. She's dead.
_Ah. Well, thank you for that information. I will have Zhethron unlock a ..._
_No!_ the dragon roars. _I will not pay a human for slaying one of my kind, no matter how much she deserved it._
Thara shrugs. _That is the end of it, then. My apologies._
I am interested in learning why Ryozo came here.

Keeper Thara looks instantly suspicious. She takes a step back. _That is private. Things like that are said in the dragon's confidence. I write it down and put it in storage, and only Hanvar's Council can see what is kept there. If they come personally._
Storage where?
She points to the east. _You passed those halls as you came in. Only I can enter there, and I will not for such a purpose. So please speak no more of it._

Trying to keep your trembling under control, you walk toward the dragon. The creature is there, standing on a basalt spire emerging from the lava. He is currently shouting at a young woman of The Kva. The force of his fury is literally blowing her hair back.
And yet, she doesn't seem to be afraid. You move closer to hear what they are arguing about.
You get close enough to listen in. Neither the dragon nor the small woman standing before him have noticed you. They are arguing about a lumpy pile of rags on the ground between them.

You approach the dragon once again. It is in its standard mood of barely controlled anger. You can see why ... There has been a fight here recently. The bloodstains have not yet been cleaned. Zhethron waves you forward ...
When you stand before Zhethron, he opens his mouth to speak. Then he is interrupted.
There is the sound of crumbling stone to the northwest. A wall crumbles. Then you hear loud, incoherent roars. A band of ogres charges through.
Zhethron roars, _Again! I am to be insulted again! Come, worms. You know you have no chance to defeat me._ The ogres attack.

Zhethron quivers with fury. For a moment, you think that he, in his bloodlust, will attack you. Instead, he breathes a mighty gout of flame toward the ceiling. _You see this? You see how thoroughly the Pact has failed me?_
_Come and speak with me, human. You see why I have called you to me. This must be stopped._
You return to the dragon's lair. It is different. The dragon is lying down, sullenly staring at the passing magma. It looks like it has been bandaged. You move closer to get a better view.
The dragon has, indeed, been injured. Huge splints have been strapped to his left wing and right forearm. He lies sullenly on his spire, and it takes him time to rouse himself.

Finally, he stands up and looks down at you, trying to regain some of his pride. _I sent for you, and you have come. As you can see, I have been attacked. This is a mortal insult. It must be answered._
_You see me injured, and you wish to speak only of your foolish human trivia. We will now speak about the one important thing here: Me!_
You have been injured.
_I was ambushed. Even a dragon can be scratched when the opposing numbers are too great._
Zhethron shifts painfully on his perch. _This is what respecting the Pact has led me to. My lands invaded by titans. In great numbers, large enough to hurt me. To hurt me!_
The dragon's rage is barely under control. _Oh, I will be avenged for this. All of the titans will die for this affront. And, if this is not done, the Pact will join in my vengeance. I promise it!_

The young woman says, _I will give you some time to calm down. Maybe a nice meal will help you to listen to reason._ She turns her back and storms off of the island. As she walks past you, she mutters, _Good luck._
Then Zhethron sees you. He rises up to his full height, and his eyes gleam with anger. _You!_ he rumbles. _You are here. You took your time! Who are you?_
I am [N]. I was sent by Avadon.
Zhethron waves his claw dismissively. _The word 'Avadon' does not scare me. I was hatched hundreds of years before your fort in the mountains was built. I sent for help._
_It has taken too long to arrive. But, now that you are here, I will have what I am owed._
I am [N]. I'm here to help. Please don't hurt me.

Zhethron nods. Your humble response calms it slightly. _I mean the Pact no harm, but I will have what was promised. It has taken too long to arrive. But, now that you are here, you will serve me, or there will be consequences._
I am [N], Hand of Avadon, and I expect to be treated with respect.
_It has taken too long to arrive. But, now that you are here, you will serve me, or there will be consequences._
What is it you need?

Zhethron casually spears the heap of rags in front of him with a claw and lifts it up. You realize that it isn't rags. It's a small dead wretch, hanging limply from the dragon's claw. Zhethron shakes the body at you. You note that it has a black 'X' painted on its jerkin.
_Look at this! The lands near my lair are infested with pests, and nothing is done. Now they invade my home! I will be rid of them._
Why don't you just eat the invaders?
_Because wretches are vile to the taste, and because hunting them is not my task! I was promised security, and I will have what I am owed._
You have had this problem for a while?
_Months!_ he roars, waving the dead wretch at you for emphasis. _I send envoy after envoy to the Pact for help, and I am ignored. I will not be ignored!_
And what do you want from me?

The dragon wrinkles his lip in disgust and drops the dead wretch to the ground. He points at the black 'X' on the creature's chest. _This mark shows that the creature is from their lair near here. The one the Pact has refused to remove._
_Destroy their lair. And then, if they are the ones who have been infesting my caverns, I will be content._
Are you sure the dead wretch was from that lair? Maybe it is a trick.
_Wretches are simple creatures. They are not capable of such subterfuge. And, if it is the wrong lair, I will send you to other lairs until the attacks on my home cease. That is what I am owed._
Where is this lair?

Zhethron describes to you how to reach it. (A new area has appeared on your world map.) _I have flown over it several times. You are not the first warrior of the Pact I have told where it is. And yet, nothing was done._
You want all of them killed?
_I want them to stop bothering me! But, considering how fast they breed and how fast they spread, great violence will probably be necessary._
He nods. _I expect it done quickly. The Pact is not giving me what I am owed, and my anger is growing. If our bargain is to continue, I will have this assistance. Go._ He waves you away.
You approach the dragon Zhethron. He seems annoyed. _Still here? Why are you not hunting wretches? And why are you wasting my time?_
There is something I want to know.
Zhethron snorts. _You want to learn of me? That is valuable knowledge, and conversation with me is not free. Aid me, and then I will speak with you. Not until then._
Tell me again what you want from me?
He points at the black 'X' on the dead wretch's chest. _This mark shows that the creature is from their lair near here. The one the Pact has refused to remove._
Never mind. (Leave.)
The dragon makes a grumbling sound and waves you away.

Zhethron is still curled up on his spire, basking in the heat and gnawing idly on cow bones. Although he seems relaxed, you can sense his power and see the tension in his muscles. It is never wise to lower one's guard around such a creature.

Zhethron is still curled up on his spire, basking in the heat and gnawing idly on cow bones. He is very tense, and, though he would pretend otherwise, his wounds are hurting. He sometimes mutters to himself, quiet and angry words.
_What do you need of me, Pact human?_
I have destroyed the wretches.

You tell Zhethron the whole tale. The dragon nods. _I believe you. The invasions have stopped. The pests have vanished. I no longer detect their vile scent. I am content, for now. You may send word to Avadon that I will be calm, as long as I am not attacked again._
_Since you have aided me, I will reward you. You have earned the right to speak with me. Briefly._
Speak with you? I was hoping for a real reward.

Zhethron's eyes flash with anger. _Avadon arrogance! Sages pay much to speak with me, and I owe you nothing! Your service was what you owed me! I will still talk to you, but do not try my patience by asking for more._
I was glad to help.
Zhethron nods. _Some sages pay much to speak with me. I hope you appreciate what I am giving, in return for only what I was owed._
Tell me about your life.

Zhethron nods slowly. _A popular topic. I enjoy speaking of my tale, and some sages and historians pay much to hear it. And yet, I will be brief. Suffice to say, I am older, much older than your Pact and your Avadon._
Why do historians pay so much?

_Because every land in Lynaeus wants to know its history. Human arrogance. And I saw much of that history with my own eyes, unclouded. Your fragile memories cannot compete with the living record that is every dragon._
_Like the Black Age. I remember the Black Age fondly._
What happened in the Black Age?

_The Pact fell apart in civil war. It was chaos everywhere. No order, no need to deal with humans. I could loot and feed at will. Oh, the lovely exposed villages, free of protection ..._ He shakes his head. _A happier, simpler time._
_Past a certain age, we dragons no longer bother with recalling mere numbers. I do know that over five hundred years have passed since my hatching._
Who raised you?
_My mother was a proud fire dragon named Racculia. I believe she still lives, though she will have seen her thousandth year by now. I honor her. Hopefully, the scars from our battle have faded._
You fought her?

_There comes a time when every young dragon is overcome with lust for its mother's hoard. Such greed compels us. It is nothing personal. Most mothers are then kind enough to only banish the young dragon, not devour it._
Zhethron flaps his injured wing slightly and winces with pain. _She would be disgusted to see what I allowed to happen to me. Because the Pact has betrayed me._
Tell me about the Pact.

_It is a durable and understandable arrangement, you humans have made. The Pact states are in the middle of Lynaeus, exposed. It is natural for them to band together, and Avadon wields the ruthlessness necessary to keep the Pact alive._
_The Pact will work well, until it dies._
The Pact will die?
_Everything dies. Humans, nations, even dragons. I have lived long enough to see how inevitable death is. I have seen enough to know your fate._
Which is?
_The Farlands despise you with all of their strength. They will try again and again to unseat you. They might even be attempting this now. To protect the Pact and our bargain, you must be wary._
Zhethron chuckles. _You can imagine how angry arrogant Pact envoys are when they pay sacks of gold to be told that._
_I can see it happening. You have lost control of your lands. Ogres and titans roam them freely. Your doom is coming. I feel it._
What is your arrangement with the Pact?
_I am one of the dragons who saw the need for change, to abandon the old ways for a time. Now I trade with the Pact, offering my strength and knowledge. The old way would only have brought death._
_And yet, when I am attacked in my own lair, what safety is the new way bringing me? I must think long on this._
What was the old way?
_The way of dragons has been to raid. To take what we want, build our hoards, and live proud in our lairs. Humans hate us, but they fear us._
_That time is past, for now, though it may rise again._
_That time was in the past, but I sense it is coming again, as the Pact loses control._
What happened to the dragons who didn't change?

_They were slain, or they fled. They wait in the wilds of the Titan Lands or The Corruption, patiently enduring until they can emerge and regain their true place: feeding upon the richness of humanity._
Zhethron sighs longingly. You have the uneasy suspicion that he harbors fantasies of pouncing, devouring you, and taking all your stuff.
You fear the Pact?
_I respect it. Dragons respect strength. If I angered the Pact or Avadon enough, they would kill me. Thus, I trade with them. Should the Pact become weak, I will rethink the arrangement._
_And know this. Now that I see how easily ogres and other creatures invade your lands, I am beginning to have doubts._
What do the envoys want from you?
_Knowledge. For me to fight on their behalf. And the prestige that comes from being allied with a dragon. In return, they pay, and pay well._
_More come for my aid than I could ever help. They recognize my wisdom and might._
You leave your lair to fight?
_At times, if the battle sounds interesting, and tribute is lavish, and I see the chance to gain much for my hoard. And to feed well._ Happily, he doesn't elaborate on that last point.
How do you decide who to help?
_Larger tributes. Work that increases my prestige. And, when I can't decide, I ask Keeper Thara. She is small and shrill, but her judgment is strong for one so frail._
Are there other jobs I can do for you?
The dragon snorts. _I do not pay for minor tasks. The humans here do that for me. If you have time to spare, spend it helping the Pact to regain control. They have grown weak and confused._
You have sent for me once again? I assume it involves the ogres.
Zhethron is absolutely livid. _You have just seen the second time they have attacked me. Twice, in my own lair! _
How did they get in?

_There are many tunnels under my lair. The wretches dug more, and the ogres finished them. The ogres burrowed through soft veins of lava rock into my lair. I have collapsed their tunnels, but I am sure there are more. Wretches are like rats._
_They must be destroyed at the source._
Why did they attack?

For a moment, Zhethron actually seems confused. _To slay me? To steal treasure? I don't know. Ogres are pathetic creatures. They must have known that they had no chance of avoiding or damaging me. All they achieved, before I slew them, was making me more angry._
_You will go to the Jhereth Deeps. You will find the ogres who did not come to attack me. You will kill them. All of them. Only this will calm my rage._
How do you know where they are?
_As soon as I knew that ogres were in these lands, I took to the sky. Ogres are large and clumsy. They were easy to spot, once I was in the right place. Still, it took three full days to find them._
_The ogres are in the Jhereth Deeps, a long day's march south of here. Though, if they are wise, they will be hiding from my wrath._ (The Jhereth Deeps are now marked on your world map.)
And you want them all dead?
_All of them, but especially their leader. No lesser punishment will do for the invasion of my lair._
I located the ogres. They have been destroyed.
Zhethron nods solemnly, but lavish rewards don't seem to be forthcoming. _Once again, the Pact has given me what I am owed, but far too late. Once again, I have no choice but to forgive the lapse._
_Also, a reward. You have proved yourself to be able. I will remember you. When I need help, I will be sure to ask for you personally._ This doesn't sound as great as Zhethron thinks it is.
I met a dragon named Zephyrine.
_A new dragon in the area. I suspected as much. I will contact her, but carefully. Relations between dragons can be complicated. And violent._
The ogres were being led by a human.
_Who is dead, yes?_ You confirm this. _That does not surprise me. That matches what has been happening. I see that now._ An odd thing to say, but the dragon doesn't elaborate.
Someone who called himself the Wayfarer contacted me. Again.
You describe him to the dragon. He doesn't seem interested. _That is human business. Not important to me._
I have nothing else to say.
_Then I dismiss you. I will return to enjoying a tranquil existence. For as long as it lasts._
I want to talk about the titans.
How did you find them?
_You think I lack my own servants, my own magic for watching my lands? You think anything as large and clumsy as a titan could be missed?_
_No, when their clan found their tunnels and settled in, I knew it. What is more, they knew I would know about it, and they prepared for me._
How did they injure you?
_I attacked in brave dragon fashion, swooping from the sky, breathing fire and raining magic upon them. And, be sure, many of them fell or were crippled for life._

_But they were expecting me! Titans were in hiding in their lair, too many of them. Volleys of spears and thrown rocks awaited me, and there were too many of them to fend off. And then they struck me on the wing with a lucky throw, and ..._ He stops speaking. _I will discuss it no longer._

_The titans must be destroyed. There was only one lair of them that I could find, but more will come if you do not show your strength. Happily, Thara has told me that the Pact is finally taking our problems seriously._
_Soldiers have already been sent there ahead of you, and I have demanded that you be put in command of them._
Can you tell me where the titans are?
Zhethron describes to you the path to reach the titan lair. (The area is now marked on your world map.) _Do not ask me to do any more scouting for your people. Not when I have been injured._
There are soldiers already there?
_There are many titans, so you will need help to defeat them. The forces sent there ahead of you should be found before you attack their lair._
_Learn from my error. They make themselves appear weak, but there are many of them._
The dragon looks at you, and you see something haunted in its eyes. A new and painful awareness of its own mortality. And then it passes.
_No. My arm pains me, and I will rest. Go and do this thing, before I grow more angry._
Do you need any more help?

Zhethron snorts. _If I do, I might send word. Or I might abandon this lair forever and return to the wilds, my arrangement with the Pact abandoned. This is no idle threat. The Pact is weak, and it has failed me._
_One more lapse, and I will have to act. Now go._ The dragon waves you away.
The titans have been destroyed.

You tell the tale to Zhethron, but the dragon takes no satisfaction in it. _So they are dead. A thousand deaths cannot pay me back for what they have done to me. I have been scarred! I was driven from the sky!_
_Go back to Avadon and report your success, and tell them of my great anger. They have failed me, and I will not forget it. Your only reward is my giving them one more chance. Go._ He waves you away.
I'd like to know something about the envoy Ryozo.
_You think I can tell one human from another? Ask Thara. She keeps the records._
I am looking for a fresh dragon tooth.
_Do not anger me. I never encourage anyone to hunt parts of the bodies of my kind. Not even scales. It leads to fortune hunters trying to slay us. You will not get a tooth here. Speak of it no more._
There is a new dragon in the area. Her name is Zephyrine.
_So I have learned. I must contact her, though it means a challenge, and ..._ He thinks. _I have asked Thara to deal with this. You should speak with her._
I have met Zephyrine on your behalf.
_So I heard. And you lived. That will please her. I will have to contact her again. On my own, of course. If she doesn't provoke the Pact into killing her._
There is a specter standing in the rear alcove of this crypt. It hovers in the air, the fading ghost of some long-dead lord. It doesn't seem to have noticed you. Or maybe it is ignoring you.
Hello? Can you speak?
Your words get his attention. His head swivels slowly toward you. His features grow more substantial, enough for you to tell that he is irritated by the disruption of his solitude.
He opens his mouth, and a long, hideous keening sound emerges. You hear a scraping sound come from the sarcophagi around you.

As you charge, his head swivels slowly toward you. His features grow more substantial, enough for you to tell that he is irritated by the disruption of his solitude. Turns out he was aware of your presence all along.
(Leave quietly.)
You back away slowly. The shade gives no indication that he knew of your presence.
In this remote cave, surrounded by pools of lava, you meet a drake. He looks like a smaller version of the dragon above, but with an even more arrogant attitude.
He looks annoyed by the intrusion. _Ahsss ... What are you doing in the lair of Fyrassa? I have not allowed you to come here, to my own private lair. You will go now._
The drake Fyrassa is still curled up in his lair, taking a long nap. He uncurls and looks at you, letting out a long hiss. _Did you not hear? This is my lair. Get out._
_The dragon Zhethron, recognizing my strength and wisdom, invited me here to aid him. I have taken these caves for my own. I stay here and rest, waiting to be called._
This is your cave? Not the dragon's?
_It is mine, a sign of respect for my strength and wisdom. I stay here, except for when I must go above and demand food from the humans. They do not treat me with the respect I deserve._
Fyrassa snorts. _A mere human, asking boons of me?_ He waves you away with a clawed hand. _I answer to the dragon, and only when I choose to._
I bring a message from the upper caves.
Fyrassa is suddenly interested. _You do? What boon am I to receive? More regular meals? Better caves? I have expected my due for some time. What will I receive?_
I'll just leave now.
Fyrassa nods and imperially waves you away.
Actually, you are being evicted.
Fyrassa lets out a snort of sulfurous smoke. _I do not believe it. If the dragon wanted me to leave, he would have come personally! Ahssss ... This is a trick._
He arches his back. _If you wish me to leave, you will have to force me._
I will force you.
Fyrassa nods solemnly. _I know why you came. Zhethron wanted to add to my hoard, so he sent your treasures to me. All I must do is relieve you of them._
He mutters a brief spell. The pools of magma surrounding you begin to bubble. Then he takes a deep breath ...
I'll just go then.
Fyrassa nods. _So I thought. Humans are frail and cowardly creatures._ He waves you away.
You are very surprised to find a scaly, red demon here. And he is surprised to have been found. He stands in front of a recently sacrificed wretch.
_What?_ he says. _Who has come to the shrine of the mighty Incarnus? A ... A human? You will leave me now. This is my cave._
The demon Incarnus watches you uncomfortably. _This is my lair. There is nothing for you here. You should leave._
_I was called by the dragon Zhethron. I aided him in works of magic when creating this place. And, when he released me, I stayed. It is better than where I came from._
_I enjoy the quiet. I come from a place of unending chaos and war. A few centuries of peace here is a valued rest._
I am a servant of Avadon and the Pact, and you will obey me.
_Avadon? The Pact? These words mean nothing to me. I only want to be left alone, to rest and to only occasionally feed on the spirits of the weak._
You are an infernal horror, and I will send you back where you came from. (Attack.)

Incarnus sighs. _I knew this day would come, but I will not submit!_ He mutters a spell. Two creatures of fire begin to form from the lava behind him. He stalks toward you. _You will not disturb my blessed rest!_
I'll just be going.
Incarnus nods. _That is wise. I would happily destroy and feed upon you if that is what it takes to continue my vacation. So go and leave me._
Incarnus decides that it is not worth the effort to stay here. You are powerful enough to cause him actual harm, a distasteful prospect to an immortal.

_Fine,_ he says. _This useless, miserable cavern is yours. Enjoy it._ He disappears in a cloud of sulfurous smoke. Something falls to the floor, left behind by his disappearance. It is a shield. The eccentric creature was wearing it as a breastplate.
Vahlfur imbibes a potion. His skin suddenly grows long, needlelike spines.
Vahlfur's spines have all broken off. His skin is back to its healthy, green shade.
Talking: The wretch snarls at you.
Firecaller Shaman
Fire Imp
Kva Scavenger
Talking: The mysterious woman runs away from you.
Onghror
Wretch Stalker
High Shaman Dvola
watches you silently.
Ayse
Kva Scout
Desert Thug
Sandy Firelizard
Leaping Lizard
Huge Mine Bat
Wretch Picker
Gkarl
Mine Rat
Vile Stinkrat
Yevner
Wretch Miner
Miner Bunger
Sonic Cavebat
Savage Pit Wolf
Young Hellhound
Shaman Greev
Shaman Wolfra
Shaman Bumblum
Shaman Incinerax
Low Chief Vahlfur
Temple Guardian
Chief Okai
Wretch Gate Guard
Trained Wolf
Shaman Blavith
Yevner follows you upstairs.
Help at last!
We've lost a man.
Can't stay out here much longer.
We can leave at last.
You hear another gate open.
You hear another gate open. You think that you might be able to escape.
No!
Let them go!
Aaah!
It's caving in!
Aaaahhh!
Aaaahh!
Aahhhhhh!
The dust on the floor has been disturbed. Someone ran through here recently.

You reach the valley that Zhethron told you about, where the wretches that have been pestering him supposedly originate. You arrive on an abandoned road, that is slowly being erased by the desert winds.
There are refuse and bones scattered along the road, and a crude wooden palisade is dimly visible across the river to the south. This seems like the right place.

Movement is visible to the west. You reflexively reach for your weapons, only to realize that it was a human waving at you. Several warriors are camped to the west. They aren't making any effort to hide themselves.
The palisade here is unguarded, letting you through to the field to the south. The open area is heaped with refuse.

There must have been a mine here once. There are rusting tracks and piles of rubble and ore. There are also smashed crates and more recent piles of garbage, the leavings of wretch raids on nearby caravans and towns.

The valley to the southwest is lined with totems, and you can hear the shrill cries of the wretches. There are two clear pathways coming out of the valley and crossing your route to the south. None of them are sitting out here in the blazing heat, but they do send out patrols looking for invaders. Like, say, you.
There is an old stone wall to the north, crumbling but still intact. This is one of this region's many abandoned mines, now infested with wretches.
The wall has had many holes knocked into it, and wretch archers watch you through the gaps. A barrage of arrows awaits you if you get closer.
The iron gate into the keep is closed. Entering this way would be extremely difficult.
As you slip through the palisade, someone walks out of the wretch valley to the south. You jump back, afraid that it is a patrol.
Then you realize that it is a human. A young woman in a leather jerkin, with a heavy bag slung over her shoulder. As you watch from behind the palisade, she walks quickly to the south.
It's hard to tell from this distance, but she seems upset. She might have just discovered the carnage you left behind.
The tracks on the ground here are a mix of wretch and lizard. A trap ahead recently exploded, turning several invading lizards into a cloud of pink, lizardy bits.
On the other side of the trap, you can see piles of crates and barrels. Someone has been slipping supplies into the wretch caverns through this remote tunnel.

You hear footsteps receding to the west, followed by a grim clang. Neray closed an old rusty gate behind her, blocking your pursuit. Even if you can get it open, by the time you do she will be long gone.

You enter the lower galleries of this abandoned mine. There used to be a lot of mining in this region, but most of the good claims were played out fifty years ago. There are still a few prospectors out in the wilds, but all of the big mines have been abandoned. And, in this case, infested by wretches.
This area is quiet and wet. Several of the passages have caved in. Some wretches have made a half-hearted attempt to dig out the rubble, but they don't have much of a work ethic.
Then you hear someone whisper in the darkness. You're not alone.
The corridor to the north is in much worse shape than the others. It is narrow and choked with rubble. The support posts are sagging alarmingly.
Too many vibrations might cause the whole thing to crumble. You suspect that you shouldn't proceed unless you are well-prepared.
This wheel controls the front gate to the wretch fortress. You turn it enough to open the gate and then smash the mechanism. You will be able to get in and out easily now.
The wheel mechanism is still smashed. The front gate is stuck in the open position.
The scouts here have had to defend themselves from quite a few wretches, a result of their being camped so openly. The bodies are piled nearby, waiting for vultures.

There are two other exhausted scouts sitting at the fire, sipping a thin lizard and cactus stew and maintaining their weapons. They are tough warriors of the desert. It would take a lot of wretches to bring them down.
One of them sees that you are looking at him. He says, _Talk to Ayse. She's the talker._
There are two grim thugs, tanned and leathery, sitting by the fire. They ignore you, probably planning robberies, muggings, stealing housepets, and other anti-social acts.
Neray is incredibly fast on her feet. You try to stop her, but she nimbly leaps around you. She pulls open a trap door and leaps nimbly down into the darkness.
You try to pull open the trapdoor, but it is securely locked.
One of the wretch hunters has spotted you. He raises his horn to his lips and lets out a loud, shrill alert.
This wheel's mechanism has been allowed to rust. No matter how hard you pull, it refuses to turn.
This sign probably once identified who owned this claim. The wind and sand have long since scoured the writing away.
There is a crude sign here. It says:
_STAY OWT BAD BAT BAD_
You suddenly hear a sound coming from either side of you. Iron picks, striking against stone walls. Dust starts to shake down from the ceiling.
And then, as you debate which way to run, the walls to either side of you crumble. The ambushing wretches charge in from both directions, screeching at you.

You hear a wolf howl to the north. And another. And another. The echoing sound rapidly becomes deafening in this tall cavern. Then the wretch wolfmaster gives a command to her charges, and they rush out of the corridor to the north.
Soon, they pick up your scent, and the hunt is on.
Wolfmaster Thya
You hear wretch howls. Jealous of the wolves, their masters run out after them, eager to join in your destruction.
As you watch the wretches fling themselves wholeheartedly into their suicidal charge, you can't help but admire their single-minded violence.
Jenell mutters, _Kind of reminds me of Nathalie._

Suddenly, the gate behind you slams shut, trapping you in this rank-smelling cavern. You start to look around for an escape route, confident in your ability to eventually get through the rusty old barrier.
Then the gate to the north slowly opens. And then you hear another gate opening, farther in. And then you hear more howling.
The wretches have trapped you in their wolf pit, and someone is releasing the hungry creatures.
You squeeze through a crack opened by a recent earthquake. You emerge from the crumbling mineshaft into a large, natural cavern.
There are tall ornate stalagmites and clusters of broad, brightly colored mushrooms. It is actually quite lovely.

Of course, the wretches are doing their best to despoil it. There is the occasional pile of trash, and the creatures have been picking the mushrooms. They might be poisonous, but wretches can eat just about anything.
The rank scent of wolves is growing thicker. You look through the open gate and see the pens where the wretches were raising them.
This gate is open, and the far gate is closed. You are starting to suspect another trap. But you are invading their home territory. There's no way out but forward.

There is a human scout sitting by a low cookfire, trying to stay in the shade of the cactus thickets. She is a warrior of The Kva. The heat barely seems to bother her. She is tired and filthy, though. These scouts have been out here for a while.

At first, she seems to think that you are a mirage. Then she jumps to her feet. _Reinforcements at last. And a warrior, not a scout. Welcome. I am Ayse, and we've been out here for a while. And ... I am sorry. Who are you?_

Ayse sits by the fire, cooking a miserable lizard stew. The other scouts sharpen their weapons and watch for wretches to kill. Based on the tracks and bloodstains, they've had to defend themselves several times.
She looks slightly suspicious. _I would be happy to tell you. If you introduce yourself._
I am [N], Hand of Avadon. Here to hunt wretches.
She seems impressed. _From Avadon? You mean we finally got your attention? We need help out here._
_We want to go back. We should have gone back days ago. But one of us was grabbed by the wretches, and we need him back._
I have been sent by Zhethron to hunt down wretches.
_The dragon sent you? Impressive. We need the help._
I am [N]. I was sent by Watcher Harissa to find you.
_Then you can tell her that three of us are well. But not the fourth. That is why we have not returned._

_We were based in the dragon's lair. Watcher Harissa sent us out to scout the vile creatures. Then they ambushed us. We were fighting our way out, but they swarmed one of our men and dragged him off. Name was Yevner._
_We won't leave one of our men in the hands of those pests. We won't go back until we have him. Or his body._
You lost a man to wretches?

_We were stupid. We let them sneak up on us. I admit it. Then they came out, and there were too many. We killed a lot of them. Dozens, even, But then Yevner tripped when we were backing away and they were on him._
And you couldn't rescue him?
_They dragged him off while we were busy fighting the others. We can't go back and tell our fellows what happened. We can't face them without having Yevner with us._
Can you help me to fight them?

She shakes her head. _We've been out here for too long. Haven't had a decent meal in days. And we are still scouts, not ready for an assault. We should have gone back a long time ago, but we've been looking for Yevner._
Tell me about Yevner.
She describes him to you. _A good scout. Years of experience. Tough. If anyone can survive the wretches, he can, but only if he's rescued soon._
If I meet him, I will help him.
_That is all we can ask. We can't stay out here for much longer._
I will find him for you.
She nods. _Good. I thank you. When he is found, let us know. We can't stay out here for much longer._

_There are a lot of them. But, the way they breed, when there are wretches, there are a lot of wretches. They're in the old mine to the south, behind thick walls. Even if we were strong enough to attack, we couldn't get through there._
How many wretches are there?
_Lots. Fewer than there were when we got there. But maybe a hundred, maybe more._
Who is leading them?

_Don't know. There must be someone, though. They're organized. Smart and careful enough to surprise us. They have proper defenses and patrols. And someone told them to come here and settle near the dragon._
Tell me about the walls.
_The mine had walls, to keep raiders and lizards out. The wretches fixed them, and there's a gate._
Wretches rebuilt the wall?
_They are organized. They're strange wretches._
How can I get in?
_Not through the gate, not without a real force. But we've been scouting, and we're sure that wretches have been getting in and out some way besides the main gate._
They have a back entrance?
_It was a mine. There are tunnels everywhere. They must have a different way to get in. Just hope it's not as guarded as the front._
Why are you out in the open like this?

_We're letting the wretches know that we're not going until we have Yevner back, dead or alive. No point in hiding. The creatures are all over the thickets. But we'll kill their scouts and raiders until we have our man._
Have you been attacked?
_Four times. We killed them and left the bodies for vultures. Or threw them in the river. We can kill a lot of them, as long as they don't surprise us. They're just wretches._
_But there's always more._
They ambushed you once. Can't they do it again?
_Now that we know what to look for, they won't surprise us again. They're still just wretches. It's not a good plan, staying here, but it's all we have. _
She nods. _I thought things seemed a little quiet. We're getting tired and sloppy, though. We should have realized what you did. We need to get back to a proper bed and meal._
_But we still can't leave without Yevner._
I found Yevner.
She nods. _We met him. We already sent him ahead to safety. We will be heading back as soon as it is dark. Too hot to march in the sun._
_Thank you for your help, [N]. We owe you a debt._
I found Yevner, but he didn't make it out alive.
She is stricken by the news. _This is a sad day. He ... We were close. Now, at least, we can return to Goldcrag. I will inform his family._
_Thank you for your help, [N]. Though you only brought us this information, we still owe you a debt._
_Good luck. We will stay here, until we find a way to rescue our lost man._

There is a woman waiting for you in this small camp. It is the same woman you saw walking out of the wretch encampment. She sits next to two squat, thuggish humans, surrounded by crates of equipment. She looks very unhappy to see you.
_Greetings, traveler,_ she says. _This is mining land, and you are in our claim. You have to go. Now._
The young woman and her thugs sit and watch you. Their hands are close to their weapons.
The woman looks at you suspiciously. _I don't have to tell you that. I don't have to tell you anything. I am a scavenger and a miner, and you're on my claim. That's all you need to know._
I am a Hand of Avadon, and I need to talk to you.
She smirks. Not the response you expected. _A Hand? So you say. Even if it's true, you're a long way from Avadon. We don't care about tyrants out here in the wilds._
I'd like to know more about these supplies.

She looks around at the crates. _There's lots of abandoned mines out here. That means old weapons and gear. We scavenge for them, and then we sell them back in The Kva. It's our right. The Stone Code allows it._
Odd. These goods don't look like they've been out in the desert for years.
These supplies look new, actually.
_And you are an expert? Well, we clean things when we find them. That means they look new._
You don't sell any of these things to the wretches, do you?
_No. That would be illegal. We would never do such a thing._
But I just saw you leaving the wretches lair.
She is nonplused. _Not to sell. I was just seeing if I could haul away any of their old trash. They said no._
_And you have no right to question me. Whoever you are, you can keep moving._ She turns away.
I don't think you're telling the truth.
_And I don't care. This is our claim, and we might do a little prospecting. Whoever you are, you can keep moving._ She turns away.
I am looking for a woman named Neray. Are you her?
The woman doesn't react to the name. She is well-trained. Her guards? Not so much. The moment you say 'Neray', one of them turns to look at her. She looks back at him with disgust.
_So you found me,_ she spits, _but only because of these fools. Now we will take the weapons from your bodies and sell them for a pile of coin. Kill them!_
The three of them jump up and draw their blades. Then, as the two thugs charge you, Neray runs for the trapdoor and leaves them to their fates.
_Good. And don't come back._

A tall, stocky wretch stands boldly before you. While the ogre might be trying to deal with you to save his skin, this bold creature is having none of it. He points a spear at you and roars a challenge.
_Stop, invader [N]! Onghror say let you by. That coward talk! You die now, on bold spear of Chief Vahlfur!_
Behind him, three shamans, all of whom look like they would be much happier just letting you go, begin to chant their spells.

When Yevner reaches the open gateway, he turns to look at you. _Thank you for saving me. I need to tell Ayse and the others that I am free, so we can return to safety. I hope you will be safe, but I must go._
He starts to say something else. Then he simply turns and runs.
This old, broken-down desk has been stuffed full of papers. The wretches, sensing that this is the purpose of a desk, jammed every scroll and scrap of paper they could find into here.

Most of the papers are old and yellowed, but, in one of the drawers, you find a leather-bound ledger. A dragon has been embossed on the cover. Flipping through it, you find records of recent meetings with Zhethron.
These must be the records you were sent to find. Some wretch must have jammed it in here, not realizing how valuable it could be, and you came here before anyone important found where it was lost.
You briefly search through the mess, but you find nothing of value.
The mechanism for this wheel has rusted stuck, and the wretches sadly lack the technical skill to repair it.
You finally reach the gatehouse for the wretch lair. Beyond it is the wheel you need to reach to open the gate and escape this trap.
However, there is a small padlock on the door. It is made of steel, shining in the sun, and you can see a small rune by the keyhole. An enchanted lock. Without the key, your escape will be delayed.
It's not usual for wretches to have access to this sort of magic. Hmmm.

You finally emerge from the lower mines into the upper corridors. These halls were once quarters for the miners. In fact, the complex is large enough that it might once have served as a trading post for the other mines in the area.
Now the wretches have taken it over. The walls are crumbling and the gates are rusting, but, under Onghror's leadership, they have repaired enough of the decay to make it usable.
There are no wretches visible here. Perhaps, fearing your arrival, most of them have fled.
Or perhaps Onghror is meeting his half of your arrangement.

You pass through the wretches' trophy hall to the east and find a large shrine. The altar is old, dating back to the days when humans lived here. The wretches have covered it with grime and carvings and converted it to their own purposes.
A tall shaman stands behind it, flanked by two armed wretches. She points a carved wooden rod at you and snarls. _So, Hand is here. We will show you! We have no fear of you._
_Onghror says he kill you. No! You taken by us! You lie on this stone and die! Is time for sacrifice!_
_Onghror take coward's way! Onghror says you live. No! You taken by us! You lie on this stone and die! Is time for sacrifice! Glory to wretches!_

You finally reach Onghror's throne room. The ogre is talking to someone, on the edge of panic. You conceal yourself at the doorway and listen. He is talking to someone to the north, but you can't see who it is from here.
The ogre says, _Wretches lie! Made no deal, I! Will kill the Hand. Always want to. Are here soon, and I kill. And Onghror gets reward!_
The ogre says, _Yes, Onghror try deal. Only to trick human. And human refuses! Will kill the Hand. Always want to. Are here soon, and I kill. And Onghror gets reward!_

Someone speaks to him. A male voice. You don't recognize it. He says, _We gave you much. You have lost it all, due to your clumsiness. Kill the invader and rebuild elsewhere. One more error, and you will be ended._
Onghror says, _I will do this._ Then you hear a door closing.
The massive ogre slumps in his throne, muttering to himself. _Flee? Not flee? Do not know!_

You walk past an old, rusty portcullis on the right. Then you stop. You can hear something stomping in the shadows beyond. Heavy, echoing footsteps, moving toward you. You move forward to get a better look.
A massive, lumbering figure moves into view. It's an ogre. He wears a suit of rusted, torn chainmail, and a massive war club hangs from his belt. He looks confused by your presence.

Titans and ogres are thought by many to be simple, foolish creatures. Warriors of Avadon know better. They can be very clever and cunning, and this specimen particularly so. You can see it in his eyes as he evaluates you quietly through the bars.
_I am Onghror. Master of these caves. The wretches, they serve me. Invaders, I slay. You are not invader. Yet._
_You warrior. Onghror sees this. Has question._
Now I have to kill an ogre as well as wretches?
His eyes flick to your weapons. _Or I kill you. I am Onghror, no wretch me. I am master of these caves. Come to see invader._
The ogre finishes sizing you up. He finally decides to break the silence. _I am Onghror. Master of these caves. The wretches, they serve me. Invaders, I slay. You are an invader._
_You sneak in. Kill my wretches. Are warrior, with skill. Why you here? My wretches, not want to waste them on you._
As Onghror talks, you hear soft sounds ahead of and behind you. Wretches sneaking up on you, trying to be stealthy.
I am [N], a Hand of Avadon, come to drive you out of here.
The moment Onghror hears the word Avadon, his jaw drops. He is terrified (and rightly so). _Av ... Avadon? Avadon comes to Onghror? But I ... Onghror was not told of this. Wait now. I must ..._
But then something happens. The sound of deep chanting fills the hall. The sound of wretch shamans, several of them. Onghror shouts, _No! Fools! Wait!_
The dragon Zhethron has sent me, to rid him of the wretches that bother him.
The moment Onghror hears the name Zhethron, he looks very nervous. _The dragon? The beast sends hunters after Onghror? Not told, I was. Said he would not ... Wait now. I must ..._
I haven't decided what I am going to do here yet.
Your vague response makes Onghror nervous. _You are no miner. No scavenger. No claim taker. You are a killer, Onghror sees. Onghror knows a hunter. Wait now. I must ..._
What is happening?

Onghror turns and runs into the shadows, bellowing for the wretches to stop what they are doing. It is too late. The chants of the shamans make the rock vibrate. Behind you, you hear wretches hammering supports out of the walls.
Chunks of stone start to fall out of the ceiling.
(Run.)

As you turn to flee, Onghror turns and runs into the shadows, bellowing for the wretches to stop what they are doing. It is too late to get away. The chants of the shamans make the rock vibrate. Behind you, you hear wretches hammering supports out of the walls.
(Escape the cave-in.)
The ceiling starts to collapse to the south, so you run to the north, trying to escape the tons of falling rubble ...
Panting, you come to a halt. The chanting ceases. The rocks are through falling. You are trapped in the wretch caves. And, somewhere, Onghror is cursing the fact that he is trapped in here with you.
Sevilin kicks at the dry sand with distaste. _These lands are not like where I was raised. The north and south Kva are very different. It is hard to adjust._
Jenell says, _I understand. When you have trained your whole life to hunt in one place, and then to come to this desolation ... It can be dangerous._
Nathalie says, _This desert could not be more different from Kellemderiel. My art depends on concentration. It is hard to focus when sand gets everywhere._
He looks at the cactus thickets. _Yes. Were I more used to this place, it might not have happened ..._
_It was not far from here that I was in an ambush. A few months ago, only a day's travel from here. Me and three other Hands. I was the only survivor._
_If I was used to these thickets, I might have spotted the attackers. As it was ..._ He shakes his head. _I will not make the same mistake again._
Shima looks at you as you walk through the mine. _Attacking like this is not the shadowwalker way. I have had to adjust to much since I came to Avadon._
What would you do differently?

_Shadowwalkers are methodical. We learn all we can about a target before we attack. Sometimes we spend months. Mapping. Watching. Planning. There is much honor in completing a mission with perfect evasion._
_But the way of Avadon is different. When Avadon acts, it wants all to know. It is not ... worse. But very different._
You are welcome to go elsewhere if you don't like it.
Shima is understandably offended. _Avadon is all I have now, and I will serve it until I die._ Then he is silent.
(Remain silent.)
Shima is silent as well.
Jenell looks down at the ground. _I'm starting to get used to tracking in the desert._
She points at the cacti to the east. _Wretches are lazy creatures. Their patrols don't go up to the thickets. We might be able to evade them by going there._
Nathalie laughs silently. _Why would you want to avoid them? Don't you want to tell Avadon that we slew as many Farlanders as possible?_
Sevilin says, _That is one path. But I'd prefer to leave as few of those Farlanders in my home as possible._

Nathalie examines one of the mushrooms. Then she takes a sample of one. _Not a variety I am familiar with. I've had much time to study alchemy while waiting to be sent on a mission. I wonder what I can do with this._
Sevilin smiles. _Just don't eat it. Not unless you want to have a very difficult time focusing for a while._
Jenell smiles. _Just don't eat it. Not unless you want to be very distracted and relaxed. Although it might do you some good._
Hearing this, Nathalie nervously wipes off her fingers on her robe. _I do not want anything to disrupt my concentration. Not after waiting so long to be sent on a mission._
The ogre Onghror is standing on the north side of a stream that bisects this cave. Two wretch shamans flank him to either side. All three of them look terrified.
Onghror says, _I was told of you. You are [N]. Told you come from Avadon. We know Avadon. Not want to fight you. Know not Avadon would come._
Onghror shakes his head. _Not saying. Onghror in enough trouble now._
Well, I am here now.
_You are. Trapped. Send wretches to trap you, but not know who you were. Now we decide what to do._
I have come to destroy you.
He shakes his head. _No. Was mistake. Send wretches to trap you, but not know who you were. Can we settle things with peace?_
I am looking for a lost scout from Zhethron's Aerie.
The ogre nods. _Is Yevner. In cells. Take him. He is unharmed. We want peace._
I want to find a smuggler named Neray.
The ogre is silent for a moment. Then he says, simply, _I know no Neray._ You doubt that he is telling the truth.
You don't want to fight me?
_Wretches are pests. They run around. Do what they want. Bother dragon. Can't control them. Wild things._ The shamans nod in agreement.
_Fighting Avadon, not for me. Want way out._
Perhaps we can negotiate a peace.
Onghror nods. _We can. I and thinking wretches. I will think. Talk with advisors. See you soon._
Actually, I think I'll just kill everyone here.
Onghror shakes his head. _No. Wait. Avadon is thinking people. I will talk with advisors. Meet you soon. Can make all happy._ He and the shamans walk off into the shadows.
So your wretches will stop attacking me?
The ogre shrugs his massive shoulders. _Pale and wild, wretches in caves are. Could try to stop them. Won't. Must talk above. Decide what to do. How we can all survive._
Are you angry about the wretches we have killed?
_Not really. Wretches are simple. If I have two left, soon have many wretches. A few make no difference._ The shamans nod sagely at this wisdom.
Then let me out of here.
_I can't. Passage out here behind me. Come to me. I find you soon. Find way to peace, and me not dying._ He and the shamans walk off into the shadows.
I will keep killing your servants until I hear from you again.
Onghror nods solemnly. _Understood. I will find you soon._ He and the shamans walk off into the shadows.

Once again, you find the ogre Onghror staring at you, this time from behind the barred windows to the east. After looking around to make sure he is alone, he leans close and whispers, _With you, Onghror can parley now._
I would be happy to. Why don't you come to the other side of these bars?
_Because you might kill me._
No wretches with you?
_Some of them wily. Can spy. For the others. Need to speak alone._
I'm listening.
_Onghror told to do things. Not told Avadon would come. Onghror will live. And leave with wretches loyal to Onghror. But must be careful, or masters kill Onghror._
I've talked to you enough. We will be fighting soon enough. (Leave.)
Onghror whispers something else, but you don't hear it. This creature sounds desperate. Then he flees into the shadows, probably to prepare his defenses.
Who has been giving you orders?
_Don't know. Just send orders. Money. Know no names. No things. Just want to escape. Not want fighting Avadon._ You doubt that this is the full truth.
What have you been trying to do?
_Was told to send out wretches. Disrupt roads. Bother dragons. Is all. Am stopping now. You stop me. Mighty Avadon. Now will just leave._
So what do you want me to do?
_Leave. Can kill any wretches that fight you. Are wild things. I stop my loyal ones. Must be careful. Must be a secret. You fight out and go. I leave treasure for you. I leave._
Wait. Why must this be secret?

_If some know I let you go, they hunt Onghror. I help you, I am killed. Wretches fight you, they think I try to kill you, they let me live._ Unsurprisingly, Onghror is still saying nothing about who was directing him.
No more attacks on me, or no deal.
Onghror shrugs his massive shoulders. _Am sorry. Some wretches spies for others. Must send them to die. Bad things. Not a help, like Onghror. Think Avadon happy to kill them._
All right. I will fight my way out. You can just leave.
Onghror nods and lets out a sigh of relief. _Kill all who kill you. Take what you want. I take other wretches and go. Attacks stop. All happy. You are wise._
Onghror turns and walks quickly off into the shadows.
I will spare you, but you must come with me to Avadon.

Onghror thinks hard about this. _The dungeons of Avadon. They break me. Strip my mind. See I will flee and never bother them again. Is hard, but ... No choice. I agree. I meet you outside mines and we go._
Before you can say anything else, Onghror turns and walks quickly off into the shadows.
Everything here is guilty of disrupting the Pact. All will pay.
