You turn and continue through the passages. Onghror shouts something, but you don't hear it. He sounds desperate. Then he flees into the shadows, probably to prepare his defenses.

There is a man crumpled on the filthy pallet on the floor of this cell. He lies perfectly still. At first you think he is dead. Then he hears you and opens his eyes. A moment later, he is on his feet.

He is a human warrior of The Kva, and, despite the length of his imprisonment here, he is surprisingly healthy. He says, _Are you rescuers? You are, aren't you? I heard the fighting. The wretches are panicking. Who are you?_
You introduce yourself. He says, _Well, I am honored, [N]. I am Yevner. And I desperately want to get out of here._
Yevner waits impatiently in the cell. _Is it time, [N]? Can we leave yet?_
_The wretches caught me, curse them! I was with a group of scouts, sent from Zhethron's Aerie. We had found this lair and were returning, only to be caught in an ambush._
Why were you looking for wretches?
_Because the creatures were making the dragon very angry. We had to calm it down, or it might ... I don't know what it would do. Nothing good for us._
How did wretches catch you?

_We were outnumbered five to one and in a fighting retreat. We were holding our own, but then I tripped._ He shakes his head, embarrassed. _Then they were on me. A swarm! Thought I was dead, but they knocked me out instead._
_When I woke up, I was here. It's as if they wanted one of us alive._
I met Ayse. She is still outside.
Yevner seems genuinely moved by this news. _They waited here? For me? That is ..._ He wipes his eyes with his sleeve. _I can't let them stay out there. We have to go!_
How have you been treated?
_I ... Well. I thought they would torture me. Or eat me. But they fed me, and the ogre asked me questions. But they've just kept me here. I think they were saving me._
They fed you?
_Disgusting food. Filthy water. Mushrooms that ... that made my head swim. It's been miserable, but I lived. I am a warrior of the Kva!_
He looks at Sevilin. His fellow soldier of The Kva nods approvingly.
Tell me about the ogre.

_Said its name was Onghror. Was ... almost intelligent. I was surprised. The moment I saw an ogre in my cell, I almost messed myself. Never met one before. Just asked me questions. Said I was being 'held ready.'_
Why do you think they were keeping you?
_Don't know. Ransom? Saving me as the feast for some wretch holiday? Or maybe ..._ He tries to think.

_I'm not sure. It happened one of the times when my mind was gone. The ogre was here. Said something about ... Said I'd be sent to be questioned by someone. Someone important. Don't know more than that._
You should come out with me.
_At last!_ Yevner walks out into the hall. A few minutes later, he returns with a weapon and armor scavenged off one of the larger wretches. He wrinkles his nose. _Smells filthy, but it will serve._
_Lead on. I am ready to fight._
He seems slightly disappointed when you inform him that the ogre is already dead. _Then I won't get revenge, only freedom._
Stay here for now.
Yevner looks disappointed. _All right. I will wait. But don't leave me here for long! I'm eager to fight!_
Yevner says, _We can speak later. Lead on. I am eager to fight._
Yevner falls to the ground, mortally wounded. His last, gasped words are, _Ayse! I ... Ayse!_ And then he dies. At least he went out fighting bravely.
Onghror looks up and sees you. _You! You are here! Did you ..._ He looks guiltily at the closed door to the north. _Hear Onghror? Hear his talk?_
I heard every word.
Onghror nods. _Avadon learns all. You have master. Makes you come here. Hunt Onghror. I have master too. Own orders. Must follow, or Onghror hunted and killed._
I heard enough to know you can't be trusted.
Onghror nods. _Could trust Onghror. Not master of Onghror. You have master. Makes you come here. Hunt Onghror. I have master too. Own orders. Must follow, or Onghror hunted and killed._
No. Didn't hear a thing.
Onghror looks up at you, thinking fast. For a moment, he looks hopeful. Then he remembers his orders. _Remember words in low caves. Wait for your words, I do._
Who were you talking to?
_Servant of master. Will be killed, Onghror will, if I say name. Will die slow, in much pain. This first thing Onghror told, when take help from outsider to make this place._
_If could choose again, would not take deal._
It is time to die, Farlander. (Attack.)

Onghror is not surprised. He knew it would come to this. He rises and draws his weapon. A wretch steps out from behind a pillar and runs up to the runed circle carved on the floor in the middle of the room.
_Onghror will destroy you now. Is only way._ The armored ogre points his blade at you and advances. The wretch begins to chant.
I'm ready for you to obey your half of our bargain.
_Would have agree. Would have opened the gates. Let you free. But then master's servant came. A few minutes sooner, all the difference. But is too late. Now things happen as they must._
I am ready to bargain with you.

_You refused Onghror. Changed mind, you have. Weak? Tired? Know I can slay you? Still listen, I would. But then master's servant came. A few minutes sooner, all the difference. But is too late. Now things happen as they must._
Explain.
_Onghror's master, he speaks. The master, he can always hunt Onghror. Can torture me. Kill me. A fool, I was. Now trapped._ He rises to his feet and draws his blade.
A wretch steps out from behind a pillar and runs up to the runed circle carved on the floor in the middle of the room.
I've heard more than enough from you. (Attack.)
Onghror is not surprised. He knew it would come to this.
We don't have to fight. Just let me go.
Onghror is surprised. He mistakenly thinks that your trying to parley is a sign of weakness. He snarls.
_Onghror will destroy you. Is only way._ The armored ogre points his blade at you and advances. The wretch begins to chant.
Onghror cries out a command. An armed wretch opens one of the southern gates in his throne room.
The wretch shaman finishes a spell. A small creature, made of flame, appears in the enchanted circle. The tiny imp lets out a shrill cackle and begins to fling little balls of fire at you.
Onghror collapses to the ground. His blade falls to the floor beside him with a loud clang. He presses his hands to his wounds, but it is too late for him. He shakes his head.
_Could have ... Could have lived ... Served ... My mistake, what was it? What should I ... I ..._ And he closes his eyes.
You notice that he wears a leather thong around his neck. You pull it out. There is a worn key dangling from it. You take it.
This infestation of wretches has been fully cleansed. Zhethron will be pleased.

The wretch shaman has been slain. She falls to the ground, the profusion of charms and baubles spreading out around her. You see the glint of metal among the teeth and bits of bone. It's a key. You take it.
Yevner runs to catch up with you.
Seeker Azarni flees to safety.
Talking: Azarni is trying to flee. She doesn't respond.
Chief Gnak'Snap
Zephyrine
Zephyrine activates another defender. Then she casts a spell. Spines grow out of her scales.
Zephyrine activates another defender. Then she casts a spell. Her scales begin to gleam.
Zephyrine activates another defender. Then she casts a spell. A powerful, glowing shield surrounds her.
You hear the sound of smashing rock in the distance.
is currently busy. She ignores you.
Zephyrine's Watcher
A stone sentinel is charging up. The tether of energy between it and the dragon grows stronger.
A stone sentinel is fully charged. It begins sending energy to the dragon.
A sentinel shares energy with the dragon!
Talking: The stone sentinel doesn't respond. It is completely inert.
Screecher Bat
Raider Vostog
Watcher Akasa
Chief Redda'Tk
Shaman Gk'Yrl
Ogre Miner
Shaman Trysk
Ogre Taskmaster
Trained War Rat
The water advances.
The water finally stops rising.
Skilled Brigand
The ogres are doomed.
Agreed.
Do we work for their employer?
And suffer the same fate?
Come. We seek our fortunes elsewhere.
After a long hike, you arrive at the Jhereth Deeps. This is a network of narrow, dry valleys, carved out of the eastern edge of a jagged mountain chain.

You are now miles into the Farlands, deep in the Wretch Lands. Any ogres who come here risk being hunted down and destroyed. Larger creatures settling in land set aside for the wretches is not good for the Pact.

There were once several mines in these valleys, and the piles of rubble and rusted cart track are still visible. You can understand why the ogres would come here. There must still be many miles of intact tunnels under your feet.

And this is definitely the right area. The ogres have made no effort to disguise their presence. The tracks of their massive feet are everywhere, along with gnawed bones and piles of fresh garbage. The creatures who have been angering Zhethron are somewhere ahead.

You enter the newly constructed dome. The walls are blocks of smooth stone, carefully fitted together. The air is icy cold, despite the punishing heat outside. The floor is polished marble. It is so strangely new and luxurious that you suspect a magical illusion.
Then you round the corner and see the occupant of this place, and everything suddenly becomes clear.

There is a dragon resting in the center of the dome. A huge creature, young and with shining blue scales. Its long fangs are sharp and white. Dragons have been coming to these lands for many years, but you did not expect to meet one here.
Of course, the creature knows that you are here. She turns and looks at you, confused by your presence. Then she slowly raises a claw and motions you forward.
There is an entrance to a mine to the southeast. The totems erected in front of it clearly advertise that these tunnels have been settled by a tribe of ogres. A large one, from the look of it.

At first, you think that you were already able to find the ogres you are hunting. Didn't take long. But then you realize that something is wrong. It is quiet. There are no guards. No livestock. No hunting wolves.
Strange. Have the creatures fled?
The valley to the northwest has been mostly closed off by a cave-in. Only a narrow opening along the north edge allows passage.
Dried blood is splattered along the path. Perhaps a week or two old.

You reach the end of the pathway and find a body, dried out by the harsh sun. She wears the long robes of a mage. There is an insignia on her collar. Looking closer, you see that it is the symbol of Avadon.

This is a Hand, ambushed and hunted down by ogres. Many Hands have left Avadon on missions recently, trying to calm unrest in many parts of Lynaeus. Most of them have not returned. In this case, you now know why.
As you bow your head, you hear something behind you. The snarling of wolves, and many heavy footfalls. The creatures who ambushed this unlucky Hand are trying the same trick again, this time on you.

It is not only ogres that have found these valleys to be a safe place to conceal their tribes. A large band of wretches has moved into the valley ahead. They have erected crude defenses and begun to excavate tunnels.
The guards watch you from the palisade. One of them shouts, _Human! You human! You go! This land of Hegra Clan. No bother you. Just go! You enter, we kill._
While not friendly, they do seem inclined to keep to themselves. You might be able to find another way around.
Nathalie notes your indecision. _They're wretches. Shouldn't we just destroy them? Better to err on the side of safety._

You have discovered the rear entrance to the ogre fortress, currently busily being converted into the new front entrance. The dragon Zephyrine was helping them to conceal themselves, but she has withdrawn her aid.
Several ogres are hammering sharpened stakes into the dirt, preparing new defenses. They easily see you coming. They turn and run back into their fort, shouting alarms.
Shima smiles weakly. _Another stealthy, carefully planned assault. My masters would be so proud to see this._
At last, you have discovered a way into the ogre fort. However, they are ready to defend themselves. Soon, they will learn what happens to Farlanders who defy Avadon.
There is new construction in this valley. A dark stone dome looms above you. Statues flank the entrance, and a shining marble floor is visible inside. You were not told to expect anything like this.
This is not ogre handiwork. It is too new and too grand. When you get closer, a draft of icy air hits you, making you shiver. This is very strange.

You look around the abandoned ogre lair. The creatures left in a hurry, or they did a credible job of making it look that way. Rubble and trash are everywhere, and little of value has been left behind.

And yet, the ogre tracks outside are still fresh, and there have been plenty of the creatures roaming the roads. It is still too early to report what you have found back to Zhethron. Whoever is responsible for the attacks might still be nearby.

You enter an old, abandoned mine, now taken over by the ogres and being rebuilt for their own purposes. You still don't know why ogres would come to settle in the Wretch Lands. Now that you have found a way into their lair, you might be able to find an answer.
The cave has some supplies and empty crates piled in the corners, equipment smuggled in by the ogres. It is quiet. No guards are here to meet you. They fled when they knew you were coming.
The tunnel to the east is full of dark, slimy water, blocking your progress. This mine has pipes and pumps to clear excess water out of the tunnels, but they aren't working right now.
Hopefully, there is some way to clear the tunnel.
This tunnel has been converted by the ogres into a small shrine. They have found a crumbling altar somewhere and dragged it down here. Now they are gathered around, swaying and chanting.
As the ogres turn to face you, you see that a lot of them have tools and shovels hanging from their belts. This must be the construction crew, taking a break from clearing out the mine tunnels.
The sign says, in large, crude lettering:
HEGRA CLAN
LAND CLAIM STAY OUT
This weathered crate looks like it's been here for over thirty years, boards cracking in the hot sun. You look inside and find a few rusting picks and shovels.
You dig deeper in the box and find a small leather pouch, placed here recently. It contains the reward the Wayfarer promised. There are several gemstones and a gold ring. You pocket them.
Sevilin is quiet, but you can see that he is seething with fury after the ambush. _That is what happened to me and my friends. They died, because creatures like that thought they could fight Avadon._

Shima is quiet, but you can see that he is seething with fury after the ambush. _I came to Avadon because it was a place where I could have honor, where I could be respected. And then these creatures think they can attack us._
Nathalie is quiet, but you can see that she is seething with fury after the ambush. _How have these creatures come to think that they can hunt us like sport? What has happened to respect for Avadon?_
_It is good that we have come here. They need to be taught a lesson._
When you get close to the wretch encampment, the creatures see your equipment. Their greed overcomes any small amount of caution these creatures might have.
The guards let out a lusty battle cry. Within moments, the wretches of the Hegra Clan are pouring forth like ants.
When you get close to the wretch guard, he bears his teeth and lets out a long, ugly hiss. These creatures have no interest in friendly conversation or trade.
There is a woman in a leather jerkin standing by this fire. She is favoring her left leg. Her right leg is wrapped in a crude, dirty bandage.
When she hears you, she whirls around, saying, _Where have you been? Those cursed ogres threw a ..._ And then she sees you.
It is Neray, the smuggler. The moment she recognizes you, she exclaims a loud, sincere expletive. Then she dives for the trapdoor in the alcove to the south.
The huge ogre miner collapses to the ground. Among the pipes and tools on his belt, you see an iron key hanging from a leather thong. You grab it.

Somewhere nearby, an ogre shouts in triumph. You hear the sound of chains scraping over stone. The gate behind you begins to close. You turn and run, but you are too slow. The rusty iron barrier hits the floor, sealing you in.
Then the water level of the pool to the north begins to slowly rise. The water creeps quickly up toward your feet. The ogres hope to drown you in here.

You run to the southern gate and struggle to lift it. As the water creeps closer, you lift with all of your might. You manage to raise the gate a foot, enough to slip under it. The corridor to the south slowly rises, giving you hope of escaping the water.

There is a small, twisted titan in chain mail standing behind the last of the crude palisades. He wears necklaces of skulls around his neck, the remains of wretches, wolves, and at least one human he has slain.
When he sees you, he points at you and roars, _There is the invader! We avenge the lost now! Merula offers much gold to any who slays a Hand!_

Titans are huge, powerful humanoids that normally live in the peaks far to the west. The Titan Peaks are one of the more remote and dangerous of the Farlands. That a titan found his way this far east is very odd.
You have succeeded in wounding the stunted titan. Enraged, he begins swinging his club around madly, charging you with berserk fury and a lack of interest in his own self-preservation.
As he charges, he yells, _Merula, you will die for bringing this to us!_
You hear a grinding, crunching sound to the north. One of the drainage pipes has broken.
As you step back to safety, the passage fills with water.

You have successfully hunted down, trapped, and destroyed Neray the Smuggler. This is a small victory for the Pact. Whatever mischief the humanoids of these hills are up to, they will have to go about it with worse weaponry.
There is a large wooden wheel here. A chain extends from it into a hole in the floor.
Turn the wheel.
You turn the wheel, pulling out a long length of the chain. You hear a grinding noise, followed by flowing water.
The water in the passage outside begins to slowly drain away.
You start to turn the wheel only to realize that you might be able to flood the mines. You leave it alone.
You leave the rusty old contraption alone.

Even though you are far from civilization, in a land infested with ogres, it somehow doesn't surprise you that the first person you meet is the Wayfarer. He emerges from the cliff shadow, still in his black shadowwalker garb. The heat seems to barely faze him.
He waves to you as he approaches. _I am glad you have finally arrived. I did not have much longer to wait. I need to speak with you. An excellent opportunity awaits you._
Weren't you in Khemeria?
He nods. _Servants of Avadon are able to travel very quickly. So can those who work with and support the servants of Avadon. Like me._
How did you find me here?
_It is our business to find out where the Hands of Avadon are at all times. Otherwise, how can we hire them? As for how we find out, I would rather not say. But don't worry._
I am interested.

_Of course. Wealth is the reward for being a Hand, after all. That is why I asked you to find information about Commander Ryozo when you went to Zhethron's lair. I wanted to tell you something about that._
The Wayfarer takes a small step back and then continues talking as if you hadn't said anything.
_I only offer you an opportunity. That is why I asked you to find information about Commander Ryozo when you went to Zhethron's lair. I wanted to tell you something about that._
_I thank you for the information. It was very helpful. We were able to use it to learn unfortunate things about Commander Ryozo. His harsh exterior conceals some ugly truths._

_You did not obtain the information about Ryozo that we desired. You no longer need to bother. We learned what we needed to on our own. Unfortunate things. His harsh exterior conceals some ugly truths._
You still want me to work for you?
_Of course. For people of power and influence, hiring Hands of Avadon to help them is a valuable tool. As long as you are a Hand, our wealth awaits you. You have but to take it._
What have you learned about Ryozo?
_I am pleased that you are interested. Commander Ryozo is not a loyal servant of Avadon. He is a turncoat, trying to hire Zhethron away from the Pact._
_Of course, the Hand that found proof of such a thing would earn great prestige in the eyes of Redbeard._
Shima looks surprised. _Ryozo is no friend of mine, but it will take proof for us to believe such a charge._ The Wayfarer nods. _You will have it._
I will not work with you. Get out of my way.
The Wayfarer lets out a loud, theatrical sigh and steps away. _Then I will find another Hand. It will not be difficult. I will not seek you out again. Of course, we might meet accidentally._
He chuckles, turns, and walks away.
I learned that Ryozo was only trying to get Zhethron to watch the Tawon Empire.
_That was only the first step. Once Zhethron was north, the fading empire could contact him and try to break his ties with the Pact. Do not be fooled. It is a complicated game._
How did you learn this?
_I deal with many people for information._

_Commander Ryozo is still in the dragon's lair, but he will not be for long. I believe that he may have letters hidden there, papers that prove his treacherous dealings. Find them, if they exist, and deliver them to the Watcher there._
_When this is done, your reward will be left in an old crate where I was hiding._ He points to the north.
And if I find nothing?
_Then do nothing more, except feel pleased that a servant of the Pact is loyal._
Where should I look for the papers?
_Hmmm. Probably his quarters in the dragon's lair. That would be the most likely place. But I would hurry, before Ryozo departs._
I will do what I can.
He looks to the north. _There is a crate over there. If you find the evidence and turn it in, a reward will be left for you there._
_It is a chance to aid the Pact and to enrich yourself. A true opportunity. We eagerly await news of any discoveries._ He gives you a brief bow and turns away.
I can't do this.
_Unfortunate, but you may change your mind._ He looks to the north. _There is a crate over there. If you find the evidence and turn it in, a reward will be left for you there._
He gives you a brief bow and turns away.
There are several Kva scouts in this clearing. They are exhausted, hungry, and close to sunstroke. Most of them are too weak to talk. This one says, _Talk to Akasa. She speaks for us._

The ogres outside had trapped a small patrol of Kva scouts in this clearing. Luckily, you were able to slay them before they had time to close in and kill these humans. They are exhausted, hungry, and weak, but one Watcher manages to rise and greet you.
_Good to see you,_ she says. _I am Watcher Akasa. We have ..._ She pauses to cough. _We are scouts. Trapped here. Thanks for the help. Were you sent for us?_
Watcher Akasa leans against the wall, hungry and exhausted. _We need to ... Need to return home. Can't stay out much longer. Need to know when it's safe._
Watcher Harissa sent me to find you.
_She did? Knew she wouldn't ... Wouldn't leave us out here. Took longer to get help than we thought._
_We still need help. Need to get out of Jhereth Deeps safely. Once we're out, we can get home ourselves._
I wasn't looking for you. I am hunting ogres.
_Well, you're of the Pact, yes? We are trapped here. Thought help would come from Watcher Harissa. Hasn't._
_We need help. Need to get out of Jhereth Deeps safely. Once we're out, we can get home ourselves._
I am [N], a Hand of Avadon on an important mission.
She looks you over. _A Hand? Avadon? Out here? We don't want to hurt your mission. But we're weak. You can see that._
Tell me why you are out here.
_When the ogres started to attack, the dragon told Watcher Harissa where he thought the ogres were. Harissa ordered us to come out here. See if we could find ogres._
She laughs dryly. _We found ogres._
You and Harissa are both Watchers? Why did she send you?
_A Watcher commands a Blade of ten soldiers. When several Blades are in one place, one Watcher is given precedence. That was Harissa._
_I didn't mind. I wanted to be out hunting. Though it's turned out to be hard._
I am looking for an ogre lair. Can you help me find it?
She nods. _Oh, there are ogres. Lots of them. They had a big fort to the southeast, but they abandoned it. Don't know where they went. They're still near, though._
Anything else you have seen?
She looks up. _A dragon. Saw it circling around. Several times over the last few days. It saw us. Didn't hunt us, didn't help us. Don't know where it lives._
One of the other scouts laughs and says, _Maybe we dreamed it._
How did those ogres trap you?
_Some of them saw us and gave chase. Then we ran into another group. Snuck up on us from behind. We were careless. Cocky. They were organized, for ogres._
That is happening a lot lately.
_Well, if we get back to warn the others, it won't happen again. No more complacency._
_We killed quite a few of them. Others trapped us here, but they were too afraid to attack. Just waited for us to pass out. Slit our throats. Then you came. Glad of it._
_We'll walk out of the Deeps. Just stay with us. Protect us if we run into ogres. That's all. But soon. We don't have much strength left._
Sevilin looks at them sadly. _My fellow warriors of The Kva, who have been through much. We need to help them now. No delays._
Jenell looks at them with sympathy. She whispers to you, _Brave warriors, trapped in this heat. We need to help them now. They won't last long._
All right. Leave. I will follow.
Watcher Akasa's command pick up their weapons and remaining provisions. _Once we are out of the depths, we can survive in the desert. Just need to be away from ogres. We know the best route. Follow._
They walk to the south, trying to stay as alert as possible. Some of them are already staggering.
Overseer Gruul
Just wait here for now.
Akasa tries to spit, but she doesn't have enough moisture left. _We don't have long out here. Help us escape soon, or the ogres will get us for sure._

You have trapped Neray in a cave here, full of supplies she was probably trying to sell to the ogres. She holds a blade in her right hand and a potion in her left. Her injured leg is causing her a lot of pain.
She spits on the ground, furious. _You again. What are you doing here? Why are you stalking me?_
What happened to your leg?
_Ogres are not like wretches. They can be dumber and they're always stronger. One of them didn't know that I was selling to their tribe. It threw a rock at me. I hope their chief flays him alive._
You are selling to the ogres?
_I sell to all creatures kept weak by the Pact. As long as they can pay, of course. The Pact has no right to decide who has the right to arm themselves._
Sevilin says, _Interesting how your morality allows you to turn a profit. Even though it allows these creatures to hunt my people._
Jenell says, _I believe in Right of Arms, but not for thugs, raiders, and killers. You are not honorable._
I have been tasked to hunt you down.
_Well, of course. I guessed that. I don't know who thinks my trade does so much harm. But, out here, there is no way to tell whether I was killed or not. I have a proposition for you..
I am [N], Hand of Avadon, and you violate our laws.
She smirks. _A Hand of Avadon? I know your kind. Your view of the law depends on the weight of the gold in my palm. I have a proposition for you._
_Let me go. I have earned a generous reward for my work here, cached throughout these hills. I will pay you, leave and never return. You say you killed me and collect your bounty._
_The smuggling ends, we all get what we want, and you don't have to risk getting killed by me. Is it a deal?_
Sevilin mutters, _I hope you don't consider it. She has blood on her hands._
Nathalie says, _I regret walking from a fight, but if we can conserve our strength and complete our mission? We should consider it._
How do I know you will leave?
_Because I am no fool. I am known. If I stay, Avadon will have my head sooner or later._
You think you can kill me?
_I do. You have stumbled into my trap. The only question is whether I will trip it._
Do you know who has been directing the ogres and wretches?
_I have an idea, but telling you will guarantee my doom. Don't waste your time asking._
It is a deal. Pay me, go, and never return.
She pulls a pouch from her belt and tosses it to you. it is heavy with gold. Then, before you can change her mind, she nods and walks out of the room.
Sevilin shakes his head.
No. You have acted against the Pact. You will die here.
The moment you say 'No,' she acts. She moves amazingly quickly. She drinks the potion. Then she lets out a loud whistle.
As you advance on her, you realize that she is moving with more confidence. The potion must be helping with her foot. She shouts, _Pets, come! Guards, come! The fool is surrounded!_
Smuggler
Shima looks over at you. He is trembling with anger. _We Hands of Avadon are a brotherhood. An attack on one is an attack on all. Someone has been murdering our fellows. They tried to kill us._
_I don't know who they are, but they will pay._
Sevilin nods. _Our honor demands it, and the Stone Code demands it. We will bring them to justice_
Jenell nods. _When I came to Avadon, I chose a second tribe. I owe my fellow Hands the same duty._
Nathalie looks over at him. _And when we have had vengeance, we can report it back to Avadon. That should get the attention of Redbeard!_ Shima doesn't seem as thrilled about that part.

You are surprised to find a familiar face here in Zephyrine's lair. It is Seeker Azarni, the Holklandan mage. She tried to learn a lost magical ritual from Zhethron. Failing that, it appears that she has come here.
She sits on a stone bench, sipping tea. You greet her, but it takes a moment for her to acknowledge your presence. She stares off into space.

Then she turns to look at you, but her eyes have a vacant, glazed expression. She says, slowly, _Hello to you. You ... I know you. You ... helped me. I am glad. To see you. A mighty dragon. Lives here._
Seeker Azarni looks up at you. Her expression is still eerily vacant. _I know you. Still. What else do. You want?_
Her robe is torn and filthy, and there is a strong odor. She has not been looking after herself. Maybe she can't.
_I ... I heard of the dragon. I came here. I have powers. The ogres could not. Touch me. See me. I came here to. Learn the ritual._
What ritual did you want to learn?
She tries to concentrate. She doesn't succeed. _The ritual of ... of ... I am not sure. It will come to me._
Where are your supplies?
_They are gone. The dragon. Feeds me. Gives me water._
_But ... Is the dragon still here? I don't sense it._
Does the dragon know the ritual?
_I ... I don't ... Don't know. It must know it. I am. Still here._
Have you met the dragon?
The Holklandan mage takes a while to answer. She is dazed. Something is clouding her mind. _The dragon. I have spoken. With it. A mighty creature. Lets me stay. Feeds me. I will. Help him._.
You want to stay here?
_How could I not? I will learn ... much. From the dragon._
How long will you stay?
She takes a deep breath. _As long as the dragon. Will have me. Its power is ... glorious. Is a joy. To be near it._ She smiles vacantly.
So you talked to the dragon and now you want to stay here?
She is confused for a moment. Then she says, _Yes. I wanted ... something. Talked. Talked so long. Dragon ... knew? What I wanted to know? Not sure. But dragon wanted my help._
And you decided to stay. After talking to the dragon.
_Yes. I wait here. Help. Is an honor._
Shima shudders with horror. _What has that wyrm done to her? This is a horror._
Nathalie frowns. _For a mage who is trying to learn how to focus her mind, she doesn't have much resistance to a magical charm._
Zephyrine is dead.
Azarni blinks. She shakes her head. _Yes. The dragon. Is. What has. Been done. To me? I ..._ She looks around, and it is as if she is seeing this hall for the first time.
_I was charmed. I must flee. I ... I thank you. Bless you. I must get away._
She takes a wand from her belt and hands it to you. Then she mutters a spell of protection and concealment, turns and runs.
You need to leave here with me.
Azarni suddenly regains the ability to focus. She looks up at you, and there is anger and mistrust in her eyes. _You would. Take me. The dragon. Warned me. I will not go. It is good here._
Never mind. You can stay where you want.
_Yes. I stay. Yes._ She calms down and sips her tea. _You upset me. Leave me._
You have been charmed. I have to take you away from here. (Pull her away.)
She jumps to her feet. At first, you think that she has come to her senses. Then she raises her hands. _The dragon said. I must. Defend myself. You will not. Take me. You will._
Flames start to rise from her outstretched hands. _Die._
_Yes. See the dragon. Talk to her. She will. Help you see._ You leave the dazed mage on her bench.
Your blow finally restores Seeker Azarni to her senses. She drops to her knees and raises her hands. _Wait. Stop._
Azarni blinks. _Yes. The dragon. What has. Been done. To me? I ..._ She looks around, and it is as if she is seeing this hall for the first time.

You approach the dragon. The creature's features are different from Zhethron. More delicate, more elegantly curved, and, when she speaks, her voice is softer and more sibilant. This must be the female of the species.
She is much younger than Zhethron, but just as much power radiates off her. And unpredictability. Youthful arrogance. Far from home, you feel much more at risk around her.

And yet, when she nods to you, she seems full of caution and respect. _Ahsssss ... Visitors. Not ogres. Human. I am Zephyrine. Who are you?_ As she speaks, your mind starts to feel cloudy. You feel compelled to respond.
I am [N].
_That is your name. And what else can I learn of you? You are a warrior. You are from the Pact. You have that much confidence. I want to know something else._
Zephyrine nods, but she seems slightly concerned. _Avadon? They are sending spies here already? That is not ... expected. I want to know something else._
I am [N]. Zhethron sent me to these lands.
Zephyrine suddenly seems interested. _Zhethron? The dragon to the north? An older specimen, but still a strong, confident male. Intriguing. I want to know something else._
You ask what Zephyrine wants, eager to help her. Then you realize that your mind is getting fogged. Fortunately, you have had the training to recognize when this is happening and fight it off.
Zephyrine is talking, but you ignore her. You concentrate and regain control. Then you look up at the dragon, who just asked you something.
Stop trying to control me.
Zephyrine shows you a broad, toothy smile. _It was not intentional. It is the power of dragons to inspire awe in all nearby._
_What do you want from me? Why have you come here?_
Are you trying to control a Hand of Avadon? Many have been killed for less.
Zephyrine shows you a broad, toothy smile, but you can see that she is slightly worried. _It was not intentional. It is the power of dragons to inspire awe in all nearby._
Stop. I have questions for you.
Zephyrine stops, surprised, She sees that her attempt to cloud your mind has failed. _I ... Yes. Of course. My kind is mighty and proud, but we want peace with the Pact._
My mission is secret.
_You do not have to say, but you should. I will not interfere, and I might help. I wish for good relations with your people. Profitable relations._
I am hunting ogres who attacked Zhethron.

You tell Zephyrine what happened. To your surprise, she is enraged. _What? Those creatures attacked one of my kind? A dragon? How dare they? They said nothing of this. I will not tolerate it! They must pay._
Some ogres have been raiding the Pact. I am looking for them.

You tell Zephyrine what happened. To your surprise, she is enraged. _What? Those creatures have been drawing the wrath of the Pact? And Avadon? They said nothing of this. I will not tolerate it! They must pay._
You have been helping the ogres?
The dragon is wary. _I help those who pay me. They asked me to help with minor tasks. They paid, and they helped to construct my new home. That is all. I break my connection with them._
I don't need any help.
_You think not. Perhaps you do not. But I will clear the way to the ogres anyway, so that you do not think me an ally to them._
_I will do this without asking tribute, because I came here to have good relations with the Pact. The ogres think they have concealed themselves from you. I will expose them._
The dragon turns and walks swiftly out of her dome. She seems genuinely angry with the ogres for drawing you here.
How will you aid me?
_I will clear the way to the ogres anyway, so that you do not think me an ally to them._
You return to speak with Zephyrine. She is still agitated. _You have returned, [N]? You should be hunting your ogres, before they flee._
_I would be happy to speak with you, but only when you are sure I am not allied with those traitorous creatures. Return here when they are destroyed and I will happily aid you._
I desire to speak with you now.
The dragon shakes her head. _I have been exposed to danger here, by the foul double-dealing of the ogres. Once they are dead, I will be safe to speak with you._
I will be back.
The dragon nods. _I wish you good hunting._

You return to the dragon Zephyrine. She seems much calmer now. _The ogres are gone. Their stink no longer bothers me. I will miss the help with construction of my new lair, but I am glad they have been punished for their foolishness and weakness._
_I wish nothing but peace with the warriors of Avadon. What do you wish of me?_

The dragon Zephyrine looks down at you, a serene half-smile on her face. You find you have to constantly concentrate to keep her aura of power from interfering with your thoughts. _What else do you wish of me?_
_I was sired and raised in southern peaks of The Corruption. When I came of age, I knew it was time to emerge and grow my hoard. Thus, I emerged from the darkness and came here._

_A place of wild, uncontrolled magic, a place where foolish humans tore the barrier between this place and the darkness of the beyond. It is full of chaos and creatures that threaten small creatures like you._
_For me, it was a joyous, wild place to come of age. But, eventually, we must emerge and find our hoard._
She flutters her eyelids and smiles, amused. _Is that not an impolite question among your kind? I am fully of age, if you must know. I emerged from my egg over two centuries ago._
Why didn't you remain in The Corruption?
_You do not understand the appeal of travel, of adventure? Why did you not stay in whatever village you were raised in?_

_I have come here to build a lair and to grow a hoard. I am not secretive like many of my kind. I have seen the wealth and respect that comes from dealing with your frail, short-lived kind, and I want a part of it._
And this is your lair?
_This is the beginnings of it. When I can find more workers to compel, I will expand it. Perhaps I can find a tribe of skilled wretches and expand into the ogre tunnels._
_One day, it will be glorious. For now, it is adequate._
What will you do for the Pact?
_Fight. Advise. Share knowledge. Simply travel and awe with my presence. I understand that Zhethron turns away most of his supplicants. Surely he will not mind if I use them to grow my hoard._
Tell me about your hoard.
_It is the great sign of prestige among my kind. Mounds of gold. Jewels. Magical artifacts. Everything else melts away. Humans. Nations. But gold is eternal, like we wish to be._
_By growing my hoard, I show my power and desirability to all of my kind, the only ones who I truly respect._
How large a hoard have you accumulated?
Zephyrine shifts uncomfortably. _It is unwise to ask a dragon such questions. Anything that makes you seem like a thief puts you in danger. We are suspicious creatures. Ask of something else._
Where is your hoard?
_That is not a question you can ask,_ Zephyrine snaps. _We dragons deal harshly with those we suspect might be thieves. I have said enough on this matter. Ask of something else._
I want to ask about you and the ogres.

Zephyrine is immediately on her guard. _I told you, very little. I helped them to become established here. They helped to build my lair. I found they were drawing the hostility of the Pact, and I abandoned them._
How exactly did you help them?

Zephyrine thinks carefully, deciding how much to tell you. You doubt that full candor is forthcoming. _I collapsed some valleys to help in their defenses. I told them of things I saw when flying overhead. I ... Nothing more. Nothing that should draw the anger of Avadon._
Did they pay you?

_They gave me labor. And a fair amount of gold. I don't know where they got the gold. I imagine they ... found it._ She speaks uncertainly, not used to deceit. You are sure that she knows more about who was helping the ogres than she says.
As powerful as the dragon is, she seems relieved. _Then you are satisfied. I ask that you leave me. I have much to do to maintain my lair._ She waves you away.
You were helping Farlanders. That is a crime.

Zephyrine rises up to her full height. The air becomes cold enough to freeze your exposed flesh. She speaks, her casual attitude completely gone. _I know you. You are from Avadon. You think you can judge me. I do not need to submit to you._
_I helped the ogres. Then I abandoned them. You will have to be content with that. I see this matter as closed._
I am a Hand of Avadon. The matter is closed when I say it is, and you must answer for your deeds.

_Ahsssss ... And you think you will make me submit? Maybe you will. Or maybe you are here, alone, far from Avadon, and I will devour you whole and nobody will ever know what became of you._ She rises and stands on all fours, ready to pounce.
_Say I am innocent, or face my wrath. Those are your choices, little human._
You are innocent. I wish no conflict.
You back down. Zephyrine stares you in the eyes and nods. _Then we can deal peacefully, once we have had time to calm ourselves. Leave me._ She waves you away.
If I have to fight you to bring you to justice, I will.
Zephyrine nods slowly. She evaluates your equipment. _Your wealth will add to my hoard admirably, and your absence will make my life much easier. I have made my decision. I will slay you now._
And she pounces ...

_I am no merchant. My services are available, for tribute. For far more than the wealth I can smell on you. But if you would let your Pact know that my power can be put at its service, I would appreciate it._
I want to talk to you about Seeker Azarni.
_My visitor? An honored guest? What do you wish to know of her?_
Why did she come to see you?
_She wished to learn of some lost Holklandan ritual. I know nothing of it. She decided to stay to offer her skills to me in building my fort. I did not refuse._
You have clouded her mind.

_I have done no such thing. She is simply in awe of my might. As she should be. If she does not choose to leave, it is no business of yours. Now go, and come back when you can be civil._ The dragon waves you away.
I don't need to know anything else about her.
_And my dealings with her are our business, not yours. What else would you know?_
I have released Seeker Azarni.
The dragon smiles. _Released? How can you say released? She was not a prisoner. But, if she wished to leave, I wish her a safe journey home. And I have nothing more to say of it._
I have a message from Zhethron.

She sits up, instantly very interested in what you have to say. _Really? You are a dragon's first envoy? You? How intriguing. I want to hear what you have to say._ The air is growing very cold. Zephyrine's claws dig into the stone. Her entire body is tense.
I ... forget.
Zephyrine slumps back to the ground. _You waste my time. You are not a worthy envoy for a dragon. I dismiss you._ She waves you away.
Zhethron wants to know what your intentions are.
Zephyrine laughs. _Why don't you all gather near and say that again._

Zephyrine laughs, a harsh, hissing noise. _I had heard that, out here, a dragon could send envoys to test another. I enter Zhethron's territory, but he sends you to face me? Well, I will tell you my intentions. If you present your strength._
She slowly begins to stalk forward.
Wait. Face you? Present my strength? What?
Zephyrine is amused. _And Zhethron didn't tell you of our ways? You aren't even prepared? How amusing. Well, don't worry. I do not want to kill you. Only try you. You might even live._
And, before you can respond, she pounces ...
Step back, lizard, or you will soon be missing a hand.

Zephyrine is thrilled. _Zhethron must have searched hard to find envoys so foolhardy. I am amused by his selection. Don't worry. I do not want to kill you. Only try you. If you live, you can say that you have pleased me._
I only came here to speak with you.

Zephyrine is amused. _You did not just speak. You challenged my right to be in Zhethron's lands. The elder wyrm didn't tell you of our ways? You aren't even prepared? How amusing. Well, don't worry. I do not want to kill you. Only try you. You might even live._
I am looking for a dragon's tooth.
_Ahssss ... Amusing. I can't help you. All of my teeth are currently in use. I would advise against your trying to borrow one._
That is all I want to know.
_Then I bid you farewell, and I hope you convey words of peace from me to the Pact. My services are available. For tribute._
Zephyrine raises a clawed hand into the air. _Hold. I am satisfied. Zhethron has shown strength._ You note that she isn't even breathing hard.
_I will tell him my intentions. I will stay here. I will encroach no farther. I will trade with humans. I mean no harm to him. I might even consider ... meeting him._
_Now go. I must have a moment to let the bloodlust pass._ She turns back to her platform.
Zephyrine roars with anger. _You dare strike me? You would have my blood? You think I have no defenses? Come, servant! Sustain me!_
One of the stone statues in the outer circles comes slowly to life. It lumbers toward you, massive granite fists raised. A faint tether of greenish light connects the creature to the dragon.

Zephyrine has been wounded. Trickles of black blood run down her flanks. Slowly, she abandons the veneer of calm and civilization she adopted. She returns to the wild, mindless, savage state of dragons of old, lunging toward you in a berserk fury.

Zephyrine screams mindlessly. Pain and rage have consumed her. Her power starts to flow out of her without limit. Whirlwinds of snow and ice begin to fill the dome, buffeting you. It becomes very hard to stay on your feet.
Zephyrine collapses, mortally wounded. In her last moments, she regains some of her calm. _So ... my sire was right ... never underestimate the ... the ... little creatures._
_I was a ... a fool. But I will be aven ... aven ... The Pact is doomed. I have seen ... seen it. I was ... told. You will ... will ..._
Her eyes lose their sight. The dragon is dead.
Remembering what Alfons told you in Goldcrag, you extract one of the dragon's teeth. It is more than fresh enough for his purposes.
Zephyrine snorts. _You cannot ask to be tested and then flee. I will reject Zhethron's message until you face me honestly!_ She calms herself and returns to her platform.

Zephyrine points at one of the huge boulders blocking the valley and mutters a spell. As you watch in awe, the rock lifts into the air and then falls away from you, clearing a path through the valley.
As you start to round the corner, you hear someone coming. You start to prepare an ambush. Then you hear voices. They are humans. Perhaps other Hands.
You step back into the shadows, trying to conceal yourself until you can see who they are.

Several humans come into view. They wear torn chain mail and leather, and an ugly assortment of weapons are hanging from their belts or slung over their shoulders. They're not Hands, though. They are too dirty and disorganized. And violent.
You watch them from the shadows, hoping to hear what they have to say.
As they talk, you notice something. Their leader only wears one glove. His exposed left hand is a twisted thing, covered with burn scars and curled into a useless lump.
Nathalie taps you on the shoulder. She whispers, _That man. I've heard of him. Sevilin told me. He's Cahil, one of the men who ambushed his patrol._
Shima tugs on your sleeve. He whispers, _That man. I've heard of him. Sevilin told me. He's Cahil, one of the men who ambushed his patrol._
Jenell taps you on the shoulder. She whispers, _That man. I've heard of him. Sevilin told me. He's Cahil, one of the men who ambushed his patrol._
You try to hear more of what they are saying. Then the brigands begin to move ...
Sevilin lets out a soft, choking noise. You turn to look at him. He is deathly pale, frozen in place. He swallows and whispers, _That is him._
_That hand ... the scars. He's Cahil, the one who ambushed my patrol. Killed my ..._ His voice trails off.
Wait. Let's see what they say.
You expect Sevilin to ignore you, to try to jump into action. He doesn't. He's frozen. Satisfied that he won't disobey you, you turn and watch the brigands.
Then the brigands begin to move ...
Come on. Let's kill them.
You expect Sevilin to jump to action, but he doesn't. He's frozen. You pull on his arm. He only shrinks farther back into the shadows.

The brigands are safely up the stairs. You step out of the shadows when you are sure that they are gone. There were a lot of them, well-armed, and fighting them now might keep you from catching the ogres in time.
Nathalie blurts out, _What? We just let them go? They murdered Hands, and we stand here?_
Shima says, _It might have been good tactics to let them pass, but it would not have been my choice._
Jenell says, _It is good that we let them pass. We have more important goals._
Sevilin says nothing. He leans in the corner, shaking, reliving the ambush where he was the only survivor.
We should chase them.
Sevilin looks at you. He is starting to regain his composure. _No. They will be dealt with. I just ... need time. Do not worry._
_We have a task to do. No more delays._ He starts to walk out into the hall.
They can be dealt with later. We have work to do.
Sevilin looks at you. He is starting to regain his composure. _Yes. You are right. They will be dealt with. Not yet. I ... need time._
_For now, we have a task to do. No more delays._ He starts to walk out into the hall.
They can be dealt with later. There is work to do.
It is difficult to allow murders of your fellow Hands to go, but calming the dragon seems like a more important task.
And you suspect that, if they are active in this area, Sevilin will learn of it sooner or later.

When you run into this room, you see a mage run for the northern gate. She wears loose robes and has a pack on her back. Then she looks back at you and realizes that she waited too long. She can't just escape. She has to fight you.

She turns and claps her hands. The gates to the north and south slam shut, trapping you in the room with her. Then she turns to face you. Her skin is pale. She must be from the northern parts of Tawon.
She says, in a soft, cultivated voice, _Greetings, [N]. I am Merula, mage of the Farlands. As, I think, you have guessed. I did not think you would reach me so easily._
The dragon Zephyrine helped me.
_Really? Probably claimed she had no idea what we were doing. She lies. That treacherous creature will help anyone with enough gold. Even Farlanders._
_But that doesn't matter. There is something I am sure your masters want to know._
I was sent by Zhethron.
_Of course. The dragon is furious, I am sure, when I sacrificed so many foolish ogres to annoy it. And, when you never return, it will be angrier still._
Criminals and Farlanders will never escape the gaze of Avadon.
_That is what you would like to think, I am sure. But soon, the number of the 'criminals' will be far beyond what you can control._
I'm not interested in talking to you.
_Really? But you should be. You can't ignore the wishes of your masters. There is something Avadon wants very much to know. _

You keep Merula talking, giving you a chance to think. Her accent sounds familiar. You suspect she is from the Tawon Empire, in the northeast corner of Lynaeus. But if that is true, she is far from home.
She responds, _They want to know who is controlling me. Who is giving the orders. Who is murdering the Hands that Avadon is sending out into the wilds as fast as it can._
Hands are being killed?
_Oh, yes. They won't tell you, so I will. One at a time, they have been whittled away. That is why ones as young and unreliable as you have been sent out on important missions._
_And yet, they did not tell you. I wonder why._
Why would you tell me anything?
_Trust me, I am no fool. I talk to you because I might not succeed in killing you. If I die, I need you to know something first._
I won't let you fill my head with lies. Die. (Attack.)

Merula sighs, disappointed. _A loyal cog to the last._ She steps into one of her magic circles. A glowing nimbus instantly surrounds her. _Then I suppose I have no choice but to live._ And she begins to cast a spell.
What message do you wish to send?

She laughs. _I have no words for the fools in your tower, squandering their last moments in pretend safety. I tried to anger the dragon Zhethron and divide him from you. I failed. That is done. Now my message is for you._

_A time is coming. A time when you can choose. When you realize that you don't have to serve Redbeard forever. You can overthrow him and join us. You will gain wealth, fame, power, all in a new world._
_Even if you kill me, you will someday have the chance to see your errors._
And spend my time hiding in a mud pit with a bunch of ogres? No, thank you.
Merula says, _If I die, it is sad that my last days will have been here. But it is what I sacrifice to give my people hope._
I will consider what you say.
She nods. _It is all I can ask. The Pact cruelly crushes the Farlands. All I ask is that they have hope._
Why would I ever turn my back on the Pact?
_I don't know. You can only answer that for yourself. But, one day, you may see the true face of those who send you off to kill and die._
No. It will never happen. (Attack.)
So what happens now?
_Now, we must fight. I think you have potential. Others do not. I have orders to kill you. I will follow them._
You speak wisdom. Perhaps I can just let you flee.
_You are kind, but I swore to obey the one that leads us. Merula is a soldier, and she trusts the wisdom of her master. Also, our master is not kind to those he suspects of collaboration._
She steps into one of her magic circles. A glowing nimbus instantly surrounds her. _And, if I can, I will live._ And she begins to cast a spell.
It's about time. (Attack.)
She steps into one of her magic circles. A glowing nimbus instantly surrounds her. _This is a punishment for my failure. But, if I can, I prefer to live._ And she begins to cast a spell.
Merula is surrounded by a shower of sparks. The air warps around you. And then ...

... she is somewhere else. She stands in a different magical circle, and two imps flank her to either side. She smiles. _I was too slow to escape, but I do have my own little tricks. I will live, if I can._
Merula has received several sharp blows. She wipes blood from her lips with the back of her hand. _Well played. You are a cunning foe. Avadon still has the best warriors._

_But I have other tricks. I had hoped not to use this, but ..._ She touches a pendant that hangs from her neck and mutters a word of command. The necklace crumbles into dust. A moment later, a reflective shield surrounds her.
With one final blow, you knock Merula out of her circle. She collapses to the ground, mortally wounded. She looks up at you. _Renounce ... Avadon. Slay ... Redbeard. Otherwise ... you will die._
Who gives you your orders? Tell me!
_You will ... learn. One day, you ... will ..._ Her eyes close. A foe of the Pact has died.
You must return to Zhethron. He will be pleased to hear of your triumph.
I will remember you and consider what you said.
Merula nods. _I can ask ... no ..._ Her eyes close. A foe of the Pact has died.
You are suffering the fate of all who fight the Pact.
Merula grimaces. _Ohhhh ... Oh ... shut ... up ..._ Her eyes close. A foe of the Pact has died.
Merula
There is nobody near Merula. She takes the opportunity to heal herself.
Merula's reflective shield fades. Long spines grow out of her robe.
Merula's spines dry up and drop off. A reflective shield surrounds her.
Talking: Merula waits for you to approach.
Neray
Neray opens the trapdoor and jumps downstairs.
You examine the stone spire. It has a strange blue tinge. Unusual, but not valuable.
You examine the stone spire. You have already mined as much ore out of it as you can.
You examine the stone spire. It has a strange blue tinge. You knock some ore off of it and put it in a sack. You won't be able to get more without a team of actual miners.
One of the escaping scouts falls in battle.
A scout flees to safety.
Talking: The scouts are too busy to talk. They're running for their lives.
Gravecaller Detra
Slimy Titan Zombie
Chief Chanakk
Charmed Bones
Frozen Bones
Arrogant Drake
A huge lizard wriggles out of the slime and muck.
Shnrunk
Wretch Slave
Talking: The wretch is too busy fleeing you to talk more.
Kva Archer
Kva Warrior
Talking: The soldiers aren't going to make small talk while the assault is in progress.
Splinterbone
Slavering Dire Wolf
Kva Commander

Conjurer Danmus
Battlemaster Khoral

Conjurer Thyslea
You are here.
We have waited for you.
Can the assault begin?
One of the western gates is now fully open. Wolves pour out.
Trained War Wolf
Gnarled Hellhound
Another of the western gates is now fully open. Wolves pour out.
The last of the western gates is now fully open. Wolves pour out.
Chanakk's Dire Wolf

You enter an enormous cactus thicket deep within the Wretch Lands. The safety of the Pact is far behind you now. And, though this is the region set aside by the Pact for wretches to breed and roam free, there are few wretches here.
Instead, the unmistakable tracks of titans are everywhere, sunk deep in the parched soil. There are also the parallel lines of sledge tracks, used by the titans to haul equipment and bricks.
Zhethron was right. This is where a large band of titans have settled. They have had plenty of time to settle in and build fortifications.
You were told that a band of soldiers were sent here ahead of you. Before assaulting the titan stronghold, it might be wise to see if you can find anyone who can aid you.

This small, dank, filthy warren is the lair of a titan. The creature has been here for some time, definitely since long before the others of his kind arrived. It smells vile. There is nothing in here you would want to touch with your hands.
The occupant is currently away, but it might be annoyed to find you here.
You manage to sneak up on the rear gate of the titan fortification. A wall of massive stones blocks this passage. Titans look out at you through narrow windows and through huge iron gates.
They lift smooth round stones, the sort they can gather, shape, and throw with lethal speed and accuracy. You might be able to kill the guards, but you won't be able to get through from this side.

Zhethron spoke truly. There is, indeed, a camp of Pact soldiers here. They have constructed their own palisade and watch for attackers. The titans know that the invaders are here, and they have lost quite a few of their number trying to dislodge the soldiers.

But these human victories have not been without cost. The soldiers are bruised and exhausted, and most of them wear red-stained bandages. When they see that you have arrived, they wave and let out a weak cheer.
You approach a titan palisade, guarded by a large band of massive defenders. The titans watch you get closer. Some lift throwing stones. Others raise huge war clubs.
The thought of breaking through these creatures' defensive lines without help gives you pause. Perhaps the soldiers Zhethron sent ahead might be able to help.

You enter the broad field in front of the titan keep. Their fortress is still under construction, and there are materials scattered all over the sandy field ahead of you. Some equipment was bought from smugglers. The rest was stolen from wretch and human colonies.
The walls of the titan fortress are visible from here. Even half-done, they are already a formidable defense. The ground before them is scorched. This must be where Zhethron attacked and was wounded.
It is lucky that you arrived when you did. Much later, and the titans will be very difficult to dislodge.
As you survey the territory ahead, the guards at the enemy gates see you. There is a burst of shouting and activity as they prepare their final charge.
You enter the titan keep, expecting a vicious battle. The result is anti-climactic.
You are surrounded by abandoned camps. And abandoned workshops. And half-finished buildings left behind by their workers.
While you were fighting to the south, the remaining titans fled. The keep is abandoned. Most surviving warriors fled into the wilds of the Titan Peaks. The tribe is broken, but not destroyed.
And yet, your work is not finished. You still need to search the keep for signs of who was directing them, and why. And, somehow, you suspect that at least one trap was left behind.
You enter the halls of the titan fortress. You expect a bunch of small, dank storage caves. The reality is far more impressive.

The titans have been building a spectacular hall down here. It is enormous, and the ceiling is held up by many pillars. Two things are obvious. One, they were planning to settle in for a long time. Two, they are well-defended from any attack from the air.

The hall has mostly been abandoned. As you suspected upstairs, most of the titans have fled. However, at least one of them remains. He is to the south, watching you through a huge steel portcullis. When he sees you, he nods and waves you forward.

This hall is still under construction. Despite all of the chaos outside, the builders are still hard at work digging in the wall to the east. Why are they still working? The question is soon answered.

Most of the workers are zombies. Animated titans, skin blue with cold, digging in the clay until their bodies literally fall apart. They are led by a stone construct, a huge, animated statue that directs them. But how did the titans obtain such sophisticated magic?
The creatures have shown no signs of noticing you. You wonder what will happen when they detect you.
Nothing has been carved into this obelisk yet. It probably awaits the name of the chieftain or something.
You turn the wheel and open the west gates. Then you smash the mechanism, leaving the gates stuck open. If the titans reclaim their fort, that is another job they will have to do.
The wheel mechanism is still smashed.

The titan returns to his lair, his pet dire wolves behind him, and finds small, irritating, delicious invaders within it. He shouts, _You in lair of Splinterbone! Little thief! I eat you! Take skull to tribe! They let me in!_
He drops the chains and releases his wolves. Then he lets out a long, angry roar, raises his club, and charges.

One of the final titans left behind to guard the fortress raises his horn to his lips and blows. A single bass note echoes through the thickets. Then, from the fort, you hear the howling of many wolves.
The pack has been summoned. The final defense of the fortress begins.
You try to open the sarcophagus. The moment you touch it, frost covers your hands. The ice races up your arms, hunting for your heart. You jump away.
You open the sarcophagus. It is full of bones and rotten scraps of cloth. There is also a silken cord that has somehow escaped decay. Seems like fair payment for the circlet. You take it.
There is nothing of value left in the stone coffin.
This shade has been down here for a long time. Its features have faded almost entirely away. You suspect it is the ghost of a human. It doesn't respond to your presence in any way.

There is a large wooden case in this corner of the trophy room. You open it and find an assortment of titan-sized weapons. Most are dented and broken, trophies taken from fallen foes. A few are intact, but far too large for you to use.

One club catches your eye. It is a ceremonial weapon, and the workmanship of the iron in the head is quite lovely. The metal is smooth and polished, and its surface has a strange pattern of dark, flowing, curving lines.
This must be the weapon Berak asked you to recover. You strap the heavy thing across your back.
This box is full of ceremonial items. Torn robes, small blocks of incense, scrolls bearing tales of titan folklore. To a sage studying titan culture, this trove would be invaluable. To you, not much.
But one item does catch your eye. It's a bronze circlet. It's human-sized, heavy with tarnish, and very, very old.
Recalling your odd encounter with the ghost in the nearby crypt, you put the circlet into your pack.
Except for ashes and a few scraps of torn parchment, this chest is empty.

You open the chest and find that it is full of papers. Crude maps. Scrawled letters, some of them in code. Chief Chanakk was trying to burn them, but he started too late. A number of the scrolls still remain. It is from such mishaps that wars can be won or lost.
Heart Miranda would be very interested in seeing these materials. Others, you are sure, would be very happy if they were destroyed.
Take the papers.
You carefully gather the surviving intelligence and place it into your pack. Avadon will be most pleased.
Burn the papers.
You take some coals from the nearby brazier and drop them into the chest. One minute later, you have a merry blaze. Two minutes later, all that remains are ashes. You kick the box shut.
You carefully close Chief Chanakk's chest.

A massive titan runs out of the shadows. It is a hideous creature, twisted, bent over, and covered with warts the size of oranges. It bares brown, chipped teeth at you and lets out an incoherent howl. A thick rope of saliva dangles down to its chest.
Then the hideous creature says, by way of introduction, _Hrrrraghhh! Shnrunk stomp! Shnrunk kill! Shnrunk eat!_ Then Shnrunk takes proactive steps to carry out this three-part plan.
Shnrunk lets out another howl of rage, if anything more bestial and mindless than the one before. He reaches deep into his insane heart and redoubles his efforts to crush you.

As you walk through this training hall, the reek of war wolves grows heavier. A closed gate is visible through the opening to the south. A huge, shadowy figure watches you from behind it. The chief, watching your progress. He shouts, _Now! Release my pets!_

The gate behind you begins to close. One of the three gates in the west wall begins to open. Chief Chanakk is determined to only face you after all those who stayed with him have a chance to kill you. You hear the howls of wolves. Big ones.

You are surrounded by piles of the chieftain's trained war wolves. A distant keening noise echoes through the halls. It takes you a moment to realize what it is: Chief Chanakk, mourning the loss of his pets.
The gate to the east slowly begins to open again. You will have to find another way deeper into the lair.

The hideous, unliving construction workers have been destroyed. With their help, the titans might have been able to continue building their defenses. Now that they are gone, this fort is free to crumble into ruin.
You hear the now-familiar sound of chains scraping over stone to the west. A gate is slowly opening. Perhaps the chieftain has finally deemed you worthy of facing him.

The head shaman of the titan tribe is still at this stained altar, seemingly unaware that anything of note has been going on outside. She reeks of rot and decay. She must be the source of the zombified titans. Her vile reek and appearance makes you think she is half zombie herself.

When you are close to her, she finally detects you. She spits and lets out a long, shrill shout. Creatures begin to emerge from the water to the east, waterlogged and covered with slime from the pools.
The chieftain's body is covered with an increasing number of nasty bruises and slashes. The pain isn't driving the creature mad with rage, though. If anything, he is more calm, more focused.
He steps back, closes his eyes, and takes a deep breath. He opens his eyes when you press the attack, and he charges back at you. His movements are faster and his aim is more precise.
The chieftain is finally starting to become winded. He stumbles and almost falls to one knee. Instead, he rallies, straightens up, and puts a hand around one of the bone charms hanging from his neck.
He squeezes it, crushing it into powder. The dust falls to the ground and then forms into several forms.
And then the last of the titans defending this fort prepares to fight to the death.

You meet a titan. He is an old, filthy, gnarled creature, flanked by a pair of enormous dire wolves. When he turns to face you, you have to cover your nose. The reek of the creature is truly overpowering.
He looks down at you and snarls, revealing his last few remaining teeth. This creature is old. He has been out here since long before the titan invaders arrived.
He says, _I Splinterbone! This my land. Was my land. You a tasty little thing. Maybe eat you. Show young titans I am strong._
The titan Splinterbone looks down at you, drooling slightly. He is clearly contemplating how delicious a meal you would be. It's a little bit unnerving.
_Doing here? This land of Splinterbone! Been so since ... many years. You on my land now!_ The wolves snarl at you. He pulls on the chains holding them back.
Do you know anything about the other titans?
_Other titans? Ghahhh!_ He breathes harder. The smell becomes worse. _Little, noisy things. Turn away Splinterbone. Laugh at Splinterbone. Need to prove I strong. Need to ... hunt?_
He inspects you, gears turning very slowly in his head.
I am from Avadon. You will assist me.
_I ... Avadon? What Avadon? Splinterbone no serve little things. Eat them!_
I was sent here to hunt titans.

Splinterbone grins. _You sent to hunt? You enemy of many titans? You what Splinterbone looks for! Thing to kill! Prove self! Join tribe! Eat good at last!_ He drops the chains he used to restrain the wolves. They leap forward.
_Kill! Splinterbone kill!_ The titan roars and begins to stomp his feet.
I have no quarrel with you. I will just move on. (Leave.)
Splinterbone looks at your weapons and nods. _You little, but strong. You hurt titans. Me stay back. You no go Splinterbone home._ He walks away, pulling his wolves behind him.
Splinterbone is wounded and furious. He begins to stamp his feet harder.

Splinterbone collapses to the ground, a big, stinking pile of dead titan. It's almost a pity. The creature only kept to himself, relatively harmless. If the other titans hadn't arrived and started bothering the dragon, he probably would have died of natural causes.
This dire wolf is huge, old, and ugly. If the titan wasn't holding it back with a chain, it would leap for your throat in an instant.

A quiet, shadowy figure steps out of the thickets behind you. Even before you turn, you have a good idea who it is. The Wayfarer gives you a little bow. Then he steps off the path and into the shadow of a large cactus.
_I am glad that you are here. I have only a little time to spare out here in these wastes. I will only take a moment of your time, and then I will be gone._
_Following the tracks of Pact soldiers. I knew they were coming to meet you. And I had some interest in seeing for myself the creatures that could bring a dragon down from the sky._
I haven't had time to deal with Commander Ryozo yet.
_Well, you should hurry. The traitor will flee soon, and then the chance will be lost._
I found the evidence of Ryozo's treachery. He has been taken.
The Wayfarer nods. _I am aware of it, and I made sure that your reward was left for you. Avadon is fortunate to have such a hard-working servant._
I found papers describing Ryozo's treachery. I destroyed them.

The Wayfarer sounds understandably annoyed. _You had the good fortune to find such obvious proof of treachery, and you destroyed it? It will be a long time before you have such a treasure dropped into your lap._
Tell me why you have sought me out.
The Wayfarer nods. _You have come here to hunt titans. The titans are doomed. They will all be dead soon. The Pact soldiers will kill them, or you will._
_When they fall, there is something that my employer wishes._
I will have no more dealings with you. (Turn and leave.)
_Your loss,_ he says. _One day you may be more receptive to my generous offers._
You walk down the path for a minute and then look back. He is leaving.
How are you so sure that they will die?
_The dragon Zhethron failed to kill them, but he did succeed in drawing attention to them. Avadon will not tolerate titans in these lands. Zhethron doomed them without realizing it._
There are Pact soldiers here?
_They were sent ahead of you. They are camped not far to the south. They have been beaten heavily, and your arrival will be a great relief to them. But enough talk. The heat bothers me._

_The titans' chieftain has papers. Maps. Letters. Correspondence from forces who supported the titans in their journey here. I will reward you very well if those papers are burned. They must never leave the titan fort._
Who is your employer?
_I think you know me well enough to know that I cannot say. But enough talk. The heat bothers me._
_I will be brief, so that I can escape this heat._
Avadon sent me to look for those papers.
_Yes, but Avadon does not expect to receive them. If you report that they were burned, you will not be questioned for a moment._
It sounds like you are asking me to act against Avadon.
_I can see how it might sound that way, but the political games in progress are very complicated. And, really, how can a few dirty scrawls in a titan's bedroom be important?_
_For all you know, I am working for other Eyes and Hands. Simply focus on the reward I offer you._
And I will be paid?
_Oh, very well. I will put the gold and gems in your hand personally when next we meet._
There is no way that I will do this.
_Disappointing. It is always sad when one is offered a route to greatness and rejects it. But you might change your mind. If you do, the reward will remain._
_That is all I have to say. I wish you victory. I must leave now. When I complete one task, two spring up._ He bows, turns, and leaves.
_I am pleased. The wisdom of your actions will become apparent in time._
Jenell looks around the crypt and shudders. _This place feels ... wrong. Never understood the desire to let your bones rot in a stone box. It's not right. And it attracts wrong things._
Shima smiles. _All respect to the Wyldrylm, but how can you expect a comfortable life in the afterworld if you don't properly seal the body in this world?_
Sevilin seems defensive. _This is the way of The Kva. It is how we give the lost a more comfortable existence in the afterworld. Or so the priests tell us, anyway._
Jenell shudders. _Can't you feel that? Whoever was buried here, they aren't in the afterworld. They're here._
What do you do with bodies in the Wyldrylm?
_We take them into the wilds and cremate them. The ashes are then sent to the dust from which we come._
_It is not what all do, but it has its points. Apart from the spiritual aspects, it makes it much more difficult to return our dead to life and send them to attack us._
_But enough talk. Let's do what we need to and leave._
You sense something ahead?
_You can't? There is a wrongness. It holds away nature. It is unlife, which defies all about how the world should work. It ..._ She sighs. _I'm sure you get the point. I don't like it._
(Move on silently.)
Jenell walks beside you, determined to settle your business and get out of here.
You notice that Sevilin is walking with a jaunt in his step. Despite the upcoming battles with gigantic, fierce titans, he seems to be in a good mood.
He looks over at you and smiles. _Sorry. Can't help but be in a good mood. I have returned home, and, at my age, I already have my own command. It's almost enough to give me hope._
Nathalie says, _Well, I thought I would be here well before now. But, now that it has finally happened, you are correct. It is nice._
Shima says, _I do not like the added responsibility. I've seen what it leads to. My father had to watch over many. It led to disaster._ Sevilin edges away from Shima a little.
As you start to enter the titans' training hall, Nathalie stops moving. Something is bothering her.
Is something wrong ahead?
_Of course something is wrong ahead. It's an obvious trap. But that is not the problem. I am thinking about the drake. The one that attacked you in the Beraza Woods. The one that got away._
Jenell rolls her eyes and mutters, _Here we go._
_I learned about it from the Eyes. They were discussing it. As an interesting specimen, not something to hunt. It attacked Hands, and we are letting it go free. Do you think that is right?_
Nathalie nods. _Of course. Let us walk into this obvious trap. But what I am thinking of will be discussed later._ She follows you.
Hunting it is a good idea.
She nods. _I thought you would say so. You are a Hand after my own heart. You will go out and hunt, even if Avadon does not recognize your value._
_But that is for after the titans are dealt with. We will discuss this later._
Those are not our orders.

_But they should be,_ she whispers. _That is a dangerous beast, and it tried to kill a Hand. it should be hunted and slain, and its head should be taken back to Avadon to teach them that they should have some spine._

As you approach the abandoned titan workshop, Shima leaps ahead of you. He runs to the entrance, moving in almost total silence. He disappears into the shadows, sitting wrapped up motionless in his cloak so that he looks like a stone.

Then he jumps up and advances from pillar to pillar, moving with remarkable deftness. Even if there were guards, they would never notice him. And, finally, satisfied that there are no traps or ambushes, he returns to you.
_Sorry,_ he says. _I need to keep my skills in practice, in case we ever infiltrate an enemy stronghold with care instead of noisily blundering into it._ He takes his place by your side.
Sevilin quietly says, _I'm actually quite a fan of blundering._

You greet the leader of this small raiding force of elite soldiers, here to help you deal with the titan incursion. He is an old, leathery veteran of many campaigns in these harsh deserts. He's probably been hunting foes of the Pact in this harsh wasteland since before you were born.

And yet, when he greets you, he bows and then gives you a sharp salute. He says, with a touch of nervous awe, _You must be [N], sent from Avadon to command us. I am Monitor Pelin. These are my troops._
_We are at your command, and still ready to fight. Lead us against the titans, and we will follow._
Monitor Pelin continues to stand at attention. He is a warrior of the old school, and he knows how much respect the warriors of Avadon command. _We are ready to fight. Just say the word._
Tell me about yourself, Monitor.
