Monitor Pelin seems slightly surprised. _Sorry, I ... Wasn't expecting any chat. Been out here a while, you know. But I will do my best._
_I'm a Monitor, but most of the Blades in my command are back safely in The Kva. I volunteered to lead this group. Don't know enough to stay where it's safe, I guess. They call me the Lion._
The Lion?

_That's the name they gave me. Just because I always end up at the front of every charge. My mother tried to give me sense. Guess it didn't take._ His soldiers chuckle. Their respect for him is apparent.
How many are under your command?
_Overall? A little over a hundred. That's a monitor's command. My second is watching over them, though, while I'm out here._
_The southlands of The Kva, born and raised. When I came of age, I became a soldier. Never looked back. Fighting for The Kva. And following the orders of Avadon, when they notice us._
And what do you think of Avadon?
Now he looks very nervous. _I'd love to talk to you about it over an ale sometime. But, for now, we should discuss the titans. If it is all right._
I think that's enough chat.
Pelin seems relieved. _Then we can discuss the assault._
Tell me the situation.

_Well, the dragon was right when it said where the titans were. They're here. Lots of them. Their first palisade is not far to the east. Their defenses aren't ready. That's the only thing that gives us hope._
_These creatures are in dire need of a lesson, and we're going to give it to them._
How many of them are there?
_At least a hundred, I think. Though less than there were before they started hitting us._
Do they know that you're here?

He looks at the scorched land outside the palisade. _Oh, yes. Didn't take them long. They've sent raiding parties at us. We've held them back, but we can't for much longer. Good thing you arrived when you did._
Tell me about their defenses.

_My scouts tell me they have three palisades, then the field below their keep, then the keep itself. The keep wall isn't finished, so we can get in there without a siege train. It won't be unfinished for long, though, so we have to attack soon._
_With the might of Avadon behind us, I don't see how we can fail._ The look on his face tells you that he sees many ways in which you can fail.
Teach them a lesson?
_The Pact is clear. This land here ..._ He points at the ground. _This is for wretches. The mountains that way ..._ He points to the west. _Those are for titans._
So what lesson will you give?

_That when titans move close to us, we drive them back. Or kill them, if we have to. That is the lesson, and we're going to give it today. Titans have no place here, or I have no business being called the Lion._
Do you have any spare supplies?

He nods. _You can take anything you find._ He points at a trapdoor in the back corner of the camp. _We found an old ruin down there, and we kept some things where it's cool. But, if you go down there, you should ... be alert._
_There's something down there. A ghost. No, I'm not heat-mad. There's a ghost down there. It keeps to itself, so we leave it alone. But try not to aggravate it._
I am ready to lead the attack.
Monitor Pelin rises. The other soldiers follow his lead. _Then we are ready. Are you sure you're prepared? We'll need to strike fast, and we'll need your support._
_And I hope you stay with us this time. We're lucky anyone survived the last botched assault._
Actually, give me a little more time.
The soldiers drop back to the ground, clearly frustrated. Pelin nods.
_All right. But hurry. We're pretty beat up here. We can't stay for much longer._
Let's go!

Pelin nods and turns to his soldiers. _Well, it's time. The titans are big. They're strong. They're brutal. And us? We're simply better! Are you ready to win a fight for the Lion?_ And you would bet every titan in the area hears the cheer his soldiers let out.
_Well, let's go then! Send the titans back where they came from!_ And the Monitor leaves the camp and begins a careful advance east.
I need to look around a bit. Wait here for now. (Leave.)
_All right. But hurry. We're pretty beat up here. We can't stay for much longer._ Not for the first time, you find yourself thankful that you're not a soldier in the Kva wastes.
You get a closer look at these soldiers. They are clearly some of the best The Kva has to offer, strong, well-trained, and properly equipped. They're also exhausted and pretty beat up.
They watch you reproachfully as you pass, blaming you for the loss of Monitor Pelin.
When you try to talk to them, they suggest that you speak with their commander.
Now that the first palisade has been secured, the soldiers look to the east, evaluating the terrain.
The Lion nods. _Yes. Not too bad, but it will get worse as we get closer._
The soldiers begin to move east, advancing carefully down the path. Some of them look with interest at some posts in the clearing to the north.
There are several posts here, each with its own pair of shackles. The blood stains in the center of the clearing give you a grim picture of what has been happening here.

As you look around, two humans emerge from a place of concealment in the thickets. They are hungry, exhausted, and sunburnt. The soldiers you are with recognize them as fellow Kva warriors, captured by the titans.

Within minutes, the two lost warriors have been fed, given water, and outfitted in scavenged armor and weapons. The two say that the titans are holding prisoners from their patrol. The assault force moves on.
The second palisade has been taken. The soldiers let out a lusty cheer.
The Lion shouts, _You see? They're big, but a sword in the guts works as well on them as anything else. Let's keep moving! Drive them from our borders!_
The soldiers turn north, advancing carefully down the path.
There are several cages on the east side of the path, where prisoners can be left to die slow, horrible deaths in the hot sun. The soldiers find two people in one of the cages.

They shout in alarm and let the two humans out. These are more prisoners, taken by the titans and left to die. Once again, they quickly rest, eat, and scavenge armor and blades. Then the assault continues.
The third palisade has been taken. The soldiers let out a loud cheer, determined to be heard by the enemy fort.
The Lion shouts, _Don't get cocky, now! You've heard what the scouts said. We're almost to the fort itself. Be ready for a bloodbath. We know that most of their numbers remain!_
The soldiers turn north, advancing toward the final defenses.
The day ends in victory. The titans have been defeated. The survivors are spreading out into the wastes. The mission of these soldiers has been completed.

You realize that they are turning away, leaving you to explore the fort alone. You tell them to wait. You command them to wait. They look at you with mistrust, blaming you for the loss of Monitor Pelin.
Soon, you are looking at their backs, as they begin the long march back to safety.
Now that Monitor Pelin is dead, another soldier has stepped up to take command. He looks at you with a notable lack of trust.
_We're ready for another assault. Barely. Say when we can attack._
The soldiers nod, but morale could hardly be lower. The warrior says, _Come on! Show some spirit! You are of The Kva! Come on! Let's send those titans back home._
And then they slowly head east, facing what they consider to be certain death.
Wait here.
_As you command. But we can't stay here much longer._ The demoralized soldiers hide in the shade.

Monitor Pelin looks at the abandoned keep. He nods approvingly. _A fine day's work. Most of the titans dead. The rest dispersed and harmless. If I know those creatures, most of them will be home within a week. We have won. Time to go home._
Meanwhile, you look at the entrance to the rest of the keep. Pelin wants to abandon you to search it yourself.
You are leaving?
Pelin nods. _We are, and I thank you, [N]. We were given a mission. It is done. Now our orders are to return. We can't ignore them._
Thank you for your help. Carry on.
Monitor Pelin salutes you. _You are a good soldier. For a Hand of Avadon. Best of luck to you. Hate to leave you like this, but orders are orders._
You must stay and help me search this place.
Pelin looks surprised. _That's not the sort of job for us. And those aren't our orders. The titans are beat. Now we have to go. I can't ignore orders. Anything else is Avadon business._
Please stay. I need help searching this place.

Surprisingly, Monitor Pelin looks sympathetic. _You have to stay here no matter what, alone in these wilds, because Redbeard says so. I understand. I've heard the stories. I'd like to stay, but ... Orders._
Fleeing is a cowardly thing to do.
Monitor Pelin looks at you with loathing. _You call me a coward. Me! You are lucky that ... that ... Typical Avadon. Arrogant. Thoughtless. But we have our orders. Come on._
He turns away, and his soldiers follow. One of them spits at your feet as she leaves.
Carry on, then.
Monitor Pelin nods gratefully. _I'm glad you understand. Don't like to leave you, but those are my orders._

A chill travels up and down your spine as you enter this crypt. You aren't alone here. There are several shades, ghosts of humans long dead. Their forms are vague and insubstantial. All of the details of their appearance in life have faded away.
And yet, one of them is still aware. It stands by a sarcophagus in the western alcove. It gestures at you, waving you forward.
The faded shade is still standing by the sarcophagus. It's hard to tell, given its insubstantial form, but you think that it is staring at you.
Can you talk?
The shade doesn't respond. It is so old that it might not even speak your language.
The shade starts to gesture with its hands. A little bit of mist appears between them. It soon adopts a vague, humanoid form. It looks up at you, waiting for a response.
I found this old circlet. (Offer it to the shade.)
You hold out the circlet. The shade reaches out for it. When it gets close, frost covers your hand.
The circlet disappears. Then a crown of mist appears on the shade's head. And then the ghosts fade away, leaving you alone in the crypt.
Very odd.
Ahhh! A ghost! (Attack.)
The shades are old and faded, but it turns out that they contain a surprising amount of raw power. They defend their tenuous existence in the world of the living.
I'll be going now. (Leave.)
The shade watches silently as you back away.
Is that a human?
The figure disappears. The shade fades, exhausted by the effort. It shrinks back into a dark corner to rest.
Is that a wretch?
Is that a titan?
The figure disappears. The shade summons up its energy. A circle of mist appears between its hands.
Is that a circle?
The circle disappears. The shade fades, exhausted by the effort. It shrinks back into a dark corner to rest.
Is that a necklace?
Is that a crown?
The circle of mist rises into the air and comes to rest on the shade's head. Then it fades away. A vague feeling of anger and desire radiates from the shade.
Then the shade fades, exhausted by the effort. It shrinks back into a dark corner to rest.
Is that a bracelet?
Is that a doughnut? Or other form of pastry?

The circle disappears. The shade fades, exhausted by the effort. It shrinks back into a dark corner, to rest and to sadly contemplate the delicious baked goods it is eternally denied in this dark tomb.
There is a young drake curled up in this remote clearing, basking in the sun. When you get close enough to awaken it from its torpor, it looks at you with amusement.
_Ahsss ... The titans promised me prey, so I came. But I did not think such succulent morsels would deliver themselvesss straight to my lair. Convenience! Sssss ... Any final words?_
We don't need to fight. I might trade with you.
_Hssss! I am no tame creature, like Zhethron! I hunt my prey and I slay it. I don't talk to it!_ The creature lunges at you.
As you prepare to defend yourself, the water around you starts to bubble.
Tell me more about the titans.
_Hsss. The titansss? They welcomed me. More alliesss as they hunt the warriorsss of the Pact. They will be jealousss when they see what victimsss they missed._ The creature lunges at you.
Stay back, creature. I serve Avadon.
_Avadon? Ahsss ... There is no Avadon in the wildsss. I will eat you. You will be gone. They will never know what happened. It isss time!_ The creature lunges at you.
Die, insolent lizard! (Attack.)
There is no more need to listen to this beast's insolence. You draw your weapon and attack.
As you advance, the water around you starts to bubble.

It turns out, to build their fort quickly and efficiently, the titans had gone out to obtain a fair amount of wretch slave labor. The pitiful creatures are hiding back here, thoroughly terrified by the sounds of battle outside.
They wear crude scavenged armor and hold inadequate weapons in their trembling hands. They stare at you, unsure if you are going to slaughter them or not.
I want to know about the titans.
All of the slaves start babbling at once, describing in detail all of the elements of the titan defenses that you have already seen. Alas, none of them have seen the dungeons in any detail.
The wretches obediently list the various clans, gangs, and disorganized clumps the titans stole them from. You very quickly receive a lot of information, absolutely none of it useful.
Ahhhh! Wretches! Die! (Attack.)
The wretches heave a collective sigh. All of their views regarding the injustice of an uncaring universe are confirmed in an instant.
You may go.
The wretches don't need to be told twice. They grab their scavenged weapons and rations and run for the exit.

The chief of the titans is watching you through the gate. At least, you would guess that he is their leader. He wields not a club but a huge, twisted iron sword, and his armor is festooned with the trophies and cracked skulls of many defeated enemies.

Though he is huge and powerful, he greets you with a somber and respectful salute. _I, Chief Chanakk, greet you. We knew the challenge would come. We thought we would defeat you. We failed. Now I and few others stay to meet you._
Where are the other titans?
_Fled, to find their way home. We tried to settle in here._ He scratches his arm with long, filthy fingernails. _Again, we failed. No need to doom them all._
Wouldn't you rather talk to me on this side of that big gate?
Chanakk chuckles. _I think we will face each other soon enough._
You wanted to meet me? You have. Now what?
_Only this. This keep is lost, but you are of Avadon. You want more. You want me, and you want the knowledge I have._
Well, I am here to meet you now. I am [N].
Chanakk nods. _Well met. Now I say what I need to. This keep is lost, but you are of Avadon. You want more. You want me, and you want the knowledge I have._
True enough.
_You can leave if you want. Maybe I will stay. Or maybe I will flee back to the Titan Peaks. Rebuild my tribe. And maybe return to have vengeance on you._
_Or, you can hunt me now. Come into my lair to try your blade against me. In return, I may have great honor. The heads of Avadon warriors, on the walls of my great hall._
_Those are your choices._
Or you could return with me to Avadon. I don't need to kill you.
_Surrender? Let them dig into my thoughts? See all I know? Leave me broken in a shell? No! Chief Chanakk bowing to you is a thing you won't have._
I must kill you. Zhethron won't be happy with less.
_Ahhhh ... The dragon. I would not have angered it. I did what I was told. Enraging it too early doomed us._
Avadon requires me to slay those who attack the Pact.
Chanakk nods solemnly. _Yes. Orders. You are commanded, as I was. My orders were to fight, but they made me draw you to us too soon. Now my people pay for that._
Sounds fair. I'll just let you go.

Chanakk chuckles. _A worthy trick, Hand of Avadon. But I know Avadon marks me for death. They will hound you until you slay me. You must follow your orders, as I did. Orders that made me draw your attention too early._
Who gave you your orders?
Chief Chanakk laughs. _You will learn. You will know soon enough. But, if I tell you, I have no chance of surviving. You must learn for yourself._
Well, if we're going to fight, step out from behind that gate.

Chanakk nods, amused. _I would, but it'd not be fair to my warriors. Some stayed, to try for honor. Killing you. They have the first chance to try you._ He claps his hands. You hear a loud sound to the west.
Then ready yourself. I am coming for you.
Chanakk nods. _I will be ready. A fight I did not choose, but I won't hide from it. But first, I have warriors. They asked a chance to try you. They want to earn honor. I won't deny them._
He claps his hands. You hear a loud sound to the west.
Be patient. I'll be back for you later.
Chanakk nods. _We will be ready. I and the warriors who stayed to win honor slaying you. But first, I have one who demanded a chance at you. Now. I won't deny him._
(See what the noise was.)
The western gate of the huge hall is slowly opening. You hear a long, incoherent roar. Something is walking toward you. Its iron boots clang as they strike the floor.
You look back at the gate in time to see Chief Chanakk walking away.

Chief Chanakk is sitting on the stone throne in his half-finished audience hall. The ceiling here is also held up by thick, stone pillars. No earthquake or bombardment of dragon fire will collapse this ceiling.
He rises to his feet and raises his sword. You notice that there is already blood on the blade. And on the floor. There has been a fight here.
_Before my people fled, some said all should stay and die. I killed them. Then, after my people left, others tried to flee rather than face you. I killed them._
_Discipline is important._
Nice throne room.
The chieftain nods. _Thank you. If we had not drawn the dragon's rage too early, you would not have been able to beat our defenses. Such a waste._
Are you ready to submit to Avadon?
_This will not happen. You will die now, or I will die. That is how this ends._
You are ready to fight me now?
_It is time. You will die now, or I will die. That is how this ends._
And you still won't tell me who told you to come here?
He solemnly shakes his head.
You seem very calm about it.
_I will be avenged. The Pact has been hurt. It doesn't know how bad. Avadon will be destroyed. The plan is in place. It's too late to stop it._
You immediately start to ask about this, trying to gain more information. Hoping you are distracted, the huge titan leaps up and rushes toward you, blade raised.
There is no way you will ever better me, Farlander.
_Maybe. If you kill me, I will be avenged. The Pact has been hurt. It doesn't know how bad. Avadon will be destroyed. The plan is in place. It's too late to stop it._

Chief Chanakk collapses to the floor, exhausted. He is not mortally wounded, but he is too beaten and bloodied to fight on. You carefully walk toward him, wondering if it is possible to knock him out and return him to Avadon for questioning.
He watches you advance. He knows what you want. He would rather die than be taken prisoner.
There are two fast motions. One moment, he has a long, wicked dagger in his hand. The next moment, it is at his throat. And, before you can save him, the titan chieftain is dead.
Talking: The Khemerian warrior stares at you with loathing, but says nothing.
Avadon!
Talking: These young Khemerians are busy running away.
Stonemaster Roth
Runner Kellen
Nixie
Runner Faiga
Edeline
Unni
Hahn
Trevar
Khemerian Stoneworker
Damra
Shaman Helia
Shaman Tress
Young Khemerian
Khemerian Keep Guard
Khemerian Thug
Hunter Salom
Lava Bat
Shock Bat
Snapfang
Laurella, where are you?
We've done nothing wrong.
What do you want, Hand?
Avadon has come.
We've done no wrong.
I will deal with you.
I am Moritz'Kri.
I am the wizard of Dhorl Stead.
I wish to help.
Let me help you.
Heard any gossip?
No? Really?
Your bread is burning.
Wait until you hear this!
A fellow warrior.
The woods are dark.
I avoid the Stead.
What brings you here, Hand?
Leave me be.
I obey your laws.
Need a new shipment.
Is the caravan here yet?
Can't get good steel here.
A visitor.
Only a Hand comes to me.
I even have wisdom for you.
Stay off my crops.
I'll never help you.
Leave us, outsider.
There are dark things in the woods.
Don't walk out at night.
Is Salom coming?
Be quiet if Salom is close.
Is the Hand listening?
The Hand. Sssshhh!
Not a fair deal.
Fifty coins more!
For this quality?
I agree.
Keep watch.
Find all traitors.
There is the Hand.
The invader is here.
Listen for treachery.
It is a disaster.
You have brought death.
Is Laurella here?
Get out.
You are not welcome.
Hmmmmm ...
Aaahhhhhh ...
Laaaaaa ...
You did it.
You brought ruin.
You will pay!
You will not pass.
Your journey ends here.
You emerge from the pylon, stumbling and gagging. The journey is getting no less wrenching as time passes.
When your vision returns, you see that the pylon is in the middle of a clearing in a forest. A cool wind blows through the trees, a nice change from the burning wastes of The Kva.

However, this pylon is very different. It is neglected. Leaves are strewn throughout the clearing, and the arrival platform is covered with moss. Also, some derogatory and obscene messages have been crudely painted on the pylon.
It provides a helpful reminder. You are in Khemeria, of the Farlands. Not only enemy lands, but prowled by some sort of vicious monster. Care will be required.

You emerge from the pathway and surprise two young Khemerians, tribesmen practicing with wooden spears. When you emerge, they stop fighting and their jaws drop. It has been years since anyone new walked down this pathway.
You watch each other awkwardly for several long seconds. Then they finally remember what they should do. They run toward their village, shouting, _Avadon! Avadon!_
Jenell smiles viciously. _That's right. Run, my young enemies. Judgment is upon you._

You enter the village of Dhorl Stead. It is a series of wooden domes, each occupied by one of the families that make up the tribe. A traditional settlement, of the sort that exists in multitudes all over Khemeria and the Wyldrylm.

Your welcome is not warm. The people here reacted quickly to news of your arrival. Some hid in their homes. You see them peeking nervously out through the doors. Others are in the streets, carrying out their business. They pretend to be unconcerned but cast nervous glances at you whenever they think themselves unobserved.

One group, however, is taking great pains to not appear scared of you. There is a group of warriors sitting around a fire in the center of town. They have chain mail coats and vicious halberds, and they have been drinking. The people in the village seem just as scared of them as of you.
You return to Dhorl Stead. The village appears much the same as before, except that Hunter Salom and his thugs are not sitting around the fire in the center.

You would imagine that, with both Salom and the Shadow Beast gone, the people of Dhorl Stead would be calmer. And yet, now that they see you have returned, they seem more terrified than before. The children are all gone, and everyone flinches when they see you looking at them.
Jenell nods. _Terrified. As they should be._
You return to Dhorl Stead, ready to carry out a grim mission. You must return Lord Carsta'Arl to Avadon, or slay him if he refuses to come. You can't imagine that he will surrender peacefully.

And it appears that, somehow, the people of Dhorl Stead were aware of what was to come. The sounds of the village are faint. Nobody is out on the pathways. Everyone appears to have fled or gone into hiding.

But then you see movement in the center of town. A patrol of hunters. Not Hunter Salom and his men, but the people of the village, preparing to die to defend it. They walk back and forth, watching for attackers, but they haven't seen you yet.
Sevilin looks somber. _Khemeria is our enemy, but I came from a town not unlike this one. I hope we can do this with less bloodshed._

To the northeast, you can see the difference between Khemeria and the Wyldrylm. There is a stone fortress here. Several circular walls, built from large, crude stones and connected by pathways. A wide, shallow moat surrounds the whole building.

The people of the Wyldrylm are more nomadic. They don't build fortresses. The Khemerians have been much more eager to copy the ways of the other lands of Lynaeus, both cultural and military. And, alas, the changes also left them more violent and greedy for territory.

Jenell, unsurprisingly, looks at the fort with disgust. _See that pile of rocks? They rely on walls and steel. We rely on our cunning and the power of our shamans. And we have defeated them at every turn._
The building at the east end of the village is made of stone. If anything separates the Wyldrylm from Khemeria, it is this land's love of buildings made of rock.

This is the workshop of the village's stonecrafter. Wagons bring huge lumps of raw stone, which are then chipped down into bricks and sent to make forts and fortifications. This is Dhorl Stead's bastion of modernity.

There is a stone circle here. Such circles are the centers of worship for the shamans of Khemeria and the Wyldrylm. However, this circle is neglected. The leaves have not been swept away. Remains of the last offerings have not been cleared.
You expect Jenell to be furious. She only seems sad. She makes a desultory attempt to clean away a little of the mess. Then she gives up. It will only return after she leaves.
The Khemerians have adopted new ways and are forgetting the old. The Wyldrylm has stuck to its traditions. Now they hate each other. Nobody knows who will prevail in the end.
The pathway suddenly becomes eerily quiet. Even the birdsong falls still. Thick clumps of spider web hang from the trees, bugs and squirrels still caught in them.
It is not uncommon for the remote forests of Lynaeus to become infested with huge arachnids. The warriors of Dhorl Stead have not yet gotten around to cleaning the pests out.
You enter Oghrym'Tor, the stone fortress that dominates the village to the south. From this huge, crude fortress, one lord can dominate tribes for many miles around.

Unlike last time, the inner gates have been left open. The lord of these lands has been expecting you. There is no pretense of keeping you out. He is willing to see you, though you can't be sure how he will react when you confront him.
ROTH
STONEMASTER OF THE DHORLA
DHORL STEAD

The disaster that has befallen her village is too much for this aging shaman. Unni sits on her carpet, rocking back and forth, chanting softly. She ignores both you and the carnage outside. You leave her.
There is a sign next to these totems. It says:
UNNI, KEEPER OF THE CIRCLES
DHORLA TRADING POST

There are several hunters in the side rooms of this hall. They watch you carefully, ready to defend their clan to the death if necessary. When you try to talk to them, they say that Runner Kellen speaks for them.
This man is Runner Faiga's husband. When you try to talk to him, he mutters that you should speak with her. Then he finds some urgent business in another room.
He is a hunter of Khemeria, but even he isn't brave enough to face down a Hand of Avadon.
Several young apprentices are hauling and shaping large blocks of stone. They do their best to pretend that you aren't there.
When you finally force one to talk to you, you learn that you should speak to Roth. He is in the hall to the south.
Several Khemerians are here, gossiping and preparing the evening's meal. You try to overhear what they are saying, but they become very quiet and still whenever you get close.
When you move away, they return to their business and pretend nothing happened.
There are several merchants in Dhorl Stead. Some are Farlanders and some are from the Pact. They are negotiating the sale of wagons full of goods.
When you listen, you note that the Farlanders tend to give Pact merchants very good terms on everything. If they don't, punishment awaits.

This hall is full of the members of one of the clans of Dhorl Stead. They are all fierce Khemerian warriors. They don't like having you in their home, and they have no interest in talking to you. Not one word.
Eventually, you have to give up and leave. Avadon or not, there is no help to be had here.
There are several Khemerians using this river to do their laundry. When you get close, they get very quiet. When you walk away, they resume talking.
There are several Khemerians out in the village, talking, tending to their crops, continuing the business of farm life.

And yet, they are not calm. They constantly are looking for foes. Sometimes they look worriedly at you. At other times, they nervously watch the road toward Oghrym'Tor and the woods at the edge of town. To live in Dhorl Stead now is to constantly fear a variety of threats.
You try to talk to this villager, but you learn nothing of value. Terror of displeasing a Hand of Avadon gets in the way of conversation.
Even though they are standing in the front of a massive stone fortress, these warriors are clearly afraid of you. When you approach them, they mutter nervously. You don't learn anything from them.
You do learn, however, that they are unable to open the gate and let you into Oghrym'Tor.
There is a group of vicious Khemerian warriors patrolling Dhorl Stead. They watch for intruders and invaders, and they consider you to be both.
When you get close, they boldly stare at you, almost daring you to start something. Their leader shakes his head and says to you, _If you want to talk, talk to me._

The master stoneworker of Dhorl Stead is sitting at his table, eating a bowl of stew. His hair is thinning and gray, and his body bears all of the marks of a long life breaking apart and shaping rock. Stone dust covers the backs of his hands.

When he looks up at you, you can see the misery and conflict in his eyes. He wants to turn you out, but he can't. He stares at you for a long moment, trying to decide what to do. Finally, he sets his spoon down.
_I am Stonemaster Roth,_ he says in a weary voice. _I never knew whether you might come. You have, and I find that my hopes and fears have both come true. But there is something I need to ask you._
Stonemaster Roth sits and stares morosely at his table. _I don't know what else to say to you. What's done is done. It's best if you leave me._
I am the one who asks questions.
He looks up at you. _You will force nothing from me, Hand. I promise you that. But, if you tell me what I want, I might aid you._
_I have lost two children. One, Aslak, was taken by a beast who roams the woods around our village. Another, Laurella, left me to go to Avadon. She sought vengeance our leaders would not give us._
For a moment, he allows himself to be hopeful. _Have you seen Laurella? Have you seen my daughter?_
I will not say who has or hasn't come to Avadon. What happens in our keep is a secret.
Roth nods. _Then I am forced to go on without knowing what has happened. Do what you will. I will not help you._ He turns away.
Laurella came to Avadon. It is because of her that I am here.
Roth nods. His joy at the news is not unmixed. _Then it is true. Laurella brought the gaze of Avadon here, and all know it. It will be ... difficult for us._
_But I thank you for telling me that my beloved daughter lives. In return, I will give you what little information I can._
You are a stoneworker?
He nods. _Thirty long years, hammering at rock and shaping it. We come late to the craft. My work is among the best in our land, but nothing compared to that in the Tawon Empire._
Why does Khemeria make stone buildings now?
_Because, as long as we live in huts and live like nomads, we are at the mercy of the eastern powers. The Tawon Empire. Holklanda. They can crush us with stone and steel._
Jenell snorts. _A little safety is not worth sacrificing all of the old ways. The Wyldrylm is safe within the Pact._
Roth smiles and takes a sip of wine. _Child, even many of us feel as you do. But one day you will learn, you are never, ever safe._
You make the stone for all of the buildings here?
He smiles. _Oh, no. My workshop only makes the pieces of quality. Trim. Finishing pieces. Many others worked the sort of crude blocks that form the walls of Oghrym'Tor._
_Though many of those workers were trained by me._
Tell me about Dhorl Stead.

_I will say a little, and know I take a great risk saying even that. We are an old village, composed of four allied clans. Once, we had a chief. Shamans. So on. But then Lord Carsta'Arl rose. Gained power. An army. Had his fortress built. And now he commands these parts._
Why can't you speak with me?
_In our little village, Hunter Salom is the arm of Lord Carsta'Arl. He enforces the law, and he loves to do it. Carsta'Arl sent word that none should help any outsiders that arrive._
_As long as Salom is near, the villagers will never help you._
How did Lord Carsta'Arl gain power?

_His great-grandfather was once merely the chief of Dhorl Stead. That elder saw that other fortresses were being built in Khemeria, closer and closer to us. He saw that, if we did not match our rivals, we would suffer bloody conquest._
_That elder began the construction of Oghrym'Tor and launched bloody conquests of his own. And the gruesome business passed to his son, and to his son, and then to Carsta'Arl. We were not consulted._
Tell me about the fortress.
_Oghrym'Tor? It is finally complete, after eighty years of constant work. And much suffering among our people. But now it terrifies our enemies. And us as well._
_While Lord Carsta'Arl rules there, with Moritz'Kri lending him power, all Khemerians near us will tremble with terror._
I want to know more about Moritz'Kri.
_He is Lord Carsta'Arl's wizard. He has a tower to the north. His powers are ... I do not know the limits to them. But I know that little is said that he does not hear, so I will say no more._
_He is gone. My son is avenged. I thank you. And I hope that, now that this is settled, you will leave us and not return._
I am hunting the shadowy creature that killed your son.
Roth involuntarily looks toward the window. _And Hunter Salom and his enforcers don't know of this? I could get in great trouble for helping you, but ..._

_There is little to say. The beast lurks outside town from time to time. Aslak, my son, he had the poor fortune to encounter it late one evening. We found the body the next morning. I saw him. He was ..._ He chokes up.
Can you describe the beast?

_I have never seen it. I know only what I have heard. The beast is huge and cunning. It seems to be surrounded by shadows that cover and conceal it. It has ... But I do not want to simply repeat rumors._
And you are sure that it was a beast?
_And not trickery? This was considered. It has been seen. It has been tracked. It is large, deadly, and very real._
How has Lord Carsta'Arl reacted?
For a moment, Roth's anger is directed somewhere other than Avadon. _At something killing us? Mere villagers? People unimportant to his fortress? His dreams of conquest?_
_The only thing that has been done is for him to send Salom to tell us to be quiet. To withstand our suffering meekly. I had to swallow my rage and accept it. Laurella could not. So she went to you._
How might I find it?

_I can't tell you where to hunt the beast. I am no hunter. But Dhorl Stead has warriors who roam deep into the woods. They have little love for Hunter Salom. One of them might have seen something in his or her travels._
Who do you think I should talk to?
_Lord Carsta'Arl and his wizard hear everything said in Dhorl Stead eventually. My family has suffered enough. If you don't want to hurt us, you will leave now._
Anything else I should know?

_Only that Lord Carsta'Arl and his wizard hear everything said in Dhorl Stead eventually. I fear for my daughter. If they learn that she has brought Avadon here ... Please leave me. You will only draw suspicion._ He turns away.
Thank you.
_I wish you good hunting. Please leave me._ He turns away.

Roth looks down at the table, and his face gets very red. _So I have heard. Hunter Salom and his enforcers have learned that you are here to hunt the beast. They came to my house and threatened me. Threatened my daughter, if she returns here alive._
_I hate the beast with all my heart, but you only bring more danger. I will help you no longer._ He turns away.
The beast that killed your son is dead.
Roth looks up at you and nods. For a moment, there is gratitude in his eyes. _I thank you. For Aslak. For ... all who will not be lost. Avadon has aided us.
_And now, I ask you a favor._
_And I have asked for you to leave us. There is little else I can say, except that I hope to have Laurella safe at home again._
_The gaze of Avadon brings only destruction to my kind. I ask you, please leave and don't return. Otherwise, I fear what might happen._
As long as you don't threaten the Pact, you have nothing to fear from us.
_But Avadon has the ability to see threats everywhere. When they want to find crimes, they will. So please, accept my thanks and leave us._
He nods to you one more time. Then he turns away to be alone with his thoughts.
I will try not to return.
_Then, one more time, I thank you. Farewell._
I am a Hand of Avadon. I go where I want, when I want.
Roth doesn't seem surprised. _It is your way. One more time, I humbly thank you. And I ask to be alone to remember my son._
I am here to deal with Moritz'Kri.

_Of course. Once Avadon starts to look for threats, it will always find them, until the land is scoured and all is dust. I know nothing of wizards. I only wish to be left alone and wait for Laurella to return. Excuse me._ He turns away.
_Then leave me. And leave us. We have suffered enough without the eye of Avadon upon us._
_And I have already said, leave me. Leave us all. We have suffered enough, and Avadon can only bring us more harm._
_I am Stonemaster Roth. I wait for my daughter Laurella to return._
Stonemaster Roth sits at the table, oblivious to the chaos outside. _You are back? I am only waiting for Laurella to return. Someone must be here for her._
Where is everyone else?
_I saw what was coming. I sent them away. Others fled too. I wait here for my daughter._
You should not be here.
His voice is hollow. _And what will my poor girl think when she returns to all this bloodshed and her family is gone? Someone has to protect her. So I wait. Do what you will._
He responds to no more of your questions.
I will leave you to wait.
He doesn't seem to hear you. His voice is hollow. _Laurella, I hope you are safe. I will even forgive you for what you brought. In these times ... all is lost._
Leave, or I will make you leave.
His voice is hollow. _Do what you will. Nothing more can be taken from me. I only want my daughter back. I will forgive her for what she brought, even if nobody else will. But I will not leave._

An aging warrior of Khemeria sits on the seat of honor, watching you approach. His face is starting to wrinkle, but he still spends many a day out in the wild. In both Khemeria and the Wyldrylm, hunting is still an important source of food and honor.

He does not like having a Hand of Avadon in his hall, but he knows that it would be unwise to keep you out. He nods to you. _I welcome you, warrior of Avadon. You are no friend to our people, but, as long as you are peaceful, you are safe under my roof._
_I am Runner Kellen. I don't know why you have come to us, but I don't think we will be able to help you._
Runner Kellen sits in his chair. He seems very calm, but the other warriors aren't. They watch you from the shadows, and they keep their weapons nearby. _Anything else to say before you depart?_
What is this hall?
_This is the home of my clan, largest of the four in Dhorl Stead. Each clan has a meeting hall here._
So all members of your clan are here?
_No. This is where we come to meet. Most of us are out in the wilds, in our own homesteads. Or hunting, of course. We would be a pitiful group indeed if we could all live here._
You are the leader of the clan?
_Leader? We are a family. There is no single man or woman who rules over us. Not as long as Carsta'Arl holds us in his iron grip._
_But I have earned a level of respect. I am asked for advice. I settle disputes._
Tell me about the other clans.
_Some are closer to us. Some less. I would not draw the eye of Avadon to them by describing them. All I will say is that they will likely be less friendly to you than we are._
_Some of us want to conquer the Wyldrylm. Others wish to reunite with our estranged brothers there. I will leave it at that._
Jenell whispers to you, _Some in my tribe would like to rejoin with Khemeria too. Of course, if they stopped trying to kill us, that would be a good start toward peace._
I would like some information.

Runner Kellen adopts a very neutral expression. _Knowledge is valuable, and Lord Carsta'Arl has told us that it is not to be shared freely. Whatever you wish to learn, I'm sure he would love to tell you._
_His keep, Oghrym'Tor, is to the northeast. You should see him there._
I have been there. Lord Carsta'Arl would not let me enter.
There is a long moment of silence. Runner Kellen ponders this. The more he thinks, the angrier he gets. _Our lord turns you away? He taunts Avadon? Brings your anger to us? This ... this ..._

He waves a hand. His warriors suddenly find their own business to attend to, pointedly not listening to your conversation. _Perhaps there are a few things I can tell you. If it satisfies you and leads to your departure._
I am a Hand of Avadon. You must answer my questions.
Kellen looks grim. _You put me and mine in a hard place. One says we must not talk. The other says we must. So I choose to stay silent. Leave us._
I will do that.
Kellen nods. _Thank you for your understanding. I wish you a safe journey. Please leave us._

Kellen looks grim. _So I have heard. Hunter Salom came to me personally. Said you were hunting dangerous prey, and that things would go hard for us if we helped you. I will not risk my clan by speaking with you a moment more._
Then, oddly, he turns his head. He seems to be looking to the northwest. He adds, _I can't help you. There are few hunters that would. But perhaps at least one. Now leave us._
Runner Kellen looks to one of his warriors. The hunter goes to the south window and looks out of it, taking care to appear nonchalant. Then he turns from the window and shakes his head.
Runner Kellen says, _This is not the best of times. Please leave us._ He will speak no more. Something is making him very nervous.
I would like to know more about the woods.
_The woods of Khemeria are deep and dark. They are full of the finest game in Lynaeus, as well as dangerous prey. Huge spiders. Drakes. Things that bring much honor from the hunting._
_And yet, the woods are not like what they were when I was young. They are far more dangerous now. There is prey now that we dare not hunt._
And you have been out there many times, I suppose.
_Since I received my first proper bow at the age of ten, it has been impossible to keep me out of the woods. Even now, when they seem to get darker with every passing day._
Why are the woods more dangerous?
His face darkens. _I don't know. I know that Lord Carsta'Arl should be helping to remove the worst of the pests, the ones too strong for a single clan to bring down, and he does not._
_As for his wizard, well, there are things that it is dangerous to say._
_But I will say that now that the wizard Moritz'Kri is gone, I think that things will be better._
What can't you hunt?

_I am ashamed to admit it, but there is some prey in the woods that I will not call a hunt for, because the loss of some of my clan would be guaranteed. And there are some deadly foes that are even beyond the strength of the clans together to destroy._
_It was not always thus, but in these last few years the shadows have grown._
Can't the clans work together?
_It is not our way. Hunting is a competition for us, for food, for honor._
Perhaps there is something I can hunt.
Runner Kellen suddenly seems very interested, perhaps thinking of traps for the Hands of Avadon. _There is a creature that has been hunting us. Not far to the north. It has slain one of our clan._
_It is a huge arachnid, called the Widow of Bones. Were you to destroy it, we would be in your debt._
And why haven't you killed it?
_We could, but the battle would be likely to kill at least one of my clan warriors. In these dark times, I am willing to shed a little honor to maintain our strength._
Why is it called the Widow of Bones?
_It is a huge arachnid, cunning for its kind. It decorates the paths around its lair with piles of bones. The remains of its prey._
_The remains of several Dhorl Stead warriors are there. Each of our clans has lost a young runner in the quest to bring the creature down._
Where can I find it?
_In the Dhorla Woods. If you are ever near the tower of Moritz'Kri, look in the woods to the south._
The Widow of Bones is dead.

The warriors listen attentively as you tell the tale of the battle. _Now I regret not being more forward,_ Runner Kellen says. _With care, I think we could have slain it with no losses. But you have done a favor for us, and we are in your debt._
Kellen takes a three-tined spear from the wall and hands it to you. _Our debt is now paid. This is a grim time, when we must turn to Avadon to lift some of the darkness._
Anything else you need me to hunt for you?
Runner Kellen looks grim. _Nothing I don't think we can handle for ourselves. We already have to endure the mockery of the other clans for asking your help once._
_Though that may change if things get worse. You might want to come back later._
Runner Kellen looks grim. _We already have to endure the mockery of the other clans for asking your help once, but there is one group of raiders that torment us all._
_Raiders from Stara Stead have been attacking our runners. None of us have been killed, but they are testing us for weakness. If nothing is done about them, soon we will be swarmed._
Stara Stead? They are Khemerians?
_The Steads of Khemeria constantly do battle. Conquer each other. Much bloodshed. That is why we need our stone fortresses._
_First there is testing. Then there is invasion. If the raiders were slain, that would send a clear message. We are not weak._
Where can I find the raiders?
_They move quickly. They are no fools. But they have been most often seen in the woods where you hunted the Shadow Beast. They know that the hunters of Dhorl Stead are afraid to go there._
Why haven't you killed them?
_Because there are a lot of them, and we would rather that you put yourself at risk._
Those Stara Stead raiders are gone.
He seems surprised. _Really?_ You tell him the tale. _Well, none of the other clans will mock us for this. They will be just as happy as us to see them gone._
He takes a broadsword from the wall and gives it to you. _This is from a Wyldrylm warrior. We would not use it, but you can. We are grateful._
Anything else I can hunt for you?
_Not yet. We will have to wait until there is a target vicious enough that we would withstand more mockery to be rid of it._
I have come to Khemeria to hunt a certain beast.
Runner Kellen looks to one of his warriors. The hunter goes to the south window and looks out of it, taking care to appear nonchalant. Then he turns from the window and nods. Kellen turns to you.
_We can speak of it. Briefly, before Salom and his thugs return to our village. The beast. Yes. The Shadow Beast, we call it. Not a creative name, but very true._
_And very real. And very dangerous._
You have seen it.
_I have. It is in the shape of a wolf, tall as a man's shoulder, wreathed in shadow. It does not always strike. Sometimes it only watches us. It makes strange noises, then flees._
_But then, at times, it does attack. It is swifter than sight, and its teeth are like razors._
Has it killed many of the people here?
_So far, a dozen. A grim tally. All of the clans have been hurt. It seems to be growing bolder. We see it more often, closer and closer to Dhorl Stead._
Where did it come from?
_We do not know. It appeared almost a year ago, and it is unlike anything in our memories or tales._
How can I find it?
Runner Kellen retrieves a map from his quarters and shows it to you. _I don't know where its lair is, but I do know where it has been seen the most. It seems the best place to start the hunt._
_You must go north to the Dhorla Woods. Find the forest around the tower of the wizard Moritz'Kri. Then find the northwest road. Follow it, and the forest will become grim and dark indeed._
(The Dhorla Woods are now on your world map.)
Has Lord Carsta'Arl sent warriors there?
_Our lord does nothing to hunt the creature. That is the only reason that I will aid you._
And, when I am there, how will I hunt it?
_It will not be difficult. In those woods, the creature will soon hunt you._
I would like to know more about the Shadow Beast.
_I have told you all I dare. Go north to the Dhorla Woods, and follow the road to the northwest. And I wish you luck._
I have hunted and destroyed the Shadow Beast.

For a brief hour, the differences between Khemeria and the Pact are forgotten. You sit with the Farlanders and tell the tale of the hunt. They listen with rapt attention and admiration. And not a little bit of awe at the might of Avadon.
Finally, you all rise. Runner Kellen nods to you. _Tomorrow, we are foes once again. But today, I thank you._
I want to know more about Lord Carsta'Arl.
_He is the ruler of Dhorl Stead and the lands beyond. His family has conquered and controlled for four generations. He enforces all of the new ways._
_I will say no more than that. It is not safe to discuss him with you, even to say kind things._
Can you tell me more about Moritz'Kri?
_He is Lord Carsta'Arl's wizard. His skill has helped Dhorl Stead to become a true power in Khemeria. And I will say no more. Little is said that he does not hear._
_He is Lord Carsta'Arl's wizard. And, if the rumors I have heard about his tower are true, we are better off without him, even if it costs us much of our strength._
I have come here to question him. And maybe return him to Avadon.
_Then you hunt more dangerous game than I ever have. My clan chooses to sit back and watch. And hope, once you have your target, you leave and turn the gaze of Avadon from us._
Hunter Kellen seems relieved. _All right. Safe travels to you._

One of the elder hunters of Dhorl Stead stands guard in the middle of the village, surrounded by armed warriors. You did not recognize him at first. It is Runner Kellen. _This is a dark day,_ he says.
One of the elder hunters of Dhorl Stead stands guard in the middle of the village, surrounded by armed warriors. He says, _I am Runner Kellen, honored member of my clan. This is a dark day,_ he says.
_We know why you have come. You are not here to hunt those who would do us harm. You hunt our leaders. You hunt us._
_We do not want to give our lives opposing Avadon, but you give us no choice. Flee, or we will do our best to kill you._
Jenell stands upright and raises her staff, ready to fight. _I knew this was coming the moment we came here. And I welcome it._
How did you know that I was coming?
_Lord Carsta'Arl sent Hunter Salom with the warning this morning. I do not know how he learned the truth. Many fled. The rest will die to turn you from our lands._
We do not need to fight.

Runner Kellen looks around sadly. He knows that this might be the last time he sees the village where he was raised. _This is our home. You are from the Pact. You are an invader. We must defend it. Our honor demands it._
_It is all we have. Without it, we are nothing._
You stand in the way of Avadon? There is only one punishment for that crime. (Attack.)
And, in an instant, Dhorl Stead stops being something you protect and becomes something you fight. The proud, fierce Khemerian warriors let out their war cries and charge.
I come only for Lord Carsta'Arl. Stand aside.

_We hate Lord Carsta'Arl. He is cruel, and he keeps us from the old ways. But he is also our protector. Without his leadership, the other Steads will crush us. We will be killed. Or worse. Far worse._
_Though we hate him, we have no choice but to protect him._
Runner Kellen gives you one final salute. Then the proud, fierce Khemerian warriors let out their war cries and charge.
This place is an enemy of Avadon. There is no future for it. The only hope for you and your families is to flee.

Hunter Kellen bows his head. To your surprise, the old warrior looks truly defeated. _I knew this day would come the moment you arrived. Curse our leaders for bringing this fate to us. But you speak true._
_We will do what we must for our clan. Though it tears our honor to shreds, we must survive. We will flee._
He looks at you one last time. Not with hate or fear. He simply mourns the inevitable. And then he and his warriors leave to follow their clan into exile.
You turn to look at Jenell. She watches them go. And, to your surprise, she doesn't seem disappointed in you. She says, _He is the best of a foul lot._
Then I will end your suffering quickly. (Attack.)
You stand at the gates of Oghrym'Tor, the fortress from which Dhorl Stead and the surrounding lands are ruled. The gates are, you can't help but notice, closed.

An elderly man stands in front of the gates, waiting for you. It is common practice all over Lynaeus for mages to wear robes to mark their profession. This man has taken it an extra step. His robes are covered with flamboyant designs, and the shoulders are heavily padded.
He nods to you and intones solemnly, _I am Moritz'Kri, wizard of Oghrym'Tor, honored adviser to Lord Carsta'Arl. And I know you, [N]. I have emerged to greet you and learn your business here._
Moritz'Kri stands solemnly and watches you. You have time to admire his outlandish robes. All mages are proud, but few of them let it go to their head to this extent.
Moritz'Kri says, in a deep and theatrical voice, _Is there anything else you need before you depart?_
I want to enter this fort.

The wizard adopts an air of surprise and sadness. _Then I must disappoint you. Alas, Lord Carsta'Arl has ordered the gates sealed. There is a ... a sickness, and this keep is quarantined. We would never put the warriors of Avadon at risk._
_Thus, I regret to say that the gates will remain closed._
Sevilin mutters, _Turn away warriors of Avadon? How dare they, sickness or no?_
Shima mutters, _Turn away warriors of Avadon? This is not allowed, and his explanation stinks of lies._
Tell me more about this disease.
_It is mysterious, but nothing that is beyond my powers, given time. But, until it is cured, nobody from outside will enter the keep. Orders of Carsta'Arl._
You will let me in. I insist, Farlander.
The wizard seems calm, but the warriors in the guardhouses are very tense. Moritz'Kri smiles.

_Then you must report our crime to Avadon and let Redbeard decide how to respond. Until then, the gates remain closed. But I assure you that any aid you could receive inside you will get from me now._
Then I will stay out here. For now.
The wizard nods. _I am grateful for your understanding._
Avadon has sent me here.
_Of course. You have some mission of great importance, and we wish to help you all we can so that your gaze can turn away from us._
_So ... Why are you here?_ He tries to act casual, but he is clearly desperate to know your purpose.
Nathalie subtly taps you on the shoulder. When you turn to look at her, she gives her head a slight shake.
Shima subtly taps you on the shoulder. When you turn to look at him, he gives his head a slight shake.
I have heard of a dark beast that roams these lands. I hunt it to learn where it comes from.

To your surprise, the aging wizard chuckles. _Then I must disappoint you. We have all heard the rumors of a dark beast in the woods. Just that. Rumors. Tall tales and the ramblings of drunken hunters._
_If there was such a beast, I would know of it. But, alas, I think you will have to return to Avadon disappointed._
I'm sorry to hear it. I will investigate a little more and return home.
_Of course. Take your time. I'm sorry that I had to disappoint you._
_Oghrym'Tor would not tolerate such a creature hunting our people. If the creature turns out to be real, I promise that I will, very soon, aid your hunt. Do you need anything else?_
I'm afraid that I can't take your word for it. My hunt continues.
The wizard seems disappointed. _Of course. We would never dream of hindering you. Take your time. I'm sorry that I had to disappoint you._
The beast exists. I have seen it.
Moritz'Kri is surprised. _Really? A shadowy, savage beast, lost in the woods. How fascinating. Rest assured that I will return to the tower and join your hunt, using my magic to aid my vision._
_Oghrym'Tor will not tolerate such a creature hunting our people. I promise that I will, very soon, aid your hunt. Do you need anything else?_
I am from Avadon, and my purpose is private.
The wizard nods, but you can see how displeased he is at this answer. _We can offer much aid, but only if we know what you seek. When you see that it is wise to trust us, I will be here._
You are a mage?
Moritz'Kri stands up straight and subtly shakes his upper torso, showing off his shoulderpads. _Not any mere sorcerer. My line has served the lords of Oghrym'Tor since its construction began._
_My line has its own tower, to the north, but I spend most of my time at this keep, ever at my master's call._
I will go now.
_Yes. Wise lord Carsta'Arl has instructed me to remain out here when you are in the area. If you need more aid, I will provide it. If I can._
You are aware that Avadon restricts the activities of Farlander wizards?

He gives you a subservient smile. _I am. We have never hidden anything from Avadon. If you can ever enter this keep, you will see that I have made sure to never exceed the powers of mages of the Pact. I am ... humble._
Where did you learn your magic?
_From my father, and from certain scrolls and tomes. All Avadon-approved, I assure you._
He nods. _Yes?_
You notice that Jenell is walking with unusual purpose in her step. Her weapon is constantly in her hand, as if she expects rampaging barbarians to rush out of the bushes at any moment.
She notices you looking at her. _I must be alert. You should be too. I am from the Wyldrylm, and the Khemerians are our blood foes. They might seem pleasant on the surface. Don't let them fool you._
Sevilin looks around and smiles. _Seems a nice enough place._ Jenell responds, _You will see._
I will remember your warning. Let's move on.
She nods, unconvinced. _I hope you heed my warning. Many have died underestimating the savages of Khemeria._
Why do the Wyldrylm and Khemeria hate each other so much?
_Once we were one land, one nation of tribes, sometimes rivals, sometimes even at war. But, in the end, we were one people, and we would always band together against outsiders._
_But the northerners were different from us in the south. They looked with envy at the weapons and walls of the east. They abandoned the old way. They become warped and twisted._
What old ways?
_The ways of the nomad and the hunter. The old standards of honor. The wisdom of the chieftains and shamans. Selecting our leaders from the wisest, instead of passing rulership from parent to child._
_They threw away everything that makes us what we are. It sickens me._
Warped and twisted how?

_Once the northerners had steel weapons and stone walls, they also adopted the savage ways of the east. Building empires. Not being content with their own lands. Sending siege trains across the west, leaving a trail of blood and screams._
_Perhaps it did not have to be this way. But it is what happened, and we of the south bore the worst of their savagery. That is what drew us to join the Pact._
So what happened then?
_They drew apart from us. Once, all of these lands were proudly called the Wyldrylm. They took the name Khemeria. 'Khemer' means 'Mighty' in the old speech._
_I hate them. I am not ashamed to admit it._
I'm counting on you to keep control.
_I am always in control. I am a warrior of the Wyldrylm. Let us continue._
She walks silently at your side, still alert.
They are Farlanders. We should hate them.

She nods. _All Farlanders are our foes, but the Khemerians will always have a special, dark place in my heart. But enough. I think I have said enough. I will follow my orders and complete my mission. Onward._
Not all Khemerians are evil, surely.

She shrugs. _Laurella seemed kind enough, it is true. But I judge them for what their people do. All of them can ..._ She pauses. _I think I have said enough. I will follow my orders and complete my mission. Onward._
You notice that something seems wrong with Jenell. She seems ... Distracted. Not ill, not angry, but something is wrong.
She sees that you are looking at her. _Forgive me. I find I am ... not myself. Do not worry. I will be ready when the battle comes._
You had better be. I am counting on you.
_I will. This village just reminded me of ... Never mind. I will be ready._ She walks silently at your side, more alert.
_It is ... It is nothing. Only, this village reminded me of ... For a moment, I thought of home. It looks the same._
Looks are deceiving. The lord here has broken the laws of the Pact.

She nods. _We are here with a purpose. A noble purpose. I have not forgotten. Only ... Part of me wishes things had been different. But I am ready. Come on. Let us finish our mission._ She walks silently at your side.
We have our orders. We must carry them out.

She nods. _Of course. My loyalty and dedication have never wavered, not for a moment, and this is still Khemeria. Only ... Part of me wishes things had been different. But I am ready. Come on. Let us finish our mission._ She walks silently at your side.
Perhaps there is some way this village can be spared.

_No. It will only be destroyed by different Hands than us. Its leader plotted against the Pact. All must pay. Forgive my distraction. Come on. Let us finish our mission._ She walks silently at your side.
As you approach the ominous gates of Oghrym'Tor, Shima stops walking. _Please wait, [N]._
_It appears that we will be fighting side by side for some time. If you are to trust me with your life, there is something you should know about me._
Sevilin listens with great interest. He has obviously been curious about Shima.
Jenell listens with great interest. She has obviously been curious about Shima.
Nathalie listens with great interest. She has obviously been curious about Shima.
I don't care about your past, as long as you follow orders.
Shima nods. He is grateful. A little. _I appreciate that, although I would have preferred ... But never mind. I appreciate your words. Let us continue._ He moves on.
_I was born into the Threespear Clan, one of the oldest and most influential clans in Holklanda. That is all in the past now. Our power raised us high, but it attracted enemies._
_My father, the head of the clan, misjudged and joined the wrong side of a political struggle. He was branded a traitor. The fight ended in his death and the dishonor and dissolution of my clan._
And what happened to you?
_My father used what remained of his fading influence to have me recruited as a Hand of Avadon. Only fear of Avadon keeps the assassins from my room at night._
What happened to the rest of your clan?
_Shamed. Exiled. Once my father was dead, only a few of our elders needed to be assassinated. Most live, but in a ... reduced state._
Why do you tell me?
_So you understand. I think we will travel far together, and you should know my background. Also, that I have enemies._
And do you seek revenge?

He is silent for a long time. Finally, he says, _I will always do my best to follow the orders of Avadon. Come. Let us continue._ As he walks on, you realize that he didn't even come close to answering your question.
As long as you fight well, you are welcome at my side.
He nods and laughs. _Then you might make a poor Holklanda, but I appreciate your understanding. My blade serves Avadon without question. Now let us continue._ He walks on.
But you are from a family of traitors?
He manages to control his anger. _You sound like a Holklandan. That is what it says on the official record, but I am as loyal to the Pact as any man living. Now let us continue._ He walks on.
The box contains spools of thread, maps of the nearby woods, some whetstones, and mixed supplies. Nothing of value.
There is also a rolled-up scroll. Your name is written on the outside. You take it and open it.

It says, _[N] - I must save the warriors of my land before they bring the doom of Avadon upon themselves. I have found that their trail leads to Jarlswood. If I do not return soon, I have made an error. I am sorry for any troubles I have caused. - Jenell_
You look at the maps in the box. You soon find where Jarlswood is. It is a day's hike to the east. (You can now go there on the world map.)

This dome is full of cooking fires and low clay ovens. It is where the clan members in Dhorl Stead come to bake their bread and socialize. The aromas of smoke and dough are heavy in the air. It is a cheery place, or, at least, it was until you arrived.

The ovens are tended to by one old woman. She approaches you with a cheery air you have come to recognize: the attitude of one who fears Avadon but is determined to be as friendly and helpful as possible until you go away.
She says, _Welcome, visitors. Have a seat. Have a fresh-baked roll. Everyone knows Dhorl Stead is a friendly place. I am Nixie, and I tend to the ovens. Can I help you?_
Nixie stands near you as you explore this small hall. She occasionally proffers to you a slice of bread with honey or a little bit of corn cake.
It's like having a loving grandmother nearby, if that grandmother were constantly afraid that you were going to destroy her entire village.
I need to talk to you.
The people in the hall suddenly become very subdued. Nixie subtly nods toward the window. Then she says, _Oh, we can talk. About little things. Nothing of importance. Not now, anyway._
And she does talk to you. About baking. The weather. Any serious questions are politely deflected. Eventually, you leave, no wiser for the time spent.
_This is the baking hall. The center of every Stead in Khemeria. People come here to cook. To talk. It is a warm place, and it is my purpose to look after it._
It is a common practice?
_Yes, all over Khemeria. And the Wyldrylm too. Many of our practices and theirs remain the same, though a border divides us now._
Jenell says, _That is right. Khemeria keeps all of the old ways. Except the ones that matter._ Nixie, wisely, ignores her.
Do people eat here?
_No, most of the villagers cook their bread and stews and then return them to their homes._
_It cuts down on the number of fires we need to tend to. During the warm days of summer, the clans can let the fires in their halls dim, knowing that they can cook here._
_I tend to the fires. I keep the ovens and firepits in good repair. And I talk to people and help to pass on the gossip._ She smiles. _Gossip is not an honorable pastime, but I can't resist._
How did you get this position?
_Like many callings, it is passed from father to daughter and mother to son. I spent my childhood cleaning the ashes out of these ovens. But I am aging, and soon I will pass the task on._
Any gossip for me?
She looks around nervously. Then she leans close and begins to whisper.
_Some think that there is a beast in the woods. Lord Carsta'Arl and his men claim that this is just a rumor. Those who wander the deep woods know better._
_The beast is gone, killed by you. But some claim that the darkness in the woods is still there. They can feel it. The Shadow Beast was only the first horror to visit us._
_Some of the maids in Oghrym'Tor have overheard arguments between the lord and his pet wizard. All is not well there._
_The hunters say that all feelings of darkness in the woods are gone. Dhorl Stead is safe and obedient now, and you can leave and not return._
I am on a mission here.

Nixie looks worried. She shakes her head. _I am a simple woman. I tend to fires. I tell tales. I don't get involved in the workings of power. Please don't say anything to me about it. I'm not the one who learns of such things._
You seem to know a lot.
_About village gossip. Not about the wilds._
Who does know?
_Lord Carsta'Arl and his servants, like Hunter Salom, know much. But they are ... I shouldn't say._
Well, who can help me?

She sighs. Her smile fades. She realizes that it is a risk to tell you, but it is also the best way to be rid of you. _The Runners, the hunters of the tribes, they go into the deep woods. They bear knowledge, and they bear it with honor._
I have slain a beast in the dark woods.
She nods slowly. There is a tiny bit of a smile on her face. _We all thank you for your help. I suppose you will be leaving now._
I came here to hunt down Moritz'Kri.
She shakes her head. _I don't want to know it. I don't want to know any of it. When you come, death follows, and it comes closer and closer to us._
When this is done, I will leave.
_So you say. But we know ... we know ... Please leave. I have work to do._ She walks unsteadily away.
Only those who oppose the Pact must fear me.
_We are Farlanders. I've lived long. I've seen. Once Avadon comes ... Once it comes ... Please leave. I have work to do._ She walks unsteadily away

Although this remote hall is full of trophies, only two people are here. A hunter and her husband. Though lines are starting to appear on her face, she is still no stranger to the woods. There is a bow over her shoulder and a blade at her belt.
She nods to you. _Welcome, travelers of the land of our foes. I am Runner Faiga. As long as you mean us well, I will give you the respect due a true warrior._
Runner Faiga sits and faces you. She is determined to show you proper courtesy, though she is ready to draw a blade at a moment's notice. A friendly Farlander is still a Farlander.
I am trying to find a shaman. Her name is Jenell. Has she come here?
Faiga nods. _I do not like to help the Wyldrylm, but I cannot refuse a shaman. She left a note for you. It is in a box in our bedroom. You may have it._
_I am a hunter, but I am clanless. I am of Dhorl Stead and welcomed by them, I am not one of the four clans who make up most of the settlement._
Clanless?

_I was born in a small settlement in Stara Stead. The raiders of Dhorl Stead destroyed it when I was three, and one of the runners could not bring himself to kill me. He brought me here and raised me instead._
Couldn't you join a clan?
_Of course, by joining with one of its members. But, fool me, I fell in love with another clanless._ She looks over at her husband. They smile. _A mistake I will never cease regretting._
Is life as a clanless difficult?
_It is not as easy, but we are not mistreated. And I have certain freedoms they do not, as I don't have a name I can dishonor._
And you do not seek revenge?
She shrugs. _It is the way of Khemeria. I am a runner of Dhorl Stead now. I might as well seek revenge by cutting off my own leg._
I am in need of information.

She looks down. _I would help you. There is nothing to be gained by resisting Avadon. However, it would be better if you went to Lord Carsta'Arl. He would be annoyed if I was presumptuous enough to deal with you before he saw you._
I have been to Oghrym'Tor. I was turned away at the gates.
You instantly have the undivided attention of Faiga and her husband. _They turned you away? Turned away Avadon? They they ... They must ..._
She shakes her head. _Let us give you the hospitality that they held back. For the good of our Stead, I mean. I will speak with you._
I want to know more about your role in the village.
_What my work is? Why we live so far out here? I am a hunter, of course. And I sometimes look for hunters from the outside to pass trophies on to._
Why do you live so far out here?
_Because I have said some things that were the cause for anger. About Lord Carsta'Arl. And his wizard._
What did you say about Carsta'Arl?

_That he has turned from the old ways. The path of Khemeria now is to build a stone keep, hide behind it, crush all nearby under your fist, and then tear apart the villages of everyone within a week's ride. A way of blood and fear._
_At least, that is my view. Carsta'Arl did not like my describing his path in such a way, so I left the protection of the Stead._
What did you say about his wizard?
_Old Moritz'Kri? Only that he is a craven, servile toady with far more power than wisdom or sense._ She smiles. _Besides that, nothing._
What do you hunt?
_Less than I used to. Wild game, and huge spiders that get too close to the village. Though I have fallen behind even in that work._
Pass trophies on?

_Some weapons and pieces of armor are trophies, meant to be passed on to those who have earned them with courage and feats of arms. I look for hunters from outside the village to take on dangerous foes. That way, we do not lose our own young._
_Finding these warriors falls to me because I am clanless. The clans are embarrassed by looking for someone to hunt for them. Even if they need it._
I am a hunter.
She nods. _So you are. Perhaps we might help each other. There is a bridge to the east. On the other side is a trapdoor leading down to some caves._

_The caves are full of bats. The large sort, that hunt our young. Kill the largest of them, the one with one of its fangs broken off, and you will have proven yourself. And I will, of course, reward you with a trophy._
I killed that bat in the caves.
She nods. Then she fetches a polished hardwood rod from the wall and gives it to you. _I took this from an enemy shaman. I pass it on to you for your bravery._

_It is a small trophy, but it is the beginning. If Avadon is to be watching our village, at least there is some good that can come of it. And there is more you can do for us, if you wish the rewards._
_You can help another traveling clanless. His name is Shavon. I asked him to aid us and sent him north to the Dhorla Woods. I have heard nothing from him since._
_Let me know what happened to him. And, if he lives, help him to complete his mission._
What was his mission?
_I don't want to let you steal his bounty out from under him. I will let him explain it. If he is dead, then I will tell you more._
_If you are exploring the Dhorla Woods, watch for a lone young hunter. Ambitious, and probably in trouble._
Shavon's mission has been completed.
_I am pleased to hear it, but it is no surprise. Shavon has already collected his reward and left. I will now give you yours._
She sighs. _I am pleased to hear it, though Shavon never collected his reward, so I suspect that things did not end well for him. You have earned his trophy._
She takes a ring out of a pouch and hands it to you. _The hunter who trained me collected that. I wore it with pride. Now it is yours._
She looks disturbed. _There is something I have learned. Something that needs ... to be looked into. But not yet. Soon, I think. Speak with me later._

She looks disturbed. _There is something I have learned. Something that needs ... to be looked into. It might not be possible for you to do this, however, as it would mean entering the tower of the wizard Moritz'Kri._
_I have heard that there are Khemerians being held prisoner in Moritz'Kri's tower. Not of our Stead, but Khemerians nonetheless. I want them freed._
Why are they being held?
_I don't know. I have only heard rumors from hunters who were in the hills above the tower. Things they saw. I don't want to guess why. I only want them out._
_In a small, gray tower to the east of the wizard's large central tower. Not far. Still within the complex. If they are held there, that is where._
There were prisoners in Moritz'Kri's tower. (Say what happened.)
You tell Runner Faiga the tale. She looks ill. _The wizard was a monster. I never thought I would say this, but I am glad that Avadon sent for him._
She brings another wand from her wall and gives it to you. _As gratitude for your help. And for purging us of this vile sickness._
I would like to earn another trophy.

_I ..._ She shakes her head. _I think I am only acting to draw you closer to us. You have helped us, but we do not want you to stay. I will only ask your help again if we are truly desperate. And maybe not even then._
I have been sent by Avadon to look for something.
She nods slowly. _I guessed as much. You must have a dread purpose to come this far._
_Will you trust me enough to tell me what you come for?_
That is private Avadon business. I can't tell you.
She seems annoyed. _Then you should leave me. I don't think we have anything else to say to each other._
I hunt the creature made of shadows that has been stalking your Stead.

She nods. _I know. You let your purpose slip, and Hunter Salom has spread the word that anyone who helps you will suffer. A blunder. But I do not fear them, not when that horror comes up to the gates of my home._
She nods. _I guessed. Few know that Stonemaster Roth's daughter left for Avadon, but I saw her leave and I watched over her until she reached the free roads._
The beast is real. It is out there. It is growing bolder. It needs to be slain, and Lord Carsta'Arl does nothing to help._
Why won't Lord Carsta'Arl help you?
_I have my guesses, but it is unwise to say overmuch. Not yet._
Tell me about the beast.
_Like a wolf, almost as tall as a man, cloaked in darkness. And fast ... I have never seen a beast so fast. It does not always attack. But when it does, it is ... terrible._
I need to find it. Where is it?
_It is everywhere and nowhere. It moves like wind and leaves no tracks._

_But I can tell you the section of the woods where it has been seen the most. Go north to the Dhorla Woods. You will be near Moritz'Kri's tower. Then find the northwest road. Follow it, and you will be near where I saw the creature._
The Shadow Beast has been slain.
You tell her the tale. She nods. _That was boldly done, and we would expect no less from a warrior of Avadon. We owe you a debt. And I am sure that is the end of your business._
_We hope you leave with our thanks. And don't return._
I was sent here to find Moritz'Kri.

_I guessed as much. The rumors began to fly the moment you arrived. I am a skilled hunter, but I will not get involved in a battle between a skilled wizard and the warriors of Avadon. I value life too much._
I have killed Moritz'Kri.

She nods. _It was as if a veil of blackness was lifted from the woods. I had no idea how far that creature's infection had spread. And now, I hope, your work is done here. You will be missed. After you are gone._
A hunter is waiting for you in her home, sword drawn. Her husband stands nearby, and they are both ready to defend themselves. _I am Runner Faiga,_ she says, _and I will not cower from you._
Runner Faiga is waiting for you in her home, sword drawn. Her husband stands nearby, and they are both ready to defend themselves. _I had hoped this would be avoided. I was a fool._
_You are from Avadon. You are a killer and a monster. We all should have known it the moment you arrived._
_And to think I bestowed trophies on you! I will never live down the shame._
_Get out of my home, or I will slay you._
I will let you leave, but you have to go. It is your only hope.
She nods sadly. _Your arrival marked our doom, but I will not throw away our lives. Especially since we are innocent. We broke no laws! My people never ..._ She chokes up.
Then she and Trevar pack up a few things for the road. It doesn't take long. She shoots you one final glance of pure loathing. Then they are gone.
You draw a blade on me, Farlander? You will pay! (Attack.)
