Runner Faiga shakes her head. _What a fool I was. But I will avenge all who are lost! Feel the wrath of Khemeria!_ And she lunges at you with amazing speed.
This is an old, wooden clan hall that has been converted into a trading post. Merchants from all over Khemeria and beyond pass through Dhorl Stead. The power of the local lords has attracted trade.
A woman is inspecting a newly-arrived shipment of bolts of cloth. When she sees you, she walks quickly over to you. This Khemerian is not happy to see warriors of the Pact in her post.
_I am Edeline,_ she says, _and this is my shop. My shop. What do you need?_
Edeline watches you grimly as you wander through her trading post. You do your best to ignore her obvious loathing.
Her dislike suddenly switches to fear. Her eyes flick toward the window. _This is not a good time to talk to an outsider. I am very busy. Excuse me._
Before you can respond, she turns on her heel and walks away.
She shakes her head. _The word came from the fortress. Hunter Salom has said that we are not to speak with you._ She points to the northeast. _Go to Oghrym'Tor. They will give you all you need._
Before you can respond, she turns on her heel.
Wait.
She ignores you. Soon she is on the other side of the hall.
The fortress has turned me away. Now you will talk to me.
Edeline's face grows flushed. She is trapped. She looks you in the eye. _I will not anger Avadon. You go where you will. Do what you will. Ask what you want and leave me alone._
Tell me about this post.
She shrugs. _Merchant caravans pass through here. From the rest of Lynaeus to Khemeria, and then back. I trade with them. I supply them._
_I hope you are not here to threaten me. I have done all I need to to comply with all of the Pact's laws, no matter how unjust._
Khemeria has a lot of trade?
_More and more every year. As we leave behind the old ways, our wealth grows. We aren't a bunch of isolated tribes, crude and dirty. We have cities and craftsmen now. We are proud._
How is the Pact unjust?
_You have merchants. So do the Farlands. But your laws make sure that your traders always have an advantage. Farlanders are not allowed to compete, and we have to pay extra taxes and tariffs to you._
I've lost interest in what you are saying.
_Of course. You don't make laws. You only use them to crush us._
And you think I am here to harm you?
_That is the only reason Avadon ever comes. But I follow all your laws, pay all your duties. So what do you want from me?_
I have come here looking for something.
She frowns. _I will help you if I can, and if it gets you to move on. What do you want?_
I am hunting a beast made of shadows.
_Ah. I have heard of it. It has even attacked one of the caravans coming here. Two guards were killed and eaten. But I am no hunter. I don't go into the wilds. I can't help you._
Who can?
_I don't know. What else do you need?_
That is a secret.
_Then I can't help you. What else do you need?_
She frowns and shakes her head. _I follow your laws. I am forced to bow to the Pact. But I will not deal with you._
She nods. _I appreciate your respect. Excuse me. I am busy._ She turns and walks away.
You refuse a warrior of Avadon? You will trade with me, or things will be difficult for you.
Her cheeks flush red. _I ... I understand. I have a few items you might find useful. I can trade with you._
All right.
You will also give me a discount. Or else.
She is silent. Then she nods, beaten. _All right. Anything to be rid of you. Let me know when you want to trade._
I'm ready to trade.
_I am thrilled to hear it. Do you wish to sell or to see what few weapons I have?_
Edeline's Trading Post
Edeline loathes you, but she is willing to trade what few arms she has gathered to get you to leave.
Edeline loathes you, but she is willing to trade what few arms she has gathered to get you to leave. You have coerced her into giving you a discount.
_All right. Do you require anything else?_
She nods. Then she turns on her heel and walks away.
This is a familiar sight in villages all across Khemeria and the Wyldrylm. An old shaman sitting behind a fire, incense heavy in the air, waiting to give advice or judgment.
But this hall has been neglected. The trophies are old and dusty. The floor is dirty. Few come here. The old woman behind the fire was asleep when you entered.
Then her eyes open. She sees you. Then she begins to croak, _Ah. [N]. Envoy of our enemy. You have arrived. Come. Step forward. Old Unni will see you now._ You step forward.

Unni sits behind the fire, cross-legged. Sometimes she lights incense or sings an old chant. Much of the time, she sleeps, alone. When you are here, she watches you calmly, hoping to do what she can for her village.
I wish to speak with you.
_And I am not supposed to talk to you. The word already comes from Oghrym'Tor. But I am a shaman, not bound by their words. I will talk to you, because it is my only way to protect our village._
I don't mean you any harm.
_Perhaps not in your heart. But we are no longer invisible. Avadon has come to us. For any Farlander, that means great danger._
I only came to hunt something.
_And I might help you. Be careful who you tell of that, though. Those who rule us can use that knowledge to do harm._
_And I might help you. I wish you had come to me first, though. Those who rule us will use the knowledge you gave them to do harm._
I am a Hand of Avadon. You will give me all the knowledge I require.
She nods slowly. _I will help you, to protect our village. And, I hope, to reach what justice you have in your heart._
So you are a shaman.
_I am. A lonely post, in this new age. I could be very useful. Giving wisdom. Making potions. Training my successor. Tending to the sacred circles. But I ... There is no place for me here now._
Jenell looks sad. _I did not expect to find any followers of the old ways in Khemeria._
Unni responds, _Child, not all of us wish to be apart from the Wyldrylm, but it is not my decision. It is not the task of a shaman to rule the land, but to serve it._
What wisdom do you have?
_I have no wisdom for Avadon. It is a strange thing to me. Far from this place. Far from what I know._
Can I buy a potion from you?
Unni says, _I sell healing brews to all, no matter who they are or where they are from._
Unni's Potions
Unni sells potions to all travelers, even those from Avadon.
Do you have a successor?

_No. None. All who might have stayed have gone off to the fortresses, using their skills for war or trade. One day, a young, traveling shaman will come here to serve. But he or she will not be of this place._
_It makes me sad._
Tell me about the sacred circles.
_There is little to tell. The stones are where we meet with nature, expose ourselves to it. Magic places, but places that can draw dark forces._
_I am old and weak, and Lord Carsta'Arl does not care about the circles. I cannot tend to them all myself, even when they fall into darkness._
I'm not interested in this.
_You are far from alone in that. What more do you need?_
There is a corrupted circle? Where?
_I have done what I can, so only one of our circles has fallen into darkness. I would like to restore it, but I lack the strength._
_It is in the Dhorla Woods. To purify it, first the dark spirits would have to be challenged. Then driven out._
Challenged how?

_The presence of the living is enough to challenge them. Stand in the circle long enough and the creatures will be drawn. But none want to expose themselves to such peril, so the circle will stay lost._
I have driven the dark spirits from the circle in the Dhorla Woods.
She looks up at you, surprised. _What? This ..._ She closes her eyes. _Yes. I feel it. A shadow has been lifted. And you ... You did this? It is a good deed, that should be rewarded._

Without opening her eyes, she raises her hand. She mutters a spell. You feel a sense of ... warmth. Of protection. Then she opens her eyes. _I have blessed you. You will be shielded as you roam through dark places._
Can you purify the stone circle now?
_Though the dark spirits are gone, reclaiming the circle is not possible. To do so, I would need ... I ... I need to think on this more. Perhaps, if you return later, I will know more._

_Though the dark spirits are gone, reclaiming the circle is not possible. To do so, I would need a totem. It was stolen from the circle. If I had it back, I might be able to purify it._ She describes it to you.
_I hesitate to ask Avadon to fetch our sacred relics, but who else would help me now?_
Where is the totem?

_It took much work, much farsight, much talking to animal kin, but I was able to track who took it. It was the wizard Moritz'Kri, who took the totem from where it belonged and carried it into his tower._
_I think you might be there soon. If so, I hope you will watch for our totem._
_I understand nothing of what that creature does. His power is not our power. He probably thought that the totem had some force he could extract and devour._
I found the totem. (Give it to her.)

You set the totem on the floor in front of her. She closes her eyes and rests her hand upon it. Soon, her features contort in grief and anger. She pulls her hand back. _That creature! He warped it! He ... corrupted it, trying to extract what he could. I have ... much to do._

Without opening her eyes, she raises her hand. She mutters another spell. The aura of warmth that surrounds you grows stronger. Then she opens her eyes. _I have added to your blessings, shielding you as you roam the wastes._
I gave the totem to Lady Antje.
Unni looks ill. She bows her head. _The lady .. she corrupts all of the old ways. The circle will not be reclaimed. It is hard to take. Please ... Leave me. I need to rest._
Is there anything else I can do to help you reclaim the circle?
_It will take time to examine the totem, to see if it can be saved or must be destroyed. Before I can enlist your help, I will need time. You do have my gratitude._
Can you tell me about your leaders?
_Yes, leaders. That is what we have. Not chieftains. I am free to speak of it. Being a shaman gives me some privileges._

_We have a Lord. Lord Carsta'Arl. He controls all of the settlements for many miles. He inherited his little empire from his family, and he controls it with a fist of steel and the power of his wizard._
_And here, in Dhorl Stead, the voice of our lord is Hunter Salom. And a harsh voice it is, too._
Tell me about Lord Carsta'Arl.

_He rules from Oghrym'Tor, and he is skilled. A fierce warrior and hunter, and a cunning leader in war. He expects total loyalty for the people in his lands. To disobey is to be crushed, in the modern Khemerian fashion._
Is he a wise leader?
_Wisdom does not matter here. He has, in his short life, added two Steads to the land of the Dhorla. A mighty achievement. Much blood has flowed at his word._
_And yet, he has drawn the gaze of Avadon. Perhaps he is not so cunning after all._
Do the people ever wish to be rid of him?
_No. As much as he is hated, he has power. Power brings safety. Khemeria is a cruel and violent place now, and only thick walls save us from being burned away by a rival Stead._
I want to know more about his wizard.
_The wizard Moritz'Kri has a personal dislike for me, and his power is great. He also seems to hear all that is said about him. I will not speak._
_The wizard Moritz'Kri has a personal dislike for me, and his power is great. I also have heard rumors that you seek him. I will not speak of him._
Hunter Salom speaks for Carsta'Arl?
_He and his warriors watch the people of Dhorl Stead closely. None are free to speak when Salom is near. Salom gets all of the honors that should go to the hunters._
_Carsta'Arl, the people fear and respect. Hunter Salom is only hated._
I wish to discuss my purpose here.
_I see. The hall of a shaman is sacred. You may speak freely here._
Actually, I don't think I will.
_That is your choice. At some point, however, you will need to trust someone. You might not want it to be Cartsa'Arl or his servants._
I hunt a beast, wrapped in shadow.
_Ahhh ... You have met Laurella. Her father, Roth, told me of his fear for her._
_I know of the beast. I can feel its darkness, how it warps the land around it. It should be hunted, but Lord Carsta'Arl pretends that it does not exist._
She thinks. _It should be hunted. And yet, perhaps, not slain._
You think it should not be slain?
_I am ... uncertain. I can feel it. It is a warped thing. And yet ... I think that it is not mindless. I am not a soldier. I cannot doom a creature unless I feel I understand it._
_I don't know. It roams deep in the woods, far from my sight. But ... The hunters. The explorers of the deep woods. They might be able to tell you more._
_I know. I felt it. I sensed the death of that poor, warped creature. It is good that it is gone._
_And yet ... I feel that darkness remains. I must think on it. The sickness in the woods has not yet been purged._
I am here to find Moritz'Kri.
_I have heard rumors. I do not know how your purpose was guessed so easily. I cannot help you in your quest. Moritz'Kri is ... I do not care for him. But even I fear acting against him._
She nods. _There was a sickness. It twisted the land. It has been purged. You have done well._
_And now ... I only hope that you are allowed not to return. Avadon's attention brings judgment and violence. I hope that you can finally turn away from us. But ... we will see._
_Now, please leave me. I am tired._ She waves you away and closes her eyes.
_Then I bid you farewell. I must rest now._ She lowers her chin to her chest and closes her eyes.

You meet a Khemerian warrior. He is in his twenties, but he bears the cruel demeanor and web of scars of a grizzled veteran far older. His armor bears the trophies of many fallen foes, a number of them human.

He steps past the warriors who escort him, stands up straight and looks you in the eye. _I am Hunter Salom,_ he says. _Watcher of Dhorl Stead and favored hunter of Lord Carsta'Arl. And thus, head hunter of all Dhorl Stead._
_What do you want here, servant of the Pact?_
Hunter Salom watches you calmly. If he feels any fear of Avadon, he hides it completely. Foolhardy, perhaps, but he is strong and cruel enough to have some reason not to fear.
_What else do you want, Pact Soldier? I have a patrol to complete._
_I aid mighty Lord Carsta'Arl in keeping Dhorl Stead safe. He seeks out and destroys our foes outside our borders. We watch and listen for treachery within._
He looks around the village. You notice that the streets are unusually clear when Salom is present. There is fear in the air. Hunter Salom smiles.
Hunter Salom looks toward the village to the southwest. _Who knows what treachery is taking place there while I am away?_
What sort of treachery do you search for?
_Words or deeds that would weaken the rule of mighty Lord Carsta'Arl. The lord brings safety to the people here. All he expects in return is loyalty._
You hunt your own village?
_It is not a mere village. It is a Stead. And we only do what the warriors of Avadon do. Watch for threats. Maintain peace. Eliminate the disloyal._
And what do you do when you find someone who is disloyal?
Salom's warriors grin viciously. _We inform Lord Carsta'Arl. Sometimes he acts. Sometimes he has me act in his place. We then make sure that, in the end, calm is returned._
I have been sent from Avadon.
Hunter Salom clearly wishes to ask you some questions. However, he has his orders. _I have been told that, now that I have found you, I am to send you to Oghrym'Tor._ He points to the northeast.
_Lord Carsta'Arl or his servants will tell you all you need to know._
_And you have been to Oghrym'Tor. Now I am free to speak with you._

_We want nothing but to give Avadon what it wants so that it can leave us. However, to do this, we need to know what it wants. Please tell me._ All of his warriors suddenly become very attentive. _Why are you here?_
Nathalie subtly taps you on the shoulder. When you turn to look at her, she looks very worried.
Shima subtly taps you on the shoulder. When you turn to look at him, he looks very worried.
Our business is private, for now.
Salom looks disappointed. _If you won't trust me, I can't help you. I will continue my patrol. When you are ready to let me aid you, search the roads._ He and his soldiers move on.
I am hunting a wild creature in the woods, fast, vicious, and wreathed in shadow.

He nods solemnly, but you can see the glint of triumph in his eyes. _Well, I can make your visit very short. It is but a rumor. A local legend. It does not exist. Sometimes wolves and spiders kill those lost in the woods, and the shaman spins the tales into lies._
_But I am curious. How did Avadon learn of our little local legend?_
That is not your concern.

_Of course. Well, I have my ways of finding out these things. I thank you for your aid. Now we must resume our patrol. The hunt for traitors never ends._ He and his soldiers move on, chuckling as they go.
A girl named Laurella.
Hunter Salom smiles viciously. _Of course. The girl. Well, we will do her best to reassure her family. Dealing with these sorts of people is what we do best._
_Now we must resume our patrol. The hunt for traitors never ends._ He and his soldiers move on, chuckling as they go.
I want to discuss the shadowy monster in the woods.

Salom shakes his head. _I told you. Lies. Illusions. Wolves. That is all. I don't know what you thought you saw, but Lord Carsta'Arl says the creature does not exist. So it doesn't exist. I can tell you nothing else._

Hunter Salom shakes his head. _I'm sure it was probably only a wolf, and you couldn't see it clearly in the shadows. I don't know what you thought you saw, but Lord Carsta'Arl says the creature does not exist. So it doesn't exist. I can tell you nothing else. _

Hunter Salom and his soldiers look grim. For a moment, you see fear in his eyes. _So we have heard. Avadon returns, and it is going to hunt. We don't know where the wizard is. Do what you need to. We have a patrol._
They walk off quickly. Salom's warriors cast nervous glances behind them as they go.

Hunter Salom and his soldiers look grim. For a moment, you see fear in his eyes. _So we have heard. That is ... We can do nothing about that. We ... We must patrol._ They walk off quickly. Salom's warriors cast nervous glances behind them as they go.
A group of Khemerian warriors stands guard at the entrance to Oghrym'Tor. After years of terrorizing the villages of Dhorl Stead, they are now faced with their own judgment from a far greater power.
Their leader steps forward. It is Hunter Salom, and terror has reached him at last. And yet, he is ready to die to protect his master. He points his weapon at your chest.

Their leader steps forward. He is, perhaps for the first time in his life, terrified. He says, _I am Hunter Salom, Watcher of Dhorl Stead and favored hunter of Lord Carsta'Arl. I am ready to die to protect my master._ He points his weapon at your chest.
_If we do one thing before we cross beyond, it will be to spill the blood of Avadon!_
I am only here for Carsta'Arl.
_Do you still not understand? This is Khemeria, land of war! Our lord and his keep are our lives! Without them and our discipline, we are lost!_
_Come, Khemerians! Today we fight for our home!_ They let out the familiar scream of challenge and charge.
We can discuss this. Avadon can spare you. You don't have to die.

_And if Carsta'Arl is gone? What will happen to us? What do you think the villagers will do to me as a reward for my protecting them? We will be hunted down by worms, eager for their little vengeance._
Your time has come, Khemerian. (Attack.)
_It is all the same to you, Hand? Each day you must spill the blood of a Farlander? Well, today you find a true and worthy foe!_

Although Khemeria and the Wyldrylm value hunting greatly, raising crops is still very important. The fields here are worked by several farmers. One of them, older and more scarred than the rest, is tying a blade to his belt.
He looks at you defiantly. _You are treading on my fields, Avadon. I am Hahn, and I am watching you._
The farmer Hahn watches you closely. His sword is old, but it is dangerous enough in a skilled hand. One thing you learned in your training: everyone is dangerous.
You are a farmer?
_I am. But before that, I was a hunter, and I won three trophies of honor. And, if I need to, I will fight! Both you and those who brought you here._
Trophies of honor?
_Our best trophies, the arms and armor, are passed down from warrior to warrior. I won my sword for slaying the Mung Rats of the Swampy Reaches. I will use it to defend Dhorl Stead._
Why did you quit hunting?
_Age. Wanting to leave prey to the ... Wait. I will tell you nothing. About anything._
You will fight those who brought me here?
_Someone told you to come here. When we find out who drew the gaze of Avadon to us, we will be sure to make them pay._

_We know you came here to hunt that beast. And we know that Roth's girl Laurella wanted to send for help to hunt the beast. If we find out that she drew the gaze of Avadon to us, we will be sure to make her pay._
I have been sent here by Avadon.
_I can't do anything about that. And I won't help you. No matter what._
Not even to find the shadowy beast that stalks you?
That stops him for a moment. But then he says, _Not even then, Pact warrior. Your coming here can bring no good. None._
Why are you so hostile?
_You ask that of a Farlander? You rule us. You crush us. When we succeed at trade, your thieves come in to take our wealth. And now you come to our town, armed and ready to kill._
He pats his blade. _This is a trophy of honor. If I have to, I will use it to defend our town._
I mean your town no harm.
_Hah! Avadon carries destruction behind it like a stink. Now that you are here, judgment and death will follow. Now leave me, and take your lies with you._
He turns and walks away across his field.
Watch your tongue, old man. I am from Avadon.
He nods. _I understand. I will not oppose you. Not until you come back to destroy our home._
There is an old farmer standing in the middle of the field. Everyone else is gone. He looks stunned. An old sword is in his hand.
He looks over at you, and you recognize him. It is Hahn, the angry farmer you met earlier. He spits and hisses at you, _You! You come to destroy us at last!_
When you get close, he looks over at you, and you recognize him. His face is twisted in rage. He spits and hisses at you, _You! You come to destroy us at last!_
_All gone!_ he screams. _All lost! Dhorl Stead is destroyed! But you will pay for what you have brought! You will die!_ He lets out a mad battle scream and charges you.
As you walk down the path, this cool autumn afternoon suddenly becomes very cold. The shadows cast by the trees deepen. And something walks into view at the end of the path.
It looks like a huge wolf, almost your height. And yet, it is hard to tell. A wreath of shadows surrounds it, hiding its form and obscuring its motions.
It stares at you, motionless.
Nathalie hisses, _Yesssss ... We can bag the beast now._
This hunt was easier than I expected. (Attack.)
You take a step forward. The creature shies away. The shadows around it grow more intense. And then it turns and flees. It is amazingly fast. You try to give chase ...
(Watch the creature.)

You face the shadowy beast, each of you waiting for the other to make the first move. You can smell the blood and rot surrounding the creature. It might be peaceful now, but it is a merciless hunter when it chooses to be.

And then it does something unexpected. It opens its mouth, and sound comes out. Not a growl or animal sound, though. It sounds like it is trying to talk. Strange hacking and gurgling noises that could almost be words.
Jenell leans toward you and whispers, _Don't be fooled. That is no beast of nature. There is still darkness in it._
Sevilin leans toward you and whispers, _Don't be fooled. Take it from a hunter. There is darkness in that thing._
What are you saying? I don't understand?
The beast makes its hacking guttural noises at you for another minute. It tries a few variations. Louder, quieter, faster, slower, it's still gibberish.
It starts to shake with fury and frustration. And then it turns to flee. It moves amazingly quickly.
(Mimic the creature's sounds back to it.)
You copy the creature's sickly gurgling noises. It takes a step back and its hackles rise. It thinks that you are trying to mock it.
Then, shaking with fury and frustration, it turns to flee. It moves amazingly quickly.
(Just listen.)
The beast makes its hacking guttural noises at you for another minute. It starts to shake with fury and frustration. And then it turns to flee. It moves amazingly quickly.

You freeze. Something is watching you from the trees. He is well-hidden, but you have been out in the wilds too long to be fooled. He steps out of the shadows, realizing that you saw him. It is the Wayfarer, stalking you once again.

He walks toward you, keeping alert for crazed Khemerians that might do him harm. When he reaches you, he gives you a little nod. _You are here, I see. I knew you would be along soon. Only a matter of time until this story comes to its inevitable end._
Its inevitable end?

_Tales involving Avadon and Farlanders only end one way. I was only sent to witness it._ He looks east toward Oghrym'Tor. _A proud fort. Soon, it will be in ruins, its guards dead, its town unguarded._
Why are you here, Wayfarer?
_I have only been sent as a witness._ He looks east toward Oghrym'Tor. _A proud fort. Soon, it will be in ruins, its guards dead, its town unguarded._
I don't have time for this. I have a mission. (Push past him.)
He steps out of the way. _Don't let me stop you. I know you have blood to shed._ He turns and walks quickly to the west, eager to avoid the upcoming carnage.
Who sent you?
He shakes his head. _I think you will find out very soon. Not yet. My employer soon has much to say to you._
And you have come to gloat?
_Gloat? You think I take any pleasure in all this death? In the destruction of Dhorl Stead, most of which was innocent? You are mistaken._
_No. As I said, I am only a witness. But, I do wonder something._ Through the hole in his mask, you see a half-smile.
Say what you have to say and get it over with.
_Do not act like I am victimizing you. It is not I whose armor is splattered with blood.  But, I do wonder something._

_The Farlanders here, seeking only protection, turned to Avadon. Then Avadon sought for criminals, found them, and now the place will be in ruins. The nearby Steads, seeing weakness, will rush in. The suffering here only begins today. It will continue for some time to come._
_And you, in the end, are the agent of this inevitable end. Do you still feel? And, if so, how?_
I only seek Lord Carsta'Arl. He plotted against the Pact. He must be stopped.
_Of course. By your logic, there is no other possible end. But perhaps there are ways of living that don't require such a merciless process._
_Go. Catch Carsta'Arl. He taunted the Pact, he was caught, and he must pay the price. But don't forget. There can be other ways._
The Wayfarer turns, and, without another word, walks away. Soon, he will be far from Oghrym'Tor.
I have orders. I follow them.
the Wayfarer nods. _Such a banal explanation, but I understand it. I look for complexity where there is none. Will you ever awaken? I do not know._
They are only Farlanders. Why should I care either way?

_Really and truly? Are you so in the thrall of Avadon that these people are only creatures to you? It is probably so. That is the result of the power and wealth of Avadon._ He steps back. _Don't let me keep you. You have orders, after all._
It bothers me, but I see no other way.

He nods. _So you do have a heart after all. Go. Catch Carsta'Arl. He taunted the Pact, he was caught, and he must pay the price. But remember your doubt this day. Perhaps, soon, other paths will open to you._
Your words sound like plotting against Avadon. (Attack.)
The Wayfarer takes a step back and laughs. _Really? Don't you wonder how I travel so quickly?_ You launch a blow. _You don't realize that I ..._
Your weapons contact him. Or, where he would have been. He is gone. Not even a puff of smoke marks his departure.

As you return to the pylon that will take you back to Avadon, you see a small figure standing by the road. She is thin, dirty, and exhausted. The journey home has been draining for her, but she is finally here.

It is Laurella, the girl whose pleas drew Avadon's attention to Dhorl Stead. She looks at the smoke rising in the air over Oghrym'Tor, smells the blood on the wind. The bag containing her belongings slips to the ground.
Then she turns and looks at you. In shock, she seems to barely recognize you.
Hello, Laurella.
She looks at you. _You ... You came. You ... Did this? I heard ... the Beast is gone ... But then? What happened?_
Greetings. Are you all right?
She looks at you, somewhat confused. _I ... I am ... What happened here? I heard ... the Beast is gone ... But then? What has happened to my village?_
This might take a little bit of explaining.

She looks at you, very confused. _I remember you. I ... I talked ... You were going to help. Help us. I heard ... the Beast is gone. I came home ... But then? What has happened to the fortress? Where is everyone?_
(Walk past her.)
You face the path home. She looks down the road to a grim future. You walk silently past each other. Your business here is done. It is time to go back to Avadon.
I was sent to recover Carsta'Arl. He did not choose to return peacefully.

_Our lord? Gone? The fortress ... So much smoke ..._ She wavers slightly. For a moment, you think she is going to faint. Then she rallies. _You did this. You came for our lord. You destroyed us. I ... Why? Why?_
I had my orders. There was no other way.
Laurella shakes her head. _Miranda said ... Said you would just come to help. Help us. Why did she ... My home is ... lost? Wait. My father? Where is my father?_
And then, tears running down her face, she runs past you toward Dhorl Stead. You are at last free to return to Avadon.
He had to be brought to justice. All of this carnage is his fault.
Laurella shakes her head. _His fault? But ... You did not just take him. The smoke. The burning. Everything is lost! My home is ... lost. Wait. My father? Where is my father?_
Don't you dare question Avadon!
She stumbles back and looks up at you. There is fear in her eyes. Only fear for now, but the hate is sure to come later. _I ... I only ... My brother ... Where is my father?_
You are right. This should not have happened.

Laurella nods. _This should not have happened. Whatever my lord did, this ... this ... But it did happen._ She looks you in the eye. _You made it happen. And my home is ... lost? Wait. My father? Where is my father?_
You hear someone talking in the center of town. The people of Dhorl Stead suddenly become very nervous.
Talking: Laurella runs past you. She is close to panic.

entries.text: This is the inventory screen, where you will pick items up off the ground and use them. You can equip (i.e. wear or ready) items like weapons and armor, and you can use items like potions and crystals.

entries.text: If there is a sort of weapon or item you use a lot (like healing pods or a favorite sword), you can put it in a Quick Use item slot and use it from the main playing screen.
